notes: Study is primarily a computational/theoretical investigation using MD (ReaxFF force field, LAMMPS) and DFT (B3LYP/6-31G(d) for PES; M06-2X/def2tzvp for BDE) of SMP-10 pyrolysis mechanism. SMP-10 is liquid at room temperature. Pyrolysis temp of 827 C is converted from the stated >1100 K threshold. MD simulations run at 2000, 2250, and 2500 K; char yields were 71%, 76%, and 83 %wt respectively. Key pyrolysis steps: (1) retro-hydrosilylation (106 kcal/mol barrier) to regenerate SMP-10; (2) retro-ene elimination of propene (50 kcal/mol); (3) sequential H2 elimination forming diene (76 kcal/mol) and triene (58 kcal/mol); (4) final H2 elimination to 1,3,5-trisilabenzene (20 kcal/mol). Si-H BDE ~88 kcal/mol, ~10 kcal/mol lower than C-H counterpart. Allylic C-C BDE ~70.6 kcal/mol. Experimental ceramic yield of 82 %wt from Key et al. referenced.

For PSZ-20, volatilization losses are 41% of total in neat sample, decreasing to 33% after 8h at 77°C. After ~5h pre-treatment exposure, dominant weight loss mechanism shifts from volatilization to decomposition.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal; dehydrocoupling reactions; possible oxidation-assisted curing noted at surface under low vacuum conditions; chemical and photo-initiator methods mentioned as alternatives

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with polystyrene standards; Agilent 1260 HPLC with Waters Styragel columns (HT 2 and HR 4E), THF eluent at 1 mL/min, Wyatt OptiLab T-rEX RI detector; samples at 0.1 wt% in THF filtered through 0.2 µm PTFE filter. Mw and Mn both increase with pre-treatment duration. Peak of weight fraction curve settles near ~500 g/mol after extended pre-treatment. Dispersity (Mw/Mn) increases with pre-treatment for both polymers.

backbone_architecture.description: Both SMP-10 and PSZ-20 described as highly branched, widely polydisperse systems. SMP-10 is an allylhydridopolycarbosilane (Si:C backbone). PSZ-20 is a polysilazane (Si:N backbone) with significant methyl side groups. Both are thermoset-type systems.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SMP-10 is a SiC-forming precursor; PSZ-20 forms Si3N4 or SiCN depending on processing conditions. SEM performed on neat and pre-treated SMP-10 samples pyrolyzed at 1000°C for 30 min.

notes: Study investigates low-temperature pre-gelation thermal treatment effects on two commercial PCPs: StarPCS SMP-10 (SiC precursor, allylhydridopolycarbosilane, Starfire Systems) and Ceraset PSZ-20 (Si3N4/SiCN precursor, polysilazane, Clariant). Treatments conducted in vacuum oven at 15 kPa, open aluminum dish, SSA 1.77 cm-1. Pre-treatment temperatures: 85°C (SMP-10), 77°C (PSZ-20) to remain below gel point. Surface gelation observed above ~90°C for SMP-10 and at higher temperatures for PSZ-20. Three concurrent mechanisms identified during pre-treatment: volatilization of small oligomers, chain scission, and polymerization. Cure enthalpy decreases by ~13% for SMP-10 and ~18% for PSZ-20 after 8h treatments. Cure peak maximum shifts ~10°C lower for both polymers after pre-treatment. DSC performed at 5°C/min in nitrogen (50 mL/min), RT to 500°C. Fiber spinning feasibility investigated via sealed syringe treatments. Viscosity evolution from Newtonian to shear-thinning behavior observed with increased pre-treatment. PSZ-20 shows ~20-fold viscosity increase at 7h/77°C vs ~5-fold for SMP-10 at 7h/85°C. GPC note: actual MW values likely larger than reported due to polystyrene standard calibration.
source: Apostolov et al. - 2020 - Effects of low-temperature treatment on the properties of commercial preceramic polymers

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-H and B-N bonds mentioned in BN precursor context; cross-linking between N-H and B-H couples forming hydrogen gas

functional_groups.other: N(H)CH3 pendant groups mentioned in poly(B-(methylamino)borazine); boron-containing pendant groups added to hydridopolysilazane

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Branching noted to increase ceramic yield; boron carbide green fibers pyrolyzed at 1000-1300 C; SiCO fibers pyrolyzed at 1000 C in air and Ar; borane-modified hydridopolysilazane exhibited greater mass loss during heating

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal crosslinking noted generally; cross-linking between N-H and B-H in BN precursors occurs at low temperatures; oxidative stabilization mentioned for SiCO fibers

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Various molecular weights mentioned contextually: PND = 32 kDa, PCmS = 3500 Da, cage-structured polysilazanes up to 800 g/mol, PVP Mw = 360,000 g/mol

backbone_architecture.description: Review discusses linear, star-branched, and cage-structured polymer architectures; branching increases molecular weight, viscosity, ceramic yield, and amorphous character; cage-structured polysilazanes with Mw up to 800 g/mol also discussed

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC, SiCN, SiBCN, Si3N4, SiOC, BN, TiO2, Al2O3, ZnO, ZrC
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Boron-containing SiCN crystallizes at ~1700 C; carbon hinders crystallization of SiO2 and Si3N4 up to 1500 C; amorphous matrix favored for high-temperature applications; non-oxide fibers can be polycrystalline or amorphous

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Electrospun fibers can withstand substantially greater stress than blow-spun fibers; fiber bundles from blow spinning impact rigidity and elasticity; non-oxide fibers have better mechanical strength and modulus than traditional oxide fibers

notes: This is a review paper covering preceramic polymer fiber fabrication methods (electrospinning, blow spinning, melt spinning, wet/dry spinning, sol-gel) and applications. No single polymer system is characterized in detail. Key polymer types discussed include polysilanes, polycarbosilanes, polysilazanes, polycarbosilazanes, polyborosilazanes, hydridopolysilazane, polyureasilazane (PUS), poly(carbomethylsilane) (PCmS), poly(norbornenlyldecaborane) (PND), poly(B-(methylamino)borazine), and blends with PAN, PMMA, PS. Electrospun fiber diameters: 10-800 nm; blow-spun fiber diameters: 80-1000 nm. Electrospun mean pore size ~5 µm, porosity ~70%; blow-spun mean pore size 6-18 µm, porosity ~97%. SiCO fibers average diameter 165 nm from PUS/PAN blend. YBCO ceramic fiber diameter 360 nm from blow spinning.
source: Approaches to Preceramic Polymer Fiber Fabrication and On-Demand Applications

bonding_structure.other_bonds: SiOxC4-x building units (x=0 to 4); sp3-hybridized carbidic carbon in oxycarbide network; sp2-hybridized segregated 'free carbon'; Si-O-Si bonds broken by Ca and Mg modifiers

functional_groups.other: gamma-aminopropyl trimethoxy silane (APS) grafting used for surface modification; MPTMS functionalization reported

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Polymer-derived SiOC remains amorphous up to 1300 C. Pyrolysis temperatures reported range from 800 C (argon) to 1400 C depending on study. Gas evolution occurs during polymer-to-ceramic conversion.

backbone_architecture.description: SiOC network composed of SiOxC4-x building units with nano-scale 'free carbon' distributed within the matrix; nano-domain structure with carbon-rich and oxygen-rich regions showing mass fractal nature; can be fabricated as powders, monoliths, thin films/coatings, or fibers

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOC up to 1300 C; contains 'free carbon' (segregated graphitic carbon); SiOxC4-x units cluster into carbon-rich and oxygen-rich regions; metal silicates, metal silicides or metallic secondary phases can form in situ in modified SiOC nanocomposites

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: High-temperature creep resistance noted; mechanical properties of SiOC films tunable via carbon content and annealing temperature (RF magnetron sputtering)

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Crystalline hydroxyapatite/apatite observed on surface of Ca/Mg-modified SiOC after SBF immersion (3 days); not a phase of the SiOC itself

notes: This is a review paper focused on biomedical applications of silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) derived from polysiloxane and alkoxysilane precursors via the polymer-derived ceramic (PDC) method. Specific polymer precursors mentioned include polymethylsiloxane, polysilsesquioxane, polymethylsilsesquioxane, vinyl-containing polysiloxane, PDMS (vinyl-terminated), and polysiloxane-divinylbenzene. Pyrolysis temperatures range from 800 C to 1400 C in argon or nitrogen. Electrical conductivity of SiOC ranges up to 10 S/m (at 1400 C pyrolysis) depending on free carbon content. SiOC nanowire composition reported as Si1O1.42C0.37 (CVD-derived). Specific surface areas reported: ~20 m2/g for polysilsesquioxane/vinyl-containing polysiloxane-derived powder, ~450 m2/g for sol-gel mesoporous powder. Ag nanoparticles (5-50 nm) incorporated for antibacterial properties. Ca, Mg, Zn, Sr, B ions incorporated for bioactivity. No single primary polymer system is described; data extracted represent ranges across multiple cited studies.
source: Arango-Ospina_2020_Silicon oxycarbide based materials for biomedical applications

polymer_name: SiAlCHO (siloxane-alumina hybrid MLD film from V4D4/TMA)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Al present; exact atomic percentages not reported in provided text. Si/Al ratio ~1:1 for 150°C deposition and ~1:2 for 200°C deposition.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Al-O bonds present from TMA incorporation; sp2 carbon (graphene-like) forms upon annealing; sp3 carbon from methyl groups prior to annealing

functional_groups.other: Cyclosiloxane ring structure from V4D4 precursor (2,4,6,8-tetramethyl-2,4,6,8-tetravinylcyclotetrasiloxane)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: In situ TEM annealing performed stepwise from 200 to 1200°C with ~15 min/100°C ramp and ~5 min hold at each temperature. Surface roughening from 300-700°C; smoothening above 700°C; graphene shell formation observed at 800°C. Film grown at 150°C shrank from 7 to 5 nm (29% shrinkage) after annealing at 900°C. Film grown at 200°C shrank from 15 to 12 nm (20% shrinkage) after annealing at 1200°C. No crystallization or phase separation observed up to 1200°C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

backbone_architecture.description: Derived from ring-opening MLD process using cyclosiloxane (V4D4) and TMA; the ring-opening reaction forms a hybrid organic-inorganic siloxane-alumina network thin film

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Quaternary silicoaluminum oxycarbide (SiAlCO); uniform element distribution without phase separation up to 1200°C confirmed by EDX. Free carbon forms as graphene-like layers (up to 4 layers for 150°C-grown film; 1-2 layers for 200°C-grown film) on surface upon e-beam-assisted annealing. Graphene interplanar distance ~0.34 nm.

notes: Preceramic polymer deposited as ultrathin film (<15 nm) by molecular layer deposition (MLD) using V4D4 and TMA precursors at 150°C or 200°C. MLD cycle timing: 6/22/2/22 s (V4D4 dose/purge/TMA dose/purge). Carrier gas: ultrahigh purity N2 at 50 sccm, reactor pressure ~1 Torr. V4D4 heated to 90°C; TMA at room temperature. Films designated SiAlCHO convert to SiAlCO PDC upon pyrolysis. E-beam exposure during in situ TEM annealing induces knock-on damage (H emission) and promotes graphene shell formation at lower temperatures (800°C) than conventionally reported (>1200°C). Carbon content and number of graphene layers controllable via MLD deposition temperature. Raman D band ~1340-1345 cm-1, G band ~1600 cm-1, 2D band ~2680 cm-1, D+G band ~2934 cm-1 observed. ZrO2 nanoparticles used as substrates for TEM studies.
source: Ashurbekova_2023_In Situ Investigation of Thermally Induced Surface Graphenization of PDC Coatings from MLD Deposited Si-based Thin Films

polymer_name: click-derived metallocene preceramic polymers (Ti-, Zr-, Hf-, and TiZrHf-based); synthesized via copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne click polymerization of 1,4-diethynylbenzene and metallocene diazides

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ti, Zr, Hf present as metallocene centers; triazole units from click reaction; no quantitative atomic percentages provided

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Triazole linkages from azide-alkyne click reaction; metal-cyclopentadienyl bonds from metallocene units (Ti, Zr, Hf); aromatic C-C bonds from 1,4-diethynylbenzene monomer; no Si-containing bonds present

functional_groups.other: Azide groups on metallocene monomers; alkyne groups on 1,4-diethynylbenzene; triazole units formed upon click polymerization; cyclopentadienyl rings from metallocenes

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis performed at 800, 1100, and 1500 degrees C. At 800 degrees C, metal oxide phases (rutile TiO2, tetragonal ZrO2, monoclinic HfO2) form with segregated amorphous/graphitic carbon. At 1100 degrees C, mixtures of metal oxide and metal carbide phases present. At 1500 degrees C, carbothermal reduction is complete and TiC, ZrC, and HfC form as dominant phases. No TGA mass loss data reported.

backbone_architecture.description: Insoluble polymer network formed by copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne click polymerization of bisalkynyl benzene (1,4-diethynylbenzene) and azide-functionalized metallocenes (Ti, Zr, Hf or combinations). Polymers are insoluble in conventional solvents due to limited conformational freedom and lack of hydrocarbon side chains. Rigid phenyl ring monomer contributes to insolubility.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: TiC, ZrC, HfC (transition metal carbides); intermediate phases include TiO2 (rutile), ZrO2 (tetragonal), HfO2 (monoclinic/cubic); excess graphitic carbon present; mixed TiZrHf system forms (Hf,Zr)C solid solution with TiC as secondary phase
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 800 degrees C: metal oxides and amorphous/graphitic carbon. At 1100 degrees C: mixed oxide/carbide with graphitic carbon (Ti system: 53% carbon by RMC; at 1500 degrees C: 27% carbon). At 1500 degrees C: predominant cubic TMC phases via carbothermal reduction. EDS shows compositional heterogeneity and phase separation of excess carbon. ZrC nanoparticles randomly distributed in carbon matrix. Mixed TiZrHf system: Hf and Zr homogeneously dispersed forming (Hf,Zr)C solid solution; TiC appears as secondary phase.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to crystalline depending on pyrolysis temperature
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: 800 degrees C: rutile TiO2, tetragonal ZrO2, monoclinic HfO2; 1100 degrees C: TiO2 + TiC mixture, tetragonal ZrO2, monoclinic HfO2; 1500 degrees C: cubic TiC, cubic ZrC, cubic HfC (with minor residual monoclinic HfO2); mixed system at 1500 degrees C: (Hf,Zr)C solid solution + TiC secondary phase

notes: This paper focuses on non-silicon metallocene-based preceramic polymers (no Si in backbone) derived from Ti, Zr, and Hf metallocenes via copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne click chemistry. These are not conventional polysilazane/polycarbosilane/polysiloxane PCPs. Characterization relied heavily on synchrotron HE-XRD, atomic PDF analysis, RMC simulations, XAS (Ti K-edge and Zr L3-edge EXAFS/XANES), Raman spectroscopy, and HAADF-STEM/EDS. RMC modeling at 1100 degrees C showed Ti system: 53% carbon, dropping to 27% at 1500 degrees C. Local coordination numbers from RMC: Ti-O CN approaches 6 (rutile, octahedral); TiC first shell CN ~5.8-5.9, second shell ~11.6-11.8 (ideal 6 and 12); Zr-C CN = 5.5 at 1500 degrees C (bulk=6); Hf-O CN ~7-7.8 depending on polymorph. Titanocene diazide noted as moderately air sensitive, leading to oxide impurities. Polymers are insoluble powders processed via SPS-compatible methods. Multi-metallic TiZrHf PCP also synthesized and characterized.
source: Atomic-scale structure elucidation of refractory metal carbides derived from metallocene-based preceramics

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-vinyl (vinylmethoxysiloxane component); thiol (mercaptopropyl) groups present for thiol-ene photopolymerization

functional_groups.other: thiol/mercaptopropyl groups; methoxy groups (vinylmethoxysiloxane); free radical photoinitiator Irgacure 819 at 0.25 wt%; free radical scavenger inhibitor at 0.2 wt%

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Cooling to room temperature at 3 C/min. Linear shrinkage of approximately 30% upon pyrolysis. Most of the preceramic polymer transforms into SiOC, consistent with low shrinkage compared to glassy carbon (up to 90% shrinkage).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV/two-photon polymerization (free radical, thiol-ene mechanism) at 780 nm center wavelength, ~100 fs pulse width, 80 MHz repetition rate

backbone_architecture.description: Siloxane-based resin crosslinked via two-photon polymerization; (mercaptopropyl)methylsiloxane and vinylmethoxysiloxane mixed at 1:1 molar ratio of thiol/vinyl groups, forming a 3D crosslinked network upon photopolymerization

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Fully amorphous SiOC with no detectable porosity by TEM. EDS composition of pyrolyzed ceramic: 20.2 atom% Si, 33.5 atom% C, 44.8 atom% O, 1.6 atom% S. Structure approximated as continuous random network of tetrahedral SiO4 units with some O replaced by C, analogous to silica glass.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Yield strength 5.0 +/- 0.3 GPa; fracture strength 6.9 +/- 0.3 GPa; Young's modulus 66 +/- 2 GPa; plastic strains typically 7-15%, up to 25% failure strain; Poisson's ratio 0.21; strength ~E/10 (theoretical limit); nanolattice effective stiffness 1-17 GPa and strength 40-860 MPa at 9-40% relative density

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases detected; selected area diffraction pattern confirms fully amorphous structure

notes: Resin formulated by mixing (mercaptopropyl)methylsiloxane (Gelest) and vinylmethoxysiloxane (Gelest) at 1:1 molar ratio of thiol/vinyl groups. TPP-DLW performed with Nanoscribe Photonic Professional GT, 63x 1.4 NA oil objective, 780 nm center wavelength laser, ~100 fs pulse width, 80 MHz repetition rate, 50 mW average power, 5000 um/s writing speed, 0.1 um hatching distance, 0.2 um slicing distance. Samples developed in toluene 40 min then isopropanol baths, dried by critical point drying. Feature sizes down to ~200 nm achievable. Ceramic EDS composition reported for pyrolyzed material (not preceramic polymer): Si 20.2 at%, C 33.5 at%, O 44.8 at%, S 1.6 at%. Deformation mechanism attributed to volume-conserving shear flow (dominant) with minor densification contribution, consistent with silica glass behavior. Ductility and ultrahigh strength demonstrated for pillar diameters 1-20 um with typical property variability of +/- 3%.
source: Bauer_2019_Additive Manufacturing of Ductile, Ultrastrong Polymer-Derived Nanoceramics

polymer_name: MK, H44, H62C (silicones from Wacker Chemie AG); PSZ20 (KiON Defence Technologies); NN120-20 (Clariant AG)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-based backbone containing C, O, N, B and H atoms described generically; methyl and phenyl groups attached to Si atoms mentioned

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups attached to Si atoms mentioned; hydroxyl (-OH) side groups involved in condensation reactions with metal alkoxides

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: nitrogen or argon (inert); air for silicate production
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: MK silicone polymer has a ceramic yield of ~84% converted into silica when fired in air. Pyrolysis typically above 800 degrees C. Amorphous SiCO and SiCN residues start decomposing via carbothermal reactions above ~1250 degrees C. Polysilazanes dried/cured at 350 degrees C for 1 h under flowing N2.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (curing at 350 degrees C for 1 h under N2 for polysilazanes); chemical (metal alkoxide condensation with -OH side groups)

backbone_architecture.description: Organo-silicon compounds based on a backbone of Si atoms containing also C, O, N, B and H atoms. Silicones have a -Si-O- backbone. Polysilazanes have Si-N backbone. Polycarbosilazane (ABSE) also referenced.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCO (silicon oxycarbide), SiCN (silicon carbonitride), SiAlOC, SiMOC, mullite, SiAlON, silicates
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Silicones fired in non-oxidative atmosphere yield amorphous SiCO with nano-sized SiC domains and free carbon clusters. Polysilazanes yield SiCN with N- and C-rich nano-areas at low temperature and Si3N4/SiC nano-regions at high temperature. Above 1300 degrees C SiAlOC yields nano-crystalline mullite and SiC. Hafnia-rich phase separates as nano-droplets at 1100 degrees C; tetragonal hafnia crystals (~5 nm) at 1300 degrees C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fracture toughness KC ~6.5 MPa·m^0.5 for ZrO2-toughened mullite composites. Addition of 1-2 wt% MWCNTs increases fracture toughness via pull-out and bridging. Graphene nano-platelets increase strength and microhardness of SiC composites. Young modulus, Poisson's ratio, CTE and bulk density unaffected by up to 2 wt% MWCNTs.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous at low pyrolysis temperatures; partially crystalline at higher temperatures
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC, Si3N4, mullite (3Al2O3·2SiO2), tetragonal hafnia, zircon (ZrSiO4), hafnon (HfSiO4), Fe3Si, Fe5Si3, beta-SiC, graphitic carbon

notes: This is a review paper covering multiple preceramic polymer systems (polysiloxanes/silicones MK, H44, H62C; polysilazanes PSZ20, NN120-20; polycarbosilanes/polycarbosilazane ABSE) and their modification with nano-sized active fillers (gamma-Al2O3, Y2O3, ZrO2, TiO2, CaCO3, MgO, ZnO, etc.) or chemical additives (metal alkoxides). Ceramic yield of 84% applies specifically to MK silicone polymer converting to silica in air. Grain size <300 nm noted for mullite monoliths. Porosity typically below 15 vol% for crack-free monoliths per Greil method. Pyrolysis temperatures above ~800 degrees C stated generally; carbothermal decomposition above ~1250 degrees C. Composite powder suspensions have solid content 20-30 wt%. Cold uniaxial pressing at 20-40 MPa; warm pressing at 180 degrees C, 20 MPa. Density of polymers ~0.8-1.2 g/cm3; amorphous Si-based ceramics ~2.2 g/cm3. Crystallite size of 5 nm refers specifically to tetragonal hafnia in SiHfOC at 1300 degrees C.
source: Bernardo et al. - 2014 - Advanced Ceramics from Preceramic Polymers Modified at the Nano-Scale A Review

bonding_structure.other_bonds: SiOC oxycarbide phase described; amorphous silica with bridging oxygens substituted by carbon atoms connecting four silicon atoms; some SiC and carbon nano-sized clusters also present

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Total ceramic yield approximately 84%; SiO2 yield approximately 64%. Pyrolysis temperatures ranged from 1000 to 1200 C; midpoint used. Ceramic residue composition estimated at 31.6% Si, 48.1% O, 20.2% C (atomic). SiOC residue contains amorphous silica, SiC, and carbon nano-clusters whose amount varies with pyrolysis temperature.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

backbone_architecture.description: Polymethylsiloxane commercial resin available in powder form; yields SiOC ceramic residue upon pyrolysis in inert atmosphere

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous silica with some bridging oxygens substituted by carbon (silicon-oxycarbide phase); some SiC and carbon nano-sized clusters also present. Upon reaction with CaO fillers, crystalline phases including wollastonite (alpha and beta CaSiO3), C2S, C3S, C3S2, HAp, TCP are formed depending on filler and temperature.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Microcellular foam compressive strength: 3.9 +/- 0.8 MPa (CaO nano-powder system); 0.7 +/- 0.2 MPa (Ca-acetate system). Foam density approximately 0.4 g/cm3, porosity approximately 85 vol%.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiOC amorphous matrix; upon reaction with CaO fillers: beta-wollastonite (beta-CaSiO3), alpha-wollastonite (alpha-CaSiO3), C2S (dicalcium silicate), C3S (tricalcium silicate), C3S2 (rankinite), HAp (hydroxylapatite), TCP (tricalcium phosphate)

notes: The paper focuses on using MK polymethylsiloxane (polysiloxane) as a preceramic polymer with CaO-bearing active fillers (CaCO3 micro-powders, Ca-acetate solution, CaO nano-particles at 170 nm) to produce wollastonite-based bioceramics. Elemental composition values (Si 31.6%, O 48.1%, C 20.2%) refer to the SiOC ceramic residue after pyrolysis, not the precursor polymer itself. Pyrolysis temperature ranged 1000-1200 C; midpoint 1100 C used in pyrolysis_temp_C field. Hold time was 1 h (60 min). Foams produced with additional PMMA sacrificial microbeads (100 micron), warm-pressed at 170 C, pre-treated at 300 C in air, then fired at 1200 C in nitrogen at 2 C/min. Sample porosity: ~10 vol% for CaCO3 and CaO nano-powder systems, ~20 vol% for Ca-acetate system.
source: Bernardo_2009_Development of multiphase bioceramics from a filler-containing preceramic polymer

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental analyses reported as wt% and mole ratios for multiple polymer/ceramic samples. ONMS polymer (run 1): C 23.1, H 8.8, N 26.0, Si 41.9, O 0.5 wt%. PNMS polymer (run 5): C 21.6, H 8.0, N 25.3, Si 44.9, O 0.5 wt%. Phenyl-substituted polysilazane (run 1 BP): C 60.6, H 5.8, N 9.67, Si 22.9, O 0.5 wt%. Hexyl-substituted polysilazane (run 6 BP): C 56.1, H 11.5, N 9.11, Si 21.2, O 0.5 wt%.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-phenyl and Si-hexyl (alkyl) substituents present in respective polymer variants. Monomeric unit -[H2SiNCH3]- described as polymer prototype.

functional_groups.other: Phenyl groups (in PPS), hexyl groups (in poly(hexylsilazane)), N-methyl groups (in ONMS and PNMS)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed under flowing nitrogen, ~30mg samples in quartz baskets, 300 measurements averaged every 4 min. Ceramic yields vary by polymer type and pyrolysis temperature: phenyl-substituted at 800C yields 50-69 wt%, hexyl-substituted at 800C yields 24-36 wt%. ONMS at 800C yields 48-50 wt%, PNMS at 800C yields 61 wt%. Secondary heating to 1600C performed in static nitrogen at ~100 kPa (room temp) rising to ~700 kPa at 1600C at ~10 C/min.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (pyrolysis/thermolysis); catalytic dehydrocoupling used for polymerization

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Vapour-phase osmometry (VPO), size exclusion chromatography (SEC). ONMS starting material: Mn=1100, Mw=4000, Mz=13000 daltons. After catalytic treatment ONMS: Mn=2300, Mw=23600, Mz=128000 daltons. Phenylsilazane polymers: Mn=800-1600 daltons. Hexylsilazane polymers: Mn=850-2210 daltons.

backbone_architecture.description: Polymers synthesized by ruthenium-catalysed dehydrocoupling of Si-H with N-H bonds. Products include linear and cyclo-oligomers. Structure described as slightly branched or containing cages or rings. Monomeric unit -[H2SiNCH3]- based. Transition metal catalysts also promote ring-opening polymerization with Si-N bond metathesis.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous at 800C; crystalline phases identified at 1600C
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis targets Si3N4 ceramic. Si-CH3 groups result in SiC formation alongside Si3N4. Amorphous ceramic products at 800C are crystallized at 1600C. Powder XRD used for phase identification. Text references SiC and Si3N4 as principal target/observed phases.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Rheometry used for polymer characterization. ONMS viscosity 5P before catalytic treatment, 98P after. Tenacity discussed qualitatively in context of fibre spinning.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Powder XRD performed for phase identification at 1600C products; specific phases (Si3N4, SiC) referenced but not explicitly listed per sample in extracted text

notes: Paper covers multiple polysilazane variants: phenylsilazane-NH3 products (runs 1-5), hexylsilazane-NH3 products (runs 6-10), ONMS (oligo(N-methylsilazane)) and PNMS (poly(N-methylsilazane)). Synthesis via Ru3(CO)12 catalysed dehydrocoupling under ammonia pressure (80-90 psi) at 60-90C. Pyrolytic volatile products identified by GC-MS, Knudsen cell MS, Py/FIMS, and TPR-MS. Volatile decomposition products include silazane oligomers (70-450C range), CH4 (major above 450C), C2H4, C2H6, C3 hydrocarbons, CH3CN, and methyleneimine. Oxygen contamination generally below 1 wt% in most materials. Molecular weights of polysilazanes rarely exceed 3000 daltons per authors' note on field conventions. Multiple ceramic yield values reported per polymer depending on pyrolysis temperature; no single value representative of all samples.
source: Blum_1989_Preceramic polymer pyrolysis-polysilazane

elemental_composition.other_elements: Al content measured via ICP-OES; SiAlCN1 and SiAlCN2 contain Al at levels reported in Table 1 (approximate Al wt% values: 0.067-0.094 for SiAlCN1 and SiAlCN2 at 1000C based on table data). Ceramic compositions include free C, SiC, Si3N4, SiO2 phases. SiAlCN2 free C vol% = 28.8 vol%.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Al-N bonds formed upon reaction with TDMAA (Al[N(CH3)2]3); Si-N-Al bonds; vinyl (C=C) groups present; Al-N stretching observed at ~920-940 cm-1 in FTIR; Si-N-Si at 889 cm-1; Si-N-H at 1165 cm-1

functional_groups.other: Dimethylamido groups from TDMAA (Al[N(CH3)2]3); Al-N functional groups introduced upon chemical modification

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramization considered complete at ~800C. Unmodified Durazane 1800 ceramic yield ~83%; Al1-Durazane 1800 intermediate; Al2-Durazane 1800 highest yield ~90%. TGA performed on crosslinked powders (pre-crosslinked at 250C). Evolved gases include CH4, ethane, ethene, H2, amine fragments, NH3, H2O, CO2. Exothermic peak beginning ~75C attributed to hydrosilylation. Heating rate of 5 C/min used for TGA; 300 C/h (=5 C/min) used for pyrolysis of monoliths. Note: range of ceramic yields 83-90%; midpoint ~86.5%.

crosslink_density.value: Qualitative; higher TDMAA content leads to greater crosslinking degree. Al2-Durazane 1800 shows more pronounced reduction in Si-H/N-H/C=C bands after crosslinking at 250C.
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (250C, 3h) combined with chemical modification by aluminum amido complex (TDMAA)

backbone_architecture.description: Poly(organo)silazane backbone (Durazane 1800) chemically modified with tris(dimethylamido)aluminum (TDMAA) to incorporate Al into the Si-N backbone via Si-N-Al linkages. Two modification ratios used: Durazane 1800:TDMAA = 10.8:1 (Al1) and 5.4:2 (Al2). Resulting precursors are viscous liquids, yellow to orange in color, and become crosslinked solid network upon thermal treatment.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiAlCN (predominantly amorphous); minor beta-SiC nanocrystallites in SiAlCN2 at 1000C; beta-SiC, AlN, beta-Si3N4 at higher temperatures
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000C: SiCN and SiAlCN1 mainly amorphous; SiAlCN2 shows minor nanocrystalline beta-SiC. At 1200C: SiCN and SiAlCN2 X-ray amorphous; SiAlCN1 shows broad beta-SiC reflections. At 1400C: SiCN retains amorphous structure; beta-SiC intensifies in SiAlCN1 and emerges in SiAlCN2. At 1500C: beta-SiC decreases in SiCN and SiAlCN1; AlN and beta-Si3N4 appear. Free carbon present as disordered/segregated phase up to 1400C; substantially reduced at 1500C. SiAlCN2 retains segregated carbon at 1500C due to suppression of Si3N4-carbon reaction by higher Al content.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Reduced elastic modulus measured by nanoindentation (Berkovich tip, max load 3000-3500 mN, avg penetration depth 3000 nm). SiCN: hardness 13.6 ± 5.7 GPa, reduced modulus 163 ± 22 GPa. SiAlCN1: hardness 15.4 ± 3.2 GPa, reduced modulus 157 ± 17 GPa. SiAlCN2: hardness 14.5 ± 4.8 GPa, reduced modulus 156 ± 18 GPa. Young's modulus calculated assuming Poisson's ratio of 0.18. Hardness and modulus remain nearly unchanged upon Al incorporation.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (nanosized), AlN, beta-Si3N4 at elevated annealing temperatures (1200-1500C); predominantly amorphous at 1000C pyrolysis temperature

notes: Study reports for the first time on thermal and mechanical properties of dense amorphous Si-Al-C-N ceramics. Thermal conductivity as low as 0.6 W/m/K for high-Al content SiAlCN2. Thermal diffusivity measured by LFA (457 MicroFlash, Netzsch) from RT to 900C under argon; Cp by DSC. Monoliths fabricated by uniaxial pressing (70 MPa, 10 min) + cold isostatic pressing (250 MPa, 5 min) + pressureless pyrolysis at 1000C/4h/argon. Solid-to-liquid volume ratio of 3:1 used for green body fabrication. Open porosity: SiCN 22.26 vol%, SiAlCN1 4.51 vol%, SiAlCN2 2.32 vol%. Bulk density: SiCN 1.763 g/cm3, SiAlCN1 2.043 g/cm3, SiAlCN2 2.123 g/cm3. Skeletal density: SiCN 2.268 g/cm3, SiAlCN1 2.139 g/cm3, SiAlCN2 2.174 g/cm3. Annealing performed under nitrogen at 1200, 1400, and 1500C for 4h each. FTIR absorption bands: N-H (3376 cm-1), C-H (2953 cm-1), Si-H (2119 cm-1), C=C (1592 cm-1), Si-CH3 (1252 cm-1), Si-N-H (1165 cm-1), Si-N-Si (889 cm-1), Si-C (751 cm-1). Al-N band at ~920-940 cm-1. Raman D band ~1360 cm-1, G band ~1580 cm-1. Free C content: SiAlCN2 28.8 vol%. Polymer synthesis under Schlenk/argon atmosphere in anhydrous toluene.
source: Boroojerdi et al. - 2026 - Synthesis and thermal properties of dense Si─Al─C─N-based polymer-derived ceramics

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH=CH (vinyl bridge from hydrosilylation of alkyne, trans isomer confirmed by J=19.3 Hz); SiC4 sites identified by 29Si NMR at 18 ppm; phenyl groups bonded to Si from diphenylsilane monomer

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups (from diphenylsilane); terminal alkyne groups (from 1,4-diethynylbenzene, consumed during polymerization); aromatic backbone (1,4-diethynylbenzene-derived phenylene units)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Four zones observed: (i) below 180°C residual toluene solvent release (endothermic, onset ~113°C); (ii) 180-400°C no significant mass loss, crosslinking likely occurs; (iii) 400-620°C second mass loss due to phenyl group release from diphenylsilane units; (iv) above 620°C thermally stable. Large exothermic DTA peak centered at 800°C indicating conversion from organic PCS to amorphous SiC. Endothermic peak at 1390°C attributed to reaction between Al2O3 crucible and SiC. Ceramic yield range 56-62 wt% for polymerization times of 5-24 h. TGA run at 5°C/min under argon 20 mL/min up to 1550°C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

molecular_weight.measurement_method: SEC with multiple angle light scattering detector (MALS/TREOS, Wyatt); dn/dc = 0.218

backbone_architecture.description: Linear polycarbosilane synthesized by Pt-catalyzed (Karstedt's catalyst) hydrosilylation of diphenylsilane with 1,4-diethynylbenzene. Backbone contains alternating phenylene and Si(Ph)2 units connected via trans -CH=CH- bridges (beta-E product). Polymer contains chains of several populations from oligomers to longer chains; higher Mw (~12200 g/mol) achievable with longer polymerization times.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: beta-SiC (cubic face-centered structure) crystallizes above 1200°C. Samples pyrolyzed below 1200°C are amorphous with free carbon present. Excess free carbon confirmed by elemental analysis and HR-TEM. Stacking faults and crystal twinning observed in SiC grains. C/SiC composite powder obtained.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Polymer solution viscosity: ~1 mPa·s at 20-100 g/L in toluene, ~2.5 mPa·s at 500 g/L; shear thinning behavior observed over 10-500 s-1 shear rate range

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (cubic, face-centered); turbostratic carbon (free carbon)

notes: Polymer synthesized from diphenylsilane and 1,4-diethynylbenzene via Karstedt's catalyst (Pt(0)) hydrosilylation in toluene at 75°C for 24h; isolated as orange powder in 93% yield. Trans (beta-E) selectivity confirmed by vicinal coupling constant J=19.3 Hz. 29Si NMR shows single peak at 18 ppm consistent with SiC4 environment, no Si-O bonds detected. Polymer soluble in acetone, THF, DMF, toluene. Grain size range 20-80 nm reported from TEM (midpoint ~50 nm used for grain_size_nm). Molecular weight evolves over days at ambient temperature due to residual Si-H recombination of oligomers. Pyrolysis temperatures studied: 800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600, 1800°C. Cooling rate 20°C/min.
source: Bouzat_2016_Preparation of C_SiC ceramics using a preceramic polycarbosilane synthesized via hydrosilylation

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O bonds appear in cured samples likely due to reaction with residual air during curing, as observed by EDS mapping showing Si-O islands within C-enriched phase

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA used to determine mass gain during thermal cure of uncured 3D printed BCP/PCS parts by heating to cure temperature at 10 °C/min and holding isothermally at 160 °C for 4 or 8 h in air. DSC used to observe onset of SMP-10 cross-linking at ~80 °C.

backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosilane preceramic polymer (SMP-10) blended with PMMA-b-PnBA-b-PMMA block copolymer (Kurarity LA4285, 25 wt% PMMA - 50 wt% PnBA - 25 wt% PMMA, Mw 64,000 g/mol, PDI 1.1912). PCP selectively associates with hydrophobic PnBA domains of the BCP. Worm-like micellular morphology in ink transitions to nano-fibrous morphology upon thermal curing.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramic nano-fibers and nanocoral (nanofoam) both identified as SiOC by EDS. Ceramic is amorphous SiOC. Oxygen incorporation attributed to reaction with residual air during curing. Nano-fibers aligned along print direction, embedded in a porous nanocoral matrix with a solid glassy shell on filament surface.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Average stress at failure 29.63 +/- 7.5 MPa; Young's modulus 5.39 +/- 1 GPa (single filament tensile testing). Individual filaments deflectable up to 40° without mechanical failure. Ceramic springs reversibly strained to 10% for over 10,000 cycles without >5% change in required force. Nano-fiber pull-out behavior observed (composite-like), average pull-out fiber length ~169 µm (n=50). Woodpile lattice recovered to 100% and 52% of original position under 20 g and 50 g loads respectively.

notes: Paper focuses on DIW additive manufacturing of SMP-10 polycarbosilane / PMMA-b-PnBA-b-PMMA block copolymer (BCP) ink blends dissolved in 1-butanol/acetone co-solvent. Ink ratio: 1.2 g SMP-10, 1.8 g BCP, 2 g 1-butanol, 1 g acetone. Nano-fiber formation occurs during thermal curing (not in ink reservoir), driven by microphase separation and filament geometric confinement (grapho-epitaxy). SAXS shows phase transition from lamellar to hexagonal packing during cure. Nano-fiber alignment is parallel to print direction. Preferred cure conditions: 1 °C/min ramp to 160 °C, held overnight. Pyrolysis: 1 °C/min to 800 °C, 1 h hold, flowing argon. Nano-fiber lengths ~300 µm; printed using 250 µm nozzles at 20 mm/s, 350 psi. BCP Mw = 64,000 g/mol, PDI = 1.1912. No UV crosslinking used (distinguishing this work from prior nanocoral study). Ceramic yield not reported. Oxygen contamination in SiOC limits high-temperature service; optimization ongoing.
source: Bowen et al. - 2025 - Nanofibrous ceramics via the additive manufacturing of self-assembling preceramic polymer and block

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-OR (alkoxy), Si-OH (silanol), Si-F mentioned in context of HF catalysis; Si-O-Si backbone formed via condensation

backbone_architecture.description: Acid-catalyzed hydrolysis with low H2O/Si ratios produces weakly branched polymeric networks (linear or chain-like, Mark-Houwink exponent a = 0.5-1.0); base-catalyzed hydrolysis with large H2O/Si ratios produces highly branched colloidal particles (a = 0.1-0.5, spherical or disk-shaped). Ladder polymers postulated for spinnable solutions. Fractal structures (mass fractal and surface fractal) described via SAXS. Cubic octamer cage oligomers also mentioned.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Sol-gel derived silica; monodisperse spherical amorphous SiO2 particles produced under Stober process conditions (R=7-25, ammonia catalyst). Fractal structures described: mass fractal (weakly branched, acid-catalyzed) and surface fractal (rough particles, base-catalyzed).

notes: This paper is a review of hydrolysis and condensation mechanisms of alkoxysilanes and organylalkoxysilanes in sol-gel processing, not a preceramic polymer pyrolysis study. The material discussed is TEOS and related organoalkoxysilanes forming SiO2-based sol-gel glasses/ceramics. No pyrolysis data, ceramic yield, or PDI values are reported. Gelation times reported for TEOS with 0.05 mol catalyst per mol TEOS in ethanol with 4 equivalents water: HF=12h, HCl=92h, HNO3=100h, H2SO4=106h, HOAc=72h, NH4OH=107h, no catalyst=1000h. Acid hydrolysis rate constants (k x 10^2, l/mol/s/[H+]) for tetraalkoxysilanes: C2H5=5.1, C4H9=1.9, C6H13=0.83, branched isooctyl=0.30. Mark-Houwink exponent a=0.5-1.0 for spinnable (linear/chain) solutions; a=0.1-0.5 for colloidal/branched systems. H2O/Si molar ratio (R) is a key processing variable ranging from ~1 to >25.
source: Brinker - 1988 - Hydrolysis and condensation of silicates Effects on structure

LBL-M total mass loss ~52.4%, CFBL-M total mass loss ~48.7%. LBL-Silica total mass loss ~45%, CFBL-Silica total mass loss ~46%. Silica/W total mass loss ~15.6%, Silica/D:W total mass loss ~17.1%. backbone_architecture.description: Lignin-silica organic-inorganic hybrid network formed via sol-gel process. Lignin (kraft lignin, aromatic phenolic macromolecule) activated by Mannich reaction with APTES and formaldehyde, then co-hydrolyzed with TEOS to form silica network. Lignin itself is a cross-linked natural phenolic polymer.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Lignin-SiO2 nanostructured composite; silica phase formed from TEOS hydrolysis; XPS confirms SiO2 phase (Si2p B at 103.3 eV, 67.9%) and aminopropyltriethoxysilane/siloxane phase (Si2p A at 102.3 eV, 32.1%)

notes: This paper does not describe a preceramic polymer system. It describes lignin/SiO2 hybrid composites formed by Mannich activation of kraft lignins (LignoBoost kraft lignin LBL and ceramic-membrane-fractionated kraft lignin CFBL) with APTES and formaldehyde, followed by sol-gel condensation with TEOS. The materials are organic-inorganic hybrids, not preceramic polymers intended for pyrolysis to ceramics. XPS data for CFBL-silica: N1s at 399.4 eV (54.4%, amine/amide/cyanides), 400.7 eV (29.7%, imide), 402.0 eV (15.8%, quaternary nitrogen); Si2p at 102.3 eV (32.1%) and 103.3 eV (67.9%, SiO2). LBL functional groups: phenolic OH total 3.99 mmol/g, aliphatic OH 1.73 mmol/g, total OH 5.72 mmol/g, COOH 0.41 mmol/g. CFBL functional groups: phenolic OH total 5.47 mmol/g, aliphatic OH 1.81 mmol/g, total OH 7.28 mmol/g, COOH 0.28 mmol/g. Most fields are null because this is not a preceramic polymer paper.

Soluble in moisture-free organic solvents including hydrocarbons, toluene, ethers, substituted ethers, acetones. Curing temperature of 230°C mentioned for Durazane 1500. Acid-catalyzed ring-opening at 160°C for 6-8 h produces waxy polysilazane. Multiple corrosion protection applications tabulated. Co-ammonolysis of dichloro-methylsilane, dichloromethyl-vinylsilane, and trichloro-methylsilane yields copolysilazanes with variable structures. notes: Study focuses on rheological investigation of crosslinking behavior of two commercial polysilazanes (Ceraset PURS and Ceraset HTT1800, Clariant GmbH) in inert (argon) and ambient (air) atmospheres using oscillatory rheometry. Crosslinking in air is faster than in inert atmosphere due to hydrolysis and polycondensation reactions confirmed by DSC and FTIR. The urea-containing derivative (Ceraset PURS) showed more pronounced moisture sensitivity. Gel points measured at 100, 120, and 140 C using CP and PP geometries. polymer_name: SPR-212, PHMS blend (PHMS + 40 wt% TPTS + 1 wt% DVD), TTCS (1,3,5,7-tetravinyl-1,3,5,7-tetramethylcyclotetrasiloxane + 1 wt% DCP)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA conducted to 1000 C at 10 C/min in 50 mL/min flowing argon. Significant mass loss up to ~800 C from volatile organics evolution. SPR-212 and PHMS blend show major mass loss near ~500 C; TTCS shows greatest mass loss at lower temperature (~425 C). Ceramization temperature trend: PHMS (~550 C) > SPR (~450 C) > TTCS (~425 C). Phase assemblage includes SiO2, SiC, and free carbon domains. Carbothermal reduction occurs at 1500 C. Phase compositions (mol%): SPR-1200: SiO2=30.69, SiC=36.63, C=32.67; TTCS-1200: SiO2=20, SiC=20, C=60; PHMS-1200: SiO2=28.30, SiC=32.07, C=39.62; SPR-1500: SiO2=26.73, SiC=44.55, C=28.71; TTCS-1500: SiO2=16.24, SiC=38.46, C=45.30; PHMS-1500: SiO2=26.60, SiC=30.27, C=43.12.

Enthalpies of formation from elements (kJ/mol): SPR-1200=-154.40±3.19, TTCS-1200=-116.35±3.48, PHMS-1200=-197.55±3.05, SPR-1500=-170.12±3.50, TTCS-1500=-167.29±3.35, PHMS-1500=-212.43±2.71. Enthalpies of formation from components (kJ/mol): SPR-1200=0.31±3.23, TTCS-1200=+6.16±3.51, PHMS-1200=-48.34±3.09, SPR-1500=-31.88±3.52, TTCS-1500=-64.80±3.38, PHMS-1500=-68.87±2.74. notes: Polymer was used to infiltrate pinewood-derived carbon (CB) templates via vacuum infiltration and pyrolyzed in flowing Ar to form hierarchically porous biomorphic C-SiOC ceramics. polymer_name: click-derived metallocene preceramic polymers (Ti-, Zr-, Hf-, and TiZrHf-based)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis performed at 800, 1100, and 1500 degrees C. At 800 degrees C, metal oxide phases (rutile TiO2, tetragonal ZrO2, monoclinic HfO2) form with amorphous carbon. At 1100 degrees C, mixed oxide and carbide phases present. At 1500 degrees C, carbothermal reduction converts metal oxides to respective metal carbides (TiC, ZrC, HfC). Carbon phase fraction decreases from ~53% at 1100 degrees C to ~27% at 1500 degrees C for Ti-based system per RMC modeling.

backbone_architecture.description: Polymers synthesized via copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne click polymerization of 1,4-diethynylbenzene (bisalkynyl benzene) and azide-functionalized metallocenes (Ti, Zr, and/or Hf metallocene diazides). Resulting polymers are insoluble in conventional solvents due to limited conformational freedom and lack of hydrocarbon side chains. Rigid phenyl ring backbone contributes to insolubility.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: TiC, ZrC, HfC (at 1500 degrees C); intermediate metal oxide phases (TiO2, ZrO2, HfO2) at lower temperatures; (Hf,Zr)C solid solution in multi-metal system
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 800 degrees C: rutile TiO2 (amorphous for Ti), tetragonal ZrO2, monoclinic HfO2 with segregated sp2 carbon. At 1100 degrees C: mixed oxide/carbide phases plus graphitic carbon. At 1500 degrees C: predominantly cubic TiC, cubic ZrC, cubic HfC with residual carbon. In TiZrHf multi-metal system, ZrC and HfC form a solid solution at 1500 degrees C while TiC phase separates. Excess carbon observed throughout as segregated phase. Dense and dispersed carbide nanoparticles distributed in carbon matrix observed by HAADF-STEM.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: As-synthesized polymers: not characterized by XRD. PDCs at 800 degrees C: rutile TiO2 (amorphous/nanocrystalline for Ti), tetragonal ZrO2, monoclinic and cubic HfO2. At 1100 degrees C: TiO2 + TiC mixture, tetragonal ZrO2, monoclinic HfO2. At 1500 degrees C: cubic TiC, cubic ZrC, cubic HfC; (Hf,Zr)C solid solution in multi-metal system

notes: Polymers are Si-free, transition-metal-based preceramic polymers. The polymer type is best described as metallocene-triazole polymers or organometallic click polymers rather than classical polycarbosilane; they are listed as PCS analogs in reference to prior literature (Bouzat et al.). Monomers: 1,4-diethynylbenzene and metallocene diazides (titanocene, zirconocene, hafnocene dichloride converted to diazides using tributylstannyl azide). Polymerization via Cu(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition. Polymers are insoluble powders, not solution-processable. A multi-metallic TiZrHf PCP was also synthesized using stoichiometric equivalents of all three metallocene monomers. Synchrotron HE-XRD, atomic PDF analysis, RMC simulations, Ti K-edge and Zr L3-edge XAS (XANES and EXAFS), Raman spectroscopy, and HAADF-STEM/EDS were used for characterization. Carbothermal reduction from metal oxide to metal carbide occurs between 1100 and 1500 degrees C. Titanocene diazide noted to be moderately air sensitive, contributing to oxide formation at low pyrolysis temperatures. RMC modeling of Ti system showed 53% carbon at 1100 degrees C and 27% at 1500 degrees C.

notes: This is a broad review article covering polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs) in general, not a study of a single preceramic polymer. Multiple polymer types and ceramic systems are discussed. Grain size of 2 nm is a midpoint estimate from the stated range of 1-3 nm for nanodomains in SiCN and SiCO. Pyrolysis temperature of 1300°C is the upper end of the stated synthesis range (1100-1300°C). notes: Paper describes a composite fabrication study using SMP-730 polycarbosilane blended with PDV-1625 (vinyl-terminated diphenylsiloxane-dimethylsiloxane copolymer) as plasticizer for carbon fiber CMC via PIP process. Ceramic yield values listed are for SMP-730 base resin alone (65%) and plasticized blends in air atmosphere. Shear thinning behavior observed for all resins; viscosity minimum at ~10 wt% plasticizer loading. Phase separation suspected at 20 wt% plasticizer. notes: Study focuses on polymer-metal-nanoparticle (PMN) systems where pyridyl-functionalized PCPs (PyHex877 from SMP-877 polycarbosilane, and PyMPS polysiloxane) are crosslinked to pyridyl-terminated SiO2 nanoparticles via ZrCl4 coordination. Dramatic 57% increase in char yield of PMN relative to summed char yields of individual components reported as synergistic effect. PyHex877 synthesized via two-step thiol-ene reaction using hexane-1,6-dithiol, 4-vinylpyridine and AIBN then reacted with SMP-877. SiO2 NPs functionalized with 4-(2-((3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl)thio)ethyl)pyridine. ZrCl4(THF)2 used as metal linker. Repeat unit MW of PyMPS is 239 g/mol with up to 23 pyridyl groups per average molar mass chain. XPS on SiC film: Si 2p shows 83% SiC and 17% SiO2 character. TEM shows guest ZrO2 particles 10-50 nm embedded in micron-sized SiO2 host particles after 1600C pyrolysis. Pyrolysis conducted in both tube furnace and graphite furnace with identical XRD results.

notes: This is a patent document describing polymer-derived ceramic (PDC) nanocomposites incorporating transition metal salts (specifically copper sulfide nanoparticles). The preceramic polymer PyMPS is synthesized via thiol-ene click chemistry and contains pyridine functional groups that act as a reducing agent and surface capping ligand. SAXS (IRENA, Unified Model, Guinier-Porod), Pair Distribution Function (PDF), FTIR, and NMR are used for characterization. Oleylamine (olam) and trioctylphosphine are used as co-ligands to control nanoparticle size and anisotropy. In-situ SAXS tracks temperature-dependent growth. Steric hindrance of the PCP controls nanostructure aspect ratio producing plate-like geometries. Applications mentioned include aerospace coatings, Li-ion battery electrodes, MEMS, and gas/high-temperature sensors. Quantitative compositional, thermal, and molecular weight data are not provided in the extracted text.

notes: This is a zirconium-based organometallic preceramic polymer (not a silicon-based preceramic polymer). Precursor synthesized from ZrCl4, phenol, acetylacetone, toluene, ethanol via formation of zirconium ethoxide intermediate followed by reflux with acetylacetone and phenol. Soluble in toluene, xylene, divinylbenzene. Air stable for long-term storage. Ceramic yield ~24% at 1200C. ZrC grain size 50-100 nm at 1500C (midpoint 75 nm; range 50-100 nm noted). Carbothermal reduction initiates at 1300C (much lower than thermodynamic prediction of 1653C due to intimate atomic-level mixing). At 1500C product contains zirconium oxycarbide and free carbon; at 1600C near-stoichiometric ZrC but with grain agglomeration. notes: This paper does not describe a preceramic polymer in the traditional sense. The precursor system uses a powder mixture of silicon powder, novolac phenolic resin (SP04 with hexamethylentetradiamine hardener), and biomorphous carbon fibres (pyrolyzed cellulose paper). The resin acts as a binder and carbon source. The process involves hot-pressing at 220 degrees C for 30 min at 5 MPa, pyrolysis at 900 degrees C in nitrogen for 2 h, sintering at 1500 degrees C for 2 h in vacuum (1.2e-2 Pa) at 300 K/h, and reactive chlorine extraction at 800-1200 degrees C to produce carbide-derived carbon (CDC). Skeletal density of SiC is 3.01 +/- 0.1 g/cm3. CDC heat conductivity 0.1-0.2 W/(m K) at RT to 700 degrees C. Raman D-band: 1317 cm-1 (FWHM 217 cm-1), G-band: 1581 cm-1 (FWHM 83 cm-1), ID/IG = 1.46.

notes: Study focuses on kinetics of polymer-to-ceramic transformation of two precursors: CERASET (polyureamethylvinylsilazane, SiCN precursor, Clariant Corp.) and TTCS (1,3,5,7-tetramethyl-1,3,5,7-tetravinylcyclotetrasiloxane, SiCO precursor, Geleset USA). Both precursors mixed with 1 wt% dicumyl peroxide and crosslinked at 653 K for 5 h in argon before pyrolysis. Four overlapping decomposition steps identified for each precursor by TG-MS and Fraser-Suzuki deconvolution. Activation energies for CERASET four steps: 154, 172, 255, 218 kJ/mol; pre-exponential factors: 1.04e8, 1.95e8, 1.05e12, 5.40e8 s-1. Processes 1, 3, 4 follow diffusion-like mechanisms; Process 2 follows random scission model. Step contributions to overall reaction: 28%, 8%, 43%, 21% respectively. Ceramic yield of CERASET notably higher than TTCS. SEM shows no significant microstructural differences between crosslinked precursor and pyrolysed residue at 1273 K. Atmosphere has strong influence: argon vs nitrogen yields different crystalline phases.

notes: This is a review paper (Materials 2021, 14, 614) covering multiple PDC systems and precursor types. No single polymer is characterized; data extracted reflects ranges across many referenced studies. Ceramic yield of 65% is specifically from a polysilazane + borane dimethylsulfide SiBCN coating system pyrolyzed to 1800 C. Porosity of 15% is from a ZrC-filled polycarbosilane SiC matrix composite. Hardness range 10-11 GPa and modulus 105-117 GPa are from a polysilylcarbodiimide-derived SiCN coating. Strength of 600 MPa refers to PIP SiC matrix composite. The review discusses polysilazane, polyborosilazane, polycarbosilane, polysiloxane, polyhydromethylsiloxane, polymethylsilsesquioxane, polysilylcarbodiimide, polyvinylsilazane, poly(methyl vinyl)silazane, polymethylsilane, and other precursor types across various applications.
source: High-Temperature Properties and Applications of Si-Based Polymer-Derived Ceramics- A Review

polymer_name: PBSZ (Polyborosilazane, Institute of Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yield of HEC/SiBCN-1 decreases from 27.25% to 21.63% with increasing pyrolysis temperature from 1200 to 1800 °C; linear shrinkage increases from 59.81% to 70.26%; ceramic yield for varying HEC content (pyrolyzed at 1400 °C) is 25%-31%. At 1400 °C: solid solutions of multi-metal carbides form via carbothermal reduction. At 1600 °C: HEC phase clearly observed with FCC structure. At 1800 °C: HEC intensities increase, β-SiC and B(C)N phases form. HEC diffraction peaks shift to lower 2θ with increasing temperature indicating expanding interplanar spacing as O replaced by C.

notes: Paper focuses on HEC/SiBCN composite porous ceramics rather than the pure PBSZ precursor alone. PBSZ is from Institute of Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Elemental composition (Si 6.3%, B nd, C 87.6%, N 5.1%, O 1%) is for carbon-rich SiBCN ceramics (with DVB) pyrolyzed at 1400 °C by EDS. Porosity range of porous HEC/SiBCN ceramics: 63.5%-79.1% (midpoint ~71.3%); density range 0.74-0.91 g/cm3. Ceramic yield range 21.63%-31% depending on conditions. HEC phase formation temperature ~1600 °C, lower than conventional powder sintering methods (>2000 °C). Thermal conductivity 0.054-0.089 W/(m·K) at room temperature. Solvothermal conditions: 150 °C, 20 h. Freeze-drying: frozen at -50 °C for 30 min, dried 48 h. Oxidation TGA: RT to 1400 °C at 10 °C/min in air.
source: In situ formation of high-entropy carbide phase in porous SiBCN ceramic for enhanced high-temperature stability

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis at 600-1000 C converts preceramic polymers into amorphous covalent ceramics. Polycarbosilanes pyrolyzed at 800-1000 C yield SiC-based materials; between 550-800 C, hydrogen and methane are evolved. Polysiloxanes yield SiOC glasses with evolution of hydrocarbons (mainly CH4) and hydrogen. Vinyl-substituted polysilazanes evolve ammonia up to 600 C via transamination; at 600-800 C, decrease in Si-H, Si-CH3, and N-H bonds with evolution of hydrogen and methane. High volumetric shrinkage up to 50 vol% reported.

Polysilylcarbodiimide gels are analogous to classical oxide gels with respect to structural and rheological properties.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous ceramics obtained upon pyrolysis at 1000-1400 C; subsequent annealing leads to polycrystalline materials. SiCN from polysilylcarbodiimide consists of amorphous carbon phase embedded in amorphous silicon nitride phase above 1000 C. SiC fibers from oxidative crosslinking show 10-12% oxygen; e-beam crosslinked SiC shows 0.2-0.3% oxygen. Ceramic compositions reported in table: Si1O1.1C0.73 (SiO2 43.10 mol%, SiC 34.98 mol%, C 21.92 mol%), Si1O0.72C2.10 (SiO2 14.73 mol%, SiC 25.97 mol%, C 59.30 mol%), Si1C2.80N1.20 (Si3N4 14.30 mol%, SiC 4.80 mol%, C 80.90 mol%).

notes: This is a review/book chapter covering the broad field of polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs) from silicon-based preceramic polymers including polysilanes, polycarbosilanes, polysiloxanes, polysilazanes, and polysilylcarbodiimides. No single specific polymer is characterized; data reflect general class-level properties. Enthalpy of formation data provided in table for SiOC and SiCN ceramics: Si1O1.1C0.73: dHf from elements = -242 +/- 3.6 kJ/mol, from binaries = -53.9 +/- 3.6 kJ/mol; Si1O0.72C2.10: dHf from elements = -149.9 +/- 4.4 kJ/mol, from binaries = -51.9 +/- 4.4 kJ/mol; Si1C2.80N1.20: dHf from elements = -50.6 +/- 6.4 kJ/mol, from binaries = -2.8 +/- 6.4 kJ/mol. Oxidation kinetics data also provided for CVD-Si3N4, CVD-SiC, SiCN fibers, and dense SiCN. Crosslinking temperature range: 100-400 C. Ceramization temperature range: 1000-1400 C. Preceramic polymer densities approximately 1 g/cm3; ceramic densities 2-3 g/cm3.
source: Ionescu - 2011 - Polymer‐Derived Ceramics

notes: This paper does not describe a preceramic polymer. It describes a biopolymer-metal oxide composite precursor (iota-carrageenan + chitin + WO3 nanoparticles) used for sustainable synthesis of porous tungsten carbide (WC) via carbothermal reduction reaction. The carbon source is renewable biopolymers, not a silicon-based preceramic polymer. All fields related to preceramic polymer chemistry (Si, N, polymer type, bonding, functional groups, crosslink density, molecular weight) are null because they are not applicable. BET surface area of synthesized WC: 67.03 m2/g. Total pore volume: 0.9 cm3/g. Pore size range: 3-120 nm, mostly mesopores (2-50 nm). Grain size increases from 17.5 nm at 960 C to 43.3 nm at 1450 C. WO3:C precursor ratio used was 1:6 by weight. Gel casting demonstrated with shrinkage of ~35-36% for WC shapes relative to original mold.
source: Islam_2017_A sustainable approach for tungsten carbide synthesis using renewable biopolymers

notes: This is a review paper focused on Si-N-C ternary phases. The specific polyorganosilazane discussed is poly(hydridomethyl)silazane yielding Si1.7N1.5C1.0 ceramic composition stable in air to 1600°C. Hydrogen content drops from 5% to 0.9 at.% after 50 h at 1300°C in N2. The paper also covers CVD and PVD synthesis routes and discusses the instability of C3N4. The alpha-Si3N4:C crystalline phase can incorporate ~6 at.% C with enhanced hardness and wear resistance. Hold time of 3000 min is derived from 50 h annealing mentioned in text.

At ~900-1000C mineralization is complete and equilibrium distribution of SiOxC4-x sites is reached.

backbone_architecture.description: Cross-linked polysiloxane networks based on mono-, di-, tri-, or tetrafunctional building units (e.g., MeSiO1.5 sesquioxane, Me2SiO siloxane, SiO2 units); also linear and cyclic oligomers formed as volatile byproducts during pyrolysis. Precursors include (MeSiO1.5)n, (HSiO1.5)n, [(Me2SiO)0.5(SiO2)0.5]n, (OMeSiSiMeO)n, [(C2H4)SiO]n, and polysiloxanes crosslinked by Si-Si or SiCH2CH2Si bridges.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At ~900-1000C, glasses described as mixture of amorphous silicon oxycarbide phase and excess carbon phase (polyaromatic carbon). Si atoms bonded to O and C only, forming distribution of tetrahedral SiOxC4-x sites (SiO4, SiO3C, SiO2C2, SiOC3, SiC4). At higher temperatures redistribution equilibria displaced by crystallization of SiC. Distribution of SiOxC4-x sites is random and controlled by O/Si ratio, not by precursor structure.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC crystallization occurs at temperatures above ~1000C displacing redistribution equilibria

notes: This paper is a review/discussion focused on redistribution reactions (exchange reactions) in the synthesis and pyrolysis of preceramic polymers, primarily polysiloxanes as precursors to SiOC ceramics, but also covering polysilazanes, polycarbosilanes, polyborazinylamines, and polysilylcarbodiimides. Key finding: at ~900C Si-O/Si-C redistributions reach equilibrium giving a random, entropically controlled distribution of SiOxC4-x sites determined solely by the O/Si ratio. Table II gives statistical distributions: at O/Si=1.2, SiO4=12.96%, SiO3C=34.56%, SiO2C2=34.56%, SiOC3=15.36%, SiC4=2.56%; at O/Si=1.8, SiO4=65.61%, SiO3C=29.16%, SiO2C2=4.86%, SiOC3=0.36%, SiC4=0.01%. EPR spectroscopy indicated paramagnetic SixO3-xSi sites in HSiO1.5 gels pyrolyzed under argon between 500-800C. Redistribution reactions account for loss of volatile organosilicon compounds reducing ceramic yield and modifying ceramic composition.
source: Journal of the American Ceramic Society - 2004 - Mutin - Role of Redistribution Reactions in the Polymer Route to Silicon

notes: This paper describes a non-silicon preceramic polymer system targeting ZrB2 ceramic rather than traditional Si-based ceramics. The polymer is a blend of a Zr-containing polymeric precursor [(C4H8O)Zr(acac)2]n and a B-containing borazine precursor (NHCH3)3B3N3H3. Grain size range given as 50-100 nm (midpoint 75 nm used). Ceramic yield theoretical value 30.1%, measured 31.9% (B/Zr=2). Formation mechanism proposed as liquid-phase reaction with homogeneous nucleation and crystal growth. FTIR analysis performed in nitrogen at 10C/min; pyrolysis heat treatment performed in argon at 2C/min. Softening point of Zr precursor: 170C.

notes: This paper is NOT about a preceramic polymer. It is an ab initio DFT computational study of the electronic structure and interatomic bonding in a 3864-atom periodic supercell model of an intergranular glassy film (IGF) in beta-Si3N4 structural ceramic. The model was relaxed using VASP (PAW/PBE-GGA, 500 eV cutoff, single k-point) and analyzed using the OLCAO method. The calculated band gap of the IGF model is 1.6 eV. The supercell dimensions of the relaxed model are a=23.141 A, b=23.149 A, c=82.614 A. The glassy IGF contains Si, O, and N with N/(N+O)=0.32. Over- and under-coordinated Si and N atoms were identified predominantly at interfacial transition layers. None of the fields for preceramic polymer characterization are applicable to this work.

Polymer descriptors are derived from simulation models rather than experimental characterization. PDMS model initial composition: Si2304C4608O2304H13824 (density 1.0 g/cm3); after 100 ns pyrolysis at 1400 K composition becomes Si1.0C1.0O1.0H2.1. Reaction mechanisms identified include methane abstraction and Kumada-like rearrangements transforming the siloxane backbone. Vibrational signatures identified: C-H stretch ~3100 cm-1, Si-CH3 ~800 cm-1, Si-O backbone ~1050 cm-1, graphitic D/G peaks 1350-1600 cm-1, interfacial C-Si bonds ~1100-1300 cm-1.

notes: This dissertation covers multiple preceramic polymer systems used for Direct Ink Writing (DIW). Chapter 2 uses Durazane 1800 (a polysilazane) with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) filler. Chapters 3 and 4 use a polycarbosilane designated SMP-10 as the primary binder/preceramic polymer in inks combined with ZrB2 powder and/or SiC chopped fibers or fumed Al2O3. The polycarbosilane-based inks (SMP-00, SMP-FA, SMP-0f, SMP-5f, SMP-10f) contain ~51-52.5 vol% SMP-10. Rheological properties reported: G'0 ranges from 2.54 to 84.6 kPa, yield stress from 371 to 3760 Pa across ink formulations. Porosity measured in pyrolyzed microrods with bubble area fractions from ~1.78% to 20.4% depending on nozzle size and ink formulation. Weibull moduli range from 2.97 to 9.94. The paper also includes a general review table of silicon-based preceramic polymer classes organized by X-group (polyborosilanes, polycarbosilanes, polysilazanes, polysilsesquiazanes, polysiloxanes, polysilsesquioxanes, polysilanes).

notes: Starting material is polydimethylsilane (PDM) converted to polycarbosilane (PCS) via reflux, then crosslinked with group IV-VI transition metal salts to form M-PCS (Zr-PCS being the primary system). ZrB2 used as passive filler to improve ceramic yield and high-temperature stability. Electrical (Joule heating) pyrolysis at 40 W, ~1073 K, ~60 s in air. Resistivity of copper coated with ceramic film: 1.36e5 Ω·cm at 293 K to 2.61e5 Ω·cm at 1422 K. Ceramic stable up to 1873 K in air. Grain size range from TEM: 20-100 nm (midpoint 60 nm used). Ceramic yield >75% targeted; weight loss ~7-10 wt% with ZrB2 filler. FTIR peaks: 3403 cm-1 (O-H), 2948/2982 cm-1 (CH3), 2087 cm-1 (Si-H), 1606 cm-1 (C=C vinyl, reduced after crosslinking), 1397 cm-1 (CH2 in Si-CH2-Si), 1244 cm-1 (Si-CH3), 1080 cm-1 (CH2 bending), 827/730 cm-1 (Si-C). notes: Precursor polymer is PMHS (polymethylhydrosiloxane) filled with varying wt% h-BN (0, 1, 5 wt%). Pyrolysis at 1000 C under argon followed by pulsed electric current sintering (PECS) at various temperatures (1100-1300 C). Ceramic yield range: 72% (neat) to 87% (5 wt% h-BN). Thermal conductivity of amorphous/porous SiOC <1 W/(m·K); dense SiOC sintered at 1300 C ~1.5 W/(m·K) temperature-invariant over 25-600 C. Electrical conduction via hopping mechanism (variable range hopping or band tail hopping). Seebeck coefficient of SiOC/1wt% h-BN: -33 uV/K at 30 C (highest reported for any PDC). n-type charge carriers (negative Seebeck). Free carbon cluster size (La) analyzed via Raman D/G band ratio using Tuinstra-Koenig equation.

notes: This is a comprehensive review paper covering many polysilazane types, not a single polymer study. Values reported span multiple polymers and references. microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous up to 1400C; after annealing 12h at 1400C, alpha-Si3N4 detected by XRD. notes: Four polyvinylsilazane samples (PI-PIV) were prepared from OVSZ (oligovinylsilazane) by ammonolysis of dichlorovinylsilane in toluene. PI: 110C/48h/toluene/no catalyst; PII: 70C/47h/hexane/Pt++ catalyst; PIII: 110C/2h/neat/no catalyst; PIV: 110C/1h/neat/Pt++ catalyst. PIII and PIV are insoluble and infusible solids. Crosslinking mechanism is primarily hydrosilylation with minor transamination. DTA shows exothermic peak 130-250C indicating crosslinking reactions during early pyrolysis. Molecular weight data: OVSZ Mn=380, Mw=600; PI Mn=720, Mw=5700; PII Mn=990, Mw=27900. Wt% composition reported, not atomic%. Heating rates given in deg C/h not deg C/min.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: All precursors undergo ~76 wt% mass loss between ambient and 1200°C. Exothermic peaks near 200°C correspond to further crosslinking. Exothermic DSC peak near 400°C indicates onset of polymer-to-ceramic conversion. Major mass changes conclude near 900°C. SMP-10 shows minor secondary exothermic mass loss between 900-1150°C attributed to carbothermal reduction of SiO2 by free carbon and SiC crystallization. Durazane-1800 ceramic yield ~75.8 wt%, highest crosslinking temperature ~300°C. PSZ-20 onset decomposition ~250°C. Hold at 400°C for 1 h included during pyrolysis ramp.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

backbone_architecture.description: Oligomeric precursors crosslinked into infusible solids. SMP-10 is a polycarbosilane with Si-C-H bonds only. PSZ-20 and Durazane-1800 are polysilazanes with additional Si-N bonds. No crosslinking catalysts used. Crosslinked at ~250°C (SMP-10, PSZ-20) or ~300°C (Durazane-1800) with ~5°C/min ramp and 4 h hold, under nitrogen atmosphere.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC(O) from SMP-10; SiCN(O) from PSZ-20 and Durazane-1800; amorphous with free carbon domains
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Microstructure consists of X-ray amorphous free carbon regions and domains of SiOxC4-x or SiNxC4-x mixed bonding network (0≤x≤4). Free carbon fraction: SMP-10 40%, PSZ-20 74.74%, Durazane-1800 78.32%. Oxygen present as impurity in all samples. Normalized ceramic compositions (a+b+c+d=1): SMP-10=Si0.34O0.18C0.48; PSZ-20=Si0.35O0.16C0.33N0.16; Durazane-1800=Si0.36O0.13C0.35N0.17. SiC crystallization noted for SMP-10 above 900°C.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: XRD performed but specific phases not enumerated in provided text; SiC crystallization inferred for SMP-10 from TGA secondary exotherm 900-1150°C

notes: Study focuses on thermodynamic stability of PDCs via high-temperature oxide melt solution calorimetry at 800°C in molten sodium molybdate (3Na2O·4MoO3). Enthalpies of formation from elements: SMP-10 (SiC(O)) = -20 ± 4.63 kJ/mol; PSZ-20 (SiCN(O)) = -78.55 ± 2.32 kJ/mol; Durazane-1800 (SiCN(O)) = -85.09 ± 2.18 kJ/mol. Enthalpies of formation from components: SMP-10 = 80.12 ± 4.65 kJ/mol; PSZ-20 = 33.89 ± 4.66 kJ/mol; Durazane-1800 = 21.4 ± 4.58 kJ/mol. Durazane-1800 displays greatest thermodynamic stability. Nitrogen addition increases thermodynamic stabilization. SiNxC4-x mixed bonds provide superior stabilization over SiOxC4-x. Characterization methods: XPS, HR-XPS, Raman, FTIR, solid-state 29Si MAS NMR, XRD, TGA/DSC. SMP-10 sourced from Starfire Systems; PSZ-20 from KiON Ceraset; Durazane-1800 from Merck. An extensive literature compilation of SiOC and SiCN(O) enthalpies of formation from components is also provided in the paper.

notes: This is a dissertation covering multiple chapters on polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs) and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). PDC chapters cover: (2) SiC fibers (Tyranno, Hi-Nicalon, Sylramic), (3) SiOC from commercial precursors SPR, TTCS, PHMS pyrolyzed at 1200 and 1500°C, (4) SiCN(O) PDCs, (5) metal-filler incorporated SiOC (Si_aO_b(M)_cC_d). Thermodynamic stabilization is the central theme - enthalpies of formation from elements and from crystalline components calculated via oxidative drop solution calorimetry at 800°C. Raman spectroscopy used to assess D/G ratios of free carbon phase. 29Si MAS NMR used in Chapter 4. HRXPS used for elemental and bonding analysis. Pyrolysis temperatures ranged from 800 to 1500°C across studies. Multiple specific polymer precursor names mentioned: SPR-212 (single source industrial precursor), TTCS, PHMS. Ceramic yields not explicitly reported in extracted text. Calorimetric data extensively tabulated for large compositional range of SiOC, SiCN(O), and metal-filled SiOC systems.

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present (B-N bonds confirmed by FTIR); ceramic product is SiBCN

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds present (FTIR peaks at 1404 and 787 cm-1); Si-vinyl groups present; C-C bonds observed at 1647 cm-1 after high temperature pyrolysis

functional_groups.other: Acrylate groups introduced via blending with acrylate monomer (20 wt%); B-N functional units in backbone

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA in nitrogen shows two-step decomposition: first step RT-200°C (evaporation of low molecular weight oligomers), second step 400-700°C (pyrolysis of crosslinked acrylate and organic moieties in PBSN). Maximum weight loss at ~450°C. Above 800°C weight change is mild indicating near-complete polymer-to-ceramic conversion. Residual weight ~59% at 1000°C. Ceramic yield stable ~58% for pyrolysis temperatures 900-1500°C with only 0.6% decrease. TGA in air at 1400°C pyrolyzed sample showed only 0.35% weight loss at 1500°C, indicating excellent oxidation resistance. Initial heating from RT to 600°C at 0.5°C/min, then 1°C/min to final temperature; cooling at 3°C/min. Higher temperature pyrolysis also conducted at 1200, 1400, 1500, and 1700°C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV/photopolymerization (DLP 405 nm light triggers crosslinking of vinyl groups in PBSN and acrylate groups in monomer); thermal crosslinking also possible via Si-vinyl and Si-H groups

backbone_architecture.description: Main chain composed of Si-N and B-N bonds with pendant Si-vinyl and Si-H groups. After UV curing, a crosslinked polymer network is formed via reaction of vinyl groups in PBSN and acrylate groups in the monomer. PBSN is described as a liquid polymer.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiBCN (predominantly amorphous up to 1500°C; β-SiC, α-SiC, β-Si3N4, BN(C)/graphitic carbon phases separate at 1700°C)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 900-1200°C: amorphous SiBCN with B-N and Si-N/Si-C bonds. At 1400°C: onset of phase separation, SiC (891 cm-1) and Si3N4 (1072 cm-1) begin to separate. At 1500°C: predominantly amorphous but with small broad XRD reflections. At 1700°C: significant crystallization of β-SiC (2θ=36°,60°,72°), α-SiC (2θ=34°), β-Si3N4 (2θ=26°,37°,50°,71°,73°), and turbostratic BN(C)/graphitic carbon (2θ=26°). BN(C) interlayers between SiC and Si3N4 crystallites enhance thermal stability.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Nanoindentation with 8 mN load. SiBCN900: hardness 7.4 GPa, modulus 58.4 GPa. SiBCN1200: hardness 7.8 GPa (maximum), modulus 54.7 GPa. SiBCN1400: hardness 6.7 GPa (reduced due to phase separation onset), modulus 64.1 GPa (highest). Bulk density at 900°C: 1.73 g/cm3; at 1200°C: 1.84 g/cm3; at 1500°C: 1.86 g/cm3. Skeleton density at 1500°C: 2.21 g/cm3. Material is not fully dense (pores from nm to several microns observed by SEM).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Predominantly amorphous up to 1500°C. At 1700°C: β-SiC, α-SiC, β-Si3N4, turbostratic BN(C)/graphitic carbon identified by XRD and HRTEM/SAED.

notes: PBSN blended with acrylate monomer at 4:1 weight ratio (80 wt% PBSN, 20 wt% acrylate) for DLP 3D printing. Mixture viscosity ~300 mPa·s. DLP printer uses 405 nm light source, 50 μm pixel DLP chip, 100 μm layer thickness. Linear shrinkage: 28.5% at 900°C, 29.0% at 1200°C, 32.1% at 1500°C. Ceramic yield values from table: 58.3% at 900°C, 58.1% at 1200°C, 57.7% at 1500°C. PBSN is a liquid polymer supplied by Laboratory of Advanced Polymer Materials, Institute of Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences. The ceramic yield reported (58.3%) is for the PBSN/acrylate blend system, not pure PBSN; pure PBSN bulk density also reported as 1.73 g/cm3. Hardness value of 7.8 GPa cited in conclusions corresponds to SiBCN1200 sample.
source: Li_2018_The fabrication of SiBCN ceramic components from preceramic polymers by digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing technology

notes: Paper is primarily a computational study developing a multiscale framework (MD + continuum heat transfer + FEM) for predicting phase transition and mechanical properties in PMHS/DVB-derived SiOC ceramics. PMHS density: 1.21 g/cm3, specific heat capacity: 1.43 J/K/g, thermal conductivity: 0.15 W/K/m. Amorphous SiOC density: 1.75 g/cm3, specific heat capacity: 1.1 J/K/g, thermal conductivity: 1.5 W/K/m. MD pyrolysis temperatures ranged from 1500 K to 2500 K with heating rate of 0.1 K/fs. Continuum-level pyrolysis simulation used a 20 mm cubic sample at pyrolysis temperature of 1273 K and heating rate of 0.63 K/s. Full ceramization completed at ~2440 s under studied heating history. Ceramic fraction defined by ratio of released gas density to maximum possible gas density.

notes: This precursor is not a traditional silicon-based preceramic polymer. It is a ZrC preceramic precursor (PZC) synthesized from ZrOCl2·8H2O (Zr source) and polyvinyl alcohol/PVA (C source) via aqueous liquid-phase reaction at 80C for 2h, dried at 70C then 120C for 5h. No organic solvent used. Pyrolysis conducted at multiple temperatures (400, 600, 800, 1000, 1100, 1200, 1300, 1400, 1500C) at 5C/min in argon for 2h each. Pure ZrC ceramic phase obtained at 1500C. PVA polymerization degree 1750±50. Particle sizes 0.2-3 um with aggregation. Ceramic product at 1500C shows C:Zr ~1:1 atomic ratio by EDS (C 51.29 at%, Zr 48.71 at%).

notes: This is a review paper on porous SiOC materials derived from polysiloxane precursors. No single polymer composition is characterized; rather, multiple precursor systems and processing strategies are surveyed. Specific surface areas reported range up to 2391.6 m2/g (from table, Ar+H2O atmosphere at 1300 degrees C, 5 h hold). Pore sizes range from single nanometers to millimeters depending on processing method. Density of pyrolyzed foams ~0.31 g/cm3. Porosity ranges: 60-90% for direct foaming, up to 88.2% total porosity, 84% for electron beam cured methylsilicone. SiOC porous network creation strategies include: ceramic replication of organic templates, direct foaming, sacrificial pore formers (expandable/nonexpandable organics, carbon templates, silica templates), molecular level pore formation, and selective species removal (carbon, SiO2 nanoclusters, SiC). Specific named precursors include: GE Toshiba YR3370 PSO, Dow Corning 217 silicone resin, PHMS, PDMS, methyl polysilsesquioxane, methylsilicone resin.

notes: Paper is primarily a computational study developing a multiscale framework (MD + continuum heat transfer + FEM) to predict phase transition and mechanical properties of PMHS/DVB-derived SiOC PDCs. No explicit ceramic yield percentage reported numerically from TGA in this paper.

Repeat unit formula: (SiC1.4NH5.4)n. CALPHAD thermodynamic modelling used to predict phase stabilities. Key invariant reactions: (1) Si3N4 + 3C = 3SiC + 2N2 at 1484 C (standard conditions), (2) thermal decomposition of Si3N4 to liquid Si + N2 at 1841 C. Nitrogen partial pressure (pN2) strongly influences reaction temperatures. DTA heating rate for separate measurement was 10 C/min. Pyrolysis experiments performed in Netzsch STA 449 F3 Jupiter. Gas flow rate 100 ml/min. Pyrolysis temperatures investigated: 1000, 1100, 1200, 1300, 1400, and 1500 C.
