notes: Study investigates four polysiloxane precursor systems (PHMS, PDMS-15PHMS, PVMS-15PHMS, PMPS-15PHMS) with varying C content and side groups (Si-H, Si-CH3, Si-CH=CH2, Si-C6H5) to produce SiOC bulk ceramics. Highest electrical conductivity achieved: 705.3 S/m at 403 °C for PMPS-15PHMS pyrolyzed at 1400 °C, claimed highest reported for this material family. Concept of 'free C connectivity' introduced to correlate with electrical conductivity. Thermal stability in air: 691-864 °C depending on composition. Pyrolysis temperatures studied: 1000, 1200, 1300, 1400 °C. Ceramic yield range midpoints used: PHMS ~83%, PDMS-15PHMS ~74.6-79.3%, PVMS-15PHMS ~77.4-79.4%, PMPS-15PHMS ~74.5-79.1%. Pt catalyst (platinum-divinyltetramethyldisiloxane complex in xylene) used at 5 ppm relative to PHMS for blends, 2.5 ppm for PHMS alone.
source: Effects of different polymer precursors on the characteristics of SiOC bulk ceramics

elemental_composition.other_elements: XPS surface compositions reported per sample: H44: C=38.6 at.%, Si=22 at.%; MK: C=9.6 at.%, Si=31.8 at.%; RSN: C=27.7 at.%, Si=29.3 at.%. Oxygen present as Si-O and SiO2 phases but not quantified in at.%.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Phenyl groups present in H44 and RSN resins (Si-C6H5); Si-O-Si backbone; crosslinking groups OR = -OH and OC2H5; C=O and C-N bonds from PVP additive (disappear after pyrolysis); after pyrolysis: Si-O-Si peak at 1030 cm-1, Si-C peak at 790 cm-1

functional_groups.other: Phenyl groups (C6H5) present in H44 and RSN; hydroxyl (-OH) and ethoxy (OC2H5) crosslinking groups; PVP added as electrospinning aid

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Mass loss measured by weighing fiber mats before and after heat treatment: ~30 wt% for MK, ~40 wt% for H44, ~25 wt% for RSN. MK and H44 pyrolyzed at 1000°C for 2 h; RSN pyrolyzed at 1000°C for 30 min (shorter time due to brittleness and decomposition of fibers). Crosslinking performed at 300°C for 3 h in air at 2.5°C/min prior to pyrolysis. Some samples also pyrolyzed at 800°C for comparison.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

molecular_weight.measurement_method: not specified; values reported as nominal molecular weights: MK=9400 g/mol, H44=2100 g/mol, RSN=2500 g/mol

backbone_architecture.description: Silicone resins described as having mainly branched molecular architecture; silsesquioxane-type structures [(RSiO1.5)n]; MK is methyl-siloxane, H44 is methyl-phenyl-siloxane, RSN is phenyl-siloxane with silsesquioxane units. Branched architecture noted to limit stretching during electrospinning.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOC ceramic produced after pyrolysis. Free carbon domains present as disordered graphitic sp2 network. H44 has highest free carbon content; MK has lowest. O1s XPS shows Si-O and SiO2 phases; MK shows predominantly SiO2. TEM shows relatively rough fiber edges attributed to volatile matter release and PVP decomposition.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: RSN fibers became brittle during pyrolysis at 1000°C for extended times, limiting hold time to 30 min

notes: Three commercial preceramic silicone resin powders studied: MK (methyl-siloxane, [(CH3)0.96(OR)0.04SiO1.5]n, MW=9400 g/mol), H44 (methyl-phenyl-siloxane, [(C6H5)0.96(CH3)0.31(OR)0.07SiO1.5]n, MW=2100 g/mol), RSN-0217 (phenyl-siloxane, MW=2500 g/mol). Fibers fabricated by electrospinning with PVP as spinning aid. Crosslinking catalysts used: Genosil GF56 for MK, Zr-acetylacetonate for H44 and RSN. Fiber diameters: MK ~1.5 to ~1 um, H44 ~1.5 to ~1 um, RSN ~3 to ~2 um after pyrolysis. BET surface area of H44-derived SiOC: 278.2 m2/g, average pore diameter 2.13 nm. Raman ID/IG: H44=1.81, RSN=1.18. Best supercapacitor performance: H44 SiOC, 50 F/g specific capacitance, ~100% retention after 2000 cycles. Best LIB performance: H44 SiOC, 578 mAh/g at 50 mA/g. Molecular weight values are nominal as-supplied values, not measured by GPC or MALDI.
source: Electrospun SiOC ceramic fiber mats as freestanding electrodes for electrochemical energy storage applications

elemental_composition.other_elements: Post-pyrolysis compositions reported as atomic fractions: SMP-10 (SiC(O)): Si=33.85 at%, C=48.24 at%, O=17.90 at%; PSZ-20 (SiCN(O)): Si=35.22 at%, C=33.50 at%, N=15.77 at%, O=15.51 at%; Durazane-1800 (SiCN(O)): Si=35.97 at%, C=34.63 at%, N=16.63 at%, O=12.77 at%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si stretching identified in Durazane-1800 crosslinked precursor; C=C bonds present in PDCs at ~1600 cm-1; SiNxC4-x and SiOxC4-x mixed bonding networks described in PDC microstructure; Si-H, N-H, C-H bonds absent after pyrolysis at 1200°C

functional_groups.other: Si-CH2-Si bridges noted in Durazane-1800; ratio of Si-vinyl to Si-CH3 groups differs between PSZ-20 and Durazane-1800

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: All precursors undergo ~76 wt% loss between ambient and 1200°C. Hold at 400°C for 1 h during pyrolysis to ensure complete crosslinking. Exothermic DSC peak near 200°C likely corresponds to further crosslinking; exothermic peak near 400°C may indicate initiation of polymer-to-ceramic conversion. Baseline TG-DSC signal subtracted to account for buoyancy effect.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - SMP-10 and PSZ-20 crosslinked at ~250°C (~5°C/min ramp, 4h hold) under nitrogen atmosphere in glove box; Durazane-1800 crosslinked at ~300°C; no crosslinking catalysts used

backbone_architecture.description: SMP-10 is a polycarbosilane containing only Si-C-H bonds; PSZ-20 and Durazane-1800 are polysilazanes with Si-N bonds in addition to Si-C-H bonds. The two polysilazanes have comparable structures differing possibly in ratio of Si-vinyl to Si-CH3 groups. No crosslinking catalysts used. Crosslinked into infusible solids before pyrolysis.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SMP-10 yields SiC(O) ceramic; PSZ-20 and Durazane-1800 yield SiCN(O) ceramics. Microstructure consists of X-ray amorphous free carbon domains and SiOxC4-x or SiNxC4-x mixed bonding network (0≤x≤4). Free carbon fraction: SMP-10=40%, PSZ-20=74.74%, Durazane-1800=78.32%. Oxygen present as impurity. Crystallized compositions of pyrolyzed ceramics: SMP-10=Si0.34O0.18C0.48; PSZ-20=Si0.35O0.16C0.33N0.16; Durazane-1800=Si0.36O0.13C0.35N0.17.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: XRD performed using Bruker D2 powder diffractometer; ceramics described as X-ray amorphous in free carbon and mixed bonding domains

notes: Study focuses on thermodynamic stability of PDCs via high temperature oxide melt solution calorimetry at 800°C using molten sodium molybdate (3Na2O·4MoO3). Enthalpies of formation from elements: SMP-10 SiC(O) = -20 ± 4.63 kJ/mol; PSZ-20 SiCN(O) = -78.55 ± 2.32 kJ/mol; Durazane-1800 SiCN(O) = -85.09 ± 2.18 kJ/mol. Durazane-1800 PDC shows greatest thermodynamic stability. Results indicate increased thermodynamic stabilization with nitrogen addition (SiNxC4-x bonds) relative to SiOxC4-x bonds. Characterization methods: XPS, HR-XPS, Raman, FTIR, solid-state 29Si MAS NMR, XRD, TG-DSC. Crosslinking performed under nitrogen atmosphere (~0.1 ppm O2) in glove box. Pyrolysis performed under flowing argon (~50 mL/min) with hold at 400°C for 1h and ramp to 1200°C at 2°C/min. Extensive thermochemical cycle data provided for a broader literature dataset of SiOC and SiCN(O) compositions.
source: Energetics and structure of SiC(N)(O) polymer-derived ceramics

polymer_name: MK (polymethylsiloxane, Wacker-Chemie GmbH); RTV 141 A and B polydimethylsiloxane (Rhodorsil)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C-H bonds broken during pyrolysis releasing H2, CH4 and other volatile compounds

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Silicone resin (poly-silsesquioxane, cage-like structure) has ceramic yield >65 wt%; linear polysiloxane (PDMS) has ceramic yield <30 wt%. Pyrolysis temperature range 800-1200 C. Transient micro-porosity generated in temperature range 400-800 C during polymer-to-ceramic conversion due to decomposition of organic moieties (CH4 and H2 gas generation); this micro-porosity is eliminated at higher pyrolysis temperatures by viscous flow densification.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal crosslinking; zirconium acetylacetonate catalyst used if necessary; PDMS crosslinked via two-component system

backbone_architecture.description: Silicone resin (poly-silsesquioxane, MK) has a cage-like structure with high ceramic yield (>65 wt%); PDMS has a linear structure with low ceramic yield (<30 wt%). Mixing these two produces porosity during pyrolysis.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOC ceramic formed upon heat treatment >800 C in inert atmosphere. PDC systems include Si-O-C, Si-N-C, Si-C, Si-E-N-C (E=B, Al, Ti). With fillers, cordierite, mullite, SiAlON, SiC also possible.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Macro-cellular foams: compression strength 1.2-12.5 MPa, flexural strength 0.5-12.5 MPa, elastic modulus 0.4-7.6 GPa, fracture toughness 0.15-0.25 MPa·m^0.5. Micro-cellular foams: compression strength 2.1-18.3 MPa, flexural strength 2.9 ± 0.01 MPa (at density 310 kg/m3), elastic modulus 1.4 GPa (at density 310 kg/m3).

notes: Paper focuses on porous SiOC ceramics derived from silicone resins (primarily MK polymethylsiloxane from Wacker-Chemie) via three fabrication methods: (1) direct foaming, (2) sacrificial PMMA microbead templates, (3) mixing silicone resin with PDMS. Porosity range 55-90 vol%, cell size 1 µm to 2 mm. Hierarchical porosity achieved via controlled thermal treatment (SSA 400-700 m2/g), high SSA filler addition, zeolite deposition, meso-porous coatings, aerogel infiltration, etching, and in situ nano-wire/tube formation. Pyrolysis temperature range 800-1200 C; midpoint 1000 C used for pyrolysis_temp_C field (range noted here). Porosity range midpoint 72.5 vol% used for porosity_pct (range 55-90 vol%). CTE: 3.75-4.6 × 10^-6 K^-1. Bulk density 250-950 kg/m3. Functional foams produced with SiC (electrical), iron silicide (magnetic) fillers. Journal of the European Ceramic Society 28 (2008) 1389-1395.
source: Engineering porosity in polymer-derived ceramics

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH=CH2 (vinyl), Si-C6H5 (phenyl) mentioned as side groups influencing carbon content and electrical properties

functional_groups.other: phenyl (Si-C6H5), pyridyl-moieties for metal coordination

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: argon, inert gas, water vapor mentioned in specific cases

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal, chemical (hydrosilylation, dehydrocoupling, condensation, coordination chemistry)

backbone_architecture.description: Various architectures discussed including linear, dendritic, hyperbranched, and block copolymer structures achievable via metal coordination and metallopolymer routes

SiCN contains non-graphitic disordered carbon and turbostratic carbon; beta-SiC forms above 1500 C. TiC, TiCxOy, Mo2C, NiO phases reported in composite systems.

notes: This is a perspective/review paper, not a primary experimental study of a single preceramic polymer. Multiple polymer types (polysiloxane, polysilazane, polycarbosilane) and ceramic systems (SiOC, SiCN, SiBCN, SiAlCN, etc.) are discussed. Electrical conductivity of SiOC-Ti composites reported up to 1176 S/cm at 950 C. Electrochemical energy storage data for various PDC anodes summarized in table (SiOC, SiCN, SiCNO composite systems pyrolyzed at 800-1100 C). Polyhydromethylsiloxane (PHMS) and divinylbenzene (DVB) used as specific precursor system with TiO2 nanoparticles. Ferrocene-containing polysiloxanes noted for magnetic properties. Ti3C2 (MXene) incorporated into polysiloxane-derived SiOC composites.

polymer_name: Ceraset PSZ 20 (poly(ureamethylvinyl)silazane), also referred to as PUMVS/Ceraset; modified variants: boron-modified silazane (Si(B)CN precursor) and hafnium-modified silazane (Si(Hf)CN precursor)

elemental_composition.other_elements: B (in Si(B)CN precursor via trimethyl borate addition ~1:1 wt% TMB:Ceraset); Hf (in Si(Hf)CN precursor via hafnium isopropoxide isopropanol at 3:1 wt ratio Hf reagent:PSZ). Post-pyrolysis XPS elemental compositions reported separately for each composite sample (see notes).

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N and B-O bonds present in Si(B)CN/CF; Hf-O-Si and Hf-O-C bonds present in Si(Hf)CN/CF; Hf-N-C observed in crosslinked Si(Hf)CN/CF; Si-O-Si stretching observed; B-N functional group observed after pyrolysis; Si2N-H observed in crosslinked samples

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Crosslinking in Ar gave higher ceramic yields than crosslinking in air. Si(Hf)CN/CF crosslinked in Ar gave 98 wt% yield; Si(B)CN/CF crosslinked in Ar gave 94 wt%; SiCN/CF crosslinked in Ar gave 89 wt%. Crosslinking in air gave lower yields: SiCN/CF 88%, Si(B)CN/CF 72%, Si(Hf)CN/CF 41%. Oxidation stability study conducted at 800, 1000, 1200, 1500 C in air with heating rate 5 C/min.

backbone_architecture.description: Poly(ureamethylvinyl)silazane (Ceraset PSZ 20) used as base precursor; modified with trimethyl borate (TMB) at ~1:1 wt% for Si(B)CN variant or hafnium isopropoxide isopropanol at 3:1 wt ratio for Si(Hf)CN variant; liquid-phase precursors crosslinked thermally to form network prior to pyrolysis

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN, Si(B)CN, Si(Hf)CN - X-ray amorphous up to 1500°C
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Quaternary PDCs remain X-ray amorphous up to 1500°C. Nanodomains of Si3N4, SiC, and h-BN reported generally for such systems. Post-pyrolysis XPS confirmed Si-N, Si-C, Si-O phases. B-N and B-O in Si(B)CN; Hf-O-Si and HfO2 in Si(Hf)CN. Free carbon phase (sp2, disordered) observed via Raman D and G bands. Post-oxidation elemental compositions at 800-1500°C provided via XPS.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Values are for Si(Hf)CN/CF composite minicomposite (highest among composites tested). SiCN/CF: strength 390 MPa, modulus 49.89 GPa. Si(B)CN/CF: strength 110 MPa, modulus 30.58 GPa. Uncoated CF bundle tensile strength ~2300 MPa. Tests performed quasi-static at 0.2 mm/min, gauge length 30 mm, 6000-fiber bundles.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: X-ray amorphous up to 1500°C; potential nanodomains of Si3N4, SiC, h-BN mentioned generically for quaternary PDC systems

notes: Paper focuses on CMC minicomposites (SiCN/CF, Si(B)CN/CF, Si(Hf)CN/CF) fabricated by drop-coating CF cloth with preceramic polymer solutions followed by crosslinking and pyrolysis at 800°C in N2 for 30 min. Base precursor is commercial Ceraset PSZ 20 (poly(ureamethylvinyl)silazane) from Clariant. Si(B)CN precursor made by adding trimethyl borate (TMB) dropwise to Ceraset at ~1:1 wt%. Si(Hf)CN precursor made by adding hafnium isopropoxide isopropanol at 3:1 wt ratio (Hf reagent:PSZ); higher ratios caused precipitation. Post-pyrolysis XPS elemental compositions (at.%): SiCN/CF: Si 41.33, C 9.84, N 1.32, O 47.51; Si(B)CN/CF: Si 40.34, C 6.84, N 0.55, O 49.00, B 3.27; Si(Hf)CN/CF: Si 28.63, C 13.56, N 1.51, O 48.12, Hf 8.18. Oxidation weight retention data provided at 800, 1000, 1200, 1500°C. Ceramic yield of ~90% noted for inert-atmosphere crosslinked samples. Modulus and strength values reported are for composite bundles, not monolithic ceramic. Nanodomains generally 10-20 Å reported for such quaternary PDC systems in literature.
source: Evaluating Use of Boron- and Hafnium-Modified Polysilazanes for Ceramic Matrix Minicomposites

notes: This paper is about NASA composite nozzle extension (CNE) development for cryogenic liquid rocket engines, focusing on carbon-carbon (C-C) and carbon/silicon-carbide (C-SiC) ceramic matrix composites. It is not a preceramic polymer chemistry paper. No preceramic polymer synthesis, characterization, or pyrolysis data are reported. The only tangential reference to pre-ceramic resins is a brief mention that HRL Laboratories uses 'pre-ceramic resins' combined with additive manufacturing to fabricate ceramic rocket engine components, but no chemical details, composition, thermal, or mechanical data for any preceramic polymer are provided.
source: Extreme-Temperature Carbon- and Ceramic-Matrix Composite Nozzle Extensions for Liquid Rocket Engines

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PIP route yields Si-O-N-C matrix phase; also referenced as Si-N-C-O in composite table. Other routes yield SiC, Al2O3, SiC+Si, SiC+Al2O3+Al phases.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Proportional limit strength 60 MPa for PIP Nicalon SiC/Si-N-C-O CFCC; interlaminar shear strength 14 MPa; thermal conductivity through thickness 1.3 W/m-K

notes: This paper is a review of CFCC fabrication routes and does not characterize a specific preceramic polymer in detail. The polymer infiltration and pyrolysis (PIP) route is described as one of five matrix-infiltration approaches, producing a Si-O-N-C (or Si-N-C-O) ceramic matrix phase. Dow Corning, Composite Optics, and General Electric are listed as PIP practitioners. The preceramic polymer is described generically as a matrix-precursor resin used in polymer/sol-gel infiltration plus pyrolysis; no specific polymer name, molecular weight, bonding structure, functional groups, pyrolysis conditions, or ceramic yield data are provided. Mechanical property data for the PIP-derived CFCC are from Table II: proportional limit strength 60 MPa, interlaminar shear strength 14 MPa, thermal conductivity 1.3 W/m-K, using Nicalon SiC fiber at 50 vol% with proprietary interface.

polymer_name: PCS (polycarbosilane) mixed with PZC (organic zirconium-containing polymeric precursor)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Zr present in PZC precursor; oxygen contained in PZC as noted by ZrO2 formation at 900°C

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Zr-O bonds implied by oxygen content in PZC; Zr-C bonds formed after pyrolysis/heat treatment

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: ZrC, SiC (beta), ZrO2 (intermediate); pure ZrC and SiC after full heat treatment at 1500°C for 120 min

notes: Grain size range stated as 100-200 nm (midpoint 150 nm used). PCS sourced from National University of Defense Technology, China; PZC from Institute of Process Engineering, Chinese Academy of Science. Mixed at 1:1 weight ratio, dispersed in xylene. Composite fabricated by PIP process with 3D carbon fiber preform (T300SC, Toray) with PyC interphase (~150 nm). notes: This paper is primarily about binder jetting additive manufacturing of silicon nitride ceramics, not about preceramic polymers. The binders described (Binder 1: UV-curable copolymer of methyl acrylate/polyurethane; Binder 2: modified starch) are not preceramic polymers in the traditional sense. They are sacrificial organic binders used to shape silicon powder green bodies, which are then reaction-sintered in vacuum at 1170-1500°C to form Si3N4 ceramics. Porosity of sintered samples: up to 60% (Binder 1) and up to 70% (Binder 2). Ceramic grain inclusions size 1-20 µm. Porosity midpoint 65% used for porosity_pct field (range 60-70%). Elemental compositions in Table 2 are from X-ray microanalysis of sintered ceramic fracture surfaces, not from the binders themselves.

notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. Interface materials discussed include pyrolytic carbon, BN, mullite, alumina, alumina-titania, zirconia, titania, and porous SiC deposited via CVD. notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. It concerns Si3N4-BN fibrous monolithic ceramics fabricated via coextrusion of ceramic powders in a thermoplastic binder system, followed by hot pressing at 1750°C for 2 hours in nitrogen. notes: This paper is not primarily about a preceramic polymer; it describes a water-based ceramic slurry photoresin (nanoCAM) for two-photon polymerization 3D printing of ATZ ceramics. notes: Paper reports on SiOC ceramic foams derived from three polysilsesquioxane precursors (SR350, SR355, H44) using two direct foaming methods. Fillers (MoSi2, alpha-SiC, graphite, copper acetate, Cu2O) added up to 80 wt% to tune electrical conductivity over several orders of magnitude (from <10e-7 to ~3.33 1/(Ohm*cm)). Pyrolysis temperatures 1000 and 1200°C in N2 (99.99%). Cu0 crystallite size range 30-80 nm (midpoint 55 nm used for grain_size_nm and crystallite_size_nm). Heating/cooling rate range 2-5 K/min (midpoint 3.5 used). Hold time 1-4 h (midpoint 2.5 h = 150 min used). Pyrolysis temperature range 1000-1200°C (midpoint 1100 used). Free carbon (sp2 and sp3) identified by Raman spectroscopy. Percolating carbon network proposed as main conduction mechanism. Cu species appear to affect free carbon structure.

notes: PCS dissolved in hexane at 125 g/L; films spun at 3000 rpm on Si wafers and SiO2 slides; as-deposited film thickness ~700 nm. Absorption enhancement achieved by ~30 nm evaporated carbon overlayer (transmittance reduced to 75%) or 5 vol% submicrometer graphite particles (transmittance reduced to 83%). Crystallite size of 8.5 nm from C-coated film on SiO2 at highest fluence, slightly larger than those from conventional pyrolysis at 1200°C. notes: Study compares six preceramic polymers pyrolyzed via conventional oven heating (flowing argon, 10°C/min, 1000-1500°C, 30 min hold) and microwave hybrid heating (2.45 GHz, 6 kW max, SiC susceptor-lined alumina insulation, stepped heating under vacuum then static argon, 1100-1500°C, 30 min hold). β-SiC nanocrystallite sizes from TEM: HPCS conventional 2 nm at 1100°C and up to 20 nm at 1500°C; HPCS microwave ~1 nm at 1100°C and 5 nm at 1500°C; PCS both methods up to 20 nm at 1500°C; DPPC microwave 5-10 nm at 1500°C. Graphitic turbostratic structures (5-8 nm long, 2-4 atomic planes of 0.35 nm thickness) observed between SiC grains in microwave-processed HPCS and PCS but absent in conventionally processed materials. Melting points: SR350=90°C, SR355=93°C, PCS=110°C, DPPC=70-130°C (midpoint 100°C), HPCS<2°C (liquid), CERASET SN<-78°C (liquid). HPCS+1wt% β-SiC powder (<50nm, Cerac) slurry also investigated; seeding found to be ineffective. Scherrer equation with pseudo-Voigt profile fitting used for crystallite size determination.

Enthalpies of formation from crystalline constituents (SiC, Si3N4, graphite) are small: S1: +3.5, S2: +4.1, S3: -2.8, S4: +3.5 kJ/mol (range -2.8 to +4.1 kJ/mol). Residual hydrogen measured by 1H MAS NMR: S1: 0.041 wt%, S2: 0.040 wt%, S3: 0.001 wt%, S4: 0.007 wt%. Carbon cluster size estimated ~1-1.5 nm by Raman spectroscopy. Heating rate of 100C/h (1.67C/min) used for pyrolysis; TGA used 5C/min. SiCN PDCs considered thermodynamically stabilized relative to crystalline end-members due to positive configurational entropy of amorphous phase. Less stable energetically than SiCO PDCs. Pyrolysis of 1-2 g precursor in silica crucible under argon flow 50 mL/min.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Weight loss levels off at ~600°C for Pt-free samples indicating majority of polymer-to-ceramic conversion complete. Pt-containing foams show decomposition onset at ~190°C (much lower than Pt-free foams at ~330°C) and ~16% higher total weight loss. Above 1000°C weight loss is negligible for Pt-containing samples. Maximum difference in weight loss between atmospheres was ~2%. Decomposition onset for unfoamed Pt-free samples ~200°C vs ~330°C for foamed Pt-free samples, attributed to ZnO in blowing agent catalyzing lower-temperature decomposition.

SSA: G-Pt1_600_N2: 295 m²/g (pores <1 nm), F-Pt1_600_N2: 363 m²/g (pores <1 nm), F-Pt2_1400_N2: 67 m²/g (pores 4-32 nm), F-Pt2_1400_Ar: 55 m²/g (pores 5-55 nm). microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Complete conversion to cubic ZrC at 1450 deg C. Lattice parameter 4.695 +/- 0.001 Angstrom (conventional XRD) and 4.69499 +/- 0.00001 Angstrom (synchrotron), indicating near-complete conversion with little dissolved oxygen. Oxygen-free ZrC1-x reported at 4.698 Angstrom. Three microstructural zones observed by HR-TEM: ZrC crystalline core, disordered surface region (~2-3 nm, contains Zr likely as oxycarbide or oxide), and graphene-like carbon wrap (<5 layers). Raman confirms pregraphitic carbon with D/G ratio evolving from 0.72 to 1.24.

notes: This paper does not concern a preceramic polymer in the traditional sense (e.g., polysilazane, polycarbosilane). It describes a sol-gel synthesis of nanocrystalline ZrC using zirconium n-propoxide and polyfurfuryl alcohol (PFA) as a carbon-yielding thermoset precursor. The PFA acts as a preceramic carbon source rather than a silicon-based preceramic polymer. Grain size range reported as 55-80 nm for c-ZrC and ~20 nm for tZrO2 precursor; midpoint of 67.5 nm used for ZrC grain_size_nm and crystallite_size_nm. Carbothermal reduction mechanism involves agglomeration and necking of nanoparticles rather than simple contracting-volume diffusion. BET surface area peaks at 1250 deg C then decreases due to agglomeration above that temperature. P123/etOH/AcAc/ZNP solution ratio: 0.05/40/1/1; ZNP/FA molar ratio: 1/2 (10C/Zr atomically). Synchrotron PDF beamline at Australian Synchrotron used at 15 keV. Rietveld analysis performed using Bruker TOPAS V4.2.

notes: Two preceramic polymer-based sintering aid formulations were studied: Powder A (polysiloxane Silres H44 + gamma-Al2O3 + amorphous Si3N4 + carbon black + Y2O3) and Powder B (polysilazane Ceraset PSZ20 + Al2O3). Both were used as 18 wt% sintering aids in alpha-Si3N4 matrix. Sintering performed by hot-pressing at 1600-1750°C with 30 MPa load in static nitrogen atmosphere (0.105 MPa). The paper text refers to 'HTT polysilazane' in Table I but the experimental section identifies the polysilazane as Ceraset PSZ20 (KiON); HTT may refer to a different designation. notes: A second preceramic polymer was also used in this study: furanic (FUR) resin (Furolite 100, TransFurans Chemicals), which produces amorphous carbon upon pyrolysis at 1000°C with a ceramic yield of 52%. FUR resin required a catalyst (HM 1448, WIZ chemicals) for crosslinking and pre-curing at 145°C for 2h. Both AHPCS and FUR resin had density ~1.0 g/cm³ and dynamic viscosity of 40-100 cPs at 25°C. The heating rate of 51°C/h (0.85°C/min) applies to the 1000°C PIP pyrolysis cycle. Graphite powder (TIMREX KS 10, 13 wt%) was mixed with AHPCS for one infiltration strategy (Case #4) to promote SiC formation during LSI. The paper primarily describes a hybrid AM process (PBF + PIP + LSI) for complex SiC ceramic structures; preceramic polymer characterization is secondary to the overall fabrication and densification study.

notes: Paper describes the Active Filler Controlled Polymer Pyrolysis (AFCOP) process for bulk ceramic component fabrication. Primary polymer studied is poly(silsesquioxane) (PSS, H 62 C, Wacker Chemie) with CrSi2 reactive filler (2-40 um particle size, H.C. Starck). Filler volume fractions up to 45 vol% used. Table A1 lists multiple preceramic polymers with ceramic yields: poly(methylsilane) 0.85, poly(methylvinylsilane) 0.83, poly(silaethylene) 0.87, poly(hydridosilazane) 0.74, poly(methylsilazane) 0.85, poly(vinylsilazane) 0.85, poly(vinylphenylsilazane) 0.85, poly(cyclomethylsilazane) 0.88, poly(borosilazane) 0.90, poly(boronsiliconimide) 0.72, poly(methylsiloxane) 0.85, poly(phenylsilsesquioxane) 0.78. Polymer density ~1 g/cm3; ceramic residue density 2.2-3.2 g/cm3 depending on phase. Porosity range 5-20 vol% with globular nanopores 1-50 nm. Volume shrinkage exceeds 50% without filler. Pyrolysis temp range for final hold noted as 1200-1500°C; midpoint 1350°C used. Heating rate range 1-2°C/min for second ramp; midpoint 1.5°C/min used. Hold time range 1-6 h (60-360 min); midpoint 210 min used. Porosity range 5-20 vol%; midpoint 12.5% used.

At 1700C: alpha/beta SiC (0.13), C (0.01), turbostratic C (0.86). At 2000C: alpha/beta SiC (0.11), C (0.01), turbostratic C (0.88). No crystalline Si3N4 detected.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Mentioned resistance to crystallization, creep deformation, and viscoelasticity at high temperatures qualitatively; no quantitative mechanical data provided

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous up to 1500C; partially crystalline at 1700C and above
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC detected at 1500C and above; alpha-SiC also present at 1500-1700C; turbostratic carbon at 2000C; no crystalline Si3N4 detected

notes: Paper focuses on carbon-rich SiCN ceramics derived from poly(methylphenylsilylcarbodiimide) S2. SAXS radius of gyration (Rg) of nanodomains: 1.04 nm at 1300C, 1.85 nm at 1500C, up to ~4.87 nm at 1700C and 4.43 nm at 2000C. Carbon lateral cluster size La (Raman): 2.01 nm at 1300C, 1.59 nm at 1500C, 1.35 nm at 1700C, 1.11 nm at 2000C. beta-SiC crystallite size (XRD): 11.26 nm at 1500C, 14.27 nm at 1700C, 57.23 nm at 2000C. Turbostratic carbon Lc: 5.67 nm at 2000C. Empirical formulas normalized on Si: 1300C Si1C4.98N1.54O0.07; 1500C Si1C5.29N1.55O0.06; 1700C Si1C4.44N0.03; 2000C Si1C4.73N0.01. Nanodomains are spheroidal at low T, with rod-like morphologies appearing at higher T for certain phases.
source: Nanodomain Structure of Carbon-Rich Silicon Carbonitride Polymer-Derived Ceramics

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH=CH2 (vinylsilyl), Si-C-C-Si, Si-O-Si (detected in ceramic nanocomposites S2/S3), Si-O-CH2 (formed after reaction with ethanolamine Ni(II) complex)

functional_groups.other: trialkylsilyl and hydrosilyl groups at oligomer chain ends; NH2 from ethanolamine modification in Ni-polysilazane precursors

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three weight loss stages observed for HTT: ~12.4% at T<300°C (H2 evolution from Si-H/Si-H and Si-H/N-H dehydrocoupling and oligomer distillation); ~9.6% at 300-530°C (NH3 from transamination); ~12% at 530-750°C (CH4 from Si-CH3 decomposition or C-C bond cleavage). Thermolysis profiles A, B, C used; Profile C (slow heating, long holds) yields highest surface area and micropore volume. Resulting ceramic phase is Si-C-N-(O).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal; slow heating rates and long intermediate holding times promote crosslinking completion

backbone_architecture.description: Polysilazane HTT with Si-N backbone bearing methyl, vinyl, and hydride substituents; contains both linear and cyclic/branched segments as indicated by 29Si NMR shifts (CH3CH2=CHSiN2 and CH3HSiN2 environments); oligomer chain ends contain trialkylsilyl and hydrosilyl groups

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramic product designated Si-C-N-(O); Ni/Si-C-N-(O) nanocomposites formed from Ni-polysilazane precursors S1, S2, S3. Si-O-Si bands appear in nanocomposites S2 and S3, indicating some oxygen incorporation. Nickel nanoparticles (~2.5 nm average diameter) embedded in Si-C-N-(O) matrix.

notes: Paper describes modification of polysilazane HTT with Ni(II) complex (via ethanolamine ligand) to form Ni-polysilazane precursors S1, S2, S3 with 6.3, 27, and 40 wt% Ni(II) complex content, respectively. The -OH groups of ethanolamine react with Si centers of HTT via nucleophilic substitution, evolving H2 and NH3. In situ Ni nanoparticles (~2.5 nm) form during thermolysis. Nickel nanoparticles catalyze H2 evolution and hydrocarbon release at lower temperatures (~250°C). Nickel nanoparticle surface areas estimated at ~4.5, 18, and 36 m2/g of ceramic for S1, S2, S3 respectively. FTIR of ceramics shows disappearance of Si-H (2148 cm-1) and N-H (3385 cm-1) bands with increasing Ni content, and appearance of Si-O-Si bands (1040, 800 cm-1) in S2 and S3 nanocomposites. 29Si NMR of HTT shows shifts at -17.70 ppm (CH3CH2=CHSiN2) and -22.80 ppm (CH3HSiN2). Polymer name inferred as HTT from context; full commercial name is HTT 1800.
source: Nanoporous Silicon Oxycarbonitride Ceramics Derived from Polysilazanes in Situ Modified with Nickel Nanoparticles

Plain H44 showed 24.5 wt% weight loss; nickel-doped H44 showed 17.8 wt% weight loss; Si-filler/nickel-doped H44 showed 5.7 wt% weight loss after pyrolysis at 1000 °C. Ceramic yield of 75.5% is midpoint estimate for plain H44 (100 - 24.5 = 75.5 wt% residue). Gas release sequence: water/ethanol 200-400 °C, benzene 420-600 °C, hydrogen 500-1000 °C, methane 700-1000 °C.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis up to 1000 °C yields amorphous Si-O-C glass (nominally SiC + SiO2 + free carbon). At higher temperatures crystallization produces SiC, C, and SiO2. In Ni-doped samples: turbostratic carbon formed at 700-800 °C, multiwall carbon nanotubes in pores from ~850 °C; SiC formed from 1000 °C. In Si-filler + Ni-doped samples: SiC/SiO2 core-shell nanowires formed in pores from 900-1500 °C with crystalline β-SiC core (lattice spacing 0.25 nm, (111) planes) and amorphous SiOx shell.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous Si-O-C below ~1000 °C; SiC (cubic β-SiC), C (graphitic/turbostratic), SiO2 at higher temperatures as verified by XRD

notes: Polymer is Silres H44 from Wacker Chemie, a poly(methylphenylsilsesquioxane) with n ≈ 20. Doped with nickel acetate tetrahydrate (Ni(ac)2·4H2O) dissolved in ethanol. Two sample types: (1) H44 + Ni(ac)2 without Si filler; (2) H44 + Ni(ac)2 + Si powder filler (d50 = 8 µm, volume ratio H44:Si = 6:4 or 8:2, with 3 wt% or 10-20 wt% Ni). Melt mixed at 80 °C for 20 min, cured at 200 °C for 4 h. Pyrolysis at 800-1500 °C in argon, heating/cooling rate 3 K/min, 1 h hold. Ni acts as catalyst (dehydrogenation, CNT and SiC nanowire nucleation). SiC/SiO2 nanowire total diameters 10-100 nm; VLS growth mechanism proposed. Polymer density given as 1-1.2 g/cm3 general range for preceramic polymers; ceramic density 2-3 g/cm3. Ceramic yield of 75.5% derived from plain H44 weight loss of 24.5 wt% at 1000 °C; pyrolysis_temp_C of 1500 is the maximum temperature studied in the paper.
source: Nanoprocesses in polymer-derived Si–O–C ceramics- Electronmicroscopic observations and reaction kinetics

molecular_weight.measurement_method: supplier specification; range given as 1000-1500 g/mol, midpoint used

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Mixed amorphous and crystalline phases after pyrolysis at 1400 C: amorphous SiOC matrix with mixed SiO4, SiO3C, SiO2C2, SiOC3, SiC4 tetrahedrals; beta-SiC nanocrystals; SiO2 nanodomains (cristobalite); turbostratic carbon (sp2-bonded, ~3-10 nm); free carbon phase acting as diffusion barrier

notes: This paper focuses on 4D-STEM characterization methodology applied to PVMS-derived SiOC ceramics rather than polymer synthesis. MW range given as 1000-1500 g/mol (midpoint 1250 used). Beta-SiC crystallite size reported as 2-10 nm by HRTEM (midpoint ~6 nm used). Turbostratic carbon cluster sizes ~3-4 nm (upper left) and ~10 nm (bottom) observed at 1400 C. RDF analysis revealed C-C bond at 1.41 Ang, O-2nd O distance at 2.60 Ang (SiO2 phase), C-3rd C pair distance at 3.80 Ang. No long-range order beyond 5 Ang. Heating rate for cooling also 1 C/min.

notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. It is a review article focused on nanostructured ceramic materials (nanoceramics) including Al2O3/SiC nanocomposites, Y-TZP, silicon nitride, and related bulk ceramic systems. No preceramic polymer chemistry, pyrolysis data, polymer molecular weight, or related descriptors are present in the text.

polymer_name: polyhydridomethylsiloxane (PHMS) crosslinked with TMTVS or DVB

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental compositions given in wt% for pyrolysed ceramics: PT2: Si=50.55, C=18.34, O=30.99, H=0.12; PT5: Si=45.67, C=27.69, O=26.45, H=0.19; PD1: Si=38.09, C=40.33, O=21.30, H=0.28; PD2: Si=29.24, C=55.15, O=14.99, H=0.62

molecular_weight.measurement_method: MW reported by supplier for PHMS (MW=1900); TMTVS MW=344

backbone_architecture.description: Linear polyhydridomethylsiloxane (PHMS) crosslinked with either cyclic 1,3,5,7-tetramethyl-1,3,5,7-tetravinyl cyclotetrasiloxane (TMTVS) or divinylbenzene (DVB) to form an elastomeric network resin

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC (amorphous at 1000 C; SiC nanocrystals + SiO2-based network at 1300 C)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000 C both PT2 and PD2 are amorphous. At 1300 C cubic SiC nanocrystals nucleate alongside SiO2-based network; larger and more intense SiC reflections in high-C PD2. Free carbon phase present as disordered graphitic clusters. Mixed Si-O-C tetrahedra (SiO3C, SiO2C2) decrease with increasing pyrolysis temperature due to phase separation.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Cured resins described as hard elastomeric transparent solids

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous at 1000 C; partially crystalline at 1300 C
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous SiO2-based network (broad hump at 2theta ~22 deg); cubic SiC nanocrystals (broad reflections at 2theta ~35, 60, 72 deg) at 1300 C

notes: Study focuses on SiOC ceramics as Li-ion battery anodes. Four compositions studied: PT2 and PT5 (PHMS/TMTVS, low carbon, 8-18 wt% free C), PD1 and PD2 (PHMS/DVB, high carbon, 32-49 wt% free C). All compositions maintain O/Si atomic ratio ~1. Carbon cluster sizes (La) from Raman: PT2@1000C=12.6 Å, PT2@1300C=15.1 Å, PD2@1000C=11.1 Å, PD2@1300C=13.1 Å. Best reversible capacity 656 mAh/g for PT5 at 1000 C; PT2 shows unusual increase in reversible capacity with higher pyrolysis temperature. Polymer precursors: PHMS (linear, Si-H bearing), TMTVS (cyclic, vinyl-bearing siloxane), DVB (organic crosslinker).
source: New Insights in to the Lithium Storage Mechanism in Polymer Derived SiOC Anode Materials

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si bonds observed as intermediates during pyrolysis; C-C bonds forming amorphous carbon clusters; Si-O backbone with random hydrocarbon side groups

functional_groups.other: various hydrocarbon side groups described as randomly distributed

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Simulation-based pyrolysis (ReaxFF/LAMMPS), not experimental TGA. System heated from 300 K to 2000 K in 0.2 ns, then to 2400 K over 0.4 ns, held at 2400 K for 2.32 ns, then heated to 2600 K over 0.38 ns and held for 2.67 ns. O atomic percent initially increases from 6.9% to 10% then decreases to 7.7%. Gas species removed during simulation. Carbothermal reduction observed above 2400 K equivalent conditions.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Weight-averaged molecular weight tracked for carbon species during simulation to monitor C cluster growth

backbone_architecture.description: Linear polysiloxane with Si-O backbone units; eight linear polymer units each having 100 Si-O backbone units, spatially randomized and consolidated into a simulation box of 93,680 atoms

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOC domains coexist with free C networks below 1300 C experimentally. Simulation shows large SiO2 cluster (29 at% O) and smaller SiO2 clusters (44 at% O) at end state, with amorphous C and graphitic regions at SiO2-C interface. beta-SiC formation referenced as experimental outcome above 1300 C but not directly observed in simulation.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC referenced as forming experimentally above 1300 C; SiO2 clusters remain amorphous and less than 5 nm in size

notes: This paper is a molecular dynamics simulation study (ReaxFF with LAMMPS) of PSO-derived SiOC pyrolysis using 93,680 atoms and ~6 ns simulation time. Key findings: (1) O removal occurs preferentially in larger SiO2 clusters; smaller SiO2 clusters (<5 nm) resist carbothermal reduction. (2) C cluster growth is inversely correlated with O content. (3) Pyrolysis temperatures in simulation are 2400-2600 K (2127-2327 C), far exceeding typical experimental carbothermal reduction onset of 1300 C. (4) Simulation pressure was 2000 atm. (5) Gas species below 40 g/mol (later 80 g/mol) were deleted during simulation. (6) Final H content ~1 wt%. (7) No experimental ceramic yield or TGA data reported; all data are from MD simulation. Elemental compositions are tracked dynamically in simulation but initial bulk atomic percentages are not explicitly tabulated.
source: New findings related to carbothermal reduction of polysiloxane-derived ceramics

polymer_name: SMP-10 (Starfire Systems) and PURS / polyureasilazane (KiON Corp.)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: ZrB2-SiC/SiC CFCCs fabricated; SEM showed closed and open porosity after greenbody cure; open pores re-infiltrated more successfully with neat resin than slurry

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Flexure tests performed on SMP-10 and PURS derived SiC/SiC-ZrB2 CFCCs; fiber reinforcement prevented catastrophic failure by increasing fracture toughness

notes: Paper is a Master's thesis (Missouri University of Science and Technology, 2013) on fabrication of continuous fiber reinforced ceramic composites (CFCCs) using polymer infiltration and pyrolysis (PIP). Two preceramic polymers used: SMP-10 (allylhydridopolycarbosilane, Starfire Systems) and PURS (polyureasilazane, KiON Corp.). Final composite target: ZrB2-SiC/SiC CFCCs for ultra-high temperature applications (>2000°C). Hi-Nicalon ceramic fibers used as reinforcement. ZrB2 used as ultra-high temperature additive. Processing included vacuum bagging, greenbody cure, low and high temperature pyrolysis cycles, and re-infiltration. Specific polymer property data (Tables 3.1 and 3.2 from datasheets) are referenced but not reproduced in the extracted text.
source: Nicholas - PROCESSING OF CONTINUOUS FIBER REINFORCED CERAMIC COMPOSITES FOR ULTRA HIGH TEMPERATURE APPLICATIONS

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ni content varied by addition of Ni(II) 2,4-pentanedionate at 19.35, 38.70, 58.05, and 77.40 wt% relative to PSO. Post-pyrolysis chemical formulas reported: SiO3C2.4 (SiOC 800C), SiO1.24C2.13 (SiOC 900C), SiO2.2C2.5 (SiOC 1100C), SiO2.61C1.97Ni0.36 (SiOC-Ni-4 800C), SiO1.75C2.07Ni0.54 (SiOC-Ni-4 900C), SiO1.89C0.59Ni0.37 (SiOC-Ni-4 1100C)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-C network in amorphous SiOC matrix; free carbon phase present; vinyl groups present from [-Si(CH3)(CH=CH2)O-] units

functional_groups.other: Phenyl groups present from [-Si(C5H6)2O-] units; Ni(II) 2,4-pentanedionate (nickel acetylacetonate) added as organometallic filler

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: argon with water vapor injection (Ar:H2O molar ratio ~5:1) at 500-700°C range; pure argon above 700°C
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yields range from ~40.84% to ~65.50% depending on Ni content and pyrolysis temperature. At same Ni content, ceramic yield generally decreases with increasing temperature. At same temperature, higher Ni content decreases ceramic yield. TGA of pyrolyzed samples performed in air from RT to 1000°C at 5°C/min; SiOC-Ni samples pyrolyzed at 900°C stable up to 1000°C with less than 6 wt% weight loss in argon. Heating rate to 500°C was 2°C/min; 500-700°C at 1°C/min with water vapor; then 2°C/min to final temperature.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal: 50°C for 12 hours then 100°C for 12 hours; Pt catalyst (2.5 ppm diluted, 1 wt% relative to PSO) used only for pure PSO without Ni; Ni(II) 2,4-pentanedionate acts as crosslinking agent for SiOC-Ni samples

backbone_architecture.description: Hypercrosslinked polysiloxane network with repeat units [-Si(C5H6)2O-]3[-Si(CH3)(H)O-]2[-Si(CH3)(CH=CH2)O-]2; carbon-rich polysiloxane chosen for desirable crosslinking ability and to impart electrical conductivity to resulting ceramic

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOC matrix with in situ formed Ni nanocrystallites (cubic Ni, JCPDS 98-012-3814) and minor NiO (hexagonal, JCPDS 98-0044-9032) and turbostratic/graphitic carbon (hexagonal graphite, JCPDS 98-006-2692). No nickel silicides detected. Pure SiOC remains fully amorphous at 800-1100°C. Ni nanocrystallites well-dispersed in matrix.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Cubic Ni (peaks at 44.49°, 51.85°, 76.38° corresponding to (111), (200), (220) planes); hexagonal NiO (peaks at 37.10°, 43.10°, 62.60° corresponding to (111), (002), (022) planes); hexagonal graphite (peak at 26.6° corresponding to (002) plane); SiOC matrix remains amorphous

notes: Grain size range: ~87.32 ± 26.24 nm (800°C), ~112.23 ± 22.45 nm (900°C), ~186.32 ± 24.59 nm (1100°C); midpoint across temperatures used for grain_size_nm and crystallite_size_nm fields (~128.62 nm average). Volume shrinkage ranges from ~25.85% to ~64.48%. Densities range from 1.70 to 2.84 g/cm3. Highest electrical conductivity ~247 S/m. Ferromagnetic behavior observed; saturation magnetization highest at 900°C pyrolysis. SiOC-Ni-4 samples at 800°C and 1100°C broke into pieces after pyrolysis. Water vapor pyrolysis used to suppress free carbon and SiC formation, thereby preventing nickel silicide formation. Surface area of SiOC-Ni-4: 41.591, 60.249, 64.534 m2/g at 800, 900, 1100°C respectively. Pore volume: 0.053, 0.093, 0.133 cc/g at same temperatures. Study from Virginia Tech, funded by NSF CMMI-1634325.
source: Nickel‐containing magnetoceramics from water vapor‐assisted pyrolysis of polysiloxane and nickel 2,4‐pentanedionate

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental compositions given as mass% in Table I. Polymer (2): Si 17.3, B 2.4, C 62.5, N 9.4, H 7.2, O 1.2 mass%; empirical formula Si2.7B1.0C23N3.0H32. Polymer (3): Si 27.4, B 2.7, C 46.2, N 10.8, H 7.0, O 4.0 mass%; empirical formula Si3.9B1.0C15N3.1H28. Polymer (4): Si 29.0, B 2.0, C 53.8, N 7.4, H 6.6, O 1.8 mass%; empirical formula Si5.7B1.0C25N2.9H36. Boron is present in all three polymers.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Ph (phenyl) bonds present in all three polymers; N-SiH2Ph groups in polymers (3) and (4); B-C2H4-Si linkages (ethylene bridge); Si-Ph units in polymer (2) replace Si-CH3; cross-linking via Si-CH3 and N-H bonds reported for related polymer (1)

functional_groups.other: Phenyl groups (Ph = C6H5) on silicon; SiH2Ph groups in polymers (3) and (4); ethylene bridge (C2H4) connecting B and Si

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Heating rate 100 deg C/h at T <= 100 deg C and 25 deg C/h at T > 100 deg C during polymer-to-ceramic transformation at 1050 deg C with 4 h isothermal hold; ceramic yield 74-75 wt%. TGA of resulting amorphous ceramics performed from 1000 to 2200 deg C at 10 deg C/min (T <= 1050 deg C) and 2 deg C/min (T > 1050 deg C) in 0.1 MPa argon, followed by 30 min isothermal hold at 2200 deg C. Continuous mass loss between 1400 and 2200 deg C: 3.0 wt% for Si2.9B1.0C14N2.9, 3.9 wt% for Si3.9B1.0C11N3.2, 3.3 wt% for Si5.3B1.0C19N3.4. Isothermal mass loss at 2200 deg C for 30 min: 0.9, 1.2, and 0.7 wt% respectively. Mass loss rates at 2200 deg C: 1.7 wt%/h for Si2.9B1.0C14N2.9, 2.4 wt%/h for Si3.9B1.0C11N3.2, 1.4 wt%/h for Si5.3B1.0C19N3.4.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal
crosslink_density.description: Polymers (2)-(4) are proposed to have reduced cross-linking compared to polymer (1) because Si-CH3 units are replaced by Si-Ph and N-H groups are replaced by N-SiH2Ph, blocking further cross-linking. Polymer (1) cross-links via Si-CH3 and N-H bonds at ~400 deg C eliminating ammonia and methane. Reduced crosslinking state proposed to provide enhanced disorder in resulting amorphous Si-B-C-N network.

backbone_architecture.description: Polyorganoborosilazane network with boron center connected via ethylene bridges (C2H4) to silicon atoms, which are further connected through N-H or N-SiH2Ph linkages. Polymer (2): [B(C2H4Si(Ph)NH)3]n - Si bearing phenyl groups, N-H linkages. Polymer (3): [B(C2H4Si(CH3)NH)2(C2H4Si(CH3)N(SiH2Ph))]n - mixed N-H and N-SiH2Ph. Polymer (4): [B(C2H4Si(CH3)N(SiH2Ph))3]n - all N-SiH2Ph linkages. Empirical formulas consistent with calculated Si3B1C24N3H30, Si4B1C15N3H30, and Si6B1C27N3H42 for polymers (2), (3), and (4) respectively.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous at 1050 deg C; beta-Si3N4 and beta-SiC crystalline phases at 2200 deg C
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous ceramics at 1050 deg C: Si2.9B1.0C14N2.9, Si3.9B1.0C11N3.2, Si5.3B1.0C19N3.4. Crystallization begins at ~1700 deg C in argon. After 2200 deg C anneal: beta-SiC and beta-Si3N4 detected by powder XRD exclusively. ~80-90 mol% of Si3N4 retained at 2200 deg C. Carbon and boron kinetically stabilize Si3N4-based composition.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-Si3N4 and beta-SiC detected exclusively in samples annealed at 2200 deg C in 0.1 MPa argon; amorphous at 1050 deg C; crystallization onset ~1700 deg C

notes: Paper reports three novel polyorganoborosilazane preceramic polymers (2), (3), and (4) yielding Si-B-C-N ceramics stable up to 2200 deg C. Ceramic yield 74-75 wt% noted as a range; midpoint 74.5 used. Heating rates during polymer pyrolysis given in deg C/h (100 deg C/h and 25 deg C/h), not deg C/min. TGA of ceramics used rates of 10 deg C/min (<=1050 deg C) and 2 deg C/min (>1050 deg C). Polymer (3) isolated in 82% yield; polymer (4) in 52% yield. Elemental compositions in mass%, not atomic%. Boron content ~2.0-3.6 mass% across all samples. All ceramics contain excess carbon relative to thermodynamically stable binary phases (SiC, BN, Si3N4). Extraordinary thermal stability attributed to kinetic rather than thermodynamic factors, specifically increased structural disorder from phenyl groups reducing cross-linking and decreasing atomic diffusivities. Reference polymer (1) = [B(C2H4Si(CH3)NH)3]n with ceramic composition Si3.0B1.0C4.3N2.0 reported for comparison.
source: Novel Silicon‐Boron‐Carbon‐Nitrogen Materials Thermally Stable up to 2200°C

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiO2 (amorphous, intermediate); final phases are Y2SiO5 (yttrium monosilicate, X1 and X2 polymorphs) and Y2Si2O7 (yttrium disilicate, alpha and gamma polymorphs) depending on Y2O3/SiO2 ratio and firing temperature
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Y-MS (Y2O3/SiO2 = 1): X1 phase forms at 1000 C, transforms to X2 phase at 1300 C. Measured density 4.53 +/- 0.01 g/cm3 vs theoretical 4.44 g/cm3. Y-DS (Y2O3/SiO2 = 0.5): X1 Y-MS forms first at 1000-1100 C, alpha-Y2Si2O7 appears at 1200 C, gamma-Y2Si2O7 forms at 1400 C. Measured density 4.15 +/- 0.01 g/cm3 vs theoretical 4.04 g/cm3. Coatings on SiC foam estimated ~10 um thick.

notes: Polymer is a commercial polysilsesquioxane (Silres MK, Wacker-Chemie) dissolved in isopropyl alcohol and mixed with Y2O3 nano-particles (30-50 nm, purity >99.95%). Two Y2O3/silicone weight ratios used: 3.16 for Y-MS and 1.58 for Y-DS. Solid content ~20 wt% in dispersions. For luminescent application, 5 mol% of Y2O3 replaced by Eu2O3 nano-particles (45-58 nm) to produce (Y0.95Eu0.05)2SiO5; red luminescence at 612 nm achieved under 394 nm excitation. Paper notes that treatment in nitrogen would yield SiOC instead of SiO2. Y2O3 nano-particles not reacted at 900 C; silicate phases begin forming at 1000 C. Pyrolysis temperature range studied: 900-1500 C.
source: Novel synthesis and applications of yttrium silicates from a silicone resin containing oxide nano-particle fillers

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiC/SiC ceramic matrix composites processed via CVI and PIP (Polymer Infiltration and Pyrolysis); BN interphase fiber coating mentioned

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: High strength, excellent creep resistance, and good transverse strength and thermal conductivity noted as requirements for 2700°F application

notes: This paper is a conference proceedings overview of NASA Glenn Research Center CMC/EBC research and does not describe a specific preceramic polymer. PIP (Polymer Infiltration and Pyrolysis) is mentioned as a processing step for SiC matrix densification, but no preceramic polymer chemistry details are provided. No preceramic polymer descriptors can be extracted from this text.
source: Overview of ceramic matrix composite research at NASA Glenn Research Center - mse044

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N, C-B-N, B-O, C-C, C-N, N-B (sp2), C-N-B, N-O bonds identified by XPS; sp3 hybridized SiC(2x) units and sp2 hybridized BNCx units present in amorphous structure

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Non-isothermal oxidation TGA performed on SiBCN ceramics (not pyrolysis of preceramic polymer). Three oxidation stages identified: RT-550C (little mass change), 550-1000/1200C (significant oxidation with mass gain up to 15 wt% for amorphous A-1), >1000/1200C (slow mass increase). Oxygen content: A-1=5.1 wt%, C-1=3.8 wt%, C-2=3.4 wt%.

backbone_architecture.description: Three-dimensional amorphous network covalent bonding structure composed of sp3 hybridized SiC(2x) (x<1) and sp2 hybridized BNCx atomic units. Synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA), not by polymer pyrolysis route.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN with boron; amorphous SiBCN (A-1), nanocrystalline SiC + turbostratic BN(C) (C-1 and C-2)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous A-1: no diffraction peaks. C-1: beta/alpha-SiC and turbostratic BN(C) microcrystals 2-5 nm. C-2: nanocapsule-like structure with SiC grains 20-50 nm encapsulated by turbostratic BN(C); BN(C) phase consists of mutually doped turbostratic carbon (tC) and turbostratic boron nitride (t-BN). Graphitization parameter g: C-1=6%, C-2=21%.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous (A-1); beta-SiC, alpha-SiC, turbostratic BN(C) in crystallized samples C-1 and C-2

notes: This paper is NOT about a preceramic polymer. It investigates amorphous and crystallized SiBCN ceramics synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA), not by polymer pyrolysis. The study focuses on oxidation behavior and kinetics of amorphous vs. crystallized SiBCN ceramics. Grain size range: C-1 beta-SiC = 3.5 nm, C-2 beta-SiC = 16.3 nm (midpoint 9.9 nm noted above). Oxidation activation energies reported: BNCx (amorphous) Ea=145 kJ/mol, SiC(2x) (amorphous) Ea=364 kJ/mol, BN(C) phase (crystalline) Ea=209 kJ/mol, SiC phase (crystalline) Ea=533 kJ/mol; synchronous oxidation above 750C changes BNCx Ea to 332 kJ/mol; nanocapsule structure decreases SiC Ea to 445 kJ/mol and t-BN Ea to 198 kJ/mol. XPS bonding data provided for samples A-1, C-1, C-2 before and after oxidation in tables.
source: Oxidation behavior of amorphous and nanocrystalline SiBCN ceramics – Kinetic consideration and microstructure

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-OH groups present in silicone resin prior to pre-treatment; urethane and ureic bonds formed during foaming; Si-C bonds in SiOC ceramic phase; free carbon (turbostratic graphite clusters) in SiOC matrix

functional_groups.other: Si-OH (silanol) groups present in SR350 prior to thermal pre-treatment at 150 C

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Conversion occurs in two steps: ~300-400 C (PU decomposition and volatilization of silicone oligomers) and ~600-800 C (breakage of organic bonds in silicone resin with methane release/ceramization). Pure SR350 ceramic yield ~84 wt% at 1200 C. PU decomposition leaves ~8 wt% carbonaceous residue. Calculated weight losses of 32 and 55 wt% for low-PU and high-PU foams respectively, consistent with experimental values. TGA performed at 10 K/min heating rate in air or nitrogen.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - SR350 pre-treated at 150 C to reduce Si-OH content; crosslinking occurs during foaming/blowing process

backbone_architecture.description: Methylsilicone resin (SR350) blended with polyurethane (PU) in either 1/1 or 5.25/1 wt ratio; phase-separated sea/island morphology with PU dispersed as particles in silicone resin matrix; after pyrolysis yields amorphous SiOC ceramic with carbon-rich islands embedded in Si-rich matrix

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) matrix with Si atoms bonded to both O and C; free carbon present as turbostratic graphite clusters; carbon-rich regions derived from PU decomposition embedded within SiOC matrix. High-PU foams oxidized at 1200 C show cristobalite formation by XRD; low-PU and as-pyrolyzed specimens remain amorphous. Total C content: 14.1 wt% (bulk SiOC), 16.2 wt% (low-PU foam), 29.6 wt% (high-PU foam).

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Flexural strength as pyrolyzed: 3.69 MPa (high-PU), 2.70 MPa (low-PU); crushing strength as pyrolyzed: 3.32 MPa (high-PU), 2.02 MPa (low-PU). Bulk density of tested specimens: 0.40 +/- 0.02 g/cc. Maximum values reported across all foam densities: crushing strength ~16 MPa, flexural strength ~12 MPa, Young's modulus ~7 GPa. Coefficient of thermal expansion: 3.5e-6 /K (20-1000 C). High-PU foams show ~30% strength decrease after oxidation at 1200 C for 12 h; low-PU foams maintain strength. Cell size: ~730 +/- 205 um (low-PU), ~430 +/- 116 um (high-PU).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: As-pyrolyzed specimens (both low- and high-PU) are amorphous; cristobalite identified in high-PU SiOC foams after oxidation at 1200 C for 12 h in air; low-PU foams remain amorphous after all oxidation treatments

notes: Paper describes SiOC ceramic foams produced by pyrolysis of foamed blends of SR350 methylsilicone resin (General Electric Silicone Products Division) and polyurethane at two weight ratios: 1/1 (High-PU) and 5.25/1 (Low-PU). Foam bulk density range: 0.2-0.6 g/cc; cell size range: 100-700 um. Pyrolysis under 99.999% N2 at 5.0 cc/min, 2 K/min heating rate, 1 h at 1200 C. Residual carbon from PU after pyrolysis: ~1.3 wt% (low-PU) and ~4 wt% (high-PU). Linear shrinkage upon pyrolysis: ~27% (low-PU) and ~35% (high-PU) at 1200 C. PU components: polyether polyols (Tercacol 3, Mw=3000 g/mol; Tercarol 1, Mw=1000 g/mol) and polyphenylmethane isocyanate (Tedimon 31). Surfactant polydimethylsiloxane also used. Key finding: low-PU foams exhibit superior oxidation resistance due to carbon-rich regions being fully embedded within SiOC matrix rather than exposed at cell wall surfaces.
source: Oxidation resistant ceramic foam from a silicone preceramic polymer:polyurethane blend

polymer_name: PHMS/TMTVS/PDMS blend (polymethylhydrosiloxane, 1,3,5,7-tetramethyl-1,3,5,7-tetravinylcyclotetrasiloxane, polydimethylsiloxane); also Durazane (polysilazane) used for SiOC(N); PMS used for aerogels

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Vinyl groups present from TMTVS; Si-N bonds present in Durazane-derived SiOC(N) samples

functional_groups.other: TMTVS provides vinyl crosslinking sites; PDMS contributes dimethylsiloxane units

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA data collected for as-received PU templates (10-80 ppi) and TPU, as well as PHMS, TMTVS, PDMS, and crosslinked preceramic polymer derived from PHMS/TMTVS. Pyrolysis at 1000°C/2h/Ar for SiOC foams and aerogels; 1200°C/2h/N2 for SiOC(N) foams using Durazane.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - two conditions used: 80°C/7h + R.T./23h (dense strut) or 220°C/2h (hollow strut); aerogels cured at 200°C/6h

backbone_architecture.description: Crosslinked polysiloxane network formed from PHMS (polymethylhydrosiloxane), TMTVS (tetravinyl cyclotetrasiloxane as crosslinker), and PDMS (polydimethylsiloxane). Weight ratios varied: PHMS/PDMS of 2/0, 1.7/0.3, and 1/1 with fixed TMTVS at 0.08 parts. PMS used for aerogel production.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD patterns collected for SiOC foams with hollow and dense struts from various PU foam templates. SiOC(N) produced using Durazane pyrolyzed at 1200°C/N2. Amorphous SiOC ceramic phase expected at 1000°C pyrolysis in Ar.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Compressive strength range across samples: 0.164-0.883 MPa. Total porosity range: 91.81-97.25 vol%. AM-made SiOC(N) cellular structures also tested. Young's modulus values reported in literature review tables for similar SiOC foams (E ~ 15-450 MPa). Tensile properties of cast aluminum alloys filtered through PDC foams also evaluated (yield strength, UTS, elongation).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: XRD patterns collected for SiOC foams; consistent with amorphous SiOC at 1000°C pyrolysis temperature

notes: This is a thesis covering production of porous PDC components (SiOC foams via replica technique using PU templates of 10-80 ppi, AM-made SiOC(N) cellular structures, and SiOC aerogels). Primary preceramic polymer system: PHMS/TMTVS/PDMS crosslinked by thermal curing; Durazane (polysilazane) used for SiOC(N) foams; PMS (polymethylsiloxane) used for aerogel production. Curing at 80°C/7h+R.T./23h gives dense struts; 220°C/2h gives hollow struts. Pyrolysis at 1000°C/2h/Ar for SiOC; 1200°C/2h/N2 for SiOC(N). Aerogels cured at 200°C/6h then pyrolyzed at 1000°C/2h/Ar with various drying solvents (acetone, ethanol, n-hexane, solvent-free) and autoclave filling levels (35-65 vol%). Applications tested: gas permeability, molten metal filtration (A357 aluminum alloy), and heat exchange. PHMS/PDMS weight ratios of 2/0 (pure PHMS), 1.7/0.3 (labeled '15'), and 1/1 (labeled '50') studied.
source: PRODUCTION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF POROUS CERAMICS FOR HIGH TEMPERATURE APPLICATIONS

notes: This paper is a review article on ceramic robocasting (additive manufacturing of ceramics such as Al2O3, SiC, Si3N4, BaTiO3, HA, TCP, ZrO2, B4C, etc.) and does not describe any preceramic polymer. No preceramic polymer chemistry data are present in the text. All fields are null as this paper is outside the domain of preceramic polymer chemistry.
source: Peng_et_al-2018-Advanced_Materials- Ceramic Robocasting Recent Achievements, Potential, and Future Development

elemental_composition.other_elements: Post-pyrolysis ceramic compositions reported per sample: SiOC/Ni: Si=41.2, O=22.4, C=32.1, Ni=4.3 atomic%; SiOC/Mo: Si=41.0, O=19.4, C=32.1, Mo=7.5 atomic%; SiOC/Co: Si=41.6, O=20.5, C=28.5, Co=9.4 atomic%; SiOC/Zr: Si=44.7, O=18.2, C=31.9, Zr=5.2 atomic%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Vinyl groups (CH=CH2) present on polymer backbone; polymer repeat unit: [-Si(C5H6)2O-]3[-Si(CH3)(H)O-]2[-Si(CH3)(CH=CH2)O-]2

functional_groups.other: APTES (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane used as complexing agent for Co-containing samples only

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: argon (SiOC/Mo, SiOC/Co, SiOC/Zr); Ar+H2O molar ratio 5:1 (SiOC/Ni)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: SiOC/Ni, SiOC/Mo, SiOC/Co pyrolyzed at 1100°C; SiOC/Zr pyrolyzed at 1400°C; Ar gas flow rate 500 cm3/min for all samples

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal: 50°C for 12 h then 120°C for 12 h (Ni, Mo, Co samples); platinum-divinyltetramethyldisiloxane catalyst used for Zr samples

backbone_architecture.description: Polysiloxane resin with mixed repeat units: [-Si(C5H6)2O-]3[-Si(CH3)(H)O-]2[-Si(CH3)(CH=CH2)O-]2; crosslinked prior to pyrolysis

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiOC/Ni: SiOC/SiO2/Ni; SiOC/Mo: SiOC/SiO2/MoC; SiOC/Co: SiOC/SiO2/graphite/CoSi/CoO; SiOC/Zr: SiOC/SiO2/ZrO2. SiOC matrix composed of SiO2, SiO3/2C1/4, SiOC1/2, SiO1/2C3/4, and SiC tetrahedral units with dispersed turbostratic/graphitic carbon. Amorphous SiO2 halo at ~22° 2theta observed for all samples.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiOC/Ni: cubic Ni (FCC, peaks at 44.5°, 51.9°, 76.4°); SiOC/Mo: MoC (peaks at 36.4°, 61.4°, 77.4°); SiOC/Co: CoSi, CoO, graphitic carbon (002 at 26°); SiOC/Zr: t-ZrO2 (29.7°) and beta-SiC (35°, 60°, 72°); all samples show amorphous SiO2 halo at ~22°

notes: Paper focuses on thermodynamic Gibbs free energy minimization modeling of phase separation in metal-modified SiOC PDC systems. Metal-to-PSO mass ratio was 0.02:1 for all systems. Empirical formulas post-pyrolysis: SiOC/Ni=SiO0.95C1.82Ni0.05; SiOC/Mo=SiO0.83C1.83Mo0.05; SiOC/Co=SiO0.86C1.60Co0.07; SiOC/Zr=SiO0.71C1.66Zr0.06. Chemical composition measured by ICP-OES using lithium borate fusion-acid dissolution. Phase fractions determined by lever rule combined with Gibbs free energy minimization (HSC Chemistry 6.0 software). Four phase separation pathways identified: pure metal (Ni), metal carbide (MoC), metal silicide (CoSi), and metal oxide (ZrO2). Ni2Si formation suppressed by water vapor addition in Ar atmosphere during SiOC/Ni pyrolysis. Ni-containing SiOC showed electrical conductivity up to ~247 S/m at 900°C.
source: Phase content prediction in polymer- derived ceramics with metal additives

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C=C vinyl bonds from DVB crosslinker; Si-H hydrosilylation with vinyl groups during crosslinking

functional_groups.other: DVB (divinylbenzene) used as crosslinking agent; platinum-divinyltetramethyldisiloxane complex used as catalyst

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Samples heated to 800 C at 1 C/min with 2 h hold, then to 1200, 1300, or 1400 C at 1 C/min with 2 h hold. Ceramic yield range 82-84.5% across all conditions. TGA in air to 1000 C at 5 C/min showed slight weight gain up to 0.25 wt% for low TiO2 content samples; 20 and 30 wt% TiO2 samples pyrolyzed at 1400 C showed substantial weight loss up to 12.8 wt% at 1000 C starting at ~480 C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic - platinum-divinyltetramethyldisiloxane complex (hydrosilylation); thermal curing at 50 C for 12 h, 80 C for 10 h, 120 C for 6 h

backbone_architecture.description: PHMS crosslinked with 60 wt% DVB (relative to PHMS) via platinum-catalyzed hydrosilylation to form a cured network; TiO2 nanoparticles (10, 20, or 30 wt%) incorporated as filler

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis yields SiOC matrix containing free carbon (graphene-like), amorphous and crystalline SiO2, and TiCxOy (solid solution of TiC and TiO) with intermediate titanium oxides (Ti2O3, Ti3O5, Ti4O7). At 1400 C, tetragonal SiO2 forms. Higher pyrolysis temperature promotes more TiC formation. SiO2 cluster size ~3 nm (sharp NLDFT peak); with TiO2 addition, larger SiO2 clusters >10 nm also present.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous SiO2 (22.9 deg hump), graphene/C (43 deg), TiCxOy cubic solid solution (36, 42, 61 deg), Ti2O3, Ti3O5, Ti4O7, rutile TiO2 (residual), tetragonal SiO2 at 1400 C (21.8 deg peak), SiC (referenced as possible high-T product)

notes: Primary focus of paper is SiOC-TiCxOy composite derived from PHMS+DVB polysiloxane system with TiO2 nanoparticle filler (anatase, <25 nm). Ceramic yield range 82-84.5%; volumetric shrinkage 45-52%; density 1.70-2.01 g/cm3. Highest electrical conductivity reported: 5.03 S/cm at 400 C in air. SDS surfactant used for surface modification of TiO2 in one sample set (30 wt% SDS-modified TiO2). Carbothermal reaction: TiO2 + C -> TiC + CO/CO2. Higher TiO2 content reduces free carbon and promotes SiO2 crystallization. Pyrolysis ceramic yield midpoint ~83.3% noted from table range 82-84.5%.
source: Phase transformation, oxidation stability, and electrical conductivity of TiO2-polysiloxane derived ceramics

elemental_composition.other_elements: Bulk ceramic elemental composition (wt%) varies with pyrolysis temperature; at 1100C: C~11.60, O~41.02, Si~balance; at 1400C: C~10.66, O~41.70, Si~balance. Empirical formula ranges from SiO1.52C0.57 to SiO1.54C0.52 depending on pyrolysis temperature.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: sp2-hybridized carbon (graphite-like, turbostratic carbon) present in ceramic phase; D and G Raman bands at ~1350 and ~1582 cm-1 identified in samples annealed at 1200C and above

functional_groups.other: Methyl groups present as methylsilsesquioxane repeat unit [CH3SiO1.5]n

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Initial pyrolysis at 800C for 30 min in flowing argon to form MKF powder. Bulk samples subsequently pyrolyzed at 1100C with 5h hold, then further annealed at 1200, 1300, and 1400C each for 5h under flowing argon. Overall ceramic composition (SiO2, SiC, free C) remains approximately constant across 1100-1400C annealing range, indicating no dominant decomposition. SiC crystallization (beta-SiC) observed at 1300-1400C. Free carbon phase evolves and forms percolating network above 1300C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal and catalytic - crosslinked at 250C for 30 min using zirconium acetylacetonate as cross-linking agent

backbone_architecture.description: Methylsilsesquioxane (T-type, RSiO1.5 units) forming a crosslinked network; after pyrolysis forms amorphous SiOC ceramic matrix with segregated free carbon and nanocrystalline SiC phases at higher temperatures

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Predominantly amorphous SiOC matrix even at 1400C. Phase composition (wt%) at 1100C: SiO2~77.02, SiC~16.23, free C~6.75; at 1400C: SiO2~78.30, SiC~15.75, free C~5.95. Nanocrystalline beta-SiC crystallization observed at 1300-1400C by XRD (111) at 2theta=35deg, (101) at 60deg, (211) at 72deg. Turbostratic graphite-like free carbon percolation network forms at 1400C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Young's modulus of 110 GPa measured by acoustic measurements on rectangular sticks. Piezoresistive gauge factor k~145 at 1400C under cyclic pressure of 8 MPa peak-to-peak at 180 Hz.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous SiOC (silica halo at 2theta~22deg); nanocrystalline beta-SiC (cubic, reflections at 2theta=35, 60, 72deg) emerging at 1300-1400C

notes: Paper focuses on piezoresistive behavior of polymer-derived SiOC ceramics. Preceramic polymer is commercial poly(methylsilsesquioxane) (Wacker-Belsil PMS MK). Crosslinker: zirconium acetylacetonate. Bulk ceramic processing: warm pressing at 25 MPa and 180C. Porosity ranges: ~7.95-8.01% at 1100-1200C, ~10.37-10.57% at 1300-1400C. Archimedes density ~2.25 g/cm3 and bulk density ~2.01-2.07 g/cm3 across all samples. Ohmic resistance drops dramatically with pyrolysis temperature: 136000 kOhm at 1100C to 3.3 kOhm at 1400C, correlating with free carbon percolation network formation. Only MK1400 shows piezoresistivity (k~145); samples at 1100-1300C show no piezoresistive effect.
source: Piezoresistive Effect in SiOC Ceramics for Integrated Pressure Sensors

polymer_name: CPBCS (crosslinked polyborosilazane); specific variants: CPBCS10-1, CPBCS5-1, CPBCS3-1

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present; weight percent compositions reported for cured precursors at 300C and ceramics at various temperatures in Table 2. Example for CPBCS5-1 cured at 300C: Si=35.40 wt%, B=1.02 wt%, C=30.10 wt%, O=19.80 wt%, N=5.33 wt%, H=8.35 wt%

functional_groups.other: boron-containing groups (BNO, B4C, BO); SiCxN4-x and SiCxO4-x tetrahedral units in ceramic phase

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Weight loss in two stages: 40-300C (escape of small molecules) and 300-800C (cleavage and escape of organic groups, NH3, CH4, H2C=CH2, methylsilanes detected by MS). Carbothermal reduction and Si3N4 decomposition detected between 1550-1600C. Ceramic yields at 1600C in argon: 98.32% (SiBCN(O)10-1), 98.29% (SiBCN(O)5-1), 95.72% (SiBCN(O)3-1). In air: 99.17%, 99.36%, 99.87% respectively. Initial curing at 100C in air then 300C for 2h under argon prior to pyrolysis above 1000C for 2h.

Si-H/C=C molar ratios of 10:1, 5:1, and 3:1 used.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiBCN(O) amorphous below 1400C; β-SiC crystallizes at 1600C; also SiO2 (high cristobalite), BN(C) detected

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: β-SiC (peaks at 35.7, 41.4, 60.0, 71.8, 75.5 degrees), SiC stacking faults (33.7 degrees), high cristobalite (~22 degrees broad), BN(C) weak peak at 1600C

notes: grain_size_nm and crystallite_size_nm set to midpoint value for SiBCN(O)5-1 at 1600C (16.4 nm); full range for SiBCN(O)5-1: 2.4 nm at 1400C, 16.4 nm at 1600C, 75.0 nm at 1800C. ceramic_yield_pct set to 98.29% for CPBCS5-1 in argon at 1600C as representative value; full range reported in tga_notes. notes: Paper focuses on SiOC/graphene oxide porous ceramic monoliths prepared via Pickering emulsion method using hexadecylamine-modified GO as stabilizer and commercial methyl polysiloxane resin (Silres MK, Wacker Chemie) as SiOC precursor. Composites designated SiOC-GO-R16(X, T°C) where X is mass ratio of modified GO. Best electrode performance: SiOC-GO-R16(23%, 900°C) with insertion/extraction capacities of ~2399/1176 mAh/g at 50 mA/g in first cycle; 350 mAh/g charge capacity after 175 cycles at 800 mA/g with 88% Coulombic efficiency. DMSO/cyclohexane volume ratio 28/72% used in emulsion. Specific surface area measured by BET; pore size by BJH. The preceramic polymer is water-sensitive.
source: Polymer-Derived Silicon Oxycarbide:Graphene Oxide Porous Ceramic Monoliths Obtained from Pickering Emulsions- Application as Active Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries

notes: This paper is a review article focused on ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTCs) including borides, carbides, and nitrides of group 4 transition metals (Ti, Zr, Hf, Ta). It discusses physical properties, thermodynamics, and synthesis methods including preceramic polymer routes, but the extracted text does not contain specific preceramic polymer characterization data. No polymer-specific descriptors (composition, bonding, molecular weight, pyrolysis yield, etc.) are discernible from the provided text sections.

notes: Ceramic yield of 68 wt% in Ar at 1000°C; ceramic composition after pyrolysis: 57.8 wt% Si, 14.3 wt% C, 26.0 wt% N, 0.8 wt% O (air contamination); solid-phase density of pyrolyzed ceramic 2.33 g/cm3; solid-phase density of infusible polymer 1.22 g/cm3; BET surface area of ceramic powder 5.5 m2/g; relative bulk densities 90-94% (open porosity 6-10%) after pressureless pyrolysis at 1000°C. Heating rate range given as 0.5-1°C/min (midpoint 0.75 used). A second polysilazane PCMSN (poly(chlorohydridomethyl)silazane) is also described: pyrolysis in Ar at 1000°C gives 72 wt% yield SiCN (Si1.1C1.5N1.4); pyrolysis in NH3 at 1000°C gives 68 wt% yield silicon nitride. PMPS (poly(methylphenyl)silane) is a third polymer described, yielding SiC upon pyrolysis in Ar at 1000°C with 68 wt% yield.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pure PCS yielded phase-pure cubic β-SiC (PDF #74-2307) with no detected graphitic carbon. Boron carbide solid solutions (B6.5C or B13C2, PDF #78-1574) detected with weak XRD peaks; boron likely partially substitutes Si in SiC lattice.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Vickers hardness ranged from 19.6 to 25.8 GPa depending on boron content and mixing route. Indentation fracture toughness ranged from 4.1 to 5.8 MPa·m^0.5 (Bpwd series, low load) and 4.5 to 4.7 MPa·m^0.5 (Bsol series, high load). Pure PCS (2050°C/10min): HV=22.4±4.2 GPa, KIC=4.2±0.8 MPa·m^0.5. Elastic modulus assumed equal to SiC (430 GPa) for KIC calculation.

notes: Paper focuses on SPS densification of polycarbosilane-derived SiC with amorphous boron additions (5 and 10 wt%). Two mixing routes studied: (1) dry mixing of B powders with pre-pyrolized PCS (Bpwd), and (2) dissolving PCS in acetone with B powders before pre-pyrolysis (Bsol). SPS performed at 1900 or 2050°C, 50 MPa, 5 or 10 min hold, under vacuum (~5 Pa), heating rate 100°C/min. Boron acted as sintering additive enabling densification; toughening via crack deflection around boron carbide phase. Bsol route gave best hardness (25.8 GPa at 10% B). Archimedes densities: pure PCS 2.12-2.44 g/cm³; Bpwd 2.70-2.97 g/cm³; Bsol 2.99-3.03 g/cm³ (theoretical SiC ~3.21 g/cm³). Ceramic yield of 68 wt% used to adjust PCS/B weight proportions.

notes: This is a review/feature article summarizing seven years of collaboration between UC Davis and TU Darmstadt on polymer-derived SiCN and SiOC ceramics. The specific polymer highlighted is poly(phenylmethylsilylcarbodiimide) [-Ph(CH3)Si-NCN-]n. Carbon domain average diameter ~15 nm estimated for polysilylcarbodiimide-derived SiCN at 800 C with 35-40 wt% C. Mass fractal dimension of SiCxO4-x units in SiOC is 2.3-2.5 (not 3), indicating fractal spatial distribution. ~3 H atoms per NC1/4Si2/4 interfacial site stabilize C-N bonds in SiCN PDC. Characterization methods used: 29Si, 13C, 15N, 1H solid-state MAS NMR, CPMAS, HETCOR, COSY, DQ NMR; micro-Raman; SAXS; XRD; HRTEM; oxide melt solution calorimetry. Ceramic yield not explicitly reported. Pyrolysis temperatures studied range from 800 C to 2000 C across various experiments.
source: Polymer-derived SiCN and SiOC ceramics– structure and energetics at the nanoscale

notes: Study focuses on production of magnetic microcellular SiOC ceramic foams using commercially available polysiloxane (MK, Wacker Chemie) as preceramic polymer, iron silicide (Fe1-xSix, 0.25 < x < 0.50) micropowders as functional magnetic filler, and PMMA microbeads (25 µm) as sacrificial pore formers. PMMA:PP+IS weight ratio kept at 80:20. Volume shrinkage ranged from 39.5% (S6012) to 64.4% (S0012). Foam densities ranged from 0.26 to 0.45 g/cm3. Soft-ferromagnetic behavior confirmed by VSM measurements; Bs values lower than expected for pure Fe-Si powder, attributed to mechanical constraint from SiOC matrix and interface pinning effects. TGA of pure IS powders showed negligible weight loss with exothermic peak at 494°C and endothermic peaks at 1053°C and 1210°C.

PMS+5vol%ZrO2 yield=89.8%; PMS+5vol%Zr(OnPr)4 yield=82.0%. TGA measured up to 1450C under flowing argon at 5C/min.

Alkoxide-modified samples are X-ray amorphous at 1100C. At 1300C and above: crystallization of ZrO2 phases; SiOC matrix begins to decompose above 1300C forming SiC, SiO2, free C, and CO gas. ZrO2 incorporation improves thermal stability and crystallization resistance.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiOC matrix amorphous; monoclinic ZrO2 (m-ZrO2) and tetragonal ZrO2 (t-ZrO2) crystalline phases present in ZrO2-filled composites at 1100C; alkoxide-modified composites X-ray amorphous at 1100C

notes: Study focuses on SiOC/ZrO2 ceramic nanocomposites derived from polymethylsilsesquioxane (PMS, MK Belsil, Wacker GmbH). Two approaches: (1) PMS filled with ZrO2 nanoparticles (50 nm, 5-30 vol%) with 1 wt% Zr(acac)4 crosslinker; (2) PMS modified with Zr(OnPr)4 alkoxide (5-30 vol%). Bulk composites prepared by warm pressing then pyrolysis at 1100C/2h/Ar. Ceramic yield of pure PMS=86%; PMS+ZrO2=89.8%; PMS+Zr(OnPr)4=82.0%. Volume shrinkage of ZrO2-filled ceramics (28-40%) lower than pure PMS (55.16%); alkoxide-modified comparable to PMS (50-52%). Open porosity: ZrO2-filled 12-15%; alkoxide-modified 7-11%. Ceramic elemental compositions given in Tables III and IV. Annealing at 1300, 1400, 1600C/5h/Ar performed. ZrO2 incorporation markedly increases thermal stability against crystallization and decomposition above 1300C. ZrO2 particle sizes from Rietveld refinement: m-ZrO2 ~19-37 nm, t-ZrO2 ~13-27 nm in composites at various temperatures.
source: Polymer‐Derived SiOC_ZrO2 Ceramic Nanocomposites with Excellent High‐Temperature Stability

notes: Paper describes SiOC/HfO2 ceramic nanocomposites derived from commercially available polymethylsilsesquioxane (PMS, MK Belsil, Wacker GmbH) modified with hafnium tetra(n-butoxide) at volume fractions of 1-30 vol%. Pyrolysis temperatures ranged from 800 to 1300C (3 h hold) in argon. HfO2 grain size <5 nm at 1000C from TEM. 29Si MAS NMR identifies SiC3O, SiC2O2, SiCO3, SiO4, and SiC4 units evolving with temperature. Si-O-Hf bonds confirmed by FT-IR at 959 cm-1. Hafnia preferred over zirconia due to stability against t-m phase transformation up to >1600C. Open porosity values for bulk pellets: PMS 18.2%, 1HfOR_PMS 11.2%, 2HfOR_PMS 8.1%, 5HfOR_PMS 5.0%, 10HfOR_PMS 2.3%. HfO2 particle diameter noted as <5 nm at 1000C (midpoint used for grain_size_nm).

notes: Polymer is filled with Si (d50=7.6 um) and SiC (d50=16 um) acting as inert fillers below 1000 C. Foaming performed at 245 C for 2 h in air.
