backbone_architecture.description: Polymeric network composed of Si, B, N, C elements. Two main synthesis approaches: (1) monomer route - polymerization of specifically designed monomer units (e.g., boron linked to Si(Cl)x via C bridges, polymerized by ammonolysis); (2) polymer route - functionalization of a polysilazane backbone with boron via hydroboration. Also copolymer-type structures with borazine groups linked through silazane backbones.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous covalent Si-B-C-N ceramics formed at 800-1000°C. Boron addition stabilizes amorphous phase up to ~2000°C. Binary (SiC, Si3N4), ternary (Si-C-N), and quaternary (Si-B-C-N) phases possible depending on composition and temperature. Crystallization of thermodynamically stable phases occurs upon post-annealing at higher temperatures.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Si-C-N ceramics noted for excellent creep resistance; SiC noted for high compressive strength and high stiffness

notes: This is a comprehensive review paper covering 30 years of Si-B-C-N PDC (Polymer-Derived Ceramics) research; no single specific polymer is characterized. Key precursor types discussed include: polysilazanes, polycarbosilanes, polyborosilazanes, borazine-type compounds. Early precursor by Takamizawa et al. (mid-1980s) combined polysilane (Si-C bonds) and organoboron compound (B-N bonds) mixed and reacted by thermolysis below 500°C. Seyferth et al. reacted cyclic silazane oligomer with borane dimethylsulfide (BH3·S(CH3)2) to form low-melting white solid with borazine groups linked through silazane backbones. Chlorosilanes (SiRxCl4-x, 0≤x≤3) are primary molecular building blocks. Ammonolysis (reaction with NH3) is a key polymerization step for polysilazanes. The PDC route enables complex shapes including fibers, membranes, coatings, and porous supports. Si-C-N amorphous phase stabilized to ~1400°C; Si-B-C-N amorphous phase stabilized to ~2000°C.
source: Polymer Derived Si–B–C–N Ceramics- 30 Years of Research

polymer_name: poly(ferrocenylsilane) (PFS), poly(ferrosinylsilane), poly[(silylene)diacetylenes], polycarbosilane (PCS), poly[1,1-ferrocenylene(methyl)silyne], poly(ferrocenylethylmethylsilane) (PFEMS)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Fe (36-43 wt% estimated by EDX for hyperbranched system), Co, Ni, Pd, Pt, Cu, Ag, Au mentioned as dopants/modifiers

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-ferrocene linkages, acetylenic (C≡C) groups coordinated to Co2(CO)8, vinyl groups, Fe-Si bonding in ceramic phases (Fe3Si, Fe3Si5)

functional_groups.other: acetylenic/alkynyl groups, ferrocenyl groups, acetylacetonate (acac) ligands on metal complexes

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yields vary widely: 35-40% for early PFS (1,2) at 500°C/N2; 60-65% for Si-H/vinyl PFS (3,4) at 600°C/N2; above 90% for cross-linked spirocyclic silaferrocenophane under N2; 48-62% for hyperbranched poly[1,1-ferrocenylene(methyl)silyne] at 1000-1200°C; 72% and 59% at 600 and 900°C for bimetallic Fe/Co system; 70-85% for inverted opal structures; 30% for thin film PS-b-PFS. Heating rate of 5 K/min reported for earliest work (Yajima 1976).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (ring-opening polymerization), UV (cross-linking PS domains), catalytic (Pt-catalyzed hydrosilylation), chemical (shell cross-linking)

backbone_architecture.description: Multiple architectures described: linear poly(ferrocenylsilane), hyperbranched poly[1,1-ferrocenylene(methyl)silyne], cross-linked spirocyclic network from fcSi(CH2)3, diblock copolymers (PS-b-PFEMS, PS-b-PFS), cylindrical micelles from block copolymers, polymer microspheres

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC, Si3N4, SiCN, SiOC, amorphous SiC/C, Fe3Si, Fe3Si5, CoSi, Ni2Si, Pd3Si/Pd4Si, Pt3Si/Pt5Si, α-Fe, Fe2O3, Fe3O4, Cr7C3, CrSi2
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramics at <900°C tend to be amorphous; crystallization observed at higher temperatures. α-Fe nanoparticles form at 1000°C (ferromagnetic); smaller particles at <900°C show superparamagnetic behavior. β-SiC crystallizes at 1200°C. Pyrolysis under argon vs nitrogen changes phase composition (e.g., Fe3Si5 under argon).

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Ceramics described as electrically conductive with porous architecture of interconnected nanoclusters (hyperbranched system). Oxidation resistance noted for Fe-Cr/PCS system (no significant weight gain at 1000°C/50h in air).

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to crystalline depending on pyrolysis temperature
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: α-Fe, Fe3Si, Fe3Si5, Fe2O3, Fe3O4, SiC, Si3N4, CoSi, Ni2Si, Pd3Si, Pd4Si, Pt3Si, Pt5Si, Cr7C3, CrSi2, β-SiC, α-Fe2O3

notes: This is a review article (Chem. Soc. Rev., 2012, 41, 5102-5116) covering multiple polymer systems and ceramic products. Values reported here span multiple studies cited within the review. Grain sizes reported in Angstroms in the text: α-Fe nanoparticles range from ~15 to 700 Å (1.5–70 nm) depending on pyrolysis conditions; α-Fe nanoparticles of 20 Å (2 nm) found in MCM-41 channels. Ceramic nanolines as narrow as 8 nm reported. Fe/Co alloy nanoparticle rings with diameters 2-12 μm noted. The review focuses on late transition metals (groups 8-11: Fe, Co, Ni, Pd, Pt, Cu, Ag, Au) incorporated into SiC and SiCN PDC systems. Pyrolysis temperatures range from 500°C to 1400°C across different systems.
source: Polymer derived non-oxide ceramics modified with late transition metals†

elemental_composition.other_elements: PB45: [B3.0N3.0H4.8]n; PB50: [B3.0N3.8H4.0]n; PB60: [B3.0N3.5H4.5]n; oxygen values <2 wt% for all samples; B and N are primary elements

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-H bonds present; B-N bonds present (six-membered borazine rings); B-N-B linkages; BHN2 and BN3 boron sites; NHB2 and NB3 nitrogen sites identified by solid-state NMR; eight-membered rings in addition to six-membered borazine rings; biphenylic and naphthalenic-type structures formed during condensation

functional_groups.other: BH hydride on boron; NH units on nitrogen; borazine ring structure (planar six-membered hexagonal ring of alternating B and N)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed in nitrogen atmosphere up to 1000°C at 5°C/min. Weight losses: PB45=70%, PB50=53.2%, PB60=8.8%. Sneddon et al. reported ceramic yield 84-93% under argon or ammonia at 900-1450°C. BN stable in air up to 900°C (no weight change by TGA); above 900°C weight gain due to boron oxide formation. PB60 pyrolyzed to 1450°C yielded turbostratic BN (B3.0N2.95) with relative density 86.3%; annealing to 1800°C increased relative density to 93%.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - dehydrocoupling reactions during thermolysis/self-condensation of BH and NH units

backbone_architecture.description: Branched-chain or partially cross-linked structure based on elemental analyses. Contains biphenylic and naphthalenic-type structural units formed via condensation of BH and NH units. Also contains six-membered borazine rings and eight-membered rings. Physical state ranges from liquid (PB45, PB50) to solid (PB60) depending on thermolysis temperature (45-60°C). Soluble in polar solvents (THF, glyme).

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Turbostratic BN formed at 1450°C (B3.0N2.95); crystallinity increases with temperature up to 1800°C where h-BN with long-range preferred orientation is obtained. XRD confirmed poor crystallization at low pyrolysis temperatures; crystallinity improves significantly above 1200°C. BN nanotubes showed turbostratic structure crystallizing above 1200°C. Sneddon et al. reported turbostratic BN structure at 900-1450°C under argon/ammonia.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Hardness 8 Hv (78 MPa) for BN from spray-pyrolysis + SPS sintering at 1840°C. C/BN composites: relative density 94.7%, open porosity 5.1 vol%. Warm-pressing of PB60 under 74 MPa at 60°C used for shaping monoliths. Thermal conductivity of bulk BN: 3.26 W/m/°C at 1450°C preparation, 6.56 W/m/°C at 1800°C preparation.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Turbostratic BN at lower temperatures (1450°C); hexagonal BN (h-BN) with increasing crystallinity at higher temperatures (1600-1800°C). XRD used to track (002) peak for interlayer spacing d002 via Bragg's law. Crystallite sizes Lc and La calculated from Scherrer relation.

notes: This paper is a review focused on polymer-derived BN ceramics from borazine derivatives (polyborazylene and poly[B-tri(methylamino)borazine]). The polymer is a poly(borazylene) - a boron-nitrogen polymer with no silicon content; the polymer_type field 'polyborosilazane' is not strictly accurate but is the closest available descriptor - it should properly be called a polyborazylene or boron-nitrogen preceramic polymer. Three polyborazylene grades reported: PB45 (liquid, very volatile, thermolyzed at 45°C), PB50 (liquid, volatile, 50°C), PB60 (solid, 60°C). Ceramic yields from Sneddon et al. were 84-93%. Weight losses in table refer to TGA up to 1000°C in N2 at 5°C/min and are not ceramic yields directly. Pyrolysis temperatures range from 900°C to 1800°C in different studies. Economy et al. viscous polyborazylene formula: B3.0N3.6H3.7. Disk-shaped BN relative density: 86.3% at 1450°C, 93% at 1800°C. BN nanopowder sintering at 1840°C under N2 gave 96.3% relative density. Polymer synthesis via self-condensation in autoclave under argon or nitrogen at 45-70°C.
source: Polymer-Derived Boron Nitride- A Review on the Chemistry, Shaping and Ceramic Conversion of Borazine Derivatives

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-C bonds present in SiOC glasses derived from polysiloxanes and polysilsesquioxanes; B-containing bonds in polyborosiloxane systems

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups present in polysilastyrene and methylphenylsilylene-containing PSH; glycidoxy groups in GPTMOS-based systems

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PSHs gave poor ceramic residue of 5-25%; PSHs heat treated at 420 degrees C gave ceramic residue of 40-85% at 900 degrees C. PCS heat treated in inert atmosphere gives amorphous SiC at ~800 degrees C, converting to beta-SiC above 1200 degrees C. Alkoxysilane-derived polymers showed ceramic residues ranging from 42 to 87 wt% at 900 degrees C depending on monomer type.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal, UV, chemical

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC/MALDI implied by table data for alkoxysilane-derived polymers; individual polymer Mn/Mw values range: Mn 1040-2420, Mw 1560-9840 g/mol for alkoxysilane systems tabulated

backbone_architecture.description: Polysiloxanes can be linear or cross-linked networks depending on functionality of side chains. Branched polysilanes and polycarbosilanes also described. Polysilsesquioxanes prepared via sol-gel process form network structures.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC, Si3N4, SiCN, SiOC, SiBC, SiOBC, SiBCN, beta-SiC
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCS gives amorphous SiC at ~800 degrees C, beta-SiC above 1200 degrees C. Carbon-rich PCS gives beta-SiC with nanodomains of carbon. Metal-modified PCS gives mixed non-oxide ceramics of metal carbide and beta-SiC or SiMCO. Polysiloxanes and polysilsesquioxanes give SiOC glasses.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Flexural strength of CMC samples: 145-173 MPa (CMC-1 to CMC-3). SiC fiber-reinforced CMC flexural strength: 236 MPa at RT, 264 MPa at 1000 degrees C. Tensile strength 153 MPa at RT, 142 MPa at 1000 degrees C. Carbon-rich SiOC glasses have superior creep resistance compared to fused SiO2.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to crystalline upon heat treatment
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC identified above 1200 degrees C; amorphous ceramic below 800-1200 degrees C

notes: This is a broad review paper covering multiple preceramic polymer systems for space applications including CMCs, protective coatings, ceramic adhesives, and lightweight ceramics. Grain size range given as 3-10 nm for beta-SiC crystallites from PCS; midpoint 6.5 nm used. Molecular weight data from table for alkoxysilane-derived polysiloxane/polysilsesquioxane systems: Mn ranges from 1040 (VTEOS+PTEOS 1:1) to 2420 (VTEOS+MTEOS 1:1), Mw ranges from 1560 to 9840 g/mol, PDI ranges from 1.24 to 4.07. Ceramic residues at 900 degrees C for alkoxysilane systems range from 42% (GPTMOS) to 87% (VTEOS+MTEOS 1:1). Atomic oxygen resistant polysiloxane coatings demonstrated on Aluminized Kapton and composite substrates. BMV (VTEOS+MTEOS) system gave highest flexural strength of 265 MPa for CMC, 285 MPa with BN-coated carbon fiber.
source: Polymer-Derived Ceramics and Their Space Applications

polymer_name: Ceraset (PUMVS), Nicalon NL-200, Hi-Nicalon, HPZ (hybridopolysilazane), N-methylpolyborosilazane

elemental_composition.other_elements: Nicalon NL-200 composition: Si0.566C0.317O0.117; Hi-Nicalon composition: Si0.624C0.371O0.005; SiZrCNO fiber composition: SiZr0.13C0.46N0.785O0.69; SiBCN fiber composition: Si3.0B1.0C5.0N2.4

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si and Si-O-C bonds formed during oxidation curing; Si-B bonds present in borosilazane systems; B-N bonds in borazine derivatives

functional_groups.other: borazine, pinacolborane (PIN), 1,3-dimethyl-1,3-diaza-2-boracyclopentane (BCP), 2,4-diethylborazine (DEB), aluminum acetylacetonate, zirconium alkoxides, titanium alkoxides

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: SiBCN fibers showed only 2.9% weight increase during oxidation treatment from 1100C to 1500C. Various pyrolysis temperatures reported: 1000C for SiZrCNO fibers, 1200C for SiC and SiBCN fibers, 1300C for SiAlCO fibers, 1400C for SiBCN fibers, 1700C for Si-Ti-C-O fibers. SiBCN ceramics retain amorphous structure up to 1600C and even 2200C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal oxidation in air (100-200C), electron beam irradiation in He gas, chemical curing with HSiCl3 followed by humid air exposure, heating to 200C in NH3 atmosphere, room temperature crosslinking via hydrolysis

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Yajima polycarbosilane reported ~1500 Da molecular weight; Ceraset average molecular weight ~400 Da

backbone_architecture.description: Preceramic polymers range from linear/branched spinnable forms to three-dimensional crosslinked networks. Ceraset (PUMVS) is an oligosilazane that forms 3D crosslinked unspinnable product upon further polymerization via vinyl group crosslinking. Boron-containing polymers modified to reduce crosslinking degree for melt-spinnability. Polysilazanes synthesized via ammonolysis or aminolysis of chlorosilanes.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC, SiCO, SiCN, SiBCN, SiAlCO, Si-Ti-C-O
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiCO fibers contain beta-SiC nanocrystals, free carbon, and amorphous silicon oxycarbide (SiCxOy). SiC fibers contain beta-SiC crystals, glassy carbon, and small amount of SiCxOy. SiBCN ceramics retain amorphous structure at 1600C; granular texture appears at 1750C due to amorphous-to-crystalline transition. Carbon hinders crystallization of SiO2 and Si3N4 up to 1500C. Boron-containing SiCN crystallizes around 1700C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Hi-Nicalon and Nicalon NL-200 tensile strength ~3 GPa, tensile modulus ~270 GPa at room temperature. Si-Ti-C-O fibers: tensile strength 3 GPa, elastic modulus 300 GPa. SiZrCNO fibers: tensile strength 2.2-2.8 GPa, Young's modulus 160-190 GPa. SiBCN fibers (Bernard): 1.5 GPa at room temperature, 1.3 GPa at 1600C. Sintered SiC (SiAlCO-derived): tensile strength >2.5 GPa, tensile modulus >300 GPa.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC, TiC-type phase, BN precipitates, Al2O3, SiO2, silicon oxynitride (SiON), silicon oxycarbonitride (SiCON), SiBCNO glass

notes: This is a review article covering multiple polymer precursor systems and ceramic fiber types. Values reported are from various cited studies and not a single polymer system. Fiber diameters: Yajima SiC ~20 um, PIN-HPZ SiBCN ~30-40 um, Bernard SiBCN ~18 um (green), 8-10 um (ceramic), SiZrCNO ~10-60 um. Melt-spinning and electrospinning both discussed as fiber fabrication routes. Oxidation curing introduces ~7 wt% oxygen; electron beam curing introduces <1% oxygen. Ceraset (PUMVS) molecular weight ~400 Da. Yajima polycarbosilane molecular weight ~1500 Da. Modulus range for SiZrCNO: 160-190 GPa (midpoint 175 GPa used). Strength range for SiZrCNO: 2.2-2.8 GPa (midpoint 2.5 GPa).
source: Polymer-Derived Non-Oxide Ceramic Fibers-Past Present and Future

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental analysis given in weight percent not atomic percent. Sample 1 (thermally crosslinked neat): Si 40.95%, N 19.36%, C 32.51%, O 6.65%. Sample 2 (Pt-catalyzed): Si 39.88%, N 17.90%, C 33.02%, O 6.62%, other 0.80%. Sample 3 (KH-treated): Si 39.46%, N 18.07%, C 33.48%, O 7.05%. Pyrolyzed ceramic samples (Table VI): Si ~45-47%, C ~29-30%, N ~20-22%, H ~0.1-0.5%, O ~1-4.6%.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH=CH2 (vinyl), sp3 C after hydrosilylation via alpha and beta addition modes producing CH2, CH, and CH3 groups; (sp3C)(sp3C)SiN2 sites from duplicate hydrosilylation observed by 29Si NMR near -3 ppm

functional_groups.other: NH groups in cyclic silazane ring; latent reactivity from SiH and vinyl coexistence enabling hydrosilylation and dehydrocoupling crosslinking

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yields always over 80%. Three pyrolyzed samples reported with yields of 83%, 85%, and 84% (midpoint 84%). Pyrolysis conditions not fully specified in provided text.

crosslink_density.value: Monitored via SiH+vinyl content (meq/g) decreasing from ~28 meq/g initially; specific crosslink density value not reported numerically
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (hydrosilylation), catalytic (hexachloroplatinic acid H2PtCl6 promoting hydrosilylation), chemical/catalytic (KH-promoted dehydrocoupling forming SiN bonds from SiH and NH)

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Size exclusion chromatography (SEC/GPC). OVSZ prepared in toluene: Mn ~310-390, Mw ~420-660 depending on solvent; typical values ca. 350 and 570 daltons. After thermal crosslinking in toluene for 72 hr: Mn 840, Mw 8400.

backbone_architecture.description: Primarily cyclic oligomers (cyclotetramer as major species confirmed by mass spectrum). IR confirms no terminal NH groups, supporting cyclic structure. Slight transamination observed (NH/SiH ratio ~0.93-0.96). Upon crosslinking, branched/network structures form via hydrosilylation and/or dehydrocoupling.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolyzed ceramics contain Si, C, N, H, O (Table VI). Ceramic phase is SiCN-type based on elemental composition. No explicit phase identification (XRD) described in provided text.

notes: Polymer is based on monomeric unit (-ViHSiNH-)n, prepared by ammonolysis of vinyldichlorosilane (ViHSiCl2) in various solvents (THF, ether, toluene, hexane). Yields 74-90%. OVSZ in toluene used for subsequent studies. Three crosslinking routes described: (1) thermal neat at 110C (insoluble in 2 hr), (2) Pt-catalyzed (H2PtCl6/2-ethylhexanol) at 110C (insoluble in 1 hr), (3) KH (7%) in THF at room temperature (dehydrocoupling, vinyl unreacted). 29Si NMR chemical shifts: (sp2C)HSiN2 from -24 to -31 ppm; (sp3C)(sp3C)SiN2 near -3 ppm (duplicate hydrosilylation); (sp3C)HSiN2 from -17 to -23 ppm; (sp3C)SiN3 from -33 to -35 ppm. Authors: Choong Kwet Yive et al., Universite de Montpellier II, 1990. Table VI ceramic sample ASi values 1.6-4.5%.
source: PolyvinylsilazaneANovelPrecursortoSiliconCarbonitride

polymer_name: PND/PMCS and PND/AHPCS blends; poly(norbornenyldecaborane) (PND), poly(methylcarbosilane) (PMCS), allylhydridopolycarbosilane (AHPCS)

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present; ceramic elemental compositions vary by blend ratio and pyrolysis temperature. Example PND/PMCS (2.55:1, 1300C): 18.3% Si, 42.8% B, 37.4% C. Example PND/AHPCS (2.63:1, 1650C): 20.74% Si, 42.72% B, 31.58% C.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-H bonds present in PND component; B-H and Si-H units still present at 400C but absent at 600C during pyrolysis of 1.21:1 PND/PMCS blend

functional_groups.other: Allyl groups present in AHPCS; norbornene groups in PND; boron-containing decaborane units in PND

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA ramp rate 10C/min to 1200C under ultra-high purity argon at 80 mL/min purge. Pure PND: 72% char yield, two-step conversion starting ~150C then ~250C. Pure PMCS: 73% char yield, single-step loss complete by 800C, stable above 200C. Pure AHPCS: 71% char yield, two-step conversion starting ~230C then ~460C. PND/PMCS blends: 83-86% char yield at 1200C. PND/AHPCS blends: 78-84% char yield at 1200C. Bulk pyrolysis hold time 1-2h for PND/PMCS, 8h for PND/AHPCS. PND/PMCS bulk char yields at 1600C and PND/AHPCS at 1650C were 10-20% lower than TGA yields at 1200C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal; interpolymer cross-linking reactions inferred from higher-than-individual-component char yields during ceramic conversion

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with light scattering detector for blend confirmation; Mw 3500 stated for PMCS (Aldrich); PND reported as ~30 kDa

backbone_architecture.description: Physical blends of two separate preceramic polymers. GPC confirmed no chemical reaction during blending, only physical mixing. PND is a high-molecular-weight (~30 kDa) polymer enabling electrostatic spinning. PMCS Mw ~3500. AHPCS is a liquid at low PND ratios.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Materials pyrolyzed to 1000C largely amorphous. beta-SiC crystallization onset at 1200-1300C (peaks at 2theta=35.7, 60.1, 72.0 deg). B4C crystallization onset at higher temperatures (peak at 2theta=37.8 deg). Residual free carbon present in PND/PMCS ceramics; much lower in PND/AHPCS ceramics; absent in 0.22:1 and 0.44:1 PND/AHPCS ceramics. Graphitic layer (interlayer spacing 0.35 nm) observed encapsulating beta-SiC nanocrystallites.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to semi-crystalline depending on pyrolysis temperature
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (JCPDS #73-1665) and B4C (JCPDS #35-0798); beta-SiC crystallization onset 1200-1300C; B4C crystallization onset above 1300C

notes: Paper describes blends of PND (boron-carbide precursor) with PMCS or AHPCS (silicon-carbide precursors) to form SiC/B4C/C ceramic composites. Ceramic density increases with pyrolysis temperature: ranges from ~1.78-2.08 g/cm3 at 1000C to ~2.29-2.42 g/cm3 at 1600-1650C for PND/PMCS; 1.93-2.66 g/cm3 for PND/AHPCS. PND/AHPCS-derived ceramics showed significant oxidation resistance up to 1200C, especially at low PND/AHPCS ratios (char 13 from 0.22:1 and char 16 from 1.21:1). PND/PMCS blends were electrostatically spun into nonwoven fiber mats (25-31 wt% in THF, 11-15 kV, 1.0 mL/h, 15 cm distance) and pyrolyzed to ceramic fibers. TGA oxidation experiments performed under dry breathing air at 5C/min to 1200C. TEM showed beta-SiC nanocrystallites of ~5-15 nm diameter with interlayer spacing 0.27 nm embedded in amorphous matrix at 1300C. Ceramic compositions are tunable by adjusting PND:PMCS or PND:AHPCS ratios. B4C to SiC ratio in ceramic increases as PND ratio increases.
source: Preceramic Polymer Blends as Precursors for Boron-Carbide:Silicon-Carbide Composite Ceramics and Ceramic Fibers

polymer_name: Nicalon polycarbosilane, Bayer carbosilazane resin, poly(methylsilazane), Tyranno (Ti-modified polycarbosilane)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ti present in Tyranno variant; nominal molar composition of Nicalon fibers: 1 SiC : 0.78 C : 0.22 SiO2

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si backbone in poly(dimethylsilane) precursor converted to Si-CH2 backbone in polycarbosilane; Si-N bonds noted as thermally labile in carbosilazane

functional_groups.other: CH2 and CH bridging units in polycarbosilane backbone; methylamine and ammonia used as reagents in silazane synthesis

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Nicalon polycarbosilane pyrolyzed to 1200C giving ceramic fibers; Bayer carbosilazane pyrolyzed to 1500C giving 45 wt% yield amorphous ceramic fibers; crystallization of beta-SiC and alpha-SiC and beta-Si3N4 observed at 1800C; Ti-modified polycarbosilane (Tyranno) gave >70% ceramic yield vs ~60% for unmodified; crystallization of beta-SiC and TiC at 1700C; above 1200C in Nicalon fibers, SiC crystallization and grain growth occur with strength loss

crosslink_density.value: qualitative - Ti-alkoxide crosslinked polymer described as more highly crosslinked than base polycarbosilane
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (cure in air at 110-190C for green fibers); chemical (titanium alkoxide (n-C4H9O)4Ti crosslinking of polycarbosilane); moisture cure in air for carbosilazane fibers at 110C for 20h

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC; Mn range 1250-1750 for Yajima polycarbosilanes; Mw up to 4222 reported by Penn et al. for carbosilazane resin

backbone_architecture.description: Nonuniformly crosslinked network polymers; contain both linear and cyclic components; carbosilazane has Si-N backbone; polycarbosilane has Si-CH2 backbone derived from rearrangement of Si-Si backbone of poly(dimethylsilane)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Bayer carbosilazane -> amorphous at 1500C, beta-SiC + alpha-SiC + beta-Si3N4 at 1800C; Nicalon polycarbosilane -> SiC + free C + SiO2 (amorphous); Tyranno -> amorphous Si/Ti/C/O at 1200C, beta-SiC + TiC at 1700C; Verbeek carbosilane resin -> SiC + ~10 wt% free carbon (amorphous by XRD); poly(methylsilazane) -> silicon carbonitride

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Nicalon fibers: tensile strength 2500-3200 MPa (midpoint 2850 MPa), Young's modulus 180-200 GPa (midpoint 190 GPa); Tyranno fibers: Young's modulus 220 GPa, high temperature strength superior to Nicalon; Nicalon fiber diameter 10-20 micrometers

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC, alpha-SiC, beta-Si3N4 (Bayer carbosilazane at 1800C); beta-SiC + TiC (Tyranno at 1700C); SiC amorphous at lower temperatures; Verbeek carbosilane ceramic amorphous by XRD

notes: This is a review paper on preceramic polymer chemistry covering multiple polymer systems including polycarbosilanes (Nicalon, Tyranno), polysilazanes, and carbosilazane resins. Tables at the beginning list ceramic yields and XRD results for metal-silicon ceramic systems (Ti, Zr, V, Nb, Mo, W) under various M:Si ratios, likely from a related section not fully reproduced. Ceramic yields from tables: TiN+SiC (72%), ZrN+SiC (82%), V5Si3+SiC (54%), NbC+NbSi2 (80%), MoSi2+Mo5Si3 (73%), Mo5Si3 (80%), WC+WSi2+W5Si3+SiC (87%), WC+W5Si3 (93%). Mn range of 1250-1750 noted as midpoint 1500 in molecular_weight field; Mw of 4222 is maximum reported. Tensile strength range 2500-3200 MPa, midpoint 2850 used. Young's modulus range 180-200 GPa, midpoint 190 used.
source: Preceramic Polymers 2

polymer_name: SILRES MK (MK), H62C, H44, PMS, YR3370

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Polysilsesquioxanes have Si bonded to 1.5 oxygen atoms per Si unit ([RSiO3/2]n backbone); silanol groups (-OH) present in partial-cage and random structures

functional_groups.other: Phenyl, ethoxy, hydroxyl (silanol) groups possible as R substituents on Si; organic functional groups depend on specific polysilsesquioxane grade

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: air (for silicate/SiO2 ceramics); nitrogen or argon for SiOC ceramics
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yield above 60% is expected after pyrolysis. Volume shrinkage up to 70% can occur due to density difference between polymer (1-1.2 g/cm3) and ceramic phases (2-3.2 g/cm3). Pyrolysis in air results in SiO2 residue; inert atmosphere yields SiOC and residual carbon. Sintering at 1550 C for 2.5 h achieved complete mullitization. Pyrolysis temperatures cited range from 800-1200 C generally, up to 1350-1550 C for specific silicate phases.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal crosslinking; sol-gel hydrolysis and condensation; ring opening polymerization

backbone_architecture.description: Polysilsesquioxanes ([RSiO3/2]n) can adopt random, ladder, double-decker, cage, and partial-cage structures. Random structures lack long-range order; ladder structures have alternating Si and O atoms in oligomeric scale; cage structures are fully crosslinked with no silanol groups; partial-cage structures retain silanol groups at one or more corners. Polysiloxanes have general formula [R2SiO]n.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC (inert atmosphere); SiO2 (air atmosphere); silicate ceramics including mullite, wollastonite, cordierite, forsterite, zircon, hardystonite, akermanite, and others when active fillers are used
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Mullitization at 1250 C yielded 96% volume fraction mullite (3Al2O3·2SiO2) from MK + nano gamma-Al2O3; increased to 99.5% above 1350 C. Complete mullitization at 1550 C with only 0.1% residual silicate glass. Low grain size silicate ceramics achieved at low sintering temperatures using nanoactive fillers. Submicron porosity appears between densified areas due to poor ionic interdiffusion.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Carbon-rich SiOC glasses show significantly improved creep resistance compared to fused SiO2. SiCN ceramics demonstrated significant strength and elastic modulus with oxidation resistance up to 1200 C. Compressive strengths of 3D-printed porous silicate scaffolds ranged from 0.6 MPa to 8.19 MPa depending on composition and porosity (see table data).

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to crystalline depending on processing
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Mullite (3Al2O3·2SiO2), cristobalite (reported absent in nano-alumina study), SiOC glass, hardystonite (Ca2ZnSi2O7), akermanite (Ca2MgSi2O7), biosilicate glass-ceramic, zircon, forsterite, wollastonite, cordierite, gehlenite, willemite, beta-SiAlON, yttrium silicates

notes: This is a review paper covering multiple preceramic polymer types and their use in additive manufacturing of silicate ceramics. The primary focus is on polysiloxane (SILRES MK, H62C, H44, PMS) and polysilsesquioxanes used with active fillers (gamma-Al2O3, CaCO3, MgO, ZnO, ZrO2, etc.) to produce silicate ceramics via pyrolysis in air at 800-1550 C. Ceramic yield threshold cited as >60%. Porosity values for 3D-printed scaffolds range from 56-80 vol%. Compressive strengths for porous scaffolds range from 0.6 to 8.19 MPa. Mullitization study used nano gamma-Al2O3 (average particle size 15 nm) with SILRES MK. General pyrolysis temperature range for oxide/non-oxide ceramics stated as 800-1200 C. Sintering at 1550 C for 2.5 h (150 min hold) cited for complete mullitization. Ceramic yield of 60% is stated as a minimum expectation, not a measured value for a specific polymer.
source: Preceramic Polymers for Additive Manufacturing of Silicate Ceramics

polymer_name: SL 680, SPR 688, SPR 212 (Starfire Systems / Polyramic brand)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Curing step performed at 200 degrees C at 5 degrees C/min over 60 min before pyrolysis. Cooling rate after pyrolysis was 10 degrees C/min. Cracks noted near voids due to evaporation of volatile elements during sintering.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (curing at 200 degrees C with 2% platinum catalyst)

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC (SL 680 noted to contain SiC fillers)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SL 680 contains SiC filler which contributes to lower void fraction and higher mechanical properties compared to SPR 688. Voids and cracks observed in all samples after pyrolysis at 900 degrees C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Composite mechanical properties vary by fibre type and infiltration: without SPR 212 infiltration, compressive strength ranges 2.5-5.5 MPa and elastic modulus 3-5 GPa; with SPR 212 infiltration, compressive strength ranges 13-73 MPa, elastic modulus 6-76 GPa, hardness 6-7 GPa. Void fraction without infiltration: 11.25-31.76%; with infiltration: 2.54-8.65%.

notes: Three polysiloxane resins (SL 680, SPR 688, SPR 212) from Starfire Systems (USA) are used. A 2% platinum catalyst is used to aid curing and reduce gas bubbles. Carbon fibre and glass fibre (S2) are used as reinforcements. Fibre mass fractions: carbon fibre/SL 680 = 36%, carbon fibre/SPR 688 = 53%, glass fibre/SL 680 = 52%, glass fibre/SPR 688 = 61%. PIP process employed with optional SPR 212 vacuum infiltration to reduce porosity. Hardness measured by nanoindentation per ASTM C1327-15. Paper focuses on composite fabrication and mechanical performance rather than polymer chemistry details.
source: Preceramic polymer composite- Fabrication process and mechanical performance

elemental_composition.other_elements: Molar ratios Si:O:C:H = 1:1.51:4.03:4.06 (not atomic percent); formula [(C6H5)0.62(CH3)0.31(OR)0.07SiO1.5]n with n approximately 20

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-OH (silanol/hydroxy groups), Si-OC2H5 (ethoxy groups), Si-O-Si crosslinks formed during curing; phenyl groups (C6H5) attached to Si

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups (C6H5), hydroxy groups (-OH), ethoxy groups (-OC2H5)

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: argon or nitrogen or air (multiple conditions studied; filler-free foams pyrolysed at 1000 C in argon; quartz-filled foams pyrolysed at 1200 C in nitrogen or air)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis in air led to oxidation of carbon and hydrogen; ceramic residue was amorphous SiO2, crystalline quartz and cristobalite with <2 wt% residual carbon. Pyrolysis in nitrogen led to >40 wt% residual carbon (relative to polymer fraction) and nanocrystalline SiC. Heating rate 3 C/min to 500 C with 2 h hold, then 5 C/min to 1200 C, hold 4 h, cool at 5 C/min.

crosslink_density.value: Degree of curing alpha = w(tp)/w(infinity); varied by pre-heating at 200 C for 1, 2, or 8 h; alpha < 0.5 considered low degree of curing
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

backbone_architecture.description: Poly(silsesquioxane) with general formula [(C6H5)0.62(CH3)0.31(OR)0.07SiO1.5]n, n~20; solid powder at room temperature, melting interval 40-60 C; crosslinks form via condensation of hydroxy and ethoxy groups with silanol groups above 200 C producing Si-O-Si intermolecular crosslinks

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC (amorphous Si-C-O); also SiO2 (amorphous and crystalline quartz/cristobalite) when quartz filler added; nanocrystalline SiC formed in nitrogen atmosphere
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Filler-free pyrolysis in inert atmosphere gives amorphous or partly crystalline Si-C-O. Quartz-filled pyrolysis in air gives amorphous SiO2, crystalline quartz and cristobalite (<2 wt% C). Quartz-filled pyrolysis in nitrogen gives significant residual carbon (>40 wt% of polymer fraction) and nanocrystalline SiC (below XRD detection). Cristobalite forms above 900 C from poly(silsesquioxane) residue.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Ceramic foam compression strength: 860 +/- 135 kPa (nitrogen pyrolysis) and 198 +/- 173 kPa (air pyrolysis). Young's modulus of foam: 19.1 +/- 6.1 MPa (nitrogen) and 8.6 +/- 2.6 MPa (air). IPC composite elastic moduli and strengths reported in table (e.g., SiO2 foam/AZ91 at 25 C: E=62 GPa, sigma_f=245 MPa).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Quartz, cristobalite (in air-pyrolysed quartz-filled samples); nanocrystalline SiC (in nitrogen-pyrolysed samples, below XRD detection limit); MgO, Mg2Si, Al12Mg17 in IPC reaction products

notes: Polymer density 1.0 g/cm3. Foaming occurs at 270 C via condensation of hydroxy and ethoxy groups releasing water and ethanol as blowing agents. Pre-curing at 200 C for 1 h gives 89% total porosity; 2 h gives 81%; 8 h gives 30%. Quartz filler (weight ratio polymer:filler = 2:3, volume fraction 0.6) reduced linear shrinkage from ~16% to ~1%. Strut density 2.24 g/cm3 (quartz-filled, air pyrolysis) and 2.21 g/cm3 (quartz-filled, nitrogen pyrolysis). Filler-free strut density 1.35 g/cm3 (nitrogen, 1000 C). Mean cell diameter ~1.2 mm, mean strut thickness 130 +/- 50 um for quartz-filled foam. IPCs fabricated by squeeze casting with Mg alloys AZ31 and AZ91 at 680 C, 86 MPa.
source: Preceramic polymer derived cellular ceramics

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental composition reported as weight% from EDX on pyrolyzed ceramics (not the polymer itself): for 50% RB sample - C 13.26 wt%, O 41.30 wt%, Si 45.44 wt%; for 60% RB - C 12.69 wt%, O 41.47 wt%, Si 45.84 wt%; for 70% RB - C 12.56 wt%, O 41.32 wt%, Si 46.12 wt%; for 80% RB - C 10.47 wt%, O 43.14 wt%, Si 46.39 wt%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Hydroxyl and ethoxy groups present that undergo cross-linking at 150-250 degrees C liberating water and ethyl alcohol; polysilsesquioxane-type T-unit structure (CH3SiO1.5)n

functional_groups.other: Hydroxyl groups, ethoxy groups

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA conducted to 800 degrees C at 5 degrees C/min under nitrogen. Silres 610 alone starts losing weight at 180 degrees C in three stages: RT-260, 260-465, and 465-800 degrees C. Composites with RB start losing weight from 45 degrees C due to moisture absorbed by RB. Total weight loss at 800 degrees C for 50/60/70/80 wt% RB composites was 52.2/58.8/66.3/73.1% respectively. DTA shows peaks at 270 and 495 degrees C for Silres 610 alone. Ceramic yield of Silres 610 alone estimated at 85% based on theoretical calculations.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

molecular_weight.measurement_method: reported from manufacturer technical data sheet

backbone_architecture.description: Polysilsesquioxane-type resin with formula (CH3SiO1.5)n; T-unit based methyl silicone resin; solid at room temperature with Tg = 41.6 degrees C and melting point 35-55 degrees C; bulk density 650 kg/m3; crosslinks via hydroxyl and ethoxy condensation reactions

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOC ceramic produced by pyrolysis at 900 degrees C. XRD performed (2-theta 10-100 degrees) but specific phase identification details not explicitly stated in extracted text. Ceramics described as amorphous. Porous structure retained after pyrolysis.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Compressive strength values for porous ceramics (Silres 610/RB ratios): 50/50 = 2.7 MPa, 40/60 = 2.43 MPa, 30/70 = 1.84 MPa, 20/80 = 1.73 MPa. Effect of crosslinking temperature on 50/50 composite: 150 degrees C = 0.92 MPa, 200 degrees C = 1.76 MPa, 250 degrees C = 2.7 MPa. Hygroscopic expansion negligible for all samples; highest expansion 0.36% for 80% RB sample after 72 h soaking.

notes: Paper focuses on porous SiOC ceramics derived from Silres 610 (methyl silicone resin, polysilsesquioxane) blended with rice bran (RB) as a sacrificial porogen. Blending ratios of Silres 610/RB: 50/50, 40/60, 30/70, 20/80 wt%. Crosslinking at 250 degrees C under 20 MPa in compression mold (heating rate 2 degrees C/min, hold 30 min). Pyrolysis at 900 degrees C (heating rate 2 degrees C/min, hold 2 h, cooling at 10 degrees C/min). Ceramic yields: 47.80% (50% RB), 41.20% (60% RB), 33.70% (70% RB), 26.90% (80% RB). Porosity estimated: 45.8%, 44.4%, 36.2%, 30.0% respectively. Volume shrinkage: 48.1-53.9%. Elemental EDX data is for the ceramic product not the raw polymer. PDI value of 3.2 from manufacturer datasheet (Mw/Mn). Polymer formula given as (CH3SiO1.5)n.
source: Preparation and characterisation of Sisingle bondOsingle bondC ceramics made from a preceramic polymer and rice bran

polymer_name: PCS (polycarbosilane, Suzhou Sailifei Ceramic Fiber Co., Ltd.)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C-C, C-Si, C-O bonds identified by XPS in C1s; Si-C and Si-N bonds in Si2p

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - crosslinked at 180°C for 2 h

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC, Si3N4, free carbon (amorphous), Al2O3; also SiC whiskers formed in situ
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Beta-SiC identified by XRD at 35.8°, 60.12°, 71.9°; free carbon at 26.55°; SiC whiskers formed via Si-O-C bond cleavage and carbothermal reduction; free carbon content and SiC content increase with PIP cycle number; in situ SiC whiskers shorten from needle-shaped to near-spherical with increasing PIP cycles

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Green body open porosity: 51.34%

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC, Si3N4 (alpha phase >93 wt%), Al2O3; after sol infiltration: TiO2 (S-T), AlPO4 (S-P)

notes: This paper focuses on PDC-SiC/Si3N4 composites for electromagnetic wave absorption prepared by SLS 3D printing followed by PIP (precursor infiltration and pyrolysis) using polycarbosilane (PCS) as the preceramic polymer. PIP was repeated 2-8 times. Raman spectroscopy showed D-band (~1340 cm-1) and G-band (~1578 cm-1) with ID/IG increasing from 1.468 (S-2) to 2.079 (S-8), indicating increasing defect density and amorphization of free carbon with more PIP cycles. Sol infiltration with Al2O3, TiO2, and Al(H2PO4)3 was performed post-PIP to tune dielectric properties. Best EMW absorption: S-4 showed RLmin of -46.79 dB at ~8 GHz, 2.4 mm thickness, EAB ~1.44 GHz; TiO2 and AlPO4 sol infiltration expanded EAB to 4.08 GHz and 3.52 GHz respectively. The polymer precursor (PCS) details beyond crosslinking temperature and pyrolysis conditions are not provided in the text.
source: Preparation and electromagnetic wave absorption properties of PDC–SiC:Si3N4 composites using selective laser sintering and infiltration technology

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA was conducted for debinding at 5 C/min from 50 to 800 C in argon atmosphere. Sintering performed at 1450 C for 2 h in air atmosphere. This paper is not about preceramic polymers but about ceramic slurry stability for stereolithography 3D printing of yttria-stabilized zirconia.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Yttria-stabilized zirconia powder used as ceramic filler in slurry for SLA printing; sintered at 1450 C for 2 h in air

notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. It concerns the preparation and stability of yttria-stabilized zirconia ceramic slurries for stereolithography (SLA) 3D printing. The photosensitive resin used is a mixture of 1,6-hexanediol diacrylate and TPO photoinitiator, not a preceramic polymer. No preceramic polymer descriptors are applicable. All preceramic polymer fields are null.
source: Preparation of High-Stability Ceramic Slurry with Gel Behavior for Stereolithography 3D Printing

polymer_name: THC-400 solid phenolic resin (PRIP resin); self-developed resole-type phenolic resin binder (BJ binder)

functional_groups.other: phenolic resin (resole-type); hydroxyl and aromatic ring functionality implied by phenolic resin chemistry

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TG-DTA conducted at 10 C/min under argon. Curing temperature identified as 190 C; carbonization temperature identified as 1000 C. BJ binder char yield: 37.89 wt%. PRIP resin (THC-400) char yield: 46.15 wt%.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - cured at 190 C for 2 h

backbone_architecture.description: Resole-type phenolic resin used as binder; THC-400 solid phenolic resin used for PRIP impregnation. No further structural details provided.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Final Si-SiC composites contain alpha-SiC (starting material), secondary beta-SiC (formed by reaction of liquid Si with pyrolytic carbon during LSI), and residual silicon. PRIP2 sample had lowest residual silicon content (10.2 vol%) and almost no residual carbon. Rietveld analysis used to determine phase volume fractions from XRD.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Highest flexural strength 257 +/- 14.26 MPa (3-point bending, 30 mm span, 0.5 mm/min) for PRIP2 Si-SiC composites. Green part compressive strength up to 7.7 +/- 0.3 MPa at 0.15 mm layer thickness. Wear resistance best for PRIP2 samples.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: alpha-SiC, beta-SiC, residual Si

notes: This paper primarily concerns binder jetting of SiC ceramics followed by phenolic resin impregnation and pyrolysis (PRIP) and liquid silicon infiltration (LSI). The preceramic polymer role is played by phenolic resin (both as BJ binder and as PRIP impregnant), which pyrolyzes to carbon at 1000 C in argon. The carbon then reacts with liquid silicon during LSI to form secondary beta-SiC. BJ binder composition: 42 wt% resole-type phenolic resin, 28 wt% ethyl alcohol, 30 wt% glycol; viscosity 9.8 mPa·s, surface tension 33.05 mN/m, char yield 37.89 wt%. PRIP resin: THC-400 solid phenolic resin dissolved in alcohol at 50 wt%; density 0.9845 g/cm3, viscosity 24.6 mPa·s, char yield 46.15 wt%. Porosity of PRIP3 SiC/C preform: 31.00 +/- 1.03%; carbon density: 0.73 +/- 0.01 g/cm3. Theoretical optimal carbon density reported as 0.92 g/cm3. This is not a traditional PDC preceramic polymer paper; phenolic resin is used as a carbon precursor rather than a Si-containing preceramic polymer.
source: Preparation of low residual silicon content Si-SiC ceramics by binder jetting additive manufacturing and liquid silicon infiltration

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-OH (silanol groups), Si-O-Si main chain backbone, phenyl (-Ph) side chains

functional_groups.other: hydroxyl (-OH), phenyl (-Ph) side chains

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Total weight loss of ~16.45 wt% from room temperature to 900 °C. Cross-linking reaction occurs at ~250 °C with release of water via condensation of Si-OH groups. Pyrolysis of main chains and oxidative removal of organic side groups (-CH3, -OH, -Ph) at ~600 °C releases CO, CO2, H2O, H2. Residual ceramic product is amorphous SiO2 below 1250 °C; cristobalite forms above 1250 °C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - network structure formed by polymerization/condensation at ~250 °C (curing at 250 °C for 4 h, heating rate 1 °C/min)

backbone_architecture.description: Main chains are -Si-O-Si- (siloxane backbone) with -CH3, -OH, and phenyl (-Ph) side chains. Upon curing at 250 °C, forms a cross-linked network molecular structure via condensation of Si-OH groups.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis of silicone resin produces amorphous SiO2 at temperatures below 1250 °C. Above 1250 °C, amorphous SiO2 crystallizes to cristobalite (beta-cristobalite during heating, transforms to alpha-cristobalite on cooling at 180-270 °C with 2.8% volume contraction). In ceramic cores with 5 wt% silicone resin: ~10.5 wt% crystallinity at 1200 °C, 27.6% at 1250 °C, 54.9% at 1300 °C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Highest bending strength of 31.15 ± 2.89 MPa obtained in ceramic cores with 5 wt% silicone resin sintered at 1250 °C. Bending strength decreases with increasing silicone resin content and decreases above 1250 °C due to microcrack formation from beta-to-alpha cristobalite transformation.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous SiO2 at temperatures below 1250 °C; cristobalite identified by XRD above 1250 °C

notes: The polymer (MK silicone resin powder, Shanghai Bohuai Chemical Co. Ltd., China) was used as a preceramic binder/precursor in fused silica ceramic core fabrication. Processing sequence: ball milling with fused silica (45 µm average diameter), pressing at 20 MPa for 3 min, curing at 250 °C for 4 h (1 °C/min), pyrolysis at 600 °C for 2 h (2 °C/min), sintering at 1200-1300 °C for 2 h (5 °C/min) in air. Silicone resin content varied at 5, 10, and 15 wt%. EDS on pyrolyzed product surface showed Si: 54.42 at% and O: 45.58 at%. The ceramic yield of 83.55 wt% refers to SiO2 residue. The paper references earlier work on TGA behavior of this specific MK resin.
source: Preparation of silica ceramic cores by the preceramic pyrolysis technology using silicone resin as precursor and binder

bonding_structure.other_bonds: PCS side chains decompose during pyrolysis stage 550-820°C; product converted from organic to inorganic

functional_groups.other: Low-molecular-weight organics volatilize in first stage (210-550°C); macromolecule crosslinking occurs

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Four exothermic pyrolysis stages identified by DSC-TG: Stage 1 (481-566°C, ~210-550°C in text) - volatilization of low-molecular-weight organics with maximum mass loss and minimum heat release; Stage 2 (566-807°C, ~550-820°C in text) - large mass loss and maximum heat release as PCS side chains decompose and product converts from organic to inorganic; Stage 3 (807-1015°C, ~820-1100°C in text) - no mass change but heat release due to crystallization; Stage 4 (1015-1236°C, ~1100°C+ in text) - no mass change but heat release due to grain growth. DSC-TG conducted at 10, 15, and 20 K/min. Uncured PCS showed less than 10% mass loss with no apparent exothermic peaks. Ceramic yield parameter C = 0.7012 listed in Table 1.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - curing at 240°C and 2 MPa for 2 hours

backbone_architecture.description: Macromolecule crosslinking occurs during first pyrolysis stage; PCS transitions from organic to inorganic during processing

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCS pyrolyzed to SiC matrix; crystallization and grain growth occur above 820°C; density of SiC matrix dc = 2.340 g/cm3

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Mechanical and thermomechanical properties measured for semi-products at various PIP stages (1I-2I and 3P-8P); in-plane tensile and out-of-plane tests conducted; thermal expansion coefficient, thermal conductivity, and specific heat capacity also measured

notes: Paper focuses on process modeling of multicycle PIP (Precursor Impregnation and Pyrolysis) for SiC ceramic matrix composites using polycarbosilane (PCS) as precursor with MT300 carbon fibre fabrics. Key parameters from Table 1: fibre volume fraction vf=0.3732, fibre density df=1.820 g/cm3, cured PCS density dp=1.038 g/cm3, SiC matrix density dc=2.340 g/cm3, ceramic yield C=0.7012, U (ratio dp/dc)=0.4416, initial porosity P1I=0.1164. Pyrolysis kinetics (Coats-Redfern method) at three heating rates (10, 15, 20 K/min) to 1300°C gave mass transformation activation energies Em of ~28-29 kJ/mol. Four-stage pyrolysis kinetics parameters also tabulated with activation energies ranging from 208.81 to 479.77 kJ/mol. Eight PIP cycles were performed. Curing conditions: 240°C, 2 MPa, 2 hours. Heating/cooling rate 10 K/min for both curing and pyrolysis.
source: Process modelling of precursor impregnation and pyrolysis used in manufacturing ceramic-matrix composites

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si bonds formed during dehydrogenation; C=C vinyl groups present before crosslinking; C=O band (~1718 cm-1) attributed to adsorbed CO2 and backbone inclusion observed after curing

functional_groups.other: N-H functional group present (absorption at 3380 cm-1); Si-H functional group present (absorption at 2120-2160 cm-1)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three mass loss events observed: (1) ~100-400°C for pure resin, ~100-180°C for catalyst-containing resin (crosslinking/hydrosilylation); (2) ~300-500°C attributed to dehydrocoupling and transamination; (3) ~550-800°C attributed to ceramization. Ceramic yield ranged from ~69.3% (uncrosslinked, 4% DCP) to ~86% (24h crosslinked, no catalyst). Heating rate: RT to 450°C at 2°C/min, 450-850°C at 0.5°C/min, hold at 850°C for 1h. TGA for DSC/TGA analysis performed at 20°C/min in nitrogen up to 1000°C. 3D printed sample after double cure cycle yielded ~76% ceramic yield.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal with chemical catalyst (dicumyl peroxide, DCP); crosslinking at 180°C for 1, 4, or 24 hours; catalyst concentrations of 0, 1, 2, 4 wt.%

backbone_architecture.description: Crosslinked polysilazane network formed via hydrosilylation (Si-C bond formation), dehydrocoupling (Si-N, Si-Si), transamination, and vinyl polymerization; free radical mechanism initiated by dicumyl peroxide via abstraction of hydrogen from perhydropolysilazane (PHPS)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous ceramic formed after pyrolysis at 850°C; ceramization occurs in range ~550-800°C converting crosslinked preceramic polymer to amorphous ceramic

notes: Catalyst used: dicumyl peroxide (DCP) at 0, 1, 2, 4 wt.%. DSC crosslinking peak temperatures: 166°C (1% DCP), 161°C (2% DCP), 157°C (4% DCP); broad range ~100-400°C for pure resin. Glass transition temperature of crosslinked resins: 343.7°C (pure resin), decreasing to 324.8°C at 4% DCP. Ceramic yield for uncrosslinked resins: 72.9% (pure) to 69.3% (4% DCP). Ceramic yield for 1h crosslinked resins: 79.8% (pure) to 78.13% (4% DCP). Highest ceramic yield ~86% obtained for 24h crosslinked resin without catalyst. Pyrolyzed density: 1.92-2.04 g/cm3 (1h crosslinked), 2.1-2.29 g/cm3 (24h crosslinked). 3D printed sample density ~2.05 g/cm3. Ceramic yield range noted; midpoint values reported where applicable. Recommended 3D printing parameters: 1 wt.% DCP, 50 wt.% crushed cured powder added to resin, crosslinking at 180°C for 24h, reheating after removal from bath. Viscosity of pure preceramic polymer ~4 mPa.s; increased to ~7 Pa.s with 50 wt.% crushed cured powder addition.
source: Processing and 3D printing of SiCN polymer-derived ceramics

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Silicon carboxide (Si-C-O) network; described as a siloxane polymer that converts to amorphous Si-C-O ceramic upon pyrolysis

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Heating at 2°C/min from 150°C to 200°C, held 1 hour at 200°C, then 3°C/min to 1000°C, held 1 hour; cooled at 3°C/min to 250°C under nitrogen. Weight-based char yields for preceramic polymers generally reported as 60-90% in text but no specific value given for Blackglas. First pyrolysis from dilute solution gave very low ceramic yield; monomer solution used for reinfiltration gave higher ceramic yield.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - B-staging at 50°C for 1 hour then 150°C for 2 hours; infrared cure-on-the-fly at 55-60°C during winding

backbone_architecture.description: Siloxane-based preceramic polymer (silicon carboxide glass); used as both a dilute solution in iso-octane for winding/shape stabilization and as a monomer solution for reinfiltration

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis at 1000°C converts Blackglas to amorphous silicon carboxide (Si-C-O) ceramic with density of 2.2 g/cm3; composite parts can withstand up to 1200°C after pyrolysis

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: C-ring flexural strength values for composites range from 51.5 to 218.7 MPa; modulus values range from 50.1 to 86.8 GPa depending on fiber system and processing (see composite tables, not intrinsic polymer properties)

notes: Blackglas is used as a matrix in CFCCs via filament winding and preceramic polymer pyrolysis. Ceramic density after pyrolysis is 2.2 g/cm3. The polymer has very low viscosity and no harmful reaction gases during cure. CTE is controllable by varying carbon content. Pot-life up to 8 hours when resin bath kept in ice chest. Seven reinfiltration/pyrolysis cycles used with ~17 hours per cycle; convergence criterion set at <2% weight change between cycles. Final composite densities range from 2.07 to 2.39 g/cm3 with 4-9% porosity and 59-63% fiber volume fraction. General preceramic polymer density range cited as 1.1-2.2 g/cm3; char yields cited as 60-90% for the class of materials but specific Blackglas value not given.
source: Processing and Performance of Continuous Fiber Ceramic Composites by Preceramic Polymer Pyrolysis- I—Filament Winding

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C=C (vinyl) double bond participates in cross-linking; Si-H absorption at 2160 cm-1; vinyl absorptions at 3056 and 1598 cm-1

functional_groups.other: Cross-linker CLC-PB055 is a nonsolvent-based siloxane polymer with Pt and peroxide; cross-linking occurs via hydrosilylation

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed at 10°C/min ramp to 800°C in nitrogen; STA performed in flowing argon up to 1400°C at 3°C/min. TGA mass loss in air and Ar up to 1400°C ranged from ~2.1% (1 PIP) to ~2.6% (3 PIP) in air and ~2.1% (1 PIP) to ~2.5% (3 PIP) in Ar.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical/catalytic - hydrosilylation using CLC-PB055 cross-linker (siloxane polymer with Pt and peroxide) at 4 wt% loading; initial cure at 220°C in air

backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosiloxane backbone with Si-H and C=C (vinyl) functional groups; cross-linker has similar functional groups but lacks Si-H and has smaller molecular weight

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Matrix described as amorphous in nature; SiC powder used as filler; presence of pores and cracks noted. XRD performed with PANalytical X'pert using Mo K-alpha radiation.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Values after 3 PIP cycles: flexural strength 66.8 ± 2.5 MPa, elastic modulus 69.5 ± 2.8 GPa. After 1 PIP: 26.1 ± 3.1 MPa, 43.2 ± 2.8 GPa. After 2 PIP: 40.2 ± 3.9 MPa, 54.1 ± 2.7 GPa. Measured by 4-pt bending (ASTM C1341) and impulse excitation respectively.

notes: MS-154 polycarbosiloxane used as preceramic polymer for PIP of binder jet 3D printed SiC composites. Density increased from 2.05 g/cm3 (1 PIP) to 2.33 g/cm3 (3 PIP). Thermal conductivity after 3 PIP cycles: 6.72-6.98 W/mK at 25°C and 7.36-7.96 W/mK at 300°C. CTE ~4 ± 1.2 ppm/°C between 200-1000°C. Pyrolysis conducted at 850°C in flowing nitrogen (250 ccm). Curing at 220°C in air. A thermo-oxidative crosslinking step (325 C, 48 h in air) was performed prior to pyrolysis to prevent re-melting of PEEK. Crosslinking heating rate: 1 K/min to 200 C, then 0.5 K/min to 325 C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Flexural strength of C/C-SiC: 80.3 ± 6.7 MPa at optimal process parameters (layer height 0.1 mm, infill density 100%, printing direction ±45°). Continuous CF-PEEK reference from literature achieved ~235 MPa flexural strength (Weibull modulus 3.21). Interlaminar shear strength (ILSSb) of CF-PEEK green bodies also measured per DIN EN 658-5. Young's modulus of PEEK matrix: 3.7 GPa (reference value).

notes: This paper does not describe a traditional preceramic polymer (e.g. polysilazane, polycarbosilane). Instead, PEEK (polyetheretherketone) is used as a carbon precursor matrix in a short CF-reinforced filament for FFF additive manufacturing of C/C-SiC ceramic matrix composites via the LSI process. The study focuses on how FFF process parameters (layer height 0.1-0.3 mm, infill density 80-100%, printing direction 0/±45/90°) affect specific surface area (SSA) of green bodies and downstream processability. Thermo-oxidative crosslinking at 325°C for 48 h in air prevents PEEK re-melting during pyrolysis. Pyrolysis at 1000°C in nitrogen yields C/C preform; liquid silicon infiltration at >1420°C in vacuum yields C/C-SiC. Carbon fiber content in filament: 10 wt-%. Filament: CarbonX PEEK+CF10 by 3DXTech. The ceramic yield of ~50 wt-% is cited from literature for pyrolysis at 1200°C in nitrogen; actual pyrolysis in study at 1000°C.
source: Processing-microstructure correlations in material extrusion additive manufacturing of carbon fiber reinforced ceramic matrix composites

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PEG 6K decomposed between 180-500C with 0% remaining mass at 1100C. Aluminum nitrate decomposed between 100-400C with 13.1% remaining mass at 1100C (theoretical 13.6% as Al2O3). Magnesium nitrate decomposed between 100-460C with 15.2% remaining mass at 1100C (theoretical 15.7% as MgO). Al/Mg nitrate mixture decomposed primarily 100-400C with 16.6% remaining at 400C and secondary decomposition 400-600C with 13.9% remaining at 1100C (theoretical 13.7%). Melting peaks: PEG 69C, Al-nitrate 84C, Mg-nitrate 97C, Al/Mg mixture 85C. Decomposition peaks: PEG 386C, Al-nitrate 159C, Mg-nitrate 446C, Al/Mg mixture 166C primary and 344C secondary.

Final TiCx structures were crack-free and resisted fracture during thermal shock testing.

notes: This paper is not primarily about a preceramic polymer. The phenolic novolac resin (Hexion Durite AD-5614) is used as a sacrificial carbon-yielding binder in a reactive additive manufacturing process for TiCx ultra-high temperature ceramics. The resin is mixed at 25 vol.% with Ti powder (75 vol.%) for selective laser sintering (SLS) green body shaping. Particle size for both Ti and phenolic: <=74 micrometers. Powder bed temperature during SLS: 50 degrees C. Heating rate of 100 degrees C/hr applies above 160 degrees C. Hold time of 840 min (14 hrs) refers to CH4 reactive dwell; pyrolysis atmosphere for phenolic carbonization alone is Ar. Final ceramic product TiCx achieved up to 98.2 wt.% yield (TiC0.90) on surface with Scheme II processing. The polymer here is not a preceramic polymer in the traditional sense (e.g. polysilazane) but serves as a carbon source and temporary binder.

notes: This paper is NOT about preceramic polymers. thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Heating rate was 10 °C/min up to 600 °C, then 2 °C/min. Reverse cycle used on cooling. Phase separation of SiOC to SiO2 + SiC + C occurs during pyrolysis. Silica volatilization via SiO gas formation noted. Some samples treated at 1570 °C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (flow induced at ~100 °C, Tg slightly below 100 °C)

backbone_architecture.description: Commercial polymethylsiloxane (silicone resin); described as more stable than polysilazanes; H44 noted as chemically analogous to SR355

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC (intermediate); β-SiAlON (final product at 1550 °C); corundum (α-Al2O3) contamination; traces of alumino-silicate (mullite/sillimanite) and SiC
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: β-SiAlON (Si2Al4O4N4, PDF#76-0598) formed at 1550 °C along with corundum (α-Al2O3, PDF#88-0826). At 1450 °C, alumino-silicates (mullite and sillimanite in ~3:2 weight ratio) dominate. SiOC phase separates to SiO2 + SiC + C. Assumed SiOC composition from polymer: Si3O4.6C8.45.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Vickers hardness (20 N load, 15 s) and indentation fracture toughness KIC (50 N load, 25 s) measured across joint region; no significant difference between joint and bulk SiAlON. Nano-indentation reduced elastic modulus and hardness in joint region comparable to or slightly higher than parent SiAlON monolith. Elastic modulus value of ~305 GPa selected from previous investigations for KIC calculation.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: β-SiAlON (Si2Al4O4N4, PDF#76-0598), α-Al2O3 corundum (PDF#88-0826), mullite (3Al2O3·2SiO2, PDF#79-1275), sillimanite (Al2O3·SiO2, PDF#74-0274), SiC (PDF#73-1708)

notes: Paper focuses on use of SR355 polysiloxane (silicone) filled with δ/γ-alumina nano-particles (NanoDur, 40-50 nm) as a joining medium for α-β Yb-SiAlON ceramics. Silicone/alumina ratio used: 0.3 g SR355 to 0.44 g alumina (as 50 wt% suspension). H44 silicone + γ-Al2O3 (Degussa, 15 nm) used as comparison powder system. Joining treatment: 1550 °C, 3 h, 98% N2/2% H2. Application of compressive load during thermal treatment was essential for robust joint formation. Pre-oxidation of SiAlON substrate at 1300 °C/3 h showed no significant microstructural benefit. Joint thickness <2 µm. Ceramic yield not explicitly reported.
source: SiAlON ceramics from preceramic polymers and nano-sized fillers- Application in ceramic joining

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-allyl groups present (absorption at 1630 cm-1); Si-H absorption at 2100 cm-1; SiCH3 absorption at 1250 cm-1. SMP-10 has higher Si-H and lower SiCH3 than SMP-877. Si-H sensitive to hydrolysis forming Si-OH.

functional_groups.other: allyl groups present on both SMP-10 and SMP-877; acrylate groups from multifunctional acrylate co-monomers (BDDA, HDDA, urethane acrylate methacrylate)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed at 10 deg C/min under argon to 1000 deg C using 50 mg samples. Major decomposition attributed to both acrylate and organic moiety in PCP. Ceramic yield above ca. 70% reported for thermally cured polymers. Pyrolysis used two-stage heating: 1 deg C/min to 850 deg C, then 3 deg C/min to 1200 deg C (microspheres) or 1300 deg C (3D printed parts), held 2 h, cooled at 5 deg C/min. Pyrolysis temp range 1200-1300 deg C; midpoint 1250 deg C noted.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV/photopolymerization - co-photopolymerization of Si-allyl groups with multifunctional acrylate groups plus homo-photopolymerization of acrylate phase; thermal crosslinking also referenced for comparison

backbone_architecture.description: Allylhydridopolycarbosilane (AHPCS, SMP-10) with general formula showing Si backbone with H and allyl substituents, X=0.1 allyl fraction. SMP-877 (AMHPCS) has R=CH3. Upon UV curing, AHPCS chains are connected by acrylate domains via co-photopolymerization of allyl groups with multifunctional acrylates, forming a composite network.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiCxOy composition with x>>y (SiC-rich) or y>>x (SiO-rich) depending on formulation and acrylate type/ratio. SMP-10 formulations tend toward SiO-rich (y>>x), SMP-877 formulations tend toward SiC-rich (x>>y). HF etching can selectively remove SiO2 phase. Potential for SiO2 phase from Si-H hydrolysis if exposed to moisture.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: UV cured composites achieve sufficient green strength for 3D printing; monoacrylate mixtures with PCP increase viscosity but do not produce significant hardening; multifunctional acrylates required for crosslinking and structural integrity

notes: Paper focuses on STL 3D printing of allylhydridopolycarbosilane (AHPCS, SMP-10) and allylmethylhydridopolycarbosilane (AMHPCS, SMP-877) mixed with multifunctional acrylates (BDDA, HDDA, urethane acrylate methacrylate). STL device: Freeform Pico Plus (Asiga), 405 nm, 39 um resolution, 4 s exposure per 50 um layer. Photoinitiators: TPOL (STL) and LTM (microspheres). Porous microspheres produced by emulsification/UV curing to study porosity. BET surface areas ranged 31-260 m2/g and pore volumes 0.024-0.33 cm3/g depending on formulation. HF etching used to remove SiO2 phase. Ceramic yield above ~70% stated for thermally cured AHPCS. Pyrolysis temperature range 1200-1300 deg C used; midpoint 1250 deg C used in pyrolysis_temp_C field. TGA to 1000 deg C only, not to final pyrolysis temp. XRD performed but results not detailed in provided text. Conductivity assessed but values not provided in text.
source: SiC and SiOC ceramic articles produced by stereolithography of acrylate modified polycarbosilane systems

backbone_architecture.description: HTT1800 polysilazane backbone modified by reaction with Hf(NEt2)4 and BH3·SMe2 to form single-source precursors (SSPs) for SiHfCN and SiHfBCN ceramics. Cross-linking produces a solid network prior to warm pressing and pyrolysis.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous SiHfCN / SiHfBCN after pyrolysis at 1100°C; upon high-temperature annealing/SPS: HfCxN1-x, β-SiC, β-Si3N4, HfB2, HfN(C) nanocrystallites in amorphous matrix

After annealing in Ar at 1700°C: HfCxN1-x + SiC for SiHfCN; HfCxN1-x + SiC + HfB2 for SiHfBCN. After annealing in N2: HfN(C) precipitates in amorphous SiBCN matrix.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: SiHfCN_05 (SPS): hardness 23.1±1 GPa (microindentation) / 26.8±3.4 GPa (nanoindentation), modulus 271±8 / 367±30 GPa. SiHfBCN_06: hardness 22.5±2.3 / 24.6±3.6 GPa, modulus 245±18 / 284±44 GPa. SiHfBCN_09: hardness 19.5±1 / 20.8±3.7 GPa, modulus 207±11 / 266±40 GPa. notes: The primary preceramic polymer is HTT1800 (a commercial polysilazane). It is chemically modified with hafnium tetrakis(diethylamide) Hf(NEt2)4 (10 or 30 vol%) and optionally BH3·SMe2 to produce single-source precursors (SSPs) for SiHfCN and SiHfBCN ceramics respectively. Cross-linking is performed thermally at 200-250°C. Warm pressing at 240-300°C/30MPa precedes pyrolysis to 1100°C. Dense UHTC nanocomposites were produced by SPS at up to 1950°C. Ceramic yield range for Hf-containing SSPs: 80-83% (midpoint ~81.6% used for ceramic_yield_pct). Mechanical property values reported are for SPS-densified ceramics, not the polymer itself. Oxidation resistance: SiHfBCN shows superior oxidation resistance vs SiHfCN; activation energies for oxidation: SiCN=220.5 kJ/mol, SiHfCN=156.5 kJ/mol, SiHfBCN powder=112.9 kJ/mol, monolithic SiHfBCN=139.7-174 kJ/mol.

Modulus value of 100 GPa is an assumed/estimated value used in stress calculations, not a directly measured property. thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Linear PDMS degrades at 290-600 C via cyclic oligomer expulsion (trimer and tetramer major products). In oxidative atmosphere, depolymerization onset ~290 C vs ~400 C in inert; ca. 10 mass% silica residue from linear PDMS in oxidative atmosphere. Cross-linked polysiloxanes (Burns et al.) yield ca. 65-75 mass% at 1100 C in inert atmosphere; O/Si ratios 1.3-1.4. After carbothermic reduction at 1800 C, residual mass 35-50 mass%. PMSQ ceramic yield ca. 80% with onset of mass loss at 750 C; PPSQ ceramic yield ca. 60% with onset at 500 C. Phenyl group introduction increases onset temperature but does not increase residual mass at 1000 C.

POSS cage structures (polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane) also discussed as components in copolymers.

notes: This is a review article covering multiple silicone resin types (PDMS, PMPhS, PEPhS, PMSQ, PPSQ, POSS-siloxane copolymers, cross-linked polysiloxanes by Burns et al.) as ceramic precursors for Si-O-C materials. Ceramic yield of 65-75% (midpoint 70%) is from Burns et al. cross-linked polysiloxanes at 1100 C in inert atmosphere; range noted as 65-75 mass%. Residual mass after carbothermic reduction at 1800 C is 35-50 mass% (midpoint 42.5%). Bond energies cited: Si-O 369.0 kJ/mol, C-O 351.5 kJ/mol, C-C 347.7 kJ/mol, C-Si 290.0 kJ/mol. Glass transition temperatures: PDMS -127 C, PMPhS -86 C. Applications discussed include fiber spinning, porous ceramics, matrix infiltration, binding agents, MEMS, thick coatings, and bulk ceramics.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis weight loss varies by wood species: Balsa 73.5%, Pine 73.8%, Oak 70.4%, Maple 74.9%, Beech 74.2%, Ebony 64.6%, Paulownia 70.17%, MDF 71.6%. Heating at ~1 C/min up to 400-500 C, then accelerated to 10-20 C/min. Carbon yield ~25-30 wt% relative to initial wood mass. ~90% carbon at 600 C. Si-infiltrated densities range from 2.02 to 2.94 g/cm3 depending on wood precursor.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Flexural/biaxial strength and elastic modulus reported for various wood-derived SiC ceramics. Biaxial strength: wood carbon template ~4 MPa, SiO-infiltrated SiC ~13 MPa, Si-infiltrated SiC ~21 MPa. Axial flexural strengths for dense bioSiC range from ~100-480 MPa depending on wood precursor and porosity. KIC ranges from 0.46 to 4.3 MPa*m^0.5 depending on species and direction.

notes: This paper is a review of biomorphic silicon carbide (bioSiC) ceramics derived from wood templates, not a preceramic polymer study. No preceramic polymer is described. The carbon template is derived directly from pyrolysis of wood (cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin), not from a synthetic preceramic polymer. All preceramic polymer descriptor fields are null. Pyrolysis temperature must exceed 800 C per text; final SiC formation by melt infiltration occurs at >1450 C (above Si melting point) in vacuum. thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yield reported as 72-78 wt% amorphous SiC after pyrolysis (midpoint 75 used). Mass loss during uncured ink TGA begins at ~75C and proceeds at constant rate until ~170C where loss rate slows. Crosslinking initiates at ~120C with peak exotherm between 170 and 200C. Pyrolysis schedule includes 1h holds at 300, 450, and 600C and 2h holds at 800 and 1200C. Prior work on SMP-10 showed mass loss reduced from 34% to 25% at 1000C after pretreatment. SiC crystallites begin to form at 1250C.

notes: SMP-10 is commercially available from Starfire Systems Inc. Curing performed in air with two-stage process: ramp to 167C at 1C/min hold 1h, then ramp to 230C at 1C/min hold 1h. Ceramic yield range is 72-78 wt%; midpoint 75 used for ceramic_yield_pct. Mw of ~7000 g/mol reported for untreated resin; increases to ~16000 g/mol after thermal/vacuum pretreatment per Apostolov et al. PDI of 5.544 explicitly stated. Two ink formulations studied: SMP-10-Z (52.5 vol% SMP-10 + 47.5 vol% ZrB2) and SMP-10-ZFA (51.7 vol% SMP-10 + 42.4 vol% ZrB2 + 5.95 vol% fumed Al2O3). Ceramic yield range noted: 72-78 wt%.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two distinct pyrolysis regimes identified: low-temperature regime A (550-700°C) dominated by evolution of silane and disiloxane fragments (Si(CH3)4, (CH3)3-Si-O-Si-(CH3)3), and high-temperature regime B (700-850°C) dominated by methane and hydrogen evolution with minor ethylene and water. Integrated weight loss: 2.85 ± 0.35% for peak A and 10.1 ± 0.8% for peak B. CHR experiments conducted at 2, 5, 10, 20, and 50°C/min. Isothermal experiments at 647°C and 734°C for 60 min. First-order reaction kinetics confirmed by Lorentzian peak shape and isothermal exponential decay fits. Samples pre-heated to 530°C at 10°C/min and held 30 min before data collection.

notes: Paper focuses on kinetics of pyrolysis reactions of sol-gel-derived methylsilsesquioxane (from methyltriethoxysilane, MTES) converting to silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) ceramic. Powder samples (~30 µm average size) used to ensure reaction-controlled (not diffusion-controlled) conditions. Activation energies extracted from CHR peak shift analysis (Redhead method adapted to 3D network). Chemical analysis of ceramic by Service d'Analyze Elementaire du CNRS, France. notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. The study focuses on disordered foam structures (10–40 PPI) versus ordered topologies (regular hexahedral RH, regular octahedral RO, regular Kelvin RK) for micro gas turbine combustor applications. No preceramic polymer chemistry, pyrolysis, TGA, molecular weight, or polymer bonding data are present. Strut densities range from 3.263 to 3.329 g/cm3; porosities of disordered foams range from 66.0% to 85.3%; ordered structure porosities range from 75.0% to 95.0% with edge lengths 4.0–8.0 mm.

notes: This paper does not concern a preceramic polymer in the traditional sense. The primary focus is on C/C-SiC-(ZrxHf1-x)C ceramic matrix composites prepared by reactive melt infiltration (RMI) using Si/Zr/Hf powders (molar ratio 70:17.15:12.85%). True density of PIP specimens: 3.00 ± 0.05 g/cm³ (He pycnometry); apparent density: 1.3 g/cm³ (Hg porosimetry); open porosity ~57-60%. Heating rate of 100 °C/h = 1.667 °C/min. Mechanical values reported are for composite PIP or CVD-coated specimens, not the PDC alone.

notes: This paper does not describe a traditional preceramic silicon-based polymer. The precursor is a multi-metal organic polymer (modified Pechini process) using metal chlorides (TiCl4, ZrCl4, HfCl4, VCl3, NbCl4, TaCl4, WCl6), ethylene glycol, and citric acid to form high-entropy transition metal carbides (HECs). Ceramic yield range 30-40% (midpoint 35% used). STA TGA heating rate was 10 C/min for analysis only; actual pyrolysis heating rate was 1 C/min. Three compositions studied: (TiHfVNbTa)C (PDV), (TiZrHfNbTa)C (PDZr), (TiZrNbTaW)C (PDW). Polymer-derived route yields superior compositional homogeneity vs solid-state method as quantified by coefficient of variation in EDS mapping. Final densification by spark plasma sintering at 1800 C under vacuum with 50 MPa axial pressure.

notes: Study uses two different preceramic polymers (polysiloxane SPR684 and allyl-hydrido polycarbosilane SMP10) as single-source precursors for high-entropy carbide (HEC) nanocomposites.
