functional_groups.other: Cyclic oligomer structure; monomeric unit contains Si-H, N-H, and -CH=CH2 per unit

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Heating rates of 50, 150, 600, and 750 deg C/h were used; ceramic yields ~84-86 wt% at 1200 deg C in N2 (1 atm) for all samples and all heating rates. No significant weight loss up to 500 deg C except hydrogen loss (~15% lower than theoretical at 500 deg C). Main changes between 500-800 deg C with loss of hydrogen and carbon. Hydrocarbon release complete at 850 deg C; hydrogen loss continues to 1200 deg C. Major gases evolved above 450 deg C: hydrogen, methane, and ethylene. TGA coupled with quadrupole mass spectrometry (2-150 a.m.u.).

crosslink_density.value: Qualitative ordering: PI < PII < PIII < PIV; Pt catalyst used at 5e-4 Pt++/OVSZ unit ratio
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal and catalytic (Pt++ catalyst); crosslinking via hydrosilylation and vinyl polyaddition

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Vapour pressure osmometry for OVSZ (Mn=380); GPC or similar for PI (Mn=720, Mw=5700) and PII (Mn=990, Mw=27900); PIII and PIV are insoluble solids, MW not measurable

backbone_architecture.description: OVSZ is a mixture of liquid cyclic oligomers with mean polymerization degree of 5.4, prepared by ammonolysis of dichlorovinylsilane. Cross-linked derivatives range from viscous liquids (PI, PII) to insoluble/infusible solids (PIII, PIV) depending on conditions.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN (silicon carbonitride), amorphous up to 1400 deg C; alpha-Si3N4 forms after annealing at 1400 deg C for 12h
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Samples are dense and amorphous up to 1400 deg C. Formation of alpha-Si3N4 indicated by XRD after 12h annealing at 1400 deg C. Thermal stability attributed to high carbon content. Open porosity forms during annealing at 1400 deg C when crystallization begins.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Ceramics are compact with some heterogeneities at slow heating rates. Microcracks observed due to volume decrease stresses. Fast heating rate creates porosity and microcracks without bloating.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous up to 1400 deg C; alpha-Si3N4 detected by XRD after 12h annealing at 1400 deg C

notes: Paper studies pyrolysis of four polyvinylsilazanes (PI-PIV) derived from OVSZ by cross-linking via four different routes (thermal in toluene at 110 deg C/48h; thermal in hexane at 70 deg C/47h with Pt; thermal neat at 110 deg C/2h; thermal neat at 110 deg C/1h with Pt). Heating rates reported in deg C/h not deg C/min: 50, 150, 600, 750 deg C/h. Ceramic yield range 83-86 wt% across all samples and heating rates. IR confirms Si-N bonds unaffected during thermal treatment. Crosslinking reactions occurring at 130-250 deg C (exothermic DTA peak) eliminate structural differences between samples prior to mineralization. Specific surface area of products heated to 1400 deg C too low to measure by BET argon adsorption.
source: Vinylsilazane

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Basic structure described as (CH3-SiO3/2)x - methyl silsesquioxane repeat unit

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TG-DSC performed in both air and argon atmospheres (STA 449C, Netzsch). Polymer-to-ceramic conversion occurs between approximately 400-600 C with gas release and volume shrinkage. B4C oxidizes above 500 C in air. Phase transformations are atmosphere-dependent above 500 C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - cured at 200 C under pressure for 1 h

backbone_architecture.description: Silsesquioxane network with (CH3-SiO3/2)x repeat structure; described as having amorphous network structure; solid solvent-free silicone resin powder

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous at low temperatures; SiO2, AlPO4 (orthorhombic and hexagonal), Al2O3, mullite, Sn, SnO, SiC identified by XRD at higher temperatures depending on atmosphere
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 200 C: Si, Al, B4C, and amorphous silicone resin peaks at ~10 and 20-25 degrees 2-theta. Above 500 C atmosphere influences phase evolution. In air: B4C oxidizes, SnO/SiO2 glass phases appear. In argon: SiC forms at higher temperatures. Mullite phase identified in both atmospheres at elevated temperatures.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Adhesive joints show toughness/yielding behavior after curing at 200 C; brittle behavior after heat-treatment above 500 C. Joint stiffness increases with heat-treatment temperature. Maximum apparent shear strength of bonded joints: 33 MPa (mullite, 1300 C, air), 26 MPa (SiC, 1100 C, Ar), 13 MPa (C/C, 1100 C, Ar) for MSABs formulation.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous network at 200 C (broad peaks at ~10 and 20-25 degrees 2-theta); crystalline phases develop above 500 C including SiO2, Al2O3, AlPO4, mullite, Sn, SnO, SiC depending on temperature and atmosphere

notes: The polymethylsilsesquioxane (PMSQ) is used as a matrix for a ceramic-joining adhesive, not as a standalone preceramic polymer. It is formulated with active fillers: Al powder (3-5 um), Si powder (0.5 um), B4C (6.5-10 um), and SnO-SiO2-P2O5 glass powder (3-4 um). The full adhesive formulation with all additives is designated MSABs; the formulation without glass is MSAB. The polymer is a solid, solvent-free silicone resin powder dissolved in isopropyl alcohol for processing. Curing conditions: 200 C, 2.5 MPa, 1 h. Optimal bonding layer thickness ~100 um; optimal viscosity 3600-3800 mPa·s. The paper focuses on adhesive bonding of C/C composites, SiC, and mullite ceramics rather than characterization of the preceramic polymer itself.
source: Wang et al. - 2015 - Joining of various engineering ceramics and composites by a modified preceramic polymer for high-temperature applic

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Epoxide-amine crosslinks between PEGDE and ETH; hydrogen bonds between low molecular weight plasticizers (EG, DEG) and the PEGDE-ETH network

functional_groups.other: Epoxide (glycidyl ether) groups from poly(ethylene glycol)diglycidyl ether (PEGDE); hydroxyl groups from plasticizers ethylene glycol (EG) and diethylene glycol (DEG)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Multi-stage heat treatment process described: plasticizer evaporation stage (up to ~200°C), debinding/binder burn-off stage, and high-temperature sintering stage. Sintering temperatures vary by material (e.g., 1300°C for nickel-zinc ferrite, 1400°C for AZO/alumina with additives, 1450°C for zirconia). The polymer binder is fully removed during debinding, yielding a porous brown-body prior to sintering.

crosslink_density.value: Optimal ETH:PEGDE volume ratio of 0.20:1 giving lowest viscosity; minimum solid loading of 52 vol% for nickel-zinc ferrite paste with shear yield stress ~400 Pa
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical (self-curing epoxide-amine reaction at ambient conditions or accelerated by heat up to 80°C)

backbone_architecture.description: Crosslinked epoxide-amine network formed by reaction of poly(ethylene glycol)diglycidyl ether (PEGDE) with EpoThin 2 Hardener (ETH); plasticizers (EG, DEG) provide flexibility via hydrogen bonding within the network

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: The polymer binder is used as a sacrificial matrix for ceramic/metal powder processing; after sintering, ceramic phases identified include zirconium oxide (JCPDS #88-1007), strontium iron oxide (JCPDS #72-0739), beta-SiC (with yttria and alumina sintering additives), nickel-zinc ferrite, AZO, and alumina. Polymer itself does not contribute to ceramic yield.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Flexural strength ~340 MPa for sintered zirconia (1450°C, 5 hours, >98% theoretical density). Copper resistivity ~5.0×10^-8 Ohm·m. Nickel-zinc ferrite magnetic saturation Ms = 74.4 emu/g at 1300°C sintering.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Zirconium oxide (JCPDS #88-1007), strontium iron oxide (JCPDS #72-0739), nickel-zinc ferrite phases confirmed by XRD at various sintering temperatures

notes: This paper does not describe a preceramic polymer system. The binder system is a sacrificial epoxide-amine polymer (PEGDE + ETH amine hardener) with low molecular weight plasticizers (ethylene glycol, diethylene glycol) used as a universal robocasting vehicle for a wide range of ceramic powders (zirconia, SiC, alumina, AZO, nickel-zinc ferrite, strontium ferrite, kaolinite) and metals (copper). The polymer is burned out during debinding and does not contribute to the final ceramic phase. Exothermic DSC curing peaks at 95.2°C and 109.2°C; curing also occurs at room temperature (~27°C). DSC performed at 0.20:1 ETH:PEGDE volume ratio. Sintering performed at material-specific temperatures (1300–1600°C). 20.6% lateral shrinkage observed for nickel-zinc ferrite from flex-body to sintered state. This is NOT a preceramic polymer paper.
source: Zhang et al. - 2019 - A 3D-printing method of fabrication for metals, ceramics, and multi-materials using a universal self-curable tec

notes: This paper is a review of ZrB2-SiC composite processing techniques (hot pressing, SPS, pressureless sintering, flash sintering, CVI, CVD, additive manufacturing, etc.) and does not describe a preceramic polymer as the primary subject. All preceramic polymer descriptor fields are therefore null.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yields vary widely by polymer type and heat treatment conditions: ~83% at 1400°C (Yu 2009), ~60% at 1200°C (Huang 2021), 53% at 1000°C / 85% at 950°C (2017), 88% at 1000°C after HT (Qian 2019), 19-20% at 1200°C (Sang 2016), 62% at 1400°C (Bouzat 2018), 40% at 1400°C (Piriou 2018). Yajima process polycarbosilane maintained 60% weight after pyrolysis to 1000°C.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC mentioned as a standard technique (listed in abbreviations)

backbone_architecture.description: Polysilanes: linear and cyclic (ring formation is thermodynamic product of Wurtz coupling); polycarbosilanes: linear (Yajima/ROP), highly branched (Grignard/Whitmarsh-Interrante hydridopolycarbosilane with linear, bifunctional, and trifunctional branch points), hyperbranched/dendritic (hydrosilylation one-pot); block copolymers also reported (anionic ROP)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis products typically amorphous at intermediate temperatures, crystallize as beta-SiC at higher temperatures (1200-1500°C). C/Si ratios reported ranging from 0.9-1.6 depending on precursor. Free carbon observed in some cases. Stacking faults and twinning noted (Bouzat 2018). Lightly crystallized beta-SiC/amorphous SiC with ordered carbon plane defects observed by TEM (Qian 2019). Polysilazanes yield Si3N4 and SiCN. Beta-SiC nanograins formed at 1200-1800°C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: SiC noted for high hardness, wear and corrosion resistance; oxide ceramics noted for higher creep vs. nonoxide ceramics at elevated temperatures

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to semi-crystalline depending on pyrolysis temperature
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC; Si3N4; SiCN; free carbon; borosilicate glass (in HfB2-SiC composites)

notes: This is a broad review paper (Chem. Rev. 2023, 123, 4188-4236) covering multiple preceramic polymer classes (polysilanes, polycarbosilanes, polysilazanes, polyborosilazanes, UHTC precursors) rather than a single polymer system. Molecular weight data from summary tables references ranges of Mn ~270-613 g/mol for oligomeric species and up to >1000 kDa for high-MW Wurtz-coupled polysilanes. Pyrolysis temperatures from summary table range 300-400°C for curing and up to 1400-1800°C for ceramic conversion. C/Si ratios in PDCs range from 0.9 to 1.6. Hold times of 6h at ~170°C noted for HT curing steps. Applications include fiber spinning, ceramic matrix composites (PIP), and additive manufacturing. Stoichiometric SiC target is 1Si/1C. UHTC phases include group IV (Ti, Zr, Hf) carbides, borides, and nitrides.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Uncrosslinked HBPCS alone yields only 11 wt% ceramic at 1000C. With SiHx crosslinker (2:1 HBPCS:SiHx by weight), yield increases to 80 wt% at 1000C. N2-atmosphere cured polymer yields only 5 wt%; N2 then O2 cured yields 59 wt%. Further heating to 1800C results in 39% mass retention relative to the SiOC intermediate due to carbothermal reduction and CO release.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal oxidative curing in air; initial hydrosilylation (Pt-catalyzed) cross-linking during gelation; heating at 1 C/min to 160C held 1h, then to 280C held 5h

backbone_architecture.description: Allyl-terminated hyperbranched polycarbosilane first described by Muzafarov et al., synthesized via Ax+By bimolecular nonlinear hyperbranched polymerization with dense network of reactive alkene sites throughout polymer structure; Si-C backbone

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOC formed at 1000C (C: 55.7, O: 23.0, Si: 21.3 at%). Heating to 1800C converts to crystalline beta-SiC (C: 49.5, O: 1.3, Si: 49.1 at%). At 1600C, onset of SiC crystallinity with residual silica domains (peak at 2theta ~22 deg). Carbothermal reduction over 1600-1800C expels oxygen as CO gas.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (prominent peaks at 1800C); minor SiC peaks and silica at 1600C

notes: Two-component PCP system: HBPCS (hyperbranched polycarbosilane) paired with SiHx (multifunctional dihydrosilane cross-linker, ~33 wt% / 2:1 HBPCS:SiHx weight ratio). Elemental composition values reported here correspond to the 2:1 HBPCS:SiHx ratio ceramic at 1000C. Table 1 shows composition varies with ratio: 6:1 (C 40.3, O 35.1, Si 23.4 at%), 4:1 (C 45.3, O 30.5, Si 23.2 at%), 2:1 (C 55.7, O 23.0, Si 21.3 at%), 1:1 (C 54.2, O 20.2, Si 25.6 at%). Crystallite size at 1600C was 3.5 nm; at 1800C was 66 nm (Scherrer equation). Raman confirms polycrystalline cubic (3C) SiC at 1800C. Residual Pt catalyst (910 ppm) from hydrosilylation polymerization likely facilitates low-temperature crosslinking. System demonstrated for aerosol jet printing; printed lines 3.0 um thick cured, 2.0 um after 800C pyrolysis.

notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. It concerns lignin-derived carbon fibers for lithium-ion battery anode applications. The precursor materials are Alcell hardwood lignin (AHL) and Kraft softwood lignin (KSL), chemically modified with acid anhydrides (acetic, phthalic, maleic, succinic). The process involves melt spinning, oxidative stabilization in air up to 249 C, and carbonization at 1000 C for 30 min in 96% Ar / 4% H2. Carbon fiber diameters were approximately 40 micrometers. Resistivity measurements were performed on individual fibers. No preceramic polymer descriptors are applicable to this paper.

polymer_name: SMP-877 (commercial polycarbosilane); PCPGNP corona: poly(1,1-dimethylpropylsilane) (PDMPS) grafted on silica nanoparticles

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Allyl (-C=C-) groups present in SMP-877; hydrosilylation reaction between Si-H and allyl groups occurs during thermal treatment; Si-H peaks in ~2000-2200 cm-1 region disappear after thermal treatment

functional_groups.other: Allyl groups in SMP-877; PDMPS is only end-functionalized with Si-H

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed before and after thermal treatment at 800°C in argon at 100 mL/min flow rate. Char yields vary significantly by PCPGNP/SMP-877 ratio (see table): e.g., pure PCPGNP (G100) BTT=28.6%, ATT=43.7%; pure SMP-877 BTT=40.5%, ATT=70.5%. Thermal treatment prior to TGA (pyrolysis) improves char yield across all compositions (ATT > BTT), with increases ranging from 6.2% to 30.0%.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: Thermal: hydrosilylation between Si-H and allyl groups of SMP-877 during thermal treatment; thermal jamming of polymer grafts on PCPGNPs also contributes to network formation

backbone_architecture.description: PCPGNPs consist of silica nanoparticles (~30 nm) with poly(1,1-dimethylpropylsilane) chains grafted from the surface. When dispersed in SMP-877, percolation of the particle network occurs between 50-60 wt% PCPGNP, resulting in solid-like behavior with entangled/overlapping grafted chains.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis of mixed PCPGNP/SMP-877 system resulted in ceramic phases distinctly stronger in SiC than produced by hybrid particles alone. Final ceramic phase details not fully quantified in this excerpt.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Storage modulus (G') and loss modulus (G'') reported as functions of frequency and strain for PCPGNP/SMP-877 mixtures. Above percolation threshold (>60 wt% PCPGNP), G' > G'' indicating solid-like behavior. Yield strain >100% for all compositions above percolation threshold.

notes: This paper studies mixtures of PCP-grafted nanoparticles (PCPGNPs: silica NPs with PDMPS corona) and commercial polycarbosilane SMP-877 across 11 compositions (0-100 wt% PCPGNP). Key findings: (1) Rheological percolation threshold between 50-60 wt% PCPGNP; (2) Thermal treatment (3°C/min to 160°C, hold 1h, then 3°C/min to 250°C, hold 1h, all under vacuum) significantly improves char yield at 800°C in all compositions; (3) Thermal jamming of polymer grafts identified as key mechanism for improved char yield; (4) XPCS reveals two diffusive modes above percolation; (5) Systems above percolation threshold are suitable for direct ink write (DIW) 3D printing at 5 psi, 20 mm/s, 410 μm nozzle; (6) Char yield values for all compositions listed in table (BTT and ATT at 800°C, argon, 20°C/min). SMP-877 is enriched in Si-H moieties; PDMPS only end-functionalized with Si-H. Pt catalyst used in PCPGNP synthesis was poisoned with pentaerythritol tetrakis(3-mercaptopropionate).

In air, no significant weight loss up to 1000°C; weight gain at ~400-500°C attributed to surface oxidation; slight weight loss between 500-700°C attributed to loss of excess surface carbon.

notes: Paper studies two precursors: CBS (cyclic monomer) and L-EPCS (linear polymer), both containing Si-CH2-Si bridging groups rather than pendent Si-CH3. Sol-gel processing under acid (HCl) catalysis. CBS gel dried at 160°C shows partial ring-opening via Si-OH-induced mechanism forming dangling CH3 groups. 29Si SSNMR shows redistribution reactions between Si-O and Si-C bonds occurring between 600-1000°C leading to statistical distribution of SiC4-xOx environments. Bridging CH2 groups increase carbidic carbon and decrease free carbon relative to pendent Si-CH3 systems. NMR unit distributions from Table 1: CBS ceramic has Q=29.0%, T=41.0%, D=23.0%, C=7.0%, O/Si=1.42, Si-C bonds/Si=1.15. L-EPCS ceramic has Q=14.36%, T=39.65%, D=36.63%, M=5.88%, C=3.49%, O/Si=1.28, Si-C bonds/Si=1.44. Pyrolysis conducted under N2 at atmospheric pressure, flow rate ~25 cm3/min. 29Si SSNMR used single-pulse experiments; 13C used CP-MAS.

Crosslinking via hydroboration and dehydrocoupling converts sp2 vinyl carbons to sp3 carbon sites.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiHfBCN amorphous at 1100°C; converts to nanostructured composites upon annealing at 1300-1700°C
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Annealing in Ar yields HfC/HfB2/SiC nanocomposites; annealing in N2 yields HfN/Si3N4/SiBCN nanocomposites. XRD/TEM data at 1700°C Ar: HfB2 (4.4 wt%, 200 nm), HfC(N) (7.3 wt%, 39 nm), SiC (88.3 wt%, 112 nm) for SiHfBCN1a; HfB2 (18.8 wt%, 330 nm), HfC(N) (9.4 wt%, 64 nm), SiC (71.8 wt%, 49 nm) for SiHfBCN2a.

notes: The polymer HTT 1800 is the base polysilazane containing Si-H and Si-vinyl groups. It is modified with Hf(NEt2)4 (10 vol% or 30 vol% relative to HTT 1800) and BH3·SMe2 to form a single-source precursor for SiHfBCN ceramics. 29Si MAS NMR of crosslinked precursor at 200°C shows SiC2N2 (-3.5 ppm, 26.2%), SiHCN2 (-24 ppm, 60.0%), SiCN3 (-31 ppm, 13.8%). Green bodies warm-pressed at 260°C, 63 MPa. Two precursor compositions prepared: 90:10 and 70:30 HTT1800:Hf(NEt2)4 volume ratios. Ceramic yield of ~80 wt% vs ~65 wt% for unmodified HTT 1800. Heating rate for crosslinking: 50°C/h (0.833°C/min). Pyrolysis heating rate also 50°C/h. Raman spectroscopy performed on annealed samples showing D and G bands for carbon phase. EDS-estimated Hf content in pyrolyzed ceramics ranges ~22-29 wt%.

polymer_name: allyl-GNP (poly(1,1-dimethylpropylsilane)-grafted silica), vinyl-GNP (poly(1,1-dimethylethylsilane)-grafted silica), styryl-GNP (poly(1,1-dimethylbenzylethylsilane)-grafted silica)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Silica nanoparticle core comprises ~25 wt% of GNPs prior to thermolysis; no quantitative elemental atomic percentages reported

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-H absorption at ~900 cm-1 present in allyl-GNP and styryl-GNP but not vinyl-GNP; aromatic C-H and C=C bonds in styryl-GNP at 1600 cm-1 and >3000 cm-1; alkyl C-C and C-H between 2800-3000 cm-1; Si-O at ~1100 cm-1; Si-C/CH3-Si-O between 700-800 cm-1; Si-CH3 at 1246 cm-1

functional_groups.other: Aromatic benzene ring present in styryl-GNP brush (poly(1,1-dimethylbenzylethylsilane)); allyl group present in allyl-GNP monomer (allyldimethylsilane)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA run from RT to 800 C at 20 C/min under argon (100 mL/min). Below 200 C all three GNPs lose <6 wt% (solvent/water). Between 200-400 C: vinyl-GNP and allyl-GNP lose ~27 wt%, styryl-GNP loses ~15 wt%. Above 400 C (main chain breakdown): vinyl-GNP and allyl-GNP lose ~40 wt%, styryl-GNP loses ~47 wt%. At 800 C polymer brush is completely degraded; remaining mass primarily silica core (~25 wt%). After thermal treatment, ceramic yield improvement: allyl-GNP +21 wt%, vinyl-GNP +20 wt%, styryl-GNP +12 wt%. TGA not run above 1000 C due to concerns about carbon/Si pyrolysis products reacting with platinum TGA fixtures.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: Thermal treatment (vacuum oven, 2 C/min ramp to 160 C held 1 h, then 2 C/min ramp to 250 C held 1 h); ATR-FTIR showed no indication of chemical cross-linking; thermal jamming/brush interpenetration is proposed mechanism for yield improvement rather than covalent crosslinking

backbone_architecture.description: Polymer brushes grafted from silica nanoparticle surfaces (10-15 nm diameter) via hydrosilylation grafting-from chemistry. Brush lengths: allyl-GNP 6.1 ± 1.1 nm, styryl-GNP ~12 ± 2.3 nm, vinyl-GNP ~3 ± 0.75 nm as measured by DLS. Allyl-GNP and styryl-GNP follow beta-insertion hydrosilylation; vinyl-GNP shows mixture of alpha and beta insertions.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC/SiO2 composite (allyl-GNP and vinyl-GNP); beta-SiC with consumed SiO2 (styryl-GNP)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Allyl-GNP and vinyl-GNP pyrolyzed to 1400 C yield amorphous SiO2 (~22 deg 2theta) and beta-SiC (peaks at ~35, ~60, ~70 deg; planes (111),(220),(311)). beta-SiC peaks are low-intensity and broad indicating small crystalline domains. Styryl-GNP yields beta-SiC with well-defined narrow high-intensity peaks at ~35, ~41, ~60, ~70 deg (planes (111),(200),(220),(311)) indicating large crystalline domains; no SiO2 present, consumed via carbothermal reaction. Turbostratic/free carbon observed by Raman in styryl-GNP at 1000 and 1200 C (D band 1312 cm-1, G band 1607 cm-1) and consumed by 1400 C. beta-SiC begins forming in allyl-GNP at 1200 C; in styryl-GNP beta-SiC present at 1000 C. TEM shows amorphous particle structure at 1000 C for both; at 1400 C allyl-GNP forms fused amorphous mass while styryl-GNP shows distinct particle boundaries with stacking faults and crystal twinning in SiC.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Rheological properties reported: allyl-GNP noise temperature X=1.16 (strongest interparticle network), vinyl-GNP X=1.26, styryl-GNP X=1.30 (weakest interparticle network). Power law index m: allyl-GNP ~0.77, vinyl-GNP 0.62, styryl-GNP 0.41. Flow point (G' crosses G''): allyl-GNP ~22% strain, vinyl-GNP ~40% strain, styryl-GNP ~120% strain. All GNPs exhibit shear-thinning and rubbery plateau viscoelastic behavior at RT.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (allyl, vinyl, styryl-GNPs after pyrolysis to 1400 C); amorphous SiO2 (allyl-GNP and vinyl-GNP after pyrolysis to 1400 C); turbostratic carbon intermediate in styryl-GNP at 1000-1200 C

notes: Study reports three preceramic polymer grafted nanoparticle (GNP) systems synthesized via hydrosilylation grafting-from chemistry on 10-15 nm silica nanoparticles: (1) allyl-GNP with poly(1,1-dimethylpropylsilane) brush from allyldimethylsilane, (2) vinyl-GNP with poly(1,1-dimethylethylsilane) brush from vinyldimethylsilane, (3) styryl-GNP with poly(1,1-dimethylbenzylethylsilane) brush from synthesized styryldimethylsilane (4-vinylphenyl)dimethylsilane. Karstedt's catalyst (Pt) used. Silica nanoparticles pre-functionalized with methylsilane monolayer via dichloromethylsilane. Allyl-GNP is from a previously reported study; vinyl-GNP and styryl-GNP are novel. The three GNPs are structurally distinct in brush length, brush composition (aliphatic vs. aromatic), and resulting ceramic phase. Aromatic brush (styryl-GNP) enables carbothermal reduction of silica core at 1400 C producing pure beta-SiC with large crystalline domains, while aliphatic brushes (allyl- and vinyl-GNP) retain amorphous SiO2 alongside small-domain beta-SiC. No molecular weight data reported. Ceramic yield improvement attributed to physical densification/thermal jamming of brushes rather than chemical crosslinking.

notes: This is a comprehensive review article (Birot, Pillot, Dunogues, University Bordeaux I) covering preceramic polymer routes to SiC, Si3N4, and Si/C/N ceramics. It covers polycarbosilanes (PCSs), polysilazanes (PSZs), and polycarbosilazanes (PCSZs). Tabulated data show ceramic yields ranging from ~2.5% to ~88% and molecular weights from ~850 to ~78,800 g/mol with PDI values from 1.1 to 16 for various polymer compositions. The review emphasizes the Yajima strategy (PDMS -> PCS via Kumada rearrangement) and direct PCS synthesis routes. Key design principles for preceramic polymers are discussed including high molecular weight, ring/cage structures, viscoelastic processability, latent reactivity for crosslinking, and low organic group content. Elemental compositions reported in tables for PCSZ series show Si ~40-52%, C ~24-42%, N ~3-23%, O ~0.8-2%, H ~7-10% by weight percent (not atomic percent).

notes: Three polymer systems evaluated as ceramic fiber interface coatings for ceramic matrix composites on SCS-0 fibers (143 micron diameter). Coating thicknesses by Auger: 40-200 nm range. Polysilsesquioxane phenyl:methyl ratios examined: 5/95, 10/90, 30/70, 50/50; diluted in methanol at 5-15 wt% for dip coating. Polyborosilazane coated from 20% THF solution. Polyvinylsilane coated from 10% cyclohexene solution. Polyborosilazane remains amorphous to 1600°C with boron incorporation at 1:4 B:Si ratio. RBSN matrix found to be non-ideal model system due to nitrogen incorporation during nitriding. Future work planned with CVD SiC matrix microcomposites. Paper presented at 19th Annual Conference on Composites, Advanced Ceramics, Materials and Structures, Cocoa Beach, Florida, American Ceramic Society.

notes: This paper is NOT about preceramic polymers. It describes a binder jetting additive manufacturing process for SiCw/SiC ceramic matrix composites using SiC whisker composite microspheres (SiCw-CMS) prepared by spray drying and chemical vapor infiltration (CVI), followed by reactive melt infiltration (RMI) of liquid silicon. The furfural resin is used only as a porous carbon precursor to create infiltration channels, not as the primary preceramic polymer for the ceramic matrix. The binder system uses acrylamide (AAm) and N,N'-methylenebis(acrylamide) (Bis) with ammonium persulfate (APS) initiator as a thermally initiated crosslinking binder for binder jetting only. CVI precursor is methyltrichlorosilane (MTS, CH3SiCl3) at 1000°C, 5 kPa, 30 h. Furfural resin pyrolysis: argon atmosphere, 900°C, 2 h, heating rate 5°C/min. RMI: vacuum, 1600°C, 1 h, heating rate 10°C/min. Composite density up to 2.89 g/cm3, thermal conductivity 110.4 W/(m·K) at room temperature, CTE 4.0-5.4×10^-6 K^-1, resistivity 7.09 Ω·cm. Most descriptor fields are null because the paper does not describe a preceramic polymer system.

It is not a preceramic polymer chemistry paper. No preceramic polymer data, pyrolysis data, bonding structure, molecular weight, or related polymer descriptors are present in the text. The document covers borides, carbides, nitrides, silicides, beryllides, oxides, ceramic fibers, and ceramic matrix composites from a performance and materials selection perspective.

notes: This paper is a materials informatics/machine learning study of polymer-derived SiOC ceramics using a dataset of 2070 records from 223 literature sources. It does not characterize a single polymer but rather analyzes trends across many SiOC precursor systems. Five sub-datasets were used: composition (638 points), density (132 points), shrinkage (311 points), yield (875 points), and strength (114 points). Features include precursor elemental composition (Si, O, C, H in atomic percent) and pyrolysis conditions. Seven ML models were evaluated (LR, BR, SVR, KR, KNN, RF, XGB). Best MAE after tuning: composition 2.72 at%, yield 8.56%, shrinkage 5.64%, density 0.196 g/cm3, strength 91.2 MPa. Correlation analysis (PCC and MIC) ranked feature importance for each target. Data collected up to August 4, 2020 from Web of Science.

SiC shows maximum relative mass loss of 2.7 percentage points between 711 and 1200 °C during preheating. (Hf0.2Ta0.8)C/SiC and (Hf0.7Ta0.3)C/SiC show mass loss onset at 827 °C and 848 °C respectively, ending at 966 °C and 989 °C. Chemical modification with Hf and Ta leads to up to 78% reduction in mass loss compared to SiC.

backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosilane-based precursor chemically modified with Hf and Ta amido complexes to form Si(HfxTa1-x)C single-source precursors; two Hf/Ta ratios used (x=0.2 and x=0.7)

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC with (HfxTa1-x)C precipitates; after oxidation: SiO2, Hf6Ta2O17, Ta2O5, HfO2, TaC phases detected
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Microstructure after FAST-densification consists of finely distributed (HfxTa1-x)C precipitates within former powder particles; beta-SiC with larger grain sizes forms sinter necks between former powder particles. (Hf0.2Ta0.8)C/SiC forms Ta2O5 and Hf6Ta2O17 upon oxidation; (Hf0.7Ta0.3)C/SiC forms Hf6Ta2O17 and HfO2 (no Ta2O5). Free carbon in graphite form (sp2) present before oxidation, disappears after. Cristobalite SiO2 detected at 1400 °C for all materials.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Values cited as general UHTC class properties (>=20 GPa hardness, >=300 GPa Young's modulus), not specific to these polymer-derived samples

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: alpha-SiC (PDF 72-0018), beta-SiC (PDF 74-2307), (HfxTa1-x)C solid solution (PDF 19-6861), free carbon/graphite (PDF 75-1621); after oxidation: cristobalite SiO2 (PDF 39-1425), orthorhombic Ta2O5 (PDF 25-0922), orthorhombic Hf6Ta2O17 (PDF 44-0998), monoclinic HfO2 (PDF 34-0104), cubic TaC (PDF 35-0801)

notes: This paper focuses primarily on oxidation behavior of polymer-derived (HfxTa1-x)C/SiC nanocomposite ceramics at 1200-1400 °C for up to 100 h, not on precursor characterization. The polymer is described as a polycarbosilane-based precursor modified with Hf and Ta amido complexes. Consolidation performed by field-assisted sintering technique (FAST). Density of (HfxTa1-x)C/SiC ~95%, SiC ~91%. Porosity of chemically modified samples: ~5% with pore size <=3 um; SiC: ~9% with pore size <=20 um. Nanosized pores up to ~30 nm found within former powder particles. (Hf0.7Ta0.3)C/SiC shows improved oxidation behavior over (Hf0.2Ta0.8)C/SiC due to Hf6Ta2O17 formation and reduced Ta2O5 cracking. Porosity midpoint used for elemental composition field: 5% reported for (HfxTa1-x)C/SiC samples.
source: Adv Eng Mater - 2024 - Petry - Oxidation Resistance and Microstructural Analysis of Polymer%E2%80%90Derived  HfxTa1 x C SiC Ceramic

elemental_composition.other_elements: After sintering at 1800C: O content 0.31 wt%, N content 0.32 wt%, with C and Si as primary elements. Intermediate SiCO-N at 1300C: Si, C, N, O present with O=18.64 wt%, N=10.08 wt%. C/Si atomic ratio ranges from 3.37 to 9.59 depending on polysiloxane:PAN ratio.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: SiC2O2 bonding identified by 29Si MAS NMR (peak at -34 ppm); beta-SiC identified by peak at -24 ppm; sp2 hybridized free carbon forming conductive pathways; C-O-N amorphous phase (SiCxOyNz) in intermediate product at 1300C

functional_groups.other: Polysiloxane provides Si source; PAN (polyacrylonitrile) provides C source; no specific functional groups on polymer precursors described beyond their role as Si and C sources

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Multi-stage processing: UV curing in air, then 1300C/1h to form amorphous SiCO-N intermediate, then 1800C/1h in inert atmosphere to form C-SiC. At 1800C, O content reduced from 18.64 wt% to 0.31 wt% and N from 10.08 to 0.32 wt%. Gaseous species SiO, CO, N2 released during high-temperature sintering. Material also stable at 2000C for 1h in Ar with ~99% mass retention.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV irradiation followed by thermal crosslinking in air atmosphere

backbone_architecture.description: Polysiloxane and PAN blended spinning solution processed by centrifugal spinning into fibrous aerogel with 3D randomly interwoven fiber network; fibers exhibit core-shell architecture after high-temperature sintering with dense SiC outer shell and loose carbon-rich core (momordica charantia-like structure)

microstructural.ceramic_phase: C-SiC (beta-SiC with free carbon; trace alpha-SiC; residual SiC2O2)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Primary phase is beta-SiC with XRD peaks at 35.6, 60.0, 71.8 degrees (111, 200, 311 planes). Weak alpha-SiC peak at (100) plane. Graphite (002) peak at 2theta=26.2 degrees. 29Si MAS NMR shows beta-SiC at -24 ppm and SiC2O2 at -34 ppm. Intermediate at 1300C is amorphous SiCxOyNz. Increasing graphitization with temperature confirmed by Raman spectroscopy.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Tensile strength 97.9 kPa; compressive resilience at strain epsilon=60% for 85 cycles; linear elastic region at epsilon<10%, plastic deformation at 10%<epsilon<65%; stable load-bearing at 10-60% strain for 10 cycles; energy loss coefficient ~25%; recovers shape after 180 degree bending; withstands load ~6500x its own weight

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (dominant, cubic, peaks at 35.6, 60.0, 71.8 degrees 2theta corresponding to 111, 200, 311 planes); alpha-SiC (minor, peak at 100 plane); graphite (002 plane at 2theta=26.2 degrees); SiCO-N intermediate at 1300C is amorphous with broad peak at ~25 degrees

notes: Precursor system is polysiloxane (Si source) and polyacrylonitrile/PAN (C source) blended at various ratios (polysiloxane:PAN ratios of 0.5 to 3). Fabrication involves centrifugal spinning, UV curing in air, pyrolysis at 1300C/1h, then sintering at 1800C/1h in inert atmosphere. Final C-SiC fibrous aerogel density: 3.9 mg/cm3. Thermal conductivity: 9.12 mW/m/K at room temperature, 181.11 mW/m/K at 1000C. Specific surface area up to 373.23 m2/g. Hierarchical pore sizes: micropores, mesopores (majority, average 4.6-7.1 nm), macropores. EMI SE up to 53.1 dB (X-band); SSE/t up to 346,828.6 dB cm2/g for C-SiC-1 sample (density 3.9 mg/cm3, thickness 0.38 mm). High-temperature stability demonstrated at 2000C/1h in Ar. Oxidation resistance up to 1000C in air (10 min). Corrosion resistance in 1M HCl and 6M NaOH for 7 days. The paper does not report specific molecular weight or crosslink density values for the polymer precursors.
source: Advanced Science - 2026 - Yang - Bioinspired Multifunctional Flexible C%E2%80%90SiC Fibrous Aerogel for Superior Electromagnetic

polymer_name: Silres H44 (silicone resin) combined with photocurable acrylate resin (FunToDo Industrial Blend Transparent)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ca from calcium nitrate tetrahydrate filler; SiO2:CaO ratio = 70:30 mol% targeting 70S30C bioglass composition

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-C bonds present in SiOC ceramic residue after pyrolysis; oxynitride phases formed at high temperatures (>=1300 C) under flowing N2

functional_groups.other: Acrylate and glycol diacrylate monomers from FunToDo resin; phosphine oxide-based photoinitiator; Span 80 (Sorbitan Monooleate) surfactant

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Heating schedule: 0.5 C/min to 500 C with 5-h dwell, then 1 C/min to 1000 C, then 2 C/min to Tmax (up to 1400 C) with 3-h dwell. Multiple Tmax investigated: 700, 900, 1100, 1200, 1300, 1350, 1400 C. Scaffolds remain predominantly amorphous at 700 C with minor crystalline CaCO3. Elongated crystals form from 1300 C onwards. Silres H44 has 53 wt% SiO2 yield.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV photopolymerization (MSLA, lambda=405 nm) followed by thermal curing at 60 C for 24 h

backbone_architecture.description: Silicone resin (Silres H44) powder combined with photocurable acrylate resin to form emulsion-based ink; emulsion contains nanoscale calcium nitrate tetrahydrate droplets dispersed in silicone-acrylate matrix stabilized by Span 80 surfactant

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 700 C: predominantly amorphous SiOC with minor CaCO3. At >=1300 C: elongated crystalline phases appear, oxynitride phases form (Si3N4 via carbothermal reduction and nitridation reactions: SiO2+C->SiO+CO, then 3SiO+3C+2N2->Si3N4+3CO). Pyrolytic carbon dispersed in C-doped silica glass matrix. Phase separation: 2SiOC->SiO2+SiC+C noted.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Compressive strength values for gyroid scaffolds at various Tmax: 700C/75%: 7.9 MPa, 700C/85%: 2.9 MPa; 900C/75%: 10.0 MPa, 900C/85%: 6.15 MPa; 1100C/75%: 10.7 MPa, 1100C/85%: 5.9 MPa; 1200C/75%: 5.3 MPa, 1200C/85%: 5.2 MPa; 1300C/75%: 8.8 MPa, 1300C/85%: 4.0 MPa; 1350C/75%: 5.5 MPa, 1350C/85%: 1.9 MPa; 1400C/75%: 5.5 MPa, 1400C/85%: 1.3 MPa. Tests on 10x10x10 mm cubic specimens, crosshead speed 0.5 mm/min, n>=5.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Predominantly amorphous at 700 C; minor CaCO3 at 700 C; elongated crystalline phases (likely Si3N4 and oxynitride phases) emerging from 1300 C under N2 atmosphere

notes: Material is a preceramic polymer-derived 70S30C bioglass analog processed via emulsion-based PDC route. Emulsion formulation: 8.74 g Silres H44 + 22 g FunToDo acrylate resin + 7.68 g Ca(NO3)2·4H2O + 2 g Span 80 surfactant. Gyroid scaffolds (75% and 85% model porosity) fabricated by MSLA (Prusa SL1S, 405 nm). Porosity ranges from ~70-91% depending on model porosity and Tmax. True densities increase with Tmax reaching up to 3.30 g/cm3 at 1400 C/85% model. Bioactivity tested by SBF immersion (Kokubo protocol) and demineralized water immersion at 37 C up to 28 days. Rapid hydroxyapatite formation observed with mild pH increases. XRD and FTIR used to track nitridation. Carbothermal reduction and nitridation reactions occur at high temperatures producing Si3N4.
source: Advanced bioceramics from vat-photopolymerization of silicone-based emulsions- From bioglass to oxynitrides

polymer_name: poly(phenyl)siloxane (PPS, H62C, Wacker Chemie) and poly(methyl)siloxane (PMS, MK, Wacker-Belsil)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-phenyl groups present in PPS; SiOC random tetrahedral network formed after pyrolysis

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups in PPS

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PPS loses 22-27 wt% during pyrolysis at 900-1500C; PMS loses 14-17 wt%. Multi-step heating: ramp to 400C at 5C/min hold 30 min, ramp to 530C at 5C/min hold 60 min, ramp to final temperature at 5C/min hold 90 min. Higher mass loss of PPS attributed to lower ceramic yield and higher free carbon content relative to PMS. Harshe et al. reported 12.5% mass loss for PMS.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal with catalyst: PPS uses platinum catalyst; PMS uses Zr-acetylacetonate (1.5 wt%) catalyst, cured at 220C in open-air

backbone_architecture.description: Polysiloxane backbone; PPS is a solvent-free liquid resin; PMS is a solid solvent-free resin. After curing, a crosslinked network is formed. Pyrolysis yields random three-dimensional arrangement of tetrahedral silicon atoms bonded to carbon and oxygen (SiOC glass).

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC (amorphous below 1300C), beta-SiC (crystalline above 1300-1500C); with Ti filler: TiC, TiSi, TiO within amorphous SiOC matrix
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOxCy formed up to 1300C under Ar; beta-SiC crystalline phase appears above 1300C (XRD peaks at 2theta=36 and 60 degrees at 1500C). With active Ti filler: TiC forms at 900C, TiSi and TiO appear at 1100-1300C, TiC dominant at 1500C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Vickers hardness (HV10, 100N load, 0.2 mm/min): neat PPS max 8.88 GPa at 1100C; neat PMS max 10.67 GPa at 1100C; Ti-filled PPS composites up to 13.20 +/- 2.05 GPa; Ti-filled PMS composites reduced hardness relative to neat PMS for all concentrations; maximum observed hardness up to ~14 GPa for PPS composites.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: amorphous SiOxCy (below 1300C); beta-SiC (above 1300C); with Ti filler: TiC, TiSi, TiO

notes: Two polysiloxanes studied: PPS (H62C, Wacker Chemie, phenyl-containing, liquid) and PMS (MK, Wacker-Belsil, methyl-containing, solid). Ceramic matrix composites (CMCs) fabricated with 60-80 wt% active Ti filler by warm pressing at 15 MPa and 220C. Pyrolysis temperatures ranged 900-1500C under Ar. Ceramic yield range: PPS 73-78% (mass loss 22-27%), PMS 83-86% (mass loss 14-17%); midpoint ceramic yield reported as 81.5% is estimated average; range noted. Ti filler reduces mass loss to ~1.5% for PMS and ~2% for PPS. Greil (ref 4) reported 20-30 wt% weight loss for similar phenyl and methyl polysiloxanes. XRD, SEM-EDX, Vickers hardness, and optical microscopy used for characterization. EDX data (wt%) for pyrolyzed regions provided in tables showing Si, C, O, and Ti distributions.
source: Akkas_2006_Silicon oxycarbide-based composites produced from pyrolysis of polysiloxanes

polymer_name: PSZ (polysilazane); PASZ (polyaluminosilazane) - SiAlCN-5, SiAlCN-10, SiAlCN-15 precursors

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ceramic product elemental compositions (EDS, at.%): SiAlCN-5: C=38.37, Si=34.68, N=26.72, Al=0.23; SiAlCN-10: C=46.76, Si=40.06, N=10.86, Al=2.31; SiAlCN-15: C=48.17, Si=36.40, N=10.23, Al=5.20. These are ceramic phase compositions, not precursor polymer compositions.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Al-N bonds present in PASZ precursors (FT-IR peaks at 1370 and 1383 cm-1); C-H stretching vibration at ~2950 cm-1

functional_groups.other: Al-N functionality introduced via dehydrogenation coupling reaction of aluminum isopropoxide (AIP) with PSZ

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pure PSZ showed total weight loss of 42.61% under N2 (ceramic yield ~57.39%). PASZ precursors showed significantly reduced weight loss of 22.39%-26.50% (ceramic yield ~73.50%-77.61%), indicating Al doping improves ceramic yield. PSZ showed continuous endothermic effect 0-600C (organic side chain cleavage), broad exothermic peak 600-800C (backbone rearrangement, dehydrocoupling, ceramization). PASZ showed additional exothermic peaks after 800C attributed to crystallization. Pre-pyrolysis step at 800C (5C/min, 1h hold) followed by hot-press sintering to 1300C (3C/min from 800C, 30 min hold at 1300C under 50 MPa). Curing at 160C (1C/min, 2h hold).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - curing at 160C under N2 for 2h; additional crosslinking via dehydrocoupling/transamination at 600-800C

backbone_architecture.description: Three-dimensional amorphous network structure characteristic of PDCs. PSZ backbone retained in PASZ with Al atoms incorporated via Al-N bond formation through dehydrogenation coupling reaction with AIP.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN / SiAlCN - amorphous for low Al content; beta-SiC and Si3N4 nanocrystals precipitate at higher Al content
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiCN and SiAlCN-5 showed predominantly amorphous structure by XRD. SiAlCN-10 showed weak crystalline peaks. SiAlCN-15 showed pronounced crystalline diffraction peaks corresponding to beta-SiC and Si3N4. Al doping promotes crystallization via heterogeneous nucleation. Free carbon phase present (D and G bands in Raman). ID/IG ratio increases from 1.37 to 2.28 with increasing Al content, indicating increasing disordered carbon defects.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to semi-crystalline depending on Al content
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC and Si3N4 (in SiAlCN-10 and SiAlCN-15); amorphous humps dominant in SiCN and SiAlCN-5

notes: Paper focuses on SiAlCN ceramics derived from polyaluminosilazane (PASZ) precursors for X-band microwave absorption. PASZ synthesized by dehydrogenation coupling of AIP and PSZ in n-octane at 55C for 36h under N2. AIP additions of 5, 10, 15 wt%. Hot-press sintering at 1300C, 50 MPa, 30 min under N2. Electrical conductivity of ceramics: SiCN=3.8e4 S/m, SiAlCN-5=9.9e4 S/m, SiAlCN-10=0.4 S/m, SiAlCN-15=18.8 S/m. Best microwave absorption: SiAlCN-5 at 2.1 mm thickness achieved RL_min=-19.94 dB and EAB=2.82 GHz in X-band. Ceramic yield range for PASZ: 73.50%-77.61% (midpoint ~75.5% used for ceramic_yield_pct field as representative value; pure PSZ yield ~57.39%). Elemental compositions in elemental_composition field refer to ceramic products not precursor polymers.
source: Al-doped SiCN ceramics for high-efficiency electromagnetic wave absorption in the X-band

elemental_composition.other_elements: Al, N, O (~0.85 wt%), C (<0.1 wt%), Cl (<0.02 wt%), Ca, Fe, Mg as impurities; CaF2 used as sintering aid

microstructural.ceramic_phase: AlN (wurtzite-type hexagonal crystal structure); secondary phases CaAl2O4 and Ca2Al2O5 detected after sintering, removed after annealing
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD shows AlN as only crystalline phase in as-synthesized powder; after sintering with CaF2, secondary phases CaAl2O4 and Ca2Al2O5 present; after 16h annealing at 1850C in carbon-containing atmosphere secondary phases eliminated by carbothermal reduction

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: AlN ceramics reported to have hardness ~10 GPa, strength 300-400 MPa; brittle-to-ductile transition reported at ~840 MPa under multiaxial loading

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: AlN (wurtzite, hexagonal); CaAl2O4 and Ca2Al2O5 as secondary phases after sintering; secondary phases absent after annealing

notes: This paper does not describe a preceramic polymer. It describes synthesis and processing of aluminum nitride (AlN) ceramic powder via gas-phase reaction of AlCl3 with NH3 at 1000-1800C in nitrogen atmosphere. The powder had specific surface area of 7.5 m2/g, oxygen content ~0.85 wt%, C <0.1 wt%, Cl <0.02 wt%. CaF2 was used as sintering aid (2 wt%). Sintering at 1800C in N2 atmosphere; annealing at 1850C in nitrogen in carbon-containing furnace for up to 16h. Thermal conductivity increased from 120 W/mK (sintered) to 220 W/mK after 16h annealing for specimen with 4 wt% CaF2. Average particle size ~0.4 micron, 90% of particles 0.2-1.2 micron. Theoretical thermal conductivity of single crystal AlN ~320 W/mK. All preceramic polymer fields are null as this paper is not relevant to preceramic polymer chemistry.
source: Aluminum Nitride Ceramic ith High Thermal Conductivity from Gas-Phased Synthesized Powders

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-C network in SiOC glass/ceramic; free carbon present; SiO2 clusters and graphitic carbon rings (6-membered) observed in MD simulation

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis of titanium isopropoxide and polycarbosiloxane at 1400 C yields TiC/SiOC ceramic with SiC and TiC phases identified by XRD

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - cured at 120 C in oven with Al2O3-based adhesive acting as catalytic curing matrix

backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosiloxane precursor used to derive SiOC ceramic/glass composite; Si, O, C randomly distributed initially, forming network upon pyrolysis

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: TiC (cubic, ~20 nm average crystallite size, spherical, uniformly dispersed) and SiC (Moissanite 3C, cubic) phases identified by XRD and TEM/EDS after pyrolysis at 1400 C; free carbon and SiO2 clusters also present

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Erosion testing showed no mass loss under normal impact conditions; minor brittle cracks ~4 um observed after erosion; no radial cracking detected

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: TiC (Titanium Carbide, Cubic, PDF 98-009-3029), SiC (Moissanite 3C, Cubic, PDF 98-001-1866), Al2O3 (Alpha, Hexagonal, PDF 98-003-2973)

notes: The polymer precursor is polycarbosiloxane combined with titanium isopropoxide (25 wt% weight ratio) to form TiC/SiOC ceramic after pyrolysis at 1400 C. The resulting TiC/SiOC material is used as an EM-absorbing filler mixed with Al2O3 adhesive (20, 50, or 80 wt%) and applied as a coating on CFRP. The paper is primarily focused on electromagnetic wave absorption performance rather than polymer precursor characterization. ReaxFF MD simulations were used to study SiOC nanostructure evolution at ~1400 C, showing formation of graphitic carbon rings and SiO2 clusters. Curing of the coating was performed at 120 C. TiC crystallites are ~20 nm in size.
source: An ultrathin polymer-derived UHTCs coating on CFRP substrate_ Effective electromagnetic wave absorber

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ti incorporated via tetrabutyl orthotitanate at Ti:Si = 0.2 mol%; final ceramic contains Si, Ti, C, N, O as confirmed by EDS

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Ti bonds formed during crosslinking via substitution reaction between Si-H of PVS and Ti-O of tetrabutyl orthotitanate; vinyl groups present

functional_groups.other: 20% methyl/vinyl and 80% methyl/hydride silazane based monomers; tetrabutyl orthotitanate used as Ti dopant precursor

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: No mass loss up to 300°C; continuous mass loss of 20.65% from 300°C to 750°C attributed to evaporation of H2, CH4, and hydrocarbons; polymer-to-ceramic transformation complete at 750°C; additional ~1% mass loss from 1100°C to 1500°C attributed to loss of hydrogen or excess oxygen from Ti precursor; total ceramic yield 78.2 wt% (theoretical yield 71.1 wt%); DSC shows exothermic peak at ~1328°C and endothermic peak at 1445°C indicating new phase development and crystallization

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal crosslinking at 300°C for 2 hours with 1 wt% dicumyl peroxide (DCP) as initiator; crosslinking involves Si-O-Ti bond formation, hydrosilylation between vinyl and Si-H groups, and polymerization of vinyl groups

backbone_architecture.description: Polyvinylsilazane crosslinked with tetrabutyl orthotitanate to form a thermoset solid; crosslinked product described as a pale yellow solid (thermoset) after heating at 300°C for 2 hours

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiTiCNO - amorphous SiCN matrix with nanocrystalline TiO2 (anatase and rutile), TiC, TiC0.3N0.7, and SiO2 nanodomains at high temperatures
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: 900-1100°C: fully amorphous monophasic SiTiCNO; 1200°C: anatase-TiO2 nanocrystals appear in amorphous SiCN matrix (crystallite size 6.1 nm); 1300°C: anatase-TiO2 (9.9 nm) + rutile-TiO2 (2.2 nm) + TiC0.3N0.7 (2.7 nm); 1400°C: anatase-TiO2 (10.4 nm) + rutile-TiO2 (13.6 nm) + TiC (4.6 nm) + TiC0.3N0.7 (3.2 nm) + SiO2 nanodomains + possible Si2N2O phase; free carbon phase (Cfree) present throughout; Ti doping accelerates Cfree separation and improves graphitic order

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: TiC phase referenced as having high hardness of 28-35 GPa (literature value cited, not measured in this study)

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Anatase-TiO2 (JCPDS 21-1272), Rutile-TiO2 (JCPDS 77-0441), TiC0.3N0.7 (JCPDS 42-1488), TiC (JCPDS 73-0472); Si2N2O (JCPDS 84-1814) identified by HRTEM only; amorphous SiCN matrix persists throughout

notes: Polymer is commercially available Durazane 1800 (polyvinylsilazane) from Merck Chemicals, doped with tetrabutyl orthotitanate (Ti(OC4H9)4, Alfa Aesar) at Ti:Si = 0.2 mol%. Crosslinking performed at 300°C for 2h under N2 with 1 wt% dicumyl peroxide. Pyrolysis temperatures ranged 900-1400°C at 2°C/min under flowing N2 (80 ml/min). Raman spectroscopy showed D and G bands for all pyrolyzed Ti-doped samples including at 900°C, indicating earlier Cfree formation than undoped SiCN. G band redshift from 1614 to 1590 cm-1 between 1200°C and 1300°C indicates graphitization. Carbon nanocrystallite lateral size (La) ~2.4-3.8 nm range across samples. TEM/HRTEM confirmed uniform distribution of nanocrystals in amorphous SiCN matrix at 1400°C. Crystallite sizes from Scherrer equation and HRTEM in good agreement. This is a preprint that has not undergone peer review.
source: Anand_2022_A Novel TiO2TiCTiC03N07CSiCN Multiphase Ceramic Nanocomposite from Preceramic

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present in varying amounts; specific atomic percentages not reported, only weight percent ranges in derived ceramics (e.g. 6 wt%, 14.2 wt%, 16.3 wt% B in ceramics)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C-B-C crosslinks; B-N bonds including borazine rings (11B NMR resonance 32-34 ppm); N=C=N carbodi-imide units in some precursors; B-C bonds from hydroboration of vinyl groups

functional_groups.other: carbodi-imide (N=C=N) groups in polysilylcarbodi-imide-derived precursors; borazine rings

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA under 0.1 MPa helium at 5 K/min: Si-B-C-N ceramic (from polymer 4, pyrolysed at 1100C) showed thermal degradation onset above 2000C; 6 wt% weight loss after 2h at 2000C. Si3B3N7 powder degradation in helium started above 1550C with 35 wt% loss at 1800C. Ceramic yield varies by polymer: up to 90 wt% for monomethyl-substituted polyborosilazane under ammonia; 62 wt% for polymer 4 under argon; 64 wt% for hydroborated methylvinylpolysilylcarbodi-imide; 70 wt% for SiBN3C fibres; 60-70 wt% for polymethylborosilazane 9.

crosslink_density.value: qualitative; increasing borane content increases crosslink density; dimethyl-substituted polysilylcarbodi-imide forms gel after 24h at room temperature with BH3·S(CH3)2
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal and chemical (hydroboration, H2 elimination during heat treatment)

molecular_weight.measurement_method: not specified; value reported as average molecular weight Mn for N-methylpolyborosilazane 8; PMVS starting polymer Mn=831 g/mol, hydroborated product 2 Mn=1224 g/mol

backbone_architecture.description: Cyclic methylsilazane units [-R1R2Si-NH-]n (n=2,3,4) crosslinked via C-B-C bonds; also linear polysilane chains branched via B-C bridges; borazine rings present in some variants; highly crosslinked three-dimensional networks for Si-B-C-N systems

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous Si-B-C-N up to >1700C; above 1700C nanocrystalline beta-Si3N4/beta-SiC composite forms. Polymer 4-derived ceramic: molar composition SiB0.34C1.47N0.68, 6 wt% B, density 2.5 g/cm3. Polymer 5-derived ceramic: SiB0.16C1.04N0.89, 3 wt% B; crystallization of beta-Si3N4 and beta-SiC above 1600C. Hydroborated methylvinylpolysilylcarbodi-imide ceramic: SiB0.26C1.85N1.x (6.1 wt% B). notes: Study investigates transient microporosity evolution in methyl-silsesquioxane microspheres (~2 µm nominal diameter) pyrolyzed in Ar, Ar-5%H2, CO2, and air at 700-1250°C. Common structural evolution detected up to 700°C across all atmospheres: redistribution reactions only, large open micropores (~1.2-1.7 nm) formed, medium-range order becomes more disordered (SAXS). At 700°C pore volumes: Ar 0.18 cm3/g, Ar-H2 0.17 cm3/g, CO2 0.20 cm3/g, average pore diameters 1.06-1.27 nm. Between 700-800°C, ceramization begins with formation of new ~1.1 nm open micropores and increased BET surface area (up to 529 m2/g in Ar at 800°C). At 900°C, open micropores partially annihilate in Ar and Ar-H2, but totally collapse in CO2 due to more silica-like viscous network. At 1250°C, SAXS detects persistent closed nanovoids (~1 nm) in Ar and Ar-H2 samples. Raman analysis at 1250°C: La (graphitic domain size) ~2.4 nm in Ar and Ar-H2, ~3.0 nm in CO2; ID/IG ratios 0.13, 0.32, and 0.21 respectively. Skeletal density stabilizes at ~2.40 g/cm3 for Ar and Ar-H2 at high temperatures; CO2 and air treated samples converge to SiO2 glass density (~2.2 g/cm3) at 1250°C. Characterization methods: TGA, FTIR, Raman, SAXS, N2 physisorption (BET/DFT), SEM, skeletal density measurements. Precursor SAXS radius of gyration Rg = 0.48 nm, hydrodynamic radius Rhs = 0.893 nm.

notes: This paper focuses on curing kinetics of SMP-10 (AHPCS) using DSC at heating rates 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, and 10°C/min over 50-400°C in nitrogen atmosphere. Sample mass ~20±2 mg. Key findings: (1) Pure SMP-10 cures at ~250°C without initiators; radical initiators lower onset curing temperature. (2) Apparent activation energy (Ea) increases with initiators: ~116-122 kJ/mol for pure SMP-10, ~141-153 kJ/mol for SMP-10+DCP, ~155-156 kJ/mol for SMP-10+Luperox 101. (3) Thermodynamic analysis via transition state theory shows the acceleration is driven by entropy of activation (ΔS‡) shifting from negative (~-63 J/mol·K, pure) to positive values (~77 J/mol·K for DCP, ~85 J/mol·K for Luperox), not by reduction in enthalpic barrier. Gibbs free energy of activation (ΔG‡): 142.78 kJ/mol (pure), 116.88 kJ/mol (DCP), 117.95 kJ/mol (Luperox). Reaction mechanism identified as nucleation-and-growth (Avrami-Erofeev A2) for all systems. SMP-10 was preheated at 100°C in vacuum oven before initiator addition to remove low molecular weight oligomers. FT-IR used to monitor Si-H, C=C, and SiCH2 group changes during curing. Kissinger Ea: 109.3 kJ/mol (pure), 133.1 kJ/mol (DCP), 170.1 kJ/mol (Luperox 101). Ozawa Ea: 111.6 kJ/mol (pure), 133.0 kJ/mol (DCP), 168.2 kJ/mol (Luperox 101).

notes: This paper is a data-driven meta-analysis and machine learning study covering 284 publications on polymer-derived SiC ceramic systems, not a primary experimental study on a single preceramic polymer. It reports a curated dataset of 785 extracted entries and 358 entries with reported curing temperatures. Key findings: median curing temperatures by catalyst type range from 120 C (iodine) to 205 C (boron-based). A supervised XGBoost classification model predicts low-temperature curing (<=140 C) with 89% accuracy. A trade-off exists between low curing temperature and ceramic yield. The 140 C threshold was adopted as upper bound for low-temperature curing based on requirements for embedded vascular channel composites and 3D-printed green bodies. Iodine and peroxide catalysts are associated with lowest curing temperatures. Specific polymer names referenced as examples include Durazane 1800 (polyorganosilazane) and AHPCS (allyl-hydridopolycarbosilane).

notes: This paper is a computational DFT study of amorphous SiOC atomic structure, not a polymer synthesis/characterization paper. No preceramic polymer is directly characterized. The study uses 864-atom SiO2 CRN supercell models with VASP (PBE functional, 300 eV cutoff). Key finding: H reverses C clustering tendency in SiOC CRN - without H, C-C interaction is attractive (negative NN interaction energy) favoring SiC4 units; with H, C-C interaction is repulsive (positive NN interaction energy) favoring SiCO3 units. Single C atom doping energies: without H = 4.89 ± 0.54 eV (DFT), with H = 8.28 ± 0.78 eV. NN C-C interaction energy without H is negative (attractive); with H passivation, positive (repulsive). Classical ReaxFF potential gave NN interaction energy of +0.47 ± 0.07 eV. SiOC synthesis methods referenced include CVD and sol-gel. Applications noted: Li-ion batteries, biotechnology, nuclear energy.
source: Ding_2015_Hydrogen reverses the clustering tendency of carbon in

notes: This paper does not involve preceramic polymers. It concerns direct ink writing (DIW) additive manufacturing of SiC ceramics using water-based SiC inks with different carbon sources (carbon black, flake graphite, graphitic carbon microspheres) followed by liquid silicon infiltration (LSI) at 1550 C for 3 h under argon. The ink composition is: water 33.4 wt%, PEG-400 0.4 wt%, stearic acid (SA) 0.2 wt%, SiC 57-63 wt%, carbon source 3-9 wt%; optimal formulation used 6 wt% carbon source. Relative densities: CB 98.6%, FG 97.2%, GCMs 98.8%. GCMs (graphitic carbon microspheres, synthesized from sucrose waste via hydrothermal carbonization and catalytic graphitization) showed best performance. SiC raw material: >=99.5 wt% purity, d50=3.5 um. CB: d50=1.67 um, BET=225.3 m2/g, O=7%. FG: d50=1.90 um, BET=16.1 m2/g, O=1%. GCMs: d50=1.48 um, BET=276.3 m2/g, O=0%. All mechanical values listed are for GCMs sample as best performer. None of the descriptors for preceramic polymer chemistry apply to this work.

Main polymer-to-ceramic conversion up to 800°C (region D) with methane and hydrogen release; further rearrangements to 1000°C in 2DVB. notes: Study focuses on transient microporosity formation during pyrolysis of PSZ and DVB-modified PSZ (2DVB). notes: Paper focuses on SiC nanowire-reinforced SiOC ceramics derived from polysiloxane pyrolysis with ferrocene (0, 3, 5 wt%) as catalyst at 1350, 1400, 1450C. Ceramic yield of 70.79 wt% (pure PSO) and 77.6 wt% (5 wt% ferrocene) measured at 800C. Empirical formulas of final ceramics range from SiC1.49O1.71 to SiC1.08O1.20 depending on conditions. Open porosity ranges 19-47%, bulk density 1.3-1.7 g/cm3. Real permittivity 3.63-10.72, imaginary permittivity 0.14-12.17 in X-band (8.2-12.4 GHz). Minimum reflection coefficient as low as -20.01 dB. notes: PCS was used as one of two precursors in a precursor infiltration and pyrolysis (PIP) process to fabricate C/SiC-HfC composite. PCS was dissolved in xylene at 50 wt% concentration and mixed with a liquid HfC precursor. The liquid HfC precursor had a ceramic yield of approximately 20 wt% (66.7% mass residue liquid-to-solid at room temperature, then 30% solid-to-HfC after 1700 degrees C for 2 h). Eight cycles of vacuum pressure impregnation and pyrolysis at 1500 degrees C were performed, followed by heat treatment at 1700 degrees C for 2 h in vacuum, then further densification cycles. The paper focuses primarily on ablation behavior of the final C/SiC-HfC composite in a plasma wind tunnel rather than characterization of the polymer precursor itself. HfC phase was uniformly dispersed with particle size less than 2 micrometers in the SiC matrix derived from PCS.

notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. It concerns zirconia porous ceramics fabricated by Material Jetting (MJ) 3D printing for thermal insulation applications. notes: Study focuses on curing kinetics of SMP-10 with micro-SiC (1 µm, β-SiC) and nano-SiC (40 nm, β-SiC) fillers at mass ratios of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 (filler:polymer). DSC performed from 50-400 °C at heating rates of 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, and 10 °C/min under nitrogen. Activation energies (KAS method): pure SMP-10 ~116 kJ/mol; micro-SiC addition decreased Ea to 92.5, 88.5, 85.8 kJ/mol at 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 loadings; nano-SiC increased or maintained Ea (120.8, 114.7, 112.4 kJ/mol at 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 loadings). Gibbs free energies of activation were relatively similar across all formulations (136-143 kJ/mol). Dominant curing mechanism for micro-SiC systems: Avrami-Erofeev nucleation and growth (A2/A3 models); nano-SiC at 0.3 loading showed reaction-order controlled mechanism (F3 model). SMP-10 viscosity: 40-100 cP at 25°C; density: 0.998 g/cm³. Pre-treatment: preheated at 110°C under vacuum to remove low-molecular-weight oligomers. Sample mass for DSC: ~20 ± 2 mg. No pyrolysis temperature or ceramic yield data reported in this study; focus is solely on curing kinetics.

notes: Crystallite size of b-SiC (from Scherrer equation) grows from 2.35 nm (1200 C) to 63.32 nm (1800 C). DC conductivity ranges from 1.91e-3 S/m at 1200 C to 2.07 S/m at 1800 C (approximately 3 orders of magnitude increase). Drastic conductivity increase occurs after 1500 C due to percolative turbostratic carbon network formation along SiC grain boundaries. Below percolation threshold, hopping conduction between carbon clusters dominates. Carbon cluster lateral size (La) increases with pyrolysis temperature up to 1600 C then decreases due to turbostratic carbon formation. Two-stage crystal growth model: slow growth (1200-1400 C) inhibited by carbon clusters; fast growth (1600-1800 C) after cluster breakdown. Disk samples: 25 mm diameter, 0.5 mm thickness, pressed at 700 Psi. Powder ground to ~10 micron in planetary ball mill.

notes: This paper does not describe a preceramic polymer in the traditional sense (e.g., polysilazane, polycarbosilane). The polymer is not itself a Si/N/B-containing preceramic polymer. Laser irradiation used: 1070 nm continuous wave fiber laser, beam diameter ~530 µm (unfocused). Three SiC formation mechanisms identified: (1) phase separation of amorphous SiOC contributing ~3 at% SiC; (2) carbothermal reduction of SiO2 contributing ~13 at% SiC (dominant); (3) direct Si+C reaction contributing ~2 at% SiC. SiC nanocrystals caged in graphitic carbon with d-spacing 0.25 nm observed in S1500. Nano-sized crystal grains 100-200 nm diameter with stacking fault networks also observed. SiC nanowires grow via vapor-solid mechanism. Heating rate for pyrolysis experiments was 10°C/min (inferred from schedule: e.g., 25-800°C in 80 min). TGA characterization used 20°C/min ramp rate.
source: Guo_2023_Synthesize and crystallization behavior of SiOC SiC nanocomposites

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental data reported as wt% for pyrolyzed ceramics, not for precursor polymer itself. See notes for ceramic composition data.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Vinyl groups (C=C) present in precursor but fully consumed after crosslinking as confirmed by FTIR (absence of nu C-H at 3053 cm-1, nu C=C at 1592 and 1402 cm-1). Free sp2-hybridized carbon (graphene-like) present in pyrolyzed ceramic.

functional_groups.other: Divinylbenzene (DVB) added as carbon filler at 0, 20, 40, or 60 wt%; dicumyl peroxide (DCP) added at 3 wt% as radical initiator

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed in Ar. Ceramic yields at 1400 C: 79 wt% (0% DVB), 77 wt% (20% DVB), 75 wt% (40% DVB), 65 wt% (60% DVB). Organic-inorganic transition begins at ~440 C. 60% DVB formulation shows severe extra mass loss of ~10% above 440 C due to excess DVB unable to integrate into network. All compositions behave similarly up to 440 C. DSC curves show exothermic reactions. Pyrolysis included 1 h dwell at 300 C and 1 h dwell at max temperature (800, 1000, 1200, or 1400 C). Heating and cooling rates of 100 K/h (1.67 C/min).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal, radical-initiated; DCP (3 wt%) initiates vinyl polymerization; crosslinking mechanisms include hydrosilylation (>100-120 C), transamination (200-400 C), dehydrogenation (>300 C), and vinyl polymerization; DVB-free: 30 min at 200 C; DVB-containing: 3-step process 10 min each at 100, 150, 200 C; additional 1 h dwell at 300 C during pyrolysis for transamination and dehydrocoupling

backbone_architecture.description: Poly(methylvinyl)silazane crosslinked into a thermoset network via hydrosilylation, transamination, dehydrogenation, and vinyl polymerization mechanisms. DVB incorporated into the polysilazane crosslinking network via radical-initiated vinyl polymerization.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous covalent ceramic (ACC) with mixed bonds confirmed by XRD. Free sp2-hybridized carbon phase (graphene-like) detected by Raman (D and G bands at ~1350 and ~1600 cm-1). Carbon ordering toward aromatic graphene layers increases with pyrolysis temperature 800-1400 C. Free carbon content: 14.5 wt% (0% DVB, 1000 C), 20.3 wt% (20% DVB, 1000 C), 18.0 wt% (20% DVB, 1400 C), 24.9 wt% (40% DVB, 1000 C), 20.8 wt% (60% DVB, 1000 C). Material described as fully dense.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Flexural strength measured by ball-on-three-balls (B3B) testing of disc samples. 20% DVB + 1000 C: characteristic flexural strength 1700 MPa (1.7 GPa), higher Weibull modulus. 40% DVB + 1000 C: characteristic flexural strength 988 MPa. 0% DVB + 1200 C: range 77-1350 MPa (high variability due to hidden defects). 60% DVB samples excluded due to warpage.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases identified (data not shown in paper, described as amorphous)

notes: Ceramic elemental compositions (wt%) from elemental analysis of pyrolyzed samples: (1) 0% DVB, 1000 C: Si=56.5, C=21.3, N=20.8, H=1.3, O=0.12, formula SiC0.88N0.74H0.64; (2) 20% DVB, 1000 C: Si=52.1, C=27.1, N=19.9, H=0.90, O=0.06, formula SiC1.22N0.77H0.48; (3) 20% DVB, 1400 C: Si=53.1, C=27.8, N=18.8, H=0.26, O=0.05, formula SiC1.23N0.71H0.14; (4) 40% DVB, 1000 C: Si=48.5, C=30.8, N=20.0, H=0.67, O=0.03, formula SiC1.48N0.83H0.38; (5) 60% DVB, 1000 C: Si=52.1, C=31.4, N=15.8, H=0.48, O=0.17, formula SiC1.41N0.61H0.25. Electrical conductivity tunable over 10 orders of magnitude (4.6e-11 to 1.3 S/cm) depending on DVB content and pyrolysis temperature. Carbon percolation network established above ~25 wt% free carbon (40% DVB threshold). Cytocompatibility demonstrated with normal human dermal fibroblasts. Lateral shrinkage 24-36%, vertical shrinkage 7-48% upon pyrolysis. Defect rate <1% among ~800 disc samples. Shaping by casting into PTFE or KOH-etched Si molds. Hierarchical microfabrication combining 2PP and casting demonstrated. Ceramic yield range for TGA: 65-79 wt% at 1400 C depending on DVB content.

notes: Paper focuses on electromagnetic wave absorption properties of polysiloxane-derived SiOC ceramics containing reduced graphene oxide (rGO). GO loadings studied: 1, 2, 3, and 5 wt%. Optimal EM absorption at 3 wt% GO: minimum reflection loss of -69.3 dB at 10.55 GHz, thickness 2.35 mm, effective bandwidth 3.4 GHz (9-12.4 GHz) at room temperature; bandwidth reaches 3.9 GHz at 673 K. SiC nanowire diameter ~50 nm, length several micrometres, grown in situ via Vapor-Solid mechanism. DC conductivity of 2 wt% G/SiOC increases from 3.2e-7 to 2.4e-6 S/m over 293-673 K. Pt catalyst concentration was 5 ppm relative to PSO. Green body pressed at 70 MPa after 10 h ball milling. Grain size of 50 nm refers to SiC nanowire diameter, not ceramic grain size per se.

notes: This is a review paper covering additive manufacturing of ceramics using preceramic polymers. polymer_name: bridged polysilsesquioxane (BTME, BTEB, BTEBP variants); Ti-EDA hybrid gel

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ti present in Ti-EDA system; C/Si ratios noted: BTME C/Si=1, BTEB C/Si=3, BTEBP C/Si=6

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si network from polycondensation of alkoxysilanes; organic bridge groups (ethylene, phenylene, biphenylene) covalently bonded between two Si atoms; Ti-O bonds in Ti-EDA system; Ti-N bonds formed during nitridation; chelation with acetylacetone in Ti-EDA system

functional_groups.other: Ethylene bridge (BTME), phenylene bridge (BTEB), biphenylene bridge (BTEBP); ethylenediamine (EDA) crosslinker in Ti-based system; acetylacetone chelating agent in Ti-based system; methoxy and ethoxy alkoxide leaving groups

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three-step weight loss observed for bridged polysilsesquioxanes under Ar: below 800°C (initial pyrolysis of organic moieties), 800-1200°C (further carbonization), above 1200°C (gradual weight loss attributed to carbothermal reduction to beta-SiC). PDCs remain amorphous SiOC at 1200°C; crystallization to SiC requires >1200°C. BTME and BTEB-derived samples contain cristobalite (SiO2) at 1500°C; BTEBP-derived samples show only SiC at 1500°C. Ti-EDA system: transforms to anatase/carbon nanocomposites on heating, then carbothermal reduction to Magneli phases; under Ar: Ti4O7 at 800°C, beta-Ti3O5 at 1000°C, mixture of Ti2O3 and TiOxNy at 1200°C, single-phase TiOxNy at 1400°C; under N2: mixture of Ti4O7 and TiOxNy at 800-1000°C, thorough transition to TiN at >1200°C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: sol-gel polycondensation (hydrolysis and condensation of alkoxysilanes); non-hydrolytic sol-gel for Ti-EDA system with EDA as crosslinker

backbone_architecture.description: Three-dimensional sol-gel network with chemical formula RSiO3/2 (polysilsesquioxane); organic bridge groups connect two neighboring Si atoms forming a bridged network; co-continuous macroporous morphology achieved via spinodal decomposition; Ti-EDA forms analogous 3D network via non-hydrolytic sol-gel

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC (amorphous, <1200°C); SiC (crystalline, >1200°C); SiC/SiOC composites (BTME, BTEB at 1300-1500°C); SiC/C composites (BTEBP at >1300°C); TiN, TiOxNy, Ti4O7, Ti3O5, Ti2O3 (Ti-based system depending on temperature and atmosphere)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: BTME (C/Si=1) and BTEB (C/Si=3) yield SiC/SiOC composites; BTEBP (C/Si=6) yields SiC/C composites; cristobalite (SiO2) found in BTME and BTEB samples at 1500°C. SiOC described as silica/carbon nanocomposite with Si/O-based nano-domains in amorphous carbon matrix with Si-C bonds. Ti-PDC phases depend on calcination atmosphere and temperature.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiOC (amorphous) at 1200°C; beta-SiC and cristobalite (SiO2) at 1500°C for BTME and BTEB; beta-SiC only at 1500°C for BTEBP. Ti system: anatase, Ti4O7, beta-Ti3O5, Ti2O3, TiOxNy (rock-salt), TiN depending on temperature and atmosphere

notes: This is a review article covering multiple preceramic polymer systems rather than a single polymer study. Two main systems discussed: (1) Si-based bridged polysilsesquioxanes (BTME, BTEB, BTEBP) producing porous SiOC/SiC monoliths via sol-gel with spinodal decomposition under Ar atmosphere; (2) Ti-EDA hybrid gels producing porous Ti-PDC monoliths (TiN, TiOxNy, reduced Ti oxides) via non-hydrolytic sol-gel with phase separation. Porous SiOC monoliths can be converted to hierarchically porous carbon monoliths via NaOH etching of Si/O nano-domains. Ti-PDCs calcined at 1200°C show conductivity >200 S/cm. Specific surface areas of Ti-PDCs: 140-200 m2/g at <1000°C. Phase separation induced by poly(ethylene oxide) in Si-based system; AcAc used as chelating agent in Ti-based system. Porous carbon monoliths from BTEBP-derived SiOC etched at 1200°C show increased micropores and specific surface area >1000 m2/g achievable.

notes: PCS is liquid at room temperature and stored at -20 degrees C. Ink formulation: 1.2 g SMP-10, 1.8 g BCP, 2 g 1-butanol, 0.05 g photoinitiator, 0.15 g thiol crosslinker, plus 1 g acetone added before printing. PCP:BCP mass ratio of 2:3. Thermal conductivity of architected lattices: 0.087-0.16 W/m·K, approximately one order of magnitude lower than bulk SiOC (1.5-2.4 W/m·K). Printing conditions: 350 psi, 20 mm/s, 250 um nozzle. Block copolymer is Kurarity LA4285 (Kuraray, Japan). Crosslinking of PCS indicated by color change from yellow to white/ivory. notes: This paper describes a hydrogel infusion additive manufacturing (HIAM) method for producing transition metal carbide ceramics (TiC, WC, MoC-Mo2C) using a single acrylate-based photopolymer hydrogel as both the structural template and carbon source. The polymer precursor is NOT a traditional silicon-based preceramic polymer (no Si, no polysilazane/polycarbosilane chemistry). Metal atoms are infused post-printing via aqueous salt solutions (Mo, W) or nonaqueous titanium isopropoxide (Ti). Carbothermal reduction occurs at 1500 C in Ar for 2 h. Linear shrinkage in drying step: 16.7-24.4% for all gels. Disordered graphitic carbon (ID/IG ~1.0) confirmed at 700 C and persists after 1500 C treatment. The paper is primarily about ceramic processing/manufacturing rather than preceramic polymer synthesis in the traditional sense.

notes: This paper is not about a preceramic polymer. Adsorption followed a Langmuir chemisorption isotherm. XRD confirmed no crystalline phase other than AlN after 96 h water leaching for stearic-acid-coated powder. notes: This paper is a broad review article on polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs) for environmental applications. It does not characterize any single preceramic polymer in detail. notes: Study focuses on Si-filler-loaded poly(methylsilsesquioxane) (60 vol% MK polymer + 40 vol% Si filler, mean particle size 60 micrometers) pyrolyzed in nitrogen at 1250-1600 C. Above 1414 C molten Si participates in solid-liquid-gas reactions forming columnar/platelet Si2ON2 crystals (10-20 micrometers). notes: Study focuses on curing kinetics of SMP-10, not pyrolysis or final ceramic properties. Key findings: (1) Thermal curing temperature of pure SMP-10 is approximately 250°C without initiators; initial crosslinking occurs 140-250°C range. (2) 2 wt% DCP or Luperox 101 lowers onset curing temperature. (3) Apparent activation energy (Ea) increases from ~116-122 kJ/mol (pure SMP-10) to ~141-153 kJ/mol (DCP) and ~155-156 kJ/mol (Luperox 101) by isoconversional methods. (4) Kissinger/Ozawa peak-based Ea: ~109-112 kJ/mol (pure), ~133 kJ/mol (DCP), ~168-170 kJ/mol (Luperox 101). (5) Entropy of activation shifts from negative (~-63 J/mol·K, pure) to positive (~77 J/mol·K for DCP, ~85 J/mol·K for Luperox), indicating dissociative transition state with initiators. (6) Reaction mechanism identified as nucleation-and-growth (Avrami-Erofeev A2 model) for all systems. (7) Physical properties of SMP-10: viscosity 40-100 cP at 25°C, density 0.998 g/cm3. (8) Samples pretreated at 100°C in vacuum oven to remove low molecular weight oligomers before kinetic study. (9) DSC performed 50-400°C at heating rates of 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, and 10°C/min under nitrogen atmosphere. (10) FT-IR confirmed Si-H, C=C, and SiCH2 groups and monitored their changes during curing.

notes: This is a literature review covering multiple polymer derived ceramic systems; no single polymer is exclusively characterized. Key systems discussed: PHPS (perhydropolysilazane), ABSE (polycarbosilazane), PCS (polycarbosilane), PSN1 (polysilazane), PHMS (poly(hydridomethylsiloxane)), and various silsesquioxanes. Filler content discussed: passive fillers (ceramic/oxide powders, 10-40 vol% typical), active fillers (Al, B, Fe, Ti, Cr elemental powders). Laser pyrolysis of PCS at 0.4-1 J/mm2 yields SiC equivalent to 1000-1200°C thermal pyrolysis; PCS film transmittance ~93% reduced to ~80% with carbon coating. Ion bombardment (C or Au ions) cleaves H bonds, enables crosslinking, increases free carbon retention, decreases density from ~2.45 to ~2.1 g/cm3. PHPS oxide layer at 1000°C after 10h ~half that of ABSE and ~1/10 that of uncoated stainless steel (~4.5 µm). Oxide layer thickness measured by GDOES depth profiling. First cure temperature: 80-200°C depending on precursor.
