microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PZC-0 yields pure disordered carbon. PZC-1 to PZC-3 yield ZrC-C ceramics. Zr content in ceramics at 1800 C: 0, 11, 18, 27 wt% for PZC-0 to PZC-3. Carbon phase consists of amorphous (A), turbostratic (T), and graphitic (G) components resolved from XRD (002) peak. Graphitization degree increases with ZrC content and heat-treatment temperature.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Disordered/turbostratic carbon (002 reflection), graphitic carbon, ZrC (in PZC-1 to PZC-3 derived ceramics). d002 values range from 0.3329 to 0.3480 nm; Lc ranges from ~21 to ~38 nm depending on sample and HTT.

notes: This paper focuses on a zirconium-containing phenolic resin precursor (PZC series) rather than a silicon-based preceramic polymer. The polymer is a phenol-formaldehyde (resol-type) resin hybridized with zirconium oxychloride. It is not a polysilazane, polycarbosilane, or polysiloxane. Polymer backbone is carbon-based (phenolic). Four variants: PZC-0 (no Zr), PZC-1 (5g ZrOCl2·8H2O, 5 wt% Zr), PZC-2 (10g, 10 wt% Zr), PZC-3 (15g, 16 wt% Zr). Ceramics formed at temperatures up to 2500 C contain ZrC and graphitizing carbon matrix. Lc values at 2500 C: PZC-0=26.26 nm, PZC-1=29.16 nm, PZC-2=37.52 nm, PZC-3=37.51 nm. ZrC catalyzes graphitization of carbon matrix. Coarsening of ZrC at 2500 C with high ZrC content has some negative effects on carbon structure order.
source: Liu_2019_Effect of ZrC Formation on Graphitization of Carbon Phase in Polymer

notes: HTTS is a polyorganosilazane synthesized by selective crosslinking of the commercial precursor KiON HTT 1800 (Merck KGaA). It was used as a preceramic polymer matrix loaded with TiB2 active filler (70/30 volumetric ratio filler/precursor). Solvent used: isopropanol or dibutyl ether; dispersant: Disperbyk (5 wt%); free radical initiator: di-cumyl peroxide (DCP) at 3.0 wt%. Coatings (~20 micron thick) were spray-applied onto sintered Fe-Mo-Ni-C steel substrates and pyrolyzed by conventional pyrolysis (CP) or plasma-assisted pyrolysis (PAP) at 900-1150 C for 2 h in nitrogen atmosphere at 3 C/min heating rate. PAP used DC pulsed plasma at 500 V, 5 A, 100 microsecond pulse, 200 Pa N2 at 99.99% purity. PAP heating rates for TGA comparison: 1.5 K/min (20-400 C) and 0.5 K/min (400-1000 C). The Si-C-N precursor system is described as SiCxN4-x (x=0,1,2). Above 1500 C, crystalline SiC, Si3N4, and graphite are expected to nucleate per literature cited.

SiBCN ceramics resist crystallization up to 1700C. Grain sizes at 1400C by Rietveld fitting: sample 1-1 = 8.5 nm, 2-1 = 6.5 nm, 2.5-1 = 4.5 nm, 4-1 ~1.0 nm (nearly amorphous by TEM). SiC grains generally <10 nm at early crystallization stage. At high temperature, beta-SiC progressively replaced by polytypes with frequent stacking faults. Heteroatom-containing ceramics exhibit thermochemical degradation of intergranular amorphous phase leading to rapid SiC grain growth.

notes: This is a review paper (Part V) summarizing results from Parts I-IV on polymer-derived ceramics in the Si-C-N-O-(H) system. Multiple precursors are studied: PCS (polycarbosilane), PCS copolymer, PVSZ (polyvinylsilazane: [-HSi(CH=CH2)NH-]), and PCSZ (polycarbosilazane) with x=0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. Ceramic compositions determined by Electron Probe MicroAnalysis after mineralisation (800-1000°C). Hold time range was 0.25-1 h (15-60 min); midpoint ~37.5 min used in thermal_pyrolysis field. Heating rate 3600 deg/h = 60 deg/min. Key finding: excess carbon (C/Si > 1) is always beneficial to structural stability and mechanical properties; heteroatoms O and N are ultimately detrimental. Nitrogen induces more thermally stable intergranular phase than oxygen. TEM (Philips EM400 and CM12) was primary characterization technique. PVSZ-derived ceramics treated under different conditions (lower heating rate, nitrogen atmosphere) and not directly comparable to PCSZ/PCS-derived ceramics. notes: This paper primarily describes development of a machine learning interatomic potential (MACE framework) for Si-C-N-H polymer-derived ceramic systems, trained on >9000 configurations. The MLIP achieves RMSE of 12.4 meV/atom for energies and 149 meV/Å for forces. Large-scale MD simulations of 8000-atom systems were performed. Key finding is phase separation where carbon domains nucleate from amorphous SiCN matrix forming graphene-like sheets. Pyrolysis temperature range noted is 800-1500 C for PDC synthesis generally. The paper is primarily a computational/ML study rather than an experimental polymer characterization paper; most polymer descriptors are not directly reported.

Elemental composition data provided is for the ceramic/derived-carbon products after pyrolysis and etching (from EDS/XPS): SiOC-1200 has C=24.49, O=34.28, Si=41.23 at%; SiOC-1200-1 (after 1 mol/L NaOH etching) has C=97.54, O=2.04, Si=0.41 at%. thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed up to 1500°C in Ar flow at 10°C/min using Netzsch STA 409. Pyrolysis conducted at both 1000°C and 1500°C producing ceramic aerogels designated Ceramic_1000 and Ceramic_1500. Linear shrinkage of 38.1% at 1000°C and 41.6% at 1500°C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic hydrosilylation - Si-H bonds of PSZ-20 reacted with vinyl groups of PSZ-20 and divinylbenzene in presence of Pt-divinyltetramethyldisiloxane complex catalyst at 150°C for 20 h in cyclohexane

backbone_architecture.description: PSZ-20 crosslinked with divinylbenzene via hydrosilylation to form a gel network; Si-H to C=C molar ratio of 1:1; 90 vol% solvent used; incomplete hydrosilylation observed by residual Si-H groups in FT-IR

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD analysis performed; ceramic aerogels at 1000°C and 1500°C characterized. Skeletal density increases from 1.80 g/cm3 at 1000°C to 2.24 g/cm3 at 1500°C suggesting densification and possible phase evolution. Specific surface area decreases from 165 m2/g at 1000°C to 153 m2/g at 1500°C.

notes: Porosity values: preceramic aerogel 94 vol%, Ceramic_1000 95 vol%, Ceramic_1500 96 vol% (midpoint used for microstructural porosity field: 95.5 for ceramic samples; range 95-96). Bulk densities: preceramic 59 kg/m3, Ceramic_1000 92 kg/m3, Ceramic_1500 96 kg/m3. SSA: preceramic 489 m2/g, Ceramic_1000 165 m2/g, Ceramic_1500 153 m2/g. Total pore volume: preceramic 1.57 cm3/g, Ceramic_1000 0.58 cm3/g, Ceramic_1500 0.56 cm3/g. Hierarchical pore size distribution from micropores to mesopores to macropores observed. CO2 insertion into polysilazane backbone occurs during supercritical drying, introducing C=O and Si-O bonds and O-Si-H units not present in xerogel control. 13C MAS NMR confirms CH3 (~0 ppm), aliphatic CH/CH2/CH3 (15-45 ppm), aromatic carbons (128, 145 ppm), residual vinyl (113, 138 ppm), and carbonyl (157 ppm, ~2.7% relative to CH3). Pt catalyst loading: 60 ppm relative to PSZ-20 mass.
source: Nguyen_2015_Synthesis and characterization of polymer-derived SiCN aerogel

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Samples sintered at 1200C show three phases: Al2O3, Cu2O, and in-situ formed CuAl2O4. Samples sintered at 1600C show only two phases: Al2O3 and CuAl2O4 due to full reaction of Cu2O. Cu2O content varied from 5 to 15 vol% in Al2O3 matrix.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Al2O3, Cu2O, CuAl2O4 identified by SEM and EDX

notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. It concerns laser direct structuring (LPKF-LDS) of Al2O3-Cu2O ceramic composite substrates for 3D molded interconnect devices (3D-MID). The material system is Al2O3 matrix with Cu2O additive (5 or 15 vol%), sintered in air at 1200-1600C for 1 hour. Porosity ranged from ~45% at 1200C to ~3% at 1600C; midpoint used for porosity_pct field (24). No preceramic polymer descriptors are applicable. A dextrin binder (molecular weight 1600-32000 g/mol) was used as a processing aid during powder preparation.
source: Novel Ceramic‐Based Material for the Applications of Molded Interconnect Devices (3D‐MID) Based on Laser Direct Structuring

elemental_composition.other_elements: Fe present from iron(III) acetylacetonate modification

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Fe bond detected by FTIR at 940 cm-1; C-O at 1267 cm-1; C=C at 1521 cm-1; C=O at 1571 cm-1; Si-O-Si at 1190, 790, 1090 cm-1; C-H at 2855, 2922, 2962 cm-1

functional_groups.other: acetylacetonate groups from Fe(III) acetylacetonate modifier; C=O and C-O from acetylacetonate ligand

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ammonolysis performed at 500, 700, 900, and 1000 degrees C. Heating and cooling rates were 100 degrees C per hour. At 500-700 C only epsilon-Fe2N crystalline phase present in amorphous SiO(N,C) matrix. At 900-1000 C, alpha-Fe appears as major phase at expense of epsilon-Fe2N. At >1100 C, Fe3Si forms. SiO(N,C) phase remains amorphous below 1000 C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal crosslinking implied during ammonolysis; Si-H consumed during cross-linking reactions at 500 C

backbone_architecture.description: Perhydropolysilazane (PHPS) chemically modified with Fe(III) acetylacetonate acting as a single-source precursor; Si-O-Fe bonding links iron into the polysilazane network

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous SiO(N,C) matrix with nanocrystalline epsilon-Fe2N and alpha-Fe; Fe3Si and Si2N2O at higher temperatures (>1100 C)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 500-700 C: 100 wt% epsilon-Fe2N crystalline phase embedded in large amorphous background. At 900-1000 C: ~24-29 wt% epsilon-Fe2N and ~71-76 wt% alpha-Fe. At >1100 C: Fe3Si and Si2N2O form additionally via VLS process. Ceramic paper shows delayed crystallization relative to cellulose-free reference, attributed to turbostratic carbon from cellulose.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: epsilon-Fe2N (P-31m, space group 162), alpha-Fe (Im-3m, space group 229), Fe3Si, Si2N2O

notes: Polymer is PHPS (NN 120-20 [A], 20 wt% solution in di-n-butylether, Merck KGaA) modified with Fe(III) acetylacetonate (1 g per 5 ml PHPS). Precursor solution refluxed at 100 C for 12 h in anhydrous toluene. Yield ~85%. Used to infiltrate cellulose-based paper (Sartorius grade 3hw) by dip-coating to form ceramic papers designated C/SiFe(N,C)O. Heating rate of 100 C/hour converts to ~1.67 C/min. Crystallite sizes from Rietveld refinement: epsilon-Fe2N ~20 nm at 500 C, ~24 nm at 700 C, ~25 nm at 900-1000 C; alpha-Fe ~25 nm at 900 C, ~18 nm at 1000 C. Mossbauer spectroscopy on precursor shows Fe(III) high spin doublet (delta=0.27 mm/s, deltaEQ=0.78 mm/s, 92% area). After 1000 C ammonolysis: doublet assigned to epsilon-Fe2N (29.5%) and sextet assigned to alpha-Fe nanoparticles (70.5%). XRD performed with Mo K-alpha1 radiation (lambda=0.70932 A) in transmission mode. Rietveld refinement using GSAS-II.
source: Ott_2021_Conversion of a polysilazane-modified cellulose-based paper into a

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Vinyl group on Si present in Durazane 1800 (from dichloromethylvinylsilane monomer); Si-N bonding of pyrolysed polysilazane noted as being oxidized during high temperature exposure

functional_groups.other: PHPS contains only Si-H and N-H groups (fully inorganic); Durazane 1800 contains vinyl and methyl substituents on Si

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Bond coat (PHPS) pyrolysed at 500°C in air for 1 h at 5 K/min; top coat (Durazane 1800 composite) pyrolysed at 1000°C in air for 1 h at 3 K/min. Significant volume shrinkage >50% noted leading to pores and cracks. Gas release during pyrolysis from polymer decomposition and dispersant decomposition resulted in pores up to 100 nm diameter.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical - 3 wt% dicumyl peroxide (DCP) added to Durazane 1800 to improve crosslinking at low temperatures

backbone_architecture.description: PHPS is an inorganic polysilazane produced by ammonolysis of dichlorosilane (SiH2Cl2). Durazane 1800 is an organosilazane synthesized by co-ammonolysis of dichloromethylvinylsilane and dichloromethylsilane, resulting in a crosslinkable network structure.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN/SiO2 matrix with ZrO2 (monoclinic and tetragonal), ZrSiO4 at higher temperatures
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After pyrolysis at 1000°C in air: monoclinic and tetragonal ZrO2 detected by XRD. At >1000°C ZrSiO4 forms from ZrSi2 oxidation. Si-N bonds oxidized to SiO2. No new phases from reaction between HTT1800 polysilazane and zirconia/glass fillers. Spinel (Mn,Cr)3O4 and Cr2O3 observed in coating at 1000 and 1100°C from substrate oxidation.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Monoclinic ZrO2, tetragonal ZrO2; at higher temperatures also ZrSiO4; no new phases from polymer-filler interaction detected

notes: Paper describes a double-layer PDC coating system on ferritic stainless steel AISI 441. Bond coat: PHPS pyrolysed at 500°C in air. Top coat: Durazane 1800 (also referred to as HTT1800 in results section) with 64.8 vol% YSZ (passive filler, D50=0.3 µm), 5.4 vol% ZrSi2 (active filler, D50=1.5 µm), 3.4 vol% glass microspheres (80SiO2-10Al2O3-10ZrO2 mol%, made by flame synthesis, ~10 µm diameter), and 3 wt% DCP crosslinker, applied by spray coating. Coating thickness ~10-15 µm. Pores up to 100 nm in diameter present. Protective at 900°C (mass gain ~half uncoated steel at 196 h); not protective at 1000-1100°C. Hydrothermal corrosion at 200°C for up to 8 days showed coating protected steel substrate. Monoclinic ZrO2 fraction increased from 67 to >70 vol% after 96 h hydrothermal exposure at 200°C. Glass microsphere CTE estimated at 2.3×10-6 K-1 (high silica content). The paper uses both 'Durazane 1800' and 'HTT1800' to refer to the organosilazane top coat precursor.
source: Parchoviansky_2018_CORROSION AND OXIDATION BEHAVIOR OF POLYMER DERIVED CERAMIC

polymer_name: methyltriethoxysilane (MTES)-derived hybrid silica gel; B-containing variant with boric acid

elemental_composition.other_elements: SiOC (wt%): Si=46.2, C=14.5, H<0.3, O=39.3; SiBOC (wt%): Si=41.0, B=3.2, C=11.8, H<0.3, O=44.1; empirical formulas: SiOC=SiC0.73O1.49, SiBOC=SiB0.22C0.67O1.87

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-O bonds present (BO3, BO2C, BOC2 trigonal boron sites); mixed silicon oxycarbide units SiCxO4-x (x=0 to 4); boron oxycarbide units; B-C bonds in graphene layers postulated (BC3 units)

functional_groups.other: ethoxy groups from MTES precursor; boric acid B(OH)3 used for B-containing variant

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Glasses are thermally stable; weight loss at 1500 C is <=1 wt%; chemical composition constant over 1000-1500 C range. Pyrolysis temperatures studied: 1200, 1400, and 1500 C for 1 h each.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal or catalytic (ammonia-promoted condensation/gelation for SiOC; room-temperature gelation for SiBOC)

backbone_architecture.description: Sol-gel derived hybrid silica gel network; B-free: MTES hydrolyzed with acidic water then condensed with ammonia; B-containing: MTES dissolved with boric acid without added water, cast and gelled at room temperature. Dried at 70 C for >=10 days.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC / SiBOC - nanocrystalline beta-SiC, sp2 carbon (graphitic nanocrystals), amorphous SiO2 nanoclusters (SiO2-B2O3 for SiBOC), mixed SiCxO4-x units
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1200 C: fully amorphous with silica halo. At 1400-1500 C: beta-SiC nanocrystals appear. SiOC 29Si NMR: SiO4=69%, SiO3C=6%, SiO2C2=4%, SiC4=21%. SiBOC 29Si NMR: SiO4=75%, SiO3C=2%, SiO2C2=4%, SiC4=19%. 11B NMR SiBOC: BO3(B(OSi)3)=92%, BO2C=7%, BOC2=1%. HF etching dissolves silica nanoclusters revealing porous structure. SSA of etched SiOC-HF at 1500C: 562 m2/g; SiBOC-HF at 1500C: 539 m2/g.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (cubic, (111) at 2theta~35, (101) at ~60, (211) at ~72); graphitic carbon (002) at 2theta~26.6 in SiBOC at 1500C; amorphous SiO2 halo at 2theta~22

notes: Study focuses on pyrolyzed ceramic glasses (PDC) derived from sol-gel precursors, not the preceramic polymer itself. Two systems studied: SiOC (B-free, B/Si=0) and SiBOC (B-containing, B/Si=0.2 atomic). Beta-SiC crystallite sizes (Scherrer, D_SiC(111)): SiOC at 1400C=2.6nm, at 1500C=3.5nm; SiBOC at 1400C=2.8nm, at 1500C=3.7nm; SiBOC-HF at 1500C=4.8nm with graphitic Lc(002)=5.3nm. Raman: D band ~1330-1335 cm-1, G band ~1590-1608 cm-1; D' band at 1617 cm-1 observed in SiBOC at 1500C indicating B incorporation into graphene layers as BC3 units. HF etching results: SiOC-HF at 1500C has SSA=562 m2/g, mesopore vol=0.23 cm3/g, micropore vol=0.33 cm3/g, avg pore size=2.8nm; SiBOC-HF at 1500C has SSA=539 m2/g, mesopore vol=0.66 cm3/g, micropore vol=0.54 cm3/g, avg pore size=4.8nm. Boron promotes SiC crystallization, increases carbon ordering at lower temperatures (1500C vs typical 1800C), and increases porosity/pore size after etching. Ceramic yield not explicitly reported; weight loss <=1 wt% at 1500C noted.
source: Pena-Alonso_2007_New Insights on the High-Temperature Nanostructure Evolution of SiOC

polymer_name: TZPC (AHPCS/TRIAZ-3 hybrid preceramic polymer); based on allyl-hydridopolycarbosilane (AHPCS, SMP-10) and triazine dendron (TRIAZ-3)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental compositions reported in weight% for pyrolyzed ceramics. Representative TZPC20-700: Si 53.23 wt%, O 12.68 wt%, C 31.80 wt%, N 1.32 wt%, H 0.91 wt%. TZPC48-700: Si 53.71 wt%, O 10.75 wt%, C 33.53 wt%, N 1.65 wt%, H 0.36 wt%. See notes for full table.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si (hydrosilylation product), Si-CH2CH2-C, C=N (triazine), C-N, N-C sp2, N=C sp2, C=C vinyl/allyl, C-O; XPS identifies SiC3O, SiC4, SiC3N, SiN(C), SiO4 environments

functional_groups.other: allyl groups (from AHPCS), triazine rings, styrene/vinylphenyl groups (from TRIAZ-3 dendron), NH linking groups

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA run from room temperature to 1000°C at 10°C/min under argon. Weight loss at ~180°C attributed to H2 release and minor molecular species from dehydrocoupling/hydrosilylation crosslinking. Further weight loss at ~450°C from disintegration of organic side groups releasing CH4 and H2. Prior dwell at 280°C for 5 hours performed to ensure crosslinking before main pyrolysis.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic hydrosilylation (Pt catalyst, platinum-1,3-divinyl-1,1,3,3-tetramethyldisiloxane, 1 wt%) between Si-H of AHPCS and vinyl groups of TRIAZ-3; also thermal crosslinking at 280°C dwell

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Mass spectrometry used for TRIAZ-3 dendron only: calculated MW = 432 g/mol (C27H24N6); measured 433.21 [M+H]+ and 455.20 [M+Na]+ by LC/MS Q-TOF. No GPC or MW data reported for TZPC polymers.

backbone_architecture.description: Hyperbranched/dendritic preceramic precursor formed by hydrosilylation crosslinking between AHPCS (linear/branched polycarbosilane backbone with Si-H and allyl groups) and TRIAZ-3 (triazine-based dendron with three vinylphenyl arms). Results in a three-dimensional hyperbranched network. TRIAZ-3 is a generation-1 dendron with 1,3,5-triazine core and N-linked 4-vinylphenyl arms.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOCN matrix. 29Si MAS NMR identifies SiC3O (~6 ppm), SiC4 (~-7 ppm), and SiC3N (~-27 ppm) environments. SiC4 dominant (53-77%) increasing with pyrolysis temperature. SiC3O and SiC3N decrease with temperature. XPS confirms SiC, SiN(C), SiC3O, SiO4 surface species. N retained as N=C sp2 and N-Si sp3 and NH-C sp2 bonds. Free carbon phase with disordered graphitic character detected by Raman (D and G bands). Carbon nanodomains embed N. No crystallization reported up to 900°C.

notes: Two reaction times studied: 20 hours (TZPC20) and 48 hours (TZPC48). Pyrolysis temperatures: 700, 800, 900°C. AHPCS:TRIAZ-3 ratio = 90:10 wt/wt. Reaction conducted under argon (Schlenk line) in anhydrous THF. Target application: SiOCN-based supercapacitors. Raman spectroscopy shows disordered free carbon (D* ~1156-1218, D ~1320-1343, D'' ~1450-1498, G ~1567-1582 cm-1); ID/IG ratio increases with temperature (0.99-1.34 for TZPC20, 1.07-1.34 for TZPC48), La ~1.36-1.56 nm. XPS C 1s shows C-Si sp3 (~41-56%), C=C sp2 (~28-42%), C=N sp2 (~12-13%), C-O sp3 (~2-4%). N 1s shows N=C sp2 (~49-77%), NH-C sp2 (~20-51%), N-Si sp3 (~2-6%). O 1s shows predominantly O-Si (~75-95%) with minor O=C (~5-25%). Elemental analysis of pyrolyzed ceramics: Si ~52-55 wt%, C ~31-35 wt%, O ~9-13 wt%, N ~1.3-1.7 wt%, H ~0-0.91 wt%. Empirical formulae range from SiO0.29C1.41N0.05 to SiO0.41C1.52N0.06.
source: Perez-Roman_2024_Innovative strategies for nitrogen-incorporating silicon oxycarbide-based preceramic polymer

polymer_name: PCS (Polycarbosilane, Institute of Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si and Si-O-C cross-linked structures formed during oxidative curing at 200°C; Si-O-C, C-C/C=C, C-O, C=O bonds identified by XPS in pyrolyzed ceramic

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis conducted in two stages: room temperature to 1100°C at 3°C/min, then 1100°C to final temperature (1300-1500°C) at 2°C/min, held for 2 h. Ceramic products are multiphase β-SiC/SiOxCy/free carbon. Gaseous CO and SiO evolved during carbothermal conversion. Fiber shrinkage and rough surface formation observed after pyrolysis. Samples also pre-crosslinked at 200°C for 2 h in air before pyrolysis.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal oxidative curing at 200°C for 2 h in air; oxygen incorporation into PCS chains via Si-O-Si and Si-O-C cross-linked structures

backbone_architecture.description: PCS used as preceramic precursor dissolved with PVP in THF/DMF solvent system and electrospun into fibrous membranes; after oxidative curing, cross-linked Si-O-Si and Si-O-C network forms; final ceramic is a 3D interconnected fibrous network

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Nanocrystalline β-SiC embedded in amorphous SiOxCy and disordered free carbon matrix. XPS shows C-Si (SiC), C-C/C=C (67.61% dominant free carbon), C-O, C=O, O-Si, O-C, Si-O-C (15.4%) bonds. β-SiC confirmed by XRD peaks at 2θ ≈ 35.6° (111), 60.0° (220), 71.8° (311) matching JCPDS No. 74-2307. Stacking faults in β-SiC observed at 1500°C. Higher PCS content increases carbon and oxygen content with decreased silicon; higher pyrolysis temperature decreases oxygen and increases silicon via carbothermal conversion of SiOxCy to β-SiC.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fibrous membranes exhibit outstanding flexibility due to 3D crosslinked fiber network structure

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: β-SiC (JCPDS No. 74-2307); amorphous SiOxCy and amorphous carbon phases also present

notes: PCS content used in spinning solutions: 1.2, 1.4, 1.6 g PCS in THF/DMF with PVP. Pyrolysis temperatures investigated: 1300, 1400, 1500°C. Optimized sample PCS-1.4-1400 (1.4 g PCS, 1400°C pyrolysis) achieved RLmin of -27.12 dB at 2.2 mm thickness and EAB of 8.22 GHz at 2.7 mm (9.78-18 GHz). Raman ID/IG ratios: 1.710 (PCS-1.2-1400), 1.682 (PCS-1.4-1400), 1.664 (PCS-1.6-1400) indicating moderated carbon disorder. Electrospun fiber diameters after pyrolysis at 1400°C: 0.373-0.625 μm depending on PCS content. Heating rate range 2-3°C/min; midpoint 2.5°C/min used for heating_rate field. Polarization loss accounts for ~60-70% of total dielectric loss. Material is nonmagnetic (μr ≈ 1). Electrospinning conditions: 9 kV, 10 cm tip-to-collector distance, 1.5 mL/h flow rate.
source: Phase evolution and broadband electromagnetic wave absorption mechanisms of electrospun polymer-derived SiC-based fibrous ceramic membranes

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramics prepared by reactive hot-pressing sintering of ZrSi2, TiSi2, B4C, and activated carbon at 1700 C/40 MPa/15 min. Phases identified include (Zr,Ti)B2, (Zr,Ti)C, SiC, and minor ZrO2. Phase volume fractions vary with Zr/Ti and (Zr,Ti)C/(Zr,Ti)B2 molar ratios. TMB2 ranges 15.4-43.5 vol%, TMC ranges 11.8-37.7 vol%, SiC ranges 56.5-62.3 vol% depending on composition.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Multiple compositions reported. Flexural strength ranges 295.5-515.2 MPa; Vickers hardness ranges 9.82-25.21 GPa; fracture toughness KIC ranges 2.73-4.51 MPa*m^0.5; open porosity ranges 0.90-1.80%; density ranges 3.98-4.36 g/cm3. Best toughness (4.51 MPa*m^0.5) and strength (515.2 MPa) for Z10T0B1C1-S; best strength/toughness balance for Z9T1B2C1-S (479.2 MPa, 3.84 MPa*m^0.5).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: (Zr,Ti)B2 (solid solution, hexagonal), (Zr,Ti)C (solid solution, cubic), SiC (PDF#29-1129), minor ZrO2 (PDF#37-1484); parent phases ZrB2 (PDF#34-0423), ZrC (PDF#35-0784)

notes: This paper is NOT about preceramic polymers. It concerns ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTCs) of the (Zr,Ti)B2-(Zr,Ti)C-SiC system fabricated by reactive hot-pressing sintering of inorganic precursor powders (ZrSi2, TiSi2, B4C, activated carbon) at 1700 C/40 MPa/15 min. No polymer chemistry, pyrolysis of polymers, or preceramic polymer descriptors are present. Rietveld-refined lattice parameters for (Zr,Ti)B2: a=3.114-3.151 Å, c=3.420-3.493 Å; for (Zr,Ti)C: a=4.654-4.669 Å. Zr/Ti molar ratios in solid solutions confirmed by Rietveld refinement. Sintering densification occurs in three stages. Chemical reactions are thermodynamically spontaneous at 1700 C (negative Gibbs free energy). All polymer-related fields are null as they are not applicable.
source: Phase tailoring of (Zr,Ti)B2-(Zr,Ti)C-SiC ceramics toward microstructural optimization for simultaneous enhancement of strength and toughnes

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramics contain (Zr,Ti)B2, (Zr,Ti)C, and SiC as primary phases with minor ZrO2. Phase volume fractions vary by sample: e.g. Z10T0B1C1-S has 23.0 vol% TMB2, 18.1 vol% TMC, 58.9 vol% SiC. Solid solutions (Zr,Ti)B2 and (Zr,Ti)C form during reactive hot-pressing sintering at 1700 C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Multiple samples measured. Z10T0B1C1-S: flexural strength 515.2 MPa, Vickers hardness 25.21 GPa, fracture toughness 4.51 MPa·m^0.5; Z9T1B1C1-S: 461.8 MPa, 17.03 GPa, 4.06 MPa·m^0.5; Z8T2B1C1-S: 448.7 MPa, 15.02 GPa, 3.74 MPa·m^0.5; Z7T3B1C1-S: 357.9 MPa, 13.69 GPa, 3.60 MPa·m^0.5; Z9T1B0C1-S: 295.5 MPa, 9.82 GPa, 2.73 MPa·m^0.5; Z9T1B1C2-S: 353.5 MPa, 13.89 GPa, 4.29 MPa·m^0.5; Z9T1B2C1-S: 479.2 MPa, 13.43 GPa, 3.84 MPa·m^0.5; Z9T1B1C0-S: 432.0 MPa, 20.68 GPa, 3.57 MPa·m^0.5

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: (Zr,Ti)B2 (PDF#34-0423 base), (Zr,Ti)C (PDF#35-0784 base), SiC (PDF#29-1129), minor ZrO2 (PDF#37-1484). Lattice parameters obtained by Rietveld refinement: for Z9T1B1C1-S TMB2 a=3.151 Å, c=3.493 Å; TMC a=4.669 Å. For Z8T2B1C1-S TMB2 a=3.125 Å, c=3.445 Å; TMC a=4.656 Å. For Z7T3B1C1-S TMB2 a=3.114 Å, c=3.420 Å; TMC a=4.654 Å.

notes: This paper is NOT about preceramic polymers. It concerns ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTCs) of (Zr,Ti)B2-(Zr,Ti)C-SiC prepared by reactive hot-pressing sintering at 1700 C/40 MPa/15 min from ZrSi2, TiSi2, B4C, and activated carbon raw materials. No polymer precursor chemistry is described. All polymer-related fields are null. Open porosity ranges from 0.90% to 1.80% across samples. Densities range from 3.98 to 4.36 g/cm3. Sintering atmosphere was argon (ball milling under argon; sintering in graphite mold). Chemical reactions occur above ~1334 C during sintering.
source: Phase tailoring of (Zr,Ti)B2-(Zr,Ti)C-SiC ceramics toward microstructural optimization for simultaneous enhancement of strength and toughness

polymer_name: CPBCS (cross-linked polyborosilazane); variants: CPBCS10-1, CPBCS5-1, CPBCS3-1

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present; full wt% compositions given for cured precursors at 300C: e.g. CPBCS5-1 (SiBCN(O)5-1): Si=35.40, B=1.02, C=30.10, O=19.80, N=5.33, H=8.35 wt%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N, B-C, B-O, B-N-O, C=C (vinyl), Si-O-Si detected by FTIR and XPS; SiCxN4-x and SiCxO4-x tetrahedral units present

functional_groups.other: Boron-containing groups (BNO, B4C, BO); vinyl groups from TMDS (1,1,3,3-tetramethyl-1,3-divinyldisilazane)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Weight loss occurs in two stages: 40-300C (small molecule escape) and 300-800C (organic group cleavage; NH3, CH4, H2C=CH2, methylsilanes detected by MS). Carbothermal reduction and Si3N4 decomposition detected between 1550-1600C (SiO, CO/N2 by MS). Ceramic yields at 1600C in argon: SiBCN(O)10-1=98.32%, SiBCN(O)5-1=98.29%, SiBCN(O)3-1=95.72%; in air: 99.17%, 99.36%, 99.87% respectively. Ceramics show small weight loss at 1580C in argon, no significant loss in air below 1600C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (cured at 100C in air then 300C for 2h under argon; hydrosilylation using Karstedt catalyst; dehydrogenation coupling)

backbone_architecture.description: Two-component system: BSZ12 (multifunctional boron hybrid silazane monomer from hydroboration of TMDS and BDMS) mixed with PNSZ (poly[imino(methylsilylene)]) and crosslinked via hydrosilylation (Si-H/C=C reaction) using Karstedt catalyst to form cross-linked polyborosilazane network with Si, B, C, N elements

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiBCN(O) amorphous below 1400C; beta-SiC crystallizes at 1600C; SiO2 (cristobalite) and BN(C) also present at high temperatures
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiBCN(O) below 1400C confirmed by XRD and HRTEM/SAED. Beta-SiC crystalline peaks at 35.7, 41.4, 60.0, 71.8, 75.5 degrees 2-theta appear at 1600C. Broad peak at ~22 degrees attributed to high cristobalite. Weak BN(C) peak present at 1600C. At 1800C SiC lattice clearly resolved (d-spacing 0.252nm, (111) plane). SiO2 amorphous regions confirmed by XPS and elemental analysis.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (at 1600C and above), high cristobalite (~22 deg), BN(C) (weak, at 1600C), SiC stacking faults (33.7 deg); 1800C shows more complete SiC crystallization

notes: Grain sizes of SiC in SiBCN(O)5-1: 2.4 nm at 1400C, 16.4 nm at 1600C, 75.0 nm at 1800C (Scherrer equation). Boron suppresses carbothermal reduction and inhibits crystallization. In air, B2O3 forms a borosilicate glass protective layer at high temperatures. Three precursor ratios studied (Si-H/C=C = 10:1, 5:1, 3:1). Full elemental wt% compositions at 300C, 1000C, 1200C, 1400C, and 1600C given in Table 2 for all three compositions. Ceramic yield midpoint used for SiBCN(O)5-1 in argon (98.29%); range across compositions in argon: 95.72-98.32%; range in air: 99.17-99.87%. Pyrolysis hold time of 2h at temperatures above 1000C. Initial curing: 100C in air then 300C for 2h under argon.
source: Polymer derived SiBCN(O) ceramics with tunable element content

notes: This is a broad review article on polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs) covering synthesis, processing, and applications in energy and environmental sectors. It does not characterize any single preceramic polymer in detail. No specific quantitative descriptors such as elemental composition, ceramic yield, pyrolysis conditions, molecular weight, or mechanical properties are reported for any individual polymer. The text discusses classes of preceramic polymers including polycarbosilanes, polysiloxanes, polysilazanes, and polysilylcarbodiimides in general terms, and mentions ceramic systems such as SiOC, SiCN, SiBCN, SiAlCN, and high-entropy ceramics. A specific mention is made of SiOC porous monolith electrodes achieving 1176 mAh/g first-cycle charge capacity and 350 mAh/g at 800 mA/g after 245 cycles, with surface area of 11 m2/g, but no preceramic polymer descriptors are quantified for this system either.
source: Polymer-Derived Ceramics- A Materials Platform for Advanced Energy and Environmental Applications

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present (SiBCN system)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-C bonds (1063 cm-1), B-N bonds (1409 and 753 cm-1), C-H bonds (2958 and 2875 cm-1), Si-O-C bonds detected by XPS, C-N bonds detected by XPS

backbone_architecture.description: Precursor is a polyborosilazane used for electrospinning into fibers; specific backbone architecture not described

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiBCN (amorphous matrix + beta-SiC nanocrystals + free carbon)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: A+B+C microstructure: amorphous SiBCN matrix (A) acting as electrically insulating phase, beta-SiC nanocrystals (B) and free carbon (C) acting as electrically lossy conductive phases. Fibers remain amorphous below 1600 °C. At 1600 °C, beta-SiC and graphitic free carbon nanocrystals form. NMR reveals SiC4, SiCN3, SiN4 coordination environments and BN3, BCN2, BC3 boron units.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (111), (220), (311) planes at 2theta = 35, 60, 72 degrees; graphite-like carbon at 2theta = 26.6 degrees (at 1600 °C); amorphous below 1600 °C

notes: Paper focuses on SiBCN ceramic nanofibers derived from polyborosilazane precursor via electrospinning followed by high-temperature annealing. Fiber diameter ~300 nm after annealing at 1600 °C. Fibers mixed with paraffin (45 wt%) for microwave absorption testing. Best EW absorption: RCmin = -56.9 dB at 10.56 GHz, thickness 2.6 mm, EAB = 3.45 GHz (8.95-12.4 GHz, X-band). Dielectric constant (real part) at 1600 °C ranges from 12.45 to 7.16; imaginary part ranges from 5.27 to 3.34; max tan delta = 0.47. ID/IG ratio decreases from 1.11 to 1.03 with increasing annealing temperature indicating amorphous to nanocrystalline graphite transformation. XPS confirms Si-N, Si-C, Si-O-C, B-N, B-C, C-C, C-N bonds on fiber surfaces.
source: Polymer-Derived Lightweight SiBCN Ceramic Nanofibers with High Microwave Absorption Performance

elemental_composition.other_elements: B mentioned as small amounts possible; isotopically labeled Si, C, O, N variants used for NMR studies

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C-N bonds at interfaces between Si3N4 and carbon nanodomains; N bonded to 2 Si and 1 C (interfacial NSi2C sites); Si-NCN (carbodiimide) linkages; sp2 C-C and C=C bonds in free carbon phase; SiCxO4-x and SiCxN4-x mixed tetrahedral units

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups (Ph) on poly(phenylmethylsilylcarbodiimide); carbodiimide (-NCN-) groups; hydrogen stabilizing interfacial C-N bonding (~3 H atoms per NC1/4Si2/4 site)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PDCs resist crystallization or decomposition to about 1500°C and higher in inert atmosphere. Hydrogen largely lost by pyrolysis near 1100°C, destabilizing mixed-bonded nitrogen coordination environments. Processing range typically 500-1400°C. SAXS modeling tracks nanodomain evolution up to 2000°C.

backbone_architecture.description: Poly(phenylmethylsilylcarbodiimide) with repeating -[Ph(CH3)Si-NCN]n- units. General classes include polyorganocarbosilanes, polyorganosiloxanes, polyorganosilazanes, and polysilylcarbodiimides.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN and SiOC (amorphous); nanodomains of sp2 free carbon, Si3N4, SiC precipitates, and mixed SiCxN4-x / SiCxO4-x interfacial regions
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiCN at 800°C: amorphous nanodomains of sp2 carbon and Si3N4 with interfacial mixed C-N-Si bonding. SiOC: partial segregation of SiO4 and SiC4 units; free carbon as turbostratic/graphene-like sheets (>70% of C atoms). SiOC network has mass-fractal dimension 2.3-2.5. Crystalline phases (SiC) form at higher temperatures. Carbon-rich SiCN and SiOC show improved crystallization resistance.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: High strength, creep and thermal shock resistance mentioned qualitatively

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: X-ray amorphous up to ~1500°C; nanosized SiC precipitates and turbostratic carbon observed by HRTEM at higher temperatures

notes: This is a review/feature article covering multiple PDC systems (SiCN and SiOC) derived from various precursor classes. The grain_size_nm of 15 nm refers to average diameter of free carbon domains in polysilylcarbodiimide-derived SiCN at lower carbon content (35-40 wt%) pyrolyzed at 800°C, estimated from 15N NMR. The polymer specifically named is poly(phenylmethylsilylcarbodiimide) (-[Ph(CH3)Si-NCN]n-). Carbon content ranges cited: 35-40 wt% (lower) and 55-60 wt% (higher, forming continuous carbon matrix). Structural characterization methods include 29Si, 13C, 15N, 1H solid-state MAS NMR, 2D COSY/DQ/HETCOR NMR, micro-Raman, SAXS, XRD, HRTEM, STEM, EELS, ELNES, and high-temperature oxide melt solution calorimetry. Interface C-N bonds stabilized by ~3 H atoms per NC1/4Si2/4 site; hydrogen lost near 1100°C.
source: Polymer-derived SiCN and SiOC ceramics – structure and energetics at the nanoscale

backbone_architecture.description: Amorphous SiOC matrix derived from preceramic polymer; SiOC serves as matrix phase reinforced with ZrB2/ZrO2 core-shell nanophases

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramic composite composed of amorphous SiOC matrix (60.0 wt%), ZrB2 (36.4 wt%), and ZrO2 (3.6 wt%) as determined by XRD phase analysis; crystallized t-ZrO2 interface exists between ZrB2 nanoparticles and SiOC matrix; ZrB2 nanoparticles are 18-50 nm in size

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: ZrB2, t-ZrO2; SiOC matrix is amorphous

notes: Paper focuses on polymer-derived SiOC reinforced with ZrB2/ZrO2 core-shell nanophase structure for high-temperature microwave absorption up to 1000 °C. ZrB2 grain size range is 18-50 nm (midpoint ~34 nm used). The preceramic polymer identity and synthesis details are not specified. SiOC real permittivity varies from 2.4 to 2.92 up to 1000 °C; composite average real permittivity ~5.39-5.47, imaginary permittivity ~1.33-1.62, loss tangent ~0.24-0.28 in Ka-band (28-40 GHz). Phase composition from XRD table: ZrB2 36.4 wt%, ZrO2 3.6 wt%, SiOC 60.0 wt%. Effective absorption bandwidth >10 GHz from RT to 900 °C at thickness ~2.9 mm. source: Polymer-derived SiOC reinforced with core–shell nanophase structure of ZrB2_ZrO2 for excellent and stable high-temperature microwave absorption (up to 900 °C)

polymer_name: polymethylsilsesquioxane (PMS, SILRES MK Wacker Chemie AG)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Hf and Ta incorporated via Hf(OnBu)4 and Ta(OC2H5)5 alkoxide modification; Hf:Ta molar ratios of 1:0, 3:1, and 2:1 investigated; PMS:alkoxide mass ratio 60:40 for modified systems

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si backbone confirmed by FTIR (~1090 cm-1); Si-O-M (M=Hf, Ta) linkages formed upon alkoxide modification (~950-970 cm-1); Si-O-C vibrations (~1000 cm-1); SiOxC4-x mixed tetrahedral environments (SiO4, SiO3C, SiO2C2, SiOC3) confirmed by 29Si MAS NMR in pyrolyzed ceramics

functional_groups.other: Alkoxy groups from residual Hf and Ta alkoxide precursors (n-butoxy, ethoxy); Si-OEt units present in PMS (13C NMR signals at 18.48 ppm and 58.40 ppm assigned to SiOCH2CH3)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed under flowing argon from room temperature to 1100 °C at 5 °C/min. Polymer-to-ceramic transformation confirmed. Subsequent annealing of ceramic powders at 1250, 1400, and 1550 °C under flowing argon (heating/cooling rate 600 °C/h, 3 h dwell) to study phase evolution. Monolith pyrolysis heating rate was 30 °C/h (0.5 °C/min), cooling at 5 °C/min with 2 h dwell at 1100 °C.

backbone_architecture.description: Methyl-substituted silsesquioxane (T-unit, MeSiO3/2) network; partially condensed trifunctional branching units confirmed by 29Si MAS NMR (~-60 ppm); upon alkoxide modification Si-O-M linkages form, increasing distribution of local silicon environments without significantly perturbing the siloxane backbone

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC with segregated free-carbon phase; HfO2-based phases crystallize at ~1250 °C; (Hf,Ta)C forms at 1550 °C via carbothermal reduction
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1100 °C: amorphous SiOC matrix with nanoscale Hf-rich oxide precipitates. At 1250 °C: onset of HfO2-related crystallization. At 1550 °C: transformation to (Hf,Ta)C carbide. Free carbon content: SiOC-Hf ~6.7 wt%, SiOC-Hf3Ta ~10.4 wt%, SiOC-Hf2Ta ~12.1 wt% (from table). Phase fractions at 1550 °C: SiOC ~82.8%, (Hf,Ta)O2 ~5.1%, free C ~12.1% for SiOC-Hf2Ta. Rietveld refinement: HfC (a=4.643 Å) for SiOC-Hf; (Hf,Ta)C (a=4.592 Å) for SiOC-Hf3Ta; (Hf,Ta)C (a=4.565 Å) for SiOC-Hf2Ta.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous after pyrolysis at 1100 °C; nanocrystalline phases develop at 1250-1550 °C
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: HfC (SiOC-Hf, a=4.643 Å); (Hf,Ta)C (SiOC-Hf3Ta, a=4.592 Å); (Hf,Ta)C (SiOC-Hf2Ta, a=4.565 Å); HfO2-related phases at 1250 °C; amorphous SiOC matrix persists

notes: Polymer is commercially available polymethylsilsesquioxane (PMS, SILRES MK, Wacker Chemie AG) modified with Hf and/or Ta alkoxides to form single-source preceramic precursors. Three modified systems studied: PMS-Hf (60 wt% PMS + 40 wt% Hf(OnBu)4), PMS-Hf3Ta (60 wt% PMS + 40 wt% Hf(OnBu)4+Ta(OEt)5 at 3:1 molar ratio), PMS-Hf2Ta (60 wt% PMS + 40 wt% alkoxides at 2:1 Hf:Ta molar ratio). Thermal conductivity at 900 °C: SiOC-Hf ~0.68 W/m/K, SiOC-Hf3Ta ~0.85 W/m/K - reported as among lowest for SiOC-related materials. Bulk densities: SiOC-Hf 2.227 g/cm3, SiOC-Hf3Ta 2.121 g/cm3, SiOC-Hf2Ta 2.140 g/cm3. Open porosity range 11.26-15.55 vol% (midpoint ~12.95 used for porosity_pct field). Specific heat capacity at 900 °C: SiOC-Hf 0.99 J/g/K, SiOC-Hf3Ta 1.30 J/g/K. Synthesis performed under argon via Schlenk technique. 29Si NMR SiOxC4-x distribution tabulated: SiOC-Hf3Ta (SiO4 37%, SiO3C 41%, SiO2C2 14%, SiOC3 7%); SiOC-Hf2Ta (SiO4 46%, SiO3C 35%, SiO2C2 12%, SiOC3 7%); SiOC-Hf (SiO4 45%, SiO3C 31%, SiO2C2 20%, SiOC3 4%).
source: Polymer-derived Si–Hf–Ta–O–C ceramics- from precursor chemistry to thermal transport

Second mass loss 500-600 C due to release of methane (m/z=15,16) and hydrogen (m/z=2). Ceramization complete at ~700 C. TGA performed to 1000 C at 1 K/min in argon (25 ml/min). Pyrolysis temperatures studied: 700-900 C; range midpoint 800 C used for pyrolysis_temp_C field.

backbone_architecture.description: Commercial vinyl-functionalized polysiloxane; specific backbone architecture not described in text

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pure SiOC ceramic is fully amorphous at all pyrolysis temperatures 700-900 C as confirmed by XRD broad halos. SiOC/ZnO nanocomposites at 700 and 800 C contain amorphous SiOC matrix with crystalline ZnO (wurtzite-type). At 900 C, ZnO reacts with SiOC matrix to form zinc silicate (Zn2SiO4) and an unidentified phase.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous SiOC (broad halos 2theta 20-40 deg); ZnO wurtzite-type crystalline phase in nanocomposites at 700-800 C; Zn2SiO4 (JCPDS 14-0653) and unidentified phase at 900 C

notes: Paper focuses on SiOC/ZnO nanocomposite for water decontamination via MB adsorption and photocatalytic degradation. Polymer is commercial vinyl-functionalized polysiloxane XP RV 200 (Hanse Chemie, Germany). ZnO nanopowders (Sigma-Aldrich, ~50 nm mean particle size, 34 m2/g surface area) incorporated at 5-20 wt%. Pyrolysis in two steps: 200 C/2h crosslinking then 700-900 C/2h ceramization, heating rate 50 C/h (0.833 C/min), cooling rate 100 C/h, argon flow 50 ml/min. Pure SiOC ceramic is microporous (pore size <2 nm, SBET up to 398 m2/g at 700 C); ZnO incorporation causes microporosity-to-mesoporosity transformation (~4 nm pores). Grain size of ZnO nanoparticles in composite ~20-25 nm by TEM/Debye-Scherrer; midpoint 22.5 nm reported. Ceramic yield 23% at 700 C. SBET values and pore volumes tabulated as function of pyrolysis temperature and ZnO content. No nitrogen in polymer or ceramic system.
source: Polymer-derived mesoporous SiOC:ZnO nanocomposite for the purification of water contaminated with organic dyes

Pyrolysis temperatures studied: 950, 1100, and 1300 C. A dwell at 230 C for 2 h was used for crosslinking prior to final pyrolysis. Cooling rate was 150 C/h.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - dwelling at 230 C for approximately 2 h to further cross-link the polymer

backbone_architecture.description: Described as a liquid polyorganosilazane (HTT1800, Clariant GmbH); further architectural details not provided in the text

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Polymer-derived SiCN ceramic confirmed by EDX (Si, C, N present). Carbon phase evolves from amorphous/disordered carbon clusters to nanocrystalline graphitic regions with increasing pyrolysis temperature, as shown by Raman spectroscopy. SiCN ceramic forms between graphite particles in composite.

notes: HTT1800 was used as a preceramic polymer mixed 1:1 by weight with commercial graphite (SLP50, Timcal) to form SiCN/graphite composite anodes for Li-ion batteries. Pyrolysis temperatures studied: 950, 1100, and 1300 C under argon. Heating rate 100 C/h (~1.67 C/min); cooling rate 150 C/h. Hold time at final temperature: 1 h (60 min). Crosslinking step at 230 C for 2 h. Raman spectroscopy shows evolution from amorphous to nanocrystalline carbon with increasing pyrolysis temperature (I(D)/I(G) ratios for pure HTT1800: 1.05 at 950C, 1.20 at 1100C, 1.71 at 1300C). Elemental compositions of pyrolyzed composites (wt%): C1 950C: C=67.25, O=6.38, N=7.17, Si=19.20; C2 1100C: C=67.62, O=2.94, N=7.65, Si=20.79; C3 1300C: C=69.50, O=0.87, N=8.22, Si=21.41. Electrochemical performance: reversible capacity ~350 mAh/g for C3 composite. HTT1800 stored in glove box (H2O/O2 < 1 ppm) prior to use. The polymer is described as a commercial liquid polyorganosilazane/polyvinylsilazane.
source: Polymer-derived-SiCN ceramic:graphite composite as anode material with enhanced rate capability for lithium ion batteries

elemental_composition.other_elements: PMS carbon content 13.2 wt%; PPS carbon content 48.2 wt%. PMS molecular composition [CH3SiO1.5]; PPS approximate composition RSiO1.5 where R is C6H5:CH3:CH2CH:H as 2.8:1.5:1:1

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C-H bonds present; Si-phenyl bonds in PPS; vinyl groups (CH2CH) in PPS

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups in PPS (C6H5)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Decomposition of polysiloxane starts above 400°C and is almost complete at ~800°C. Amorphous silicon oxycarbide glass forms above 800°C. Ceramic yield reported as up to 85 wt% for polysiloxane. Heating cycle: ramp to 550°C at 5 K/min, hold 4 h, then 1-2 K/min to final temperature (1000-1400°C) with 4 h dwell, cool at 5 K/min. Heating rate range 1-2 K/min for second ramp; midpoint 1.5 K/min used.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (warm pressing at 230°C, 30 MPa, 30 min)

molecular_weight.measurement_method: not specified; average molecular mass reported for PMS only

backbone_architecture.description: PMS: [CH3SiO1.5] ladder/network polysiloxane, solid powder at room temperature. PPS: RSiO1.5 polysiloxane, low viscosity liquid at room temperature. Both are T-type (RSiO1.5) siloxane networks.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous silicon oxycarbide (SiOxCy) glass matrix forms below 800°C. At higher temperatures SiC and SiO2 can crystallize from amorphous Si-O-C glass. Filler reaction products Mo2C, Mo3Si, Mo5Si3 embedded in SiOxCy matrix. PMS-derived ceramic residue: SiO1.47C0.73; PPS-derived: SiO0.97C2.46. mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fracture toughness up to 5 MPa·m^0.5 for PMS:Mo pyrolyzed at 1400°C; 2.5 MPa·m^0.5 for PPS:Mo. Density up to 97% theoretical. Maximum hardness of 92 GPa and E-modulus of 250 GPa reported for 60 vol% PMS:(10 vol% SiC + 30 vol% Mo) system.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Mo2C (forms above 800°C), Mo3Si (above 1200°C), Mo5Si3 (with SiC filler substitution), unreacted Mo; SiC and SiO2 can crystallize from amorphous Si-O-C at higher temperatures

notes: Paper investigates two polysiloxane precursors (PMS and PPS) with Mo reactive filler for fabrication of Mo2C-containing ceramic composites. Pyrolysis temperature range studied: 1000-1400°C. Ceramic yield of up to 85 wt% cited from references for polysiloxane generally. Molecular weight of 22862 g/mol reported for PMS only (described as average molecular mass, method unspecified). Heating rate for second ramp given as 1-2 K/min; midpoint 1.5 K/min noted. Hold times are 4 h (240 min) at both 550°C intermediate hold and final temperature. Porosity of 2.5% at 1400°C for PMS:Mo system. Hardness of 92 GPa appears in text but may be a typographical error in the original paper (likely 9.2 GPa); reported as stated in the source text.
source: Polymer-filler derived Mo2C ceramics

backbone_architecture.description: Low viscosity liquid PCS with average molecular weight of ~1500 g/mol

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCS pyrolysis yields SiC microcrystals; in combination with Si90Zr10 alloy RMI, composite phases include SiC, ZrC, ZrSi2, Si, and C as identified by XRD

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: PCS-Si90Zr10 slurry RMI-derived C/C-SiC-ZrC composite bending strength: 306.4 MPa; C/C preform bending strength: 70.4-71.0 MPa; T-C/C-SiC-ZrC (traditional RMI) bending strength: 292.8 MPa

source: Polymer-metal slurry reactive melt infiltration- A flexible and controllable ceramic modification strategy for irregular C:C components

elemental_composition.other_elements: Cu: 2.28 wt% in cPCP; 0.21 wt% in cPCP-Ex (residual catalyst impurity)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: 1,2,3-triazole units formed via azide/alkyne click reaction; Cu-N coordination between triazole nitrogen lone pairs; C-N pyridinic bonding in carbon matrix at high pyrolysis temperatures

functional_groups.other: azide groups (from bis(azidomethyl)dimethylsilane monomer), alkyne groups (from 1,4-diethynylbenzene monomer), triazole rings formed in backbone

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: cPCP (with Cu, 2.28 wt%) gives 35% char yield; cPCP-Ex (Cu extracted, 0.21 wt%) gives 15% char yield. No significant difference below ~420 C. Mass loss of cPCP reduces between 730 and 1500 C. Theoretical ceramic yield is 13.5% for pure SiC and 37.8% for SiC/graphite mixture. Reintroduction of 1 wt% Cu catalyst complex into cPCP-Ex increased ceramic yield by ~15% (doubling). Intermediate pyrolysis temperatures of 800 and 1100 C also studied.

backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosilane backbone formed via Cu-catalyzed azide/alkyne click polymerization of 1,4-diethynylbenzene and bis(azidomethyl)dimethylsilane, incorporating 1,2,3-triazole units in the chain. Inter- and intra-chain Cu chelation possible via triazole nitrogen lone pairs.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Both cPCP and cPCP-Ex yield beta-SiC and graphite after pyrolysis at 1500 C. Crystalline elemental Cu observed at 800 C; Cu-Si intermediate (copper silicide, CuxSiy) observed at intermediate temperatures. Hexagonal SiC (6H polytype) confirmed absent. Cu and Cu2O residual phases present after 1500 C pyrolysis. Pyridinic N-C also present in carbon matrix. SiO2 detected at lower temperatures, attributed to surface oxidation or residual air during curing.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Preceramic polymer is broadly amorphous; after pyrolysis at 1500 C: beta-SiC (cubic), graphite, residual Cu/Cu2O; CuxSiy intermediate at 800-1100 C; elemental Cu at 800 C

notes: Polymer synthesized via Cu-catalyzed azide/alkyne click reaction using (PPh3)3CuCl catalyst. Two batches studied: cPCP (washed with hexanes and IPA only, 2.28 wt% residual Cu, 1 Cu per 400 triazole rings) and cPCP-Ex (additionally extracted with aqueous EDTA-K2 solution, 0.21 wt% residual Cu). Cu impurities catalyze SiC formation via molten Cu/copper silicide intermediate above 1085 C (Cu melting point), significantly increasing ceramic yield from 15% to 35%. Build direction (X) shrank more than in-plane directions, indicating mild anisotropy. notes: Study is a review/overview of Si-(B-)C-N ceramics derived from preceramic polymers, focusing on phase formation kinetics and thermal stability. O content 2-3 at.% (midpoint 2.5 used); H content 4-7 at.% (midpoint 5.5 used). Pyrolysis temperature range 1000-1450 C across materials (midpoint 1225 used); heating rate range 1-25 C/min depending on material and step. Si-C-N amorphous state stable to ~1500 C; Si-B-C-N stable to ~2000 C. Crystallization activation enthalpy 12.5 +/- 1.0 eV for SiCN1. JMAK exponent n=2.3-2.5 indicating 3D diffusion-controlled growth with slightly decreasing nucleation rate. Bulk ceramics produced by uniaxial hot-pressing at 40-50 MPa, 200-400 C. Characterization by XRD (CoKalpha), TEM, SAXS, SANS, NMR, n-RBS, EDX, Nuclear Resonant Reaction Analysis.

notes: Study compares two preceramic precursors: polysilazane HTT1800 and cyclotrisilazane (CTS), both modified with hafnium(IV) n-butoxide. HTT1800 reacts at both Si-H and N-H sites with the alkoxide (unique, unreported previously), while CTS reacts only at N-H sites. This leads to homogeneous Hf distribution in HTT1800-derived ceramic vs. local Hf enrichment (stringlike regions) in CTS-derived ceramic. Raman FTIR data: for HTT1800 with 30 wt% alkoxide, Si-H band decreases ~47.5% and N-H band ~62.9% (FTIR); with 50 wt% alkoxide, Si-H ~64.1% and N-H ~78.6%. Pyrolysis at 1100°C yields amorphous SiCN/HfO2 nanocomposites. The precursor architecture critically determines microstructure and high-temperature behavior. HTT1800-derived ceramic shows superior thermal stability at 1600°C. NMR chemical shifts for HTT1800: 0 ppm (Si-CH3), 0.6 ppm (N-H), 4.5 ppm (Si-H), 5.7 and 6.0 ppm (vinyl). Ratio per vinyl group: ~4 Si-H, 5 N-H, 5 methyl groups.

notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. notes: Two gel systems studied: Gel A (boron-free) and Gel B (boron-containing, B:Si=0.02 actual). Precursors: triethoxysilane (TREOS) and methyldiethoxysilane (MDES), TREOS:MDES=2. Boron source: triethylborate (TEB), nominal B:Si=0.1, actual B:Si=0.02 after evaporation during processing. 29Si MAS NMR identified silicon sites: HSiO3 (-85 ppm), HSiCO2 (-34 ppm), SiO4 (-110 ppm), SiCO3 (-64 ppm) in gels. Gel A ceramic yield: 89 wt% at 1000C. Gel B ceramic yield: 97 wt%. Chemical analysis given in wt% not atomic %. Paper focuses on boron catalysis mechanism for enhanced ceramic yield in SiOC precursor gels.

notes: This paper is primarily an XPS characterization study of sol-gel-derived silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) glasses, not a polymer characterization study per se. The precursors are triethoxysilane (HSi(OEt)3) and methyldiethoxysilane (HMeSi(OEt)2) co-hydrolyzed to form gels which are then pyrolyzed. Two compositions studied: M-0.1 (1/0.1 molar ratio) and M-1 (1/1 molar ratio). O/Si and C/Si atomic ratios reported by XPS at 1000, 1400, and 1500°C (see table). notes: Study focuses on polymer-derived SiOC glasses fabricated from crosslinked polysiloxane precursors. PHMS (MW 1900) crosslinked with TVTMS (low carbon) or DVB (high carbon) via Pt-catalyzed hydrosilylation. Pyrolysis at 1200°C in Ar flow. SiOC network composition SiCxO2(1-x) with x~0.4-0.5 held approximately constant across samples while free carbon varied from ~18 to ~60 vol%. Nanoindentation performed on polished, resin-embedded samples. Poisson ratio of 0.13 used (average of silica 0.15 and SiOC 0.11 literature values). High-C samples less prone to cracking during pyrolysis, attributed to lower elastic modulus. Earlier study on y=0 SiOC found E up to 110±6 GPa and H up to 9.3±0.4 GPa for SiC0.37O1.25.

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: argon or CO2 (CO2 used up to 800°C then switched to Ar for CO2 cycle; Ar used throughout for inert cycle)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: SiOC in Ar: stable to ~400°C then major weight loss ending at ~800°C (~14 wt% loss). SiOC in CO2: weight increase starting ~300°C with maximum at ~350°C, then weight loss up to ~600°C, stable above with small change at ~800°C. SiCN in Ar: decomposition starts at lower temperature than SiOC, first weight loss 200-300°C (evaporation of low MW fragments), stable above 800°C. SiCN in CO2: same initial weight loss then mass increase around 350°C persisting to ~550°C. TGA in air similar to CO2 but shifted to lower temperatures. Ceramic yields (disk samples): SiOC-Ar 88.8%, SiOC-CO2 95.4%, SiCN-Ar 77.2%, SiCN-CO2 89.5%.
