Polymer found formulas: 1M: Si3B1.1C6.5N3.0H20; 1P: Si3B1.1C6.2N3.2H18; 2P: Si3B1.0C6.2N4.3H17; 2D: Si3B1.0C6.1N2.5H17; 3P: Si3B1.0C9.1N2.9H23

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds implied by borosilazane backbone; B-H observed in IR of 2P at 2477 cm-1; C=C (vinyl) residual groups observed in 1P and 2P; Si-N-H deformation bands at ~1160-1172 cm-1; 4-fold coordination of boron centers confirmed by 11B MAS NMR

functional_groups.other: Residual vinyl (C=C) groups present in 1P and 2P due to incomplete hydroboration under heterogeneous conditions; B-H hydride observed in 2P

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed in flowing argon at 50 cm3/min, 25-1100 deg C, heating rate 2 deg C/min for polymer-to-ceramic conversion monitoring. Bulk ceramization at 25-1400 deg C, 1 deg C/min, 3h dwell. Ceramic yields: 1M: 88% (at 1400 deg C); 2P: 84% (at 1100 deg C); 3P: 55% (at 1100 deg C). Mass loss for 1M: 25-250 deg C: 0%, 250-750 deg C: 11%, 750-1400 deg C: 1%. Mass loss for 2P: 25-300 deg C: 0%, 300-700 deg C: 14%, 700-1100 deg C: 2%. Mass loss for 3P: 180-700 deg C: 45%. High-temperature TGA in argon up to 2200 deg C (heating rate <1400 deg C: 5 deg C/min, >1400 deg C: 2 deg C/min) shows ceramics stable up to 2000 deg C. High-temperature TGA in air up to 1700 deg C also performed; materials show oxidation resistance via self-protection.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: Reactive vinyl/Si-H groups enable thermal crosslinking; dehydrogenative coupling (n-BuLi catalyst) used for 2D; hydroboration used for P-route compounds; ammonolysis used for M-route compounds

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Not determined; authors state molecular weights could not be determined due to poor solubility

backbone_architecture.description: Boron-modified polysilazane network of type {B[C2H4Si(R)NH]3}n where C2H4 bridges connect boron centers to silicon centers; highly cross-linked silsesquiazane structures (R=(NH)0.5) also described; polymers are colorless solids or waxes with poor to very low solubility indicating network/highly branched character

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: As-obtained ceramics are fully amorphous. Crystallization occurs at 1550-1750 deg C depending on composition: alpha-SiC or alpha-SiC/beta-Si3N4 phases form. Ceramic formulas (from elemental analysis): 1M: Si3B1.2C4.9N3.1; 1P: Si3B1.1C5.3N3.0; 2P: Si3B1.1C3.0N4.0; T21: Si3B1.0C4.3N2.0

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Si-B-C-N ceramic fibers derived from related N-methylpolyborosilazane precursor reported to have remarkable high-temperature mechanical properties (referenced to Baldus and Jansen work, not quantified in this text)

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: alpha-SiC and alpha-SiC/beta-Si3N4 identified after annealing at 1550-1750 deg C; as-pyrolyzed ceramics fully amorphous

notes: Multiple compounds synthesized via three routes: monomer ammonolysis (M), polymer hydroboration (P), and dehydrogenative coupling (D). Boron incorporation via hydroboration of vinyl groups using BH3·S(CH3)2. All precursors extremely sensitive to moisture and air. Ceramic yields improved from 50% (R=CH3 reference) to 83-88% by substituting bulky groups with lower-weight and/or reactive entities. High-temperature stability demonstrated up to 2000 deg C in inert atmosphere. Oxidation resistance studied by TGA in air up to 1700 deg C and SEM/EDX. Crystallization investigated at 1400-2000 deg C in graphite furnaces. XRD used Siemens D5000 with Cu Kalpha1 radiation. Solid-state NMR: 29Si, 13C CP-MAS, and 11B MAS performed; 11B NMR shows broad signal at ~0 ppm indicating 4-fold boron coordination in solid state. Oxygen impurities <2 atom% noted in ceramic analyses.
source: Synthesis and Thermal Behavior of Novel Si−B−C−N Ceramic Precursors

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental analysis (found) for hydridopolycarbosilane (aqueous workup): C 28.26 wt%, H 7.36 wt%, Si 48.71 wt%, Cl 1.63 wt%, O 0.02 wt%. Best NMR-based formula approximation: [SiH1.86Et0.15CH2]n

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si carbosilane backbone units; residual Si-Cl (minor, ~1.63 wt% Cl found); Si-OEt and Si-Et side groups from ether solvent side reactions; Si-CH2 bridging units forming branched network

functional_groups.other: Ethyl groups (Si-Et) and ethoxy groups (Si-OEt) incorporated as minor side products from reaction with diethyl ether solvent; chloromethyl end groups (minor); SiH3, SiH2, and SiH units present as evidenced by 29Si NMR DEPT

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Paper notes the polymer undergoes facile thermal cross-linking reactions leading to high ceramic yields, but no specific TGA data or ceramic yield values are reported in the extracted text

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC using polystyrene standards (200-470000 amu) in HPLC-grade toluene at 40°C; Waters Ultrastyragel columns (100, 500, 10000 Å porosity); RI detection

backbone_architecture.description: Highly branched polycarbosilane with Si-CH2-Si backbone. Contains four types of structural units: tail (SiCl3CH2-/SiH3CH2-), linear (-SiCl2CH2-/-SiH2CH2-), single-branched (>SiClCH2->SiHCH2-), and double-branched (>SiCH2-). Branching results from trifunctional SiCl3 monomer undergoing head-to-tail Grignard coupling. MW distribution broad: 300 to ~50000 amu, majority 300-3000 amu

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Polymer described as precursor to near-stoichiometric silicon carbide due to nearly 1:1 Si:C ratio in backbone

notes: Polymer synthesized by Grignard coupling of (chloromethyl)trichlorosilane [Cl3SiCH2Cl] with Mg in diethyl ether, followed by LiAlH4 reduction. Theoretical average formula [SiH2CH2]n; best NMR approximation [SiH1.86Et0.15CH2]n. Chloropolycarbosilane intermediate has theoretical formula [SiCl2CH2]n. Overall yield ~40% from Cl3SiCH2Cl. Polymer is a viscous, transparent, pale yellow oil; not pyrophoric; reasonably air-stable. 29Si NMR (coupled) shows JSi-H ~200 Hz. IR of hydridopolycarbosilane: strong Si-H stretch at 2140 cm-1. Side reactions with diethyl ether solvent incorporate minor Et and OEt groups. Residual Cl ~1.63 wt%. Authors: Chris K. Whitmarsh and Leonard V. Interrante, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, 1990.
source: Synthesis and structure of a highly branched polycarbosilane derived from (chloromethyl)trichlorosilane

notes: This paper is not about preceramic polymers. It describes the isothermal nitridation of Li-doped aluminum melt (2.3 wt% Li in Al) at 1273 K to produce high-purity AlN powder. The process involves direct melt nitridation, not polymer pyrolysis. None of the preceramic polymer descriptors are applicable.
source: Synthesis of High Purity AIN by Nitridation of Li-Doped AI-Melt

microstructural.ceramic_phase: Ti3SiC2, TiC, SiC, TiSi2, TiSixAly, Al4C3
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Phase composition depends on preform type (TiC or TiC-C) and infiltrant (Si melt, Al melt, or Al-Si alloy). Ti3SiC2 formed in TC-S, TC-AS, and T-AS samples. TiSi2 and SiC present in TC-S. TiSixAly and Al present in T-AS and TC-AS. Al4C3 present in TC-A. No residual Si found in T-AS.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Ti3SiC2, TiC, SiC, TiSi2, TiSixAly, Al, Al4C3 identified by XRD depending on sample; Ti-Si rich eutectic alloy detected by EDS but below XRD detection limit in some samples

notes: This paper is NOT about preceramic polymers. It concerns the fabrication of Ti3SiC2-based MAX phase ceramics via reactive melt infiltration (RMI) of TiC and TiC-C preforms with Si melt, Al melt, and Al-Si alloy. No polymer precursors are involved. All fields related to polymer chemistry are null. Infiltration conducted at 1500 degrees C for 2 h under vacuum. Preforms pre-sintered at 1400 degrees C in flowing argon for 1 h. TiC-SiC interface lattice misfit reported as -0.76%. Twin boundary energies cited: pure TiC 0.927 J/m2, Si-doped TiC 0.325 J/m2, Al-doped TiC -0.073 J/m2. Ti3SiC2 intermediate layer thickness approximately 20 nm observed by TEM.
source: Synthesis of Ti3SiC2-based materials by reactive melt infiltration

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si bonds formed during oxidative curing; C-O bonds present in cured polymer; allyl (C=C) groups present in HBPCS; Si-Si bonds possible via dehydrocoupling

functional_groups.other: allyl end groups on HBPCS; dense SiH2 groups on SiHx cross-linker

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Uncrosslinked HBPCS alone yields only 11 wt% ceramic at 1000 C. After addition of SiHx cross-linker (2:1 HBPCS:SiHx by weight) and oxidative curing, ceramic yield rises to 80 wt% at 1000 C. N2-atmosphere cured sample yields only 5 wt%. N2-then-air cured sample yields 59 wt%. Further heating to 1800 C results in 39% mass retention after carbothermal reduction converting SiOC to SiC.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal oxidative curing (air, up to 280 C); initial hydrosilylation cross-linking (Pt-catalyzed); Si-H groups react with alkenes to form Si-C bonds; Si-O-Si bonds form during oxidative curing

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC relative to polystyrene standards; three molecular weights synthesized: 7.7, 29, and 43 kDa

backbone_architecture.description: Allyl-terminated hyperbranched polycarbosilane based on Muzafarov synthesis; dense network of reactive alkene sites throughout the polymer structure; Si-C backbone

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC at 1000 C; beta-SiC at 1800 C
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000 C: amorphous SiOC with C=55.7, O=23.0, Si=21.3 atomic% (2:1 HBPCS:SiHx ratio). At 1800 C: crystalline beta-SiC with C=49.5, O=1.3, Si=49.1 atomic%. Silica domains evident at 1600 C (2-theta ~22 deg). Carbothermal reduction between 1600-1800 C expels oxygen as CO gas. SiOC samples at 1000 C show carbon D and G bands in Raman (1342 and 1558 cm-1). Raman of 1800 C sample shows polycrystalline cubic 3C-SiC (TO at 797, LO at 971 cm-1).

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous at 1000 C; semi-crystalline at 1600 C; crystalline at 1800 C
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (prominent peaks at 1800 C); onset of SiC crystallinity and silica domains at 1600 C

notes: Two-component PCP system: HBPCS (allyl-terminated hyperbranched polycarbosilane) + SiHx (silane-rich small molecule cross-linker with dense SiH2 groups). Primary ratio studied: 2:1 HBPCS:SiHx by weight (1.5 equiv SiH relative to alkene). Elemental compositions for varying HBPCS:SiHx ratios from EDS (atomic%): 6:1 -> C=40.3, O=35.1, Si=23.4; 4:1 -> C=45.3, O=30.5, Si=23.2; 2:1 -> C=55.7, O=23.0, Si=21.3; 1:1 -> C=54.2, O=20.2, Si=25.6. Crystallite sizes: 3.5 nm at 1600 C and 66 nm at 1800 C by Scherrer equation. Platinum catalyst (910 ppm by weight) retained after polymerization facilitates initial low-temperature cross-linking. Aerosol jet printing demonstrated; printed lines 3.0 um thick after curing, 2.0 um after 800 C pyrolysis. Commercial silazane (1,1,3,3-tetramethyldisilazane) used as comparison cross-linker yielded only 25.2 wt% ceramic. Pyrolysis to 1800 C results in 39% mass retention. Molecular weights of 7.7, 29, and 43 kDa had similar ceramic yields at 2:1 ratio.
source: Synthesis of a Two-Component Carbosilane System for the Advanced Manufacturing of Polymer-Derived Ceramics

polymer_type: hafnium-containing single-source liquid precursor (polymer-derived ceramic precursor)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Hf-containing single-source aqueous-based solution; specific elemental percentages not reported

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Hf-C bonds implied from HfC ceramic product; specific precursor bonding structure not described in the text

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Liquid-to-ceramic yield ranges from ~22.79% to ~28.08% depending on pyrolysis temperature and additives; crosslinked-to-ceramic yield ranges from ~50.12% to ~56.32%. Heating rate reported as 60 deg C/sec (equivalent to 3600 deg C/min) in one-step laser SLRP process. Range of pyrolysis temperatures tested: 1700, 1800, 2000 deg C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (DCP - dicumyl peroxide) or UV/photo (BZP - benzophenone); in one-step SLRP process crosslinking and pyrolysis are combined simultaneously via CO2 laser

backbone_architecture.description: Described as a saturated, aqueous-based single-source liquid precursor; detailed backbone architecture not reported

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD, SEM, and TEM confirmed crystallinity and phase purity of synthesized HfC powder. Thermal activator (DCP) yielded pure HfC phase. Furnace-based reference [31] produced HfC/HfO2 mixture. No oxide or secondary phases reported for laser-based SLRP baseline process.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Vickers hardness of 23.5 GPa and elastic modulus of 461 GPa reported as literature reference values for HfC ceramic (not measured in this study). Thermal conductivity: 21-28 W/mK (literature reference).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: HfC

notes: Paper focuses on a novel one-step selective laser reaction pyrolysis (SLRP) method using a CO2 IR laser (10.6 µm wavelength, up to 120 W peak power) to convert liquid SHP199 Hf-containing precursor directly into HfC ceramic without separate crosslinking and furnace pyrolysis steps. Ceramic yield (liquid-to-ceramic) range: 22.79%-28.08%; crosslinked-to-ceramic yield range: 50.12%-56.32% depending on pyrolysis temperature (1700-2000 deg C) and additives (DCP or BZP). Heating rate of 60 deg C/sec noted in text. Hold time 2 min at target temperature. Comparison to furnace-based references [31] and [32] also provided in tables. HfC coatings were deposited onto carbon-carbon (C/C) composite substrates. Additive ratios tested: DCP at 100:1, 50:1, 25:1 (precursor:additive wt); BZP at 25:1 and 10:1 with 5 or 30 min UV pre-exposure. The ceramic yield values in the notes field represent the full range; the midpoint of liquid-to-ceramic yield across all conditions is approximately 25.76%.
source: Synthesis of hafnium carbide (HfC) via one‐step selective laser reaction pyrolysis from liquid polymer precursor

polymer_type: multi-metal polymer via modified Pechini process (polyesterification/chelation)
polymer_name: PDV, PDZr, PDW (multi-metal polymeric precursors for (TiHfVNbTa)C, (TiZrHfNbTa)C, (TiZrNbTaW)C respectively)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ti, Hf, V, Nb, Ta, Zr, W in equimolar ratios depending on composition; carbon provided by citric acid; oxygen from ethylene glycol and citric acid

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C=O ester (1730 cm-1), C=O carboxylate asymmetric/symmetric stretching (1653, 1558 cm-1), C-O carboxyl/ester (1180 cm-1), C-O ethylene glycol (1070, 1030 cm-1), C-H deformation (860-880 cm-1), Me-O-C stretching (632, 621, 649 cm-1 depending on composition)

functional_groups.other: ester groups (from esterification of citric acid and ethylene glycol), carboxylate groups (chelating metal ions), metal alkoxide groups (from alcoholysis of metal chlorides with ethylene glycol)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Main weight loss (~60 wt%) occurs between 150-500 degC. Endothermic at ~200 degC corresponds to decomposition/evaporation of ethylene glycol (m/z=62) and HCl (m/z=37). Endothermic at ~240 degC due to citrate decomposition with release of CO2 (m/z=44) and CH4 (m/z=16). Slight weight loss at 470 degC with CH4 and H2 evolution attributed to carbon chain cleavage/charring. Above 500 degC mass is stable. Ceramic yield range 30-40%, midpoint 35% used.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (esterification/polyesterification at 110 degC for 1h)

backbone_architecture.description: Polymer network formed by polyesterification between citric acid and ethylene glycol, with metal cations chelated by citrate groups and sterically entrapped within the polymer network; metal chlorides first reacted with ethylene glycol to form stable alkoxides, then chelated with citric acid; molar ratio of metal chlorides:ethylene glycol = 1:1:1:1:1:12; metal to citric acid molar ratio = 1:0.68

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Single phase rock-salt HEC formed after SPS at 1800 degC. PDZr showed trace tetragonal (ZrxHfy)O2 <5 vol%. Pyrolyzed precursor powders consist of mixture of nanocrystalline metal oxides and amorphous carbon. Metastable tetragonal HfO2 observed in polymer-derived precursor vs monoclinic HfO2 in solid-state precursor. TaVO4 phase observed in pyrolyzed PDV precursor. PDV lattice parameter 4.4220(5) Å, space group Fm-3m, theoretical density 9.393 g/cm3.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fracture toughness KIC = 4.29 MPa·m^1/2 for polymer-derived (TiHfVNbTa)C (PDV) sintered at 1800 degC. Hardness, elastic modulus measured by nanoindentation (Oliver-Pharr method, max load 10 mN, loading/unloading rate 0.5 mN/s, dwell 10 s, 50 tests per sample). Fracture toughness measured by Vickers indentation (49.03 N, dwell 15 s, 10 indentations per sample) using Niihara's method.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Pyrolyzed precursor: mixture of nanocrystalline metal oxides (including metastable tetragonal HfO2, TaVO4) and amorphous carbon. After SPS at 1800 degC: single-phase rock-salt HEC (Fm-3m). Rietveld refinement confirmed phase-pure (TiHfVNbTa)C.

notes: This paper focuses on multi-metal polymer precursors for high-entropy carbide synthesis via a modified Pechini process, not conventional preceramic polymers (polysilazane/polycarbosilane etc.). The polymer is a metal-organic network rather than a silicon-based preceramic polymer. Metal chlorides used: TiCl4, ZrCl4, HfCl4, VCl3, NbCl4, TaCl4, WCl6. Citric acid serves dual role as chelating agent and carbon source. Pyrolysis at 800 degC under argon yields amorphous carbon + metal oxide nanocrystals. Final HEC formation occurs during spark plasma sintering at 1800 degC under vacuum via carbothermal reduction. STA heating rate for characterization was 10 degC/min in argon; actual pyrolysis heating rate was 1 degC/min. Ceramic yield range 30-40% (midpoint 35% reported in ceramic_yield_pct field).
source: Synthesis of high-entropy carbides from multi-metal polymer precursors

elemental_composition.other_elements: Si, C, O confirmed present via XPS, EDS, and FTIR in pyrolyzed ceramic; exact atomic percentages not reported in main text

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Crosslinking step performed under vacuum at 1 C/min with 1 h holds at 160 C and 230 C prior to pyrolysis at 800 C. Burnout of BCP and HP porogens occurred concurrently with PCS-to-SiOC conversion.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

molecular_weight.measurement_method: as reported by supplier (Starfire Systems)

backbone_architecture.description: SMP-10 is described as a commercially available polycarbosilane (PCS) used as a SiC/SiOC precursor; no backbone architecture details provided in the text

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCS converts to SiOC ceramic upon pyrolysis at 800 C in Ar. Si, C, and O confirmed in ceramic struts via XPS, EDS, and FTIR. Both amorphous and crystalline states noted as possible depending on phase separation, decomposition, and crystallization kinetics. Oxygen content may vary due to native oxides on Si wafer substrates.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Prior work reported extraordinary mechanical properties for SiOC nanocoral approaching nanoarchitected material performance; specific values not reported in this paper

notes: This paper primarily describes the BCP/PCS blend system for templating porous SiOC ceramics. SMP-10 (polycarbosilane, Starfire Systems) is the preceramic polymer component blended with PMMA-b-PnBA-b-PMMA block copolymer and PMMA homopolymer in 2-ethylhexanol solvent. PCS content controls micelle morphology (spherical: >50 wt% PCS; wormlike: 40-50 wt% PCS; bicontinuous: <30 wt% PCS). Ceramic strut widths were ~17-18 nm across all morphologies. Porosity varied by morphology: spherical 24.2±2.0%, wormlike 35.7±2.0%, bicontinuous 29.6±0.3%. Characteristic lengths from SAXS: bicontinuous 42 nm, wormlike 35 nm, spherical 40 nm. PCS preferentially swells the PnBA block of the BCP. Detailed elemental percentages from XPS referenced to supporting information but not given in main text.
source: Tailorable Micelle Morphology in Self-Assembling Block Copolymer Gels for Templating Nanoporous Ceramics

polymer_name: PhTES, MTES, PhTES:MTES 2:1, PhTES:MTES 1:1, PhTES:MTES 1:2 (sol-gel derived polysiloxanes from phenyltriethoxysilane and methyltriethoxysilane)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental data reported as wt% in ceramics after pyrolysis. PhTES: C=39.6 wt%, O=29.1 wt%, Si=31.3 wt%, Cfree=37.2 wt%, formula SiO1.63C2.96; PhTES:MTES 2:1: C=30.3 wt%, O=30.9 wt%, Si=38.9 wt%, Cfree=25.3 wt%, formula SiO1.39C1.82; PhTES:MTES 1:1: C=25.9 wt%, O=32.4 wt%, Si=41.7 wt%, Cfree=20.2 wt%, formula SiO1.36C1.45; PhTES:MTES 1:2: C=25.4 wt%, O=32.2 wt%, Si=42.4 wt%, Cfree=19.4 wt%, formula SiO1.33C1.40; MTES: C=13.3 wt%, O=41.2 wt%, Si=45.5 wt%, Cfree=9.4 wt%, formula SiO1.59C0.68

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-phenyl bonds present in PhTES-containing samples; Si-O-Si backbone (polysiloxane); mixed bond tetrahedra SiO4, SiO3C, SiO2C2, SiOC3, SiC4 identified by 29Si MAS-NMR in ceramic products

functional_groups.other: Phenyl groups directly bonded to Si (from PhTES); ethoxy groups (OC2H5) as leaving groups during hydrolysis

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Mass loss up to 1000°C: PhTES=32.2%, PhTES:MTES 2:1=29.2%, PhTES:MTES 1:1=20.5%, PhTES:MTES 1:2=20%, MTES=15%. Two main mass loss events: below 350°C (residual Si-OH and Si-OEt) and between 470-600°C (redistribution reactions and methane evolution). Mass loss from 1000 to 1400°C is only 1.2-1.4% additional for PhTES:MTES 1:2 and MTES. Heating rate stated as 100°C/hour = ~1.67°C/min.

backbone_architecture.description: Sol-gel derived polysiloxane network formed by hydrolysis and condensation of triethoxysilane monomers (PhTES and/or MTES); dried gels show broad FTIR band at 1100-1000 cm-1 characteristic of long-chain/network siloxanes; fully condensed 3D network gel structure

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiOC at 1000°C with mixed bond tetrahedra (SiO4, SiO3C, SiO2C2, SiOC3) and disordered free carbon phase. At 1400°C, phase separation into SiO4-rich and SiC4-rich domains with nanocrystalline SiC detected by XRD (broad peak at 35°). Free carbon phase shows disordered graphitic character by Raman (D~1330 cm-1, G~1590 cm-1). Free carbon content ranges from ~9.4 wt% (MTES) to ~37.2 wt% (PhTES).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous SiOC with broad peak at 22° (amorphous silica) at 1000°C; at 1400°C additional broad peak at 35° corresponding to nanocrystalline SiC appears

notes: Study investigates SiOC ceramics derived from sol-gel polysiloxanes as Li-ion battery anodes. Carbon crystallite sizes La (from Raman Ferrari-Robertson formula): 13.5-14.7 Å at 1000°C, increasing to 17.5-20.1 Å at 1400°C. Electrochemical performance: best capacity ~939 mAh/g (1st cycle C/20) for PhTES:MTES 1:1; reversible capacity up to 600 mAh/g after 140 cycles. Coulombic efficiency first cycle: 60-65% for carbon-rich samples, ~25% for MTES. Heating rate of 100°C/hour corresponds to 1.67°C/min. Multiple polymer compositions studied simultaneously; all descriptors above reflect the family of materials.
source: Tailoring of SiOC composition as a way to better performing anodes for Li-ion batteries

elemental_composition.other_elements: Al incorporated via Aluminum-tri-sec-butoxide (ASB) precursor; final ceramic is SiAlCN

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Al-containing network bonds from ASB incorporation; amorphous ceramic alloy described as containing Si, O, C, N

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - dicumyl peroxide (DP) used as thermal initiator; crosslinked at 150°C for 24h

backbone_architecture.description: Amorphous ceramic network derived from polysilazane (HTT1800) modified with aluminum-tri-sec-butoxide; predominantly amorphous ceramic alloy after pyrolysis

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Predominantly amorphous; described as amorphous ceramic alloy consisting of silicon, oxygen, carbon, and nitrogen with aluminum incorporated

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Reported to have good micro-mechanical machinability with feature size as small as 20 μm

notes: Paper focuses on temperature sensor fabrication using polymer-derived SiAlCN ceramic. Precursor formulation: 8.8 g HTT1800 + 1.0 g ASB mixed at 120°C for 24h, then 0.2 g dicumyl peroxide added, cross-linked at 150°C for 24h, ball-milled to ~1 μm powder, pressed into discs, and pyrolyzed at 1000°C for 4h in nitrogen. Sensor operated up to 830°C with resistance decreasing monotonically with temperature. Thermistor equation constants: c1 = -3235, c2 = -3.6. Maximum measurement error ~4°C at 730°C. Ceramic possesses semiconducting behavior enabling temperature sensing.
source: Temperature sensor made of polymer-derived ceramics for high-temperature applications

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis performed in two steps: first at 200 C for 2 h to promote crosslinking, then at 700-900 C for 2 h. Heating rate 50 C/h, cooling rate 100 C/h. Free carbon formation promoted at elevated pyrolysis temperatures (800-900 C) as evidenced by Raman D and G bands. Specific surface area decreased with increasing pyrolysis temperature. Pyrolysis temperature range 700-900 C studied; midpoint 800 C used.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

backbone_architecture.description: Vinyl-functionalized polysiloxane used as preceramic polymer; structural architecture not explicitly described beyond vinyl functionalization

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pure SiOC ceramic is amorphous. SiOC/TiO2 composites contain anatase and rutile at 700 C; at 800 C anatase disappears and Ti4O7 forms with residual rutile; at 900 C Ti4O7 and Ti2O3 dominate. SiOC/N-doped TiO2 composites retain both anatase and rutile at 800 C due to nitrogen retarding anatase-to-rutile transformation; Ti4O7 and Ti2O3 form at 900 C.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiOC matrix is amorphous; TiO2 filler phases identified as anatase (JCPDS 21-1272) and rutile (JCPDS 21-1276); at higher pyrolysis temperatures Ti4O7 (JCPDS 77-1392) and Ti2O3 (JCPDS 43-1033) also identified

notes: Paper focuses on SiOC ceramic composites with TiO2 and N-doped TiO2 fillers for photocatalytic applications. Preceramic polymer is commercial vinyl-functionalized polysiloxane XP RV 200 (Hanse Chemie, Germany). Pyrolysis temperature range 700-900 C; heating rate 50 C/h (0.833 C/min). SiOC ceramic SBET values: 398, 248, 60 m2/g at 700, 800, 900 C respectively. SiOC is microporous (<2 nm pores); composites with TiO2 are mesoporous (~4 nm pores). TiO2 filler content studied at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 wt%. Raman spectroscopy confirms free carbon (D band at 1317 cm-1, G band at 1546 cm-1) in SiOC at 800 and 900 C but not at 700 C. N-doped TiO2 produced by ammonolysis of commercial TiO2 at 700 C for 2 h under NH3; nitrogen content ~1.7 wt% by XPS. Ceramic yield not reported.

notes: This paper focuses on UV curing of Durazane 1800 polysilazane highly filled with metallic fillers (80 vol.%) for corrosion protection coatings. Porosity range for UV-cured coatings: 30-33%; thermally cured ~31% (midpoint used: 31.5%). Coating thickness 18-22 µm (UV-cured) and ~22 µm (thermally cured). notes: This paper focuses on PDC-SiOC/ZrB2 nanocomposites for microwave absorption. The polymer is a commercial polycarbosiloxane (liquid precursor) from Extreme Environment Materials Solutions, LLC. Processing steps: (1) mix ZrB2 nanopowders in liquid precursor, (2) disperse under electromagnetic stirring, (3) cure/crosslink at 110-200°C, (4) crush and ball mill to ~1 micron (90 min), (5) uniaxial press at 700 Psi into 15 mm discs, (6) pyrolyze at 1000°C/3h/Ar/1°C per min. DC conductivity of pristine PDC-SiOC is ~10^-6 S/m. Average real permittivity of pristine PDC-SiOC is 4.24 and imaginary permittivity is 0.06 in Ka-band (26.5-40 GHz), making it a wave-transmitting (low-loss) matrix material. The composite NL32.5 achieved 60% microwave absorption at 26.5-40 GHz with 3 mm thickness.

notes: This paper focuses on characterization of two SiOC polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs) by 29Si and 13C MAS NMR spin-lattice relaxation to study nanometer-scale structure. MK1100 derived from Wacker-Belsil PMS MK polysiloxane; PR1100 derived from Polyramics RD-684a. A third sample MK1100-G was prepared with 0.08 wt% (800 ppm) Gd2O3 as paramagnetic dopant for relaxation studies. MK1100-G precursor was crosslinked at 200 C for 1.5 h before pyrolysis. 13C CPMAS NMR shows two carbon environments: sp2 graphitic carbon (isotropic shift ~130-139 ppm, ~70% in MK1100 and ~81% in PR1100) and sp3 SiC-type carbon (isotropic shift ~11-13 ppm). Si species distribution from 29Si MAS NMR: MK1100 has SiO4=44.0%, SiO3C=30.4%, SiO2C2=16.1%, SiOC3=3.0%, SiC4=6.5%; PR1100 has SiO4=32.4%, SiO3C=22.1%, SiO2C2=20.6%, SiOC3=8.0%, SiC4=16.9%. Mass-fractal dimensions D~2.5 for oxygen-rich SiCxO4-x units and slightly lower for carbon-rich units. SiOC ceramics thermodynamically stable vs. isocompositional mixture of cristobalite, SiC, and graphite. Polymer precursor pyrolysis heating rate stated as 100 C/h = 1.67 C/min.

notes: This is a review article covering polymer-derived Si-based ceramics (PDCs) including SiC, SiOC, SiCN systems. Specific polymer descriptors (elemental composition, bonding, molecular weight) are not reported for a single polymer but discussed broadly across multiple systems. Grain size range noted as 1-5 nm for Si-rich nanodomains (midpoint 3 nm used). Porosity of 73.4 vol% refers to open-cell SiC foam from Colombo's group using PMMA pore-forming agent. Modulus of 768.5 MPa and compressive strength of 65.5 MPa refer to DLP-printed Si3N4 honeycomb ceramics. Fracture strength of 108 MPa refers to PVSZ-derived thin-films after 3 PIP cycles. Electromagnetic wave absorption: minimum reflection coefficient -51 dB, EAB 3.0 GHz at 2.7 mm for CNW-modified SiCN. Specific surface areas up to 494 m2/g (freeze cast PDC nanocomposites) and ~400 m2/g (freeze cast SiOC with Ni). Cu-doped SiOC electrical conductivity: 9.32e-2 S/cm.

notes: Polymer synthesized from liquid polysilacarbosilane (PSCS) and Al(acac)3 at 9 wt% ratio in autoclave under inert atmosphere. Softening point: 220.7°C. Al content: 1.24 wt%. Pyrolysis conducted in temperature range 300-1800°C with heating rate 5-10°C/min (midpoint 7.5 used) and 1 h hold at each temperature in argon atmosphere. Raman analysis of pyrolysis residues: G band shifts from 1606 cm-1 (1100°C) to 1583 cm-1 (1800°C); ID/IG increases from 1.25 to 1.81 over 1100-1600°C range then drops to 0.75 at 1800°C; La increases from 1.5 nm (1100°C) to 6.61 nm (1800°C), indicating graphitization. Al inhibits beta-SiC grain growth and promotes alpha-SiC formation at 1600-1800°C. No nitrogen present in polymer system. Elemental compositions also reported for pyrolysis residues at 1300°C (Si: 55.75 wt%, C: 34 wt%, O: 8.24 wt%, Al: 2.01 wt%) and 1800°C (Si: 64.41 wt%, C: 33.9 wt%, O: 1.12 wt%, Al: 0.57 wt%).

notes: The paper primarily studies porous SiOC-bonded SiC ceramics, not the polymer precursor itself. The silicone resin (RSN-6018, Dow Corning) is used as a preceramic binder/bonding phase at 10-25 wt% loading with SiC powders. PMMA microbeads (40-60 um) are used as pore-forming agents at 5-20 wt%. Corrosion resistance of resulting ceramics better in acid (H2SO4) than alkali (NaOH). Darcy permeability of final ceramics: 7.02e-14 to 1.45e-12 m2. notes: This is a review paper on additive manufacturing (3D printing) of polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs). It does not describe a single polymer precursor in detail but surveys multiple systems and research groups. Key additive manufacturing methods discussed: DLP, SL, DIW, FDM, BJ, SLS, TPP, CLIP. Ceramic systems covered: SiOC, SiCN, SiC, Si3N4, SiBCN, ZrOC. Table provides comparative data for multiple SiOC and SiCN systems made by different AM techniques. Ceramic yields from table range: SiCN DLP 80% and 25.3%; SiOC DLP 44.1%, 40.1%, 29.63%, ~30%; SiOC DIW 94%, 31.3-58.84%; SiOCN DIW 77%; SiOC SLS 82%; SiOC BJ3DP 16.5%. Linear shrinkages range from 3% to 62.9%. Densities range from 1.05 to 2.64 g/cm3. Key challenges noted: cracking, deformation, and collapse during pyrolysis due to gas evolution from organic functional group decomposition. notes: This paper describes sol/gel synthesis of silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) glasses from alkyltrimethoxysilane precursors (methyl-, ethyl-, propyl-, phenyltrimethoxysilane). These are not traditional preceramic polymers but sol/gel-derived ceramic glasses. Carbon content in gels: 14% (methyl), 24% (ethyl), 32% (propyl), 57% (phenyl); carbon content in glasses: 12% (methyl), 17% (ethyl), 18% (propyl), 41% (phenyl). Hydrolysis conducted with H2O and HCl at pH 3, 60-80C for 4h; gelation initiated with 2M NH4OH at pH 8; dried at 85-90C for 7 days; heat-treated at 900C in flowing argon. >95% of methoxy groups hydrolyzed confirmed by 1H NMR. notes: This is a review paper covering SiOC, SiCN, SiBCN, and SiOCN polymer-derived ceramics as anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. No single polymer is characterized; multiple precursor systems are discussed. Table includes electrochemical data for numerous SiOC and SiCN compositions with free carbon content (wt%), reversible capacity (mAh/g), irreversible capacity (mAh/g), coulombic efficiency, cycling current, and capacity retention from literature references. Reversible capacities range from 69 to 794 mAh/g for SiOC and SiCN systems; some composites reach 1300-3000 mAh/g. Key precursors mentioned: PMPS, PPSSO, polysiloxane, polycarbosilane, sesquisilane, polysilazane, polysilocarbodiimide, polyethylenimine, polyphenylvinylsilicon carbide imide, polysilicone ethylenediamine, PEOS siloxanes. microstructural.ceramic_phase: HfO2, SiO2, HfSiO4 (at 1600°C for SHP-199/TEOS); HfC (at 1600°C for SHP-199 alone)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SHP-199 alone at 1000°C (S10): monoclinic m-HfO2 (~50%) and tetragonal t-HfO2 (~50%), crystallite sizes 13 nm and 9 nm respectively, plus amorphous phase and disordered carbon. SHP-199 alone at 1600°C (S16): predominantly HfC (crystallite size 43 nm, lattice parameter 4.636 Å, estimated HfC0.96), trace m-HfO2. SHP-199/TEOS at 1000°C (M10): m-HfO2 (~90% of crystalline content, 25 nm) and t-HfO2 (~10%, 14 nm), strong amorphous background. SHP-199/TEOS at 1600°C (M16): α-cristobalite-SiO2 (~60%, 60 nm), HfSiO4 hafnon (~20%, 50 nm), m-HfO2 (~20%, 40 nm), trace t-HfO2 (<1%); no SiC or HfC detected. Free carbon present in all samples per Raman. Carbothermal reduction kinetically hindered in M samples.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Monoliths described as robust; ~32% diameter shrinkage upon drying without fracture; fibers at 1600°C display rough, porous surfaces indicating release of gaseous species; fibers at 1000°C exhibit smooth surface textures

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SHP-199 alone at 1000°C: m-HfO2, t-HfO2; SHP-199 alone at 1600°C: HfC (dominant), trace HfO2; SHP-199/TEOS at 1000°C: m-HfO2, t-HfO2; SHP-199/TEOS at 1600°C: α-cristobalite-SiO2, HfSiO4, m-HfO2, trace t-HfO2

notes: SHP-199 is the first commercially available polycarbohafnium precursor, supplied by Starfire Systems as a brown aqueous solution (~30-40 wt% polymer). The polymer is synthesized from HfCl4 and 2-butyne-1,4-diol in water, producing poly(hydroxyhafniumdioxobutyne) with HfOCl2·8H2O as a co-product. The SHP-199/TEOS mass ratio used was 1:2, giving approximately 1:1 molar ratio of TEOS ethoxy groups to water and an Si:Hf elemental ratio of ~10:1. Gelation occurred within 10-15 minutes. Fiber widths ranged from 10-100 µm. Raman spectroscopy confirmed free carbon (D and G bands) in all pyrolyzed samples; M samples showed more ordered carbon than S samples. HfSiO4 (hafnon) confirmed by both XRD and Raman in M16. Crosslinking method enables fabrication of monoliths and fibers not achievable with SHP-199 alone. Sacrificial graphite sheets upstream of sample crucible used to scavenge oxygen impurities during pyrolysis. Crystallite sizes: S10 m-HfO2=13 nm, t-HfO2=9 nm; S16 HfC=43 nm; M10 m-HfO2=25 nm, t-HfO2=14 nm; M16 SiO2=60 nm, HfSiO4=50 nm, m-HfO2=40 nm.

notes: Paper focuses on SiOC-BNNT composite electrodes for Li-ion batteries and supercapacitors. TTCS is the preceramic polymer; composites contain 0.25, 0.5, or 2.0 wt% BNNTs and are supported on reduced graphene oxide (rGO, 40 wt%). Best LIB performance: SiOC-BNNT-0.25wt% showed 410 mAh/g first cycle reversible capacity at 100 mA/g, stabilizing at 238 mAh/g at 1600 mA/g. Best supercapacitor performance: SiOC-BNNT-0.5wt% showed 78.93 F/g at 1 A/g with 86% retention after 185 cycles. XPS Si 2p peak at 103.21 eV indicates Si-O bonds. BNNT average internal diameter ~4 nm confirmed by TEM. Charge storage mechanism attributed to pseudocapacitive/faradaic processes.

notes: Primary focus of paper is on electronic/electrical properties of carbon-rich polymer-derived SiCN ceramics. Electrical conductivity (dc): 0.148 S/cm at 1100C, 4.71 S/cm at 1400C, 9.26 S/cm at 1600C (record high RT conductivity of 9.6 S/cm reported for monolith at 1600C). Anomalous n-type to p-type charge carrier transition observed from 1100C to 1400-1600C via Hall measurement. Carrier density: 6.42e18 cm-3 (1100C), 8.45e19 cm-3 (1400C), 1.63e19 cm-3 (1600C). Carrier mobility: 1.45e-1, 3.52e-1, 3.55 cm2/Vs respectively. Raman spectroscopy used to characterize sp2 carbon evolution. Crystallite size La range noted in notes field: 7.66 nm (1100C) to 10.08 nm (1600C). Inter-defect distance LD: 7.58-8.69 nm. Defect density nD: 7.52e11 to 5.71e11 cm-2. Average continuous graphene length Leq: 11.06-17.76 nm. I2D/IG ratio ~1.7 (<=3 graphene layers) at all temperatures. Polymer mixed with 50 wt% DVB crosslinker.

notes: Polymer synthesized via two-step route: hydroboration of dichloromethylvinylsilane with borane dimethylsulfide, followed by aminolysis with methylamine. Glass transition temperature Tg ~ 38 C. backbone_architecture.description: Elemental analyses suggested branched-chain or partially cross-linked structures. Contains six-membered borazine rings and eight-membered rings. Structure includes biphenylic and naphtalenic-type arrangements. Degree of crosslinking controlled by synthesis temperature.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis of PBZ yields BN ceramic. BN nanoparticles from spray-pyrolysis of borazine at 1400C gave B1.0N0.9 composition. Hollow BN nano-polyhedrons composition B1.04N1.05O0.04 after annealing at 1800C in flowing nitrogen.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Microstructured disk-shaped BN from BN nanoparticles: relative density 96.3%, average hardness 8 Hv (78 MPa) sintered at 1840C. BN coating on SiBNC fibers showed no decrease in mechanical strength.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: BN (hexagonal); microporous BN architectures showed lack of long range ordering

notes: This is a review paper focused on boron nitride (BN) derived from B-N-H-containing molecular and polymeric precursors including ammonia-borane (AB), borazine (BZ), polyaminoborane (PAB), polyiminoborane (PIB), and polyborazylene (PBZ). PBZ is synthesized by self-condensation of borazine at low temperature in autoclave; synthesis temperature controls crosslinking and physical state (solid at 60C, liquid at 50C). Microporous BN architectures showed bimodal pore size distribution with micropore volume ~0.20 cm3/g, specific surface area 568 m2/g, total pore volume 0.78 cm3/g. BN nanoparticles from borazine spray-pyrolysis: specific surface area 34.6 m2/g, helium density 1.95 g/cm3, average particle size 89 nm. Ceramic yield of 90.9% noted for solid PBZ at 60C. The polymer contains only B, N, and H; no silicon, carbon, or oxygen in backbone.
source: Bernard_2014_Nanostructured and architectured boron nitride from boron ni

elemental_composition.other_elements: PB45: B3.0N3.0H4.8 (referenced to B3.0, O < 2 wt%); PB50: B3.0N3.8H4.0 (referenced to B3.0, O < 2 wt%); PB60: B3.0N3.5H4.5 (referenced to B3.0, O < 2 wt%); Economy et al. viscous polyborazylene: B3.0N3.6H3.7

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-H bonds (BH units), B-N bonds within borazine-type six-membered rings; B(HN2) and B(N3) boron sites; N(HB2) and N(B3) nitrogen sites identified by solid-state NMR; eight-membered rings in addition to six-membered borazine rings; biphenyl- and naphthalenic-type B-N structural units

functional_groups.other: B-H hydride on boron centers; N-H on nitrogen centers; reactive BH and NH units susceptible to dehydrocoupling crosslinking

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Weight losses measured by TGA in nitrogen atmosphere up to 1000 °C at 5 °C/min: PB45 = 70 wt%, PB50 = 53.2 wt%, PB60 = 8.8 wt%. Sneddon et al. reported ceramic yields of 84–93% and chemical yields of 89–99% for pyrolysis under argon or ammonia at 900–1450 °C. BN stable in air up to 900 °C (no weight change by TGA in air); weight gain above 900 °C due to boron oxide formation. Pyrolysis to 1450 °C yielded turbostratic BN; annealing to 1800 °C increased crystallinity and density.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - dehydrocoupling of BH and NH units during thermolysis/self-condensation

backbone_architecture.description: Branched-chain or partially cross-linked structure formed by self-condensation of borazine. Contains six-membered borazine rings and eight-membered rings; biphenyl- and naphthalenic-type structural units. Physical state controlled by thermolysis temperature: liquid at 45–55 °C (PB45, PB50), solid at ≥60 °C (PB60). Soluble in polar solvents (THF, glyme) despite crosslinked structure.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: hexagonal BN (turbostratic to hexagonal depending on pyrolysis temperature)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Turbostratic BN obtained at 1450 °C (B3.0N2.95, relative density 86.3%); increased crystallinity and relative density (93%) after annealing to 1800 °C. BN nanotube arrays produced at 1200–1800 °C; distinctly ordered wall structures at 1800 °C. Spray-pyrolysis BN sintered at 1840 °C gave relative density 96.3%. C/BN composites: relative density 94.7%, open porosity 5.1 vol%.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Average hardness of spray-pyrolysis/sintered BN bulk: 8 Hv (78 MPa). Warm-pressed PB60 monoliths shaped under 74 MPa at 60 °C. Thermal conductivity of disk-shaped BN: 3.26 W/m·°C at 1450 °C preparation, 6.56 W/m·°C at 1800 °C preparation.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to turbostratic to hexagonal depending on pyrolysis temperature
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: turbostratic BN at 1450 °C; hexagonal BN (h-BN) upon annealing above 1450 °C up to 1800 °C; crystallite sizes Lc and La calculated from Scherrer relation; interlayer spacing d002 from Bragg's law on (002) peak

notes: Paper is a review focused on polymer-derived boron nitride (BN) via PDCs route from borazine and trichloroborazine precursors, specifically polyborazylene and poly[B-tri(methylamino)borazine]. Three polyborazylene samples characterized: PB45 (thermolysis 45 °C, liquid, extremely volatile, [B3.0N3.0H4.8]n, 70 wt% loss), PB50 (50 °C, liquid volatile, [B3.0N3.8H4.0]n, 53.2 wt% loss), PB60 (60 °C, solid, [B3.0N3.5H4.5]n, 8.8 wt% loss). Oxygen content < 2 wt% for all samples. Hardness value of 0.078 GPa converted from 78 MPa as reported in text. Polyborazylene crosslinks before melting, preventing melt-spinning for fiber production. Dialkylamine-modified polyborazylenes explored as melt-processable alternatives (Sneddon et al.). Economy et al. polyborazylene formula B3.0N3.6H3.7 from self-condensation at 70 °C for 40 h in nitrogen. The paper also discusses poly[B-tri(methylamino)borazine] derived from trichloroborazine but detailed characterization data for that polymer were not extracted here as they appear in later sections not fully provided.
source: Bernard_2014_Polymer-Derived Boron Nitride A Review on the Chemistry Shap

functional_groups.other: hydroxyl (-OH, 3423 cm-1)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed in flowing air at 10 °C/min. Pure SiOC showed 97.2% residual weight with oxidation onset ~746.8 °C. SiOC-CNT composites showed higher oxidation resistance (~700 °C) than pure MWCNTs (~530 °C), attributed to protective ceramic shell. Residual weights used to calculate SiOC weight fraction in composites: 83.8% (SiOC-CNT-5), 76.3% (SiOC-CNT-8), 68.3% (SiOC-CNT-10).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - crosslinked at 400 °C for 4 h in inert atmosphere with 1 wt% dicumyl peroxide as initiator; pure SiOC crosslinked at ~300 °C in argon for 4 h

backbone_architecture.description: Cyclotetrasiloxane ring structure (4-membered Si-O repeat units in a cyclic arrangement) with methyl and vinyl substituents. Upon pyrolysis on CNT surfaces, forms shell/core architecture with SiOC ceramic shell surrounding MWCNT core.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD confirmed amorphous ceramic when processed at 1000 °C. Amorphous structure consists of ~1-2 nm size domains of silica wrapped by graphitic carbon chains. Oxygen-rich phases (SiO2C2, SiO3C, SiO4) and carbon-rich phases (SiOC3, SiC4) present. Nanovoids and silicon/carbon dangling bonds also present.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: SiOC-CNT composites showed no mechanical cracking or delamination after electrochemical cycling; SiOC alone showed micrometer-size cracks. Electrical conductivity of cold-pressed composite pellets: 1.2e-5 S/cm (SiOC-CNT-5) to 6.05e-5 S/cm (SiOC-CNT-10); pure SiOC at 1000 °C is electrically insulating (<1e-12 S/cm).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: amorphous - no crystalline phases identified at 1000 °C pyrolysis temperature

notes: Paper focuses on SiOC-CNT composite synthesis and electrochemical performance as Li-ion battery anodes. Precursor TTCS pyrolyzed at 1000 °C for 5 h in Ar at 5 °C/min after crosslinking at 400 °C for 4 h. Three composite compositions prepared: SiOC-CNT-5, SiOC-CNT-8, SiOC-CNT-10 (wt% CNTs in TTCS). Best electrochemical performance from SiOC-CNT-5: first cycle reversible capacity 841.8 mAh/g, 686.3 mAh/g after 40 cycles, 81.5% capacity retention, 99.6% average Coulombic efficiency. SiOC-CNT-5 calculated to have ~3 monolayers of SiOC on CNT surface. Hold time at pyrolysis temperature was 5 h (300 min). Ceramic yield of 97.2% refers to pure SiOC from TTCS.
source: Bhandavat_2013_Stable and Efficient Li-Ion Battery Anodes Prepared from Pol

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Fully dense amorphous SiCN ceramic; composition SiC0.99N0.85 with ~3 wt% oxygen; no detectable defects by SEM; density 2.23 g/cm3

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: PDCs reported to possess high hardness and fracture strength at room temperature; creep hardening behavior noted in general PDC literature cited

notes: Paper focuses on oxidation behavior of polymer-derived SiCN ceramic. Oxidation studied in air at 900-1200°C. Parabolic rate constants (kp): 900°C=0.39e-18 m2/s, 1000°C=1.3e-18 m2/s, 1100°C=2.8e-18 m2/s, 1200°C=4.8e-18 m2/s. Activation energy for oxidation = 120 kJ/mol, close to CVD and single-crystal SiC. Oxidation mechanism identified as oxygen diffusion through silica layer, similar to SiC. Disk samples: ~9 mm diameter, 2-3 mm thick, ~30% linear shrinkage from polymer to ceramic. Crosslinking initiator: 2-4 wt% dicumyl peroxide. Ceramic disk is black in appearance. Ceraset SN is liquid at room temperature.
source: Bharadwaj_2004_Oxidation Behavior of a Fully Dense PolymerDerived Amorphous

polymer_name: TDAl (Al-doped ladder-like polysilsesquioxane xerogel); T/D=2/1 (undoped polysilsesquioxane xerogel)

elemental_composition.other_elements: EDS after pyrolysis - SiOC glass: Si 32.17 at%, O 63.13 at%, C 4.70 at%; SiAlOC glass: Si 19.73 at%, Al 1.34 at%, O 52.01 at%, C 26.92 at%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Al bridges present in Al-doped xerogel; Al-OH groups present; Si-OH (silanol) groups present; Si-O-Si bridges present; [AlO4] tetrahedral units confirmed by Raman and NMR; Q4(1Al) and [AlO4] species confirmed by 29Si and 27Al MAS NMR

functional_groups.other: SiOH (silanol) groups; Al-OH groups; acetylacetone chelating agent residues (C-C and CH3 from AcAcH detected by Raman)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Total mass loss ~23.5% up to 1000 °C for TDAl xerogel. Initial loss <0.5% below 200 °C (residual solvents, ongoing polycondensation). Major loss of ~23% between 200-800 °C due to release of branched T/D oligomers and CH4/H2 from Si-C/Si-O redistribution and C-H bond cleavage. No further mass loss above 800 °C, confirming ceramization endpoint. Mass loss smoother and more consistent for Al-doped material vs undoped (21% loss for undoped T/D=2/1 in same range), indicating less violent glass formation process with Al3+ addition.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (two-step: drying at 70°C for 7 days, then annealing at 800°C for 30 min in argon)

backbone_architecture.description: Ladder-like silsesquioxane structure confirmed by XRD amorphous halos at 2theta ~10.38° (d1=8.52 Å, intramolecular chain width) and ~22.10° (d2=4.04 Å, interchain distance), and by MIR/Raman spectroscopy. Al-doped xerogel (TDAl) shows slightly increased d1 (+0.31 Å) vs undoped but same d2. Synthesized from MTES (T units) and DMDES (D units) with molar ratio T:D:Al = 2:1:0.15 via sol-gel hydrolysis and polycondensation.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous black glasses confirmed by XRD (no sharp reflections after pyrolysis at 800°C). Free carbon phase partially released from glass network upon Al3+ doping as suggested by EDS (higher C content in SiAlOC: 26.92 at% vs 4.70 at% in SiOC) and Raman. Al introduced into glass network as [AlO4] tetrahedra (Q4(1Al) in 29Si MAS NMR, [AlO4] in 27Al MAS NMR). SiAlOC surface flat with no cracks; SiOC surface shows bulges and cracks.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases detected; only amorphous halos present in both xerogel and pyrolyzed glass XRD patterns

notes: Precursor polymers: methyltriethoxysilane (MTES, T units) and dimethyldiethoxysilane (DMDES, D units) with aluminum tri-sec-butoxide (Al(OC4H9)3) and acetylacetone (AcAcH) as chelating agent. Molar ratio T:D:Al = 2:1:0.15. Sol-gel synthesis with HCl catalyst. Two-step thermal treatment: aging at 70°C (7 days in air) then annealing at 800°C (30 min, argon). Pyrolysis at 800°C chosen based on TGA showing no further mass loss above 800°C. Al3+ addition improves thermal stability (up to 1500°C reported in literature), reduces carbothermic reduction (weight loss minimized to ~3%), and produces smoother surface microstructure. Free carbon sp2 nanodomains (~1-2 nm) reported in literature for similar materials below 800°C. Potential application as anti-corrosive coatings and protective-conducting layers for metallic interconnects in Solid Oxide Fuel Cells. EDS elemental compositions reported are from pyrolyzed glasses (post-800°C), not from the preceramic polymer itself.
source: Bik_2019_SiAlOC glasses derived from sol-gel synthesized ladder-like

notes: Precursors: methyltriethoxysilane (MTES) and dimethyldiethoxysilane (DMDES) as organosilicon precursors; aluminum trisec-butoxide as Al3+ source; acetylacetone as chelating agent; HCl as catalyst. Coating applied by dip-coating (2 repetitions, 5 cm/min withdrawal, 60 s immersion, 15 min between immersions). Dried at 70 C in air for one week before pyrolysis. Substrate: Crofer 22APU ferritic stainless steel. FTIR confirms Si-C bonds preserved after thermal treatment. Formation of Si-O-Cr bridges observed after oxidation, believed crucial for oxidation suppression. Al addition improves performance over SiOC baseline (kp SiOC = 6.59e-14 g2 cm-4 s-1). notes: This paper focuses on the oxidation protection performance of SiAlOC PDC coatings on 48-2-2 TiAl alloy at 750 C for up to 1000 h in dry and humid air. The preceramic polymer synthesis and pyrolysis details are referenced to prior publications [26,27,36] and are not described in this text. Coating thickness after pyrolysis was ~650 nm with a ~140 nm interdiffusion/reaction zone. The SiAlOC coating reduced mass gain ~2.5x compared to uncoated TiAl after 1000 h, with coated specimens showing ~0.5 mg/cm2 mass gain. Free carbon in the SiAlOC glass was confirmed by Raman spectroscopy (D and G bands). Amorphous alumina was detected at the inner coating region. The coating promoted alpha-Al2O3 scale formation and suppressed outward Ti diffusion.

DSC shows slight decrease ~450 C (carbothermal reduction of Sn from Sn(Ole)2 decomposition) and significant drop ~650 C (preceramic to ceramic phase transition). TGA heating rate for characterization was 5 C/min in argon at 250 ml/min.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: radical/thermal - using dicumylperoxide (DCP) as radical initiator and HDDA (1,6-hexanediol diacrylate) as crosslinker at 140 C, aged at 140 C for 24 h

backbone_architecture.description: Q-T polysiloxane with hyperbranched PEOS (Q-type, tetraethyl orthosilicate-based) core and vinyl-functional T-silane (vinyltrimethoxysilane, VTMS) shell. Core-shell design with diffuse distribution of functional silanes at surface. Described as a compact dendrimer. Average Si connectivity ~3.2. microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD identified beta-Sn (nanocrystallite), SnO (incomplete carbothermal reduction, absent in SiOC/Sn-2.5), and amorphous SiO2 phases. notes: The preceramic polymer (funPEOS, XenCure V35) is a vinyl-functional Q-T polysiloxane with vinyl loading of 1 mmol/g, provided by Siloxene AG, Switzerland. It is blended with tin dioleate (Sn(Ole)2) at different mass ratios (funPEOS:Sn(Ole)2 = 2:1, 2:1.5, 2:2, 2:2.5) and HDDA crosslinker (0.5 g) with DCP initiator (20 wt% noted in table but contextually used as initiator). Pyrolysis at 1000 C in argon yields SiOC/Sn nanocomposites used as Li-ion battery anodes. Best electrochemical performance: ~650 mAh/g at 372 mA/g and ~750 mAh/g at 18.6 mA/g after 400 cycles. Ceramic yield range midpoint reported as 62.5% (range: 52-65 wt% depending on composition). TGA for characterization used 5 C/min; pyrolysis used 3 C/min.

polymer_name: THDH1, THDH2, THDH9 (sol-gel derived siloxane networks from TREOS/MDES mixtures)

backbone_architecture.description: Cross-linked siloxane network (polysiloxane gel) derived from co-hydrolysis and co-condensation of triethoxysilane (TREOS) and methyldiethoxysilane (MDES) in molar ratios of 1:1, 2:1, and 9:1 (TREOS:MDES). Network contains Si-H and Si-CH3 pendant groups within a Si-O-Si backbone.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC (silicon oxycarbide glass); SiC and free Si crystallites at high temperature
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000C: fully amorphous SiOC glass with mixed SiCxOy tetrahedra. At 1200C: THDH1 shows 100% SiC (crystalline trace ~1nm), THDH2 and THDH9 mostly amorphous with minor SiC. At 1400C: THDH1 16wt% SiC + 84wt% amorphous; THDH2 27wt% SiC + 1wt% Si + 72wt% amorphous; THDH9 8wt% SiC + 2wt% Si + 90wt% amorphous. At 1500C: THDH1 30wt% SiC + 70wt% amorphous; THDH2 12wt% SiC + 1wt% Si + 87wt% amorphous; THDH9 6wt% SiC + 4wt% Si + 90wt% amorphous. Density increases from gel (~1.26-1.54 g/cm3) to 1000C (~2.24-2.45 g/cm3). SSA decreases from gel (46-673 m2/g) to near zero at 1400-1500C.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC (beta-SiC) and Si crystalline phases appear above 1200C; material is amorphous at 1000C; SiO4 and mixed SiCxOy units in amorphous matrix identified by 29Si NMR

notes: Three distinct precursor gel compositions studied: THDH1 (TREOS:MDES=1:1), THDH2 (TREOS:MDES=2:1), THDH9 (TREOS:MDES=9:1). Precursors: methyldiethoxysilane (MDES) and triethoxysilane (TREOS). Sol-gel synthesis at pH 4.5, H2O/OEt=1, EtOH/Si=2. Dried at 120C. Pyrolysis at 1000C in Ar (100 cm3/min, 10C/min, 1h). Further annealing at 1200, 1400, 1500C in Ar using graphite furnace (10C/min, 1h). TGA under He atmosphere. 29Si NMR shows SiO4, SiCO3, SiC2O2, SiC3O, SiC4 and Si species with proportions varying with temperature and composition. Grain size range from crystallite size data: THDH1 SiC at 1200C ~1nm to 2.4nm at 1400C; THDH2 SiC 1.5-3nm, Si 30-31nm; THDH9 SiC 2.5-16nm, Si 14.5-19.2nm; midpoint reported as ~10.75nm. Paper focuses on structural characterization of SiOC glasses using multi-technique approach including 29Si/1H MAS NMR, FTIR, Raman, XRD, neutron diffraction, RDF, INS, HRTEM, density, and SSA measurements.

notes: This paper focuses on fabrication of ultrathin polyorganosilica (POSi) membranes via room-temperature oxygen ICP-RIE plasma treatment of poly(DMSco-MHOS) polysiloxane films for H2/CO2 separation, not classical preceramic polymer pyrolysis. The precursor polysiloxane is formed by mixing vinyl-PDMS (Wacker Dehesive 944), PMHS crosslinker (Cross-linker V24), and Pt catalyst (Catalyst OL) at mass ratio 63:23:14 in hexane/toluene (~0.83 mass% solution). Excess PMHS leads to residual Si-H groups that convert to Si-OH (confirmed by FTIR). Best membrane performance: H2 permeance 880 GPU, H2/CO2 selectivity 67 at 150°C (ICP 200W, RIE 20W, 100 mTorr, 120s, 20 sccm O2). Polysiloxane surface roughness Ra = 1.4 nm; POSi surface Ra = 0.6 nm. Water contact angle of polysiloxane ~110°, reduced to <10° immediately after plasma but recovers over time due to silanol condensation or PDMS migration. GIWAXS penetration depth ~8.1 nm at incident angle 0.08°.

notes: This paper focuses on Cf/(Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2Nb0.2Ta0.2)C-SiC high-entropy ceramic matrix composites fabricated by PIP. The (Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2Nb0.2Ta0.2)C precursor is a metal-organic preceramic precursor (not a conventional Si-based preceramic polymer). Grain size of (Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2Nb0.2Ta0.2)C powder reported as ~180-300 nm (midpoint 240 nm used). notes: Study focuses on quantitative structural evolution of polysilazane (HTT1800, Kion Corp.)-derived SiCN ceramics annealed at 1000, 1100, 1200, and 1300°C under UHP Ar. 29Si MAS NMR (19.6 T, 165.5 MHz) used to quantify SiC4, SiCN3, SiN4 populations. Demixing equilibrium reaction 4SiCN3 = SiC4 + 3SiN4 found to have positive enthalpy and positive entropy. Raman spectroscopy (532 nm) shows D peak (~1350 cm-1) and G peak (~1600 cm-1) with ID/IG ratios of 1.48, 1.26, 1.77, 2.04 at 1000, 1100, 1200, 1300°C respectively; lateral graphite domain size La of 1.54, 1.42, 1.69, 1.81 nm at those temperatures. EPR (X-band 9.5 GHz and G-band 406 GHz) revealed two kinds of carbon dangling bond defects: edge and interior of nanographite. Free carbon graphitization follows 2-D grain growth process. Si-containing area and free carbon area have positive enthalpy and entropy changes; interface area has negative enthalpy and entropy changes.

notes: Paper is an overview of polysiloxane microspheres prepared from PHMS via water emulsion/hydrosilylation crosslinking. Crosslinker: 1,3-divinyltetramethyldisiloxane (DVTMDS); catalyst: Pt(0) Karstedt complex. Macroporous variants produced by addition of metal salts (NiCl3, FeCl3, AgNO3) before emulsification via osmotic pressure mechanism. Core-shell capsules with n-eicosane core also described for PCM applications. Mechanical property midpoints noted: hardness range 10.6-12.4 GPa, modulus range 112.4-120.4 GPa across 1000-1400°C pyrolysis temperatures. Pyrolysis hold time for SSA table: 1 h or 5 h as indicated.

notes: This is a review paper covering multiple borazine-based preceramic polymer systems for BN fiber production. Key polymers discussed: (1) polyborazine 1 from tris(methylamino)borane B(NHCH3)3, Mw ~900, Tg 73 C, melt-spun at 150 C, yielded BN tubes rather than fibers; (2) polymers 6 and 7 from thermolysis of 2,4,6-tri(methylamino)borazine (4) and 2,4-di(methylamino)-6-(dimethylamino)borazine (5), both with Tg 65-90 C; (3) second-generation polyborazylenes with dipentylamino groups showing melt-spinnability. Melt-spinning conducted through 0.2 mm capillary spinneret. B-tri(methylamino)borazine identified as most promising candidate. All syntheses conducted under argon due to moisture sensitivity. Polymer-to-ceramic conversion under ammonia then nitrogen up to 1800 C. Presence of alkylamino groups on boron essential for melt-spinnability; alkyl groups on borazinic nitrogen atoms detrimental to polymer-to-ceramic conversion for fiber production.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TG/DTA conducted in N2 from RT to 1000C for perhydropolysilazane fibers; silicon nitride fibers analyzed from 1000C to 1500C. TG/DTA curves show difference in ceramic yield between fiber types (I) and (II) but similar pyrolysis behavior. Weight gain at ~1350C in fibers (B) attributed to elemental Si reacting with N2. Weight loss above ~1400C corresponds to oxygen loss. No exotherm observed in DTA associated with alpha-Si3N4 crystallization in either fiber type.

The polymer-derived SiBCN is described as having viscoelastic/viscous glassy properties (referred to as 'black glass'). Detailed polymer characterization (molecular weight, functional groups, elemental composition) is referred to external references [10,31] and not reproduced in this paper text. Hot pressing carried out in Ar atmosphere at 40 MPa. Heating rate 10 C/min (RT to 1000 C), 5 C/min (1000 to 1600 C). Densification mechanism studied via Bernard-Granger and Guizard creep model: n=1, Qd=123±5 kJ/mol (grain boundary sliding accommodated by atom diffusion, 1300-1400 C); n=2, Qd=249±5 kJ/mol (viscous flow of amorphous SiBCN, 1300-1400 C); n=3-5 at higher temperatures (lattice/intra-granular diffusion creep). ZrO2 addition decreases viscosity of amorphous SiBCN by oxygen ion diffusion.

Solvents: THF and TPM (1:1 v/v). TMPTA added as reactive diluent (final 22.86 wt%); photoinitiator 819 at 3.5 wt%. Viscosity before rotary evaporation: 50-80 mPa·s; reduced ~53% with TMPTA addition. Grain size range: 2-5 nm at 1000 °C, 4-8 nm at 1200 °C; midpoint 6 nm used for grain_size_nm field. EDS composition values are weight percent, not atomic percent. Two interfacial states observed: reconstructed carbide/SiC interfaces and coherent MXene/SiC interfaces. (Ti,V,Cr,Mo)Cx carbide shows FCC structure with d(220)=1.50 Å and d(311)=1.27 Å. SiC lattice fringes d-spacing 2.52 Å corresponding to 3C-SiC (111) / 6H-SiC (0006).

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three-stage pyrolysis: Stage 1 (RT to 237 C): ~7.37 wt% loss attributed to removal of hydroxyl groups and adsorbed water. Stage 2 (237 to 680 C): ~27.52 wt% loss corresponding to organic-to-inorganic transformation, breakdown of organic-inorganic molecular chains and departure of organic groups. Stage 3 (above 680 C): ~31.24 wt% loss linked to boron-carbon thermal reduction, release of CO, CO2, and B2O3, gradual formation of metal borides.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (stepwise curing at 100, 140, 180, 200, 220, 250 C each for 1 h)

backbone_architecture.description: Organic-inorganic hybrid network formed via cohydrolysis and polycondensation of metal acetylacetonate alkoxides with water (MAAs:H2O = 1:1 molar ratio); borate ester and allyl-functional novolac resin incorporated as boron and carbon sources respectively

microstructural.ceramic_phase: high-entropy diboride: (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb)B2, (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta)B2, (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb,Mo)B2, (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,Mo)B2 — all hexagonal close-packed (HCP, AlB2-type structure); also minor (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta)C carbide phase in sub-optimal compositions
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Single-phase HEB borides formed at 1800 C for systems with size difference factor delta < 3.9%. Systems with delta > 3.9% (e.g., (Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta,W)B2 and (Ti,Zr,Hf,Mo,W)B2) show impurity phases including (Mo,W)2B5, W2B5, minor (Ti,Zr,Hf,Mo,W)C and B4C. C content <0.9 wt%, O content <0.7 wt% in optimal single-phase powders.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Hexagonal (HCP, AlB2-type) single-phase solid solution for (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb)B2, (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta)B2, (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb,Mo)B2, (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,Mo)B2; SAED confirms single-crystal hexagonal structure for (Ti,Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta)B2; HR-TEM lattice spacing 0.2097 nm for (101) plane

notes: This paper does not describe a silicon-based preceramic polymer. The precursor system is a metal alkoxide/borate ester/novolac resin hybrid used to synthesize high-entropy transition metal diboride (HEB) ceramic powders via liquid-phase precursor pyrolysis and boro/carbothermal reduction. Grain size range reported as 340-570 nm (midpoint 455 nm used). Optimal M:B:C molar/mass ratio is 1:16:30. Single-phase formation is governed by the size difference factor delta; delta must be below ~3.9% for single-phase boride formation. The paper references precursor impregnation pyrolysis as a ceramic composite fabrication route. Metal sources: Ti(OC3H7)4, Zr(OC3H7)4, HfA, NbA, TaA, MoA, WA (prepared from metal chlorides and n-propanol). Boron source: self-made borate ester. Carbon source: self-made allyl-functional novolac resin.
source: Gong_2023_Synthesis and Characterization of High-Purity High-Entropy D

elemental_composition.other_elements: Zr, Hf, Nb, Ta, W, C, O - ceramic products are (Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)C with C vacancies 4.20-8.51% and O impurities 0.89-0.96 wt%; exact precursor elemental composition not reported

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Metal-O bonds (M-O, M = Zr, Hf, Nb, Ta, W) from metal alkoxide precursors; metal-C bonds form during carbothermal reduction; W-O, Nb-O, Ta-O, Hf-O, Zr-O detected by XPS during pyrolysis; final ceramic has M-C bonds in FCC rock-salt structure

functional_groups.other: Metal alkoxides (M-OR groups, e.g. Zr(OC3H7)4 zirconium n-propoxide); hydroxyl groups present in precursor (dehydration observed below 230°C)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three-stage pyrolysis: (1) ambient to ~230°C, 6.46 wt% loss from dehydration of hydroxyl groups and absorbed water; (2) 230-600°C, 10.38 wt% loss from organic-to-inorganic conversion releasing H2O, CO2, CH4; (3) above 600°C, 27.76 wt% sharp decrease from carbothermal reduction releasing CO and CO2. Carbothermal reduction sequence: W-O and Nb-O at ~800°C, Ta-O and Hf-O at ~1000°C, Zr-O at ~1200°C. Single-phase carbide achieved at 1500°C. Powder pyrolyzed at 1600°C used for sintering due to low oxygen content and high sintering activity.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - stepwise curing at 100, 120, 160, 180, 200, 220, 250°C each for 1 hour at 3°C/min

backbone_architecture.description: Metal alkoxide-based polymer precursor with multi-metal coordination; transforms to amorphous ceramic at 600°C, then to oxide/carbide mixed phases, finally to single-phase FCC rock-salt (Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)C via carbothermal reduction

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Final ceramic phase is single-phase FCC rock-salt high-entropy carbide (Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)C. Intermediate phases during pyrolysis include (Zr,Hf)6(Nb,Ta,W)2O17, (Nb,W)C, (Nb,W,Ta,Hf)C, t-(Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)O2, m-(Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)O2. Lattice constant of HEC-W20 is 4.5155 Å. Carbon vacancies 4.20-8.51% and oxygen impurities 0.89-0.96% present in sintered ceramics.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fracture toughness (KIC): HEC-W0 3.87±0.25, HEC-W5 2.55±0.18, HEC-W10 2.38±0.16, HEC-W20 2.12±0.18 MPa·m^0.5. Vickers hardness: HEC-W0 21.28±0.33, HEC-W5 23.82±0.49, HEC-W10 24.30±0.16, HEC-W20 22.80±0.28 GPa. Elastic modulus: HEC-W0 427.53±7.92, HEC-W5 447.07±3.71, HEC-W10 451.27±5.25, HEC-W20 449.72±7.66 GPa. Flexural strength: HEC-W0 491.84±28.98, HEC-W5 654.86±15.71, HEC-W10 515.80±19.32, HEC-W20 138.92±13.20 MPa. Best overall performance: HEC-W5 (5 mol% W). Relative density 96.15-98.37%.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Single-phase FCC rock-salt (Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)C in final ceramics; intermediate phases (Zr,Hf)6(Nb,Ta,W)2O17, (Nb,W)C, t-(Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)O2, m-(Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)O2 observed during pyrolysis; amorphous at 250°C and 600°C

notes: This paper concerns a polymer-derived ceramic (PDC) route using metal alkoxide precursors (not silicon-based polysilazane/polycarbosilane) to produce high-entropy carbide (HEC) nano-powders (Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)C with tunable W content (0, 5, 10, 20 mol%). Average particle size of powders at 1600°C: 40-65 nm (midpoint 52.5 nm used for grain_size_nm). Average grain size of bulk ceramics after hot-pressing at 1900°C/50 MPa/1h: HEC-W0 0.47 μm, HEC-W5 0.95 μm, HEC-W10 1.13 μm, HEC-W20 2.31 μm. Ceramic_phase field corrected: phase is (Zr,Hf,Nb,Ta,W)C high-entropy carbide, not SiC. DFT-calculated melting points >3800°C for perfect ceramics, estimated 3300-3700°C accounting for defects. Formation energies range from -76.92 to -58.70 kJ/mol. The polymer precursor is metal-alkoxide based (not silicon-based), making this non-standard for polysilazane/polycarbosilane classification. Hardness and modulus values reported as averages across compositions for the JSON fields.

The precursor is a commercial polysilsesquioxane (MK Belsil PMS, Wacker) with formula Si1O3C1H3.3. Specific surface area of SiCaMgOC powder: 20 m2/g (BET). Zeta potential of SiCaMgOC-1100 in SBF at pH 7.5: -29.4 ± 7.9 mV. Pyrolysis temperatures studied: 700, 900, 1100, and 1300 C. thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Under nitrogen alone: ~90 wt% weight loss, ceramic yield ~10.5%. Under ammonia alone: ~82.7% weight loss from 50-600°C, ceramic yield ~17.3%. Two-step decomposition under ammonia: step 1 (50-200°C, ~18.3 wt% loss), step 2 (200-650°C, ~64.4 wt% loss). DTG shows at least 8 decomposition mechanisms under nitrogen. Gases evolved include H2, CH4, C2H2, CH3NH2 (methylamine), and monomeric fragments m/z=101. Actual pyrolysis protocol: 0.5°C/min to 200°C under ammonia (1h dwell), then 1°C/min to 1000°C under nitrogen (2h dwell at 1000°C), cooled at 5°C/min.

backbone_architecture.description: Polysilazane rings cross-linked via -C-B-C- bridges. General formula [B(C2H4SiCH3NCH3)3]n where C2H4 = CHCH3 or CH2CH2. B atom connects three silazane units via ethylene bridges.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After pyrolysis to 700°C: BN3, BCN2, SiN4 domains and Si-C-N units of mixed composition coexist. After 1000°C: amorphous SiBCN network consisting of B(C)N domains, SiCxN4-x units (x=0,1,2) and free carbon. Subsequent crystallization at 1400-2000°C gives SiC, turbostratic B-(C)-N layers encapsulating Si3N4, and free carbon. Hollow fiber ceramics have empirical formula Si3.0B1.0C5.8N2.0.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: TMA shows BmPS RT exhibits >90% dimensional change under 0.9 N compressive load upon heating to 200°C (fusible). BmPS 200 (cured under ammonia at 200°C) is almost stable under compressive load, indicating infusibility after curing.

notes: Polymer synthesized by hydroboration of dichloromethylvinylsilane (DMVS) followed by aminolysis of tris(dichlorosilylethyl)borane (TDSB) with methylamine in THF at 0°C. Polymer is sensitive to oxygen and moisture. Key distinction from [B(C2H4SiCH3NH)3]n analogues: NCH3 groups instead of NH groups, giving improved processability (spinnable) but lower ceramic yield due to lack of SiH, NH, SiCH=CH2 cross-linking sites leading to depolymerization. Ceramic yield range noted for [B(C2H4SiCH3NH)3]n analogues: 54-62 wt%. Study focuses on intermediate pyrolysis steps using TGA-DTG/GC-MS, solid-state 11B, 13C, 29Si MAS NMR, and FTIR. Hollow fiber morphology obtained due to surface cross-linking while core depolymerizes. Polymer repeat unit molecular weight calculated as 326.3 g/mol for [Si3.0B1.1C11.8N3.6H37.7]n.

notes: Paper focuses on electrochemical performance of poly(phenylvinylsilylcarbodiimide)-derived SiCN ceramics as anode material for Li-ion batteries. Elemental composition data given for pyrolyzed ceramics (wt%), not for the precursor polymer itself. Polymer elemental composition not explicitly reported. Heating rate of 1.67 C/min (100 C/h) used for lower temperature experiments; 5 C/min used for higher temperature experiments (1700, 2000 C). notes: This is a review paper focused on electrochemical performance of polymer-derived SiOC and SiCN ceramics as Li-ion battery anodes. Specific preceramic polymer names/designations are not given. Key findings: free carbon phase is the primary reversible Li storage site in both SiOC and SiCN; SiOC matrix contributes significantly to irreversible Li storage due to ionic Si-O bonds; SiCN matrix contributes less due to more covalent Si-N bonds. Optimal free carbon to ceramic matrix ratio ~1:1 by weight. Li-ion diffusion coefficient ~10^-9 to 10^-11 cm2/s. Reversible capacity threshold for SiCN reached at ~50% free carbon phase. Extrapolated capacity of pure SiCxO2(1-x) phase ~1300 mAh/g; pure free carbon phase ~400 mAh/g. Pyrolysis temperature range 1000-1100 C for data shown in figures, up to 1300 C for SiCN amorphous regime.
source: Graczyk-Zajac_2015_New Insights into Understanding Irreversible and Reversible

notes: Paper focuses on the Active Filler-Controlled Polymer Pyrolysis (AFCOP) process using poly(silsesquioxane) (PSS, H 62 C, Wacker Chemie) as the primary polymer matrix with CrSi2 as the primary reactive filler (particle sizes 2-40 um). The paper also surveys multiple other preceramic polymers (polycarbosilanes, polysilazanes, polyborosilazanes, polysiloxanes) and their ceramic yields as tabulated in Panel A. Ceramic yield of 85% for poly(methylsiloxane) and 78% for poly(phenylsilsesquioxane) are listed in the table. Porosity range noted as 5-20 vol% with globular nanopores of 1-50 nm; midpoint 12.5% used for porosity_pct. Pyrolysis temperature range 1200-1500°C; midpoint 1350°C used. Heating rate range 1-2°C/min for second ramp; midpoint 1.5°C/min used. Hold time range 60-360 min; midpoint 210 min used. PSS is stable in air and has excellent electrical and hydrophobic properties. Poly(siloxanes) are restricted to application temperatures <1200°C; oxygen-poor Si-B-C-N matrices from poly(borosilazanes) used at higher temperatures.

notes: Paper describes a double-layer environmental barrier coating system on steel: PHPS bond coat (perhydropolysilazane, forming SiNO) and HTT1800-based composite top coat filled with ZrO2 (25 vol%), borosilicate glass 8470 and barium silicate glass G018-311. Filler content varied from 30 to 80 vol%. HTT1800 used with 3 wt% dicumylperoxide (DCP) as crosslinking agent. Coatings applied by dip-coating and pyrolyzed in air at up to 800C (3 K/min, 1 h hold). Total coating thickness up to 100 micrometers achieved. Cyclic oxidation tests at 700C (3 cycles, 10 K/min, 30 min hold) showed no damage or oxidation of mild steel substrate. TGA ceramic yield of 82 wt% measured at 1000C in air for pure HTT1800.

backbone_architecture.description: Polyvinylsilazane backbone modified by boron incorporation via dehydrocoupling (B-N) and hydroboration (B-C), creating a crosslinked network. Photocurable acrylate or methacrylate units grafted onto N-H sites via isocyanate coupling. High viscosity at Si/B=17 indicates high crosslinking rate.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiBCN (amorphous); described as composed of SiC, Si3N4, BN and free carbon nanodomains
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiBCN amorphous microstructure with nanodomains of SiC, Si3N4, BN and free carbon. Boron introduction stabilizes against crystallization at high temperature. SiCN also produced from boron-free PVZ photoresists.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Young's modulus range: 55-65 GPa for SiCN micropatterns (aPVZ10, pyrolyzed at 1000°C); ~39 GPa for SiBCN micropatterns (aPBVZ30-10). Brittle behavior confirmed by load-displacement curves. RMS surface roughness: ~0.8 nm (aPVZ10) and ~2.9 nm (aPBVZ30-10). No micro- or nano-cracks detected by AFM.

notes: Study reports first synthesis of UV-curable polyborovinylsilazane photoresists for direct photolithography of SiBCN ceramic MEMS. Two Si/B ratios studied: 17 (complete hydroboration) and 30 (partial hydroboration). Photoresists designated e.g. aPBVZ30-10 (acrylate-modified PBVZ, Si/B=30, 10 wt% IEA) and mPBVZ30-10 (methacrylate-modified). Optimal UV exposure: 1800 mJ/cm2 (90 s at 20 mJ/cm2, 365 nm). Micropattern dimensions 20-200 µm. Micropattern thickness after pyrolysis: ~250-300 nm (aPVZ10) and ~110 nm (aPBVZ30-10). Strong radial shrinkage observed during pyrolysis. Boron presence reduces photosensitivity due to reduced N-H availability for acrylate/methacrylate grafting. Ceramic yield midpoint reported as 75% for aPBVZ17-10 (highest yield sample).

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed to 1200 °C at 10 °C/min. At Ar flow of 5 ml/min, total mass loss ~26% at 1200 °C (ceramic yield ~74%); at 10 ml/min Ar flow, mass loss ~39% (ceramic yield ~61%). Three regions: 30-200 °C (~3% loss, evaporation of low MW components); 200-780 °C (21-37% loss, cleavage of Si-CH3, loss of methane and hydrocarbons); >780 °C (slight additional loss, residual hydrogen loss). DSC shows weakly exothermic peaks at 350 °C and 600 °C. Transformation to amorphous SiC begins ~680 °C by TGA, ~600 °C per FTIR. Ceramic yield midpoint reported as 74% based on 5 ml/min Ar condition; range 61-74% depending on Ar flow rate.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: reported as range 1500-2500 g/mol; midpoint 2000 used

backbone_architecture.description: PCS with Si-CH2-Si backbone inferred from FTIR bands; specific architecture not described

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCS converts to amorphous SiC upon pyrolysis at 700 °C for 1 h in argon. FTIR confirms near-complete transformation at 800 °C. Final coatings contain Si, C, Al, and O as identified by EDS elemental mapping. Dense, crack-free coatings ~40 µm thick achieved with C and Al fillers.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Coatings described as dense and well-adhered to stainless steel substrate; adhesion strength noted to be reported elsewhere. No gaps or cracks at metal-coating interface observed.

notes: Study focuses on using PCS as a preceramic precursor for SiC coatings on stainless steel with carbon (passive, <50 nm) and aluminum (active, 0.8-10 µm) fillers to reduce shrinkage cracking and tune hydrophobicity. Ceramic yield of 74% based on 5 ml/min Ar flow TGA to 1200 °C; pyrolysis for coating fabrication performed at 700 °C/1 h/Ar. Water contact angles ranged from 42° (PCS alone) to 145° (PCS/C/Al with 0.8 µm Al). Molecular weight given as range 1500-2500 g/mol; midpoint 2000 used. Ceramic yield range: 61-74% depending on Ar flow rate.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous silicon carbonitride up to 1400C with high carbon content; at 1400C under N2: Si3N4 54.3wt%, SiC 20.2wt%, SiO2 8.5wt%, C 17.0wt%; at 1400C under Ar: Si3N4 55.9wt%, SiC 21.1wt%, SiO2 5.7wt%, C 17.3wt%; selective crystallization of SiC or Si3N4 possible depending on processing conditions

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous up to 1400C; at 1400C Si3N4 and SiC crystalline phases identified

notes: Paper is Part I of a multi-part study by Bahloul et al. (1993) on pyrolysis of (ViSiHNH)(MeSiHNH) copolysilazane. Precursor synthesized by ammonolysis of equimolar mixture of dichlorosilanes, then thermally cross-linked at 120C/15h. Study temperature range 20-1450C under various atmospheres. Gaseous evolution tracked by TGA/MS: NH3, H2, CH4, C2H4, C2H2, C3H6 identified under inert atmosphere; CO2, CO, N2, H2O, N2O additionally under oxidative conditions. Heating rate significantly affects ceramic yield. Loss of silicon species during pyrolysis is negligible due to high cross-linking degree. Second table appears to show a different sample set (possibly oxidative atmosphere data) with empirical formulas at 200, 400, 500, 600, 800, 1400C. Authors: Bahloul, Pereira, Goursat (Limoges) and Choong Kwet Yive, Corriu (Montpellier).
