elemental_composition.other_elements: RE metal elements (Yb, Ho, Er, Lu, Tb, Tm, Gd) incorporated via mixed RE metal acetate hydrates at 1:1 weight ratio with PSO

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pure PSO ceramic yield ~75%. RE-containing precursor mixtures (1:1 RE acetates:PSO by weight) yield 60.1-64.5% after pyrolysis at 1100C. Theoretical yield estimated 57-60% based on individual component yields. RE acetate hydrates lose crystallization water at 150-200C; decompose to amorphous RE2O2CO3 at 340-640C; (5RE0.2)2SixO2x+3 phase forms in situ above 800C. Significant mass loss at 1500C in pure SiOC due to carbothermal SiO2/C reactions; RE-containing ceramics show ~11% less mass loss at 1500C due to stabilization by (5RE0.2)2SixO2x+3 phase.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (PSO crosslinks during pyrolysis; RE acetate hydrates lose crystallization water and form anhydrous acetates at 150-200C)

backbone_architecture.description: Polysiloxane (Si-O backbone) mixed with RE metal acetate hydrates at 1:1 weight ratio to form composite precursor

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After pyrolysis at 1100C: amorphous SiOC matrix with in situ formed (5RE0.2)2SiO5 (X1-type) nanoparticles. At higher temperatures (5RE0.2)2SiO5 transforms from X1 to X2 type, and at 1500C+ transforms to (5RE0.2)2Si2O7. SiOC matrix composed of amorphous SiOyCz, SiO2, beta-SiC and free carbon. Phase compositions of RE silicate and SiOC phases range from ~39-62 wt% and ~38-61 wt% respectively depending on sample and temperature. After SPS densification at 1500-1600C, phase converts to (5RE0.2)2Si2O7.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Density of (5RE0.2)2SixO2x+3/SiOC nanocomposites ~3.2 g/cm3, approximately 40% higher than pure SiOC. Open porosity of SPS-sintered monoliths: 4.23-5.94% (see Table 3 data). SPS conditions: 50 MPa, 20 min dwell, 1500 or 1600C in vacuum.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: After pyrolysis at 800-1100C: X1-type (5RE0.2)2SiO5 crystalline phase within amorphous SiOC matrix. At higher temperatures: X2-type (5RE0.2)2SiO5, then (5RE0.2)2Si2O7. Pure SiOC remains amorphous even after annealing at 1200C. Free carbon present as disordered carbon (D-band ~1350 cm-1, G-band ~1580 cm-1 in Raman) up to 1400C; largely consumed by 1500C via carbothermal reactions.

notes: This paper reports the PDC-derived preparation of (5RE0.2)2SixO2x+3/SiOC nanocomposites (RE = Yb, Ho, Er, Lu, Tb/Tm/Gd; x=1 or 2) for environmental barrier coating applications. Three precursor systems were studied: YbHoErLuTb-PSO, YbHoErLuTm-PSO, and YbHoErLuGd-PSO. Grain sizes at 1100C: 8.3-11.4 nm; at 1500C: 43.8-56.7 nm (powder); SPS samples: 49.9-60.7 nm. Ceramic yield range for RE-PSO precursors: 60.1-64.5% (midpoint ~62.6%). Porosity range for SPS monoliths: 4.23-5.94% (midpoint ~5.0%). Grain size range for powders at 1100C: 8.3-11.4 nm (midpoint ~10.3 nm used in grain_size_nm and crystallite_size_nm fields). PDC method enables atomic-level RE homogeneity and fabrication at 800-1100C. Best water-vapor corrosion resistance shown by Tb-containing (Yb0.2Ho0.2Er0.2Lu0.2Tb0.2)2Si2O7/SiOC nanocomposite with specific weight change rates of ~0.0036 mg/(cm2·h) at 1400C and ~0.0334 mg/(cm2·h) at 1500C.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PSE ([SiH2CH2]n) shows ceramic yield of 86-90% by TGA (theoretical SiC yield is 91%). Over 90% of gaseous product is dihydrogen with traces of methane, C2 hydrocarbons and methylsilanes. Crosslinking occurs between ~300-400C via 1,1-H2 elimination from Si-H bonds leading to silylene intermediates, then Si-H insertion and Kumada rearrangement. Homolytic Si-C bond breakage begins at 450-600C. Final product is nanocrystalline beta-SiC at 1000C. Diethoxy-PSM pyrolyzed to 1000C yields silicon oxycarbide (SiOxCy).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - via 1,1-H2 elimination from SiH2 groups leading to silylene intermediates, interchain Si-H insertion, and Kumada rearrangement; also platinum-catalyzed crosslinking via Si-H bond activation

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Solution NMR (end-group analysis, degree of polymerization ~250) gave Mn ~10000; GPC (polystyrene standards) gave Mn ~20000 for linear PSE. HBPSE: Mw/Mn = 1000/600 by GPC coupled with vapor-pressure osmometry, degree of polymerization ~13. TEDSCB-derived PSE: Mw = 7000.

backbone_architecture.description: Linear [SiH2CH2]n (PSE) prepared by ROP of TCDSCB followed by LiAlH4 reduction, with regular alternating -SiH2CH2- structure and small concentration of (H)SiC3 branch sites (~1 per chain). Hyperbranched HBPSE prepared by Grignard coupling of ClCH2SiCl3 followed by LiAlH4 reduction, with [H3SiCH2]w[H2SiCH2]x[HSiCH2]y[SiCH2]z structure where w/x/y/z = 11:20:8:2. Various symmetrically disubstituted and asymmetrically monosubstituted linear PSMs also prepared.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PSE pyrolysis to 1000C yields nanocrystalline beta-SiC retaining Si/C 1:1 ratio. Diethoxy-PSM pyrolysis to 1000C yields amorphous silicon oxycarbide (SiOxCy) with carbon in tetrahedral Si4C sites, described as hybrid of SiO2 glass and SiC. Yajima polycarbosilane-derived ceramics contain free carbon.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: [SiF2CH2]n indexed by orthorhombic unit cell with c-axis dimension 3.30 Angstrom (all-trans planar zig-zag conformation); symmetrically disubstituted n-alkyl PSMs [SiR2CH2]n (R=ethyl to n-hexyl) are crystalline at low temperatures; dialkoxy PSMs [Si(OR)2CH2]n are highly crystalline

notes: Paper reviews poly(silylenemethylene) (PSM) chemistry from Interrante group at RPI. PSMs are described as inorganic/organic hybrid polymers bridging polyolefins and polysiloxanes. Glass transition temperatures for various PSMs are tabulated and compared with analogous polyolefins and polysiloxanes (see table). Symmetrically disubstituted n-alkyl PSMs show unusual first-order pre-melting transitions (Tm range 55-96C) attributed to mesomorphic columnar hexagonal phase, similar to dialkyl polysiloxanes. [SiF2CH2]n is described as Si-analogue of PVDF (poly(vinylidene fluoride)), showing DSC endotherm at 140-170C possibly due to solid-solid transition, decomposes at ~250C. HBPSE/HPCS used commercially as SiC matrix precursor for SiC/SiC composites. Ceramic yield range 86-90% noted; midpoint 88 used in ceramic_yield_pct field.

notes: This paper is a structural characterization study of polymethylsilsesquioxane (PMSQ) and DT-type methyl silicone resin (MeDT), not a preceramic polymer pyrolysis study. No pyrolysis, ceramic yield, or PDK/SiCN/SiOC ceramic data are reported. Molecular weights from GPC tables: PMSQ-1 Mw=6370, Mn=1140; PMSQ-NA Mw=790, Mn=500; MeDT-1 Mw=4220, Mn=1040; triple-detector GPC: PMSQ-2 Mn=3640, Mw=17400; MeDT-2 Mn=3700, Mw=24600. Mark-Houwink exponent ~0.3 for methyl resins, indicating compact molecular shape. One T3(6)T2(2) isomer isolated and identified as a cage structure by X-ray crystallography. Si-O bond lengths 1.601-1.630 Angstrom; Si-C bond lengths 1.819-1.848 Angstrom from crystal structure. Siloxane bond rearrangement identified as important mechanism in molecule build-up. Materials synthesized by hydrolytic polycondensation of methyltrichlorosilane (and dimethyldichlorosilane for MeDT) with excess water in MIBK solvent.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: VH-SQ (S1) pyrolyzed at 800 C: amorphous SiOC with empirical formula SiO0.9C0.5 + 0.05Si free. At 1400 C: SiO0.9C0.6. At 1600 C: SiO1.0C0.7. At 1800 C: SiC. notes: Two precursor systems studied: VH-SQ (R=vinyl, target S1 composition near SiC-SiO2 tie line) and St-H-SQ (R=styryl, target S2 carbon-rich composition). Synthesis via sol-gel route using vinyl-trimethoxysilane, triethoxysilane, and tetramethyldisiloxane. Goal is PDC route for binary beta-SiC/amorphous SiO2 nanocomposites. Pyrolysis at 800 C under N2 (2h heat-up, 1h hold). Heat treatment at 1400-1800 C under Ar at 10 C/min with 1h hold. TG/MS heating rate 20 C/min under He. Elemental compositions in wt% not atomic%. thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA conducted in helium at 20 °C/min. Pure PSZ ceramic yield ~39.55 wt%; metal-modified 70T1Z1H1T1-30PSZ yield ~68.76 wt%. Mass loss after 250 °C curing was 9.26 wt% (vs 52.04 wt% for unmodified PSZ). Three-stage decomposition: RT-250 °C (9.26 wt% loss, oligomer evaporation/hydrosilylation); 250-800 °C (~21.83 wt% loss, main decomposition with H2 release); above 800 °C (further conversion). microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After SPS at 2200 °C: (Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta)CN content 64.95-80.05 wt% depending on composition. Lattice parameters of (Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta)CN: 4.542-4.606 Å. notes: Paper focuses on (Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta)CN/SiCN ceramic nanocomposites derived from novel multi-metal polysilazane single-source precursors (SSPs). Three SSP compositions synthesized: 70(Ti0.25Zr0.25Hf0.25Ta0.25)-30PSZ, 70(Ti0.1Zr0.3Hf0.5Ta0.1)-30PSZ, 83(Ti0.1Zr0.3Hf0.5Ta0.1)-17PSZ. Weight ratios metal amides/PSZ = 70/30 and 83/17. Reactions at 80 °C. SPS densification at 2200 °C, 75 MPa, 10 min, argon, 450 °C/min heating rate. Density of SPS monoliths: 7.276-7.489 g/cm3; open porosity: 0.19-1.18%. Linear ablation rate at ~2200 °C for 83ST1Z3H5T1CN-SPS: 0.033 μm/s (2 orders of magnitude lower than other multicomponent UHTCs). Mechanical property ranges used for midpoint calculation: hardness 35.75-37.36 GPa (mid 36.39), modulus 357.92-417.97 GPa (mid 384.3), flexural strength 532.24-603.41 MPa (mid 559.51). TGA heating rate of 20 °C/min stated for TGA/GC-MS analysis; pyrolysis hold time of 2 h at 1100 °C stated in text.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis of polysiloxane in an inert atmosphere yields SiOxCy with a weight loss of about 13%, implying a ceramic yield of approximately 87%.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis of polysiloxane yields SiOxCy (silicon oxycarbide). Porous SiOC ceramics with closed-cell or open-cell structure depending on process. No crystallographic phase identification reported.

notes: Study focuses on processing of porous SiOC ceramics from blends of polysiloxane (YR3370) and poly(methyl methacrylate-co-ethylene glycol dimethacrylate) microbeads (~20 µm and ~50 µm). Two processes described: (1) pyrolysis of extruded blends producing closed-cell SiOC, and (2) CO2 foaming followed by pyrolysis producing open-cell SiOC. Porosity ranged from ~27% to ~88%; cell density ranged from 2.6×10^7 to 1.0×10^9 cells/cm^3. Pyrolysis temperature 1200°C, 1 h, argon, 2°C/min. Ceramic yield ~87% (weight loss ~13%) stated for polysiloxane. No detailed bonding, molecular weight, or elemental composition data provided for the preceramic polymer.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-phenyl bonds present from phenyltriethoxysilane precursor; SiO4, SiO3C, SiO2C2 tetrahedral units identified by 29Si MAS-NMR; Si-O bonds exchanged with Si-H and/or Si-C bonds during redistribution reaction

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramic product consists of SiOxCy structural units (SiO4, SiO3C, SiO2C2 tetrahedra) and free carbon phase. SiO4 tetrahedra dominate (76-78%). notes: Paper focuses on SiOC/graphite composites derived from phenyltriethoxysilane (PhTES) via sol-gel + pyrolysis for lithium-ion capacitor (LIC) anodes. Preceramic precursor is PhTES (not a polysilazane). Composites designated SiOCPhTES, SiOCPhTES/C2g, /C4g, /C10g. Pyrolysis at 1000°C under Ar, heating rate 100°C/h (1.67°C/min), dwell 1 h, Ar flow 40 mL/min. Raman spectroscopy confirmed graphite D and G bands; ID1/IG ratio decreased with increasing graphite content (from 2.69 for pure SiOC to 1.24 for C10g). XPS showed Si2p binding energies 103.2-103.4 eV consistent with SiO2C2 and SiO3C units. Electrochemical: SiOCPhTES reversible capacity 479 mAh/g (1st cycle), SiOC/graphite composites show enhanced rate capability at 1.86 A/g. No molecular weight data reported. Polymer described as preceramic polymer/precursor, not characterized in polymer form by GPC or MALDI.
source: Knozowski_2020_Silicon Oxycarbide-Graphite Electrodes for High-Power Energy

Carbothermal reduction of SnO2 to metallic Sn occurs above 700°C, consuming free carbon and Si-C bonds in the ceramic phase. CO2 release during carbothermal reduction creates porosity in the ceramic region.

notes: This paper focuses on SiOC/graphite/Sn ternary nanocomposites as Li-ion battery anodes. The preceramic polymer is PMHS/DVB (1:1 w/w). Heating rates noted in °C/h in text: 100°C/h to 250°C and 150°C/h to 1000°C; converted to per-minute values: ~1.67 and 2.5°C/min respectively; midpoint 2.5°C/min used for primary pyrolysis step.

notes: PBSZ was used as a sintering additive (2.64 mass%) for ZrB2 ceramics, not as a standalone preceramic polymer system. It was synthesized according to Riedel et al. (Nature, 1996). notes: This paper does not describe a conventional preceramic polymer (e.g. polysilazane, polycarbosilane). The precursor is a poly(furfuryl alcohol)-based liquid precursor incorporating five transition metal halides (TiCl4, ZrCl4, HfCl4, NbCl5, TaCl5) in equimolar ratio dissolved in ethanol. The final ceramic product is a high-entropy carbide nanopowder with average particle size 132 ± 5 nm, specific surface area 24.5 m2/g, and oxygen content 0.22 wt%. Pyrolysis in vacuum to 1400 C yields binary carbide mixtures; heat treatment at 1800-2000 C in flowing argon yields single-phase HEC. Many standard preceramic polymer descriptor fields are not applicable to this system.

notes: Paper investigates polycarbosilane/siloxane hybrid polymers from CBS (cyclic) and L-EPCS (linear) as precursors to silicon oxycarbide (SiOxCy) ceramics via sol-gel processing and pyrolysis under N2. Key finding: Si-CH2-Si bridging groups increase carbidic carbon and decrease free carbon content compared to pendent Si-CH3 groups (MTES). CBS gel undergoes Si-OH-induced ring-opening during drying, forming dangling CH3 groups and 'SiCH2Si(O)CH3' average formula. L-EPCS gel has nearly pure SiC2O2 microenvironment initially, converting to statistical distribution of SiC4-xOx environments between 600-1000°C via Si-O/Si-C redistribution reactions. 29Si SSNMR performed on Chemagnetics CMX-360 (L-EPCS) and MSL300 Bruker (CBS). Gel yield for L-EPCS ~90%. Comparative NMR data for all systems (MTES, B-EPCS, CBS, L-EPCS) provided in Table 1. Sol-gel twice processed L-EPCS also characterized (ceramic free carbon 59.7%).

notes: Two precursor systems studied: (1) SiOC precursor from MTES/MDES (molar ratio 3:1) hydrolyzed with acidic water (pH 1, HCl), H2O/OEt=1, gelled at 60 deg C for 3 h; (2) SiZrOC precursor from MTES/MDES with Zr(OnPr)4 added at Zr:Si=0.2 molar ratio, gelled at 80 deg C for 1 day. Raman spectroscopy shows graphitization of free carbon increases with temperature in both ceramics but is always lower in SiZrOC. ZrO2 presence suppresses carbothermal reduction and beta-SiC crystallization. Beta-SiC crystallite sizes: 3.1 nm (1400 deg C), 3.7 nm (1500 deg C), 4.3 nm (1600 deg C) for SiOC. t-ZrO2 crystallite sizes in SiZrOC: 3.4 nm (1000 deg C) to 29.4 nm (1600 deg C). thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis under argon yields silicon oxycarbide glasses with free-carbon phase; pyrolysis under ammonia up to ~1000°C yields silicon oxynitride glasses with low carbon content. Linear polysiloxanes give zero or poor ceramic yields due to depolymerization. Highly cross-linked polysiloxanes give much higher ceramic yields. Carbothermal reduction occurs above ~1450°C. Redistribution reactions (Si-C/Si-O exchange) occur above ~500°C; Si-H/Si-O exchange above ~300°C. Ceramic yields for individual precursors range from 47% (T/D under argon) to 98% (T-H under ammonia) as reported in Tables 2 and 3.

notes: This is a review paper covering multiple polysiloxane precursors pyrolyzed to silicon oxycarbide (under argon) or silicon oxynitride (under ammonia) glasses. Precursors include: T-H (HSiCl3), T (MeSiCl3), T-F- (MeSi(OEt)3 with NH4F catalyst), T-Vi (ViSiCl3), T-Ph (PhSiCl3), O1.5SiC2H4SiO1.5 (Cl3SiC2H4SiCl3), D/Q (Me2SiCl2 + SiCl4), T/D (MeSiCl3 + Me2SiCl2), T/D-H (MeSiCl3 + MeHSiCl2), Me2Si2O2 (MeCl2Si-SiMeCl2), CPSE and COVS (ViHSiCl2). Ceramic yields under argon range from 47% to 89%; under ammonia from 54% to 98%. Silicon loss during pyrolysis (1-Si/Si%) ranges from 2% to 50%. The paper is from UMR CNRS 5637, Université de Montpellier 2, received April 8, 1998. Key pyrolysis reactions discussed: depolymerization, silanol condensation, Si-C/Si-O and Si-H/Si-O redistribution, mineralization (500-1000°C), carbothermal reduction (>1450°C), nitridation by ammonia, and carbon removal under ammonia atmosphere.

After pyrolysis at 1100°C/argon, the ceramic was surface-impregnated with Fe(acac)3 at 0.2, 1, and 5 wt% Fe loading and heat-treated at 1300°C. Raman spectroscopy shows increasing graphitization with Fe content: AD/AG decreases from 1.9±0.1 (0Fe) to 1.3±0.2 (5Fe); La increases from 10.1±0.6 to 15.6±1.8 nm; LD from 8.7±0.3 to 10.8±0.7 nm; Leq from 20.2±1.9 to 31.6±4.4 nm. XPS confirms C=C (284.2 eV), pi-pi* (290.2 eV), and carbidic Si-C/M-C (283.2 eV) bonds. Electrocatalytic ORR onset potential improved from 0.81 V to 0.85 V vs RHE with Fe incorporation in 0.1 M KOH. Fe addition promotes 4-electron ORR pathway. ADF-STEM/EDX confirmed Fe incorporation into HEC lattice. SLS (solution-liquid-solid) growth mechanism proposed for Fe distribution via Fe-Si-C liquid phase at 1300°C.

Final relative density after 7 PIP cycles was 0.90 with ~10 vol% residual porosity. microstructural.phase_composition_notes: HTT1800 converts to SiCNO ceramic upon pyrolysis. Composite coatings also contain YSZ, barium silicate glass phases, and AYZ (Al2O3-Y2O3-ZrO2) passive filler phases including tetragonal ZrO2 and YAG (Y3Al5O12).

notes: HTT1800 (Merck KGaA) is used as the matrix-forming preceramic polymer for composite top-coat EBC coatings on AISI 441 stainless steel. A perhydropolysilazane (PHPS, Merck KGaA) is used separately as the bond-coat material applied by dip coating and cured at 450°C in air. Four composite coating systems (C1-GF, C2-GM, C3-PP, C4-PP) were developed using HTT1800 filled with YSZ, commercial barium silicate glasses (G8470, G018-311, G018-385), and AYZ passive fillers in glass microsphere or precursor powder form. Optimized coatings were crack-free up to 93 μm thick after treatment at 750°C. Oxidation tests at 850°C for 24 h in synthetic air showed coatings remained undamaged. The pyrolysis temperature range investigated was 700-800°C; midpoint 750°C used as primary reported value.

notes: This paper focuses on UV Raman spectroscopy (256.7 nm, 4.8 eV) characterization of polymer-derived SiOC ceramics with two carbon contents (~1 vol.% and 10 vol.% segregated carbon). Two precursors used: (1) poly(methyl)silsesquioxane PMS MK (Wacker AG) cross-linked at 250°C, pyrolyzed at 1100°C/2h/Ar, yielding 10 vol.% free carbon; (2) polysiloxane microspheres Tospearl 2000B pyrolyzed in H2 yielding <1 vol.% free carbon. Lateral size La of turbostratic carbon estimated at ~2 nm (from visible Raman at 514 nm), remaining approximately constant between 1400-1600°C. G band FWHM decreases only slightly from 51 cm-1 (1400°C) to 47 cm-1 (1600°C). Results argue against single-layer graphene network model and support turbostratic carbon description. No polymer characterization data (MW, yield, TGA) reported; paper is focused on ceramic characterization post-pyrolysis.

notes: Study focuses on porous PDC foams for thermal insulation. Two polymer systems studied: polysilazane Durazane 1800 (CAS 503590-70-3, viscosity <100 cps at 20°C) yielding SiCN(O) ceramics, and polysiloxane SPR-036 (viscosity 50-500 cps) yielding SiOC ceramics. Two PU foam templates used: MTP-55 (partially closed cells, density 0.055 g/cm3) and PPI-60 (open cells, density 0.025 g/cm3). Bulk densities of final ceramic foams range from 0.03 to 0.56 g/cm3; total porosity 75-98 vol%. Skeletal densities ~2.0-2.3 g/cm3. Thermal conductivity as low as 0.03 W/m/K at RT. Gibson-Ashby model estimates strut thermal conductivity: 2.1 W/m/K for SiCN(O) and 1.8 W/m/K for SiOC. CTE: ~1.72e-6/K for SiCN(O), ~1.93e-6/K for SiOC (30-850°C). Pt catalyst loading: 100 µL of 0.1% Pt solution per 1 g polymer precursor. Oxygen in SiCN(O) attributed to PU template decomposition and processing atmosphere contamination.

polymer_name: Ceraset Polyureasilazane (KiON Corp.), VL20 (KiON Corp.), Ultra II polyvinylsilazane (KiON Corp.), ABSE (ammonolysed bis(dichlorosilyl)ethane), polyvinylsilazane (Hoechst), SiCBN precursor (borazine modified allylhydridopolycarbosilane)

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal, UV, X-ray, E-beam, chemical (thermal initiator dicumyl peroxide, photo initiator Irgacure 369), air exposure

backbone_architecture.description: Preceramic polymers with vinyl side chains acting as negative-type resists; crosslinking via radiation-induced vinyl activation or hydrogen elimination and recombination; liquid precursors used for casting and moulding processes

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous bulk ceramics containing elements Si, C, N and sometimes B, O. SiCN PDC nanostructure can be adjusted by tailoring precursor polymer and processing. Nanocarbon formation during pyrolysis reported. SiCBN also produced.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Young's Modulus of 150 GPa for SiCN electrostatic actuator obtained from voltage-deflection data, consistent with indentation techniques. notes: This is a review paper covering multiple preceramic polymer systems used in MEMS/NEMS fabrication, not a single-polymer study. Polymers discussed include: (1) Ceraset Polyureasilazane (KiON Corp.) used as negative resist and for microcasting; (2) VL20 (KiON Corp.) functionalized for two-photon stereolithography (NSL), achieving woodpile structures with 9 µm edge length; (3) Ultra II polyvinylsilazane (KiON Corp.) used for embossed microfluidic channels; (4) ABSE precursor crosslinked by X-ray via hydrogen elimination; (5) polyvinylsilazane from Hoechst with composition SiN1.5C2.0H5.0 used for photonic crystals (pyrolysis to 1100°C, lattice constant 85 µm); (6) SiCBN precursor (borazine modified allylhydridopolycarbosilane) with 92 wt% ceramic yield at 1200°C. Applications include: electrostatic actuators, micro-grippers, photonic crystals, microfluidic components, micro igniters/glow plugs (>1000 glow cycles at 40 mA, temperatures up to 1450°C in air). Pyrolysis temperature range spans 1100-1600°C depending on application. Two-photon stereolithography achieved ~120 nm feature resolution. Silica filler (10 nm, up to 40 wt%) used to reduce pyrolysis shrinkage. Structures <50 µm diameter and 20 µm thickness can be pyrolysed on substrate without cracking.

notes: Study focuses on solution-based freeze casting of preceramic polymers (MK and H44 polysiloxanes) with cyclohexane as solvent and APTES as cross-linking agent. Filler particles include preceramic (MK- or H44-based, cross-linked with 1 or 50 mol% APTES, ball-milled to d50=2.63-3.34 µm) and ceramic (alumina platelets d50=7.5 µm, silica spheres 1.0 µm) types. Overall solid loading 40 wt% for monoliths; filler solid loading 30 wt% during filler synthesis. Pyrolysis temperatures of 600 °C and 1000 °C investigated. BET surface areas: Ref/600 = 451 m2/g, H1/600 = 607 m2/g, H50/600 = 546 m2/g; Ref/1000 ~0.58 m2/g. Open porosity 60-65%, pore size 13-21 µm monomodal. Porosity midpoint used: 62.5%. Strength range noted: 6.5 MPa (Ref/600) to 35 MPa (Ref/1000); 25M1/1000 approximately 66 MPa based on factor 1.9. Filler particle mean size d50 = 2.63-3.34 µm (midpoint ~2.99 µm). Pyrolysis temperatures of 600°C and 1000°C both used across samples.

notes: Study involves nine preceramic polymers: three alkoxysilanes (MTES, PTES, VTMS) each at B/Si ratios of 0, 0.1, and 0.5. Sol-gel synthesis without solvent; boric acid (H3BO3) used as boron source. Precursors dried at 70 C for at least 10 days. Powders sieved to <=106 micron before use. Pyrolysis yields 18 ceramic materials (SiOC and SiBOC). Crystallite size (t) calculated by Scherrer formula with K=1; values range from 0.65 to 18.51 nm depending on ceramic type and annealing time (see table). XPS elemental composition of ceramics reported in atomic % for C, O, Si, and B. PTES-derived ceramics show highest C content (up to ~76 at%) and highest SiC crystallization. Boron content in ceramics is 0.72-1.79 at% B. Ceramic yield measured at 800 C under N2 in TGA. Reaction and gelation times increase with boron content. Annealing at 1 h and 3 h studied for all ceramics.

notes: Study focuses on 29Si spin-lattice relaxation NMR to determine mass fractal dimensions. GM35 (polysilsesquicarbodiimide-derived): mass fractal dimension Df ~3, indicating efficient 3D packing of SiN4 tetrahedra. PMVS (polymethylvinylsilazane-derived): mass fractal dimension Df ~2.5, indicating inefficient packing due to mixed SiNxC4-x bonding environments. 29Si MAS NMR peaks: GM35 at ~-48 ppm (SiN4); PMVS at -49 ppm (SiN4), -34 ppm (SiCN3), and ~-18 ppm shoulder (SiC4). N/Si ratio in GM35 ~2.2, higher than stoichiometric Si3N4 (N/Si=1.33). Both samples provided by external collaborators (Mera and Tavakoli); synthesis details in referenced prior publications.

polymer_name: Silres H62C (LH62C as received; CH62C after crosslinking)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-vinyl bonds present; Si-phenyl groups implied by 'methyl-phenyl-vinyl-hydrogen polysiloxane' designation; hydrosilylation crosslinking via Si-vinyl and Si-H bonds at 250-260 degrees C

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups

A second pyrolysis at 1400 degrees C under argon for 4 h at 3 degrees C/min was also performed to induce phase separation and crystallization, yielding nanocrystalline beta-SiC (26 wt%, crystallite size 1.5 nm) and turbostratic carbon (74 wt%, crystallite size 0.7 nm).

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1100 degrees C: mainly amorphous SiOC with minor turbostratic carbon and worm-like carbon precipitates; 29Si NMR shows SiO4, SiC4, SiO3C, SiO2C2 units. At 1400 degrees C: phase separation yields 26 wt% beta-SiC and 74 wt% turbostratic carbon; no crystalline SiO2 observed. notes: Polymer is commercially available Silres H62C (Wacker Chemie GmbH), a methyl-phenyl-vinyl-hydrogen polysiloxane. Two forms used: LH62C (as-received liquid) and CH62C (pre-crosslinked at 250 degrees C/2 h in argon, then ball-milled to <=60 micron powder). Phase compositions (vol%): XF0: 50.91% Si3N4, 42.33% SiO2, 6.76% Si, 0% rGO; XF1: 60.38% Si3N4, 27.85% SiO2, 10.20% Si, 1.56% rGO; XF2: 57.84% Si3N4, 20.58% SiO2, 19.13% Si, 2.45% rGO; XF5: 37.84% Si3N4, 44.22% SiO2, 14.48% Si, 3.46% rGO; XF10: 49.81% Si3N4, 37.57% SiO2, 5.14% Si, 7.47% rGO. Increasing rGO suppresses crystallization of Si3N4. rGO particles consist of 8-10 graphene layers with interlayer distance 0.37 nm; aspect ratios 20-40; mesopores present.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fracture toughness of Si3N4 improved by ~235% (2.8 to 6.6 MPa·m^1/2) at 1.5 vol% graphene loading referenced from literature; not measured directly in this study

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: X-ray amorphous at 1100°C; alpha-Si3N4 identified at 1400°C and above in Ar atmosphere

notes: Polymer synthesized by reacting SiCl4 (5g) with HMDS (5.9g) in toluene (20ml) with pyridine (5ml) as catalyst at 0°C for 2h then room temperature overnight; solvent removed in vacuum (10^-2 mbar, 40°C). GO/polysilazane composites prepared by adding SiCl4 to HMDS solutions containing dispersed GO. Heating rate for pyrolysis was 100 K/h (1.67°C/min). Porosity of hot-pressed monolithic samples: XF0 32.9%, XF1 42.4%, XF2 25.9%, XF5 38.6%, XF10 44.6%. Electrical conductivity increases with rGO volume fraction: XF0 1.09E-11 S/m, XF10 2.64E-1 S/m; percolation threshold below 3.46 vol% rGO. Study focused on rGO/Si3N4 nanocomposites for dielectric/EMW applications.
source: WANG_2016_Synthesis of polymer-derived graphene silicon nitride-based

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Urea linkages implied by poly(ureasilazane) designation

Gaseous pyrolysis products include evaporating monomer/oligomer fragments (M/e 41-45), C2H6 and C2H4 (M/e 26-30), CH4, NH3, and H2O (M/e 15-18), and H2 (M/e 2). Gases with higher molecular weight have intensity peaks at lower temperatures. Ceramic yield ~75% in argon or nitrogen.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN amorphous; crystallizes to Si3N4/SiC nanocomposite
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous Si-N-C after pyrolysis at 1040 °C. After 1550 °C/2 h in nitrogen: alpha-Si3N4, beta-Si3N4, and SiC nanocrystals (<10 nm) in amorphous matrix. After 1650 °C/2 h: majority crystallized, grains ~30 nm, phases alpha- and beta-Si3N4 and SiC with higher SiC proportion. After 1700 °C: fully crystalline, only SiC phase present due to nitrogen depletion.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: After crystallization: alpha-Si3N4, beta-Si3N4, SiC; at 1700 °C only SiC

notes: Grain size range: <10 nm at 1550 °C treatment, ~30 nm at 1650 °C treatment; midpoint 20 nm noted in grain_size_nm and crystallite_size_nm. Heating rate given as 5-25 °C/h (midpoint ~15 °C/h), converted to ~0.25 °C/min midpoint; range was 5-25 °C/h. Two consolidation routes explored: (1) warm-pressing (260-350 °C, 100 MPa) followed by pyrolysis - yields open porosity; (2) prepyrolysis of powder (600-800 °C) followed by binding with liquid polymer, cold isostatic pressing (450 MPa), and pyrolysis - yields higher density, no detectable open porosity. Crystallization treatments conducted at 1550-1750 °C in nitrogen for 2 h. Supplier: Commodore Polymer Technologies, Columbus, OH.

polymer_name: Ceraset (polyurea methylvinyl silazane) modified with aluminum isopropoxide

elemental_composition.other_elements: Al present; ceramic compositions given as SiAl0.02C0.84N0.90 (SiAlCN-5), SiAl0.04C0.83N0.93 (SiAlCN-10), SiC0.99N0.85 (SiCN); samples contain ~3 wt% oxygen

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Al-O bonds implied from aluminum isopropoxide incorporation; SiO4 tetrahedral network observed in oxide scale by 29Si NMR

functional_groups.other: aluminum isopropoxide (AIs) used as Al source reacted with polysilazane at 150C

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Crosslinking performed at 400C for 4h, pyrolysis at 1000C for 4h in nitrogen; pressure-assisted pyrolysis under 50 MPa isostatic pressure to prevent cracks and pores

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal with 3 wt% dicumyl peroxide as initiator at 150C for 0.5h solidification, then 400C for 4h crosslinking

backbone_architecture.description: Liquid-phase polyaluminasilazane formed by reaction of polyurea(methylvinyl)silazane (Ceraset) with aluminum isopropoxide at 150C for 4h in flowing argon; crosslinked and pyrolyzed under isostatic pressure to yield fully dense ceramics

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: All ceramics are amorphous as-pyrolyzed; oxide scales formed during oxidation are also amorphous (confirmed by XRD); 29Si NMR shows SiO4 tetrahedral at ~-100 ppm in oxide scale; aluminum not incorporated into SiO2 network per NMR

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases detected; all oxide scales confirmed amorphous by XRD

notes: Study focuses on oxidation behavior of polymer-derived SiAlCN ceramics at 900-1200C in dry air. Two SiAlCN compositions prepared: SiAlCN-5 (CER:AIs = 9.5:0.5 wt) and SiAlCN-10 (CER:AIs = 9:1 wt). Precursor is Ceraset (KiON, polyurea methylvinyl silazane) reacted with aluminum isopropoxide. Fully dense discs produced by pressure-assisted pyrolysis at 50 MPa. Parabolic oxidation rate constants measured at 900-1200C; at 1200C steady-state rates for SiAlCN-10 (~0.025e-18 m2/s) are ~200x lower than SiCN and an order of magnitude lower than CVD SiC and Si3N4. Oxidation atmosphere for kinetics study: dry air. Powder samples ~1-3 micron diameter used for NMR and XRD characterization of oxide scales.
source: Wang_2005_Oxidation of PolymerDerived SiAlCN Ceramics

polymer_name: Ceraset (polyurea(methylvinyl)silazane); polyaluminasilazane (Ceraset reacted with aluminum isopropoxide)

elemental_composition.other_elements: SiCN ceramic composition: SiC0.99N0.85O0.11; SiAlCN ceramic composition: SiAl0.08C0.80N0.95O0.15 (these are ceramic-state compositions, not polymer-state)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Al-N or Al-O bonds implied by aluminum isopropoxide incorporation into polysilazane backbone; details not specified

functional_groups.other: Ceraset is described as polyurea(methylvinyl)silazane, implying urea linkages; aluminum isopropoxide used as modifier

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis carried out under isostatic pressure of 50 MPa to prevent formation of cracks and pores; cross-linking performed prior to pyrolysis

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

backbone_architecture.description: Liquid-phase polyaluminasilazane precursor synthesized by reaction of Ceraset and aluminum isopropoxide at 150°C in flowing argon, then cross-linked to form a network prior to pyrolysis

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiAlCN (amorphous matrix with oxide scale of cristobalite and mullite after oxidation); SiCN (oxide scale of pure cristobalite after oxidation)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After 200 h annealing in water vapor at 1100°C: SiCN oxide scale = pure cristobalite (a=0.49836 nm, c=0.67559 nm); SiAlCN oxide scale = cristobalite + small amount of mullite (a=0.49980 nm, c=0.70785 nm). Fully dense ceramics prepared by pressure-assisted pyrolysis.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Paper notes that corrosion-associated surface defects (cracks, roughness) cause remarkable decrease in strength; SiAlCN surface remained smooth and crack-free after 100 h in water vapor, implying better retention of mechanical strength

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Oxide scale on SiCN: cristobalite; Oxide scale on SiAlCN: cristobalite + mullite (after water vapor oxidation at 1100°C for 200 h)

notes: Study focuses on water-vapor corrosion behavior of polymer-derived SiCN and SiAlCN ceramics at 1100°C in 100% water vapor flowing at 4.4 cm/s. SiAlCN prepared from Ceraset reacted with aluminum isopropoxide (Si:Al atomic ratio = 100:8). Paralinear kinetics: SiCN kl=3.7e-3 mg/(cm2·h), kp=38.2e-5 mg2/(cm4·h); SiAlCN kl=0.96e-3 mg/(cm2·h), kp=5.5e-5 mg2/(cm4·h). Corrosion rate of SiAlCN is ~order of magnitude lower than CVD SiC and Si3N4. Polymer-state elemental composition not reported; only ceramic-state compositions given in Table I.

polymer_name: PUMVS (polyurea(methylvinyl)silazane); polyaluminasilazane (PUMVS reacted with aluminum isopropoxide)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Al present in SiAlCN variants; ceramic compositions given as SiC0.99N0.85 (SiCN), SiAl0.04C0.83N0.93 (SiAlCN-10), SiAl0.08C0.80N0.95 (SiAlCN-20), SiAl0.12C0.78N0.91 (SiAlCN-30); all samples contain less than 3 wt.% oxygen

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Al-N and Al-O bonds implied by incorporation of aluminum isopropoxide into polysilazane backbone

functional_groups.other: aluminum isopropoxide (AIP) used as co-reactant to introduce aluminum into the polymer network

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis noted to be usually performed at 800-1000 °C for PDCs generally; specific pyrolysis conditions for these samples not detailed in the text. Pressure-assisted pyrolysis technique was used.

backbone_architecture.description: Polyaluminasilazane synthesized by reaction of PUMVS and aluminum isopropoxide (AIP); specific architecture not described

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN, SiAlCN (amorphous as-pyrolyzed); oxide scales after oxidation at 1400°C consist of cristobalite, with minor mullite for high-Al content samples
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: As-pyrolyzed ceramics are amorphous. After oxidation at 1400°C for 200h: SiCN and SiAlCN-10 form cristobalite only; SiAlCN-20 forms cristobalite with very small amount of mullite; SiAlCN-30 forms cristobalite plus mullite. Aluminum dissolves into cristobalite increasing lattice parameters.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Ceramics described as fully dense; excellent thermomechanical properties noted generally for Si-based PDCs including resistance to creep

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: As-pyrolyzed: amorphous. Oxide scale after 1400°C oxidation: cristobalite (major), mullite (minor, in SiAlCN-30 and trace in SiAlCN-20)

notes: Paper focuses on oxidation kinetics at 1400°C of polymer-derived SiAlCN ceramics. Precursor for SiCN is commercial PUMVS; SiAlCN precursors are polyaluminasilazanes made by reacting PUMVS with aluminum isopropoxide (AIP) at ratios of 90:10, 80:20, and 70:30 (PUMVS:AIP). Ceramics prepared by pressure-assisted pyrolysis. SiAlCN-20 shows lowest parabolic oxidation rate constant (kp = 0.47e-18 m2/s), over an order of magnitude lower than CVD SiC and Si3N4. Ceramic compositions are expressed as atomic ratios relative to Si. Lattice constants of cristobalite: SiCN a=0.4936nm, c=0.6780nm; SiAlCN-10 a=0.4939nm, c=0.6960nm; SiAlCN-20 a=0.4979nm, c=0.7104nm; SiAlCN-30 a=0.4946nm, c=0.7007nm.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: PHPS contains large number of Si-H groups; PHPS backbone contains Si-N bonds; PHMS backbone contains Si-O bonds (polysiloxane)

functional_groups.other: PHPS produced by ammonolysis of dichlorosilane SiH2Cl2 and subsequent base-catalyzed dehydrogenative coupling; hydroxyl-reactive Si-H groups in PHPS

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PHPS completely crosslinked around 150-200 C with no significant weight loss/gain during crosslinking; main weight gain by oxygen incorporation occurs 200-400 C despite loss of ammonia and hydrogen; after 400 C no significant weight change indicating completion of ceramic conversion. PHMS crosslinked at 150 C for 2 h then pyrolyzed at 800 C for 2 h. ZrSi2-filled SiOC powder gained ~3.5% during 2h pyrolysis then continued to gain ~3% more over 100 h. SiON gained 3.4% during pyrolysis and only ~0.16% additional over 200 h.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - PHMS crosslinked in humid air at 150 C for 2 h with Ru3(CO)12 catalyst (0.05 wt% to PHMS); PHPS crosslinked thermally or by humidity/amine/acid/peroxide

backbone_architecture.description: PHMS is a linear polysiloxane; PHPS is a polysilazane produced by ammonolysis of dichlorosilane. PHPS described as having a large number of Si-H groups.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiON (from PHPS pyrolyzed in air below 1000 C); SiOC (from PHMS pyrolysis)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PHPS converts to Si3N4 in inert atmosphere and SiON in air/oxygen below 1000 C. Ceramic matrix from PHMS pyrolysis is amorphous SiOC. Coatings described as dense and amorphous. ZrSi2 active filler oxidizes to form oxide shell. TGO (thermally grown oxide) layer forms at ceramic-metal interface during oxidation.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Combined ceramic layer modulus 60.0 GPa, thickness ~21.5 um, CTE ~1.0e-6 K-1; bond coat modulus 77.4 GPa, thickness 1.5 um; substrate (Inconel 617) modulus 160 GPa, CTE 11.6e-6 K-1

notes: Paper describes two PDC systems: (1) PHMS (HMS992, Gelest) polyhydromethylsiloxane used as matrix for ZrSi2-filled SiOC composite coatings with 30 vol% ZrSi2 active filler, catalyzed by 0.05 wt% Ru3(CO)12, deposited by dip coating and pyrolyzed at 800 C in air; (2) PHPS NN 120-20 (20 wt% solution in dibutyl ether, Clariant) perhydropolysilazane used for SiON bond coat, pyrolyzed at 800 C in air. Heating rate range 2-3 C/min; midpoint 2.5 used. SiOC composite coating density after pyrolysis at 800 C: 2.57 g/cm3. Coating thickness: SiOC composite ~15 um (at 500 mm/min withdrawal); SiON ~1.5 um (at 100-500 mm/min, 0.5-1.5 um range). Substrate: Inconel 617 superalloy. TGO thickness at ceramic-metal interface grew from 0.378 um (0h) to 1.586 um (200h) for SiOC-coated samples. All three coating systems tested at 800 C in air with ambient humidity 30-50% for up to 200 h. Combined SiON bond coat + ZrSi2-filled SiOC top coat provided near-complete oxidation protection of Inconel 617 at 800 C for 100 h.
source: Wang_2011_High performance environmental barrier coatings Part II Acti

polymer_name: HTZN-0.5 (allylhydridopolycarbosilane-based single-source precursor with HfCl4, TaCl5, ZrCl4, NbCl5)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Hf, Ta, Zr, Nb present in equimolar ratios (Hf0.25Ta0.25Zr0.25Nb0.25); AHPCS formula: [SiH1.30(CH3)0.60(CH2CH=CH2)0.10CH2]n

bonding_structure.other_bonds: M-C bonds (M = Hf, Ta, Zr, Nb) formed via dehydrochlorination between MCln and Si-H; vinyl (C=C) groups present in AHPCS, consumed via hydrosilylation in SSPs; M-Cl bonds in precursor metal chlorides

functional_groups.other: allyl groups (CH2CH=CH2) in AHPCS; allyl groups consumed by hydrosilylation upon SSP formation

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Mass retention over 90% at 1100 degrees C reported for SSP. Pyrolysis at 900 degrees C for 2 h under argon yields amorphous ceramic powders. Subsequent annealing at 1100-1600 degrees C for 2 h produces SiC/(Hf0.25Ta0.25Zr0.25Nb0.25)C/C nanocomposites.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - crosslinking at 160 degrees C for 6 h under nitrogen flow, producing a black solid

backbone_architecture.description: AHPCS-based single-source precursor with Hf, Ta, Zr, Nb incorporated into the polycarbosilane chains via dehydrochlorination (M-Cl + Si-H) and hydrosilylation (C=C + Si-H); liquid SSP crosslinked thermally to solid network

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC/(Hf0.25Ta0.25Zr0.25Nb0.25)C/C nanocomposite; amorphous after pyrolysis at 900 degrees C
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiC@C and (Hf0.25Ta0.25Zr0.25Nb0.25)C@C core-shell nanostructures identified. High-entropy carbide phase (Hf0.25Ta0.25Zr0.25Nb0.25)C forms in situ. After SPS at 2200 degrees C, dense monolithic nanocomposite obtained. Phase composition adjustable by metal content in SSP.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fracture toughness KIC = 3.59 +/- 0.24 MPa·m^0.5 (HTZN-0.5-bulk after SPS at 2200 degrees C, 50 MPa, 15 min); hardness 27.47 +/- 0.46 GPa; modulus 324.00 +/- 13.60 GPa; bulk density 3.34 g/cm3; open porosity 0.41 vol%

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous after pyrolysis at 900 degrees C; crystalline phases develop upon annealing at 1100-1600 degrees C and after SPS
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC, (Hf0.25Ta0.25Zr0.25Nb0.25)C (high-entropy carbide solid solution), C (carbon); characterized by XRD and SAED

notes: The preceramic polymer is AHPCS (allylhydridopolycarbosilane, formula [SiH1.30(CH3)0.60(CH2CH=CH2)0.10CH2]n) modified with equimolar HfCl4, TaCl5, ZrCl4, NbCl5 to form a liquid single-source precursor (SSP). Three SSP variants prepared: HTZN-1 (MCl:AHPCS 1:2), HTZN-0.5 (1:4), HTZN-0.25 (1:8). Si-H reaction degree increases with higher MCln feed ratio: HTZN-1 ~71%, HTZN-0.5 ~64%, HTZN-0.25 ~61%, AHPCS-blank ~4%. Final dense monolithic ceramic HTZN-0.5-bulk produced by SPS at 2200 degrees C, 50 MPa, 15 min under argon. Ceramic yield >90% at 1100 degrees C. Crosslinking at 160 degrees C for 6 h under N2. Pyrolysis at 900 degrees C for 2 h under Ar. Annealing range 1100-1600 degrees C for 2 h.

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present in PSNB; elemental mapping confirms Si, C, O, N, B uniformly distributed in SSA0.5

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds present (from PSNB, IR peak at 1350-1450 cm-1 and 1384 cm-1 post-pyrolysis); Si-O-Si bonds (1080 cm-1 from PHMS); Si-CH2CH2- bonds formed by hydrosilylation (1049 cm-1); C=C bonds from DVB crosslinker (1602 cm-1); free carbon C=C (1630 cm-1 post-pyrolysis)

functional_groups.other: B-N groups in PSNB; Si-O-Si groups in PHMS; divinylbenzene (DVB) used as crosslinking agent

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yield ranged from 45.86% (SSA0.25) to 51.94% (SSA1); higher PHMS content led to higher ceramic yield as SiOC yield exceeds SiBCN yield; average linear shrinkage ~32% for all samples after pyrolysis at 1200 C; high-temperature annealing also performed at 1600 C for 60 min in Ar for stability studies

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (solvothermal at 160 C for 20 h) with Pt-catalyzed hydrosilylation; Si-H bonds in PHMS and PSNB react with C=C bonds in DVB to form Si-C linked 3D network; Karstedt catalyst (0.1 wt% Pt in xylene) used

backbone_architecture.description: Complex three-dimensional nanoparticle network formed by hydrosilylation crosslinking of PSNB and PHMS with DVB crosslinker; pearl-chain-like amorphous nanoparticle structure retained after pyrolysis; hierarchical porous structure with mesopores and macropores (pore diameters mostly 10-70 nm)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Aerogel composed of uniformly distributed amorphous SiBCN and SiOC nanophases with free carbon; SAED confirms fully amorphous character at 1200 C; broad diffuse XRD scattering peaks confirm amorphous state; after 1600 C treatment in Ar, composite aerogel retains amorphous nanoparticle pearl-chain-like structure; introduction of SiOC inhibits crystallization of SiBCN at high temperatures

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Pure SiBCN aerogel (SA) compressive strength 0.147 MPa; SSA0.5 optimal compressive strength 0.507 MPa (260% improvement); specific strength increased from 1256 to 3756 N·m·kg-1; all samples showed brittle behavior (stress peaked then dropped sharply with increasing strain)

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases detected; broad diffuse scattering peaks only for all SSA samples pyrolyzed at 1200 C; amorphous structure retained even after 1600 C heat treatment

notes: Paper describes SiBCN/SiOC composite ceramic aerogels prepared from PSNB (polyborosilazane) and PHMS (polyhydromethylsiloxane) precursors with DVB crosslinker via solvothermal crosslinking (160 C, 20 h), freeze-drying (-50 C, 48 h), and pyrolysis (1200 C, 2 h, Ar). PSNB:PHMS mass ratios studied: 1:0.25 (SSA0.25), 1:0.5 (SSA0.5), 1:0.75 (SSA0.75), 1:1 (SSA1). Density range 0.12-0.16 g/cm3. Thermal conductivity 0.044-0.051 W/m/K at room temperature; 0.052 W/m/K after 1600 C treatment (SSA0.5). BET surface area: SA=56.39, SSA0.5=116.18 m2/g. EMW absorption: optimal RL=-55.39 dB, EAB=6.7 GHz at 2.5 mm thickness for SSA0.5. Ceramic yield range 45.86-51.94% noted for midpoint calculation. High-temperature stability tested at 1600 C in Ar for 60 min with linear shrinkage ~10% and density ~0.081-0.095 g/cm3 post-treatment.
source: Wang_2026_Robust and thermally insulating SiBCN SiOC ceramic aerogel w

polymer_name: polyborazylene (PB), DPA-modified polyborazylene, B-HPZ, PIN-HPZ, DEB-HPZ, B-TTS, B-HCT, HPZ

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present in all polyborazylene and polyborosilazane systems; compositions given as atomic ratios in tables, e.g. HPZ: Si1.00 N1.04 C1.16 H4.69; B-HPZ-2: Si1.00 N0.99 C1.17 H4.61 (B3N3H5)0.045; PIN-HPZ-3: Si1.00 N0.90 C0.86 H3.93 (C6H12BO2)0.18; PB: B3.0 N3.2 H3.6; DPA-4: (B3.0N3.12H3.9)(NPn2)0.47

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-H bonds present in polyborazylene and borosilazane systems; B-N bonds present throughout; N-Si cleavage reactions noted for HMD-modified polymers; B-N crosslinks formed during pyrolysis via dehydrocoupling

functional_groups.other: pendant dipentylamine (DPA) groups, pendant diethylamine (DEA) groups, hexamethyldisilazane (HMD) derived N-SiMe3 groups, pinacolborane (PIN) groups (C6H12BO2), borazine rings (B3N3) retained in polymer backbone, alkyl groups (ethyl, propyl) on B-alkylpolyborazylenes

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: argon and ammonia (varies by sample; DPA-4 fibers pyrolyzed under ammonia to 1000 C; TGA studies under argon)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PB converts to BN in 84-93% ceramic yield and 89-99% chemical yield. B-alkylpolyborazylenes showed ceramic yields near 50% (lower than predicted 63-72%), attributed to volatilization of lower-MW species and loss of alkylborazine species by TGA-MS. DPA-modified polymers show onset of decomposition/weight loss increasing to ca. 100 C. Bulk ceramic conversion values from tables: B-TTS 37.8% (N2) and 26.1% (Ar); B-HCT 54.3% (N2) and 36.2% (Ar); B-HPZ-2 70.0% (N2) and 51.1% (Ar); PIN-HPZ-3 59.1% (N2) and 53.7% (Ar); HPZ 57.0% (N2) and 42.4% (Ar)

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - dehydrocoupling reactions between B-H and N-H groups form B-N crosslinks; amine functionalization used to reduce low-temperature crosslinking; HMD-modified polymers showed additional crosslinking via pendant HN-SiMe3 groups

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC implied; multiple polymers reported: PB Mn=500-900, Mw=3000-8000; DEA/DPA-modified Mn=450-800; HMD-modified Mn=1500; B-alkyl Mn~540 (ethyl), ~468 (propyl), Mw~926 (ethyl), ~824 (propyl); after hydroboration Mn=1349; HPZ Mn=25800; B-HPZ-1 Mn=24000; B-HPZ-2 Mn=23300; B-HPZ-3 Mn=13300; B-HPZ-4 Mn=5492; PIN-HPZ-1 Mn=6110; PIN-HPZ-2 Mn=2655; PIN-HPZ-3 Mn=2205; DEB-HPZ-1 Mn=3710; DEB-HPZ-2 Mn=3260; DEB-HPZ-3 Mn=2730; B-TTS Mn=1356; B-HCT Mn=3201

backbone_architecture.description: Polyborazylene has a complex structure related to organic polyphenylenes with linear, branched-chain and fused-cyclic segments; borazine ring structure retained in polymer; layered structure in solid state by powder XRD. Borosilazane polymers (B-HPZ etc.) formed by reaction of silazane with borane species with borazine rings pendant or incorporated into silazane backbone.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: BN (turbostratic) from polyborazylene/DPA systems; SiNCB from borosilazane systems; SiC from HPZ
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: DPA-4 derived BN fibers confirmed turbostratic BN by XRD and DRIFT. Bulk ceramic compositions from tables: B-TTS (N2): Si1.00N5.52C0.21B5.26; B-HCT (N2): Si1.00N3.89C0.64B2.78; B-HPZ-2 (N2): Si1.00N1.08C0.44B0.09; PIN-HPZ-3 (N2): Si1.00N1.02C0.67B0.15O0.26; HPZ (N2): Si1.00N0.97C0.41. High carbon contents (2.0-6.5%) found in ceramics from B-alkylpolyborazylenes. BN fiber elemental analysis: B1.00N1.03C0.00H0.20; surface by RBS: B1.5N1.0O0.2 (B2O3 surface layer).

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: DPA-4 derived BN fibers (~30 um diameter): tensile strength ~0.18 GPa, elastic modulus ~14 GPa. Kimura poly(aminoborazine)-derived BN fibers (10 um): tensile strength ~1 GPa, elastic modulus 78 GPa (cited for comparison). BN fibers described as flexible.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: turbostratic BN (from DPA-4 derived ceramic fibers and bulk samples); polyborazylene shows layered structure by powder XRD

notes: Paper reviews multiple polymer systems: (1) polyborazylene (PB) and amine-modified polyborazylenes (DPA, DEA, HMD series) as BN precursors; (2) B-alkylpolyborazylenes (ethyl, propyl); (3) borosilazane polymers (B-TTS, B-HCT, B-HPZ series, PIN-HPZ series, DEB-HPZ series) as SiNCB precursors; (4) HPZ (hydridopolysilazane) as reference. Two sets of ceramic conversion data are given in separate tables, likely corresponding to different pyrolysis atmospheres (N2 vs Ar). DPA-4 polymer Tg reduced to -90 C enabling melt-spinning. Glass transition temperatures reported for select polymers in table: HPZ 87.0 C, PIN-HPZ-1 120.9 C, PIN-HPZ-2 110.9 C, PIN-HPZ-3 102.3 C, DEB-HPZ-1 78.3 C, DEB-HPZ-2 49.7 C, DEB-HPZ-3 23.0 C. Ceramic densities also reported in tables. B-TTS and B-HCT densities 1.7 g/ml; B-HPZ-2 2.3 g/ml; PIN-HPZ-3 2.3-2.45 g/ml; HPZ 2.6 g/ml. Authors: Wideman, Fazen, Su, Remsen, Zank, Sneddon; institutions University of Pennsylvania and Dow Corning. Published in Applied Organometallic Chemistry 12, 681-693 (1998).

GM35: Si surrounded by three carbodiimide groups and one phenyl substituent (SiN4 tetrahedral environment dominant in ceramic). thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis performed at 800 and 1100 C. Heating rate 100 C/h (1.67 C/min). 2 h dwell time at final temperature. Significant H loss upon increasing pyrolysis temperature from 800 to 1100 C. All samples X-ray amorphous after pyrolysis.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Low carbon PDCs (GM35, 35-40 wt% C) at 800 C: amorphous nanodomains of sp2 carbon and silicon nitride (a-Si3N4) with interfacial mixed bonding (N, C, Si). No mixed bond tetrahedra (SiCxN4-x) detected; structure is phase-separated a-Si3N4 and a-C nanodomains. Nanodomains 1-3 nm in size. All samples X-ray amorphous up to 1100 C.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases detected by XRD at 800 or 1100 C. Beta-SiC crystallites appear at 1500 C; alpha-SiC and turbostratic carbon appear at 2000 C.

notes: Study focuses on pyrolyzed SiCN polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs), not the precursor polymers directly. Two precursors studied: GM35 (poly(phenylsilsesquicarbodiimide), branched) and HN1 (poly(phenylvinylsilylcarbodiimide), linear). Ceramic samples designated GM35-800, GM35-1100, HN1-800, HN1-1100. Atomic fractions (g-atom, v+w+x+y+z=1) from calorimetry table: GM35-800: Si 0.096, C 0.346, N 0.244, O 0.041, H 0.273; GM35-1100: Si 0.134, C 0.435, N 0.285, O 0.015, H 0.130; HN1-800: Si 0.121, C 0.594, N 0.149, O 0.020, H 0.116; HN1-1100: Si 0.126, C 0.671, N 0.151, O 0.019, H 0.034. NMR identifies SiN4 tetrahedral environment dominant (29Si at -47 ppm), sp2 carbon at 123-127 ppm and 150 ppm (C with N neighbors), NC1/4Si2/4 and NSi3/4 nitrogen environments. 15N and 13C isotopic enrichment used for GM35 samples.

notes: Study focuses on 18 different polysiloxane compositions pyrolyzed to silicon oxycarbide glasses for Li-ion battery anode applications. Key finding: only C and H atoms evolve during pyrolysis, allowing prediction of char stoichiometry from initial polymer composition and char yield. Final char properties depend on stoichiometry, not initial polymer composition. Chars showed reversible Li capacity >800 mAh/g. Samples 40, 41, 42 chosen to produce identical stoichiometry from different polymer precursors. XAS at Si K-edge confirmed identical local Si environment in all three chars at 1000 °C. Pyrolysis atmosphere: ultrahigh purity argon (99.999%). Cooling rate ~4 °C/min. Char yields per sample ranged 53-86% (see table). Polymers synthesized by hydrolysis/condensation of alkoxysilanes with acid catalyst, then base-catalyzed equilibration, and end-capping with chlorodimethylvinylsilane.

Ceramic yields: SiCN-1200: 63.7%, SiCN-1300: 62.4%, SiCN-1400: 61.1%, SiCN-1500: 60.5%. notes: This is a review paper covering multiple preceramic polymer systems and fabrication routes for SiC-based ceramic microstructures. Polymers discussed include: polymethylsilane (PMS), allylhydridopolycarbosilane (AHPCS, SP matrix), polycarbosilane (PCS, commercial, Starfire/Nippon Carbon), polysilazane (VL-20, KiON Corp.), and polyureamethylvinylsilazane. Target ceramics include SiC, SiCN, and SiBCN. Fabrication routes include sacrificial template infiltration (silica spheres 112-700 nm, porous carbon 3DOM, nanoporous SBA-15, KIT-6, alumina membranes) followed by curing and pyrolysis, and lithographic techniques (soft lithography MIMIC/microtransfer molding, stereolithography via two-photon absorption). Porous SiC monolith channels demonstrated for NH3 decomposition to H2 with Ru catalyst. Shrinkage during pyrolysis noted as critical issue; controlled by adding ceramic nanoparticles. Mesoporous BN also briefly mentioned (precursor: tri(methylamino)borazine, template: CMK-3, surface area 540 m2/g, pore size 4.4 nm). Multiple pyrolysis temperatures reported: 800 C (SiC line patterns), 1000 C (AHPCS/silica nanocasting), 1250 C (SiCN/polysilazane, PMS/alumina nanotube), 1400 C (PCS/SBA-15 beta-SiC crystallization), 600 C (3D woodpile stereolithography).

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Polymers are described as precursors for silicon nitride ceramics; no characterization of actual pyrolyzed ceramic microstructure reported in this text

notes: HPZ1 synthesized by ammonolysis of chloro(N,N-diethylamino)silane (H2SiCl(NEt2)) with NH3 in THF at -60°C. HPZ2 synthesized by ammonolysis of bis(N,N-diethylamino)silane (H2Si(NEt2)2) with NH3. Both have Mn ~1000 g/mol and Si:N ~1:1 atomic ratio. Both are low-molecular-weight polysilazanes that rapidly self-condense to gel at high concentration. In 35 wt% THF solution (HPZ1) or 45 wt% THF solution (HPZ2) at 20°C, higher molecular weight polysilazanes form with Mw up to 85000 (HPZ1) and 45000 (HPZ2). Silylation with TMCS (≥20 mol%) suppresses gelation, extending it to ~2 days. Approximately 1/6 of N-H groups are silylated at 20 mol% TMCS addition. All synthesis operations performed under dry nitrogen atmosphere. 29Si CP/MAS NMR also used for characterization. Paper is in Japanese with partial English content.

notes: Paper describes a series of polysilane precursor polymers [R1R2Si]n with R1=CH3 and R2=H, C2H5, C3H7, C4H9, C6H11, C8H17, or C6H5, plus polydimethylsilane and polydiethylsilane. Elemental analyses reported as weight percent C and H (not atomic percent) for selected polymers: [Me2Si]n C expected 41.4% found 39.6%, H expected 10.3% found 10.4%; [MePhSi]n C expected 70.0% found 66.8%; [MeHSi]n C expected 27.3% found 21.8%; [Et2Si]n C expected 55.8% found 49.9%. backbone_architecture.description: Perhydropolysilazane with Si-N backbone; specific architecture not detailed beyond being a preceramic polymer convertible to SiO2

Cured at 60 C for 1 h then 7 days at ~20 C. PDS layer thickness approximately 109 A (~10.9 nm) for PP/PDS/Si buried sample. PHPS average molecular weight ~10,000 g/mol; estimated precursor radius ~2 nm. Low-density surface PDS layer ~50 A thick observed in all samples. DSC melting point data provided for before pyrolysis and after pyrolysis at 900-1300 C (Tm ranging from 1111-1146 C). Ceramic yield of 75% inferred from stated 25 wt% total weight loss. Polymer 2 (1,2-dimethylsilazane): principal endotherm 375-385C, Si3N4 content 50-60%, yield 15-20%. Polymer 3 (1,2-dimethylsilazane-1-methylsilazane copolymer): principal endotherm 286-287C, Si3N4 content 80-85%, yield 50-55%.

notes: Paper by Barry Arkles (1986), J. Electrochem. Soc. 133, 233, Petrarch Systems Inc. Three polymers compared: [1] poly(1,1-dimethylsilazane) cyclic (bp 186-188C, viscosity >1000 ctsk), [2] 1,2-dimethylsilazane cyclic (bp 56C, sp.gr. 0.99, viscosity 600-700 ctsk), [3] 1,2-dimethylsilazane-1-methylsilazane copolymer cyclic (bp 202-206C, sp.gr. 1.04, viscosity 150-250 ctsk). Ceramic yield pct in table refers to pyrolysis yield per polymer: polymer 1: 5-10%, polymer 2: 15-20%, polymer 3: 50-55%. 1,2-dimethylsilazanes convert at lower temperatures to higher silicon nitride levels versus 1,1-dimethylsilazanes due to lower N-CH3 bond dissociation energy. notes: Five terpolymer samples (A-80, B-160, C-240, D-360, E-600) with targeted DP of 80, 160, 240, 360, 600 and targeted Mw of 6300, 12400, 18600, 27800, 46100 g/mol respectively. backbone_architecture.description: Crosslinked polymeric gel network formed via dehydration and condensation reactions (esterification) between glycerol, tartaric acid, and boric acid forming borate ester linkages (B-O-C). conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: B4C (primary, confirmed by (104) and (021) planes); residual graphite (002) at 26.5 deg and (100) at 44 deg in some samples; cubic B2O3 (310) at 28 deg in some samples at 1400 deg C

notes: This paper describes a modified sol-gel approach (not a traditional preceramic polymer) using glycerol, tartaric acid, and boric acid with elemental nano boron (<250 nm) to synthesize B4C powders. This is not a silicon-based preceramic polymer system. The polymer is a borate ester network (B-O-C precursor) that converts to B4C upon heat treatment. Elemental nano boron acts as: (1) additional reducing agent for B2O3 reduction, (2) seeding particles enhancing B4C crystallization. Final B4C particle size: GT25-1500 average 1.3 micron; B25GT25-1500 and B50GT25-1500 average 0.5-0.7 micron. Rietveld refinement used to quantify graphite content (~1 +/- 5 wt%). XRD performed with Cu Kalpha radiation, 10-80 deg 2theta, 1 deg/min. DTA/DSC performed in argon at 5 deg C/min to 1400-1600 deg C.

Three fiber variants: SiC-HfC1 (no pyrolysis, sintered 1800°C), SiC-HfC2 (pyrolyzed 1600°C/Ar, intermediate oxidation 700°C/air, sintered 2000°C/Ar), SiC-HfC3 (same as HfC2). XPS C/Si ratios: 1.9, 1.2, 1.1 for HfC1, HfC2, HfC3. Fabricated by polymer-derived ceramics (PDC) method. Intended for CMC reinforcement in aerospace, nuclear, and military applications.

polymer_name: DHTF gel series (DHTH 1/1, DHTH 1/2, DHTH 1/9), T, TQ, TTH, DHQ

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yields vary by DH/TH ratio: DHTH 1/1 = 87%, DHTH 1/2 = 91%, DHTH 1/9 = 94%. Weight loss occurs in multiple steps: below 400C (H2O, EtOH, H2, C2H6 evolved); 400-600C (largest loss, volatile silicon species including silanes (CH3)xSiH4-x); 600-1000C (H2 and CH4 predominantly). Midpoint ceramic yield 91% used; range 87-94% noted.

crosslink_density.value: Degree of condensation by 29Si NMR: DHTH 1/1 = 100%, DHTH 1/2 = 100%, DHTH 1/9 = 93%, T = 97%, TQ = 90%, TTH = 97%, DHQ = 93%

backbone_architecture.description: Si-O-Si network formed by hydrolysis-condensation of organically modified alkoxysilanes. Precursor units include DH (methyldiethoxysilane, difunctional), TH (triethoxysilane, trifunctional), T (methyltriethoxysilane, trifunctional), Q (tetraethoxysilane, tetrafunctional). Mixed-unit gels produce branched/crosslinked polysilsesquioxane-type networks.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Silicon oxycarbide (SiOxCy) amorphous metastable phase in which Si atoms are bonded to both O and C simultaneously. Stoichiometric formulas at 1000C: DHTH 1/1: SiC0.31O1.38 + 0.07C (excess C); DHTH 1/2: SiC0.25O1.49 + 0.05C (excess C); DHTH 1/9: SiC0.15O1.70 + 0.06Si (excess Si). XRD used for phase identification before and after heating.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiOxCy described as amorphous metastable phase; XRD used to identify structures before and after heating but specific phases not enumerated in the provided text

notes: Study focuses on organic-inorganic hybrid sol-gel precursors for SiOC ceramics. Precursors are alkoxysilane-based (not classical polymer chains): DH = (CH3)HSi(OEt)2, TH = HSi(OEt)3, T = CH3Si(OEt)3, Q = Si(OEt)4. Gels dried stepwise at 40, 60, 80, 100, 120C. TGA performed under helium (99.999% purity), 25 cm3/min, samples 400 mg, particle size 100-350 um, Al2O3 crucibles. Chemical analysis: Si by ICP, C and H by high-temperature combustion/IR, O by difference. Ceramic yield range 87-94% across DHTH series; midpoint 91 used in ceramic_yield_pct field. Key finding: residual Si-OH and Si-OEt react with Si-H (200-700C) and Si-Me (above 450C) during pyrolysis. Redistribution reactions of Si-O/Si-H/Si-C bonds dominate 400-600C regime.

polymer_name: AHPCS (Allylhydridopolycarbosilane, SMP-10) and modified variants: ATi, AB, ABTi

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-N(CH3)-Ti linkages confirmed by FTIR and NMR; C-N bonds present; B-O and B-N bonds possible in ABTi; Si-CH2-Si backbone; allyl groups (vinyl) present in AHPCS but consumed by hydrosilylation upon modification with TDMATi; carbosilane chains (-Si-C-C-C-Si-) formed via hydrosilylation

functional_groups.other: N(CH3)x (x=1,2) groups from TDMATi; allyl groups in AHPCS (consumed in ATi/ABTi); boron-containing groups (BC3, BN3, BO4, BO3) in AB and ABTi

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Initial pyrolysis at 1000 C in flowing argon at 5 C/min with 2h dwell. High-temperature heat treatments performed from 1400 to 1800 C in argon at 5 C/min with 2h dwell. For warm-pressed pellets, heating at 1 C/min to 1000 C and 2 C/min cooling. High-temperature TGA performed up to 1800 C at 5 C/min in flowing argon. Continuous evolution of carbon and nitrogen contents observed above 1400 C due to carbothermal reduction reactions.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical - reaction of AHPCS with TDMATi and/or BDMS; boron pre-addition increases crosslinking degree of ABTi compared to ATi as evidenced by broadening of 29Si NMR signals related to Si-N bonds

backbone_architecture.description: AHPCS is a polycarbosilane with Si-CH2-Si backbone and pendant allyl and methyl groups. Modification with TDMATi introduces Si-N(CH3)-Ti bridges. Modification with BDMS introduces boron crosslinks via hydroboration of Si-H groups. ABTi shows higher crosslinking degree than ATi. ATi described as highly viscous gel; ABTi and AB described as solid compounds amenable to warm-pressing.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After pyrolysis at 1000 C: single-phase amorphous Si-Ti-C-N(B,H) ceramics. After heat-treatment at 1400 C: TiCxN1-x (0<=x<=1) nanocrystals in SiCxN4-x-type matrix (0<=x<=4). Above 1400 C: continuous carbothermal reduction forming carbide phases and releasing nitrogen-containing species. At 1800 C: porous, fully crystallized TiC(N)/SiC(B) nanocomposites.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous after pyrolysis at 1000 C; crystalline after heat-treatment at 1800 C
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: TiCxN1-x and SiC(B) phases identified after high-temperature treatment; fully crystallized at 1800 C

notes: Paper describes four preceramic polymer variants: A (pure AHPCS, SMP-10), AB (AHPCS + BDMS, Si:B ratio 30), ATi (AHPCS + TDMATi, Si:Ti molar ratio 5), and ABTi (AHPCS + BDMS + TDMATi). All empirical formulas normalized to Si1.0 with O content omitted. Ceramic samples labeled P-T (polymer type + two-digit temperature). Optical selectivity (alpha/epsilon) of final nanocomposites measured at RT: ABTi_10=1.208, ABTi_14=1.302, ABTi_16=1.398, ABTi_18=1.675 (maximum). Warm-pressing conditions: 74 or 100 MPa, 100-110 C, 0.5h. AHPCS density 0.998 g/cm3. Open porosity of objects ranged from 6% (ABTi_10) to 38% (ABTi_16). ICP used for Si and Ti; hot gas extraction for C, N, O, H in pyrolyzed ceramics. Target application: selective solar absorbers (SSA) for concentrating solar power (CSP) above 900 C.

polymer_name: PS1, PS2, PMV, PCSZ1, PCSZ2, PCSZ2-MV

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si bonds (464 cm-1), Si-phenyl bonds (1949, 1887, 1815 cm-1), cyclic Si4N2 skeleton (peaks at 1116/840 cm-1 for PCSZ1 and 1156/908 cm-1 for PCSZ2), C=C vinyl stretching (1589 cm-1)

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups on PS1; ammonium chloride impurity (NH4+) detected at 3145 cm-1 in PCSZ1

PS1 yield 68.5 wt%, PS2 yield 45.0 wt%, PMV yield low (8 wt% polymer yield, ceramic yield not separately stated), PCSZ1 yield 43.3 wt%, PCSZ2 not separately tabulated. Blends of PS1/PCSZ1 showed observed ceramic yields higher than calculated by rule of mixtures, attributed to crosslinking reactions between Si-H, vinyl, and amine groups. Si powder and PS2/Si mixtures showed weight gain between 1500-1600 C due to Si3N4 formation. For PMV, PCSZ2, and PCSZ2-MV, crystallization heating was to 1650 C at 3 C/min with 3 h hold; for PS1, PS2, and blends/mixtures, crystallization was to 1600 C at 2 C/min with 2 h hold.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - reactions between Si-H, N-H, and vinyl (C=C) groups during pyrolysis; crosslinking inferred from higher-than-calculated ceramic yields in blends and co-polymer

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC calibrated with polystyrene standards; chloroform eluent for polysilanes, THF eluent for polycyclodisilazane and co-polycyclodisilazane-silane. Individual values: PS1 Mw=65000, Mn=4470, PDI=14.5; PS2 Mw=3570, Mn=1560, PDI=2.3; PMV Mw=2490, Mn=1240, PDI=2.0; PCSZ1 Mw=3050, Mn=1340, PDI=2.4; PCSZ2 Mw=3640, Mn=1370, PDI=2.7; PCSZ2-MV Mw=3020, Mn=1260, PDI=2.4

backbone_architecture.description: Polysilanes (PS1, PS2, PMV) prepared by alkali metal dechlorination reaction; polycyclodisilazanes (PCSZ1, PCSZ2) contain cyclic Si4N2 skeleton; PCSZ2-MV is a co-polycyclodisilazane-silane with reactive Si-H, N-H, and vinyl groups. PS1 is a co-polymerized substituted polysilane; PS2 is a ter-polymerized substituted polysilane; PMV is a homopolymer (polymethylvinylsilane).

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: All three synthesis strategies produced SiC-Si3N4 composites. Polysilane precursors yielded beta-SiC (XRD peaks at 2-theta 36, 61, 72 deg corresponding to (111), (220), (311) planes). Polycyclodisilazane precursors yielded alpha-Si3N4 (>20 XRD peaks) with minor SiC. Si powder heated in nitrogen yielded alpha-Si3N4/beta-Si3N4 mixture. Residual carbon reaction with Si3N4 may produce minor SiC in nitride-derived ceramics.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Literature values cited for SiC-Si3N4 nanocomposites (not from this study): up to 1500 MPa room temperature strength and 970 MPa at 1400 C. No mechanical data reported for materials synthesized in this study.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC from polysilane-derived ceramics (2-theta: 36, 61, 72 deg); alpha-Si3N4 from polycyclodisilazane-derived ceramics; alpha-Si3N4/beta-Si3N4 mixture from Si powder nitrided in nitrogen; SiC + Si3N4 in blends, mixtures, and co-polymer after crystallization

notes: Paper describes three strategies for SiC-Si3N4 composite synthesis: (1) blending polysilane (PS1) with polycyclodisilazane (PCSZ1); (2) mixing polysilane (PS2) with reactive Si filler powder; (3) single-source co-polycyclodisilazane-silane precursor (PCSZ2-MV). Softening points: PS1 90 C, PS2 115 C, PMV liquid, PCSZ1 65 C, PCSZ2 40 C, PCSZ2-MV 38 C. Polymer synthesis yields (not ceramic yields): PS1 40 wt%, PS2 48 wt%, PMV 8 wt%, PCSZ1 58 wt%, PCSZ2 68 wt%, PCSZ2-MV 36 wt%. XRD scan range 10-90 deg 2-theta, step 0.021 deg, CuKalpha radiation 0.15406 nm, 35 kV, 20 mA. Cracking and slight bloating observed in pressed pellets after pyrolysis. No shape-forming or morphology control was investigated. Published 1999, Loughborough University.
source: Bao_1999_Different_strategies_for_the_synthesis_of_silicon_carbidesil

polymer_name: P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7, P8, P9 (series of co- and ter-polysilanes)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si backbone (peak at 464 cm-1), Si-phenyl vibration (1949, 1887, 1815 cm-1), C-H stretching in phenyl group (3050, 3067 cm-1)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis occurs in three stages: stage 1 (up to 300C) less than 2% weight loss; stage 2 (300-700C) major weight loss due to decomposition and evolution of methane and hydrogen; stage 3 (above 700C to 900C) further ~2% weight loss. TGA measured at 10 C/min in nitrogen. Individual polymer pyrolytic yields range from 23.6 wt% (P1) to 67.9 wt% (P9). Best SiC foams produced from precursors with 50-60 wt% pyrolytic yield.

backbone_architecture.description: Polysilane backbone (Si-Si bonds). Homopolymers, copolymers, and terpolymers synthesized by alkali dechlorination (Wurtz-type coupling) of chlorinated silane monomers with molten sodium in refluxing toluene/THF. Higher functionality monomers (trichloro-) introduce branching. Overall functionality F ranges from 2.0 to 3.2 depending on monomer composition.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Residues amorphous up to 1100C in nitrogen; crystallize to beta-SiC above 1100C. XRD peaks at 2-theta = 36, 61, 72 degrees corresponding to (111), (220), (311) planes of beta-SiC. Pore sizes vary: lower yield precursors give 700-1800 micron pores (foam); intermediate yield 400-800 micron pores (best foams); higher yield give 5-20 micron micropores.

notes: Paper describes synthesis of SiC foams from a series of polysilanes (P1-P9) and blends (B1-B4) thereof. Monomers used: dichloromethylphenylsilane (MP, f=2), dichloromethylsilane (MH, f=3), dichlorophenylsilane (PH, f=3), trichloromethylsilane (TCM, f=3), trichlorophenylsilane (TCP, f=3), dichloromethylvinylsilane (MVin, f=4). Crystallization heating also performed from 1100-1700C at 2 C/min in nitrogen with 2h soak. Polymer blends B1-B4 made from P2/P9 in ratios 80/20, 60/40, 40/60, 20/80 with pyrolytic yields of 38.9, 48.9, 59.0, 64.1 wt% respectively. Molecular weight data per polymer: P1 Mw=7680 Mn=1520 PDI=5.1; P2 Mw=4270 Mn=1840 PDI=2.3; P3 Mw=6970 Mn=1670 PDI=4.2; P4 Mw=3570 Mn=1560 PDI=2.3; P5 Mw=12000 Mn=2460 PDI=4.9; P6 Mw=4240 Mn=1510 PDI=2.8; P7 Mw=5240 Mn=1600 PDI=3.3; P8 Mw=7700 Mn=1580 PDI=4.9; P9 Mw=8700 Mn=2580 PDI=3.4. polymer_name: polycyclodisilazane (PCDMZ, PCMPZ, PCMHZ, PCPHZ, PCDMMHZ, PCDMPHZ)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Chemical analysis of PCMHZ crystallized residue (wt%): C 8.82, N 28.0, O 1.80; ceramic phase identified as 70 wt% Si3N4 and 25 wt% SiC after heat treatment at 1600 C

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups present in PCMPZ, PCPHZ, PCDMPHZ

backbone_architecture.description: Polycyclodisilazanes with cyclodisilazane rings in the backbone, synthesized via Wurtz-type polymerization of N,N'-bis(chlorodialkylsilyl)tetraalkylcyclodisilazanes; polymodal molecular weight distributions typical of alkali dechlorination products; some polymers are viscous liquids, others solids

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCMHZ residue after 1600 C heat treatment: 70 wt% Si3N4 and 25 wt% SiC. Amorphous after pyrolysis at 900 C; crystallization occurs above 1500 C. More SiC formed in residues from polymers with phenyl substituents.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: silicon nitride (Si3N4) and silicon carbide (SiC)

notes: Six polycyclodisilazanes synthesized and studied: PCDMZ [(CH3)2SiNH]3,4-based, PCMPZ [CH3PhSiNH]3,4-based, PCMHZ [CH3HSiNH]3,4-based, PCPHZ [PhHSiNH]3,4-based, PCDMMHZ and PCDMPHZ (mixed). Synthesis route: ammonolysis of dichlorosilanes -> cyclosilazanes I, then reaction with dichloroalkylsilanes -> dichlorocyclodisilazanes II (Wannagat method), then Wurtz-type polymerization with Na in toluene -> polycyclodisilazanes III. Pyrolytic yields from cyclosilazanes, dichlorocyclodisilazanes and polycyclodisilazanes all reported in Table 4 (stages I, II, III). Tube furnace pyrolysis at 2 C/min to 900 C with 2 h hold in N2; TGA at 10 C/min to 900 C. Chemical analysis of PCMHZ residue: C 8.82 wt%, N 28.0 wt%, O 1.80 wt%. All polymers soluble in toluene; PCMHZ and PCPHZ are solids, others viscous liquids.

notes: Paper focuses on SiC foam fabrication by immersing polyurethane foam in polysilane precursor solutions followed by pyrolysis in nitrogen. Monomers: dichloromethylphenylsilane (MP, f=2), dichloromethylsilane (MH, f=3), trichlorophenylsilane (TCP, f=3), dichloromethylvinylsilane (MVin, f=4). notes: Study compares three PSZ/PCS weight ratios (1:1, 2:1, 3:1). Bulk density decreases with increasing PSZ/PCS ratio (1.70 to 1.36 g/cm3). Open porosity ranges from 24.0% to 30.9%. Samples pressed into cylindrical specimens 18 mm diameter at 60 MPa. Crosslinking conditions: 400°C, 60 min, N2. Reference ceramic yield of 77.8% noted from literature for PCS:PSZ:Xylene:DCP = 2:2:1:0.05 at 120°C, 2 MPa, 6 h. Porosity value of 28.0% and ceramic yield of 85.4% correspond to PSZ/PCS=2 at 1500°C.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: N-Si bonds formed via replacement of N-H in branched structures; Si:N ratio varies from ~1:1 (linear) to ~3:1 (branched)

functional_groups.other: silanediamine [SiH2(NH2)2] intermediate identified; imide group linkages in crosslinked structures

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Shrinkage of ~20% reported at pyrolysis temperature of 400°C. Dehydrogenation reaction occurs during pyrolysis. Branched polysilazane produces denser structure and lower shrinkage. Linear polysilazane (Si:N ~1:1) favors silicon nitride film formation; branched (Si:N ~3:1) favors mixed silicon/silicon nitride or oxide-nitride films.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical - spatial crosslinking via polycondensation with ammonia, forming bonds between two silicon atoms through imide groups with hydrogen release

molecular_weight.measurement_method: vapor pressure osmometry (Osmomat 070, Gonotec GmbH) at 80°C in pyridine; molar weight ranges from 610 ± 80 g/mol (high NH3 flow, 4.0 g/min) to 3000 ± 400 g/mol (low NH3 flow, 0.5 g/min)

backbone_architecture.description: Architecture controlled by ammonia flow rate. High ammonia flow yields short-chain linear polysilazane with retained N-H bonds and Si:N ~1:1. Low ammonia flow yields highly branched polysilazane with few N-H bonds and Si:N approaching 3:1. Spatially crosslinked network structures also described.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: Si3N4 or mixed Si/Si3N4 or oxide-nitride depending on polysilazane structure
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Linear polysilazane (Si:N ~1:1) favors silicon nitride films; branched polysilazane (Si:N ~3:1) yields mixed silicon and silicon nitride; branched polysilazane in humid environment used for oxide or oxide-nitride films

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Films described as having high hardness (9H pencil hardness scale), resistance to high temperatures, abrasion resistance, acid resistance, and resistance to atmospheric air

notes: Synthesis by ammonolysis of dichlorosilane (SiH2Cl2) in pyridine solvent. Intermediate adduct SiH2Cl2·2Py formed. NH4Cl byproduct removed by filtration under N2. Optimal pyridine:dichlorosilane molar ratio is ~2.6:1 (minimum for high yield); ratio of 3:1 recommended for resource efficiency. Polysilazane yield ~65-72% (not quantitative due to dichlorosilane disproportionation). Synthesis conducted at -30°C to avoid high-MW gel formation (at 20°C product was too high MW to filter). Pyridine replaced by dibutyl ether or xylene for storage to prevent gelation and catalyzed condensation. IR absorption at 3380 cm-1 assigned to N-H bonds. Molecular weight data from Table 2 spans 610-3000 g/mol depending on NH3 mass flow (0.5-4.0 g/min). Polymer used for protective coatings with good adhesion to glass, polycarbonate, PMMA, polyethylene, metals, marble, and lacquers.

backbone_architecture.description: Organosilicon polymer (polysilazane) used as ceramic precursor for thin film coatings

notes: This is a 1992 French doctoral thesis (Ecole Centrale de Lyon) by Sandrine Bec, funded by Rhône-Poulenc Chimie, studying micro-pyrolysis of polysilazane precursor ceramic thin films. The work focuses on cracking and delamination mechanisms during pyrolysis of thin coatings. Maximum crack-free coating thickness reported as approximately 0.5 µm. ESCA depth profiling revealed significant oxygen incorporation near the surface, decreasing with depth. Critical thickness for cracking calculated at different pyrolysis temperatures: at 540°C critical thickness ~9 µm (measured ~1.7 µm), at 600°C ~0.4 µm (measured ~1.4 µm), at 650°C ~0.1 µm (measured ~1.1 µm). Pyrolysis temperature range stated as 800–1200°C in text but micro-pyrolysis experiments described at lower temperatures (540–650°C). Hardness range noted as 5.3–14.3 GPa and modulus 64–110 GPa depending on deconvolution hypothesis.

notes: Paper investigates three polysiloxane gel precursors to silicon oxycarbide glasses: MeSiO1.5, PhSiO1.5, and COVS (crosslinked oligovinylsiloxane). Key finding: redistribution reactions involving Si-C and Si-O bond exchange occur above 500-600C, leading to random silicon environment at 1200C. Increasing R group size increases excess carbon in final glass without significantly modifying oxycarbide phase composition. Modifying O/Si ratio of precursor is necessary to modify oxycarbide phase composition. COVS crosslinked by hydrosilation gives high ceramic yield (89%) with O/Si close to 1. Silicon oxycarbide is metastable; decomposes to SiC + SiO2 above 1350C and undergoes carbothermal reduction above ~1500C with CO loss.

Peak-to-peak EPR distances (G): 700°C=9.09, 800°C=7.03, 1050°C=0.88, 1400°C=1.08. Characterization methods: multinuclear solid-state NMR (13C, 29Si, 27Al, 1H MAS), EPR, FT-IR.
