elemental_composition.other_elements: B and N present (boron nitride precursor); exact atomic percentages not reported

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds (both interring and intraring); B-N(methylamino) groups; borazine ring structure

functional_groups.other: methylamino groups attached to boron; borazine rings

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two-step weight loss from 25 to 1000 C observed. First weight loss involves cross-linking/ammonolysis and condensation reactions with large evolution of methylamine. Second weight loss involves mineralization (cleavage of interring B-N bonds, methylamine evolution) and ceramization (cleavage of intraring B-N bonds, ammonia evolution, planar consolidation of BN hexagons). Multiple heating rates used: 0.8, 1.6, 3.2, 6.4, 13, 20 K/min. Activation energies from Kissinger method: 50.0 kJ/mol (first peak) and 121.2 kJ/mol (second peak). Five diffusion-type transport mechanisms identified via Friedman isoconversional method with Ea ranging from 38.73 to 146.64 kJ/mol.

backbone_architecture.description: Borazine-ring-based polymer with methylamino substituents on boron; melt-spinnable; forms highly cross-linked network upon curing

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Polymer converts to boron nitride fibers upon pyrolysis up to 1800 C; planar consolidation of BN hexagons occurs during ceramization step

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Mechanical and structural properties of boron nitride fibers are closely related to controlled achievement of the two-step weight loss from 25 to 1000 C

notes: This paper focuses on kinetic modeling of the polymer-to-ceramic conversion of poly[B-(methylamino)borazine] into boron nitride fibers. It is not a synthesis or characterization paper per se, but a kinetic study using TGA at multiple heating rates (0.8-20 K/min). Five diffusion-controlled mechanisms (D2, D3 alternating) govern the conversion. Kissinger activation energies: 50.0 kJ/mol (first weight loss) and 121.2 kJ/mol (second weight loss). Friedman method Ea values: 38.73, 46.67, 82.73, 124.01, 146.64 kJ/mol for regions 1-5. The polymer is oxygen-free. KiON Ceraset Polysilazane, PCS, and PHPS are mentioned only as commercial examples of preceramic polymers in general context, not as the subject of study.

Oligomeric carbosilanes H-(SiMe2CH2)n-H with MW up to ~1000 g/mol (n<=13) reported. Si/C ratio of product from Me3SiH is 3:1. Redistribution with SiH4 proposed to adjust Si/C ratio. notes: This paper focuses on catalytic synthesis mechanisms rather than polymer characterization or ceramic conversion. Ruthenium complexes of type (PR3)3Ru(H)3(SiR'3) catalyze dehydrogenative coupling of trialkylsilanes at 150 degrees C to produce carbosilanes H-(SiR2CR'2)n-SiR3. Addition of olefin hydrogen acceptors (e.g., neohexene, trimethylsilylethylene, cyclohexene) lowers the required reaction temperature to 80 degrees C. Coupling of alkylgermanes yields oligomeric polygermanes (Ge-Ge) via a demethanative coupling mechanism rather than carbosilanes. Redistribution of groups on silicon competes with dehydrocoupling, especially for secondary and primary silanes. No ceramic yield, pyrolysis conditions, or polymer molecular weight data are reported.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Polymers described as preceramic precursors to silicon carbide; no pyrolysis or ceramic characterization data reported in this text

notes: This report covers catalytic synthesis of polycarbosilane preceramic polymers via dehydrogenative coupling of trialkylsilanes (primarily Me3SiH, Et2SiH) using ruthenium trimethylphosphine complexes (e.g., (PMe3)3RuH3(SiMe3), (arene)Ru(H)2(SiR3)2) and Cp*Rh analogs. Key reactions: (1) dehydrogenative coupling of tertiary alkylsilanes to carbosilanes (Si-C backbone); (2) transfer dehydrocoupling using t-butylethylene as hydrogen acceptor giving Mn ~700-800 Da, ~10 Si atoms, at temperatures as low as 80 C; (3) secondary silanes give polysilanes (Si-Si backbone) rather than carbosilanes, Mn=892, Mw/Mn=1.6, highly branched; (4) polygermanes from demethanative coupling of HGeMe3 using Ru(PMe3)4(GeMe3)2, Mw 10^4-10^5 by SEC/viscometry, 80-90% yield; (5) arylsilane synthesis by cross-coupling of arenes with Et2SiH. No pyrolysis, ceramic yield, or mechanical property data are reported. Mn range of 700-800 reported; midpoint 750 used in molecular_weight field.

The study focuses on boron-nitrogen chemistry, reaction pathways, transition states, and free energy barriers for B-H bond redistribution processes. No preceramic polymer descriptors are applicable.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-vinyl bonding mentioned for polyvinylsilazanes; C-N bonds in polysilylcarbodiimides; sp2-bonded free carbon in SiOC and SiCN ceramics; Si-vinyl and Si-CH3 ratios vary by commercial precursor type

functional_groups.other: Volatile groups -CH3 and -H released as gaseous byproducts during pyrolysis

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis typically occurs between 800 and 1800 degrees C under active or inert atmosphere. Volatile components such as -CH3 and -H are released as gaseous byproducts. SiC remains amorphous at initial pyrolysis at 900 degrees C even after 4-hour hold; crystallinity increases with temperature up to 1650 degrees C. SiOC remains amorphous below 1100 degrees C; SiCN crystallization occurs at higher temperatures. Si3N4 remains amorphous up to approximately 1200 degrees C. Microwave and photothermal heating explored to reduce processing times. Under optimised conditions (1150 degrees C, 1-hour hold) average SiC crystallite size was approximately 3 nm.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal/UV/catalytic - thermal curing below polymer degradation temperature; UV light used when material is sufficiently transparent; catalyst can accelerate thermal curing

backbone_architecture.description: Review covers polycarbosilanes, polysilazanes (including polyvinylsilazanes in cyclic or linear variants), polysiloxanes, polysilsesquioxanes, polyborosilazanes, polysilylcarbodiimides, and polycyclodisilazanes. Backbone architectures vary by polymer class and are not uniformly specified for a single material.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC, Si3N4, SiOC, SiCN, SiBCN, SiHfBCN, SiBON, SiZrC, SiCNO
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiC: amorphous at low pyrolysis temperatures with small crystalline SiC domains; crystallinity increases with temperature up to 1650 degrees C; beta-SiC and alpha-SiC phases noted in fibres. SiOC: amorphous below 1100 degrees C; two phase models proposed - SiCxO2(1-x) or amorphous SiOxC4-x with mixed tetrahedral units and free carbon sp2 bonds; upon crystallization splits into beta-SiC embedded in amorphous SiO2. Si3N4: amorphous to ~1200 degrees C, crystalline Si3N4 dominates above 1600-1700 degrees C with residual beta-SiC. SiCN: single-phase amorphous SiCxNy from vinyl precursors; three-phase amorphous system (Si3N4, alpha-SiC, free carbon) from polysilylcarbodiimides; crystallization at higher temperatures increases beta-SiC.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Multiple mechanical properties reported in tabular data for various PDC systems with different precursors and heat treatments; e.g. SiC tensile strength 2.12 MPa (coating), SiOC bending strength 218.7 MPa, shear strengths 7.9-26.6 MPa for various bonding applications; flexural strengths 30-458 MPa and tensile strengths up to 21.3 MPa for DIW-printed structures depending on precursor and fillers.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC, alpha-SiC, Si3N4 (alpha and crystalline forms), amorphous SiO2, amorphous SiOC, amorphous SiCN, free carbon (sp2)

notes: This is a broad review paper covering multiple preceramic polymer types and PDC systems rather than a single material. No single polymer is characterized in detail; all descriptors reflect information summarized across the review. Polymer types discussed include: polycarbosilanes (SiC precursors), polysilazanes/polyvinylsilazanes (SiCN, Si3N4 precursors), polysiloxanes/polysilsesquioxanes (SiOC precursors), polyborosilazanes (SiBCN precursors), polycyclodisilazanes (Si3N4 precursors), and polysilylcarbodiimides (SiCN precursors). Commercial precursors mentioned include HTT1800, Ceraset, Durazane 1800, SMP-10, SMP-877, SR350, V-PMS, Nuva-Sil 5039, and Polymethylsilesquioxane. Grain size of 3 nm refers specifically to SiC crystallites under optimised pyrolysis at 1150 degrees C with 1-hour hold. Pyrolysis temperatures across systems range from 600 to 1800 degrees C. Ceramic yields of 70-88% noted for some DIW-printed systems.

polymer_name: PCS (polycarbosilane precursor for SiC-based ceramic fibers)

SiNHSi: 8%, 33%, 62% at those temperatures respectively. Pyrolysis temperatures studied range from 800 to 1600°C for PCS filaments.

notes: This is a French doctoral thesis (1989) by Eric Bouillon on pyrolysis of organosilicon precursors for SiC-based ceramic fibers. The primary precursor studied is a polycarbosilane (PCS) analogous to the precursor for Nicalon fibers. Functional model polycarbosilanes (Si-H, Si-Si, SiNHSi, SiNHMe, SiNMe2, SiOSi, SiC4Si, SiC2ArC2Si) are also studied as model compounds. Elemental composition of pyrolysis residues (atomic %): at 800°C: Si~31, C~33, N~18, O~18; at 1000°C: Si~31, C~44, N~13, O~12; at 1400°C: Si~34, C~52, N~12, O~2 (from one table for PCS). XPS/ESCA analyses provide surface composition data at multiple pyrolysis temperatures. Ceramic yield of model precursors (wt%): Si-H: 5% (or 85% for Si-H*), Si-Si(Na,s): 11%, Si-Si(Na,i): 77%, Si-Si(K,s): 43%, Si-Si(K,i): 59%, SiNHSi: 37%, SiNHMe: 24%, SiNMe2: 33%, SiOSi: 54%, SiC4Si: 14%, SiC2ArC2Si: 24%. Nicalon NLP-101 fiber: Si 60 wt%, C 27 wt%, O 13 wt%; NLM-102: Si 56 wt%, C 35 wt%, O 9 wt%.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yield strongly dependent on vinyl group content: I (no vinyl, SiH2 end groups) 12%; II (no vinyl, SiH3 end groups) 30% with one terminal vinyl; III (two terminal vinyl groups) 56%; IV (Si-H and Si-vinyl along chain) 60%. Exotherm at ~200 °C observed by DTA/DSC for vinyl-containing polymers (III, IV) attributed to hydrosilylation crosslinking; absent for polymer II (no vinyl groups). notes: Paper reports four poly(carbosilane) oligomers (I-IV) prepared by catalytic hydrosilylation polymerization of chlorosilane monomers followed by LiAlH4 reduction. Key finding: ceramic yield increases with vinyl group content due to in-situ hydrosilylation crosslinking at ~200 °C during pyrolysis. Polymer II (no vinyl) alone gives 30% yield but when mixed with IV (2.5:1 ratio) gives 59% yield, demonstrating crosslinking efficiency. Rhone-Poulenc Pt catalyst (H2PtCl6 in 2-ethylhexanol, ~16 mmol/L Pt) used for hydrosilylation. Pyrolysis performed at 5 °C/min to 1400 °C, 2 h hold, under N2 in Al2O3 boat. SiH/Si(vinyl) ratios in Table I: I=infinity (no vinyl), II=21, III=10, IV=1, mix=4.5. All polymers are colorless to yellow oils or pastes, air sensitive, stable under N2 at -15 °C for months. IR bands noted: SiH ~2100-2205 cm-1, SiCH=CH2 at 3050, 3004, 1910, 1592 cm-1, SiCH2CH2Si at 1140 cm-1.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Cured (pre-pyrolysis) Shore A hardness of 70A indicating elastomeric properties. notes: SMP-10 self-condensation via hydrosilylation begins at 180C; three DSC exothermic curing peaks at ~120C, ~200C, ~230C. B-staging performed at room temperature and pressure using Pt-catalyzed hydrosilylation. Crosslinker is 1,4-dimethyldisilethane (Gelest SID4235) at 6 mol% (upper limit before precipitate formation). Catalyst is Pt-cyclovinylmethyl-siloxane (Gelest SIP6832.2) diluted 2:1 in toluene. DSC heating rate 3C/min to 250C. Chalk-Harrod mechanism considered most plausible for hydrosilylation; side reactions and isomers observed (shoulder at 1645 cm-1 for 9.5 and 12.5% Pt). Off-gassing attributed to hydrogen gas from hydrolysis of SiH by trace water in presence of Karstedt catalyst. FTIR key peaks: Si-C at 747 cm-1, Si-H stretch at 2110 cm-1, Si-H bend at 930 cm-1, allyl C=C at 1630 cm-1, allyl C-H at 3077 cm-1. notes: This is a French-language thesis on additive manufacturing (robocasting and FDM) of SiC-based ceramics via the Polymer-Derived Ceramics (PDC) route. Two main preceramic polymers are studied: SMP-10 (allylhydridopolycarbosilane, liquid at RT, density 0.998 g/cm3, viscosity 80-100 mPa.s at 20°C) and SMP-730 (solid thermoplastic polycarbosilane at RT, density 1.0 g/cm3). Chemical modification of SMP-10 with borane agents (BDMS and BDMA) introduces boron into the polymer to produce SiBC ceramics. SMP-730 is thermally pre-treated at 100-140°C to adjust viscosity for FDM processing. Ceramic formulations include SiBC30 powder fillers and h-BN particles. Pyrolysis performed at 1000°C under argon; high-temperature sintering up to 2000°C and SPS sintering also investigated. Specific quantitative elemental compositions and ceramic yields present in tables (Tableaux III-1, III-4, III-7, IV-2, IV-3, V-1, V-2, V-5) but numerical values not fully extracted in the provided text segments.

notes: Paper is written in Polish and describes the Yajima process for SiC fiber production. Precursor polymer is polycarbosilane (PCS) obtained by rearrangement of polydimethylsilane at 400-500°C in autoclave for several hours (e.g. 470°C, 14h), followed by removal of volatiles at 280°C/1.3 hPa. Fibers are melt-spun at 350°C with diameter 8-20 micrometers. Paper also discusses polysilazanes as precursors for Si3N4 but notes difficulty in obtaining suitable linear polymers due to thermodynamic stability of cyclosilazane rings. Ceramic yield of 60% is estimated from the statement that ~40% volatiles form during pyrolysis. The text is a review article covering preceramic polymers broadly, with PCS/Yajima process as the primary detailed example.

notes: Study reports a 'one-step' atmospheric-pressure pyrolysis synthesis of PACS from PDMS and Al(AcAc)3 in xylene solvent at 450°C under N2, as an alternative to the traditional 'two-step' route. Five samples prepared: PCS (0% Al(AcAc)3), PACS-1 (1%), PACS-2 (2%), PACS-3 (3%), PACS-4 (4%). PACS-2 identified as optimal with highest Mn (4302), highest softening point (192.5°C), and highest ceramic yield (67.09% at 1000°C). Al content tunable from 0.07-0.47 wt% and Mn from 1909-4302 by varying Al(AcAc)3 loading. Reaction mechanism: PDMS undergoes Kumada rearrangement at 450°C (Si-Si → Si-C-Si + Si-H), then Si-H reacts with Al(AcAc)3 to form Si-O-Al containing PACS. 27Al NMR shows Al in AlOx coordination (x=4,5,6) with hexacoordinate dominant. XPS confirms C-O, C-C/C-H, C-Si bonds for carbon; Si-O/Si-OAl, Si-C, Si-H for silicon; O-Si, O-C, O-Al for oxygen. Softening points: PCS=170.4°C, PACS-1=175.3°C, PACS-2=192.5°C, PACS-3=162.8°C, PACS-4=163.0°C. Ceramic yields at 1000°C: PCS=64.34%, PACS-1=65.33%, PACS-2=67.09%, PACS-3=62.68%, PACS-4=59.28%. Air infusibilization of PACS-2 at 180°C (1°C/min, hold 1h) raises ceramic yield to 84.32%. Melt spinning at 330°C, spinneret diameter 0.25 mm, pressure 0.4 MPa.

Kamal-Sourour autocatalytic model parameters for crosslinking: ko1=1.66e13 s-1, Ea1=124.73 kJ/mol, m=2.54; ko2=2.38e16 s-1, Ea2=143.12 kJ/mol, n=1.11. Principal crosslinking reactions include hydrosilylation, vinyl polyaddition (promoted by DCPO), dehydrogenation (Si-H/N-H), and transamination. DSC heating rate for compound kinetics study: 2 K/min. notes: Paper focuses on in situ monitoring of hyperbranched polycarbosilane (hb-PCS) synthesis using a novel coupled instrumentation platform: dynamic rheometer + FTIR spectrometer + fibered Raman spectrometer + SEC-MALS. FDM approach used PLA scaffolds filled by dip-coating with preceramic polymer solutions, then pyrolyzed. conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous up to 1700 C (very broad diffraction line). At 1800 C: alpha-Si3N4, beta-Si3N4, beta-SiC identified by XRD. h-BN not detected (BN remains amorphous).

notes: Polymer synthesized by reacting perhydrosilazane (Mn ~900, average MW) with tris(dimethylamino)borane in pyridine at 120 C for 3h in autoclave with 10g NH3. NH3 atmosphere is required for high B incorporation via transamination. Reaction in absence of NH3 yields low B content product (Si/B = 3.8 vs 1.2 with NH3). Polymer obtained as white powder after solvent removal (50-70 C, 400-800 Pa); yield 19.6g. 29Si NMR shows HSiN3/H2SiN2 (-37 ppm) and H3SiN (-51 ppm) units; no Si-O or Si-B bonds detected. 11B NMR single peak at 27 ppm assigned to BN3 in substituted borazine. Borazine ring confirmed by IR band at 700 cm-1 (N3B3N3 skeletal vibration). Si/B ratio preserved through pyrolysis indicating no boron volatilization. Elemental mass% of untreated polymer: Si 30.2, N 9.9, H 0.8, B 5.7, C 35.8 (includes solvent contribution), O 17.6 (from table). Elemental mass% of 1700C pyrolyzed sample: Si 40.1, N 13.2, H 1.1, B 5.6, C 0.7, O 39.3 — note O value appears anomalously high for a low-oxygen product; text states 1.1 mass% O in pyrolysis product, suggesting possible table transcription error. Further heating schedule: 1500 and 1700 C in carbon furnace, BN boats, 10 C/min heating rate, 1h hold.
source: FUNAYAMA_1996_Synthesis_and_Pyrolysis_of_Polyborosilazane_with_Low_Oxygen

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental data given in wt% not atomic%: Si=42.7, C=35.4, O=15.5, N<0.1, H=6.3 for original PCS fiber; ammoniated variants at 673K, 873K, 1073K also tabulated

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-N-Si asymmetric stretch observed at 900 cm-1 after ammoniating at 600C and above; Si2N2O phase identified by 29Si MAS-NMR

functional_groups.other: NH2 radicals involved in nucleophilic displacement reactions

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three-stage nitrodation process: stage 1 (RT to 50C) weight gain ~8.0wt% due to physical absorption and surface reactions; stage 2 (50-560C) slow weight loss ~7.5wt% due to NH3 desorption, net gain 0.5wt%; stage 3 (560-1000C) weight loss up to 20wt% due to PCS decomposition and evolution of CH4, H2. Heating to 800C at 0.5C/min, then to 1250C at 3.5C/min, held 1hr at 1250C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (air crosslinking at 200C for 4-10 hours prior to ammoniating); NH3 crosslinking at 400C also noted as possible

backbone_architecture.description: Normal repeating unit is -(-CH3HSiCH2-)x- but actual structure is complexly branched with CH3HSiCH2 and Me2SiCH2 functionality; Si-C backbone

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: 29Si MAS-NMR of pyrolyzed fiber shows peaks at -44.4 ppm (SiN4), -51.5 ppm (beta-Si3N4), and -64 ppm (Si2N2O), indicating Si bonded to nitrogen phases in final ceramic

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Average tensile strength >1.60 GPa; some fibers reached up to 3.0 GPa. Tested at room temperature per Japanese industrial standard R 7601-1986.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-Si3N4 and Si2N2O identified by 29Si MAS-NMR

notes: Paper describes ammoniating of PCS fibers to produce Si-C-O-N ceramic fibers. Ammoniating carried out at 400-800C for 6-12hr with NH3 flow of 20-50ml/min. Nitrogen content increases with ammoniating temperature (2.1wt% at 360C, 12.5wt% at 600C), NH3 concentration (2.0wt% at 10vol% NH3, 3.2wt% at 100vol% NH3), and time. Mechanism: nucleophilic displacement of H (via Si-H, lowest bond strength 315 kJ/mol) at lower temperatures (~400C) and C (via Si-CH3) at higher temperatures (>600C) by NH2 radicals. Elemental wt% data given in table for original PCS and ammoniated variants; not converted to atomic%. Si bond strengths: Si-H=315 kJ/mol, Si-C=319.2 kJ/mol. Strength range 1600-3000 MPa; midpoint ~2300 MPa used for notes.
source: Fan_1999_PREPARATION_OF_SICON_CERAMIC_FIBERS_FROM_POLYCARBOSILANE_I_A

elemental_composition.other_elements: Empirical formula B3N3H4 (ideal poly(borazylene)); crude material B2.7N3.0H3.0, purified material B3.1N3.0H2.7 by elemental analysis

bonding_structure.other_bonds: N-B linkages between borazine rings; B-N bonds within borazine rings; 11B NMR broad peak at 31 ppm in borazine region consistent with borazine-type B-N bonding

functional_groups.other: B-H and N-H groups implied by dehydrocoupling mechanism; linked borazine ring units

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Initial ~2% weight loss between 125 and 300 °C attributed to polymer cross-linking, followed by gradual ~4% loss ending by 1100 °C. Total weight loss ~6%, ceramic yield 85-93% (theoretical 95%).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - cross-linking inferred from initial weight loss at 125-300 °C during pyrolysis

molecular_weight.measurement_method: SEC/LALLS (size exclusion chromatography / low-angle laser light scattering)

backbone_architecture.description: Proposed linked borazine rings analogous to poly(phenylene); branched-chain or partially cross-linked structure inferred from elemental analysis and SEC/LALLS chromatograms showing high molecular weight early-eluting components and heterogeneous UV absorbance. Possible fused-ring structures also noted. N-B inter-ring linkages proposed.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: White boron nitride powders of excellent purity; diffuse reflectance IR consistent with BN; X-ray powder diffraction characteristic of turbostratic boron nitride

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: turbostratic boron nitride

notes: Polymer is synthesized by thermally induced dehydrocoupling of liquid borazine (B3N3H6) in vacuo at 70 °C for ~48 h. Yield of crude material: 90%; reprecipitated (glyme/pentane): 61%. Ceramic yield range 85-93%; theoretical ceramic yield 95%. Density of BN product 1.7-1.9 g/mL. Crude material Mw=4000, Mn=1400, PDI=2.86; reprecipitated material Mw=7600, Mn=3400, PDI=2.23. Polymer is soluble in THF and glyme, stable as solid under vacuum at room temperature, but sensitive to moisture. This is a boron-nitrogen ceramic precursor polymer, not a silicon-based preceramic polymer; many silicon-related fields are not applicable.
source: Fazen_1990_Thermally_induced_borazine_dehydropolymerization_reactions_S

elemental_composition.other_elements: B: ~40-42 wt%, N: ~52-55 wt%, H: ~3.4-3.9 wt%, C: <0.5 wt% (for parent polymer I); empirical formula range B3N3H3.4 to B3N3H3.9 for crude polymers, B3N3H2.65 to B3N3H3.8 for precipitated samples, average B3N3.1H3.6

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds within retained borazine ring structure; B-H bonds present; fused borazine ring linkages (B-N inter-ring); polymer converts to BN via two-dimensional cross-linking

functional_groups.other: B-H hydride groups; N-H groups; alkyl-substituted variants (ethyl, propyl) also synthesized

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yields range 84-93% (midpoint ~88.5%) at temperatures 900-1500 °C under Ar or NH3. Chemical yields 89-99%. TGA performed under argon at 10 °C/min. TGA/MS used to analyze evolved gases. Conversion to BN via two-dimensional cross-linking mechanism. Alkyl-substituted polymers show inhibited cross-linking with initial weight losses at slightly higher temperatures.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (two-dimensional cross-linking during pyrolysis); transition-metal catalyzed hydroboration for alkylated variants

molecular_weight.measurement_method: SEC/VISC (viscometric detection) for Mn; SEC/LALLS/UV for Mw. SEC/VISC gives Mn 500-900 g/mol; SEC/LALLS gives Mw 3000-8000 g/mol. Individual polymer I: Mn=506, Mw=1467, PDI=2.90 (SEC/VISC).

backbone_architecture.description: Complex structure with linear, branched-chain, and fused-cyclic segments analogous to organic polyphenylenes. Borazine rings linked by B-N bonds. Structural units include diborazine (1,1'-B6N6H10) and borazanaphthalene (B5N5H8) as models. Layered structure in solid state suggested by powder XRD.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis under Ar or NH3 at 900-1500 °C gives BN with B:N ratio ~1.0:1.0-1.06. d(002) spacing 3.39-3.63 Å. Density of ceramic 1.72-2.04 g/mL. H and C <0.5 wt% in final ceramic. Polymer solid state density 1.5-1.6 g/cm3.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Layered structure suggested by powder XRD for polymer; hexagonal BN after pyrolysis with d(002) = 3.39-3.63 Å

notes: This paper describes polyborazylene, a boron-nitrogen preceramic polymer (not silicon-based). Polymer synthesized by dehydropolymerization of borazine (B3N3H6) at 70-110 °C in vacuo. Isolated as white solid soluble in ethers (glyme, THF). Yield 81-91%. Multiple polymer variants synthesized (I-XIV) with varying substituents and conditions. Alkyl-substituted polyborazylenes (X-XIV) show increased organic solubility. Polymer used to coat carbon and ceramic fiber bundles producing BN coatings confirmed by AES. X-ray structures of diborazine and borazanaphthalene reported as structural models. Pyrolysis range midpoint for ceramic yield: range 84-93%, midpoint ~88.5%; temperature range 900-1500°C. SEC/VISC Mn range 500-900 g/mol; SEC/LALLS Mw range 3000-8000 g/mol.
source: Fazen_1995_Synthesis_Properties_and_Ceramic_Conversion_Reactions_of_Pol

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Polymer converts to amorphous SiO2 via thermo-oxidative decomposition

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Silica yield of 84 wt% after thermal decomposition in air. Cross-linking step performed first at 350 °C (0.5 °C/min, 1 h hold), then ceramization at 600 °C (same heating rate and hold time). Low temperature selected to prevent CaCO3 decomposition while converting silicone to amorphous silica.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - cross-linked at 350 °C

backbone_architecture.description: Commercial polymethylsiloxane (SILRES MK, Wacker-Chemie); described as a solid preceramic polymer dissolved in isopropanol for ink formulation

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD after ceramization at 600 °C showed only calcite (CaCO3, PDF#85-0849) with no other crystalline peaks; silica is amorphous. Final composite is 35 wt% SiO2 and 65 wt% CaCO3. Fumed silica (Aerosil R106) contributed 10 wt% of the silica fraction.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Compressive strength: t-1 design = 2.9 ± 0.7 MPa (open porosity 64%); t-2 design = 5.5 ± 0.3 MPa (open porosity 56%). Midpoint 4.2 MPa noted in notes field.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Calcite (CaCO3, PDF#85-0849); silica is amorphous (no crystalline silica peaks observed)

notes: Polymer used as preceramic binder in a composite ink with CaCO3 filler for direct ink writing (robocasting) of bone scaffolds. Final ceramic is 'silica-bonded calcite' (35 wt% SiO2 / 65 wt% CaCO3). Fumed silica (Aerosil R106) added to improve rheology of the ink. Bulk density: t-1 = 0.93 g/cm³, t-2 = 1.07 g/cm³; skeletal density: t-1 = 2.56 g/cm³, t-2 = 2.43 g/cm³; true density both ~2.57 g/cm³. Open porosity range 56-64% (midpoint 60% used for porosity_pct). Compressive strength range 2.9-5.5 MPa (midpoint 4.2 MPa used for strength_MPa). Scaffolds showed in vitro bioactivity (HCA formation in SBF) and biocompatibility with ST-2 bone marrow stromal cells.
source: Fiocco_2017_Direct_ink_writing_of_silicabonded_calcite_scaffolds_from_pr

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Vinyl groups present in HTTS; five-membered carbosilazane rings and bridging linear carbosilazane units in ABSE

functional_groups.other: N-H groups; crosslinking via vinyl polymerization, hydrosilylation, dehydrocoupling, and transamination

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three well-defined steps during pyrolysis: no mass loss up to 250°C; cross-linking and slight mass loss at ~250°C due to volatile oligomers and ammonia; highest mass loss between 300-700°C with transformation to amorphous SiCN ceramics and release of CH4; above 700°C almost no mass loss but amorphous structure rearranges; crystallization above 1400°C. Ceramic yields: ABSE 63%, ML33S 70%, HTTS 79%.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - via vinyl polymerization, hydrosilylation between Si-H and Si-Vinyl groups, dehydrocoupling between Si-H and N-H groups, and transamination; also catalytic cross-linking used in synthesis of ML33S and HTTS

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC using DMAc as eluent, calibrated with polystyrene standards; ABSE: Mw=2174 g/mol, PDI=3.0; ML33S: Mw=9937 g/mol, PDI=4.3; HTTS: Mw=8010 g/mol, PDI=9.4

backbone_architecture.description: Non-linear structure composed of a mixture of branched and cyclic structures. ABSE contains five-membered carbosilazane rings and bridging linear carbosilazane units. ML33S and HTTS are copolymers derived from selective cross-linking of liquid oligosilazanes (ML33 and HTT1800).

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiCN ceramics formed after pyrolysis between 300-700°C; amorphous structure rearranges above 700°C; crystallization begins above 1400°C

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Storage modulus G' and loss modulus G'' measured in oscillatory shear from 75-150°C; loss modulus dominant over storage modulus for ABSE and ML33S across full temperature range; HTTS shows crossover (G' exceeds G'') at ~170°C due to crosslinking

notes: Paper focuses on linear viscoelastic properties of three polysilazanes (ABSE, ML33S, HTTS) using oscillatory rheometry and time-temperature superposition (WLF equation). Glass transition temperatures: ABSE 59°C, ML33S 65°C, HTTS 73°C. All are colourless, brittle, meltable solids sensitive to moisture/air. Measurements performed in inert (nitrogen) atmosphere. ABSE synthesized by hydrosilylation of dichloromethylvinylsilane and dichloromethylsilane followed by ammonolysis. ML33S and HTTS derived from commercial oligosilazanes ML33 and HTT1800 (Clariant/AZ-EM). Ceramic yields from table: ABSE 63%, ML33S 70%, HTTS 79% after pyrolysis to 1400°C. Molecular weights from GPC (Mw): ABSE 2174 g/mol (PDI 3.0), ML33S 9937 g/mol (PDI 4.3), HTTS 8010 g/mol (PDI 9.4). TGA heating rate 5 K/min in nitrogen to 1400°C. DSC performed in nitrogen, heating rate 5 K/min.
source: Flores_2015_Rheological_behaviour_of_tailored_polysilazane_melts_for_the

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si backbone bonds confirmed by 29Si NMR; Si-N stretches observed by ATR-FTIR at 912 cm-1 (950-920 cm-1 range reported); possible Si-N(R)H centers from partial ring-opening not excluded; after air exposure, Si-O stretch at 1022 cm-1 and O-H/N-H at 3370 cm-1 appear

functional_groups.other: N-allyl group (allylamine-derived substituent, CH2CH=CH2 on nitrogen); olefin C=C stretch at 1625 cm-1 confirmed by ATR-FTIR

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: Speculated crosslinking in P2 (lithium-promoted) arising from ring-opening and interchain recombination during Wurtz coupling; evidenced by decreased solubility and additional 29Si NMR features relative to P1

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with UV detection at 254 nm, THF eluent, polystyrene standards; values shown are for highest Mw polymer P2 (Table 2, entry 8); P1 (Table 1, entry 5): Mn=1310, Mw=4470, PDI=3.41

backbone_architecture.description: Poly(cyclosilazane) based on a six-membered Si5N heterocyclic repeat unit (five Si atoms and one N atom in the ring) connected via Si-Si bonds through Wurtz reductive polymerization; P2 may be crosslinked network based on NMR and solubility evidence; polymer is atactic with possible mixture of Si-N(R)-Si and Si-N(R)H centers

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: P1 (Na-promoted) is a light-yellow gel; P2 (Li-promoted) is a light-yellow powder; P1 soluble in Et2O, CHCl3, CH2Cl2, THF; P2 soluble in THF and sparingly soluble in CHCl3

notes: Monomer Si5N is a chloro-functionalized six-membered cyclosilazane (Si5N ring) synthesized in 82% overall yield, isolated as 70:30 trans:cis diastereomeric mixture (HRMS: [M+] C11H30Si5NCl2 = 386.0602). Reductive Wurtz polymerization performed with Na (toluene, 110°C or THF, rt) or Li (THF, rt). Na-promoted polymer P1: Mn=1310, Mw=4470, PDI=3.41 (THF, 72h). Li-promoted polymer P2 (best): Mn=1930, Mw=6920, PDI=3.59 (2.2 equiv Li, THF, 6h). All molecular weights are relative to polystyrene standards by GPC. 29Si DEPT NMR: resonances -40 to -55 ppm assigned to Si-Si2 signals; 0 to -15 ppm assigned to Si-N features. Optical characterization consistent with extended sigma-conjugation upon polymerization. Monomer Si5N GPC: Mn=441, Mw=523, PDI=1.19. P2 is hydrolytically sensitive; after one week air exposure, allylamine fragment lost and Si-O/O-H bonds appear by ATR-FTIR. Si5N elemental analysis: calcd C 34.17, H 7.56, N 3.62; found C 33.59, H 7.59, N 3.69 (low C attributed to SiC formation during combustion).
source: Folster_2020_Reductive_halocyclosilazane_polymerization

polymer_name: polyborosilazane (derived from perhydropolysilazane and trimethyl borate)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental composition given in wt%: Si=46.00, N=23.40, B=6.30, O=10.30, C=7.10, H=6.80. Empirical atomic ratio: SiN1.35B0.09C0.36H4.1O0.D9 (as reported, some values unclear in text)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds (IR ~1370 cm-1, 11B NMR 22 ppm), B-O bonds (IR ~1350 cm-1, 11B NMR 15 ppm), C-H bonds (IR ~2800 cm-1), Si-O-B linkages, ternary BN2O and BNO2 species identified by XPS in pyrolyzed material

functional_groups.other: Methoxy groups (OCH3) identified by 1H NMR at 3.5 ppm and 13C MAS-NMR at 53 ppm; HSiON2 units identified by 29Si NMR at -43 ppm; structural units: HSiN3, H2SiN2, H3SiN, HSiON2, N-B(OCH3)2, NB(OCH3)N

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: anhydrous ammonia (initial pyrolysis to 1000°C); nitrogen (subsequent annealing 1000–1800°C)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Weight loss starts ~100°C, complete ~800°C in ammonia. Two regions: below 200°C ~10% loss from residual solvent; 200–800°C ~10% gradual loss from organic bond breaking. No weight gain (unlike perhydropolysilazane which gains weight from nitridation). Weight residue of polyborosilazane constant up to 1700°C in N2 after 1000°C NH3 pre-pyrolysis; boron doping suppresses SiO volatility and Si3N4 decomposition. Heating rate for annealing step explicitly stated as 10°C/min; initial pyrolysis rate inferred as ~5°C/min (room temperature to 1000°C in 200 min).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (thermosetting; does not melt on heating in N2 up to 500°C)

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC using chloroform as solvent, polystyrene standards

backbone_architecture.description: Polymer consisting mainly of HSiN3, H2SiN2, H3SiN, and HSiON2 silicon units interconnected via Si-N-Si and Si-O-B linkages, with boron incorporated via B-N and B-O bonds; thermosetting character implies crosslinked network. 29Si NMR ratio HSiN3:H2SiN2:H3SiN:HSiON2 ~ 30:13:6:1.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous silicon nitride (Si3N4) up to 1700°C; crystalline alpha-Si3N4 and beta-Si3N4 at 1800°C
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis at 1000°C in NH3 yields amorphous product. Remains amorphous after annealing to 1700°C in N2. Crystallization to alpha-Si3N4 and beta-Si3N4 occurs at 1800°C under N2. IR at 900 cm-1 shows absence of resolved features confirming amorphous nature through 1700°C. Boron and oxygen doping inhibit crystallization and SiO volatility.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: alpha-Si3N4 and beta-Si3N4 identified by XRD after annealing at 1800°C in N2

notes: Perhydropolysilazane (precursor): Mn ~2800 g/mol, wt% composition Si=59.80, N=34.80, O=0.80, C=0.40, H=4.20, B=0.00. Polyborosilazane synthesized by reacting perhydropolysilazane with trimethyl borate in pyridine at 120°C for 3 h. Ceramic yield stated as above 80 wt%. After 1000°C NH3 pyrolysis: Si=50.20, N=30.90, B=7.10, O=10.40, C=0.60, H=0.80 wt%. After 1700°C N2 anneal: Si=50.10, N=32.80, B=7.00, O=9.50, C=0.40, H=0.10 wt%. After 1800°C N2 anneal: Si=55.80, N=36.40, B=7.30, O=0.30, C=0.20, H=ND wt%. XPS of 1700°C-annealed sample: Si 2p at ~101.4 eV (Si-N) and ~103.5 eV (Si-O); B 1s at ~190.4 eV (B-N), 193.8 eV (B-O), 191.5 eV and 192.7 eV (ternary BN2O, BNO2 species). Polymer soluble in toluene, THF, chloroform. Annealing hold time 1 h at each temperature. Pyrolysis rate to 1000°C: room temperature to 1000°C in 200 min (~5°C/min). O/B atomic ratio in polyborosilazane is 1.09.
source: Funayama_1993_Synthesis_of_a_Polyborosilazane_and_Its_Conversion_into_Inor

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds, B-O bonds, B-H bonds (formed transiently during pyrolysis), Si-O-Si, Si-O-B, Si-N-B, B-N-B, B-O-B networks; OCH3 (methoxy) pendant groups present in polymer

functional_groups.other: methoxy groups (OCH3) on boron and silicon; structural units HSiN3, H2SiN2, H3SiN, HSi(OCH3)N2, NB(OCH3)2, NB(OCH3)N

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three regions observed in TGA under NH3: (1) below 400C, ~12% weight loss due to residual solvent evaporation; (2) 400-600C, ~3% weight gain due to nitridation via reaction of Si-H with NH3, partially offset by decomposition; (3) 600-1000C, ~2% slight weight loss. Ceramic yield ~90% at 1000C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - three-dimensional Si-N-Si, Si-O-Si, Si-O-B network formed during pyrolysis in anhydrous ammonia; no separate curing process required

backbone_architecture.description: Polyborosilazane derived from perhydropolysilazane and trimethyl borate (Si/B = 3 atomic ratio). Polymer consists mainly of structural units HSiN3, H2SiN2, H3SiN, HSi(OCH3)N2, NB(OCH3)2, and NB(OCH3)N. Converts to three-dimensional Si-N-Si, Si-O-Si, Si-O-B network upon pyrolysis without a separate curing step.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramic at 1200C is an amorphous hydrogenated solid composed of SiN4-xOx (x=0,1,2,3) and BN3-yOy (y=0,1), cross-linked through Si-N-Si, Si-N-B, Si-O-Si, Si-O-B, B-N-B, and B-O-B bonds. XRD shows broad amorphous peak at 2theta=20-40 degrees for 600 and 1200C pyrolysed samples, attributed to amorphous silicon nitride character.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous; broad XRD peak at 2theta ~20-40 degrees observed for 600 and 1200C pyrolysed samples attributed to amorphous silicon nitride-like structure

notes: Polymer synthesized by reacting perhydropolysilazane with trimethyl borate (Si/B=3 atomic ratio) in pyridine at 120C for 3h in autoclave, yielding white powder. Elemental composition values in the JSON are wt%, not atomic%. Empirical ratios given in text: polymer SiB0.36N0.99O0.42C0.40H4.86; 1200C ceramic SiB0.38N1.21O0.38C0.03H0.68. Free spin density increases from no detectable spins in polymer to 6e17 spins/g in 1200C pyrolysed sample (ESR). Borazine and trimethoxysilane detected as volatile byproducts during 400-600C pyrolysis. CH4 detected 400-800C; H2 detected throughout. Paper focuses on pyrolysis mechanism in anhydrous ammonia atmosphere. Intended application as precursor for continuous ceramic fibres for automotive ceramic gas turbine program.

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental compositions given in wt% for multiple PCS/PHPS ratios. For PCS/PHPS=1/4: Si 65.60 wt%, N 7.81 wt%, Ti 1.14 wt%, O 1.56 wt%, C 23.20 wt%, H 0.70 wt%. For PCS/PHPS=1/9: Si 64.30 wt%, N 14.00 wt%, Ti 1.15 wt%, O 1.65 wt%, C 18.20 wt%, H 0.70 wt%.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si (1020 cm-1), Si-O-Ti bonds suggested, C-H bonds (2900, 2950 cm-1), OCH2 groups (3.75 ppm), SiH2 and SiH3 groups identified by 29Si NMR at -37 and -51 ppm

functional_groups.other: OCH2 (n-butoxide residue), N-H groups from PHPS, Si-CH2-Si bridging units

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA of PCS/PHPS=1/1 copolymer in nitrogen: weight loss starts ~100°C, complete ~800°C. Three regions: below 300°C ~2% loss (titanium n-butoxide decomposition); 300-550°C ~10% loss (PHPS and PCS block decomposition); 550-800°C ~5% loss (PCS block decomposition, H2 and CH4 evolution). Pyrolysis to 1000°C yields ~80 wt% ceramic yield. Heating rate of 10°C/min calculated from room temperature to 1500°C in 150 min.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - dehydrogenation of Si-H and N-H bonds; titanium n-butoxide (Si/Ti > 100/1) and PHPS (PCS/PHPS > 4/1 silicon ratio) both required for thermosetting behavior

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with chloroform solvent, polystyrene standards (value given for starting PCS only)

backbone_architecture.description: Block copolymer of polycarbosilane (PCS) and perhydropolysilazane (PHPS) linked through titanium n-butoxide bridges, forming a thermosetting network. Si-O-Ti bonds suggested as linkage between PCS and PHPS blocks. Crosslinked via dehydrogenation of Si-H and N-H bonds upon heating.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Main phase at 1500°C in nitrogen is small crystallite β-SiC. PCS/PHPS=1/1 yields β-SiC of small crystallite size. notes: Study investigates copolymers of polycarbosilane (PCS, Shin-Etsu Chemical, Mn=1300) with perhydropolysilazane (PHPS) using titanium n-butoxide as compatibilizer/crosslinking promoter. notes: This paper is primarily a thermodynamic modelling study of Si-C-N polymer-derived ceramics (SiCN PDC), not a polymer synthesis paper. molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with Wyatt Dawn Heleos-II detector, PS standards, THF eluent at 1 mL/min, 30°C. Note: values shown are for PACS-6. LPCS: Mn=1090, Mw=1880, PDI=1.72; PACS-2: Mn=2420, Mw=5750, PDI=2.37; PACS-3: Mn=2970, Mw=5220, PDI=1.76; PACS-8: Mn=4110, Mw=7420, PDI=1.81; PACS-10: Mn=7050, Mw=11000, PDI=1.56

backbone_architecture.description: LPCS is a polycarbosilane with SiC4 and SiC3H units and short -[-Si-]n- segments; PACS formed by crosslinking LPCS with Al(acac)3 through Si-H bond consumption, incorporating Al-O coordination sites (AlO4, AlO5, AlO6). GPC shows bimodal distribution for all PACS precursors. Softening points range from 189°C (PACS-2) to 227°C (PACS-10).

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Si-C-Al-O-6 fiber: XRD and TEM/SAED confirm 3C-SiC (JCPDS 29-1129) with (111), (220), (311) diffraction planes. Low degree of crystallization; sample composed of small SiC crystals and amorphous phases. Elemental composition of Si-C-Al-O-6 fiber: Si 54.11 wt%, C 33.73 wt%, O 8.73 wt%, Al 1.32 wt%; empirical formula SiC1.46O0.28Al0.03. Elements uniformly distributed.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Values reported for Si-C-Al-O-6 fiber (from PACS-6 precursor, pyrolyzed to 1300°C under nitrogen). Average diameter 11.6 μm. Single-filament tensile test, gauge length 25 mm, average of 25 filaments.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: 3C-SiC: diffraction peaks at 2θ = 35.6° (111), 60° (220), 72° (311)

notes: Paper reports a series of melt-spinnable polyaluminocarbosilane (PACS) precursors synthesized by reacting low-softening-point polycarbosilane (LPCS) with varying mass ratios (2, 3, 6, 8, 10 wt%) of Al(acac)3. LPCS was prepared by pyrolysis of polydimethylsilane (PDMS) at 420°C for 10h. PACS synthesis conducted at 310°C for 5h then 400°C for 5h under nitrogen. PACS-6 selected as representative for fiber fabrication (melt-spin at 300°C/N2, cure at 180°C/air, pyrolyze to 1300°C/N2). Si-H content decreases and molecular weight increases with increasing Al(acac)3 ratio. 29Si NMR: SiC4 at 0 ppm, SiC3H at -16 ppm, -[-Si-]n- at ~-40 ppm. 27Al MAS NMR confirms AlO4, AlO5, AlO6 coordination in PACS. Ceramic yield midpoint noted as PACS-6 value; full range: 54.8-60.5% for PACS series.
source: Gou_2016_Facile_synthesis_of_melt_spinnable_polyaluminocarbosilane_us

elemental_composition.other_elements: Fe present (ferrocenyl groups); ceramic microsphere EDS: Fe 9.8%, Si 32.5%, C 50.0%, O 7.8% (these are ceramic product compositions, not polymer)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Cipso-Si bond (ferrocenyl-silicon linkage); Si-CH3 confirmed by FT-IR peaks at 1252 and 776 cm-1; ferrocenyl C-H at 3080 cm-1; ferrocenyl vibration peaks at 1633, 1420, 1160, 1031, 830 cm-1

functional_groups.other: ferrocenyl groups (cyclopentadienyl-Fe-cyclopentadienyl); SiMe groups and SiMe2 groups confirmed by 1H-NMR at 0.75 ppm and 0.4 ppm respectively

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three-stage pyrolysis: Stage 1 (25-350°C, 11.2% weight loss, evaporation of water m/z:18); Stage 2 (350-600°C, 57.5% weight loss, main pyrolysis - sub-stage 350-400°C 5.1% loss from Si-CH3 cleavage generating CH4, sub-stage 400-600°C 52.4% loss from ferrocenyl decomposition and Cipso-Si cleavage releasing CHx and ferrocene m/z:184-186); Stage 3 (600-1000°C, 8.3% weight loss, CO release m/z:28). Pyrolysis starts at 350°C and nearly complete above 600°C. Heating rate 10°C/min for TGA, 50 mL/min gas flow.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with Dawn Heleos-II detector, PS standards, THF eluent, 1 mL/min, 30°C

backbone_architecture.description: Synthesized in two steps: first, ferrocenyldilithium reacts with dichlorodimethylsilane to form soluble linear intermediate; second, trichloromethylsilane is added to create hyperbranched structure. Soluble in THF and CDCl3. Yields golden solid.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000°C: Fe5Si3 present. Crystalline transformation from Fe5Si3 to Fe3Si as temperature increases from 1000 to 1400°C. β-SiC appears at 1400°C. XRD: Fe5Si3 (JCPDS 89-2047) peaks at 40.7°, 41.2°, 45.2°, 46.5°, 46.9°; Fe3Si (JCPDS 45-1207) peaks at 45.4°, 66.2°, 83.8°; β-SiC (JCPDS 73-1665) peaks at 35.6°, 41.5°, 60.1°, 71.9°.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Fe5Si3 (at 1000-1200°C), Fe3Si (at higher temperatures), β-SiC (at 1400°C)

notes: Polymer is hyperbranched polyferrocenylsilane synthesized from ferrocenyldilithium, dichlorodimethylsilane, and trichloromethylsilane. Target ceramic is Fe/Si/C. PDI of 18.9 calculated from Mn=2700 and Mw=51000 (very broad, consistent with hyperbranched architecture). Ceramic yield estimate: total weight loss ~77% (11.2+57.5+8.3%), implying ~23% ceramic yield, though this is for TGA to 1000°C only. Microspheres sintered at 1400°C under nitrogen at 3°C/min with 2h hold. Porous ceramic microspheres obtained with EDS composition Fe 9.8%, Si 32.5%, C 50.0%, O 7.8 at%. Referenced work (Sun et al.) reported ceramic yield 48-62% at 1000-1200°C for similar hyperbranched polyferrocenylsilane under Ar/N2. Heating rate for bulk pyrolysis was 15°C/min; TGA heating rate was 10°C/min.
source: Gou_2016_Synthesis_of_Iron_Containing_Preceramic_Polymer_and_Preparat

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present (molar ratios of BCl3 to total chlorosilanes varied at 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 for HPBCS-1, HPBCS-2, HPBCS-3)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-H bonds present (2500 cm-1), B-C bonds in -BCH2- units, Si-CH2-Si linkages, BCH2 and BC2H units identified by 11B NMR (10-20 ppm and 20-35 ppm respectively)

functional_groups.other: B-H groups, Si-CH2-Si bridging units, -BCH2- units

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA measured in argon at 10 C/min from RT to 1000 C. HPBCS lost only 4.4% below 300 C vs 16.7% for HPCS. Over 300-500 C, HPBCS lost 3.9% vs 26.7% for HPCS. Over 500-1000 C, HPBCS lost ~8% vs ~11% for HPCS. Ceramic conversion complete near 900 C. Boron introduction suppressed volatile gas evolution (CH3CH3, SiH4, CH3SiH3) in 300-500 C range. HPCS ceramic yield was 45.5% for comparison.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with THF eluent at 35 C, calibrated with narrow polystyrene standards (Agilent 1100 system)

backbone_architecture.description: Hyperbranched structure formed via Grignard coupling of Cl3SiCH2Cl, Cl2Si(CH3)CH2Cl and BCl3, followed by LiAlH4 reduction. 29Si NMR shows SiC4, C3SiH, C2SiH2, and CSiH3 environments confirming branched structure. Boron is incorporated into the backbone via B-C linkages.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramics pyrolyzed at 900 C then annealed at 1800 C in argon. HPCS-derived ceramic shows sharp beta-SiC peaks (2theta = 36, 42, 60, 72, 75 deg) with stacking fault shoulder at 34 deg. HPBCS-derived ceramics show broader and weaker beta-SiC reflections indicating inhibited crystallization and smaller crystallite size. Boron content increasing further suppresses crystallization.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC identified after annealing at 1800 C; alpha-SiC stacking faults also noted in HPCS-derived ceramic

notes: Three HPBCS variants synthesized: HPBCS-1 (BCl3:chlorosilanes = 0.1), HPBCS-2 (0.2), HPBCS-3 (0.3), all with Cl2Si(CH3)CH2Cl:Cl3SiCH2Cl = 1:2. Corresponding 1800 C ceramics: SiCB-1, SiCB-2, SiCB-3. After annealing at 1800 C in argon for 2 h, mass residues were: HPCS-derived SiC = 61.2%, SiCB-1 = 70.8%, SiCB-2 = 81.2%, SiCB-3 = 88.5%, demonstrating boron improves high-temperature stability. HPCS (no boron) had Mw = 1800 g/mol and PDI = 8.9 for comparison. Overall polymer yield was 62.3%. The PDI and Mw values reported in text appear to be for HPBCS and HPCS respectively; the text states 'Mw of HBPCS and HPCS are 900 and 1800, and the PDI of HBPCS and HPCS are 1.6 and 8.9' - the JSON Mw and PDI values correspond to HPBCS.
source: Gui_2014_Single_source_precursor_Synthesis_and_High_temperature_Behav

elemental_composition.other_elements: Hf present; elemental compositions reported for pyrolysis products (not precursor polymer): e.g. PHNCS-1 at 1000C: Hf=42.90wt%, Si=29.37wt%, C=13.43wt%, N=11.46wt%, O=2.84wt%. PHNCS-2 at 1000C: Hf=26.52wt%, Si=45.85wt%, C=19.13wt%, N=6.57wt%, O=1.93wt%. PHNCS-3 at 1000C: Hf=16.28wt%, Si=55.60wt%, C=21.34wt%, N=5.15wt%, O=1.63wt%.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-N-Hf structure confirmed by FTIR at 1106 cm-1; Hf-N bonds at 485 cm-1; C-N-Hf at 1369/1146 cm-1; Si-CH2-Si present; Hf-N-CH2-CH3 groups; Si-Si bonds in LPCS backbone; vinyl (CH=CH2) groups in LPCS

functional_groups.other: Si-CH2-Si linkages; Hf-N-CH2-CH3 (diethylamino groups from TDEAH); Si-N-Hf bridging units

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two-stage pyrolysis: ramp to 350C at 1C/min held 1h, then to 1000C at 3C/min held 1h. Ceramic yields: PHNCS-1=57.80wt%, PHNCS-2=71.62wt%, PHNCS-3=67.04wt%, LPCS=56.92wt%. Primary organic group removal between 150-600C releasing CH3, C2H2, C2H6, C3H3, C3H5, C3H6, C3H7, methylsilane, diethylamine. TG-FTIR-MS run under helium at 40C/min to 900C. High-temperature annealing subsequently performed at 1600, 2000, 2400C at 10C/min, 1h holds in argon in graphite furnace. Thermal weight loss of pyrolysis products at high temperatures: 10.60-19.67wt%.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal; Si-N-Hf bond formation promotes crosslinking between precursor molecular chains during pyrolysis

molecular_weight.measurement_method: reported for precursor LPCS component; method not explicitly stated (implied GPC)

backbone_architecture.description: PHNCS is a liquid, branched polyhafniumnitrocarbosilane formed by one-pot reaction of liquid polycarbosilane (LPCS) with tetrakis(diethylamino)hafnium (TDEAH). LPCS contains Si-CH3, Si-CH2, Si-H, Si-Si, and CH=CH2 units. Reaction of Si-H in LPCS with Hf-N-C in TDEAH forms Si-N-Hf bridges releasing C2H6. Less reactive LPCS limits over-crosslinking, maintaining liquid state at room temperature. Precursor remains liquid (not solid network), suitable for PIP processing.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000C: amorphous, no HfO2 detected. At 1600C: weak HfCxN1-x crystallisation (x=0.50-0.58), no significant beta-SiC peaks. At 2000C: HfCxN1-x (x=0.86-0.91) + beta-SiC two-phase ceramic. At 2400C: HfCxN1-x nearly converted to HfC (x=0.92-0.96) + beta-SiC. Phase fractions at 2000C: PHNCS-1: HfCxN1-x 55.0wt%, SiC 45.0wt%; PHNCS-2: 35.9/64.1wt%; PHNCS-3: 21.6/78.4wt%. Phase fractions at 2400C: PHNCS-1: 69.4/30.6wt%; PHNCS-2: 42.7/57.3wt%; PHNCS-3: 29.9/70.1wt%. Adjustable HfCxN1-x content 21.6-69.4wt%. Oxygen content in pyrolysis products 1.63-2.84wt%, mainly surface-distributed.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: SEM of PHNCS-1000 shows smooth dense surface without obvious defects, suggesting potentially superior mechanical properties compared to LPCS-1000 which had minor cracks and pores.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: At 1000C: fully amorphous; At 1600C: HfCxN1-x (FCC solid solution); At 2000C and 2400C: HfCxN1-x + beta-SiC

notes: Grain sizes reported as 17.4-114.9 nm range (midpoint ~66.15 nm used); exact values depend on sample and temperature. PHNCS synthesized from TDEAH (tetrakis(diethylamino)hafnium) + LPCS (liquid polycarbosilane) by one-pot Schlenk technique under argon at 0C to room temperature, 3h reaction. Synthesis yields 98.02-98.84wt%. Viscosity of precursors: PHNCS-1=38.8, PHNCS-2=57.8, PHNCS-3=136.1 mPa·s at room temperature (25C). TDEAH/LPCS ratios: PHNCS-1=4/1, PHNCS-2=1/1, PHNCS-3=1/2 wt/wt. PHNCS-2 shows shear-thinning with viscosity 40.7 mPa·s at 10 s-1. Storage stability tested over 6 months under argon: viscosity increased from 57.8 to 79.2 mPa·s without gelation. HfCxN1-x lattice parameters 4.612-4.639 Å (between Hf2CN 4.583 Å and HfC 4.641 Å). Rietveld refinement used for phase quantification (GSAS-II). Hf content in pyrolysis products adjustable 16.28-42.90wt% depending on TDEAH/LPCS ratio. Non-oxygen system confirmed by absence of HfO2 phase. LPCS molecular weight data (Mn=2130, Mw=6237, PDI=2.93) refer to the LPCS precursor feedstock, not the final PHNCS product.
source: Guo_2025_Synthesis_inorganic_transformation_and_hightemperature_evolu

polymer_name: PCS (various designations: LPCS, PCS-2, PCS-6, PCS-8, PCS-10, PCS-16, PCS-24)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si bonds present in precursor PDMS; Si-Si rearranges to Si-C during pyrolysis. Dehydrogenation and demethanization condensation reactions occur at 440-460 C. Intramolecular cyclization and branched structures noted. Si-H content decreases with increasing Mn.

functional_groups.other: Ring structures and branched structures increase with higher molecular weight components

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Synthesis pyrolysis of PDMS performed at 400 C under N2 to form LPS; subsequent polycondensation at 420-460 C to form PCS. No ceramic yield or TGA data reported.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC (Wyatt Technology DAWN HELEOS-II, s-Styragel column, THF solvent/eluent, elution rate 1 mL/min)

backbone_architecture.description: PCS composed of four molecular weight components: ML (Mn~531), MM (Mn~1207), MH (Mn~2731), MSH (Mn~10977). Lower Mn components (ML, MM) are more reactive; higher Mn components have increased branching and ring structures. MH has predominantly linear structure. Backbone is Si-C based formed by rearrangement of Si-Si bonds from PDMS precursor.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCS used as precursor for SiC fibres via melt spinning, curing, and high-temperature pyrolysis. No direct ceramic microstructural data reported in this text.

notes: Paper focuses on molecular composition and spinnability of PCS rather than ceramic properties. PCS synthesized from PDMS via pyrolysis-rearrangement at 400 C (N2) to form LPS, then polycondensation at 450 C. Molecular weight data by sample: LPCS (Mn=552, PDI=1.6), PCS-2 (Mn=1008, PDI=2.7), PCS-6 (Mn=1505, PDI=2.6), PCS-8 (Mn=1679, PDI=2.9), PCS-10 (Mn=1758, PDI=3.4), PCS-16 (Mn=2275, PDI=4.1), PCS-24 (Mn=2661, PDI=5.3). Melting points range from <20 C (LPCS) to >300 C (PCS-24). Optimal spinnability achieved with three-component PCS (ML+MM+MH): MH 30-45%, MM 30-51%, ML 18-25%. Spinning conducted at 0.2-0.3 MPa, 240-294 m/min takeup rate. Melt-spinning defoaming at 140-160 C above initial melting point for 2 h. Molecular weight measurement method applies to all samples listed.
source: Guodong_2018_Evolution_of_molecular_composition_of_polycarbosilane_and_it

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-C (101.2 eV, 12.2%), Si-N (102.1 eV, 55.8%), Si-O (103.2 eV, 32.0%) from XPS of pyrolyzed ceramic; N2Si(Csp3)2, Si(Csp3)N3, and (H)SiN3 environments observed by 29Si NMR; SiCxN4-x units with x=0,1,2

functional_groups.other: methacrylate groups grafted via 2-isocyanatoethyl methacrylate (IEM); acrylate groups for UV curing; isocyanate-derived urethane linkage

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pristine PVSZ ceramic yield 70%, mPVSZ 61%, mPVSZ green body with 10 wt% silica nanoparticles and UV post-cure 80%. TGA conducted under nitrogen at 2 C/min to 1000 C. Once pyrolyzed, ceramic showed almost no weight loss in Ar or air up to 900 C. 20 wt% weight loss observed for the green body during pyrolysis.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV photopolymerization (DLP, 405 nm) for green body formation; thermal crosslinking at 300 C at 1 C/min; post-cure UV (280-440 nm, 18 W, 30 min); hydrosilylation crosslinking observed by 29Si NMR at 400 C

backbone_architecture.description: Polyvinylsilazane backbone grafted with 2-isocyanatoethyl methacrylate (IEM) at 7:1 PVSZ:IEM weight ratio to introduce photocurable acrylate groups; forms crosslinked network upon UV curing and further crosslinks thermally during pyrolysis

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous SiCN ceramic verified by XRD; mixed Si-C, Si-N, Si-O chemical environments by XPS; SiCxN4-x units (x=0,1,2) by solid-state NMR; silica nanoparticles (10 wt%) incorporated contributing Si-O component; no crystallinity at 1000 C pyrolysis

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Values at 1000 C pyrolysis for mPVSZ with 10 wt% silica nanoparticles measured by nanoindentation (Vickers hardness and elastic modulus). Without silica: modulus 68 GPa, hardness 8 GPa. Reference reported values for PVSZ-derived SiCN: 82-140 GPa modulus, 8.3-11.3 GPa hardness. Final density 2.28 g/cm3.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases detected; fully amorphous SiCN at 1000 C pyrolysis temperature

notes: Composite preceramic resin consists of mPVSZ (polyvinylsilazane modified with IEM) with 10 wt% surface-modified silica nanoparticles (15 nm, amorphous, MEK-EC-2130Y from Nissan Chemical), photoinitiator cocktail (4.0 wt% of mPVSZ: 3:1:1 ratio of DMAP/HMPP/TPO), and UV absorber HMBS (0.5 wt%). PVSZ:IEM grafting ratio 7:1 by weight at 65 C for 18 h under argon. 3D printing via DLP at 405 nm, 40 um layer thickness, 11 s cure per layer. Isotropic linear shrinkage of 20% in all three dimensions upon pyrolysis to 1000 C. Silica nanoparticles serve to increase ceramic yield and promote isotropic shrinkage. Ceramic used as microreactor for ammonia cracking at up to 1000 C, showing 99% conversion; no cracks after 48 h exposure to corrosive ammonia at 1000 C.

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present (borazine ring backbone); full atomic percentages not reported numerically

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds (borazine ring, BN3 environment at 28.46 ppm in 11B NMR); B-NH-B and Si-NH-B linkages; vinyl groups (CH=CH2) present on precursor, consumed during polymerization

functional_groups.other: Borazine ring as backbone rigid unit

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TG-MS performed from 40 to 900°C at 10 K/min under argon. Two-stage degradation: 100-200°C mass loss ~19.5% (water and NH3 emission, attributed to moisture uptake); 200-400°C mass loss ~14.1% (polycondensation/crosslinking via transamination, NH3 and CH4 emission); 400-700°C mass loss ~5.7% (alkyl segments and CO2 emission). Ceramic yield reported as 60.7% (abstract) and ~61% (text). Pyrolysis also performed at 1200 and 1400°C with 4 h hold.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (addition polymerization of vinyl groups using dicumyl peroxide initiator; stepwise heating: 130°C/1h, 160°C/2h, 190°C/1h)

backbone_architecture.description: Borazine ring as rigid backbone unit with vinylsilyl terminal groups. After polymerization via addition polymerization of vinyl groups, a three-dimensional network is formed (polyborocarbosilazane). The borazine ring is retained in the final ceramic random network.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiBCN (amorphous up to 1400°C; graphite and h-BN crystallize at 1500°C)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XPS confirms SiBCN ceramic at 1200°C with Si-N, B-N, B-O, N-B, N-C, and C-C bonds. XRD shows amorphous phase until 1500°C; graphite (PDF-89-8487) and hexagonal BN (PDF-34-0421) appear at 1500°C. Si3N4 and SiC crystal formation suppressed by boron. Raman confirms disordered graphitic sp2 carbon (D band ~1350 cm-1, G band ~1600 cm-1) at 1200 and 1400°C; h-BN not detected below 1500°C by Raman.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Text mentions enhanced hardness, stiffness, and high-temperature durability as general properties of borazine-derived ceramics, but no specific measured values reported for TSAB-derived ceramic

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous up to 1400°C; partially crystalline at 1500°C
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Graphite (hexagonal, PDF-89-8487) and h-BN (hexagonal, PDF-34-0421) at 1500°C; amorphous below 1500°C

notes: Precursor molecular formula: (B{NH[Si(CH3)2CH=CH2]}NH)3 (TSAB). Single source precursor designed for electronic/MEMS applications. Room temperature conductivity of SiBCN ceramic increases with pyrolysis temperature: ~8e-6 (ohm·cm)^-1 at 1200°C, ~4.23e-5 (ohm·cm)^-1 at 1400°C, ~3.94e-4 (ohm·cm)^-1 at 1500°C. Photoluminescence observed at 417, 466, 498, and 593 nm (2.97, 2.66, 2.49, 2.09 eV) under 380 nm excitation for ceramic pyrolyzed at 1400°C. Ceramic yield in abstract given as 60.7%; body text states ~61%. TGA heating rate for pyrolysis of cured polymer was 5 K/min (polymer synthesis section); TG-MS analysis used 10 K/min.
source: HE_2018_Borazinetype_single_source_precursor_with_vinyl_to_SiBCN_cer

polymer_name: D-PFC (fluorinated polycarbosilane), derived from D-PClC (poly(dichlorocarbosilane)) and D-PBrC (poly(dibromocarbosilane))

elemental_composition.other_elements: Fluorine content >30 wt% in D-PFC (LiF-fluorinated product). Precursor D-PClC empirical composition: SiCl1.7H3.0C12.0; precursor D-PBrC empirical composition: SiCl1.3H2.4Br2.0. Partial fluorination with NH4F gave F content ~42% exchange rate on D-PBrC with 83% Br exchange.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-F bonds present in fluorinated products; Si-Cl in D-PClC precursor; Si-Br in D-PBrC precursor; Si-Si bonds mentioned as present in halogenated polycarbosilanes; OH groups and siloxane bridges formed as side products with aqueous fluorinating agents

functional_groups.other: Phenyl groups in precursor D-PPC (poly(diphenylcarbosilane), composition [SiPh2(CH2)1.09]y); CH3 end groups formed as side products during fluorination; fluorine substituents on Si in D-PFC

backbone_architecture.description: Polymeric carbosilane backbone with Si-C repeating units; described as oligomeric/polymeric; precursor D-PPC has composition [SiPh2(CH2)1.09]y suggesting linear repeat unit; Si-Si bonds also mentioned as part of backbone

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Fluoropolycarbosilanes intended as precursors and sintering aids for SiC ceramics; fluorine expected to create lattice defects increasing elasticity of resulting SSiC ceramic material

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Increased elasticity of resulting SiC ceramic expected due to lattice defects from fluorine during pressureless sintering

notes: Paper describes synthesis of fluorine-containing polycarbosilanes by fluorination of fully halogenated poly(dichlorocarbosilane) (D-PClC) and poly(dibromocarbosilane) (D-PBrC) using various fluorinating agents (ZnF2, KHF2, SbF3, NH4F, NH4HF2, HF, LiF). LiF was the most successful fluorinating agent, yielding D-PFC with >30 wt% fluorine and high hydrolytic resistance. Starting material was D-PPC (poly(diphenylcarbosilane)) from Solvay Deutschland GmbH via direct synthesis. ZnF2 gave only 4.7% halogen exchange (0.9 wt% F with D-PBrC); wet ZnF2 gave 7% exchange but introduced ~7 wt% oxygen via siloxane bridges. KHF2 gave max 14% Br exchange (2.7 wt% F). Aqueous SbF3 gave 20 wt% F but with side reactions including oxygen and antimony incorporation and backbone cleavage; yield only 30 wt%. NH4F gave 83% Br exchange with 42% yield from D-PBrC, but some Si-C bond cleavage occurred. NH4HF2 and 100% HF destroyed the oligomeric framework. D-PFC characterized analytically and spectroscopically (1H NMR mentioned). Intended application: sintering aid for pressureless sintering of SiC ceramics.
source: Habel_1992_Synthese_fluorhaltiger_Polycarbosilane

polymer_name: Poly(diorganylsilylen-co-para-xylylen); specific variants: Mg-PPXyC, Mg-P(PM)XyC, Mg-PMXyC, Mg-P(MH)XyC, Mg-P(MVi)XyC

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental analysis reported in weight percent (not atomic percent). Si, C, H, Cl/Br values given per polymer variant in Table 1. E.g. Mg-PPXyC: Si 10.5 wt%, C 79.3 wt%, H 5.5 wt%, Cl/Br 2.9 wt%; Mg-P(PM)XyC: Si 14.4 wt%, C 74.2 wt%, H 6.7 wt%, Cl/Br 3.1 wt%; Mg-PMXyC: Si 18.6 wt%, C 68.3 wt%, H 7.3 wt%, Cl/Br 4.5 wt%; Mg-P(MH)XyC: Si 30.2 wt%, C 57.4 wt%, H 7.1 wt%, Cl/Br 3.1 wt%; Mg-P(MVi)XyC: Si 23.6 wt%, C 63.3 wt%, H 7.6 wt%, Cl/Br 2.7 wt%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2Ar (carbosilan bridge), Si-C6H5 (phenyl), Si-CH=CH2 (vinyl), Si-Si (polysilane blocks), p-xylylene bridging units; IR bands at 1000-1100 cm-1 and ~800 cm-1 for framework vibrations; Si-H at 2150 cm-1; C=C stretch at 1610 cm-1

notes: Paper describes chemical vapour curing (CVC) of polycarbosilane (PCS) fibres using unsaturated hydrocarbon vapours (cyclohexene, 1-hexyne, 1-octyne) in argon to produce low-oxygen SiC fibre. Mn = 2060 g/mol for PCS; a related polytitanocarbosilane precursor (PC, Mn = 1310) used for Si-Ti-C-O fibre with Ti/Si atomic ratio 0.012. Oxygen content in CVC SiC fibre (1-hexyne-cured) was 1.5-1.7 wt%. Crystallite size of 13.6 nm reported after 8 h at 1500°C (~3x that after 1 h). Heating rate during curing was 10°C/h (= 0.167°C/min). Heating rate during pyrolysis was 100°C/h (= 1.67°C/min). Strength of 4500 MPa is midpoint approximation; text states 'increased to 4.5 GPa'. Si-Ti-C-O fibre CVC showed improved modulus but limited thermal stability improvement due to oxygen from titanium alkoxide precursor.

notes: Study focuses on curing-induced structure-property relationships, not pyrolysis to ceramics. Three curing protocols applied: N1 cured up to 80°C (6 h total), N2 cured up to 140°C, N3 cured up to 250°C (47 h at final temperature). Glass transition temperatures: N1 78°C, N2 157°C, N3 187°C (intrinsic max Tg of fully postcured network 191°C by second DMTA heating cycle). PALS identified two void populations: smaller ~310 pm diameter, larger ~650 pm diameter; intensities shift from 36%/64% (N1) to 21%/79% (N3) with increasing curing. MD simulations showed total geometric free volume increases to 10.47% at high conversion with fewer, larger void domains. Si-H stretching band monitored at 2115 cm-1 by FTIR. Swelling experiments in toluene (72 h) used to determine crosslink density. Crosslink density value of 6.2 mmol/cm3 for N2 inferred from table data; text states range 3.1 to 8.0 mmol/cm3 across N1-N3. No pyrolysis/ceramization performed in this study.

notes: a-TSEB is a single source precursor for SiBCN ceramics based on a borazine ring with formula [B{CH(CH3)(SiR3)}NH]3 where R is an acrylate group. It was synthesised via hydroboration of trichlorovinylsilane with BCl3 and triethylsilane, followed by cyclisation with hexamethyldisilazane and substitution with hydroxyethyl acrylate. UV curing used benzoin dimethyl ether as photoinitiator (1 wt% optimal); ~84% double bond conversion achieved within 1 min under UV irradiation. DPC studies showed maximum polymerisation rate at 15°C (0.1245 s-1) and optimal light intensity around 66 mW/cm2. Companion molecule a-TSMB ([B{CH2(SiR3)}NH]3) also described with methylene carbon bridge and 3 acrylate groups. Molecular weight of TSEB precursor before acrylate substitution: 5.15 g per 0.0091 mol implies ~566 g/mol for TSEB. Yellow solid obtained after UV curing. SEM and XRD used to characterise final ceramic.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Perhydropolysilazane: ceramic yields close to 100% in ammonia, 82-93% in inert gas depending on crosslinking degree. Verbeek early work gave only 45% ceramic yield. Residual solvent loss below 400 C; ammonia reacts with Si-H between 400-600 C; amorphous SiN4-tetrahedral solid forms 600-1000 C; crystallisation complete by 1400 C. Carbon still detectable (0.2%) after 1000 C in ammonia. Vinyl-containing polymers develop crosslinks from ~300 C but higher sp2 carbon content. Transamination/nitrogen loss 200-500 C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (hydrosilylation of Si-H and vinyl groups), chemical (strong base), exposure to moist air, co-ammonolysis with trifunctional chlorosilanes; UV exposure also mentioned for thin films

backbone_architecture.description: Mainly linear polymers described in Table 1; Ceraset formed of large cyclic oligomers with urea-derived linking groups; polycyclosilazanes with direct Si-Si bonds also described; cross-linking introduces cyclic structures; strongly cross-linked insoluble network possible (e.g. CySiCl3 + Li3N metathesis product)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Perhydropolysilazane yields Si3N4 (alpha and beta phases); polyorganosilazane yields amorphous SiCN at lower temperatures crystallising to alpha-Si3N4 + SiC; atmosphere controls phase: alpha-Si3N4 in ammonia above 1000 C, SiC in Ar above 1400 C, alpha-Si3N4 + SiC in N2 above 1600 C; amorphous ceramics contain SiN4, SiN3C, SiN2C2, CSi4 tetrahedral units plus sp2 carbon; SiO2 surface layer forms on oxidation

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Perhydropolysilazane-derived Si3N4 fibres (10 micron diameter): tensile strength 1700-2200 MPa, tensile modulus 180-200 GPa, density 2.5 g/cm3. Cubic Si3N4 bulk modulus 290(5) GPa. Ceramics oxidation resistant to 1600 C; creep deformation at high temperature but material hardens and becomes highly creep resistant during process.

notes: This is a review paper covering multiple preceramic polymer systems for silicon nitride and related materials. No single polymer is exclusively described; data represents ranges and examples across polysilazane families. Perhydropolysilazane (no carbon, from SiCl2H2 + ammonia in pyridine) sold commercially by Merck as spin-on dielectric. Polyorganosilazanes commercially available as KiON Ceraset and Merck Durazane. Ceramic yield of Verbeek early work: 45%. Perhydropolysilazane inert gas ceramic yield: 82-93%. Ammonia atmosphere ceramic yield: ~100%. Si3N4 fibre tensile strength range 1.7-2.2 GPa noted in notes field. Ordered mesoporous Si3N4 from perhydropolysilazane surface area 772 m2/g. Poly-N-methylsilazane crystallisation inhibited up to 1400 C. MAS-NMR, IR, mass spectrometry used to characterize ceramisation. PDF studies confirm corner-sharing SiN4 tetrahedra structure.

notes: This paper concerns PAN-b-PMMA block copolymers as preceramic polymer precursors, not silicon-based preceramic polymers. The preceramic function is derived from PAN (carbon precursor) and ferrocene-containing side chains (iron oxide precursor). notes: This paper is primarily a ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulation study of PHPS conversion mechanism, not a synthesis or materials characterization study. A new Si/N/O/H ReaxFF force field was developed using JAX-ReaxFF. MD simulations were run at 1600 K (temperature-acceleration strategy) with effective gas pressures of ~86-172 atm (pressure-acceleration strategy); results are not directly comparable to experimental conditions. PHPS repeat unit: [-SiH2-NH-]n. O2 accelerates Si-O bond formation and promotes dense SiOx surface layer that impedes further O2 diffusion. H2O facilitates NH3 release and Si-N bond cleavage. Six simulation cases with varying O2/H2O ratios were studied (Case 0 = vacuum control; Cases 1-5 = varying O2/H2O ratios with total O atom count fixed at 2000). Gas-phase simulation box: 80x80x80 Å3 with 20 PHPS molecules; condensed-phase simulation box: 80x80x200 Å3 with 200 PHPS molecules. Total simulation time: 2 ns per case. Applications mentioned: dielectric layers, electronic encapsulation, oxidation-resistant coatings, corrosion protection, hydrophobic coatings.

notes: PHBCN is a novel Hf-B-C-N polymeric precursor (not a silicon-based polymer) synthesized from tris(methylamino)borane (TMB, B(NHCH3)3), chloroacetonitrile (ClCH2CN), and HfCl4 via dehalogenative substitution. notes: This paper focuses on rheological measurement methodology for PCS melt rather than pyrolysis or ceramic conversion. Preheating at 315°C under nitrogen (ex-situ and/or in-situ) was used to minimize air bubble interference in rheological measurements. Softening point increased with preheating: raw=216°C, ex-situ=257°C, in-situ 10min=225°C, in-situ 1h=245°C, ex-situ+in-situ 2h=267°C. GPC showed molecular weight distributions shifted upon preheating due to decomposition of small molecules. Mn range of 1000-2000 g/mol stated as typical for PCS; midpoint 1500 g/mol used as estimate.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA of AlO-gel showed 89.6% mass loss with endothermic peaks at 80 and 260 C corresponding to moisture evaporation and gamma-alumina phase transition. Final sintered body is dense alpha-alumina.

notes: This paper does not describe a preceramic polymer. It describes an alumina sol-gel composite (SGC) slurry system using aluminum nitrate nonahydrate and urea as an inorganic binder for polymer-free ceramic 3D printing via material extrusion (DIW/LCP process). The sol-gel solution forms an inorganic hydroxyaluminum network (AlO-gel) that converts to alumina nanoparticles during sintering. Solid loading up to 50 vol% alumina powder (AHP-200, 0.4 micron corundum, Nippon Light Metal). Citric acid added at ~0.1 wt% as dispersant. All fields related to preceramic polymer chemistry are not applicable to this work.

notes: This is a review/overview paper discussing three preceramic polymer systems (polycarbosilanes, polysilazanes, polysilsesquioxanes) as CMC matrix precursors at NASA Lewis Research Center. notes: Paper investigates ceramization mechanism of PCS-20mass%PVS hybrid polymer fiber cured by 2MeV electron beam irradiation at 15MGy under vacuum. PCS supplied by Shin-Etsu Chemicals (Mn=2000); PVS supplied by Mitsui Chemicals (Mn=960). Hybrid fiber melt-spun at 490K; PCS reference fiber at 600K. Heat treatments performed from 473-1673K for 1.8ks (30 min). ESR measurements show radical concentration in PCS-20%PVS fiber immediately after irradiation is ~60% of that in PCS fiber (~1.7x10^17 spins/g implied), attributed to easier radical recombination due to lower MW and flexibility of PVS. Radical accumulation above 1000K indicates onset of polymer-to-ceramic conversion restricting molecular motion. FT-IR analysis confirms Si-H2 and Si-H3 bond cleavage below 773K. The paper describes a blend/hybrid of two polymers (PCS and PVS), not a single-component polymer; molecular weight given (Mn=2000) refers to the PCS component; PVS Mn=960. Low oxygen content in fiber due to radiation curing contributes to high tensile strength and thermal resistance. Hold time of 1.8ks (~30 min) used for intermediate heat treatments; 3.6ks (~60 min) used for pyrolysis at 1273K.

Ceramic yield values in table correspond to midpoint doses: 5.4, 10.8, 15.3, 20.7 MGy. Mn of PVS stated as 9.6x10^2 = 960 g/mol based on text. SiC XRD lines (111, 220, 311) appear above 800°C. Ceramic char contains free carbon and no oxygen by ESCA.
