notes: Paper describes synthesis of four silylene-acetylene polymers (3, 4, 10, 11) via a novel one-pot TCE route where trichloroethylene is quantitatively converted to dilithioacetylene with n-BuLi at -78°C then quenched with dichlorosilanes. Polymer yields >90% by this route. Polymers are white powders, melt reversibly (softening points: polymer 3 155-175°C, polymer 4 125-140°C, polymer 10 117-135°C, polymer 11 70-100°C), soluble in THF/benzene/chloroform, insoluble in alcohols/aliphatics. Electrical conductivity ~10^-15 S/cm (insulators); iodine doping raises to ~10^-7 S/cm. UV spectra show no extended conjugation (λmax <250 nm). IR vc≡c ~2039-2040 cm-1 for all polymers. The polymers are not polysilazanes or polysiloxanes but rather poly(silyleneacetylene) and poly(disilyeneacetylene) - classified as polycarbosilane-type preceramic polymers targeting SiC ceramics. Pyrolysis atmosphere confirmed as helium for TGA.
source: IjadiMaghsoodi_1990_Efficient_onepot_synthesis_of_silyleneacetylene_and_disilyle

polymer_name: T1, T2, T3 (polycyclic silicones from D4V and D4H)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-C-C-Si and Si-C-Si bridges formed via hydrosilylation; ethylene bridges connecting cyclic siloxane units

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: nitrogen (TGA to 900°C); argon (furnace pyrolysis at 1200°C and 1500°C)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA conducted under nitrogen from RT to 900°C at 10°C/min. Onset decomposition temperature (Td5) in range 600-630°C. Ceramic yields at 900°C: T1=82%, T2=85%, T3=84.4%. Initial weight loss up to 300°C negligible (<1% for T1 and T2, ~3% for T3). Polymers further pyrolysed at 1200°C and 1500°C in tubular furnace under argon for 1 hour.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic (Pt-assisted hydrosilylation; self-crosslinking via residual Pt catalyst at 30±2°C for 2 weeks)

backbone_architecture.description: Polycyclic network structure formed by hydrosilylation of tetrafunctional cyclic oligomers D4V (2,4,6,8-tetramethyl-2,4,6,8-tetravinylcyclotetrasiloxane) and D4H (1,3,5,7-tetramethylcyclotetrasiloxane); cyclic siloxane rings interconnected by ethylenic (Si-C-C-Si) bridges

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC at 1200°C; SiC (beta-SiC) with residual SiOC and free carbon at 1500°C
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1200°C: amorphous SiOC confirmed by broad XRD halo at 22-28° 2theta and Raman D/G bands indicating free carbon. At 1500°C: beta-SiC (JCPDS 29-1129), graphitic carbon (JCPDS 75-1621), cubic silica (JCPDS 86-1629). SiC fibers from T1 contain small amount of oxygen (3-5%). Nanostructures include wires and fibers.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC, graphitic carbon, cubic silica (identified at 1500°C); amorphous SiO2 broad halo at 1200°C

notes: Three polymer compositions synthesized: T1 (D4V:D4H = 1:0.5), T2 (D4V:D4H = 1:1), T3 (D4V:D4H = 1:2). Ceramic yield range 82-85% at 900°C; midpoint 83.8% used for ceramic_yield_pct. SiC nanostructure morphologies at 1500°C: T1 shows fibers 200-300 nm diameter; T2 shows uniform fibers 1-2 μm diameter; T3 shows mixture of nanowires and nanofibers. Catalyst used: Karstedt's catalyst (Pt(0) 1,3-divinyl-1,1,3,3-tetramethyldisiloxane complex) at 0.07 wt%. SiC nanostructure formation mechanism attributed to vapor-solid mechanism and shape-memory synthesis involving in-situ derived free carbon reacting with SiO vapor.
source: Indulekha_2018_Polycyclic_silicone_polymer_as_novel_single_source_precursor

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2- backbone (carbosilane); Si-allyl (Si-CH2CH=CH2); Si-OR (alkoxy derivatives, R = Me, Et)

functional_groups.other: allyl groups (Si-CH2CH=CH2); alkoxy groups (Si-OR, R = Me, Et)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: AHPCS alone yields ca. 70-80% ceramic. 50:50 AHPCS/PB mixture yields 88% ceramic yield. Alkoxy derivative gels pyrolyzed to 1000 °C yield SiOxCy with retained high surface area (~250 m2/g). Further annealing to 1400 and 1600 °C performed on SiC/BN composites.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (thermosetting); also sol-gel processing for alkoxy derivatives

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC and NMR (implied by reference to GPC studies in figure caption)

backbone_architecture.description: Hyperbranched polycarbosilane of type [R3SiCH2-]x[-SiR2CH2-]y[-SiR(CH2-)1.5]z[-Si(CH2-)2]l where R = H, -CH2CH=CH2, or OR. AHPCS nominally [Si(CH2CH=CH2)2CH2]0.1[SiH2CH2]0.9.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC (from AHPCS); SiOxCy (from alkoxy derivative); SiC/BN two-phase (from AHPCS/PB blend)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiC-rich phase and BN-rich phase in AHPCS/PB composites. SiC-rich bright region contains ~20 at% each B and N with Si and C in 1:1 ratio. BN-rich dark region contains ~6 at% each Si and C. Alkoxy gel-derived SiOxCy retains ~250 m2/g surface area and ~20 Å pore size after pyrolysis to 1000 °C. SiC partially crystallizes at 1600 °C; BN remains apparently amorphous.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Vickers hardness measured by diamond indenter on SiC/BN composites (80:20 and 50:50) and AHPCS-SiC at 1000, 1400, and 1600 °C. SiC/BN composites show substantially lower hardness and reduced cracking compared to AHPCS-SiC alone. Crack blunting observed in 50:50 SiC/BN at 1600 °C suggesting unusual toughness.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC (partially crystallized at 1600 °C); BN apparently not crystallized at 1600 °C

notes: Mn range given as 600-1000 AMU; midpoint 800 used. AHPCS is commercially available (Starfire Systems). Alkoxy derivative gels have BET surface area 750-900 m2/g (midpoint ~825) with pore size peak at ~20 Å. Thin films of '[Si(O)CH2]n' gel show dielectric constants as low as 2.0 after heating to 400 °C. SiC/C composites show C phase as ~1 µm droplets in SiC matrix with high oxidation resistance. AHPCS/PB blends undergo phase separation yielding two-phase SiC/BN ceramics with BN droplets of 1-10 µm in SiC-rich matrix (80:20 ratio). Paper covers multiple polymer variants: HPCS, AHPCS, alkoxy-HPCS, and blends with polyborazylene (PB).
source: Interrante_2002_Silicon_based_ceramics_from_polymer_precursors

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ti present; pyrolysed PTC chemical compositions (wt%): Si 49.2-52.5, C 33.6-34.8, O 8.7-9.5, Ti 2.05-7.13; chemical formulas e.g. SiC1.55O0.30Ti0.023 to SiC1.62O0.31Ti0.070

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Ti bonds formed during condensation reaction; Si-CH2-Si bonds present in polycarbosilane backbone; Si-O-Ti-O-Si cross-linking bonds

functional_groups.other: Si-CH2-Si units present in backbone; tetra-alkyltitanate substituent groups (isopropyl, n-butyl, 2-ethylhexyl)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA shows three weight loss steps: 250-450°C (vaporization of low molecular weight organosilicon compounds), 450-600°C (evolution of hydrogen and ethane), 600-800°C (degradation of main chain). Weight residue stabilizes above 800°C. Higher Ti concentration in PTC leads to smaller weight loss in third step and higher overall weight residue. Higher Ti concentration PTC exhibits much better weight residue than low Ti concentration PTC.

crosslink_density.value: Effective functional groups per molecule: 3.0 for tetra-isopropyl titanate, 2.2 for tetra-n-butyl titanate, 1.4 for tetra-2-ethylhexyl titanate; gel fraction increases with tetra-alkyltitanate concentration
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - condensation reaction at 300°C between Si-H bonds in polycarbosilane and substituent groups of tetra-alkyltitanate forming Si-O-Ti-O-Si cross-links

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with THF eluent, polystyrene standard, Toyo Soda HCL-801A at 40°C, 1 ml/min

backbone_architecture.description: Cross-linked structure formed by condensation of Si-H bonds in polycarbosilane with tetra-alkyltitanate, creating Si-O-Ti-O-Si cross-linking points. Pendant structures also estimated. Starting polycarbosilane has linear/branched backbone with Si-CH2-Si and Si-CH3 units.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous SiTiCO; beta-SiC crystallization inhibited by Ti at high temperatures
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysed PTC retains amorphous state composed of Si, Ti, C, O up to high temperature in inert gas. Ti inhibits crystalline grain growth of beta-type SiC. Densification proceeds above 800°C as indicated by Si-C bond energy increase. Higher Ti concentration leads to higher Si-C bonding energy in the densified inorganic material.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Continuous Si-Ti-C-O fibre derived from PTC reported to have high mechanical strength; higher Ti concentration improves heat resistance and oxidation resistance

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (crystallization inhibited by Ti at high temperatures); X-ray diffraction performed with CuKa radiation, Rigaku diffractometer

notes: PTC is synthesized by reaction of polycarbosilane (PCB, Mw=1500, synthesized from polydimethylsilane 100g + polyborodiphenylsiloxane 3g at 340°C under N2 for 12h) with tetra-alkyltitanate (3.45e-4 to 1.25e-3 mol/g PCB) at 300°C in nitrogen. Three tetra-alkyltitanates compared: tetra-isopropyl titanate (activation energy 17.04 kcal/mol), tetra-n-butyl titanate (20.07 kcal/mol), tetra-2-ethylhexyl titanate (31.07 kcal/mol). Tetra-2-ethylhexyl titanate found most advantageous for narrow MW distribution, low gel fraction, and high Ti concentration. PTC is precursor for Si-Ti-C-O continuous fibre. Reaction mechanism involves nucleophilic attack of oxygen lone pair on silicon atom. Alkane gas evolved as byproduct (propane, butane, or 3-methylheptane depending on titanate used). Reacted substituent percentages: 75% (isopropyl), 54% (n-butyl), 35% (2-ethylhexyl) after 270 min at 300°C.
source: Ishikawa_1992_Production_mechanism_of_polytitanocarbosilane_and_its_conver

polymer_name: Perhydropolysilazane (PHPS); variants: PHPS-A, PHPS-HP, PHPS-HX, PHPS-IM

elemental_composition.other_elements: Cl detected by ion chromatography; polymer contains only Si and N (plus H); Cl content reported as N.D. or <20 ppm depending on sample

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-N-Si bending (1050-787 cm-1); SiH, SiH2, SiH3 groups confirmed by 29Si-DEPT NMR; NH (not NH2) confirmed by IR and 15N-DEPT NMR; N-H at 3390 and 1195 cm-1; Si-H at 2170 cm-1

functional_groups.other: NH (secondary amine linkage); SiH, SiH2, SiH3 groups; branching units -SiH< and >N<; no NH2 present

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Decomposition temperature range 150-600°C in N2. Ceramic yields in N2: PHPS-A 82%, PHPS-HP 88%, PHPS-IM 93%. Ceramic yields in NH3: PHPS-A 100%, PHPS-HP 98%, PHPS-IM 105% (>100% due to nitridation of excess Si by NH3). Ceramic yield increases with branching parameter (sum of >SiH- and >N< contents). Nitridation in NH3 commences at ~350-450°C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal crosslinking via dehydrogen condensation between Si-H and N-H bonds, and disproportionation at SiH sites, in the presence of pyridine catalyst; also imidation with NH3

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC using Shimadzu LC-6 with TSK Gel G2000HXL and C4000HXL columns, chloroform solvent, polystyrene standards. Ranges: PHPS-A 300-18800; PHPS-HX 300-20000; PHPS-HP 260-36000; PHPS-IM 260-48000. PHPS-A Mn=700, Mw=1000; PHPS-HP Mn=1400, Mw=4370; PHPS-IM Mn=1600, Mw=5200

backbone_architecture.description: Polymer contains SiH, SiH2, SiH3 and NH, N structural units. Branching introduced via -SiH< (trifunctional Si) and >N< (trifunctional N) units. Higher branching content correlates with higher ceramic yield. No quaternary Si (Si without H) detected. Heat treatment in pyridine increases branching units.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Target ceramic is high-purity silicon nitride. Excess Si present in pyrolysis products when fired in N2 (Si/N ratio above stoichiometric 0.75). In NH3 atmosphere, excess Si reacts with NH3 to approach stoichiometric silicon nitride. Free Si in amorphous matrix promotes Si3N4 crystallization at relatively low temperatures.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Silicon nitride ceramic noted for high strength, high modulus, high thermal shock resistance, and good oxidation resistance at elevated temperatures

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Silicon nitride (Si3N4) crystallizes from amorphous matrix upon pyrolysis; free Si promotes crystallization

notes: Four PHPS variants studied: PHPS-A (oligomeric liquid, base material from ammonolysis of DCS-pyridine adduct at 0°C); PHPS-HP (solid, heat-treated in pyridine at 120°C, 4h); PHPS-HX (liquid, heat-treated in xylene at 120°C, 4h); PHPS-IM (solid, heat-treated in pyridine with NH3 at 120°C, 4h). Pyridine acts as catalyst promoting polymerization and branching; xylene suppresses polymerization. Ceramic yield range 82-93% in N2, 98-105% in NH3. Si/N atomic ratios from table: PHPS-A ~0.84-1.00, PHPS-HP ~0.86-1.12. Gellation times: PHPS-IM <1 day, PHPS-HP 7 days, PHPS-A 1 day (neat). Polymer is composed of only Si, N, H elements (no carbon). IR peaks: N-H at 3390 and 1195 cm-1, Si-H at 2170 cm-1, Si-N-Si at 1050-787 cm-1. 1H NMR peaks: SiH2+SiH at 4.72 ppm, SiH3 at 4.3 ppm, NH at 1.33 ppm. 29Si-DEPT NMR: SiH at -37.0 ppm, SiH2 at -35.3 ppm, SiH3 at -51.4 ppm. Ceramic yield midpoint noted as 87.5 (range 82-93% in N2).
source: Isoda_1992_Perhydropolysilazane_precursors_to_silicon_nitride_ceramics

polymer_name: poly(ureamethylvinyl)silazane (PUMVS), trade name Ceraset, KiON Corporation

elemental_composition.other_elements: Mg present as active filler (metal powder); ceramic products (SN1Mg10 through SN5Mg10) contain Si, Mg, C, N, O at varying atomic percentages as detailed in Table 1

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Mg-N bonds form upon Mg incorporation above 900 C; Mg3N2 and Mg2Si observed as reaction intermediates; MgSiN2 forms at higher pyrolysis temperatures

functional_groups.other: urea linkages present in backbone per polymer name (poly(ureamethylvinyl)silazane)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two-step mass loss observed for neat PUMVS and Mg-filled composites in range 300-900 C. First step: ammonia evolution. Second step: methane and hydrogen evolution, accelerated with increasing Mg loading, completing at temperatures 100-300 C lower than neat PUMVS. SN5Mg shows additional ~14% mass loss up to 1000 C attributed to Mg volatilization. Ceramic yields at 1000 C estimated from elemental analysis (assuming constant Si): ~81, 80, 79, 69, 59% for SN1Mg10 through SN5Mg10. MgO condensation on TG crucibles observed, obscuring mass balance calculations. Heating rate was 100 C/h = 1.67 C/min; cooling rate 300 C/h. Additional hold of 5 h at 550 C included for Tpyr > 500 C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - crosslinked at 300 C for 6 hours in Teflon moulds within steel dies; partial pre-crosslinking at 170 C for 2-3 hours under constant stirring in flowing nitrogen

backbone_architecture.description: Crosslinked poly(ureamethylvinyl)silazane network; commercially available as liquid prior to crosslinking. Chemical structure provided by supplier (Scheme 1 referenced in paper but not reproduced in text).

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN (amorphous Mg-Si-C-N at 1000 C); SiC, Si3N4, MgSiN2, MgO at higher temperatures
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000 C: predominantly X-ray amorphous Mg-Si-C-N with up to 15 mol% Mg; SN1Mg10 fully amorphous, higher Mg loadings show broad 2H-SiC peaks. At 1200 C: SiC and beta-Si3N4 microcrystalline phases appear. At 1400 C in Ar: SiC crystalline; in N2: MgSiN2 + SiC. At 1600 C: increasing SiC crystallinity. MgO crystallites 10-30 nm present. Calculated phase compositions include MgSiN2, Si3N4, SiC, free C, Mg, MgO, SiO2 depending on sample.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: At 1000 C: amorphous matrix with 2H-SiC (broad) for higher Mg loadings, MgO (small amounts all samples below 1200 C), Mg2Si and Mg3N2 intermediates at 500-800 C. At 1200 C: SiC + beta-Si3N4. At 1400 C in Ar: SiC; in N2: MgSiN2 + SiC. Mg metal present at 400 C, consumed by 500 C for loadings below 40 wt%.

notes: Paper reports synthesis of Mg-Si-C-N ceramics via reactive pyrolysis of PUMVS filled with Mg metal powder (10-50 wt% Mg loadings). Mg incorporation proceeds in two steps: (1) conversion of Mg metal to Mg compounds, (2) solid-state diffusion assisted by vapor phase transport into amorphous Si-C-N-H bulk. Homogeneous Mg distribution at length scale >100 nm achieved. SiC nanocrystals 2-10 nm diameter observed in TEM. MgO crystallites 10-30 nm. Grain size range 2-10 nm reported for SiC nanocrystals; midpoint 6 nm used. Ceramic yield midpoint ~80% used (range 59-81% for Mg-filled samples). Pyrolysis temperatures ranged from 500 to 1600 C; maximum 1600 C reported. Heating rate 100 C/h (1.67 C/min). Hold time 5 h (300 min) at max temperature. Elemental analysis methods: ICP for Mg and Si, combustion for C, carrier gas hot extraction for N and O. XRD by Guinier-Hagg film camera with Cu-Ka1. TEM identified MgCN2 phase tentatively in SN1Mg10. Pyrolysis in N2 atmosphere promotes MgSiN2 formation vs Ar which promotes SiC.
source: Janakiraman_2006_Synthesis_and_phase_evolution_of_MgSiCN_ceramics_prepared_by

polymer_name: poly(ureamethylvinyl)silazane (PUMVS), commercially known as Ceraset (KiON Corporation)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental composition reported for pyrolyzed ceramic samples, not the precursor polymer itself. See notes for ceramic sample compositions.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C-H bonds detected by FT-IR at 1403 cm-1; Si-H at 2129 cm-1; Si-CH3 at 1255 cm-1; Si-N at 910, 985, 1040 cm-1; Si-C at 780 and 900 cm-1. These bonds decrease with increasing pyrolysis temperature and are undetectable in SiCN-110001.

functional_groups.other: urea groups implied by poly(ureamethylvinyl)silazane designation

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: argon (up to 1100°C); nitrogen (above 1100°C for annealing stage)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA and TMA performed from RT to 1000°C at 5 K/min in flowing argon. Multiple pyrolysis schedules used: single-stage for 800-1100°C (100 K/h heating rate, 1 h hold), two-stage for 1200-1500°C (first stage at 1000°C, second annealing at 10 K/h above 1000°C with 12 h hold). Hydrogen content decreased continuously with increasing thermal treatment, falling below detection limits at 1200°C and above. Oxygen contamination present from air handling.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - cross-linked at 260°C for 5 hours in nitrogen atmosphere

backbone_architecture.description: Liquid polysilazane precursor thermally cross-linked to form fully dense, transparent infusible green bodies; cross-linked network structure inferred from casting and thermosetting behavior

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN - amorphous to nano-crystalline depending on pyrolysis temperature
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Samples from 800-1100°C are amorphous SiCN. At higher temperatures (1200-1300°C), phase segregation occurs with segregation and ordering of carbon clusters into nano-crystalline graphitic regions. Free carbon calculated for SiCN-120012: SiC0.33N0.77O0.18 + 0.62 Cfree; for SiCN-130012: SiC0.36N0.76O0.14 + 0.54 Cfree. Accelerated surface crystallization observed when graphite felt used above 1100°C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Hardness range across samples: 7.9-11.3 GPa (peak at SiCN-100001: 11.3 GPa). Young's modulus range: 82-140 GPa (peak at SiCN-120012: 140 GPa). Poisson's ratio range: 0.21-0.245. Density range: 1.85-2.16 g/cm3. Thermal diffusivity range: 3.99-8.08 x 10^-7 m2/s. Measured by resonance frequency analysis (RFDA) and Vickers indentation.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to semi-crystalline depending on pyrolysis temperature
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: XRD used for structural characterization; nano-crystalline graphitic carbon regions identified by Raman at higher pyrolysis temperatures (1200-1300°C)

notes: Paper focuses on pyrolyzed SiCN ceramic specimens derived from liquid PUMVS (Ceraset, KiON). Elemental compositions reported are for the ceramic products, not the precursor polymer. Ceramic sample compositions: SiCN-080001 (Si 25.86, C 25.75, N 20.30, H 26.02, O 2.07 at%); SiCN-090001 (Si 27.33, C 26.92, N 23.09, H 21.39, O 1.27 at%); SiCN-100001 (Si 29.56, C 29.60, N 23.71, H 15.07, O 2.06 at%); SiCN-110001 (Si 31.31, C 29.96, N 24.99, H 12.12, O 1.63 at%); SiCN-120012 (Si 33.85, C 32.26, N 25.98, H <1.8, O 6.11 at%); SiCN-130012 (Si 35.45, C 31.98, N 26.77, H <1.8, O 4.89 at%). Specimens are disc-shaped, 19 mm diameter, 1 mm thick green bodies; thinned to ~300 microns for mechanical testing. Pyrolysis above 1400°C resulted in heterogeneous microstructure rendering samples unsuitable for characterization. Raman spectroscopy showed D and G peaks (disordered carbon) emerging from SiCN-090001 onward, with increasing I(D)/I(G) ratio and decreasing D peak width indicating growth of ordered aromatic graphene clusters at higher temperatures. Cross-linking conducted at 260°C/5h; cross-linking temperature range noted as optimum - lower temperature/time gave rubber-like bodies, higher temperature deformed PTFE mould.
source: Janakiraman_2009_Fabrication_and_characterization_of_fully_dense_SiCN_ceramic

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ceramic elemental compositions given by mass%: TSDM ceramic: Si 30.7, B 11.6, N 34.8, C 20.8, O 1.4; DSDM ceramic: Si 30.5, B 12.3, N 26.8, C 30.8, O 0.8. These are ceramic not polymer values.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds present (IR ~1351-1377 cm-1); B-C bonds confirmed by IR (~1097-1099 cm-1) indicating survival of Si-CH2-B methylene bridge; Si coordinated tetrahedrally by one C and three N atoms (29Si MAS NMR at -15.1 ppm); B trigonally planar coordinated by one C and two N atoms (11B MAS NMR)

functional_groups.other: Methylene bridge (Si-CH2-B) as key structural feature; terminal NH groups observed by IR at ~3440 cm-1; methylammonium hydrochloride byproduct eliminated during synthesis

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: inert gas (argon or nitrogen not specified further)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Degradation proceeds in two well-resolved stages for both polymers. Stage 1 (200-450 °C): polycondensation with methylamine elimination; mass loss 7.1% (TSDM) and 18.1% (DSDM). Stage 2 (~600 °C): highest weight loss due to methane evolution from terminal methyl groups; mass loss 22.6% (TSDM) and 34.4% (DSDM). No third decomposition step (nitrogen loss at 1100-1300 °C) observed unlike previously reported polyborosilazanes. Ceramic yields: 70.3% (TSDM) and 47.5% (DSDM); midpoint 58.9% noted in notes field.

crosslink_density.value: Qualitative only; NH group intensities at ~3440 cm-1 used to estimate degree of crosslinking
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical - aminolysis with methylamine (dehydrohalogenation)

backbone_architecture.description: Polyborocarbosilazane network formed by aminolysis/polycondensation of chlorosilane-chloroborane single-source precursors with methylamine. Si-CH2-B methylene bridge is retained in backbone. Silicon tetrahedrally coordinated (SiCN3), boron trigonally coordinated (BCN2). Polymer is a viscous liquid that can be solidified by further thermal treatment.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous SiBNC (X-ray amorphous after pyrolysis at 1500 °C)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: TSDM ceramic: empirical formula Si3B3N7C5; DSDM ceramic: Si3B3N5C7. Both X-ray amorphous at 1500 °C. After heating to 2000 °C: TSDM ceramic shows Si3N4 and SiC by XRD; DSDM ceramic shows only SiC. Macroscopic density ~1.93 g/cm3 for both, ~30% below comparable crystalline phases. No macroscopic porosity observed.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Reduced brittleness noted qualitatively due to amorphous nature (lack of lattice planes guiding crack propagation); excellent creep resistance attributed to absence of grain boundaries

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: X-ray amorphous at 1500 °C. After 2000 °C: Si3N4 and SiC (TSDM ceramic); SiC only (DSDM ceramic)

notes: Two single-source precursors studied: TSDM (Cl3Si-CH2-BCl2, trichlorosilyl dichloroboryl methane) and DSDM ((CH3)Cl2Si-CH2-BCl2, dichlorosilyl dichloroboryl methane). Both contain Si:B = 1:1 linked by methylene bridge. Crosslinked with methylamine. Ceramic yields differ: 70.3% (TSDM) vs 47.5% (DSDM); midpoint 58.9% used for ceramic_yield_pct field. Pyrolysis at 1500 °C in inert atmosphere. High-temperature stability tested to 2000 °C in He flow at 10 K/min: final weight loss 19% (TSDM) and 12% (DSDM). Oxidation resistance tested to 1300 °C in pure O2 at 10 K/min: TSDM gains 2.4% mass (passivating SiO2-rich layer); DSDM gains 2.8% but shows 6.8% mass decrease at 700 °C suggesting volatile oxidation product. 29Si MAS NMR of TSDM polymer: single broad resonance at -15.1 ppm (SiCN3 tetrahedral). 11B MAS NMR: quadrupolar coupling constant 2.88 MHz, asymmetry parameter 0.23, isotropic shift 33.0 ppm (BCN2 trigonal planar). Elemental compositions in table are mass% of ceramics not polymers.
source: Jaschke_2004_Synthesis_and_characterization_of_new_amorphous_Si_B_N_C_cer

elemental_composition.other_elements: Empirical formula TiC5.4H8.1O3.6 from elemental analysis of 1:1.5 H2O hydrolysis product with acid catalyst: C 36.50 wt%, H 4.67 wt%, Ti 27.86 wt%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Ti-O-Ti units confirmed by IR broadening below 900 cm-1; Ti-OFu (furfuryloxy) groups indicated by furan ring C=C stretching at 1597 and 1504 cm-1 and C-O at 1223 cm-1; Ti-O-n-Bu groups present (C-H stretching 2958, 2932, 2872 cm-1); poly(furfuryl alcohol) component indicated by carbonyl bands at 1762 and 1718 cm-1

functional_groups.other: Furfuryloxy groups (-OFu) from furfuryl alcohol; n-butoxy groups (-O-n-Bu); furan rings with olefinic C-H at 3112 cm-1; poly(furfuryl alcohol) component from acid-catalyzed condensation

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA of 1:1 Ti:FuOH precursor under argon (40-1260 °C) shows three weight-loss steps: (1) 150-270 °C attributed to condensation polymerization of furfuryl groups and decomposition of Ti-O-n-Bu groups; (2) 270-480 °C attributed to decomposition of furan rings (forming carbon); (3) 760-1250 °C attributed to carbothermic reduction of TiO2 to form TiC. Heating rate 200 °C/h (3.33 °C/min). Hold times ranged 3-12 h depending on experiment.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: acid-catalyzed condensation polymerization of furfuryl alcohol component (H2SO4 catalyst)

backbone_architecture.description: Polymeric solid formed by hydrolysis and condensation of Ti(0-n-Bu)4 partially exchanged with furfuryl alcohol, yielding Ti-O-Ti linked network with pendant furfuryloxy and n-butoxy groups, plus interpenetrating poly(furfuryl alcohol) network formed by acid-catalyzed condensation. Approximate molecular formula of precursor unit: [O0.5Ti(OFu)1-x(O-n-Bu)x]n

microstructural.ceramic_phase: TiC or TiN depending on pyrolysis atmosphere

notes: This paper describes poly(aminoborane) (NH2BH2)x as a boron nitride preceramic polymer, not a silicon-based preceramic polymer. It is isolated as a white powder by-product during synthesis of borazine from NaBH4 and (NH4)2SO4 in tetraglyme. Yield of polymer isolation was approximately 5% (about 1g). The polymer is air-stable, unlike borazine oligomers. Solid-state 15N and 11B NMR confirmed chain-like structure with tetracoordinated N (NH2B2, NHB2) and B (BH2N2, BNH3) sites. Above 200C, dehydrogenative condensation converts linear chains to B3N3 ring structures confirmed by NMR and IR. DSC heating rate was 10C/min to 500C; TGA heating rate was 10C/min to 1000C. Furnace pyrolysis conducted at 1000-1400C for 3h periods in nitrogen. The 75% ceramic yield to BN is noted as relatively high compared to SiC and carbon precursors. Classified as a graphitizable BN precursor. Mass spectra at 30-40C identified dimeric (B2N2H9, 59 m/e) and trimeric (B3N2H12, 73 m/e) fragments; no borazine monomer at 81 m/e detected in fresh samples.

TOF-SIMS shows compositional gradient in VUV-converted films: SiOx-rich near surface (0-30 nm), higher Si-N concentration at depth. notes: PHPS is distinguished from organopolysilazanes by its completely carbon-free backbone (Si, N, H only). Synthesized by ammonolysis of DCS-pyridine adduct (Isoda and Arai, 1985) or by reaction of DCS with NH3 in polar solvents (Seyferth, 1983). Must be handled strictly under dry inert atmosphere (N2 or Ar) due to moisture sensitivity. FTIR signature: Si-H at 2160 cm-1, Si-N at 840 cm-1, Si-O at ~1070 cm-1. VUV (172 nm) curing produces SiNx with refractive index >1.74 (up to 1.88 with prolonged exposure) under N2 atmosphere; effective photon penetration depth ~200 nm. Increasing humidity during VUV curing decreases refractive index from 1.73 to 1.64 (0% to 60% RH). High-purity SiNx, SiOx, and SiOxNy networks accessible by selecting conversion route and atmosphere. Applications include barrier coatings for flexible electronics (OLEDs, PSCs), STI dielectric fill in semiconductors, corrosion-protective coatings, aerospace atomic oxygen resistant coatings, and silicon nitride ceramic fibers/nanocomposites. Nitrogen content decreases from 33.6% to below 0.5% after ammonia vapor catalytic curing. Ceramic yield range 82-93% noted; midpoint 87.5% used for ceramic_yield_pct field but 82% (lower bound of Isoda/Arai range) entered as representative; Seyferth reported ~70%. PDI not reported.

notes: PCS is described as a dark black brittle solid with melt point 125–135 °C. DVB (boiling point 138 °C) serves dual role as diluent and crosslinking agent. NH3 atmosphere pretreatment tested but showed low efficiency for carbon removal. Extraction of soluble PCS with xylene before pyrolysis (removing 8–10 wt%) improves pyrolysis quality. backbone_architecture.description: Liquid highly branched polycarbosilane (HBPCS) with vinyl or allyl end groups; forms three-dimensional network upon UV curing

notes: This paper focuses on UV curing kinetics and mechanism of HBPCS, not on pyrolysis or ceramic conversion. Key findings: (1) UV curing in N2 is controlled by photolysis of photoinitiator with activation energy ~12.07 kJ/mol (without TPGDA) and ~12.81 kJ/mol (with TPGDA); (2) UV curing in air shows lower activation energies (~2.62 kJ/mol without TPGDA, ~5.59 kJ/mol with TPGDA) due to additional oxygen-assisted curing and Norrish type I reactions; (3) FTIR confirms vinyl/CH=CH2 group consumption during crosslinking (3073 cm-1 and 1630 cm-1 bands reduced); (4) Si-OH formation observed at 3700 cm-1 in air-cured samples due to oxidation of Si-H; (5) study conditions: 4 wt% photoinitiator, 0 or 10 wt% TPGDA, light intensity 38.8 mW/cm2, temperatures 0-75 degrees C; (6) modified autocatalytic kinetic model used with diffusion correction term.
source: Li_2008_UV_curing_kinetics_and_mechanism_of_a_highly_branched_polyca

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2 backbone linkages; vinyl (C=C) groups present; IR integration ratio Si-H/Si-CH3 decreases from 7.94 to 5.71 upon heat treatment indicating consumption of Si-H groups

functional_groups.other: Vinyl content varies between samples: 3% in one batch, 9% in another batch (calculated from 1H-NMR)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three-stage weight loss observed: first between 150-290 C (distillation of light oligomers), second between 290-490 C (hydrosilylation and dehydrocoupling reactions), third above 490 C (evolution of methane and hydrogen gases). Exothermic DSC peak at ~230 C from hydrosilylation/dehydrocoupling and at ~380 C from vinyl polymerization. Average ceramic yields range from ~55.5% to ~62.01% depending on curing/catalyst conditions and pressure. Pyrolysis under 0.1 MPa pressure increases ceramic yield by 5-8% compared to ambient pressure.

crosslink_density.value: Gel content: untreated sample 17.7%; increases with heat treatment temperature, plateaus above 250 C; catalyst (H2PtCl6) improves crosslinking degree
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (170 C for 6 h under argon); catalytic with chloroplatinic acid (H2PtCl6·6H2O, 0.2 wt%) promoting hydrosilylation; reactions include hydrosilylation, dehydrocoupling, and vinyl polymerization

backbone_architecture.description: Liquid highly branched polycarbosilane synthesized by Grignard coupling of chloromethylmethyldichlorosilane (Cl2MeSiCH2Cl), (chloromethyl)trichlorosilane (Cl3SiCH2Cl), and allyl chloride (ClCH2CH=CH2), followed by reduction with LiAlH4

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: HBPCS is described as a precursor to SiC-based ceramics; specific phase composition of pyrolyzed ceramic not detailed in this text

notes: Two batches of HBPCS were studied: one with 3% vinyl content (Mn=756, PDI=3.06) and one with 9% vinyl content. Ceramic yield data from Tables 1 and 2: without catalyst averages 55.5% and 58.2%; with chloroplatinic acid catalyst averages 59.6% and 61.5% respectively. Pyrolysis under 0.1 MPa argon gas pressure increases yield by 5-8% over ambient pressure. Heating rate of 4 C/min during pyrolysis gave higher ceramic yield than 1 C/min. Post-treatment temperature (200-400 C) increases crosslinking and pyrolysis yield but has little effect on final ceramic yield (liquid polymer to ceramic conversion). Ramping time from 170 to 200 C (20 to 4320 min) has little effect on final ceramic yield. TGA-DSC conducted in argon at 10 C/min (Netzsch STA 409C). Gel content measured by Soxhlet extraction with xylene.
source: Li_2009_Effect_of_curing_and_pyrolysis_processing_on_the_ceramic_yie

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Allyl groups (CH2CH=CH2) attached to Si; chemical formula [SiH1.2(CH3)0.71(CH2CH=CH2)0.09CH2]n

functional_groups.other: allyl groups (CH2CH=CH2), content 0.0039 mol/g as determined by 1H NMR

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV/photo-initiated radical polymerization using Photocure-1173 (2-Hydroxy-2-Methyl-Phenyl-Propane-1-one) as photoinitiator; TPGDA used as reactive diluent to accelerate crosslinking

backbone_architecture.description: Highly branched polycarbosilane (HBPCS) in liquid form with allyl end groups; repeat unit formula [SiH1.2(CH3)0.71(CH2CH=CH2)0.09CH2]n; average molecular weight reported as 670 g/mol

notes: Paper focuses on UV curing behavior of HBPCS using DPC measurements, not on pyrolysis or ceramic properties. Molecular weight reported as 670 g/mol (likely Mn based on context) with PDI of 2.9. Optimal UV curing conditions identified: 4 wt% photoinitiator (Photocure-1173), 10 wt% TPGDA, 25°C, 38.8 mW/cm2 light intensity (320-500 nm, 100W Hg lamp). Nitrogen atmosphere gives higher maximum curing rate but lower ultimate conversion than air. TPGDA content >10 wt% reduces ultimate conversion due to rapid dense network formation increasing viscosity. Allyl group content in HBPCS: 0.0039 mol/g by 1H NMR. Polymerization enthalpies used: allyl 84 kJ/mol, acrylate 77.9 kJ/mol.

polymer_name: CPSZ (copolysilazane); specific designations: CPSZ1, CPSZ2, CPSZ3

elemental_composition.other_elements: Compositions reported as average formula per Si: CPSZ1 polymer SiC1.19N0.74O0.03; CPSZ2 polymer SiC1.15N0.80O0.03; CPSZ3 polymer SiC1.12N0.89O0.03. See notes for ceramic compositions.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three main weight loss regions: 0.5-2 wt% (180-300C) from transamination/low-MW oligomer distillation; 3 wt% (300-500C) from ammonia and hydrogen evolution via transamination and dehydrogenation; 13 wt% (500-900C) ceramization step involving dehydrogenation and demethanation. Polymer-to-ceramic conversion complete at 900C. Ceramic yield range 81-84% (midpoint 82.5% used). For pyrolysis above 900C, heating rate was 40C/min with 10 min hold.

crosslink_density.value: Vinyl reaction degree (P_vinyl) = 34%; Si-H reaction degree (P_Si-H) = 10%; N-H reaction degree (P_N-H) = 9% at 180C after 24h
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - cured at 180C for 24h in argon atmosphere via hydrosilylation and transamination reactions

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC in THF at 35C against narrow polystyrene standards (Agilent 1100 system). CPSZ1: Mn=400, Mw=1700, PDI=4.2; CPSZ2: Mn=500, Mw=2300, PDI=4.6; CPSZ3: Mn=600, Mw=4500, PDI=7.5. Values are per-polymer; null used here as multiple polymers reported - see notes.

backbone_architecture.description: Branched copolysilazane network derived from coammonolysis of CH3SiHCl2 (difunctional), CH3Si(CH=CH2)Cl2 (difunctional), and CH3SiCl3 (trifunctional). The trifunctional CH3SiCl3 introduces branching points [CH3Si(NH)1.5] units. Structural units: [CH3HSiNH], [CH3(CH2=CH)SiNH], and [CH3Si(NH)1.5]. Wide molecular weight distribution attributed to branching.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN (amorphous at 900C; crystalline SiC forms at 1600C)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 900C: amorphous SiCN with Si-N and Si-C bonds confirmed by FTIR. At 1400C: similar amorphous structure. At 1600C: crystalline SiC formation indicated by sharpening of Si-C bands at 780 and 900 cm-1. Ceramic compositions per Si at 900C: CPSZ1 SiC0.69N0.86O0.09; CPSZ2 SiC0.66N0.88O0.12; CPSZ3 SiC0.60N1.01O0.15. At 1400C: CPSZ1 SiC0.71N0.86O0.08; CPSZ2 SiC0.70N0.93O0.09; CPSZ3 SiC0.68N1.04O0.16.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous at 900C and 1400C; crystalline SiC indicated by FTIR at 1600C. XRD, Raman, and TEM used for microstructural characterization but specific XRD phases not detailed in provided text excerpt.

notes: Three copolysilazane variants synthesized with CH3SiHCl2/CH3Si(CH=CH2)Cl2/CH3SiCl3 feed molar ratios of 3/1/1 (CPSZ1), 3/1/2 (CPSZ2), and 3/1/4 (CPSZ3). Molecular weight data per polymer: CPSZ1 Mn=400 g/mol, Mw=1700 g/mol, PDI=4.2; CPSZ2 Mn=500 g/mol, Mw=2300 g/mol, PDI=4.6; CPSZ3 Mn=600 g/mol, Mw=4500 g/mol, PDI=7.5. Ceramic yield range 81-84% (midpoint 82.5 used). Pyrolysis above 900C used 40C/min heating rate with 10 min hold. Polymers reported as liquid, not sensitive to air/moisture. One-step synthesis via coammonolysis in hexane solvent. Synthesis yield approximately 60%. Reactions involved in polymer-to-ceramic conversion: hydrosilylation, transamination, dehydrogenation, and demethanation. 29Si NMR peaks: -14 to -17 ppm (N2Si(CH3)CH=CH2), -22 ppm (N2Si(H)CH3), -22 ppm (N3SiCH3), -32 ppm (NSi(H2)CH3).
source: Li_2011_Synthesis_and_polymertoceramic_conversion_of_tailorable_copo

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental composition reported for final ceramic fiber (wt%): Si 21.25, B 27.54, N 50.26, O 0.62, C 0.12; formula Si0.3BN1.4

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds identified by FT-IR at 1380 and 801 cm-1; amorphous Si-N at 986 cm-1

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Uncured polyborosilazane fibers show 65 wt% weight loss up to 1000°C in Ar (ceramic yield ~35%). Fully HSiCl3-cured fibers show ceramic yield up to 73 wt% in Ar. TGA conducted under Ar at 5°C/min.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: Chemical vapor curing with trichlorosilane (HSiCl3) at 80°C for 0.5 h (heating rate 4°C/min); partial curing used to produce hollow fibers

backbone_architecture.description: Synthesized via one-pot approach using boron trichloride and hexamethyldisilazane as starting materials; hypothesized structure referenced in supporting information but not described in main text

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD confirms amorphous structure; FT-IR identifies BN and amorphous Si-N phases; hollow fiber diameter ~16 μm with inner hollow pore ~4 μm

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Average tensile strength 1.03 GPa (max observed 1.68 GPa); elastic modulus 106 GPa; measured by single filament tensile test with 25 mm gauge length

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases identified; fully amorphous by XRD

notes: Paper reports fabrication of hollow Si-B-N ceramic fibers from polyborosilazane precursor fibers (~23 μm diameter) via melt-spinning at 190°C in N2, partial chemical vapor curing with HSiCl3 at 80°C for 0.5 h, and pyrolysis at 1000°C under NH3. The hollow structure arises because outer fiber is cured (high ceramic yield) while uncured inner core decomposes during pyrolysis. Dielectric properties: average real part of dielectric constant (εr) = 3.06, loss tangent (tan δ) = 0.0032 at 2-18 GHz. Ceramic yield of 35% for uncured fibers is midpoint interpretation; text states 65 wt% weight loss, implying ~35 wt% ceramic yield.
source: Li_2012_Preparation_of_hollow_Si_B_N_ceramic_fibers_by_partial_curin

notes: m-PVSZ synthesized by reaction of PVSZ with 1,1-bis(acryloyloxyethyl) ethyl isocyanate (BAEI) at 25°C for 72 h in THF under dry nitrogen; yield 70.8%. Photocuring characterized by DPC: strong exothermic peak within 10 sec of UV irradiation at 250 nm; peak heat flow 7.5 W/g (more than double that of single-acrylated i-PVSZ at 3.3 W/g). FT-IR shows >90% decrease in C=C absorption at 1407 cm-1 within 1 second of UV irradiation. Used as negative-type inorganic photoresist. Line patterns with smallest width 235 nm fabricated by TPA stereolithography at 780 nm. UV imprint patterns: ~125 nm depth, ~1.60 μm width. Photoinitiator Irgacure 369 used at 5 wt%. microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD shows strong HfC peaks indexed to fcc HfC (JCPDS 65-0964) and weak graphite C peaks from carbon fiber substrate. Lattice constant a=4.6472 Å (bulk HfC a=4.6500 Å). High-purity stoichiometric HfC nanowires confirmed. HRTEM lattice fringe spacing 0.267 nm consistent with (111) planes of HfC. mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Hardness 26.1 GPa and modulus 350-510 GPa (midpoint 430 GPa) are cited as bulk HfC properties, not measured for the synthesized nanowires in this study

notes: Paper focuses on synthesis of HfC nanowires by catalyst-assisted pyrolysis of PHC (a hafnium-containing organometallic preceramic polymer) on carbon fiber substrates using Ni(NO3)2·6H2O as catalyst. Ceramic yield of ~50% refers to total mass loss at >1200°C stage. Heating rate range 3-5°C/min for curing and 5-10°C/min for high-temperature pyrolysis; midpoint values used (4 and 7.5°C/min respectively). Pyrolysis temperatures investigated: 1450, 1500, 1550, 1600°C; optimal temperature identified as 1550°C. Optimal catalyst concentration: 2 wt% Ni(NO3)2·6H2O. Nanowire diameters 50-200 nm, length several micrometers at optimal conditions. Growth mechanism identified as solid-liquid-solid (SLS). Mechanical properties cited are for bulk HfC from literature, not experimental measurements. Ceramic yield pct 50 represents the weight loss above 1200°C stage; note total weight loss from RT is ~50% but first stage (RT-500°C) accounts for ~40%.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed under N2 atmosphere at 10°C/min from 50 to 1000°C. Ceramic yield of TBPB-cured LHBPCS was 79.0 wt% vs 66.4 wt% for as-received. Pyrolysis protocol: ramp at 10°C/min to 1000°C, hold 1 hour, then ramp at 5°C/min to final temperature (1200, 1400, or 1600°C), hold 1 hour. Ceramic yields at different temperatures: 1000°C=79.0 wt%, 1200°C=81.0 wt%, 1400°C=81.0 wt%, 1600°C=77.5 wt%.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous at 1000°C; partially crystalline beta-SiC at 1200°C (broad XRD peaks at 2theta=35.6° (111), 60.0° (220), 71.8° (311)); increasing crystallinity with temperature; well-crystallized beta-SiC at 1600°C. conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous at 1000°C; semi-crystalline at 1200-1400°C; crystalline at 1600°C
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (cubic); diffraction peaks at 2theta=35.6° (111), 60.0° (220), 71.8° (311)

notes: Crosslinking with 1 wt% TBPB at 80°C for 1 hour suppressed dehydrocoupling and hydrosilylation side reactions observed in traditional thermal curing (DSC exotherms between 200-275°C nearly eliminated). Rheology showed gelation point at ~4 min for 1 wt% TBPB and ~8 min for 0.5 wt% TBPB at 80°C. PDI calculated from reported Mn=665 and Mw=2376 g/mol (PDI=3.57). notes: PSZ synthesized from dichloromethylsilane and dichlorodimethylsilane with NH3 in the authors' laboratory. Primary JSON fields populated for PATCS-1 as the main studied material. Ceramic yield range for PATCS series: 67.34-70.34%. Pyrolysis temperature for fiber production was 1373 K (1100 C); TGA only measured to 1273 K (1000 C). Curing performed at 473 K (~200 C) in air for ~1 h. 29Si NMR shows SiC4/SiC3H ratio changes: PCS 1.00:1.90, PACS 1.00:1.35, PATCS 1.00:1.02, indicating consumption of SiC3H (Si-H) units during polymerization. PATCS-4 (high metal content) is a crosslinked solid. Synthesis performed at 583 K for 1 h under N2 by reaction with n-hexane as solvent followed by distillation.

notes: PBSZ is not a conventional polyborosilazane; it is a phenolic resin-based preceramic polymer containing Si, Zr, and B introduced via coordination chemistry using TEOS, ZrOCl2·8H2O, and H3BO3. Polymer type field uses 'polyborosilazane' loosely; more accurately it is a boron-silicon-zirconium containing phenolic resin precursor. The polymer is carbon-rich (60.33 at% C). Grain size range: ~200 nm at 1800°C to ~500 nm at 1900°C; midpoint 350 nm reported. Raman analysis showed D and G band evolution with increasing graphitization order; 2D peak appeared at 1500°C and FWHM decreased from 96 to 65 cm-1 between 1500°C and 1900°C indicating increasing carbon order. SiC whiskers grow via vapor-solid (VS) mechanism. Synthesis involves condensation of phenol/paraformaldehyde, hydrolysis of ZrOCl2 and TEOS, coordination with acetylacetone, ligand exchange, and condensation with boric acid.

notes: This is a doctoral thesis covering multiple related preceramic polymer systems: polycarbosilane (PCS, analogous to Nicalon precursor) and polycarbosilazane (PCSZ-I, II, III). PCSZ synthesized from PSSZ (polysilylsilazane). Three PCSZ variants differ in molecular weight and crosslink density. Pyrolytic ceramic residues are Si-C-N-O quaternary ceramics. Gas evolved during pyrolysis: H2 (10.2-17.6 mol/kg) and CH4 (4.0-6.6 mol/kg). Oxidation kinetics of ex-PCSZ-II filaments studied in dry oxygen at 1000-1400°C; silica scale forms with parabolic growth kinetics (activation energy ~170 kJ/mol). Pilling-Bedworth coefficient for Si-C-N-O system ~1.26-1.41. Pyrolysis stages: organic-to-inorganic transition occurs between ~450-850°C. Elemental compositions of ceramic residues at various temperatures are tabulated. Pyrolysis heating rate of 200K/h = ~3.33 K/min = ~3.33 C/min; final heat treatment at 1673K at 460K/h in graphite furnace. Pyrolysis temperature stated as 1373 K (1100 C). Heating rate given as 200 K/h = ~3.33 K/min.

Fiber from blended precursor maintains strength at 1673 K but loses it at 1773 K. When blended precursor cured at lower temperature (443 K), ceramic fiber maintains strength at 1773 K but intrinsic room-temperature strength is ~0.5 GPa. Gauge length 10 mm, measurements averaged over 10 tests.

notes: Study investigates blends of 0%, 10%, and 20 wt% PVS in PCS melt-spun into fibers. PVS lowers precursor melting point enabling spinning at lower temperatures (590K for 0% PVS, 520K for 10%, 480K for 20% PVS). bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si bonds present in precursor polymer backbone; Si-Si bond scission occurs during pyrolysis (~400-450°C) with transition to polycarbosilane backbone

functional_groups.other: Reactive Si-H sites noted as numerous and important for high ceramic yield

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Four regions observed in TGA/DTA: (I) solvent loss below 100°C; (II) sharp weight loss with exothermic events 200-500°C including Si-Si bond scission peaking at ~450°C (PMS NX) or ~400°C (PMS L); (III) constant gentle weight loss 600-850°C; (IV) increased weight loss with exothermic peak above ~850°C. Samples heated to ≤400°C held 0.8 h; samples heated to >400°C held 1.5 h. Ceramic yields: PMS N ~10% (TGA), PMS NX ~78%, PMS L ~74%.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic (dimethylzirconocene, DMZ, for PMS NX); monomer conservation during synthesis for PMS L

backbone_architecture.description: Three variants synthesized: PMS N (low molecular weight, low crosslinking ~41%, fluid/not specified physical state), PMS NX (catalytically crosslinked with DMZ, ~50% crosslinking, viscous oil), PMS L (highly crosslinked 60-70%, solid, produced by conserving volatile monomer with -20°C condenser). General formula (MeHSi)x(MeSi)y. Si:C ratio of 1.0 in polymer state.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis yields >95% SiC with elemental Si as primary contaminant. Amorphous below ~733°C; beta-SiC crystallization begins near 800°C with broad XRD peaks. Crystallite size remains small even at 1000°C.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous below ~733°C; beta-SiC peaks first appear near 800°C, peaks narrow with further heating to 1000°C

notes: Three PMS variants compared: PMS N (no monomer conservation, no DMZ crosslinking, ~41% crosslinking, ~10% ceramic yield by TGA), PMS NX (no monomer conservation, DMZ crosslinked, ~50% crosslinking, viscous oil, ~78% ceramic yield), PMS L (monomer conserved, no DMZ crosslinking, ~61% crosslinking, solid, ~74% ceramic yield). Porosity of ~2-7 vol% observed at 400°C and 800-900°C pyrolysis temperatures (Type I isotherms, microporous). Materials dense to N2 at other temperatures. BET surface areas measured by N2 adsorption at 77K. TGA/FTIR identified three gas evolution periods: MeSiH (200-400°C), CH4 (375-575°C), complex C-H/Si-C/Si-H signals above 625°C. H2 not detectable by FTIR. Porosity development above 800°C attributed to thermochemistry, gaseous product evolution, and/or microstructural changes (crystallization onset). Precursor structure had little apparent effect on porosity development. Ceramic yield midpoint used for porosity_pct: range stated as ~2-7 vol% for PMS L at 866°C, midpoint 4.5%.
source: Nebo_1996_The_influence_of_precursor_structure_on_the_development_of_p_osti266617

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-OEt (triethoxysilane groups present in backbone); after hydrosilylation: Si-CH2-CH2-CH2-O- linkage to grafted PEO chains

functional_groups.other: triethoxysilane groups; allyl-terminated PEO grafted via hydrosilylation; propenyl ether isomer as side product

crosslink_density.value: 0.29 to 0.72 mol PEO grafted per 10 mol Si-H (grafting density delta)
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: moisture curing at room temperature (hydrolysis and condensation); hydrosilylation grafting at 80°C with Karstedt's catalyst under argon

backbone_architecture.description: General formula -(SiR1R2-NR3)n- polysilazane backbone (polymethylhydrosilazane) with triethoxysilane groups; crosslinked by moisture curing via hydrolysis and condensation; PEO chains grafted onto backbone via hydrosilylation of Si-H groups

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Polysilazane described as ceramic precursor for Si/C/N for high-temperature applications; no pyrolysis performed in this study; coatings used as moisture-cured hybrid organic-inorganic materials

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Coatings noted to have excellent resistance against corrosion and abrasion, high brightness, non-stick surface, resistance to heat, fire and UV irradiation (qualitative, from Clariant formulation description)

notes: This paper focuses on grafting of allyl-terminated poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO, MW 350/750/2000 g/mol) onto polysilazane (PSZ, polymethylhydrosilazane with triethoxysilanes, supplied by Clariant) via hydrosilylation using Karstedt's catalyst at 80°C under argon. The resulting PSZ-PEO hybrid coatings are applied by moisture curing at room temperature for anti-fouling (marine bacteria adhesion prevention) applications. No pyrolysis or ceramic conversion was performed. Grafting density ranges from 0.29 to 0.72 mol PEO per 10 mol Si-H depending on PEO MW and Si-H/allyl ratio. Isomerization of allyl-PEO to propenyl ether is a competing side reaction. Coating thicknesses of 0.3 to 50 micrometers are noted for PSZ-based coatings generally.
source: Nguyen_2013_New_hybrid_materials_based_on_polyethyleneoxidegrafted_polys

polymer_name: Zr/Si precursor (zirconium propoxide + triethoxymethylsilane derived preceramic polymer)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Zr and Si present; molar ratio of zirconium propoxide to triethoxymethylsilane is 5:4; exact atomic percentages not reported

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Zr-O-C stretching at 1530 cm-1, Zr-O-Si at 931 cm-1, Zr-OH at 610 cm-1, Si-OH at 854 cm-1, Si-O-Si at 1020 cm-1, Si-(CH3)2 at 794 cm-1, Zr-O-Zr networks; after sol-gel with phenolic resin: Zr-O-C and Si-O-C bonds formed

functional_groups.other: Zirconium hydroxyl (Zr-OH), silicon hydroxyl (Si-OH), acetylacetone chelating groups, Zr-O-C groups

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Zr/Si precursor shows small weight loss before 500 °C due to solvent evaporation and decomposition of organic groups; residual weight ~80% at 900 °C in both N2 and air atmospheres. Hybrid aerogels pyrolyzed first at 1100 °C for 2 h under argon at 2 °C/min, then heat treated at 1700 °C for 2 h under argon at 10 °C/min. R900 in N2 for hybrid aerogels ranges from 50.81% (PR-ZS10) to 61.05% (PR-ZS40). R900 in air increases with Zr/Si content from 13.11% to 28.90%.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal/chemical - HMTA-catalyzed crosslinking at 80 °C for 2 days, post-cured at 120 °C for 2 hours; Zr/Si precursor participates in crosslinked network via Zr-O-C and Si-O-C bonds with phenolic resin

backbone_architecture.description: Zr-O-Zr, Zr-O-Si, and Si-O-Si inorganic networks formed from hydrolysis and condensation of zirconium propoxide and triethoxymethylsilane; chelated with acetylacetone; hybrid aerogel network incorporates Zr-O-C and Si-O-C bonds connecting preceramic polymer to phenolic resin backbone

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After carbonization at 1700 °C, hybrid aerogels transform to carbide ceramic aerogels with ultrafine nanocrystalline ZrC and SiC particles embedded in carbon matrix. Carbothermal reduction converts ZrO2 and SiO2 precursor-derived phases to ZrC and SiC. Intermediate amorphous SiO2 and ZrO2 phases form during lower-temperature pyrolysis.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Compressive stress at 5% strain: PR=1.54 MPa, PR-ZS10=1.03 MPa, PR-ZS20=4.75 MPa, PR-ZS30=3.37 MPa, PR-ZS40=6.83 MPa, PR-1700=2.20 MPa, PR-ZS20-1700=3.35 MPa. Materials with density <0.41 g/cm3 show ductile nonlinear porous deformation; above 0.41 g/cm3 transition to brittle behavior. Linear ablation rate as low as 0.017 mm/min for ceramic aerogel.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: ZrC and SiC nanocrystalline phases identified after carbonization at 1700 °C; precursor and hybrid aerogels presumed amorphous prior to carbonization

notes: This paper describes hybrid phenolic resin (PR) aerogels incorporating a Zr/Si preceramic polymer derived from zirconium(IV) propoxide and triethoxymethylsilane (molar ratio 5:4) chelated with acetylacetone, dissolved in n-propanol, hydrolyzed with deionized water at 80 °C for 8 h, and concentrated to 35 wt% solids. The preceramic polymer acts as both a crosslinking agent and ceramic precursor within the phenolic aerogel matrix. Hybrid aerogel loadings of 10-40 wt% Zr/Si precursor were studied. Thermal conductivities: PR=0.056, PR-ZS10=0.048, PR-ZS20=0.046, PR-ZS30=0.048, PR-ZS40=0.054, PR-1700=0.141, PR-ZS20-1700=0.189 W/(m·K). BET surface area of PR-ZS20-1700 = 96.22 m2/g. Porosity range 53.25-76.90%. Backside temperature below 330 °C at 20 mm depth after 300 s butane torch test with ~960 °C front temperature.
source: Nie_2025_Preceramic_polymer_hybridized_phenolic_aerogels_and_the_deri

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Zr-B bond (stretching vibration at 1375 cm-1 for ZSB-1, 1347 cm-1 for ZSB-2); Si-O bending at 434 and 612 cm-1; O-H stretching at 1637 and 3448 cm-1 in ZSB-1; Si-C stretching at 822 cm-1 in ZSB-2

functional_groups.other: Phenolic resin contains hydroxyl (O-H) groups; crosslinks upon curing at 175 °C

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two pyrolysis temperatures studied: 1500 °C (ZSB-1) and 1650 °C (ZSB-2). At 1500 °C, incomplete conversion with residual ZrSiO4 and SiO2 present alongside ZrB2. At 1650 °C, complete conversion to ZrB2-SiC. Multi-step heating schedule used with varying rates (0.5-3 °C/min) and dwell times at intermediate temperatures. Volatile products such as CO2 evolved during heat treatment, resulting in porosity and density below theoretical value.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - cured at 175 °C for 2 hours to remove volatiles and crosslink the phenolic resin

backbone_architecture.description: Phenolic resin (PF) used as a carbon precursor in a preceramic slurry with ZrSiO4 and B4C; specific backbone architecture not described

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: ZSB-2 (1650 °C): ZrB2 (JCPDS 04-004-5887) and SiC (JCPDS 04-002-9070) in volume ratio 60:40. ZSB-1 (1500 °C): ZrB2, unreacted ZrSiO4 (JCPDS 01-071-4913), and SiO2 (JCPDS 04-002-8291). No impurities (ZrC, ZrSi, borosilicate) detected in ZSB-2.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: ZrB2 (JCPDS 04-004-5887), SiC (JCPDS 04-002-9070) in ZSB-2; ZrSiO4 (JCPDS 01-071-4913), SiO2 (JCPDS 04-002-8291), and minor ZrB2 in ZSB-1

notes: This paper describes a preceramic slurry route to synthesize ZrB2-SiC ultra-high temperature ceramic powder using zirconium silicate (ZrSiO4), boron carbide (B4C), and phenolic resin (carbon source/binder) in weight ratio 6.6:1:3.6, with ethanol as solvent. The precursor is not a silicon-based preceramic polymer (polysilazane, polycarbosilane, etc.) but rather a phenolic resin used as a carbon precursor. Crystallite size of ZrB2 = 69 nm, SiC = 47 nm (by Scherrer equation). Average particle size of ZSB-2 = 6.6 μm. Density of ZSB-2 = 3.77 g/cm3 (lower than theoretical 4.89 g/cm3 by rule of mixtures, due to porosity from volatile evolution). Specific heat of ZSB-2 = 0.17 cal/g/°C. Raw materials ball milled at 110 rpm for 8 h, then cured stepwise up to 175 °C before pyrolysis. Pyrolysis at 1500 °C (ZSB-1) gave incomplete conversion; pyrolysis at 1650 °C (ZSB-2) gave complete conversion. SEM showed coral-like, irregular, agglomerated morphology.
source: NithinChandran_2019_Synthesis_of_Zirconium_diboride_based_ultra_high_temperature

elemental_composition.other_elements: Theoretical formula (CH)n: C 92.31 wt%, H 7.69 wt%; found H ~6.9 wt%, C low and variable (not reliably determined)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C-C network backbone (sp3 tetrahedral carbon); C-H aliphatic at 2976 and 2869 cm-1; C-C stretch at 1083 cm-1; no C=C, C-O, C=O, or C-Cl detected

functional_groups.other: Pendant hydrogen on each tetrahedral carbon; cyclopropane-type ring structures indicated by 1H-NMR peak at ~0.3 ppm

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yield reported as typically 10-40%, highly dependent on processing conditions and molecular weight of polymer. Comparable to poly(phenylcarbyne) yield of 40-45%. Product is hard crystalline lonsdaleite (hexagonal diamond) with some darker material.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC (Polymer Laboratories PL-GPC 220, THF solvent, polystyrene standards)

backbone_architecture.description: Three-dimensional network of tetrahedrally bound carbon atoms, each with a single pendant hydrogen; formula (CH)n; cyclopropane-type ring structures also present

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Primary phase is lonsdaleite (hexagonal diamond, JCPDS 19-0268); possible minor cubic diamond contribution at d=2.06 Å is tenuous due to overlap with lonsdaleite reflections; no graphite or other carbon forms detected. Unit cell: a=2.53 Å, c=4.12 Å.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Described qualitatively as a hard crystalline substance; transparent particles refracting light like gem-quality diamond observed visually

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Lonsdaleite (hexagonal diamond, JCPDS PDF 19-0268); possible trace cubic diamond

notes: Polymer synthesized by electrochemical polymerization of chloroform (1.2 M in acetonitrile) at -6.0 V for 4 h using stainless steel electrodes with 0.1 M tetrabutylammonium tetrafluoroborate electrolyte, under N2, at room temperature. Yield of polymer: 30-40%. Purification involved LiAlH4 reflux to remove halogen, followed by precipitation with hexane from dichloromethane. Chlorine gas emitted during synthesis. Carbon elemental analysis unreliable/low due to rapid conversion to ceramic during combustion analysis, a known phenomenon for ceramic precursors. Polymer soluble, enabling films/fibers/coatings of any shape. 1H-NMR broad resonances at 0.5-2.1 ppm (aliphatic H) and ~0.3 ppm (cyclopropane-type H); no sharp resonances indicating electrolyte contamination. Ceramic yield range 10-40% used; midpoint 25% reported in ceramic_yield_pct field.
source: Nur_2008_Facile_Synthesis_of_Poly_hydridocarbyne_A_Precursor_to_Diamo

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH (methine) bonds present; no C=C, Si-Cl, SiHx, C-O, or C-Cl detected on backbone

functional_groups.other: methine (CH) groups attached to silicon

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA run under nitrogen from 25-850 °C at 20 °C/min. Small weight loss ~10% up to ~300 °C from condensation, solvent/moisture release, and crosslinking. Maximum weight loss ~40% from 280-800 °C due to release of hydrogen and organic moieties during polymer-to-ceramic conversion. Ceramic formation begins at 500 °C under air.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with refractive index detector, TSKgel AM GPC Gel column, DMF eluent, calibrated with polystyrene standards

backbone_architecture.description: Unique network structure of tetrahedral bonded carbon and silicon atoms; primary backbone formula (SiCH)n; methyl substituents added to increase hydrophobicity and moisture resistance

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiO2 (various crystalline polymorphs depending on temperature)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 500 °C: mixture of Coesite, Quartz, and SiO2. At 750 °C: mixture of Coesite, Moganite, and Tridymite. At 1000 °C: mixture of Tridymite-M syn and Moganite. All ceramics are polycrystalline. Crystal size mostly in micrometer scale.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Coesite, Quartz, Tridymite-M syn, Moganite (phases vary by pyrolysis temperature); at 500 °C also some amorphous SiO2 component noted in abstract

notes: Polymer synthesized electrochemically from trichloro(dichloromethyl)silane monomer using TBAFB electrolyte in DME solvent, followed by LAH reduction and MeLi methylation. Polymer yield ~75%. SiO2 ceramic yield ~40%. Pyrolysis performed under ambient air atmosphere (not inert), which is the key novelty enabling SiO2 formation rather than SiC. TGA was conducted separately under nitrogen at 20 °C/min; actual ceramic production used air atmosphere at 10 °C/min with 24 h hold. Abstract mentions 500 °C product as Coesite and amorphous SiO2, while results section states Coesite, Quartz, and SiO2 at 500 °C - minor inconsistency in paper.
source: Nur_2017_Facile_Synthesis_of_SiO2_From_Poly_silyne_co_hydridocarbyne

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si (sp3), Si-Ph (phenyl), Si-CH2, C-C (sp3); possible residual Si-Cl and Si-OH from workup; Si-CH2-Si group present

functional_groups.other: phenyl groups on backbone; CH2 groups; methine (CH) attached to silicon; alkyl chloride and SiCl3 functional groups in monomer (replaced by methyl and hydrogen post-synthesis)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA run from 25 to 850°C at 20°C/min under nitrogen. Initial ~10% mass loss up to ~130°C from residual solvent/moisture. Exothermic behavior onset above 180°C indicating ceramization. Overall weight loss ~80% above 750°C. Decomposition between 200-400°C involves Si atom redistribution between Si-O and Si-C bonds with release of volatile organo-silicon compounds. Ceramic formation achieved above 750°C under inert atmosphere.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: electrochemical polymerization; inherently highly crosslinked backbone from synthesis without post-polymerization crosslinking; no Kumada rearrangement required

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with refractive index detector, DMF eluent, TSK gel AM column, calibrated with polystyrene standards; noted that calibration with linear polystyrene underestimates MW for network polymers

backbone_architecture.description: Highly crosslinked backbone with tetrahedral Si-C network structure (polysilyne/crosslinked polysilane). Extended crosslinked structure from bifunctional monomer (alkyl chloride + SiCl3 groups) without post-polymerization crosslinking. Random network structure confirmed by broad NMR resonances.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Crystalline SiC with moissanite crystals produced at 1000°C for 12 and 24 h under Ar. Crystallinity increases with longer pyrolysis duration. Minimum 12 h at 1000°C recommended for optimal crystallinity.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC (moissanite); crystallinity increases with pyrolysis duration from 3 to 24 h at 1000°C

notes: Polymer synthesized by electrochemical reduction (electrolysis at -8.0 V, 8 h, room temperature, Ar atmosphere) of TMPS monomer in DME with TBAFB supporting electrolyte using 430 SS cathode and Cu anode. Post-electrolysis treatment includes LiAlH4 (hydrogenation, 12 h reflux), MeLi (methylation, overnight), and isopropyl magnesium chloride (Grignard alkylation, overnight reflux) to replace Cl with H and CH3 and improve hydrophobicity. Polymer obtained as light-brown/yellowish-brown powder in 70-80% yield. Stable in air for hours. UV/Vis shows broad absorption at ~200 nm from phenyl groups. Pyrolysis samples designated SiC-12 (12 h hold) and SiC-24 (24 h hold). Semi-quantitative FTIR area ratio A(24h)/A(12h) = 0.89 and intensity ratio I(24h)/I(12h) = 0.98 for 2924 cm-1 peak, suggesting most transformation occurs within 12 h. Ceramic yield of ~20% implied by ~80% weight loss. TGA ceramic yield note: weight loss ~80% stated at >750°C, implying ~20% ceramic yield; pyrolysis temperature for ceramic production is 1000°C in Ar, not 850°C (TGA limit).
source: Nur_2025_The_Electrochemical_Synthesis_of_Crosslinked_Polycarbosilane

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH=CH2 (vinyl), Si-CH2-CH2-Si (ethylene bridge formed after hydrosilylation), C=C stretching observed at 1598 cm-1

functional_groups.other: ethylene spacers (-CH2-CH2-) formed after hydrosilylation of vinyl groups

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yields range from 65-89% depending on hydrogensiloxane type and molar ratio. D4Vi-D4H networks yielded 86-89%, while D4Vi-linear hydrogensiloxane networks yielded 65-76%. Approximately 30 mg sample used. TGA conducted from 30 to 1000 degrees C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic hydrosilylation using Karstedt's catalyst (Pt(0)-1,3-divinyl-1,1,3,3-tetramethyldisiloxane complex)

backbone_architecture.description: Highly cross-linked polysiloxane networks formed by hydrosilylation of 1,3,5,7-tetravinyl-1,3,5,7-tetramethylcyclotetrasiloxane (D4Vi) with linear hydrogensiloxanes (HMMh, HMDMh, HMD2Mh) or cyclic hydrogensiloxane (D4H). Cyclotetrasiloxane rings from D4Vi are linked by linear or cyclic siloxane bridges through ethylene spacers. Products are glassy solids except for HMDMh and HMD2Mh at 0.75 molar ratio to D4Vi which are viscous liquids.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis between 800-1300 degrees C results in silicon oxycarbides (SiCxO4-x, 0<=x<=4), often two-phase Si-C-O systems of silicon oxycarbides and free carbon ('black glasses'). Above 1300 degrees C, transforms to SiC and SiO2, then SiC and C. Products before and after pyrolysis described as monolithic, pore-less materials.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Silicon oxycarbide 'black glasses' exhibit better mechanical properties than conventional quartz glass

notes: Preceramic polysiloxane networks prepared by hydrosilylation of D4Vi with linear hydrogensiloxanes (HMMh, HMDMh, HMD2Mh) and cyclic D4H at various molar ratios (0.75-3.0 for linear; 1.0-2.0 for cyclic). Reactions conducted at 28 degrees C for 48 h under dry Ar atmosphere with Karstedt's catalyst at Pt:SiH molar ratio of 1e-5. FTIR used to monitor SiH consumption via SiH/SiCH3 area ratio. Ceramic yields reported per hydrogensiloxane type: HMMh (3.0)=71%, HMMh (1.5)=76%, HMDMh (3.0)=65%, HMD2Mh (1.5)=76%, HMD2Mh (3.0)=69%, D4H (2.0)=89%. Midpoint ceramic yield of 77% used as summary value; range 65-89% noted.
source: Nyczyk_2011_Preceramic_polysiloxane_networks_obtained_by_hydrosilylation

elemental_composition.other_elements: Composition given in wt%: Si 50.1, C 39.0, O 1.48, H 7.02

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis performed at various temperatures from 1000 to 1500 C in argon gas flow. Curing/pre-heating in air at 190 C for 6 h with 0.5 h hold resulted in 9.4 wt% weight gain due to oxidation.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal/oxidative - pre-heating in air at 110 to 200 C introduces oxygen which cross-links PC molecules and renders the fibre infusible

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Hitachi 117 vapour pressure osmometry

backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosilane prepared by thermal decomposition of polydimethylsilane in an autoclave, then fractionated by precipitation with benzene and methyl alcohol

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiC-A (no air pre-heat): amorphous beta-SiC at 1000-1100 C, microcrystalline beta-SiC at 1200 C, crystalline beta-SiC at 1500 C. SiC-B (air pre-heated): amorphous beta-SiC and SiO2 at 1000-1300 C, mixed at 1400 C, nearly perfect beta-SiC crystallites at 1500 C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Tensile strength and tensile modulus of SiC-A (no air cure) higher than SiC-B (air cured) at 1000-1200 C. Tensile strength of SiC-A highest at 1100 C heat treatment. Both SiC-A and SiC-B have nil tensile strength at 1500 C (fully crystalline beta-SiC). Fibre diameter 15-20 micrometers.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to crystalline depending on pyrolysis temperature

notes: Paper focuses on the effect of oxidative curing (air pre-heating) of polycarbosilane fibre on the tensile strength of the resulting coreless SiC fibre. (PC)H was dissolved in xylene (1 g/1 cm3) and fibres drawn by hand. Pre-heating in air at 190 C for 6 h plus 0.5 h hold caused 9.4 wt% weight gain (oxidation/crosslinking). SiC-B fibres contain SiO2 phase due to oxygen introduced during curing, which reduces density and tensile strength relative to SiC-A. Melt-spinning of lower Mn (~1500) PC also mentioned as standard process but (PC)H with Mn 15900 was used here and solution-drawn.
source: Okamura_1983_Effect_of_oxidation_curing_polycarbosilane_fibre_on_tensile
