backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosilane backbone; polytitanocarbosilane formed by reaction of polycarbosilane with titanium tetrabutoxide in xylene under N2 at elevated temperatures

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous silicon oxynitride (Si-N-O fibers); mixture of beta-SiC, TiC, and alpha-cristobalite (Si-Ti-C fibers at 1200C); beta-SiC and TiC at 1500C
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Si-N-O fibers are amorphous up to at least 1300C; crystallization increases with temperature; alpha-cristobalite forms in Si-Ti-C fibers due to oxidative curing. PC pyrolyzed in NH3 gives alpha-Si3N4. At 1300C in air, Si-N-O fibers show alpha-cristobalite formation.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Si-N-O fibers at 1300C: tensile strength 1.80+/-0.37 GPa, Young's modulus 139+/-17 GPa, density 2.22 g/cm3. Si-N-O fibers at 1400C: Young's modulus 188+/-7 GPa, tensile strength 1.29+/-0.32 GPa, density 2.59 g/cm3. Si-Ti-C (Ti/Si=0.10) fibers at 1200C: tensile strength 0.94+/-0.18 GPa, Young's modulus 129+/-28 GPa, density 2.30 g/cm3. Gauge length 25mm, crosshead speed 2mm/min, n=30 fibers. Fiber diameter ~13 um (Si-N-O).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Si-N-O fibers: amorphous (broad XRD patterns); alpha-Si3N4 from bulk PC pyrolysis in NH3; Si-Ti-C fibers: beta-SiC, TiC-type compound, alpha-quartz at 1200C; beta-SiC and TiC at 1500C; alpha-cristobalite in Si-Ti-C fibers

notes: Paper describes synthesis of two fiber types from polycarbosilane precursor: (1) Si-N-O fibers via nitridation in NH3 gas, and (2) Si-Ti-C fibers from polytitanocarbosilane (PC + titanium tetrabutoxide). PC(Ti) designation -0.05, -0.10, -0.15 refers to Ti/Si molar ratio. Additive quantities: 17.8g, 35.6g, 53.4g of Ti(OBu)4 added to 50g PC. Mn of PC used for PC(Ti) synthesis was 860 g/mol; Mn of PC used for Si-N-O fibers was 1500 g/mol. Ceramic yield of 52% is from PC(Ti)-0.15 which is the maximum reported. Si-N-O fiber at 1400C composition: SiN1.15O0.47. Fibers are colorless, transparent, and electrically insulating.
source: Okamura_1985_SiN0_Fiber_and_SiTic_Fiber_Obtained_from_Polycarbosilane

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C=O stretching observed at 1710 cm-1 after gamma-ray irradiation; Si-O-Si and Si-O-C bonds observed in 1100 cm-1 region upon oxidative crosslinking

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PC fibres heated from room temperature up to 1200°C in vacuum after gamma-ray curing to produce SiC fibres

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: gamma-ray irradiation (Co-60, dose range 10^4 to 10^9 R at 4.5x10^5 R/h) in air; crosslinking mediated by oxygen introduction

backbone_architecture.description: PC synthesized by thermal decomposition and condensation of polydimethylsilane (2000 g) with borodiphenylsiloxane (103 g) at 450°C for 10h under nitrogen

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 10^8 R dose, microcrystalline beta-SiC observed. At 10^9 R, amorphous beta-SiC plus amorphous alpha-cristobalite (broad halo at 2theta~21.9°) due to high oxygen uptake during irradiation

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Tensile strength ~1.8 GPa and tensile modulus ~100 GPa for SiC(gamma) fibres at ~12 micron diameter in dose range 10^6 to 2x10^8 R; comparable pre-heat treatment SiC fibres show ~2.0 GPa strength and ~111 GPa modulus. At 5x10^8 and 10^9 R, both properties are low.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (microcrystalline at lower doses, amorphous at 10^9 R); amorphous alpha-cristobalite at 10^9 R

notes: PC fibres were melt-spun at 280°C into ~12 micron diameter, ~100 mm long fibres. Curing by gamma-ray irradiation requires dose >=10^6 R in air; optimal range is 10^6 to 10^8 R. Synthesis of PC used polydimethylsilane with borodiphenylsiloxane additive, implying possible boron incorporation, but no explicit elemental composition data reported. Fibre diameter ~12 microns. Pre-heat treatment curing in air performed at 110-190°C for comparison. Paper received April 1984.
source: Okamura_1985_ray_irradiation_curing_on_polycarbosilane_fibres_as_the_prec

elemental_composition.other_elements: Oxygen content in resulting SiC fibers ranges from <0.5 to 10.8 mass%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Peroxy radicals (Si-O-O) formed during oxygen-atmosphere irradiation; radical species -Si(CH3)-CH2- identified

functional_groups.other: Peroxy radicals formed upon oxygen exposure

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Heat treatment performed at various temperatures (1473 K and 1773 K) in Ar stream; SiO and CO gas evolution occurs above 1573 K leading to crystal structure changes

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: radiation (gamma-ray and electron beam irradiation); also radiation oxidation in oxygen atmosphere

backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosilane melt-spun into fibers at 583 K in N2 gas flow by monohole method; cross-linking occurs between polycarbosilane molecules via radical recombination

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Resulting fiber is amorphous with ~10 mass% oxygen when thermally oxidation-cured; oxygen-controlled SiC fibers prepared by radiation curing have oxygen contents ranging from <0.5 to 10.8 mass%; crystal growth of SiC occurs near surface during heat treatment

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Tensile strength of SiC fibers after heat treatment at 1773 K: ~2.5 GPa; Young's modulus ranges from 181 to 220 GPa depending on oxygen content (see table); tensile strength ranges 2.49-2.64 GPa across fiber types

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC (crystallizes during high-temperature heat treatment above 1573 K)

notes: Paper focuses on radiation curing (gamma-ray and electron beam) of polycarbosilane fibers as alternative to thermal oxidation curing, aimed at controlling oxygen content in resulting SiC fibers. Two curing routes described: (1) oxidation curing in oxygen atmosphere controlling oxygen uptake via dose and dose rate, and (2) crosslinking in vacuum/He atmosphere followed by annealing to eliminate residual radicals, yielding low-oxygen SiC fibers. Free radicals on Si and C atoms produced during irradiation; H2 and small amounts of CH4 evolved. Residual radical concentration ~1% after annealing at 513 K. Young's modulus and high-temperature tensile strength increase with decreasing oxygen content. Gauge length for tensile tests: 25 mm; crosshead speed: 2 mm/min.
source: Okamura_1992_Application_of_radiation_curing_in_the_preparation_of_polyca

elemental_composition.other_elements: F present as organofluoric groups (OCH2CF2CF3 side chains); exact atomic percentages not reported

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-C bonds at 1100 cm-1; C-F bonds at 1200 cm-1 (from OCH2CF2CF3 side chains); Si-Cl bonds at 480 cm-1 in intermediate PCCl; Si-CH2-Si bonds at 1100 cm-1; Si-O-Si bonds formed during pyrolysis

functional_groups.other: Organofluoric groups (OCH2CF2CF3); hydroxyl groups present

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis occurs in three stages: (1) below 300°C - 15.9% weight loss due to evaporation of low molecular species; (2) 300-600°C - 40.1% weight loss (largest stage) due to decomposition of OCF side chains; (3) 600-1000°C - 7.0% weight loss due to decomposition of Si-CH3 and C-H bonds. Ceramic yield of PCOCF itself is 37% at 1000°C vs. 19% for unmodified PC. When coated on SiC powder, ceramic yield improves to 55% at 1000°C with reduced weight loss at each stage (13.6%, 25.6%, 5.6% respectively).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - Si-O-Si bond formation during pyrolysis stage 2 (300-600°C)

molecular_weight.measurement_method: reported as mean molecular weight for the starting unmodified PC (Nippon Carbon, Type L); method not specified

backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosilane backbone (Si-CH2-Si repeating units) with OCH2CF2CF3 organofluoric side chains introduced via reaction of Si-Cl intermediate with sodium fluoric alkoxide (NaOCH2CF2CF3); Si-CH3 side chains also present

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis of PCOCF at 1000°C yields nanocrystallites of beta-SiC. Product at 800°C is amorphous with chemical composition close to SiC. FTIR at 1000°C matches beta-SiC crystal spectrum.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC confirmed by selected-area electron diffraction (TEM)

notes: PCOCF synthesized in three steps: (1) PC chlorinated to PCCl via CCl4/BPO converting Si-H to Si-Cl; (2) sodium fluoric alkoxide (NaOCH2CF2CF3) prepared from CF3CF2CH2OH and NaH in THF; (3) PCCl reacted with NaOCH2CF2CF3 to yield PCOCF. Starting PC is Nippon Carbon Type L (mean MW 800). Unmodified PC ceramic yield is 19% vs. 37% for PCOCF at 1000°C. Green body density increased from 1.88 g/cm3 (uncoated) to 1.98 g/cm3 with 5 wt% PCOCF coating on SiC powder. TGA performed under helium flow. Density of both unmodified PC and PCOCF given as 1.1 g/cm3. Crystallite size of ~1 nm determined by TEM at 1000°C.
source: Okuzaki_1999_Synthesis_and_Properties_of_Chemically_Modified_Polycarbosil

elemental_composition.other_elements: B, N present in borazine (B3N3) core; polymer contains B, N, C, H, S (thiophene), no quantitative atomic percentages reported

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds in borazine core (IR band at 1353 cm-1, B-N stretching); N=N azo bonds; B-C bonds (boron linked to carbon aryl groups); thiophene C-C and C-S bonds

functional_groups.other: azobenzene (azo, -N=N-) groups; borazine (B3N3) core; hexyl side chains; octyl side chains; triflate (OTf) groups on precursor; boronic ester (BPin) groups on monomer precursor

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA shows 5 wt% mass loss starting at 203 C and approximately 30 wt% loss at 351 C; polymer is not a preceramic polymer and is not pyrolyzed to ceramic; DSC shows Tg at ~112 C, no melting or crystallization peaks observed, suggesting amorphous nature

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC relative to polystyrene standard in THF (+2% Et3N) at 30 C; degree of polymerization (DP) = 9

backbone_architecture.description: Conjugated polymer backbone formed by Suzuki cross-coupling polycondensation; repeat unit contains borazine (B3N3) core linked via aryl groups to azobenzene-functionalized 3-hexylthiophene units

notes: This paper does not describe a preceramic polymer. P(AB-3HT-borazine) is a BN-doped conjugated organic polymer (borazine-doped polythiophene) designed for optoelectronic applications, not ceramic precursor chemistry. The borazine core (B3N3) is an inorganic benzene analog incorporated into the polymer backbone. Key properties: optical band gap 2.27 eV (from absorption onset at 548 nm in solid state), electrochemical band gap 2.28 eV, HOMO -5.36 eV, LUMO -3.08 eV. Polymer shows intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) behavior and solvatochromism. Polymer does not undergo photoisomerization switching unlike the small molecule azo-borazine-3. Azo-borazine-3 small molecule (not the polymer) shows reversible E/Z photoisomerization at 360 nm irradiation. Molecular weight of 13.2 kDa (Mn) with dispersity 1.92 and DP=9 measured by GPC. Polymer is soluble in CH2Cl2, CHCl3, THF, toluene but insoluble in acetone, methanol, n-heptane. Tg ~112 C by DSC.
source: Oubaha_2019_Photoactive_Boron_Nitrogen_Carbon_Hybrids_From_Azo_borazines

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si bridges (790-900 cm-1), Si-O ring with 4 Si atoms (565-585 cm-1), Si-OH groups present in intermediate T4OH; C-H stretching (2900-3000 cm-1)

functional_groups.other: ethoxy groups (introduced via substitution of Si-H with ethoxyls prior to polycondensation); silanol (Si-OH) groups in intermediate

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed at 10 K/min in argon atmosphere. Multi-step annealing: 70C/2h, 120C/4h, 200C/4h, then final temperature (600, 700, 800, or 900C) for 30 min. Mass loss percentages recorded at each annealing step for various samples; e.g., T:D sample showed 25.06%, 15.74%, and 4.38% mass loss in steps I, II, and III respectively.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (sol-gel polycondensation with HCl catalyst at pH 4.5, followed by thermal annealing)

backbone_architecture.description: Macromonomer based on 2,4,6,8-tetramethylcyclotetrasiloxane (4-membered Si-O ring, D4H) modified with chlorodimethylsilane to attach D structural units; contains both T units (Si bonded to 3 oxygen atoms and 1 carbon) and D units (Si bonded to 2 oxygen atoms and 2 carbons). After polycondensation, forms a networked polysiloxane gel.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Silicon oxycarbide (black glass) with glassy Si-O phase and free carbon phase (turbostratic carbon domains or graphene-like sheets). Carbon atoms either incorporated into Si matrix replacing oxygen pairs, or present as free-carbon phase. Carbon per silicon atom ratio in final material ranged approximately 0.64-0.94 depending on sample composition and annealing temperature.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Increased bond density and composite structure reported to enhance mechanical resistance (referenced, not measured in this study)

notes: Study investigates multiple precursor compositions with varying T:D structural unit ratios (1:1, 3:2, 2:1, 4:1) using either macromonomer (T4D2.67, T4M2.67H) or simple monomers (triethoxymethylsilane + diethoxydimethylsilane) as references. Key finding: macromonomer approach prevents formation of volatile carbon-rich oligomers, improving carbon retention. Elemental analysis reported as carbon atoms per silicon atom rather than atomic percent; values at 700C and 800C range from 0.64 to 0.94 C/Si depending on sample. Pyrolysis temperatures investigated: 600, 700, 800, and 900C. XRD measurements performed (5-65 deg range, Cu Ka). 29Si NMR used for macromonomer structure confirmation. IR spectroscopy (MIR, 4000-400 cm-1) used for structural characterization. Sol-gel synthesis used HCl catalyst at pH 4.5, 2 mol water per mol Si, stirred 4h (simple monomers) or 48h (complex monomers).
source: Owinska_2021_Macromonomers_as_a_Novel_Way_to_Investigate_and_Tailor_Silic

elemental_composition.other_elements: Zirconium-based precursor (zirconium alkoxide + benzene-1,4-diol carbon source); final ceramic is ZrC

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Zr-O bonds in precursor xerogel; Zr-C bonds in carbide product after carbothermal reduction; precursor contains metal chelate (Zr-acac), Zr-O-C linkages via transesterification and polycondensation with benzene-1,4-diol

functional_groups.other: Acetylacetonate (chelating ligand), hydroxyl groups from benzene-1,4-diol, alkoxide groups from zirconium(IV) butoxide

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: argon (initial pyrolysis at 800°C); vacuum at 10^-2 mbar (carbothermal reduction at 1300°C)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis at 800°C under argon for 1 h decomposes xerogel to ZrO2 and carbon; subsequent carbothermal reduction at 1300°C under vacuum converts ZrO2 + C to ZrC. Heating rate 200°C/h (~3.33°C/min) used for both steps.

backbone_architecture.description: Precursor xerogel presumably contains cyclic as well as linearly connected polymers formed by polycondensation of zirconium alkoxide chelate with benzene-1,4-diol

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Sol-gel route produces ZrC via carbothermal reduction; incomplete reduction may result in oxygen, oxide, or oxycarbide impurities. Chlorination of ZrC at 700-900°C yields carbide-derived carbon (CDC) with micro- and mesoporosity. Commercial ZrC-CDC yields primarily microporous carbon.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: ZrC (from XRD analysis of carbide samples); carbon materials analyzed by XRD and Raman spectroscopy

notes: This paper is not about a preceramic polymer in the traditional sense (e.g., polysilazane/polycarbosilane). It describes a sol-gel derived zirconium carbide precursor xerogel synthesized from zirconium(IV) butoxide and benzene-1,4-diol with acetylacetone as chelating ligand. The ZrC is then chlorinated to produce carbide-derived carbon (CDC) for supercapacitor electrodes. Sol-gel ZrC surface area: 65 m2/g (BET); Sol-gel ZrC-CDC surface areas: 1290 m2/g (700°C), 1570 m2/g (800°C), 450 m2/g (900°C) by BET. Sol-gel ZrC-CDC has both micro- and mesoporosity; commercial ZrC-CDC has primarily micropores. Chlorination flow rate: 50 ml/min Cl2; post-chlorination H2 treatment at 900°C for 1 h for dechlorination.
source: Paalo_2025_Synthesis_of_zirconium_carbide_via_sol_gel_method_as_a_precu

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH=CH- (silylene-vinylene backbone); Si-Ph (phenyl on silicon in polymer 5); Si-CH2CH3 (ethyl on silicon in polymer 8); vinyl C=C double bonds in main chain

functional_groups.other: phenyl group on silicon in polymer 5; ethyl group on silicon in polymer 8; residual terminal acetylene end groups detected by IR (weak absorptions at 2037 and 3294 cm-1)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Decomposition started at ca. 300 °C; maximum rate of decomposition between 450 and 500 °C. Polymer 3 (dimethyl): char yield irreproducible, 15-42% (theoretical SiC yield 47.6%), char carbon content 39.8% at 1100 °C. Polymer 5 (methylphenyl): methane only volatile product up to 500 °C, hydrogen evolved at higher temperatures; char carbon content 74.4% at 1100 °C. Polymer 8 (diethyl): char yield ~17% (theoretical 35.7%), ethylene evolution starting at 200 °C. All chars were black and oxidatively stable at 1200 °C in air. XRD confirmed beta-SiC phase.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV (low-pressure mercury arc lamp) surface cross-linking applied to melt-spun fibers of polymer 5 prior to pyrolysis; cross-linking proceeds in inert gas or air

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with THF eluent, calibrated against narrow-dispersity polystyrene standards; Perkin-Elmer Series 601 with Waters R401 RI detector, five alpha-Styragel columns

backbone_architecture.description: Polymers 3 and 5 are predominantly linear with regular alpha,beta-silylene-vinylene structure confirmed by NMR. Polymer 8 (diethyl substituents) is branched as indicated by very broad multimodal GPC (PDI=36) and weak additional 13C NMR signals; branching attributed to hydrosilylation of main-chain double bonds under harsh polymerization conditions (160 °C, 9 h)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: X-ray powder diffraction of pyrolysis chars from polymers 3, 5, and 8 revealed only beta-SiC. Chars were black. Char from polymer 5 contained 74.4 wt% carbon at 1100 °C, suggesting excess free carbon alongside SiC.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Polymer 8 described as elastic, sticky resin. Polymer 5 can be melt-spun into flexible fibers >100 cm long. Pyrolyzed fibers from polymer 5 showed dense surface microstructure by SEM.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (in pyrolyzed ceramic product)

notes: Three main polymers reported: polymer 3 = poly(dimethylsilylenevinylene) (Mw=30381, PDI=4.82, white powder, softening point 95-105 °C, melts at 108 °C); polymer 5 = poly(methylphenylsilylenevinylene) (Mw=11410, PDI=2.5, pale-yellow transparent resin); polymer 8 = poly(diethylsilylenevinylene) (PDI=36, elastic sticky resin, branched). Polymerization via CPA (H2PtCl6)-catalyzed hydrosilylation of diorganohydridoethynylsilanes (intramolecular 1:1 Si-H to ethynyl ratio). Regular alpha,beta-regiochemistry confirmed by 29Si NMR (single resonance) and 13C NMR (single vinyl carbon at ~150 ppm) for polymers 3 and 5. Polymer 5 fibers UV-crosslinked and pyrolyzed to SiC ceramic fibers at 1100 °C under helium flow. GPC molecular weights reported as Mw only against polystyrene standards; Mn not separately reported in text.
source: Pang_1993_Catalytic_synthesis_of_silylene_vinylene_preceramic_polymers

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ni and Co present in polymer backbone/pendant groups; exact atomic percentages not reported

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C≡C alkyne bonds coordinated to Co2(CO)6; Ni-N bonds in macrocycle; C=O carbonyl bonds from Co2(CO)6 (FTIR: 2088, 2051, 2019 cm-1); C=O amide-type bonds (~1658 cm-1)

functional_groups.other: alkyne groups coordinated to Co2(CO)6; Ni(II) macrocycle (Goedken's macrocycle); carbonyl ligands on cobalt

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed under nitrogen at 10 °C/min from 25 to 800/1000 °C. Pyrolysis of thin films of 6F and 6F-[Co2(CO)6]2 at 800 °C for 3 h under N2/H2 (95:5) yielded amorphous nanomaterials containing Ni/Co. Ceramic yield percentage not explicitly reported.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC in THF with conventional calibration against polystyrene standards

backbone_architecture.description: p-conjugated copolymer with Ni(II) Goedken's macrocycle units connected via alkyne linkers to fluorene spacers; post-polymerization functionalization with Co2(CO)8 coordinates to alkyne groups pendant to backbone

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis of 6F-[Co2(CO)6]2 at 800 °C for 3 h under N2/H2 (95:5) yielded amorphous nanomaterials containing Ni and Co. XRD used to characterize pyrolysis products; phases not further specified beyond amorphous.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: amorphous (powder XRD used; pyrolysis products described as amorphous nanomaterials)

notes: This paper describes metallopolymers containing Ni(II) complexes of Goedken's macrocycle copolymerized with organic spacers (fluorene, thiophene, bis(hexyloxy)benzene) via Sonogashira coupling. The primary preceramic material discussed is 6F-[Co2(CO)6]2, a heterobimetallic copolymer formed by post-polymerization reaction of copolymer 6F with Co2(CO)8. These are not traditional silicon-based preceramic polymers (no Si, N, O in backbone); they are Ni/Co-containing conjugated metallopolymers used as precursors to Ni/Co-containing amorphous ceramic nanomaterials. GPC data for all copolymers: 6F Mn=7825, Mw=11800, PDI=1.51; 6F-[Co2(CO)6]2 Mn=7700, Mw=10900, PDI=1.41; 6T Mn=6575, Mw=18250, PDI=2.77; 6B Mn=7700, Mw=13600, PDI=1.76. Ceramic yield not reported numerically. Thin films pyrolyzed at 800 °C, 3 h, 10 °C/min, N2/H2 95:5.
source: Paquette_2016_Synthesis_characterization_and_preceramic_properties_of_conj

elemental_composition.other_elements: B and C primary elements; polymer contains polyolefin backbone with pendant decaborane (B10H14) units; no Si, N, or O ceramic-forming elements present

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-H bonds in decaborane cage units; C-C polyolefin backbone; B-C linkages connecting hexenyl chain to decaborane cage

functional_groups.other: pendant decaborane (B10H13) cage units; hexenyl linker chain

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Decomposition begins ~225 °C; ceramic conversion essentially complete by 600 °C. TGA ceramic yield 65%, bulk ceramic yield 60%, theoretical ceramic yield 68%. Samples heated to 1000 °C are amorphous; onset of boron carbide crystallization at 1250 °C (1 h); highly crystalline material obtained at 1850 °C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal crosslinking occurring at ~220 °C during pyrolysis, retarding volatilization and enabling high ceramic yield

backbone_architecture.description: Polyolefin backbone (from polymerization of 6-hexenyl-decaborane monomer via Cp2ZrMe2/B(C6F5)3 catalyst) with pendant decaborane cage units; inorganic/organic hybrid structure; white solid, air-stable, highly soluble in organic solvents

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Elemental analyses indicate B4C composition (carbon-rich side of boron carbide range, 8.8-20 atom% C). Black glassy ceramic at 1000 °C (amorphous); onset crystallization at 1250 °C; highly crystalline at 1850 °C. Companion molecular precursor 6,6'-(CH2)6-(B10H13)2 yields boron-rich compositions B7.7C to B8.3C.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous at 1000 °C; semi-crystalline at 1250 °C; crystalline at 1850 °C
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: boron carbide (B4C) crystalline phase identified by XRD at 1250 °C and above

notes: Paper describes two boron carbide precursors: (1) polymeric polyhexenyldecaborane (polyolefin backbone with pendant B10H13 units, Tg 50-60 °C, carbon-rich B4C product) and (2) molecular bis(decaboranyl)hexane 6,6'-(CH2)6-(B10H13)2 (boron-rich B7.7C-B8.3C product, decomposition complete by 400 °C, crystallization onset at 1025 °C after 3 h). Ceramic yield range for polyhexenyldecaborane: 60-65% (midpoint 62.5% used). Both precursors used with nanoscale alumina templates to produce boron carbide nanofibers (~250 nm diameter, ~45 µm length) and nanocylinders (~250 nm diameter, ~50 µm long), and with silica sphere templates to produce nanoporous boron carbide (~50 nm pores). No silicon, nitrogen, or oxygen containing elements; this is a boron carbide (not silicon-based) preceramic system.
source: Pender_2003_Molecular_and_polymeric_precursors_to_boron_carbide_nanofibe

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental data given in wt% for precursor resin: C 35.4%, H 9.7%, N 21.9%, Si 29.6% (experimental); monomer: C 32.9%, H 11.8%, N 31.6%, Si 21.5% (experimental)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: N-CH3 groups identified by IR (950-1150 cm-1 in monomer, 1050 cm-1 in resin); C-H bonds present

functional_groups.other: N-methylamino groups (N-CH3); Si-CH3 (methylsilyl)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: 38% weight loss occurred during pyrolysis of precursor fibers. Heating from room temperature to 1200°C in 7 h, then 1200°C to 1500°C in 2 h. Fibers were humidity-conditioned at 100°C and 95% RH for 20 h prior to pyrolysis.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (humidity conditioning at 100°C/95% RH for 20 h prior to pyrolysis, followed by thermal pyrolysis)

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with THF solvent, universal calibration, intrinsic viscosity by Ubbelohde viscometer at 30°C in THF; Mw values at 1.5h=1533, 3.0h=2472, 4.5h=4222 g/mol (weight-average)

backbone_architecture.description: Polycarbosilazane resin formed by polymerization of tris(N-methylamino)methylsilane at 520°C; yellow to reddish-brown, brittle, transparent product soluble in methylene chloride and chloroform

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Shiny-black amorphous fibers described; X-ray diffraction analysis performed with Phillips diffractometer but phase identification results not explicitly stated in provided text

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Tensile rupture modulus up to 29.2 x 10^3 psi (approx 201 GPa) for 0.39-mil diameter pyrolyzed fiber; tensile strength up to 105,000 psi (~724 MPa) for 0.39-mil fiber; elongation 0.36% for 0.39-mil fiber. Precursor fibers: tensile strength 13,800 psi for 0.52-mil diameter. Electrical resistivity ~6.9 x 10^8 ohm-cm for ~0.5-mil diameter pyrolyzed fibers.

notes: Polymer synthesized from tris(N-methylamino)methylsilane via reaction of methylamine with methyltrichlorosilane. Polymerization carried out at 520°C using total reflux distillation apparatus over glass Raschig rings. Molecular weight increases with polymerization time: 1533 (1.5h), 2472 (3.0h), 4222 (4.5h) g/mol by GPC (weight-average). Melt drawing at 220-250°C under inert atmosphere to form precursor fibers. Ceramic yield of 62% (38% weight loss). Final SixNyCz fibers are shiny-black and described as amorphous by Verbeek reference. Electrical resistivity ~6.6-7.2 x 10^8 ohm-cm. Modulus value of 29 x 10^6 psi cited for 0.4-mil diameter fiber in abstract. Mechanical strength is strongly diameter-dependent. Two elemental composition tables present: one for monomer (C4H15NSi theoretical) and one for precursor resin.
source: Penn_1982_Preparation_of_silicon_carbidesilicon_nitride_fibers_by_the

polymer_name: polymethylsilsesquioxane (SILRES, Wacker Chemie AG) modified with triethyl phosphate

elemental_composition.other_elements: P incorporated at 5, 10, 15, 20 wt% TEP/polymethylsilsesquioxane; Ti used as catalyst at 0.5 wt%. Post-pyrolysis compositions given as empirical formulas in Table 1, e.g. SiP0.05O1.41C0.35H0.76 (5KP), SiP0.10O1.73C0.40H0.85 (10KP), etc.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si network (broad band ~1100 cm-1), P-O bonds (phosphate tetrahedra Q0 symmetric stretch ~960 cm-1, asymmetric ~1000-1100 cm-1), C-O stretching at 1436, 870, 740 cm-1, Si-O nonbridging oxygen (Si-ONBO), C-N bonds (~1445 cm-1 after NH3 treatment)

functional_groups.other: Phosphate groups (PO4 3-) from triethyl phosphate; ethoxy groups from TEP hydrolysis; nonbridging siloxane bridges (Si-ONBO)

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: nitrogen (N2, 150 ml/min, purity 99.9997%); also NH3/N2 (3:1 ratio, 150 ml/min) and Cl2/N2 (4:1 ratio, 100 ml/min) in subsequent treatments
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA in air flow (100 ml/min). KP samples show two oxidation events at ~450 and ~650 C, increasing with P content. NKP samples show improved oxidation resistance with higher P. KPC samples show highest oxidation resistance increasing with P. KPCN samples show weight loss below 500 C decreasing with P. NKPC samples show no weight loss below 700 C but increased oxidation above 700 C with increasing P.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (pyrolysis at 750 C); also reactive atmosphere crosslinking via NH3-assisted thermolysis and Cl2 chlorination

backbone_architecture.description: Polymethylsilsesquioxane (CH3SiO1.5)n base polymer crosslinked with hydrolyzed triethyl phosphate via sol-gel process; titanium(IV) butoxide used as catalyst (0.5 wt%). Forms a silicophosphate network upon pyrolysis.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiOC (silicon oxycarbide) with silicophosphate matrix and free carbon phase; after NH3 treatment: SiCN/SiCNO; after chlorination: carbide-derived carbon (CDC) with silicophosphate matrix
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Free carbon phase characterized by Raman D and G bands indicating amorphous/turbostratic carbon. Chlorination removes carbide phases to produce porous carbon. NH3 treatment before chlorination preferentially modifies free carbon phase with P incorporation. Chlorination before NH3 produces silicophosphate matrix preventing N incorporation into free carbon. SAXS used for microstructural analysis.

notes: Preceramic precursor prepared from commercial polymethylsilsesquioxane (SILRES, Wacker Chemie AG, empirical formula (CH3SiO1.5)n) modified with triethyl phosphate (TEP) at 5, 10, 15, 20 wt%. Ti(IV) butoxide used as catalyst at 0.5 wt%. Gelled at RT for 36 h then dried at 50 and 110 C. Multiple sample series produced: KP (N2 pyrolysis), NKP (NH3 thermolysis), KPC (N2 pyrolysis + Cl2), KPCN (N2 pyrolysis + Cl2 + NH3), NKPC (NH3 + Cl2). BET surface areas range from ~21 to ~517 m2/g depending on treatment. Predominantly mesoporous (>86% mesoporous surface in most samples). Raman analysis shows amorphous carbon with D, G, D', D* bands; ID/IG used to calculate interdefect distance LD. SAXS performed at ALBA synchrotron BL11-NCD-SWEET beamline. XPS and UV-Vis also performed. This paper focuses on post-pyrolysis ceramic/carbon materials, not the preceramic polymer itself.
source: Perez_2022_Defective_structure_of_doped_carbons_obtained_from_precerami

polymer_name: PCS (Sailifei Ceramic Fiber Co., Ltd., Suzhou)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C-H side groups described as active functional groups; main chain consists of Si-C-Si bonds; Si-C main chain undergoes depolymerization and reorganization during pyrolysis yielding Si-H containing intermediates

functional_groups.other: C-H groups on side chains described as active functional groups capable of participating in crosslinking curing reactions

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PCS shows ~42 wt% mass loss from 200-700°C in three stages: (i) 200-350°C volatilization of low-molecular-weight components and decomposition of Si-CH3 groups yielding CH4 and C2H6; (ii) 350-530°C depolymerization and reorganization of Si-C main chain with H2 release; (iii) above 530°C transformation into inorganic Si-C networks. Ceramic yield approximately 58%. Printed body with 15 wt% PCS showed ~32 wt% total mass loss by 700°C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV photopolymerization (DLP at 405 nm); C-H groups on PCS participate in crosslinking curing reactions

backbone_architecture.description: Main chain consists of Si-C-Si bonds with Si-CH3 side chains and C-H functional groups. PCS described as a transparent liquid with low refractive index used as powder coating in this study.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1100°C: PCS pyrolyzes to amorphous SiC and β-SiC with fine grain sizes forming network structures and SiC whiskers. At 1900°C: amorphous SiC transforms to β-SiC; SiC whiskers grow into SiC nanofibers and SiC columnar grains depending on PCS content. High-purity SiC ceramic primarily composed of Si and C with minor O from surface oxidation.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Flexural strength increased from 46.1 MPa to 56.2 MPa for specimens sintered at 1900°C with increasing PCS content (6 to 15 wt%), measured by three-point bending test (GB/T 6569-2006) on 3mm x 4mm x 30mm samples, span 24mm, crosshead speed 0.5 mm/min

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: β-SiC; amorphous SiC at lower temperatures; full crystallization to β-SiC at 1900°C

notes: PCS was used as a SiC precursor (6, 9, 12, 15 wt%) in a DLP-based additive manufacturing process combined with micro-scale SiC powders (5.0 and 20.0 μm). PCS was dissolved in n-hexane and coated onto SiC particles to form PCS@SiC core-shell structures. The PCS content ranged from 6 to 15 wt% (samples SP-6, SP-9, SP-12, SP-15). Debinding conducted in vacuum: ramp to 410°C at 0.2°C/min (hold 30 min), then to 600°C at 0.3°C/min. Sintering in vacuum at 1°C/min to peak temperature (1100°C or 1900°C), hold 120 min, cool to 600°C at 3°C/min then natural cooling. Ceramic yield of PCS reported as approximately 58%. Flexural strength range reflects lowest PCS content (46.1 MPa) to highest PCS content (56.2 MPa) at 1900°C sintering temperature.
source: Ping_2026_Curing_behavior_and_mechanical_properties_of_polycarbosilane

elemental_composition.other_elements: Polymer contains only Si, C, and H elements as stated in text

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2- (methylene bridges from hydrosilylation), Si-phenyl-Si (arylene bridges from BDSB monomer), C=C aromatic (phenyl ring); IR bands: Si-H at 2127 cm-1, Si-CH3 and Si-CH2 at 1250 cm-1, Si-C stretching at 760-798 cm-1

functional_groups.other: Phenyl groups (arylene linkers from 1,4-bis(dimethylsilyl)benzene); residual Si-H noted at 2127 cm-1 in BDSB monomer; allyl groups consumed during hydrosilylation (tetraallylsilane monomer)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis followed by TGA-DSC coupled with mass spectrometer from room temperature to 1400°C in argon at 10°C/min. Ceramic yield calculated as mass ratio of pyrolysis products to precursors, excluding initial solvent loss up to 150°C. Pyrolysis at various temperatures between 800 and 1700°C also performed in tube furnace under flowing argon with 1 h dwell time.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic (Karstedt's catalyst, hydrosilylation step-growth polymerization leading to gel/network formation)

backbone_architecture.description: Hyperbranched polycarbosilane synthesized via hydrosilylation of difunctional monomer 1,4-bis(dimethylsilyl)benzene (BDSB, f=2) with tetrafunctional monomer tetraallylsilane (TAS, f=4) using Karstedt's catalyst at 1:2 TAS:BDSB molar ratio. Gel-like behavior observed at alkene conversions above ~0.55, consistent with Flory-Stockmayer critical conversion of 0.58.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis at 1400°C led to porous materials with β-SiC and free carbon. Phase composition identified by XRD (Siemens D5000, Cu-Kα radiation, λ=1.54056 Å).

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Storage modulus monitored by dynamic rheology during polymerization; storage modulus increased by five orders of magnitude for alkene conversion change of ~25% above critical conversion of ~0.5; above gel point, storage modulus was up to two orders of magnitude greater than loss modulus.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: β-SiC (after pyrolysis at 1400°C)

notes: Synthesis: hydrosilylation of BDSB and TAS (molar ratio 1:2 TAS:BDSB) with 0.1 mol% Karstedt's catalyst in toluene at 75°C for 24 h; yield 94%. Polymer characterized by 1H, 13C (liquid and solid-state CP-MAS), 29Si CP-MAS NMR, and ATR-FTIR. 29Si NMR shows two Si environments: Si(CH2)4 at 1.1 ppm and SiAr(CH2)3 at -3.5 ppm. Gel point critical conversion experimentally ~0.55, theoretically 0.58 by Flory-Stockmayer. Overall second-order kinetics determined for hydrosilylation. Polymerization monitored in situ by combined rheology (plate-plate, 1 Hz, 0.5% strain) and FT-IR at 25°C. Maximum alkene conversion of 0.71 reached after 6000 s under monitoring conditions. Porous ceramics or aerogels noted as potential application of gel precursors.
source: Piriou_2018_Rheological_and_thermal_behaviours_of_a_hyperbranched_polyca

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-OH (residual silanols); Si-O-Si siloxane backbone; Q2-Q4 silicon environments observed by 29Si CP/MAS NMR; T2 sites at -60 ppm corresponding to =Si(CH3) with residual SiOH

functional_groups.other: Residual silanol groups (SiOH)

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: 3D cross-linked network; each Si atom has one CH3 group and up to three bonds participating in cross-linking via Si-O-Si linkages; additional cross-linking possible via condensation of residual silanols upon drying

backbone_architecture.description: 3D cross-linked polymethylsiloxane; each Si atom bears one CH3 group with up to three Si-O bonds participating in cross-linking; described as intermediate between linear PDMS and methylated nanosilica; less flexible than PDMS but soft because only three of four Si bonds can participate in cross-linking

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Described as a soft powder/gel-like material; aggregates of nanoparticles and agglomerates can be easily rearranged under any treatment

notes: This paper primarily studies PMS (polymethylsiloxane) blended with fumed nanosilica A-300 under different hydration and mechanical loading conditions. PMS is used as a commercial hydrogel (Enterosgel, ~7-8 wt.% PMS, 93-92 wt.% water). Dried PMS (dPMS) contains ~0.7 wt.% residual water after room-temperature drying for one week. Fumed silica A-300 was hydrocompacted (mixed with water 1:5 and dried at 160°C) to increase bulk density from 0.05 to 0.25 g/cm3. BET surface areas of individual and blended samples range from 98 to 453 m2/g. Pore volumes range from 0.390 to 1.808 cm3/g. Average pore radii <RV> range from 18-25 nm for blends. The paper focuses on textural, morphological, and interfacial characterization rather than pyrolysis or ceramic conversion. 29Si CP/MAS NMR identifies T2 sites at -60 ppm for =Si(CH3) with residual SiOH and Q2-Q4 sites for silica. No pyrolysis data reported.
source: Protsak_2019_Nanostructured_Polymethylsiloxane_Fumed_Silica_Blends

polymer_type: polycarbosilane, polycarbosilazane, polysilazane, polytitanocarbosilane, polytitanocarbosilazane, polyzirconocarbosilazane
polymer_name: AHPCS (SMP-10), HTT 1800, perhydropolysilazane, poly[(methylvinyl)-co-(methyl)]silazane, polymethylsilazane (PMSZ), polytitanocarbosilane (AHPTiCS, PPTiCS, PAMTiCS), polytitanocarbosilazane (PMTiSZC), polyzirconocarbosilazane

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ti and Zr incorporated into polymer backbone via reaction with titanocene dichloride, alkyl-bis(cyclopentadienyl)titanium compounds, or tetrakisdiethylamino zirconium (TDEAZr); final ceramic systems include Si-C-Ti, Si-N-Ti-(C), Si-N-Zr-(C)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-CH=CH2 (allyl groups in AHPCS); Ti-N bonds in polytitanocarbosilazanes; Zr-N bonds in polyzirconocarbosilazanes; cyclopentadienyl-Ti bonds in titanocene-derived precursors

functional_groups.other: allyl groups (-Si-CH2-CH=CH2); cyclopentadienyl ligands on Ti precursors; dialkylamino groups on metal precursors (tetrakisdimethylamino Ti, tetrakisdiethylamino Zr)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Multiple polymer systems studied. Ceramic yields from table: methylsilane/Ar 85%, methylvinylsilane/Ar 83%, methylsiloxane/He 85%, hydridosilazane/N2 74%, hydridomethylsilazane/Ar 72%, methylsilazane/NH3 85%, vinylsilazane/N2 85%, cyclomethylsilazane/Ar 88%, borosilazane/Ar 90%, titanocarbosilane/N2 75%. AHPCS converted to SiC up to 1000°C and studied up to 1400°C; polytitanocarbosilazanes pyrolyzed under N2 and NH3 up to 1000°C then studied to 1600°C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal crosslinking; AHPCS crosslinking temperature 121-204°C; HTT 1800 crosslinking temperature 175-200°C

backbone_architecture.description: AHPCS is an allylhydridopolycarbosilane with Si-C backbone bearing allyl and hydride substituents; polysilazanes have Si-N backbone with methyl and vinyl substituents; polytitanocarbosilanes incorporate Ti into Si-C backbone; polytitanocarbosilazanes incorporate Ti or Zr into Si-N-C backbone; single-source precursor approach used for metal-containing polymers

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC, TiC, TiN, Si3N4, SiCN, ZrN, SiC/TiC nanocomposites, TiN/Si3N4 nanocomposites, SiC/ZrN
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiC-Ti-X nanocomposites formed from AHPCS with Ti nanoparticles or polytitanocarbosilanes; TiC crystallites formed at 1200°C; Si-N-Ti-(C) and Si-N-Zr-(C) nanocomposites formed from polymetallo(carbo)silazanes; TiN/Si3N4 dense nanocomposite pieces elaborated from polytitanocarbosilazane; materials studied from 1000 to 1600°C under N2

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: SiC-Ti-10: hardness 17±1 GPa, modulus 161±4 GPa; SiC-Ti-1: hardness 20.9±0.6 GPa, modulus 186±3 GPa; reference TiC: hardness 31.38 GPa, modulus 439.3 GPa; measured by microindentation

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC (cubic), TiC (cubic, Fm3m), TiN, Si3N4, ZrN; TiC and ZrC have face-centered cubic structure; microstructural evolution tracked by XRD from 1000 to 1600°C

notes: This is a French PhD thesis (Université Montpellier, 2016, Vanessa Proust) covering multiple preceramic polymer systems for SiC, Si3N4, SiCN, and metal-containing (Ti, Zr) nanocomposite ceramics. Main polymer precursors: AHPCS (SMP-10) for SiC; HTT 1800 (poly[(methylvinyl)-co-(methyl)]silazane) and PMSZ (polymethylsilazane) for Si-N systems; polytitanocarbosilanes (AHPTiCS-X, PPTiCS-X, PAMTiCS-X) synthesized from AHPCS + titanocene dichloride or alkyl-bis(Cp)Ti for Si-C-Ti ceramics; polytitanocarbosilazanes and polyzirconocarbosilazanes for Si-N-M-(C) ceramics. Ceramic yield midpoint of 83% noted from range in table (83% for methylvinylsilane/Ar). TiC crystallite sizes ~20-25 nm at 1200°C. Optical properties (emissivity, absorbance) studied for solar absorber applications. He ion implantation used to simulate nuclear irradiation effects. AHPCS properties: viscosity 0.1 Pa.s, density 0.998 g/cm3, flash point 89°C. HTT 1800 properties: viscosity 20-50 mPa.s, density 1.0 g/cm3, flash point 16.25°C.
source: Proust_2016_Elaboration_de_nanocomposites_ceramiques_carbures_nitrures_a

polymer_name: thiol-functional polysiloxane / vinyl-functional polysiloxane crosslinked network (T1, T2 with Vi1-Vi4)

elemental_composition.other_elements: S detected by SEM-EDS on modified cotton surfaces; representative EDS values (T1Vi1(T) after washing): C 32.2%, O 53.9%, Si 11.8%, S 2.1%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si backbone confirmed by FT-IR; C-H stretching at 2962 cm-1 (methyl); Si-CH3 bands at 1259 and 798 cm-1; thioether (C-S) linkages formed via thiol-ene coupling; no residual C=C detected after crosslinking

functional_groups.other: thiol (-SH) groups on polysiloxane backbone (mercaptopropyl substituents); thioether linkages formed after crosslinking

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV (DMPA photoinitiator, 320-500 nm, 30 min) and thermal (AIBN, 90°C, 30 min); thiol-ene radical mechanism; molar ratio of vinyl to thiol groups 1:1

backbone_architecture.description: Crosslinked polysiloxane network formed on cotton fiber surface via thiol-ene coupling between two thiol-functional polysiloxanes (T1: 13-17% mercaptopropylmethylsiloxane-dimethylsiloxane copolymer; T2: 4-6% mercaptopropylmethylsiloxane-dimethylsiloxane copolymer, both trimethylsiloxy terminated) and four vinyl-functional organosilicon crosslinkers (Vi1: cyclic tetravinyl siloxane; Vi2: vinylmethylsiloxane-dimethylsiloxane copolymer; Vi3: 1,3-divinyl-1,1,3,3-tetramethyldisiloxane; Vi4: vinyl-terminated PDMS ~1900 g/mol)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Not a preceramic system; coatings remain as organic polysiloxane networks on cotton; no pyrolysis or ceramic conversion described

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Bending length and flexural rigidity measured on coated cotton fabrics; values vary by crosslinker type (e.g., T1Vi1(T): bending length 22.5 mm, flexural rigidity 23.5 µJ/m; T1Vi2(T): 14 mm, 5.7 µJ/m; T1Vi3(T): 17.5 mm, 11 µJ/m; T1Vi4(T): 16 mm, 8.4 µJ/m); unmodified cotton: 15 mm, 7 µJ/m

notes: This paper describes fluorine-free hydrophobic finishing of cotton textiles using thiol-ene crosslinking of polysiloxane networks, not a preceramic polymer pyrolysis study. No ceramic conversion, TGA, or pyrolysis data are reported. The polymer system consists of two thiol-functional polysiloxanes (T1 and T2 differing in -SH content) crosslinked with four vinyl-functional organosilicon compounds (Vi1-Vi4) under UV (DMPA) or thermal (AIBN) initiation. Add-on values ranged from ~6.75 to 7.86% before washing. Water contact angle durability was demonstrated over 10 washing cycles. SEM confirmed continuous coatings; SEM-EDS confirmed Si and S on fiber surfaces. FT-IR confirmed Si-CH3 groups and consumption of vinyl groups. The system is fundamentally a functional textile coating study, not a preceramic polymer study.
source: Przybylak_2026_Thiol_Ene_Crosslinking_of_Polysiloxane_Networks_on_Cotton_fo

elemental_composition.other_elements: B: 0.1-0.8 wt% depending on degree of modification. Polymer compositions given as ratios relative to Si=1.0: AHPCS-9-BBN-1: Si1.0C1.39H4.21B0.005(O0.07); AHPCS-9-BBN-2: Si1.0C1.49H4.33B0.020(O0.06); AHPCS-9-BBN-3: Si1.0C1.31H4.47B0.015(O0.35); AHPCS-9-BBN-4: Si1.0C1.45H4.64B0.022(O0.12); AHPCS-9-BBN-5: Si1.0C1.73H5.31B0.040(O0.06). Parent AHPCS: Si1.0C1.25H4.30(O0.20)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2 backbone bonds; Si-allyl groups; C-B bonds from anti-Markovnikov hydroboration of allyl groups by 9-BBN; 9-BBN moiety attached via CH2CH2CH2 tether to Si backbone

functional_groups.other: allyl groups (residual unreacted); 9-BBN (boracyclic) groups attached via propylene tether; SiH2 groups

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed under argon purge. Char yields at 1600°C range from 75.9% to 84.9% for AHPCS-9-BBN samples vs 58.9% for parent AHPCS. Thermal stabilities of AHPCS-9-BBN polymers reported as similar to parent AHPCS. Pyrolyses also conducted at 1800°C and 2000°C on pre-pyrolyzed 1600°C chars; ceramic yield range noted across all samples and temperatures.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal or chemical (allyl groups provide latent reactivity for curing; BH3-based hydroboration led to gelation/crosslinking, whereas 9-BBN modification preserved processibility without crosslinking)

molecular_weight.measurement_method: SEC with dual-angle light scattering detector (static light scattering), toluene mobile phase at 35°C. Values shown for AHPCS-9-BBN-1; parent AHPCS Mn=36800, Mw=170800; AHPCS-9-BBN-2 Mn=260700, Mw=820000; AHPCS-9-BBN-3 Mn=151400, Mw=473200

backbone_architecture.description: Highly branched polymer with general empirical formula [(H3SiCH2)a(SiH2CH2)b(Si(allyl)2CH2)c(SiH(CH2)2)d(Si(CH2)3)e]. Parent AHPCS empirical formula (SiH2CH2)0.95(Si(allyl)2CH2)0.05. After 9-BBN modification, some allyl groups are hydroborated giving compositions ranging from (SiH2CH2)0.95(Si(allyl)2CH2)0.044(Si(allyl)(CH2CH2CH2-9-BBN)CH2)0.006 to (SiH2CH2)0.95(Si(allyl)2CH2)0.012(Si(allyl)(CH2CH2CH2-9-BBN)CH2)0.038.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramics described as SiCB. At 1600°C ceramic compositions (Si=1.0 basis): AHPCS-9-BBN-1 Si1.0C1.29B0.004; AHPCS-9-BBN-2 Si1.0C1.31B0.022; AHPCS-9-BBN-3 Si1.0C1.19B0.015; AHPCS-9-BBN-4 Si1.0C1.42B0.032; AHPCS-9-BBN-5 Si1.0C1.48B0.034. Densities at 1800°C range 2.54-2.75 g/cm3; at 2000°C range 2.56-2.98 g/cm3. Boron incorporation (<1%) enhances SiC sintering and density.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC (identified by XRD powder diffraction using Cu Kα radiation)

notes: Paper reports a series of AHPCS-9-BBN polymers (samples 1-5) with varying degrees of boron incorporation (5.0% to 37.2% modification of allyl groups). Molecular weight increases and intrinsic viscosity decreases with increasing boron incorporation. Ceramic yields and grain sizes reported at multiple pyrolysis temperatures (1200, 1600, 1800, 2000°C). Parent AHPCS has Mn=36800, Mw=170800. Pyrolysis at 1600°C under argon; 1800 and 2000°C under vacuum. Grain sizes at 1600°C: 9-23 nm; at 1800°C: 93-119 nm; at 2000°C: 131-272 nm. Densities measured by flotation in halogenated hydrocarbons. The ceramic_yield_pct and pyrolysis_temp_C fields use representative values for AHPCS-9-BBN-1 at 1600°C as primary example; full data in tables. BH3-based reagents caused gelation; 9-BBN selected for controlled, non-crosslinking hydroboration. Polymer is soluble in aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons as a viscous yellow liquid.
source: Puerta_2002_Synthesis_and_Ceramic_Conversion_Reactions_of_9_BBN_Modified

elemental_composition.other_elements: XPS depth-profiling data for pyrolysed fibres: at 700C: C=71.2, Si=8.6, O=19.4, N=0.3 at.%; at 800C: C=50.8, Si=15.5, O=33.4, N=0.4 at.% (these are ceramic product compositions, not precursor polymer compositions)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-N bonds partially oxidized to Si-O (siloxane) upon mixing with water/PAA; SiO2C2, SiO3C, SiO4 mixed oxycarbide units identified by NMR in pyrolysed fibres; C-C (free carbon, graphitic and amorphous) identified by Raman; -CH(COOH)-CH2- from PAA

functional_groups.other: carboxylic acid (-COOH) from poly-acrylic acid component; cyclic silazane ring structure (8-membered ring)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed from 100 to 1000C at 10C/min in either N2 or synthetic air (10 ml/min) on cross-linked, pyrolysed TTCSZ/PAA and neat PAA samples. Pyrolysis conducted at three temperatures: 600, 700 and 800C. N1s peak disappears by XPS above 600C pyrolysis. Free carbon content increases with pyrolysis temperature; graphitic carbon increases while amorphous carbon decreases with temperature.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (160C, 24h in air, using dicumyl peroxide (DCP) as radical initiator at 10 wt% in TTCSZ)

backbone_architecture.description: TTCSZ is an 8-membered cyclotetrasilazane ring (cyclic, not linear); upon mixing with PAA/water, significant oxidation of silazane rings to siloxane rings occurs. PAA component provides linear polymer backbone with -CH(COOH)-CH2- repeat units. Overall hybrid is cyclic silazane/linear polyacrylic acid composite precursor.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Carbon-rich SiOCN fibres; mixed oxycarbide units (SiO2C2, SiO3C, SiO4) identified by 29Si MAS NMR at 600C; SiO3C decreases and SiO2C2 disappears at higher temperatures leaving mostly SiO4 (silica tetrahedral); free carbon (graphitic sp2 and disordered/amorphous) confirmed by Raman D and G bands; N content very low after pyrolysis (0.3-0.4 at.% by XPS)

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fibre diameter range 1-10 microns by SEM; fibres are porous at the surface. Literature reference cited: PDCFs can reach up to 2.5 GPa tensile strength and 300 GPa modulus (not measured in this work).

notes: Hybrid precursor composition: TTCSZ:DCP:PAA = 45:5:50 wt%. Viscosity of neat TTCSZ+DCP ~0.1 Pa s at 37C; hybrid TTCSZ/PAA ~25 Pa s (250 P) enabling sol-gel fibre spinning. Cross-linking at 160C for 24h in open air before pyrolysis. Significant nitrogen loss occurs before pyrolysis, hypothesized to result from reaction of Si-NH- with water forming NH3. The silazane rings partially convert to siloxane rings upon mixing with PAA/water as evidenced by 29Si NMR shift from -17.5 ppm (TTCSZ) to ~-33 ppm (siloxane). This explains the high oxygen content and SiOCN rather than SiCN ceramic product. XPS elemental data in the table represent pyrolysed ceramic fibre compositions, not the precursor polymer. Pyrolysis temperatures studied: 600, 700, 800C.
source: Ren_2019_Preparation_and_structure_of_SiOCN_fibres_derived_from_cycli

elemental_composition.other_elements: B present (SiBCN ceramic product implies Si, B, C, N in polymer)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-vinyl groups present; B-containing bonds implied by polyborosilazane structure

functional_groups.other: Acrylate groups from TPGDA reactive diluent added to resin formulation

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed from room temperature to 1000 C at 10 C/min under nitrogen on ~5 mg sample. Ceramic yield of 51.1% measured after pyrolysis at 1200 C. Original polymer ceramic yield stated as ~65 wt%. Pyrolysis protocol included holds at 460 C for 3 h and 900 C for 3 h; additional annealing at 1400 C for 4 h under nitrogen. Pyrolysis ramp rate was 1 C/min to 900 C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV/photoinitiated free radical polymerization of vinyl groups; post-print UV cure at 100% intensity for 5 min

backbone_architecture.description: Described as having a more caged structure with Si-vinyl groups, in contrast to a mostly linear structure referenced in prior work. The caged structure is stated to lead to more certainty and a more stable structure after printing.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolyzed at 900 C for 4 h to yield SiBCN ceramic. Linear shrinkage of 27% observed during polymer-to-ceramic conversion. Density of pyrolyzed SiBCN is approximately 2 g/cm3 with slight residual porosity.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Nanoindentation performed at 600 nm indentation depth on polished surfaces (1 micron finish); measurements taken after heat-treatment at 1400 C for 3 h

notes: Study focuses on crosslinking mechanism of a two-component polysiloxane preceramic system (MSE 100 + DMS-S12) catalyzed by bis-2-ethylhexanoate tin (organotin catalyst, 0.5-4.0 wt% Sn2+). Three MSE/DMS weight ratios studied: 84:16 (5/1), 70:30 (4/2), 37:63 (2/4). Crosslinking monitored by viscometry and 29Si-MAS-NMR. Key finding: methoxy groups are the primary crosslinking-active species; DMS-S12 provides water in situ via condensation of its OH end groups, enabling hydrolysis of MSE 100 methoxy groups and subsequent Si-O-Si bond formation. T1 and T2 units in MSE 100 are converted to T2 and T3 units upon crosslinking. The Si-C bond does not react due to high bond energy (356±17 kJ/mol). Organotin hydroxide (from partial hydrolysis of catalyst) is proposed active catalytic species forming Sn-O-Si intermediates.

notes: Study focuses on oxidative curing (infusibilization) kinetics of melt-spun PCS fibers from Shin-Etsu Chemical. Fibers melt-spun at 573-603K in Ar atmosphere. Curing performed in Ar-O2 mixtures with pO2=5-100 kPa at 413-463K. Mass gain rate used as proxy for curing rate. Early-stage kinetics follow contracting-disc model: 1-(1-X)^(1/2)=kt, consistent with interfacial reaction control. Apparent activation energy = 87.7 kJ/mol (abstract) / 94.2 kJ/mol (body text, from Arrhenius plot of initial rate). Literature value for PCS powder oxidation in air: 85.4 kJ/mol. Late-stage curing controlled by oxygen diffusion through the cured (oxidized) layer. Oxygen content of 443K-cured fibers: ~4.5 mass%; 483K-cured fibers: ~28.9 mass%. Rate constant k proportional to pO2 and inversely proportional to fiber diameter. Fibers melted/fused at elevated pO2 or temperatures above ~463K. Pyrolysis temperature of 1973K noted as 1700 degrees C.

notes: This paper focuses on the hydrolysis behavior of the BTB precursor (1,4-bis(triethoxysilyl)benzene) under acidic conditions (HCl catalyst), studied by liquid-state 29Si NMR. Key finding: one -Si(OEt)3 group is preferentially hydrolyzed over the other, contrary to inductive effect predictions, attributed to intramolecular through-space interaction and/or negative hyperconjugation via the phenylene pi system. Sixteen distinct 29Si NMR signals for monomeric hydrolyzed species were identified and assigned. Condensation products (T1 species) appear at -62 to -64 ppm at high water content (water/BTB=9) after 4.25 h. Comparison with 1,2-bis(triethoxysilyl)ethane (BTE) showed no preferential hydrolysis, confirming the role of the phenylene pi orbitals. No pyrolysis, ceramic yield, mechanical, or molecular weight data are reported.

notes: This is a broad review paper on preceramic inorganic polymers (PCIPs) covering polysilazanes, polysiloxanes, polycarbosilanes, and polyborosilazanes for environmental applications. No single specific polymer system is characterized with quantitative descriptors. Key synthesis routes discussed include sol-gel, Wurtz-type coupling, Kumada rearrangement, anionic ring-opening polymerization, hydrosilylation, Grignard coupling, and condensation polymerization. Environmental applications include water purification membranes (SiOC), catalytic converters, air filters, wastewater treatment, and electromagnetic shielding. SiOC/Ni composites prepared by vat-based photopolymerization for CO2 methanation are noted. Ceramic stability up to 2000 degrees C reported. Most quantitative data in the tables relates to composite ceramic systems (SiOC, SiBCN, SiCN, Si3N4) rather than the preceramic polymer precursors themselves.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si and Si-C bonds confirmed by DRIFTS at 1030 and 800 cm-1 respectively; D (C2SiO2), D' (C(H)SiO2), D'' (C(C=C)SiO2), M(CSiO), T (CSiO3), Q (Si(OSi)4) units identified by 29Si MAS NMR

functional_groups.other: Cyclic siloxane oligomers; polycyclic network formed via Pt-catalyzed hydrosilylation

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two distinct weight loss events: first at 300-600°C (organic evolution, likely CH4); second at 600-900°C (further mineralization). High residue at 600°C due to high interconnection of siloxane units. Polymer density ~1.0 g/cm3, amorphous ceramic density ~1.9 g/cm3 at 1000°C with ~53% volume shrinkage for bulk SPN.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (hydrosilylation via Pt catalyst at 70°C for 3 hours)

backbone_architecture.description: Polycyclic siloxane network (SPN) formed by Pt-catalyzed hydrosilylation of cyclic siloxane oligomers; described as high-interconnected silicone network that hinders viscous flow during pyrolysis

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Random distribution of SiC4 (22.3%), SiC3O (27.7%), SiC2O2 (20.4%), and SiO4 (29.5%) sites determined by 29Si MAS NMR deconvolution at 1000°C. Phase is amorphous by XRD. Composites contain SiC or Si3N4 as inert fillers producing SiC/SiCxO4-x and Si3N4/SiCxO4-x composites.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Flexural strength, flexural modulus, impact resistance, nominal fracture initiation energy, and toughness Kc reported for composites CMC1-CMC6 (see Table 3). CMC1 had maximum flexural strength; CMC4 had maximum flexural modulus; CMC5 had highest nominal fracture initiation energy (250 kJ/m2) and toughness Kc (5.09 MPa.m^0.5). All composites showed brittle failure.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiCxO4-x phase is amorphous; XRD shows only peaks from ceramic filler powders (SiC or Si3N4)

notes: Polymer used as preceramic binder in ceramic matrix composites (CMC1-CMC6) with SiC or Si3N4 fillers at various polymer/filler ratios. Green bodies pressed at ~80 MPa and cured at 70°C for 3 hours before pyrolysis. Structural evolution monitored from 200 to 1000°C by DRIFTS and 29Si MAS NMR. At 400°C no residual Si-H or Si-C=C groups detected. Composites classified as 'Inter' type per Niihara classification with dispersoid at grain boundaries. Heating rate of 20°C/min stated in TGA figure caption. Pyrolysis used multi-step heating schedule (details not fully specified). Composites showed porosity ranging from 15.0% (CMC5) to 32.8% (CMC3).
source: Schiavon_2001_Processing_of_Monolithic_Ceramic_Bodies_from_Polysiloxane_Pr

elemental_composition.other_elements: Si (wt%): PBS-I calc 39.4, PBS-II calc 39.4; B (wt%): PBS-I calc 3.0, PBS-II calc 3.0; B/Si molar ratio = 0.2 for both polymers

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-B bonds (borosiloxane bridges) confirmed by FTIR at 894 cm-1 (nu B-O-Si) and 675 cm-1 (delta B-O-Si); B-O-B bonds at 1414-1419 cm-1; B-OH at 1195 cm-1; BO3 trigonal units connected to SiO4 tetrahedra

functional_groups.other: Ethoxysilane groups (from vinyltriethoxysilane in PBS-II); boric acid B(OH)3 cross-linking units; cyclic siloxane D4H units

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two main degradation steps: first at ~80-150 C with 2.8 wt% loss (PBS-I) and 1.4 wt% loss (PBS-II) associated with boric acid release, water evolution, and free oligomer loss; second step at ~500-800 C associated with polymer-to-ceramic conversion forming SiBCO glass. Ceramic yields at 1000 C: PBS-I = 90.8 wt%, PBS-II = 89.8 wt%. Range: 89.8-90.8 wt%, midpoint ~90.3 wt%.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: Boron (BO3 units) acts as crosslinker via B-O-Si bonds; PBS-II also crosslinked via hydrosilylation using platinum catalyst

backbone_architecture.description: PBS-I: polycyclic network formed by dehydrogen coupling of D4H (1,3,5,7-tetramethyl-1,3,5,7-tetracyclotetrasiloxane) with boric acid; boron introduced at cross-linking points via Si-O-B bonds. PBS-II: network formed by hydrolysis/condensation of vinyltriethoxysilane with boric acid followed by hydrosilylation with D4H using Pt catalyst; D4H/VTES molar ratio = 1.0.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiBCO (boron and silicon oxycarbide glass), amorphous
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: 29Si MAS NMR of 1000 C products shows mixed Si sites: SiO4 (~34.6-40.1%), SiCO3 (~31.7-36.9%), SiC2O2 (~24.1-28.2%), SiC4 (~4.4% in PBS-I only). No crystalline B(OH)3 or B2O3 detected by XRD in pyrolyzed samples. Boron retained in amorphous sites. Phase separation reported in literature to begin above 1300 C.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Precursor polymers: broad halo at 2theta=22 degrees (amorphous borosilicate network) plus crystalline boric acid peaks at 2theta=14.7 and 28 degrees. Pyrolyzed samples at 400, 700, 1000 C: fully amorphous, no crystalline phases detected.

notes: Two poly(borosiloxane) variants studied: PBS-I (dehydrogen coupling route of D4H + boric acid in dry ethanol at ~78 C for 24 h) and PBS-II (hydrolysis/condensation of vinyltriethoxysilane + boric acid followed by hydrosilylation with D4H using 1 wt% Pt catalyst). Both have B/Si molar ratio of 0.2. Ceramic yield range: 89.8 (PBS-II) to 90.8 (PBS-I) wt%; midpoint 90.3 wt% used in thermal_pyrolysis field. FTIR confirms Si-O-B connectivity at ~880 cm-1. 11B MAS NMR shows trigonal B(OSi)3 at 12.5 ppm and boric acid/B(OB)3 at 19.6 ppm. Significant boron loss observed up to ~400 C, especially for PBS-I. Silicon content in PBS-II ceramics lower than PBS-I. Cooling rate also 10 C/min. Intermediate pyrolysis temperatures of 400 and 700 C also studied. SiBCO glasses described as X-ray amorphous up to 1200 C per literature.
source: Schiavon_2008_Novel_poly_borosiloxane_precursors_to_amorphous_SiBCO_cerami

polymer_name: SMP-10 (Starfire Systems), SPR-212a (Starfire Systems), HTT-1800 (KiON Specialty Polymers)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH=CH2 (vinyl) bonds present; imidonitride bonds (Si-NH) form upon ammonolysis; SiN4 and NSi3 environments identified as important for microporosity

functional_groups.other: Imidonitride groups (Si3N4-2x(NH)3x) form during ammonolysis

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: NH3 (ammonolysis step at 300-800 C), then argon (second step at 750 C); or argon only
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ammonolysis step: 300-800 C for 1 h at 100 C/h heating rate. Second thermolysis step under Ar at 750 C for 3 h at 50 C/h heating rate. Microporosity collapses above 600 C under inert atmosphere alone; NH3 treatment stabilizes microporosity up to 750 C. Above 800 C viscous flow and ripening of micropores lead to macroporous ceramic with low surface area.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (thermolysis under NH3 and/or Ar atmosphere); ammonolysis promotes dehydrocoupling and transamination reactions converting Si-H, Si-CH3, Si-CH=CH2 to Si-N bonds

backbone_architecture.description: Three distinct polymer classes used: polycarbosilane (SMP-10), polysiloxane (SPR-212a), polysilazane (HTT-1800); backbone architecture not explicitly described beyond polymer type

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Polysilazane and polysiloxane transform to microporous SiCNO ceramics. Polycarbosilane-derived materials remain non-porous by N2/CO2 adsorption but SAXS indicates latent pores <0.35 nm. Silicon imidonitride (Si3N4-2x(NH)3x) intermediate formed during ammonolysis. SiN4 and NSi3 environments responsible for micropore formation.

notes: Study focuses on NH3-assisted thermolysis (ammonolysis) of three preceramic polymers to synthesize microporous PDCs. BET surface areas: HTT-1800 derived ceramics up to 400 m2/g (NH3 route), SPR-212a up to 413 m2/g, SMP-10 up to 95 m2/g. NH3-treated then Ar-thermolyzed samples: HTT up to 266 m2/g, SPR up to 306 m2/g. Micropore volumes up to 0.16 cm3/g (N2) and 0.26 cm3/g (CO2-DA). SAXS used to detect latent pores in polycarbosilane-derived samples (pore size <0.35 nm). Dubinin-Astakhov analysis applied to CO2 isotherms. Heating rates given in C/h not C/min: ammonolysis at 100 C/h, Ar thermolysis at 50 C/h. XRD performed with Mo Ka radiation. Carbon determined by CS800 analyzer, N/O by Leco TC-436, H by ICP-AES, Si calculated by difference.
source: Schitco_2015_NH_3_assisted_synthesis_of_microporous_silicon_oxycarbonitri

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental composition given as weight percent for ceramic product: Si 30.15 wt%, B 11.67 wt%, N 45.08 wt%, C 11.44 wt%, O 1.25 wt%; empirical formula Si1.0B1.0N3.0C0.9O0.1 (idealized SiBN3C)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds present (borazine ring); B-CH3 bonds present in monomer; Si-N bonds confirmed by IR at 923 cm-1 (polymer) and 978/485 cm-1 (ceramic); B-N antisymmetric stretching in ceramic at 1380 and 793 cm-1; SiN4 tetrahedral coordination; BN3 and BN2C trigonal planar boron environments

functional_groups.other: Borazine ring (B3N3 heterocycle); SiCl3 groups on monomer; methylamine (HN(CH3)) crosslinking groups; B-CH3 groups; N-CH3 groups

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three-stage degradation: polycondensation completed at 450 C releasing methylamine (m/z=31) and small amounts HCN (m/z=27); major weight loss of 23.1% between 450-650 C releasing methane (m/z=16) from terminal N-CH3 groups; above 600 C N2 and H2 eliminated with 1.7% weight loss. Ceramic stable up to 1840 C; above 1840 C rapid mass loss; 13% weight loss after heating to 2000 C. Only 0.49% weight gain up to 1300 C in pure oxygen flow.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical - crosslinking with methylamine (amination of SiCl and BCl groups)

backbone_architecture.description: Polymer derived from borazine-ring-containing monomers [(SiCl3)NB(Cln(CH3)1-n)]3 crosslinked with methylamine; silicon attached to borazine core via nitrogen bridges; soluble in hexane and benzene after crosslinking; SiN4 tetrahedral units connect borazine rings

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous by XRD after pyrolysis at 1400 C. At 1600 C small SiC reflections appear. After 1800 C annealing for 3h: crystalline SiC, BN, and Si phases present. Density of ceramic: 1.80 g/cm3. Borazine ring identified as constitutive building unit of ceramic by IR.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous at 1400 C; SiC (small reflections) at 1600 C; SiC, BN (boron nitride), and Si (crystalline silicon) at 1800 C after 3h anneal

notes: Monomer is a mixture of borazine derivatives [(SiCl3)NB(Cln(CH3)1-n)]3 (n=0,1,2,3) with Cl:CH3 ratio ~1:2 on boron. B3N3 ring in chair conformation (non-planar), dihedral angles 20.6 and 21.4 degrees. Single crystal structure in space group Pnma (No. 62). B-N bond lengths ~1.45 A indicating partial double bond character. Ceramic composition SiBN3C (Si1.0B1.0N3.0C0.9O0.1); improved thermal stability (onset weight loss 1840 C) and oxidation resistance (up to 1300 C in pure O2) compared to related borazine-precursor-derived SiB1.44N2.20C0.92O0.21 ceramic. Crystalline Si observed at high temperature attributed to thermal decomposition of Si3N4 with N2 evolution. Carbon present as terminal CH3 groups, no free carbonaceous regions inferred from oxidation behavior.
source: Schurz_2010_Borazine_based_molecular_single_source_precursors_for_Si_B_N

elemental_composition.other_elements: Al, N, H, C, O present based on formula AI(NHR)3 with n-propylamine; exact atomic percentages not reported

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Al-N bonds present; Al-H bonds possible (alane-type intermediate); Al(NHR)3 simplified formula with n-propyl R group

functional_groups.other: n-propylamine-derived iminoalane units; tetraalkylammonium salt used as electrolyte additive

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: ammonia, nitrogen, or argon depending on experiment
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Three-stage pyrolysis observed. Stage 1: endothermic weight loss to 220°C. Stage 2: continued weight loss to ~550°C with two DTA exothermic maxima at 313°C and 490°C. Total weight loss at 540°C ~58%. Stage 3: weight increase from ~550°C to 960°C attributed to nitridation of carbide contamination. No distinct crystallization exotherm observed. Heating rate 1-2.5 K/min to 400°C with 60 min hold, then 2.5-5 K/min to final temperature.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - gel formation upon solvent evaporation and heating; solid gel obtained after vacuum/thermal treatment

backbone_architecture.description: Polymeric, gel-like intermediate described as polyiminoalane [AlH(NR)]n; formed by anodic dissolution of metallic aluminum in n-propylamine electrolyte; transforms from syruplike fluid to polymer foam to solid gel upon solvent removal

microstructural.ceramic_phase: AlN (aluminum nitride, wurtzite-type structure); amorphous oxynitride phases possibly present
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Calcination in ammonia at 850°C yields microcrystalline AlN; full crystallinity at 1100°C matching literature XRD. Inert gas calcination results in higher carbon content and broader XRD peaks indicating lower AlN conversion. Amorphous oxynitride phases suspected but not detected by XRD. Carbon contamination causes lattice distortions in wurtzite structure.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Isostatically pressed samples densified to 97.9% of theoretical density without sintering aid or applied pressure

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: semi-crystalline to crystalline depending on calcination temperature
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: AlN wurtzite-type; microcrystalline at 850°C, fully crystalline at 1100°C

notes: This paper concerns a non-silicon preceramic polymer - a polyiminoalane precursor for AlN ceramics, not a silicon-based preceramic polymer. Polymer synthesized by anodic dissolution of metallic Al in n-propylamine/acetonitrile/tetraalkylammonium salt electrolyte at 25 A/m2, up to 30V dc, 6-9 h. Simplified precursor formula AI(NHR)3 where R = n-propyl. Ceramic yield approximately 42% (100% - 58% loss at 540°C) though final yield not explicitly stated. Crystallite sizes by Scherrer equation: 26.4 nm (850°C, NH3), 30.8 nm (1100°C, NH3), 13.9 nm (975°C, N2/Ar), 15.4 nm (1300°C, N2/Ar), 43.1 nm (1500°C, N2/Ar). Carbon content after calcination: NH3 600°C = 0.8%, NH3 975°C = 1.6%, Ar 850°C = 28.3%, Ar 975°C = 25.0%. Oxygen content: NH3 600°C = 2.5%, NH3 975°C = 9.1%, Ar 850°C = 1.8%, Ar 975°C = 2.2%. Particle sizes mostly in micrometer range (13% ≤1 µm by laser granulometry). Ceramic yield midpoint noted; heating rate range 1-2.5 K/min (midpoint 1.75) to 400°C, then 2.5-5 K/min (midpoint 3.75) to final temp.
