elemental_composition.other_elements: Polymer contains Si, H, N only; no Cl detected; no O detected (absence of Si-O-Si bands confirmed by IR). Ideal formula given as [H2SiNH]n.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-N-Si linkages confirmed by IR bands at 1020-840 cm-1; N-H stretching at 3390 cm-1; Si-H stretching at 2172 cm-1; N-H bending at 1180 cm-1; no Si-O-Si bands in 1150-1000 cm-1 region

functional_groups.other: NH groups (secondary amine); Si-H hydride groups confirmed by NMR multiplets at 4.3 and 4.7 ppm; N-H broad resonance between 1.0 and 1.7 ppm; Si-H/N-H area ratio of 3.3

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA conducted at 1.0 C/min from room temperature to 1200 C. Weight loss began at ~50 C and was virtually complete at 450 C, amounting to 31% of initial weight. Decomposition proceeded smoothly and asymptotically with no inflections. Final TGA product was a black solid. Ceramic yield approximately 69% (100-31%). Pyrolysis in Ar at 1150 C for 5 h gave mixture of alpha-Si3N4, beta-Si3N4, and elemental Si. Pyrolysis in N2 at 1150 C for 12 h gave predominantly alpha-Si3N4 with only a trace of elemental Si.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - oil solidifies at room temperature over 3-5 days without significant weight loss; also crosslinked by heating to 200 C for 1 h under Ar flow

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Cryoscopy (cryoscopic molecular weight measurement, reported by Stock and Somieski for the oil product in earlier work)

backbone_architecture.description: Oligomeric/polymeric silazane oil deviating from ideal [H2SiNH]n formula due to cross-linking processes. Initially low viscosity oil that crosslinks over time at room temperature (3-5 days) to form a glassy solid. Ideal repeat unit would be [H2SiNH]n.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis in N2 at 1150 C for 12 h yielded predominantly alpha-Si3N4 with only a trace of elemental Si. Pyrolysis in Ar at 1150 C for 5 h yielded mixture of alpha-Si3N4, beta-Si3N4, and elemental Si. Immersion density of ceramic pieces measured at 2.5 g/cm3.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Open porosity >10%; immersion density 2.5 g/cm3; SEM showed cracking and blistering; crack spacings on order of 20-30 micrometers; fine grain structure ~0.2 micrometers suggested desirable mechanical properties for fibers or bodies

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: alpha-Si3N4 (primary phase after N2 pyrolysis); beta-Si3N4 and elemental Si also identified after Ar pyrolysis; only trace elemental Si after N2 pyrolysis

notes: Paper by Seyferth, Wiseman, and Prud'homme (MIT, 1983). Polymer synthesized by ammonolysis of dichlorosilane (H2SiCl2) with gaseous NH3 in dichloromethane or diethyl ether solution. NH4Cl byproduct removed by filtration; volatiles removed by high-vacuum distillation. Product is a liquid polysilazane oil (not the insoluble silicon diimide [Si(NH)2]n formed from SiCl4 ammonolysis). Oil must be stored under dry N2 or Ar due to hydrolytic sensitivity of Si-N bonds; stable indefinitely at -30 C but crosslinks at room temperature over 3-5 days. Grain size of ~0.2 micrometers reported from SEM (converted: ~200 nm). Porosity noted as >10% open porosity. Ceramic yield of ~70% stated in abstract. Molecular weight of ~350 g/mol from historical cryoscopic measurement. This is a preliminary communication; full structural characterization was ongoing at time of publication.
source: Seyferth_1983_A_Liquid_Silazane_Precursor_To_Silicon_Nitride

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ti-based polymer; ceramic residue (n-butylamine product): 76.7% Ti, 22.1% N, 0.26% C, 0.9% O, 0.08% H by weight; ceramic residue (diamine/CH3NHCH2CH2NHCH3 product): 74.2% Ti, 23.5% N, 1.4% C, 0.5% O by weight

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Ti-N bonds present; Ti-N(alkyl) bonds; amido (NH2) and imido functionalities; Ti coordinated to alkylamino and dimethylamino groups

functional_groups.other: dimethylamino groups [(CH3)2N], primary alkylamino groups (n-butyl, n-hexyl, n-octyl, methoxyethyl), diamine-derived chelating ligands (methylethylenediamine, ethylethylenediamine)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two-stage heating: RT to 250°C at 10°C/min, hold 0.1 h (6 min); 250 to 1000°C at 5°C/min, hold 0.3 h (18 min). Pyrolysis in NH3 stream gave golden-yellow TiN residue (32.3% yield for n-butylamine product; 26.7% yield for diamine product). Pyrolysis in Ar to 1000°C gave black solid containing Ti(45.5%), N(9.9%), C(30.9%) — titanium carbonitride. Pyrolysis to 1500°C under NH3 gave crystalline TiN confirmed by XRD.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: cryoscopy in benzene for diamine products (225–350 average MW); primary amine products reported as >1100 average MW; FAB mass spectrometry used for oligomer identification

backbone_architecture.description: Primary amine products formulated as polymeric [(RN)2Ti]x with possible cyclic structures; diamine products mainly mononuclear Ti species (oligomers) with some di-, tri-nuclear species; primary amine-derived materials are in preceramic polymer molecular weight range (>1100)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Golden-yellow TiN from NH3 pyrolysis to 1000°C; crystalline TiN confirmed by powder XRD at 1500°C under NH3. Black TiCN from Ar pyrolysis at 1000°C containing 45.5% Ti, 9.9% N, 30.9% C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: TiN noted as very hard (8–9 Mohs scale) in introduction as general material property

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: crystalline (after 1500°C pyrolysis); amorphous or poorly crystalline at 1000°C
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: TiN (powder XRD lines matched authentic TiN after 1500°C pyrolysis under NH3)

notes: Paper describes preceramic polymer route to TiN and TiCN from titanium amide polymers derived from [(CH3)2N]4Ti reacted with primary amines or diamines. Polymer type is titanium amide, not silicon-based. Ceramic yield for n-butylamine product: 32.3% (theoretical 32.6%). Major drawback noted: low TiN content potential (67.4% of initial weight must be lost). Diamine-derived precursors are oligomeric (MW 225–350); primary amine-derived materials are higher MW (>1100) and processable (soluble in organic solvents). Atmosphere switch from NH3 to Ar changes ceramic product from TiN to TiCN. Pyrolysis heating rate note: range given as 5–10°C/min; midpoint 7.5°C/min used. Hold time range: 6 and 18 min at different stages; total noted in tga_notes.
source: Seyferth_1988_Preparation_of_titanium_nitride_and_titanium_carbonitride_by

polymer_name: silyl-substituted poly(dimethylsilene) / hybrid polymer with polysilane

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si backbone (polysilmethylene); Si-CH(SiMe2R) pendant groups; Si-Si bonds present in polysilane component [(MeSiH)x(MeSi)y]n

functional_groups.other: chloromethyl (SiMe2CH2Cl) pendant group present in some variants; phenyl group in some model compounds

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Unmodified poly(dimethylsilene) thermally stable to ~400 C, then rapid decomposition complete at ~675 C with no ceramic residue. Silyl-substituted poly(dimethylsilenes) show two-stage decomposition: initial ~25% weight loss between 80-240 C, then rapid weight loss leaving 0-2% ceramic residue between 450-625 C. Hybrid polymer (polysilane:vinyl-substituted polycarbosilane molar ratio 4.0) gave 68% ceramic yield at 1000 C under argon (curve B). Pyrolysis to 1500 C (held 7 h) gave crystalline beta-SiC with further weight loss of 3-9%. Products at 1000 C were amorphous; sample held at 1000 C for 1 h before ramping to 1500 C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: AIBN-catalyzed hydrosilylation between Si-H groups of [(MeSiH)x(MeSi)y]n polysilane and vinyl-substituted poly(dimethylsilene)

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC (toluene, polystyrene standard) and cryoscopy in benzene; GPC showed three fractions: two in 1000-3000 Da range and one very broad peak in 50000-200000 Da range; cryoscopic molecular weight of poly(dimethylsilene) = 2018 Da

backbone_architecture.description: Linear poly(dimethylsilene) (Me2SiCH2)n backbone with pendant silyl groups introduced by metalation/silylation at approximately every 4th CH2 unit; hybrid polymer formed by hydrosilylation cross-linking with [(MeSiH)x(MeSi)y]n polysilane

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramic product at 1000 C was amorphous (only weak broad XRD peaks). After heating to 1500 C, beta-SiC identified by XRD with no elemental silicon detected. Elemental analysis of ceramic from molar ratio 4.0 hybrid polymer: 91 wt% SiC + 9 wt% elemental carbon. Molar ratio 7.5 gave 94 wt% SiC + 6 wt% carbon.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (after pyrolysis to 1500 C); products at 1000 C amorphous

notes: The preceramic polymer system described is a hybrid of a modified poly(dimethylsilene) polycarbosilane {[Me2SiCH2]3[Me2SiCH(SiMe2CH=CH2)]}n and a liquid polysilane [(MeSiH)0.65-0.85(MeSi)0.15-0.35]n (prepared by Na condensation of MeSiHCl2 in hexane/THF). The best ceramic yield reported is 68% at 1000 C (molar ratio polysilane:vinyl-polycarbosilane = 4.0). Pyrolysis at 1500 C gave beta-SiC as confirmed by XRD. Unmodified (Me2SiCH2)n gives no ceramic residue. Ceramic yield range 54-68% noted for molar ratios 1.5-4.0. The polysilane component alone gave ~60% ceramic yield with ~74 wt% SiC and ~26 wt% elemental Si at 1000 C, but no elemental Si observed in hybrid polymer ceramic at 1500 C. AIBN used as hydrosilylation catalyst. Paper focuses primarily on synthesis chemistry.
source: Seyferth_1991_Preparation_of_preceramic_polymers_via_the_metalation_of_pol

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Si backbone bonds; CH3SiH2 end groups present; Si atoms bonded to three other Si atoms at cross-linking sites

functional_groups.other: CH3SiH2 end groups; tertiary and secondary Si-H bonds

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Base polysilane (uncatalyzed) gave only 12%-27% ceramic yield. After catalytic cross-linking with ((eta-C5H5)2ZrH2)n, TGA ceramic yield increased to 74%; furnace pyrolysis gave 72% yield. Catalytic cross-linking with (eta-C5H5)2Zr(CH3)2 gave 71%-85% ceramic residue yields. XRD of ceramic heated to 1500C showed beta-SiC and elemental Si for uncatalyzed product; after catalytic treatment, beta-SiC dominant with little or no elemental Si.

crosslink_density.value: Variable; compositions range from ((CH3SiH)0.75(CH3Si)0.25)n to ((CH3SiH)0.1(CH3Si)0.9)n; after catalytic cross-linking with ZrH2 catalyst composition shifted to ((CH3SiH)0.65(CH3Si)0.35)n from starting ((CH3SiH)0.80(CH3Si)0.20)n
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic - group IV metallocene complexes (Zr and Ti cyclopentadienyl complexes) via dehydrogenative coupling; thermal (reflux) or UV irradiation activation

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Cryoscopic molecular weight measurement in benzene; average degree of polymerization n = 14 to 16

backbone_architecture.description: Polysilane with Si-Si backbone; linear segments interrupted by tri-functional Si cross-linking sites (Si bonded to three other Si); CH3SiH2 end groups present; degree of branching/cross-linking depends on synthesis conditions and catalyst treatment. THF-prepared product more highly cross-linked (60 mol% cross-linking sites).

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Uncatalyzed pyrolysis: 77.3 wt% SiC and 23.7 wt% Si (elemental). After ZrH2 catalytic cross-linking: nominally 98.0 wt% SiC, 1.6 wt% ZrC, 0.4 wt% Si. After Zr(CH3)2 catalytic cross-linking: 93.3 wt% SiC, 5.6 wt% ZrC, 1.0 wt% Si in one experiment. After ZrHCl catalytic cross-linking: 96.6 wt% SiC, 1.7 wt% ZrC, 1.7 wt% Si. After Ti(CH3)2 catalytic cross-linking: 94.8 wt% SiC, 1.2 wt% TiC, 3.9 wt% Si. XRD confirmed beta-SiC phase.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous precursor; partially crystalline ceramic after pyrolysis and heating to 1500C
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (dominant after catalytic treatment); elemental Si (present in uncatalyzed pyrolysis product; absent or trace after catalytic cross-linking); two unassigned weak lines in ZrH2-catalyzed sample ceramic

notes: Starting monomer: CH3SiHCl2 (methyldichlorosilane), C:Si ratio of 1. Polymerization via Na condensation in hexane/THF. Degree of polymerization n=14-16 (cryoscopy). Base polysilane composition approximately ((CH3SiH)0.80(CH3Si)0.20)n. Catalysts used: ((eta-C5H5)2ZrH2)n, (eta-C5H5)2Zr(CH3)2, (eta-C5H5)2ZrHCl, (eta-C5H5)2Ti(CH3)2 at 0.7-1.6 mol%. Catalyst loading ~0.57 mol% for ZrH2 example. THF-prepared highly cross-linked solid: ((CH3SiH)0.4(CH3Si)0.6)n, 60% pyrolysis yield but still 25.6 wt% excess Si. Ceramic elemental analysis for ZrH2-catalyzed product: 29.89% C, 69.90% Si, 1.48% Zr, <0.5% H. Paper title: 'Near-Stoichiometric Silicon Carbide from an Economical Polysilane Precursor.' Pyrolysis temp range noted as up to 950C at 10C/min; XRD analysis performed after additional heating to 1500C.
source: Seyferth_1992_NearStoichiometric_Silicon_Carbide_from_an_Economical_Polysi

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Ureido C=O (amide carbonyl) at ~165 ppm; Si-NCO linkages (isocyanate) observed at 2270 cm-1 in DRIFTS and ~125 ppm in 13C NMR; SiH2 functionality at -30 ppm in 29Si MAS NMR

functional_groups.other: ureido (NHC(O)NH) groups incorporated from urea reaction; isocyanate (NCO) groups as minor component from thermal decomposition; SiH2CH3 functionality from cyclosilazane rearrangement

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two-step thermal decomposition profile. First step (100-500 C): loss of silicon-containing species with Si-H, Si-CH3, SiNSi absorptions, NH3, NCO, C2H2, and residual solvent. Second step (~500 C): primarily methane evolution from methyl group cleavage. Ceramic product is amorphous to 1400 C; heating at 1500 C for 8 h failed to induce crystallization of Si3N4 or SiC. TGA at 10 C/min to 950 C in argon for 4:1 ratio gave 83% yield. For 16:1 ratio, ceramic residue yield was 62% at 960 C. Pyrolysis to 1000 C in NH3 followed by 1400 C in Ar gives ceramic with <2% C. Ceramic yields from two-stage pyrolysis (argon to 1000 C then 1400 C) range from 61-76% depending on CH3Si(H)NH/urea ratio.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - reaction of cyclic [CH3Si(H)NH]n oligomers with urea in pyridine at 85 C for 24 h; degree of crosslinking decreases with increasing CH3Si(H)NH/urea ratio

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Not determined - molecular weight determinations by VPO or GPC were not undertaken due to moisture sensitivity of the polymers

backbone_architecture.description: Complex, nonuniform mixture of linear and cyclic components derived from reaction of cyclic [CH3Si(H)NH]n oligomers with urea. Higher CH3Si(H)NH/urea ratios yield more linear, less crosslinked products (solids to gums to liquids). Building blocks include Si-NH-C(O)-NH-Si ureidosilazane linkages and cyclic silazane units. Products range from white solid (4:1) to colorless gum (10:1) to liquid (16:1).

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis in argon to 1000-1400 C gives black amorphous silicon carbonitride. Pyrolysis in NH3 to 1000 C gives grayish-white silicon nitride with <2% C. Best NH3 pyrolysis result: 55.20% Si, 41.87% N, <0.5% C (12:1 ratio). Argon pyrolysis ceramics contain Si, N, C with Si ~49-59%, N ~21-38%, C ~0.5-14% depending on ratio and conditions. No Si-O species observed by 29Si NMR in any ceramic. Ceramic remains amorphous to 1400 C; 1500 C for 8 h insufficient to crystallize Si3N4 or SiC. 13C NMR shows amorphous SiC phase development at 500-800 C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fibers several meters in length could be drawn by hand from a melt of 6:1 PUSZ; after 1-h air cure, pyrolysis in argon gave black ceramic fibers

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases identified up to 1400 C; heating at 1500 C for 8 h failed to induce crystallization of Si3N4 or SiC

notes: PUSZ synthesized by reaction of cyclic [CH3Si(H)NH]n oligomers (from ammonolysis of CH3SiHCl2) with urea at CH3Si(H)NH/urea molar ratios of 4:1 to 16:1 in pyridine at 85 C for 24 h. Physical form varies with ratio: 4:1 and 6:1 are white solids, 10:1 is colorless gum, 16:1 is liquid. Ceramic yield for starting cyclosilazane oligomer alone is only 15-20% (TGA), rising to 62-83% for PUSZ. Ceramic elemental compositions reported in tables for two pyrolysis conditions: (I) two-stage argon to 1400 C and (II) NH3 to 1000 C then argon to 1400 C. 13C and 15N isotopic labeling with labeled urea used extensively for structural characterization. NCO functionality detected as minor component (~125 ppm 13C NMR, 2270 cm-1 DRIFTS) attributed to thermal chain cleavage during preparation in refluxing pyridine. 29Si MAS NMR shows SiH2 at -30 ppm and Si-H at -20 ppm in 6:1 PUSZ. 15N CPMAS NMR of unlabeled 6:1 PUSZ shows ureido N at 65 ppm and backbone silazane N envelope at ~20 ppm. Pyrolysis in argon to 800 C results in complete loss of C=O functionality and methyl groups, leaving amorphous SiC as detected by broad 13C NMR peak at 25 ppm. Paper from MIT/Alcoa, received 1995.
source: Seyferth_1995_Poly_ureidosilazanes_Preceramic_Polymeric_Precursors_for_Sil

notes: This paper describes organomagnesiumoxanealumoxane oligomers as preceramic precursors for MgAl2O4 (spinel) ceramics, NOT silicon-based preceramic polymers. Polymer type is alumoxane/magnesiumoxanealumoxane. Characterized by 1H, 13C, 27Al NMR, IR spectroscopy, SEM, TGA, XRD, and elemental analysis. Hydrolytically stable in air and soluble in organic solvents. Fiber-forming properties at Al:Mg = 2:1 and 1:1. Softening temperatures (T1) range 48-106°C, melt temperatures (T2) 87-126°C, fiberization zones 95-148°C, decomposition temperatures (T3) 123-160°C. Prepared by co-condensation in ethanol or toluene at 30-70°C. All elemental composition values are in wt%, not atomic%.
source: Shcherbakova_2017_Preceramic_organomagnesiumoxanealumoxanes_Synthesis_properti

Pyrolysis was also conducted at 900°C and 1500°C in air furnace to yield xMgO·yAl2O3 binary ceramics.

backbone_architecture.description: Alumoxane backbone with organomagnesiumoxane groups in side chains at aluminum atoms; oligomeric structure with Mg-O-Al linkages; chelated alkoxyalumoxane core with alumoxane bonds preserved upon reaction with Mg(acac)2; contains four-, five-, and six-coordinate aluminum centers

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Binary ceramic xMgO·yAl2O3 obtained by pyrolysis in air at 900°C and 1500°C; target phase is magnesium aluminate spinel MgAl2O4; phase compositions determined by XRD using ICDD PDF Release 2003 data with Cu radiation (λ=1.54178 Å)

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Organomagnesiumoxanealumoxane oligomers described as brittle solid substances; fiber-forming properties exhibited at Al:Mg molar ratios of 2:1 and 1:1; softening points 48-106°C, fiberization temperature ranges 95-148°C, melting/solidification points 123-160°C

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: X-ray amorphous (preceramic polymer); ceramic products contain MgAl2O4 spinel and MgO/Al2O3 phases identified by XRD

notes: This paper describes preceramic organomagnesiumoxanealumoxanes (not silicon-based preceramic polymers) synthesized from chelated alkoxyalumoxanes (ethoxyhydroxyalumoxane ethylacetoacetate or ethoxyisobutoxyhydroxyalumoxane ethylacetoacetate) reacted with magnesium acetylacetonate Mg(acac)2. The polymers are intended as precursors to MgAl2O4 spinel ceramics. They are hydrolytically stable in air, soluble in organic solvents (ethanol, toluene, CDCl3, C6D6), and exhibit fiber-forming properties at Al:Mg=2:1 and 1:1 molar ratios. TGA ceramic yield range across samples approximately 29.40-32.82 wt% (reported as Al2O3 equivalent). NMR performed on Bruker Avance 600 MHz; 27Al NMR shows three aluminum coordination environments. SEM performed on Philips SEM 505 with EDX. The polymer is alumoxane-based, not silazane/carbosilane/siloxane-based.
source: Shcherbakova_2017_Synthesis_of_preceramic_organomagnesiumoxanealumoxanes

Average molecular weight 1000-1300 g/mol by GPC. Dark brown solid, highly soluble in toluene and hexane. General formula I described in paper (metallocarbosilane with incorporated metal atoms via Si-N-M linkages).

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After ceramization at 1250C under argon: amorphous/nanocrystalline SiC (moissanite-3C, PDF-2 [29-1129]) with crystallite size ~2 nm, plus graphite admixture (peak at 2theta ~26.5 deg). After higher temperature treatment (XRD refinement result): beta-SiC (space group F-4-3m No.216, a=4.3602 Å) = 80.2 wt% and Ta0.8Zr0.2C (space group Fm-3m No.225, a=4.4998 Å) = 19.8 wt%. Refractory metals in amorphous state or incorporated into crystal lattice at 1250C. Crystallization exotherm at ~1147C. Target ceramic phases: SiC modified with mixed carbides TaxZryCz or TaxHfyCz.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Values cited from reference [11] for SiTaC(O) fibers from polytantalocarbosilane (TaPCS), not from the Ta(Zr/Hf)PCS materials synthesized in this study. Tensile strength 1.9 GPa, Young's modulus 202 GPa, fiber diameter 20 micrometers.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: As-synthesized metallocarbosilanes are X-ray amorphous. After ceramization at 1250C: amorphous/nanocrystalline beta-SiC + graphite. After higher temperature treatment: beta-SiC (F-4-3m) and Ta0.8Zr0.2C (Fm-3m).

notes: Six different metallocarbosilane compositions synthesized with varying Ta/Zr or Ta/Hf molar ratios (2:1 overall Ta/M ratio in synthesis). Si-H content in precursor oligomers ranges 0.72-0.75 wt%. Polymer fiber formation by melt-spinning demonstrated for entry 1 (Ta/Zr, Ta/M=4, fiber formation temperature 250-260C). Entry 4 (Ta/Hf) does not possess fiber-forming ability. Entries 5 and 6 show weak fiber-forming ability. Carbidization studied at 1250, 1500, and 1900C under argon. Mixed carbides targeted: Ta4ZrC5 (mp 3810-3840C) and Ta3HfC4 (mp 3820-3920C). Synthesis by co-condensation of oligodimethylsilylenemethylenes with mixtures of Ta[N(CH3)2]5 and M(NR2)4 (M=Zr or Hf). XRD Rietveld refinement parameters: Rp=8.7%, Rwp=11.4%, RBragg=9.6% (SiC) and 7.5% (Ta0.8Zr0.2C).

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Polymer-to-ceramic transition occurs in two steps: volatilization of silicon oligomers around 300-400 C, then organic bond breaking with CH4 release at 600-800 C. Weight loss of ~12% for pure MSR (no PMMA). PMMA decomposition starts ~210 C and completes by 400 C under nitrogen at 5 C/min. Pre-pyrolysis hold at 400 C for 1 h in vacuum at 1 C/min to eliminate PMMA. Pyrolysis at 800, 1000, and 1200 C with 2 C/min heating rate and 2 h dwell.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) - amorphous ceramic in which Si atoms are bonded to both O and C atoms. Confirmed amorphous by X-ray diffraction. IR spectra show only Si-O and Si-C bonds.

notes: Study focuses on microcellular SiOC ceramics produced from methylsilicone resin (SILRES 610, Wacker-Chemie) using PMMA microbeads (M-100, avg 4.7 um, <15 um) as sacrificial pore-forming agents. PMMA added 0-80 wt%. Pyrolysis at 800-1200 C in vacuum. Volume shrinkage stabilizes above 1000 C, reaching ~60% at 80 wt% PMMA. Spherical micropores 1-10 um formed across all PMMA loadings. Open-cell structure forms above 30 wt% PMMA with open pore size >0.5 um. Bulk density at 80 wt% PMMA ~0.4 g/cm3 (green density 1.20 g/cm3). Mn calculated from Mw=9400 and PDI=3.6 giving Mn~2611 g/mol. Glass transition temperature of MSR is 41.9 C. Zinc acetylacetonate used as cross-linking catalyst at 0.1 wt%.

notes: Study focuses on chemical stability improvement of perhydropolysilazane via HMDS (1,1,1,3,3,3-hexamethyldisilazane) end-capping. HMDS reacts primarily with terminal SiH3 groups via N-H of HMDS attacking SiH3, forming Si-N bonds with H2 elimination. Mn increase rate of HMDS-modified polymer (~0.3/day) is 10x slower than raw perhydropolysilazane (~3/day) when 5 atomic% HMDS radical is introduced (corresponding to 30 wt% HMDS feed). Polymer synthesized by ammonolysis of dichlorosilane-pyridine adduct. HMDS radical content controllable by HMDS feed concentration; approximately 30% of fed HMDS bonds to polymer. Polymer is soluble in chloroform, cyclohexane, and dibutylether. Stability evaluated at 40C over 40 days in m-xylene solution under dry N2. Elemental compositions reported in wt% for four HMDS concentrations (5, 10, 20, 30 wt%) and raw perhydropolysilazane as shown in table.

notes: Two PCS samples studied: PCS_1 (Mn=2350, Tm=210 C, Ts=250 C, Tc=180-220 C, Tpy=1200 C) and PCS_2 (Mn=2979, Tm=250 C, Ts=280 C). Synthesized from polydimethylsilane with ZSM-5 zeolite catalyst at 350 C for 10-20 h then 400 C for 10 h. Molecular weight adjusted by additional heating at 400 C for 5-15 h. Fiber diameter 20-30 um after melt spinning at 230-250 C. Optimum curing condition found to be 200 C isothermal oxidation (13 wt% gain after 5 h). Isothermal oxidation weight gains: 180 C = ~5.5 wt% after 2 h plateau; 190 C = 7.3 wt% after 5 h; 200 C = 13 wt% after 5 h. At temperatures above 1400 C, amorphous SiOC decomposes into SiO(g) and CO(g). Paper published in Asian Journal of Chemistry, Vol. 26, No. 13 (2014), pp. 4121-4124.

notes: This paper does not describe a preceramic polymer. It describes a double complex salt (DCS) inorganic single-source precursor [Pd(NH3)4][AuCl4]2 used for thermolysis synthesis of Au-Pd nanoporous alloy structures. No silicon, polymer backbone, or ceramic conversion is involved. Grain size of 14±3 nm refers to ligament diameter of the nanoporous structure observed by HR-TEM. Crystallite sizes from XRD Scherrer analysis range from ~5.5 nm to ~42 nm depending on phase and temperature (see tables). Specific surface area measured by Ar thermal desorption (BET). In situ synchrotron XRD performed at VEPP-3, wavelength 1.731 Å. Final alloy composition Au0.67Pd0.33 confirmed by EDX and XRD lattice parameter analysis using Vegard's law.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: White boron nitride powder produced. IR and XRD characteristic of turbostratic BN at 1200 C. Density increases from 1.8 g/mL to 2.1 g/mL upon heating to 1450 C, approaching h-BN (2.2 g/mL).

notes: Paper describes multiple boron-containing preceramic polymers: poly(borazine)/poly(borazylene), poly(vinylborazine), and poly(vinylpentaborane). Target ceramics are boron nitride and boron carbide (not silicon-based ceramics). Poly(borazine) is isolated as finely divided white powder, soluble in polar solvents (ethers), stable at room temperature under vacuum. Molecular weight up to 8500 reported. Ceramic yield range 90-95%; midpoint 92.5% used. Poly(vinylpentaborane) described as the only polymeric precursor to pure boron carbide. Copolymers of styrene and vinylborazine also synthesized. AIBN used as radical initiator for poly(vinylborazine) at 50 C. Transition metal catalysts [(Cp*)IrCl2]2 and RhH(CO)(PPh3)3 used for vinylborane synthesis. Thin film applications explored for B4C thermoelectric materials and BN coatings.
source: Sneddon_1989_Synthesis_and_properties_of_new_preceramic_materials

functional_groups.other: Borazine rings (inorganic B3N3 aromatic units); N-H groups implied by borazine structure

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Polyborazylene pyrolyzed under argon or ammonia to 1200C gives white boron nitride powders in ceramic yields 85-95% (theoretical ceramic yield 95%). Poly(B-vinylborazine) requires ammonia atmosphere to achieve low-carbon boron nitride due to carbon backbone. Fiber coatings formed by heating to ~900C under ammonia or argon.

backbone_architecture.description: Polyborazylene: branched-chain or partially crosslinked structure with empirical formula B3N3H3; complex structure with linear, branched, and fused chain segments inferred from isolation of N:B coupled dimer and borazanaphthalene. Poly(B-vinylborazine): carbon backbone with pendant borazine rings; molecular weight distribution skewed to high MW suggesting some crosslinking or branching via B-N linkages.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: White boron nitride powders of excellent purity formed from polyborazylene at 1200C. Poly(B-vinylborazine) gives low-carbon BN under ammonia. Metal borides (TiB2, ZrB2) formed from decaborane/dinitrile polymer with TiO2 or ZrO2 at >1450C in >90% yield.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: BN fiber coatings noted to enhance composite strength by decreasing interfacial shear strength and increasing fiber pullout toughness; no quantitative values given

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: TiB2, ZrB2 confirmed highly crystalline by XRD with no unreacted MO2 or other ceramic phases detected

notes: Paper covers multiple boron-based preceramic polymer systems: (1) poly(borazylene) - Mw 7600, Mn 3400, empirical formula B3N3H3, ceramic yield 85-95% to BN at 1200C; (2) poly(B-vinylborazine) - prepared via AIBN free-radical route, Mw ~18000, Mn ~10700; (3) poly(styrene-co-B-vinylborazine) copolymers with varying styrene content (22-100 mol% feed, observed 67-100 mol%), Mw range 11000-23400; (4) decaborane/dinitrile polymer used as precursor to TiB2 and ZrB2 at >1450C in >90% yield. No silicon-containing polymers described. Ceramic fiber coatings (BN) demonstrated on alumina, SiC, Si3N4, and carbon fibers. Molecular weight midpoint for polyborazylene reported; ceramic yield range 85-95% midpoint 90 used.
source: Sneddon_1991_Molecular_and_polymeric_ceramic_precursors

Polyborazylene alone reported to convert to boron nitride in 90-94% ceramic yield. At 800C for 9.5h, significant hydrogen still present (B1.03:N1.0:H0.79), indicating crosslinking still occurring. At 1000C for 2h, titanium metal fully consumed and crystalline TiN forms. TiB2 crystallinity observed at 1000C after 3 days or at 1200C after 1h.

Also mentions borazine-modified polysilazanes as precursors to Si3N4/BN composites (in preparation, not detailed). Ceramic yield midpoint for Ti composite: (96.0+95.5+94.9)/3 = 95.5% approx; range noted in tga_notes.

notes: Paper covers multiple polymer systems including polyvinylborazine, polyborazylene, borazine-modified hydridopolysilazane (HPZ), poly(styrene-co-B-vinylborazine), decaborane-based metal boride precursors, and polyborazylene-based TiB2/TiN composite precursors. The primary preceramic polymer described in detail with compositional table data is the borazine-modified hydridopolysilazane. Polyborazylene (separate polymer): Mw ~7600, Mn ~3400 by SEC/LALLS/UV; branched-chain or partially crosslinked structure; ceramic yield 85-93% to 1200°C under argon or ammonia to give boron nitride. Unmodified HPZ ceramic yield ~57%. The ceramic yield range in the table spans 51.1-69.9%; midpoint used for ceramic_yield_pct field is 65.36 (range noted here). Polymer synthesis: HPZ reacted with liquid borazine at 73°C for 2.2-7.0 hours.

notes: Polysilazanes synthesized by co-ammonolysis of MeHSiCl2 and Me2SiCl2 in benzene under NH3 atmosphere, followed by thermal polymerization at 300-480 C for 1-1.5 h under N2. Optimal Me2SiCl2/MeHSiCl2 molar ratio is 1:1 to 1:2 for spinnable PSZ. Thermal polymerization proceeds via dehydrocoupling reactions between Si-H and N-H groups. IR absorptions: C-H at 2960, 2900, 1410 cm-1; Si-CH3 and Si-C at 1260, 825, 690, 630 cm-1; N-H at 3400, 1180 cm-1; Si-N-Si at 920 cm-1; Si-H at 2150 cm-1; Si3N at 1040 cm-1. Ceramic heat treated at 1400 C and 1500 C in argon: Si-N-C ceramic retains composition better than Si-N ceramic at elevated temperatures. Ceramic yield not explicitly reported as a percentage. Institution: Changsha Institute of Technology, China.

notes: Polymer synthesized by co-pyrolysis of polydimethylsilane (PDMS) and polyvinylchloride (PVC) at PVC/PDMS weight ratios of 3-7 wt%. Key molecular weight and PDI data by sample: PC-P5-2 (Mn=1201, PDI=2.03), PC-P5-4 (Mn=1271, PDI=1.98), PC-P5-6 (Mn=1370, PDI=1.76), PC-P5-7 (Mn=1575, PDI=1.89), PC-P5-8 (Mn=1711, PDI=2.07), PC-P5-10 (Mn>5000), PC-P3-6 (Mn=1385, PDI=2.13), PC-P7-6 (Mn=1671, PDI=2.06). Melting points range from 134-215 degrees C for spinnable samples. Carbon introduction is less than 2 wt% relative to base PCS. Mechanism proposed is hydrosilylation between Si-H bonds of silane oligomers and double bonds from PVC pyrolysis fragments, forming Si-C-C bridges and preventing pitch formation. Products intended as precursors for SiC-C fiber via melt-spinning, curing, and heat treatment.

Strong exotherm in DSC at first weight loss. Char yields: 78% at 1250°C/1h, 64% at 1450°C/12h, 49% at 1900°C/25h in argon/vacuum. notes: This paper describes a preceramic polymer that is NOT a silicon-based polymer; it is a boron-based decaborane-dinitrile polymer used as a precursor to metal borides (TiB2, ZrB2, HfB2, NbB2, TaB2) via dispersion with metal oxides and pyrolysis. The polymer formula is (-B10H12-NC-(CH2)5-CN-)x. Ceramic yield of 86% observed by TGA at 500°C completion. Bulk pyrolysis char yields: 77.9% at 1250°C/1h, 64% at 1450°C/12h, 48.5% at 1900°C/25h. All elemental compositions reported as weight percent, not atomic percent. Pyrolyses below 1900°C under flowing argon at 10°C/min; at or above 1900°C under vacuum in graphite furnace. Metal boride grain sizes: TiB2/ZrB2 nanometer-scale at 1300°C, 2-5 nm at 2000°C by SEM; NbB2/TaB2 average 1.0 µm at 1480°C. TiB2 coatings on graphite plates also demonstrated. Paper from University of Pennsylvania, received 1993.

notes: Paper describes a series of borazine-substituted HPZ polymers (labeled 1-4) with increasing borazine content synthesized by reaction of HPZ with borazine at 60-90 C. Molecular weight values reported above are for Polymer 2 as a representative example; full MW data given for HPZ, HPZ control, and polymers 1-4 in notes. Densities of ceramics: HPZ=2.58, Polymer 2=2.31, Polymer 3=2.32, Polymer 4=1.84 g/cm3. Model study with hexamethyldisilazane and borazine identified B-(N(SiMe3)2)-borazine and N-Me3Si-borazine products, supporting proposed B-to-N linkage mechanism via trimethylsilane or H2 elimination. notes: Paper covers multiple topics: (1) zinc phosphate conversion coatings for steel, (2) pre-ceramic polymetallosiloxane (PMS) coatings for aluminum substrates, and (3) PEEK polymer characteristics. JSON fields above pertain specifically to the PMS polymer system. Precursor organosilane monomers include N-[3-(triethoxysilyl)propyl]-4,5-dihydroimidazole (TSPI) and 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane (GPS). Metal alkoxides used include Ti(OR)4, Zr(OC3H7)4, and Al(OC3H7)3. HCl used as hydrolysis catalyst; CH3OH and water as solvent medium. Films applied as corrosion-protective coatings on aluminum substrates. Four key factors for good film: (1) organopolymetallosiloxane formation at 150°C sintering; (2) pyrolytic conversion at 350°C to amorphous network with enhanced Si-O-M linkages; (3) non-crystalline phases; (4) interfacial oxane bond between PMS and Al oxide. Thin films <1 micrometer thickness targeted to reduce microcracking.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si cross-links formed during EB curing; C-H bonds in Si-CH2-Si main chain; Si-O-Si bonds formed via peroxide decomposition during EB oxidation curing

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis conducted stepwise from 500 to 2000 K in 100 K increments. Two major reaction steps: (1) 800-1200 K with H2 and CH4 evolution from Si-H and Si-CH3 scission; (2) 1000-1700 K with H2 evolution from C-H bonds in Si-CH2-Si main chain. CO evolves above 1700-1800 K for high oxygen content fibers. Minor gases include H2O, CO2, C2H6, C2H4.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: Electron beam irradiation (in He or air) or thermal oxidation; EB curing forms Si-CH2-Si cross-links; thermal oxidation and EB oxidation form Si-O-Si cross-links

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Not specified

backbone_architecture.description: PCS main chain with Si-CH2-Si backbone; cross-linking introduced via EB irradiation forming Si-CH2-Si bridges between chains, or Si-O-Si bridges via oxidative curing

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Beta-SiC crystal formed as final ceramic product. High oxygen content fibers yield SiCO phase. Organometallic-to-mineral transition at 823-1073 K, SiC nucleation at 1273-1473 K, SiC grain coarsening above 1673 K.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: SiC fibers described as flexible with high tensile strength; tensile strength decreases above ~1500 K for high-oxygen Nicalon-type fibers

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC

notes: PCS fibers were 20 +/- 2 um in diameter. Melting point of PCS was 506 +/- 2 K. Spun at ~583 K in N2 at ~3 m/s. Curing conditions: (1) EB cross-linking: 1.3 kGy/s, 12 MGy in He, O2 content 1.1 wt%; (2) EB oxidation: 1.9 kGy/s, 2.5 MGy in air, O2 content ~1.2 wt%; (3) EB oxidation: 1.9 kGy/s, 3.5 MGy in air, O2 content ~1.7 wt%; (4) Thermal oxidation: 460 K in O2, O2 content ~1.3 wt%. Nicalon fibers contain ~10 wt% oxygen and decompose above ~1500 K. Thermal stability improved significantly when oxygen content reduced to less than 0.4 wt%. Gas analysis performed by GC with molecular sieve 5A and Polapack-S columns. Pyrolysis heating rate was 1.8 K/min (approximately 1.08 deg C/min) for final temperature step, with 3.6 K/min ramp to previously reached temperature.
source: Sugimoto_1995_Reaction_Mechanisms_of_Silicon_Carbide_Fiber_Synthesis_by_He

elemental_composition.other_elements: Oxygen content in cured PCS fibers ranged from 1.1 to 17 wt% depending on curing conditions

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C-H bonds present in PCS main chain; Si-CH3 bonds cleaved during pyrolysis; peroxy radicals formed in presence of oxygen

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Heat treatment from 400 to 2000 K. Pyrolysis converts PCS to SiC via free radical mechanisms.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: electron beam irradiation (EB) and thermal oxidation

backbone_architecture.description: PCS fibers spun at ~583 K from melted PCS into fibers of 20 ± 2 µm diameter; main chain contains Si-C bonds with Si-H and Si-CH3 side groups

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCS fibers converted to SiC fibers upon pyrolysis; oxygen content in cured precursor affects thermal stability of resulting SiC fibers

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: SiC fibers described as flexible and long with high thermal resistance and high tensile strength

notes: Paper focuses on ESR analysis of free radical reactions during pyrolysis of radiation-cured PCS fibers. Oxygen content in cured PCS varied: 1.1 wt% (EB cross-linking, 12 MGy in He), 12 wt% (EB oxidation, 2.5 MGy in Air), 17 wt% (EB oxidation, 3.5 MGy in Air), 13 wt% (thermal oxidation at 460 K in O2). Maximum radical concentrations ranged from 3.38 to 5.36 x10^19 spins/g with Si atoms per radical ratio of 180-250. Radicals on Si atoms formed by Si-H cleavage at 800-1000 K; radicals on C atoms formed by C-H cleavage at 1000-1800 K. Pyrolysis temperature range in text is 400-2000 K (127-1727°C); max temperature noted as 2000 K = 1727°C. Heating rate given as 3 K/min.

polymer_name: PHEC (Polymer precursor of High Entropy Carbide)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ti, Zr, Hf, Ta - total metal content 28 wt%; n(Ti):n(Zr):n(Hf):n(Ta) = 1.00:1.02:1.04:1.05 (approximately equiatomic)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Ti-O (661 cm-1), Hf-O (442 cm-1), Zr-O and Ta-O (543 cm-1), metal-acetylacetonate coordination (C=O at 1593 cm-1, C=C at 1518 cm-1, C-CH3 at 1275 cm-1), metal-propoxide (M-OPr) bonds, terminal vinyl C=H from allyl novolac (3082 cm-1), hydroxyl O-H (3443 cm-1)

functional_groups.other: acetylacetonate (acac) chelating ligand, metal propoxide (M-OPr), hydroxyl groups (residual, low content after hydrolysis), allyl-functional novolac resin (AN) as carbon source

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed in N2 at 10 deg C/min from RT to 1450 deg C. Four mass loss stages: (1) RT-250 deg C ~5 wt% loss (water/residual OH); (2) 250-500 deg C ~20 wt% loss (organic framework pyrolysis, organic-to-inorganic conversion); (3) 500-900 deg C ~6 wt% loss (further pyrolysis to inorganic); (4) 900-1450 deg C ~16 wt% loss (carbothermal reduction of metal oxides by carbon). Curing program before pyrolysis: 160, 180, 200, 220, 250 deg C each for 1 h at 3 deg C/min.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (curing at 160-250 deg C, 1 h each step, 3 deg C/min)

backbone_architecture.description: Metal alkoxide copolymer formed by controlled co-hydrolysis and polycondensation of Ti, Zr, Hf, Ta alkoxides with acetylacetonate stabilization, combined with allyl-functional novolac resin as carbon source. Metal atoms coordinated via acac and propoxide bridges forming a metal-oxo polymer network in propanol solution.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: (Ti, Zr, Hf, Ta)C high entropy carbide, FCC structure
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: 600 deg C: amorphous; 800 deg C: t-ZrO2 and oxide solid solutions (Ti,Zr)Ox, (Ti,Hf)Ox, (Hf,Ta)Ox; 1000 deg C: carbide solid solutions (Zr,Hf)C and (Ti,Ta)C begin forming via carbothermal reduction; 1200 deg C: two carbide solid solution peaks converging, residual HfO2 and m-ZrO2; 1400 deg C: oxide peaks diminishing, single broad carbide peak; 1500 deg C: carbothermal reduction nearly complete; 1800 deg C: symmetric FCC single-phase (Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta)C with lattice parameter 0.45293 nm (Vegard's law value 0.45282 nm). Lattice fringes of 0.260 nm correspond to (111) FCC plane. Graphitic carbon shell ~2 nm thick around particles observed by HRTEM.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: High entropy carbide ceramics noted in introduction as having high hardness and high modulus (general class property), but no measured values reported for the specific ceramic powder produced in this work

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: (Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta)C FCC single phase at 1800 deg C; intermediate phases at lower temperatures include t-ZrO2, m-ZrO2, HfO2, oxide solid solutions (Ti,Zr)Ox, (Ti,Hf)Ox, (Hf,Ta)Ox, and carbide solid solutions (Zr,Hf)C and (Ti,Ta)C

notes: This paper reports a liquid polymer precursor route to (Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta)C high entropy carbide ceramic nanopowders. The precursor PHEC is not a classical Si-based preceramic polymer (polysilazane/polycarbosilane/etc.) but a metal alkoxide-based preceramic polymer. Ceramic yield 28.6 wt% at 1800 deg C. Viscosity 150 mPa·s as synthesized, 162 mPa·s after 60 days storage at RT (8% increase). Grain size range from 8 nm (1400 deg C) to 42 nm (1800 deg C) by XRD/JADE analysis. Final particle size ~100 nm by SEM and TEM. Metal ratio n(Ti):n(Zr):n(Hf):n(Ta) = 1.00:1.02:1.04:1.05. No Cl- present (advantage over metal chloride routes). Soluble in polar solvents (propanol). TGA heating rate 10 deg C/min in N2; pyrolysis heating rate 3 deg C/min in vacuum.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: CG Nicalon: SiC1.31O0.36 - excess carbon and significant oxygen; Hi-Nicalon: SiC1.39O0.01 - mainly SiC microcrystals and amorphous carbon, little oxygen; Hi-Nicalon type S: SiC1.05O0.01 - near-stoichiometric highly crystalline SiC with slight excess carbon and trace oxygen. Oxide layer after high-temperature air exposure is amorphous SiO2, cristobalite, or mixture.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Hi-Nicalon elastic modulus 220 GPa (lower than monolithic SiC >400 GPa). Hi-Nicalon type S strength 1.8 GPa after 10 h argon exposure at 1873 K. Tensile strength measured by single-filament method (JIS R 7601) with 25 mm gauge length.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC microcrystals in Hi-Nicalon and Hi-Nicalon type S; amorphous carbon in Hi-Nicalon; cristobalite (SiO2) forms in oxide layer after exposure at 1473-1673 K in air; amorphous SiO2 oxide layer at lower temperatures

notes: This paper primarily studies the oxidation behavior of PCS-derived SiC fibers (CG Nicalon, Hi-Nicalon, Hi-Nicalon type S) rather than the preceramic polymer itself. Polymer information is limited to synthesis route and repeat unit. CG Nicalon fiber: SiC1.31O0.36, density 2.55 g/cm3, radius 7 um, as-received oxygen content 11.7%, MW(SiCxOy)=49.5 g/mol. Hi-Nicalon fiber: SiC1.39O0.01, density 2.74 g/cm3, radius 7 um, as-received oxygen content 0.5%, MW(SiCxOy)=44.8 g/mol. Hi-Nicalon type S: SiC1.05O0.01, density 3.10 g/cm3, radius 6 um, as-received oxygen content 0.2%, MW(SiCxOy)=40.8 g/mol. Oxidation tests in humid air (2 vol% H2O), dry air (<2.6 ppm H2O), and argon at 1273-1673 K for 1-100 h. Oxide layer growth follows parabolic law. Cristobalite formation degrades fiber strength due to thermal expansion mismatch and beta-to-alpha phase transition (-8.8% volume decrease) on cooling.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis performed at discrete temperatures from 673 K (400 C) to 973 K (700 C). Radiation-cured powder lost ~0.5% weight relative to raw PCS at 673 K; thermally cured powder gained ~10% weight due to oxygen incorporation. Radiation-cured powder yielded higher ceramic yield than thermally cured powder due to smaller amount of evolved gas (H2 and CH4). Major decomposed gases were H2 and CH4; thermally cured powder also evolved H2O at low temperatures from hydroxyl group decomposition.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: radiation (electron beam, 2 MeV, 12 MGy) for radiation-cured; thermal oxidation (473 K, 1 h in air) for thermally cured; further crosslinking occurs during pyrolysis via cleavage of Si-H and Si-CH3 bonds and deformation of Si-CH2-Si

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Conversion of PCS to SiC by pyrolysis. Micropores of radius ~0.4 nm (close to reported network space of PCS) formed during pyrolysis. At 973 K micropores disappeared for radiation-cured powder; some pores remained for thermally cured powder. Target application is hydrogen separation membrane.

notes: Study compares radiation-cured (electron beam, 2 MeV, 12 MGy in helium, followed by annealing at 673 K) vs. thermally cured (oxidation at 473 K, 1 h in air) PCS powder. Average powder diameter was 4 micrometers. Pyrolysis performed in argon (purity >99.995%, residual O2 <10 ppm) at 723, 773, 823, 873, 973 K for 30 min. Density measured by Archimedes method (apparent density). FT-IR in ATR mode used to observe crosslinking. Nitrogen adsorption isotherm at 77 K used for pore size distribution (t-plot method). Total pore volume refers to pores with diameter less than ~60 nm; micropores defined as pores with widths not exceeding ~2 nm. Radiation-cured powder showed narrower micropore size distribution (desirable for H2 separation membrane, kinetic diameter 0.289 nm) compared to thermally cured powder due to smaller evolved gas volume preventing pore aggregation. Pyrolysis temperature range given in Kelvin: 673-973 K (400-700 C). Ceramic yield figures referenced but numerical values not explicitly tabulated in text.

notes: Paper focuses on solid-state 29Si CP/MAS NMR characterization of oxidation-cured polycarbosilane fibres. PC synthesized by thermal decomposition of polydimethylsilane (PDMS) in nitrogen flow. Fibres melt-spun at 310 C in nitrogen, then cured in oxygen at 145-175 C. Four samples studied: P151-F (uncured), P145-1, P160-1, P175-1. Key finding: oxygen attacks SiC3H bonds converting them to Si-O-Si bonds as curing temperature increases. NMR measured at 11.9 MHz for 29Si using Jeol FX-60Q spectrometer with magic-angle spinning at ~1.6 kHz. Chemical shifts referenced to TMS via PDMS external reference (-34.1 ppm vs TMS). Cured fibres are insoluble in any solvent.

notes: Study focuses on electron irradiation curing mechanism of polycarbosilane fibres using solid-state 29Si and 13C NMR. Fibres melt-spun at 310°C in nitrogen atmosphere. Irradiation performed in vacuum with 2 MeV electrons. 29Si-NMR signals at -0.5 ppm (SiC4) and -17.5 ppm (SiC3H). Dipolar dephasing used to assign protonated vs non-protonated Si. Si-H bond cleavage identified as primary crosslinking mechanism; relative SiC3H signal decreases linearly with dose. C-H bond cleavage also implicated. Thermal oxidation curing at 175°C in oxygen introduces Si-O-C and Si-O-Si bonds not present after electron irradiation curing. Gel fraction measured by THF insolubility. Paper published 1987.

notes: Paper focuses on oxidation curing mechanism of polycarbosilane (PC) fibres studied by solid-state 13C and 29Si CP/MAS NMR. PC synthesized by thermal decomposition of polydimethylsilane (PDMS) in nitrogen, melt-spun at 310 C, then cured in oxygen gas flow at 145-195 C. Six silicon bonding environments quantified: Si-C, Si-H, Si-Si, Si-O-Si, Si-O-C(I), Si-O-C(II). During oxidation curing, Si-H bonds are attacked by oxygen first converting to Si-O-Si, then above 175 C also forming Si-O-C(II) and Si-O-C(I). Oxygen content increases linearly with curing temperature. All oxidation-cured fibres are insoluble in all solvents. NMR measured at 11.9 MHz for 29Si, 15.04 MHz for 13C, spinning frequency ~2.0 kHz. Chemical shifts referenced to TMS via solid PDMS standard at -34.1 ppm relative to TMS.

notes: Study focuses on solid-state NMR characterization (29Si CP/MAS, 13C CP/MAS, 1H CRAMPS) of uncured, oxidation-cured, and electron irradiation-cured PCS fibers. notes: Polymer synthesised by one-pot condensation of boron trichloride (BTC), trichlorosilane (TCS) and heptamethyldisilazane (HpMDZ) in molar ratio 1:1:4 in n-hexane; excess HpMDZ used to limit molecular weight; Me3SiCl and HpMDZ byproducts removed by in situ distillation. Softening point ~143°C. Green fibres melt-spun at 172°C in N2-filled glove-box yielding continuous fibres >600 m length and ~15 µm diameter. N-CH3 groups from HpMDZ play key role in reducing cross-linking and improving processability versus hexamethyldisilazane (HxMDZ)-based route. Absence of Si-H and N-H groups in starting monomers is critical to avoiding premature dehydrogenation cross-linking. Fibre diameter after pyrolysis ~10 µm. No chlorine detected in final polymer.

notes: Paper investigates decarbonization mechanisms of electron beam-cured PCS fibers pyrolyzed in hydrogen to produce near-stoichiometric SiC fibers analogous to Hi-Nicalon Type S. Key finding: Si-CH2-CH2-Si groups in PCS backbone are responsible for carbon over-removal (C/Si < 1) via thermal cleavage of C-C bonds and subsequent methane release. Softening point of PCS precursor: 200 C. As-cured fiber average diameter: 28 micrometers. Oxygen content of as-cured fibers: 1.88 wt%. FTIR bands: Si-H at 2100 cm-1, Si-CH3 at 1250 cm-1, C-H at 2950/2900 cm-1, CH2-CH2 at 1425 cm-1. Raman band at 710 cm-1 assigned to C-C bonds. Pyrolysis in nitrogen yields C/Si ~1.40 at equivalent temperatures. Fibers must be immediately heat-treated in argon after hydrogen pyrolysis to annihilate free radicals and prevent oxidation.

notes: This paper is a PhD thesis (Hussein Termoss, Université Claude Bernard Lyon I, 2009) focused on preparation of BN coatings via the PDC (Polymer Derived Ceramics) route. Three main precursors studied: poly(alkylamino)borazine, borazine monomer, and polyborazylene (PBN). PBN synthesized at 4 temperatures (45, 50, 55, 60°C) in autoclave for 120h with pressures 11-85 bar. B/H ratio R decreases with polymerization temperature (0.88 borazine to 0.53 PBN60C). Coatings deposited by dip-coating on graphite, quartz, titanium, copper, aluminum, Pyrex substrates. Film thicknesses measured by m-lines spectroscopy: 1014-6164 nm depending on withdrawal speed and heat treatment. Refractive index of BN films measured: n=1.539-1.551 as-deposited, increasing to 1.666 at 800°C. XPS chemical compositions reported for coatings at various pyrolysis temperatures. Solvents used: toluene (bp 110.6°C) and dichloromethane (bp 40°C). The paper is primarily about BN ceramic coatings, not a conventional preceramic polymer characterization paper.

notes: This is a French PhD thesis (Université de Limoges, 2025) on development of Si-(Al)-O-N ceramic fibers from preceramic polymers via melt-spinning. elemental_composition.other_elements: Composition reported as wt% in ceramic residues after pyrolysis. TVS at 1000C: Si 42.5, N 30.8, C 25.6 wt%; HVNG at 1000C: Si 50.3, N 26.9, C 20.6 wt%; ABSE at 1000C: Si 43.9, N 19.4, C 27.7 wt%. At 1500C: TVS Si 43.4, N 29.1, C 26.3 wt%; HVNG Si 50.8, N 26.2, C 20.9 wt%.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH=CH2 (vinyl) units present in TVS and HVNG; Si-CH2-CH2-Si ethylene bridge in ABSE; CSi4 tetrahedral carbon in Si-C-N network observed by 13C MAS-NMR

functional_groups.other: Ethylene bridge (-CH2-CH2-) in ABSE precursor formed by hydrosilylation before ammonolysis

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Free carbon appears above 600C from cracking and reorganization of aliphatic hydrocarbons to aromatic hydrocarbons. Residual H bonded to free carbon eliminated at 800-1200C. Growth and ordering of graphitelike carbon clusters occurs at 1200-1500C. Free carbon content in final ceramics ranges from 24.4 mol% (HVNG) to 35.6 mol% (TVS). Cross-linking of TVS and HVNG performed at 300C for 5h in N2. Pyrolysis carried out in steps of 100C up to 1600C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: TVS and HVNG: hydrosilylation and radical polymerization using dicumylperoxide (DCP) followed by thermal treatment at 300C for 5h in nitrogen. ABSE: hydrosilylation before ammonolysis.

backbone_architecture.description: TVS: each Si connected to other Si atoms via three nitrogen bridges (-CH=CH2Si(NH)1.5 units), theoretical formula SiN1.5C2H4.5. HVNG: two structural units -CH=CH2Si(NH)1.5 and -H(CH3)Si(NH), theoretical formula SiN1.25C1.5H4.75. ABSE: ethylene-bridged structure -CH3(NH)Si-CH2-CH2-Si(NH)CH3, theoretical formula SiNC2H6, prepared by hydrosilylation before ammonolysis.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000C: amorphous Si-C-N-(H) matrix with free-carbon phase (amorphous, no detectable graphitic clusters by HR-TEM). At higher temperatures (>1200C): disordered carbon D and G bands appear in Raman. Thermodynamically stable phases at high Tp: SiC, Si3N4, and free carbon (graphitic). At 1500C amorphous intermediates still present. Residual open porosity ~10-15% in bulk monolithic samples. Carbon cluster size estimated ~1 nm from Raman.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous at 1000C (diffuse SAD ring). At higher temperatures: SiC, Si3N4, and graphitic/turbostratic free carbon expected as stable phases.

notes: Three in-house-synthesized polysilazane precursors studied: TVS (solid), HVNG (liquid, also studied in prior work), and ABSE (solid). Precursors synthesized by reaction of difunctionalized and trifunctionalized chlorosilanes with gaseous NH3. Si-C/Si-N ratios reported: TVS precursor 1/3, at 1000C 0/4, at 1500C 0/4; HVNG precursor 1/2.5, at 1000C 0.8/3.2, at 1500C 0.9/3.1; ABSE precursor 2/2, at 1000C 1.3/2.7. Free carbon content at 1000C: TVS 35.6 mol%, HVNG 24.4 mol%, ABSE 31.0 mol%. Static 13C NMR tensor values reported: TVS sigma_parallel 8.4, sigma_perp 179.4, sigma_iso 122.4 ppm, 100% sp2/0% CSi4; HVNG sigma_parallel 9.2, sigma_perp 183.2, sigma_iso 125.2 ppm, 82% sp2/18% CSi4; ABSE sigma_parallel 3.5, sigma_perp 178.1, sigma_iso 119.9 ppm, 72% sp2/28% CSi4. Microwave conductivity at ~12 GHz used to characterize free-carbon phase. Conductivity increases from ~2.6e-6 (Ohm*cm)^-1 at 400C to ~1.0e-2 (Ohm*cm)^-1 at 1500C for HVNG; TVS-derived ceramic reaches ~2.6e-1 (Ohm*cm)^-1 at 1550C. Porosity range 10-15% noted as midpoint 12.5% in porosity_pct field.
source: Trassl_2002_Characterization_of_the_FreeCarbon_Phase_in_SiCN_Ceramics_Pa

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Repeating units of silicon and nitrogen atoms in backbone; vinyl and methyl substituents implied by poly(methylvinyl)silazane designation

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: argon (route I, PMMA) or nitrogen (route II, ADA)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Main decomposition of pre-cured VL20 occurs between 400 and 800C with ~19% weight loss. Ceramization predominantly 500-800C. Between 800 and 1200C weight loss nearly negligible. PMMA decomposes 220-420C. Measured total mass loss at 1100C: 73.8% (P-SiCN-1, 30/70) and 82.3% (P-SiCN-2, 20/80). Theoretical ceramic yield referenced as 81% for pre-crosslinked VL20. Literature ceramic yield for PUMVS (closely related) is 70-80% at 1100C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (pre-crosslinking at 300C, 1C/min, 8h hold under Ar for route I; curing at 300C, 4h, 2C/min under N2 for route II; hydrosilylation and vinyl group addition)

backbone_architecture.description: Poly(methylvinyl)silazane with Si-N backbone; partially pre-crosslinked prior to processing; described as similar to PUMVS (polyurea(methylvinyl)silazane) but without urea functionality and with fewer low molecular weight silazane components

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous SiCN (or SiOCN with oxygen contamination)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD confirmed X-ray amorphous at 1100C. Literature indicates material is in Si3N4, SiC, and carbon tri-phase equilibrium area and stable up to 1440C. P-SiCN-1: SiO1.61C1.85N0.17; P-SiCN-2: SiO0.78C0.59N0.36; A-SiCN-1: SiO0.03C0.66N0.60; A-SiCN-2: SiO0.10C0.66N0.70; A-SiCN-3: SiO0.10C0.66N0.74. Oxygen contamination significant in PMMA-route samples (up to 33 wt% O in P-SiCN-1).

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Compressive strength range ~1-11 MPa across all samples. P-SiCN-1 (30/70): 11.6 ± 1.1 MPa; P-SiCN-2 (20/80): 5.6 ± 0.7 MPa; A-SiCN-1: 2.89 ± 1.04 MPa; A-SiCN-2: 3.31 ± 1.38 MPa; A-SiCN-3: 1.08 ± 0.56 MPa. Midpoint ~6.6 MPa noted in notes field.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases detected at 1100C; literature indicates nano-SiC and Si3N4 crystallize at higher temperatures

notes: Two processing routes used: (I) PMMA sacrificial microsphere templating with warm pressing, pyrolysis under Ar at 1100C; (II) azodicarbonamide (ADA) physical blowing agent with liquid polysilazane, cured and pyrolyzed under N2 at 1100C. Porosity range 60-80 vol%, mostly interconnected. Strength value of 6.6 MPa in mechanical_properties is the midpoint of the reported range (1-11 MPa). Pre-crosslinking of VL20 done at 300C, 1C/min, 8h under Ar. Route I pyrolysis: 0.5C/min to 450C (hold 3h), then 2C/min to 1100C (hold 2h). Route II pyrolysis: 2C/min to 1100C (hold 2h). ADA decomposes completely in 200-300C range. TGA performed at 2C/min to 1200C under Ar (route I) or N2 (route II). Oxygen contamination in PMMA-route foams attributed to humidity on PMMA beads, moisture sensitivity of precursor, silicone oil mold lubricant, and volatile C component evaporation. Cell sizes 5-15 microns (PMMA route); larger macro-cells for ADA route. Bulk densities: P-SiCN-1: 0.885 g/cm3, P-SiCN-2: 0.520 g/cm3, A-SiCN-1: 0.687 g/cm3, A-SiCN-2: 0.811 g/cm3, A-SiCN-3: 0.830 g/cm3.
source: Vakifahmetoglu_2009_Highly_porous_macro_and_micro_cellular_ceramics_from_a_polys

elemental_composition.other_elements: Zr present in PZrCS variants; weight % compositions at 1650C from EDS: PCS: Si=86.78%, C=13.22%; PZrCS-1: Si=95.24%, C=3.96%, Zr=0.80%; PZrCS-3: Si=93.24%, C=3.92%, Zr=2.84%; PZrCS-5: Si=91.17%, C=3.62%, Zr=5.21%

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si backbone linkage; Si-Zr bonds formed by condensation reaction with Zr(acac)4; small amounts of Si-O-Zr and Si-Zr-C in main chain; Zr(acac)4 ligand C=O and C=C bonds present in PZrCS

functional_groups.other: Acetylacetonate ligands from Zr(acac)4 partially retained in PZrCS; CH2 groups in Si-CH2-Si backbone

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yields (wt%): PCS=37%, PZrCS-1=62%, PZrCS-3=63%, PZrCS-5=76%. Three pyrolysis stages identified: (1) RT to ~650C: evolution of low-boiling oligomers, H2, CH4 from Si-H and C-H bond cleavage; (2) 650-800C: organic-to-inorganic transition, decomposition of organic bonds, evolution of CH4 and H2; (3) above 800C: formation of amorphous covalent ceramic. Organic groups almost completely decompose by ~700C. Heating rate given as 60 C/h = 1 C/min.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical - condensation reaction of PCS SiH bonds with Zr(acac)4 ligands; also thermal curing at 300C under vacuum for 3h

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with THF eluent, polystyrene standards; values given for base PCS only

backbone_architecture.description: PCS has a linear -Si-C-Si-C- backbone with organic side chains including Si-CH3 and Si-H groups. PZrCS incorporates Si-Zr linkages into the chain via condensation, with small amounts of Si-Zr-C and Si-O-Zr in the main chain.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCS at 1650C yields beta-SiC only. PZrCS at 1650C yields beta-SiC + ZrC (non-oxide). At 1300C: beta-SiC + ZrO2. At 1500C: beta-SiC + ZrO2 + ZrC. At 1650C: carbothermal reduction completes, ZrO2 disappears, only beta-SiC and ZrC remain. Free turbostratic carbon also observed in PZrCS-5 ceramic.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: SEM shows increased surface cracking and porosity with higher Zr content in PZrCS ceramics at 1650C; ZrC/SiC phase is described as much denser than SiC alone

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (2theta = 36, 42, 60, 72 deg); ZrC (2theta = 32, 38, 57 deg); ZrO2 (2theta = 30, 50, 60 deg) at intermediate temperatures; amorphous below 900C

notes: Study examines three PZrCS variants (PZrCS-1, PZrCS-3, PZrCS-5) with 1, 3, and 5 wt% Zr(acac)4:PCS ratios respectively. PCS purchased from NaBond, China (density 1.15 g/cc, softening point ~150C). Zr(acac)4 from Sigma Aldrich. Pyrolysis performed at multiple temperatures (500, 900, 1300, 1500, 1650C) with 3h hold at each. Grain size of 50-60 nm for beta-SiC from PCS at 1650C (midpoint 55 nm used). HRTEM confirms ZrC and beta-SiC crystallites with compatible grain boundaries and no stacking faults in PZrCS-5 at 1650C. Carbothermal reduction of ZrO2 to ZrC completed by 1650C. Raman confirms SiC (TO at 796 cm-1, LO at 967 cm-1) and carbon D/G bands; ZrC is Raman inactive.

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: nitrogen (primary sintering at 1500°C); argon (for 2300°C sintering of 55 wt% and 60 wt% SiC samples)
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Curing performed at 200°C for 4 h. Sintering at 1500°C under N2: ramp at 5°C/min to 900°C, hold 1 h, ramp at 5°C/min to 1500°C, hold 1 h, cool at 10°C/min. Sintering at 2300°C under Ar: ramp at 20°C/min, hold 2 h, cool at 100°C/min.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal (curing at 200°C for 4 h)

backbone_architecture.description: SMP-10 is described as a commercially available preceramic polycarbosilane used as a liquid-phase binder and ceramic precursor; detailed backbone architecture not described in text

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Beta-SiC particles (97.5% purity, 45-55 nm particle size) embedded in SiOC matrix derived from SMP-10 pyrolysis. XRD used to identify SiC polytypes at both 1500°C and 2300°C sintering temperatures; phase identification performed using Rigaku MiniFlex software against standard databases.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Compressive strength of printed SiC/SiOC lattice structures ranged from 5.62 ± 1.75 MPa to 9.62 ± 1.10 MPa (midpoint 7.62 MPa); density of sintered composites 2.05-2.34 g/cm³

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC polytypes identified at 1500°C and 2300°C sintering temperatures using XRD; specific polytypes not enumerated in extracted text

notes: SMP-10 polycarbosilane (Starfire Systems Inc., USA) was used as both the liquid phase and ceramic precursor in a solvent-free, binder-free DIW ink system. Beta-SiC particles (NanoAmor, USA, 45-55 nm, 97.5% purity) were incorporated at 0-60 wt% (~31.8 vol% maximum). Inks with ≥50 wt% SiC exhibited shear-thinning behavior suitable for DIW. 60 wt% SiC ink showed best shape retention. Gel point values (G'=G'') at various solid loadings: 50 wt% = 204.76 Pa, 53 wt% = 726.26 Pa, 55 wt% = 1079.52 Pa, 60 wt% = 10523.35 Pa. Maximum solid volume fraction from Heymann model fit: 33.75% (62.09 wt%). Compressive strength range noted in notes field. Sintering at 2300°C under Ar used for 55 wt% and 60 wt% SiC samples to avoid silicon nitride formation.
source: Viswanadha_2025_Solvent_and_binder_free_additive_manufacturing_of_polymer_de

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ceramic phase compositions reported as empirical formulas: SMP-10 at 1700C under Ar: SiC1.28O0.03; Silres H62C at 1700C under Ar: SiC1.36O0.08H0.03. After pyrolysis under NH3: Si25.6C13.0N14.9O5.4H41.0 (atomic %) for SMP-10_NH3; under Ar: Si35.8C47.3N0O5.2H11.7 (atomic %) for SMP-10_Ar; under NH3/Ar: Si36C37N6.8O6.9H13.4 (atomic %) for SMP-10_NH3/Ar

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-vinyl (Si-CH=CH2), Si-phenyl (Silres H62C), Si-O-CH3 (methoxy), Si-O-CH2CH3 (ethoxy), Si-CH2-Si (SMP-10 backbone)

functional_groups.other: Phenyl groups (Silres H62C), methoxy and ethoxy groups (Silres MK, Silres H62C), silyl hydride (RSiH3, R2SiH2, R3SiH in SMP-10)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA conducted on SilresMK, Silres H62C, and SMP-10. Mass spectrometry analysis of evolved gases performed. H2 evolved 400-900C (SMP-10), CH4 300-750C, CO/ethylene 350-650C, vinyl fragments 400-625C. Crosslinking onset: Silres MK ~234C, Silres H62C ~183C (71 J/g), SMP-10 ~184C (182 J/g). Pyrolysis studied at 1000, 1400, and 1700C under argon.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - hydrosilylation and polyaddition (Silres H62C, SMP-10 under inert atmosphere); hydrolysis/condensation (Silres MK under air). Platinum complex catalyst used for SMP-10. UV/photopolymerization used for DLP formulations.

backbone_architecture.description: Silres MK: polysiloxane with methyl, methoxy, and alcohol functions (solid powder, T/D/M units by 29Si NMR: T=45.5%, D=32.4%, M=22.4%). Silres H62C: polysiloxane with methyl, phenyl, vinyl, and silyl functions (liquid). SMP-10: polycarbosilane with vinyl and silyl functions (liquid, Si-CH2-Si backbone). RsiH3 (25%), R2SiH2 (54%), R3SiH (21%) distribution in SMP-10.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC (beta/3C-SiC primary phase), with free carbon
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After pyrolysis at 1700C under Ar: SMP-10 yields 83.5 wt% SiC + 16.5 wt% carbon phase (8.2 wt% free carbon); Silres H62C yields 77.7 wt% SiC + 22.3 wt% carbon phase (17.2 wt% free carbon). XRD identifies 3C-SiC, 2H-SiC, and 4H-SiC polytypes. Amorphous at lower pyrolysis temperatures, crystallization occurring progressively. SiOC system for Silres H62C, SiC system for SMP-10.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: SMP-10 pyrolyzed at 900C N2: E=122 GPa, H=14 GPa; at 1200C Ar: E=108 GPa, H=13 GPa (Poisson ratio 0.17); at 1500C Ar: E=91 GPa, H=11 GPa. Reference sintered SiC: E=440-460 GPa, H=20-32 GPa, strength=550 MPa.

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous to crystalline depending on pyrolysis temperature
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: 3C-SiC (beta-SiC), 2H-SiC, 4H-SiC polytypes identified by XRD as a function of pyrolysis temperature

notes: This is a French PhD thesis on preceramic polymers (polycarbosilane SMP-10 and polysiloxanes Silres H62C and Silres MK) for DLP additive manufacturing of SiC ceramics. Three commercial polymers characterized: SMP-10 (polycarbosilane, liquid, sensitive to oxidation, crosslinks under inert atmosphere via hydrosilylation with Pt catalyst), Silres H62C (polysiloxane, liquid, crosslinks under air or inert atmosphere), Silres MK (polysiloxane, solid powder, crosslinks under air via hydrolysis/condensation). Photopolymerizable formulations developed by blending preceramic polymers with acrylate resins (HDDA, PEG-DA), photoinitiators (Irgacure 819, TPO, etc.), and photoabsorbers (BBOT, Sudan I) for DLP printing at 365 nm. Metallic silicon filler also explored as reactive filler. Pyrolysis up to 1700C under argon studied. TEM analysis performed on ceramics pyrolyzed at 1400 and 1700C. SiC phase compositions reported as empirical formulas at various pyrolysis temperatures. Hardness values range for SiC from literature: 13-27 GPa depending on system and temperature.
source: Vry_2021_Elaboration_de_ceramiques_hautes_performances_par_voie_polym

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si backbone linkage present; oxidation products include Si-O-Si, Si-C-O-Si, and Si-C-O-Si-O-C-Si crosslink structures

functional_groups.other: Si-CH2-Si groups present in backbone

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Oxidation curing in air at 150-250°C results in a maximum weight gain of 16% under normal curing conditions. Weight gain is used as the primary metric for curing degree. Si-H, Si-CH3, and Si-CH2 bonds contribute to the weight gain during oxidation.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal oxidation in air (150-250°C); crosslinking proceeds from fiber surface inward via oxidation of Si-H and C-H bonds

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC (Waters-244); Mn values reported per fiber type: F1=1697, F2=1290, F3=1120 g/mol

backbone_architecture.description: Repeat unit approximated as [CH3SiH-CH2]; prepared by thermal decomposition and rearrangement of polydimethylsilane followed by melt spinning (Yajima route)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PCS fibers are precursors to SiC fibers; oxidation curing introduces Si-O-Si crosslinks as intermediate structures before pyrolysis to SiC

notes: Study focuses on oxidation curing kinetics of PCS fibers (not bulk polymer pyrolysis). Three fiber types used: F1 (Mn=1697, mp=210°C), F2 (Mn=1290, mp=195°C), F3 (Mn=1120, mp=180°C), all measured by GPC Waters-244. First-order kinetic model: dw/dt = k(wm - w) with activation energy E=79.27 kJ/mol and pre-exponential factor A=7.50e6 (F1), 1.80e6 (F2), 3.00e6 (F3). Maximum weight gain wm=16% under normal air curing conditions. IR evidence shows decrease in Si-CH3 (1250 cm-1), Si-CH2-Si (1400 cm-1), and Si-H (2100 cm-1) bands upon oxidation curing.

polymer_name: hyperbranched polycarbosilane with allyl end groups

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2CH2CH2-Si (beta addition product, >98%); Si-CH(CH3)CH2-Si (alpha addition product, <2%); C=C (allyl end groups retained after polymerization)

functional_groups.other: allyl end groups (CH2=CH-CH2-Si); Si-H present in monomer but fully consumed during hydrosilylation polymerization

backbone_architecture.description: Synthesized via hydrosilylation of methyldiallylsilane using Karstedt catalyst; degree of branching (DB) = 0.58; average number of branches (ANB) = 0.42; Mark-Houwink exponent a = 0.33 indicating compact/sphere-like architecture; dendritic (Si-D), linear (Si-L), and terminal (Si-T) units in ratio 1:1.39:0.66; predominantly beta addition product (>98%)

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Paper mentions potential use as ceramic precursor but does not report pyrolysis to ceramic phase

notes: This paper focuses on UV curing kinetics of hyperbranched polycarbosilane blended with tripropylene glycol diacrylate (TPGDA) reactive diluent, studied by differential scanning photocalorimetry (DPC). Effects of TPGDA concentration (20, 30, 40 wt%), light intensity (19.4-99.8 mW/cm2), atmosphere (N2 vs air), and temperature (0-60 degrees C) on curing behavior were investigated. Oxygen inhibition was observed in air atmosphere. Polymerization kinetics modeled with autocatalytic model; activation energy Ea ~3.18 kJ/mol (N2) and ~3.22 kJ/mol (air). The polymer is described as a potential ceramic precursor but no pyrolysis or ceramic characterization data are reported in the extracted text. Monomer precursor methyldiallylsilane elemental analysis: C 66.62%, H 11.14% (calc. C 66.67%, H 11.11%) for C7H14Si.

polymer_name: PCSN (ethynylaniline-terminated polysilazane); variants: PCSN-1, PCSN-2, PCSN-3, PCSN-4

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Terminal alkyne C≡C (2156 cm-1, overlapping with Si-H), C≡C-H (3285 cm-1), aromatic C-H (3039 cm-1) and C=C (1600 cm-1), Ph-N N-H (3392 cm-1); Si-H confirmed by 29Si NMR at -62.6 ppm (H-Si-CH3); Si-O bond introduced by hydrolysis of MeSiHCl2 with trace water

functional_groups.other: Terminal ethynyl groups (C≡C-H) introduced via p-aminophenylacetylene (APA); aromatic/phenyl rings from p-phenylenediamine and APA

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA conducted under N2 from room temperature to 1000°C at 10°C/min. Residual mass at 900°C: PCSN-1=70.6%, PCSN-2=77.8%, PCSN-3=84.4%, PCSN-4=82.4%. T_d5 values: PCSN-1=302°C, PCSN-2=341°C, PCSN-3=564°C, PCSN-4=487°C. Ceramic conversion at 1450°C for 6h: PCSN-1=55.2%, PCSN-2=63.1%, PCSN-3=78.4%, PCSN-4=69.6%. PCSN-3 showed best thermal stability. Sintering schedule: 800°C/2h → 1000°C/2h → 1200°C/2h → 1450°C/6h at 20°C/min under argon.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal; crosslinking via hydrosilylation and Diels-Alder reactions of terminal ethynyl groups and Si-H groups; cure schedule: 160°C/2h → 180°C/2h → 200°C/2h → 220°C/3h → 240°C/3h → 260°C/4h → 270°C/3h → 280°C/3h → 300°C/2h

backbone_architecture.description: Linear polysilazane backbone synthesized from ammonolysis/condensation of MeSiHCl2 with p-phenylenediamine, with terminal ethynyl groups introduced via APA end-capping; Si-N backbone with pendant methyl and hydride groups on Si; benzene rings incorporated from both p-phenylenediamine and APA; structure confirmed by FTIR, 1H, 13C, and 29Si NMR

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: After sintering at 1450°C under argon, PCSN-3 thermoset converted to black solids composed of β-silicon carbide (β-SiC), β-silicon nitride, α-SiC, and free carbon; phases identified by XRD

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: β-SiC, α-SiC, β-Si3N4, free carbon (identified after sintering at 1450°C under argon)

notes: Four PCSN variants synthesized with varying n(N):n(Si) molar ratios: PCSN-1 (1:1.3), PCSN-2 (1:1.5), PCSN-3 (1:1.8), PCSN-4 (1:2). Synthesis yields: 90.04%, 91.23%, 88.71%, 87.29% respectively. All resins are yellow viscous liquids. PCSN-4 has lowest curing temperature (237.1°C) and highest crosslinking enthalpy (863.0 J/g) due to highest terminal ethynyl content. PCSN-3 showed best overall thermal stability (T_d5=564°C, residual mass at 900°C=84.4%) and highest ceramic yield at 1450°C (78.4%). Gel temperatures from rheology: PCSN-1=250°C, PCSN-2=230°C, PCSN-3=220°C, PCSN-4=201°C. O content not theoretically predicted (NA) but detected experimentally due to hydrolysis of MeSiHCl2. Possible chlorine contamination from Et3N·HCl noted. Molecular weight and PDI ranges span all four samples; midpoint values used in molecular_weight fields. DSC peak temperatures: PCSN-1=264.8°C, PCSN-2=251.5°C, PCSN-3=249.6°C, PCSN-4=237.1°C.

notes: Paper focuses on improving PCS yield by recycling liquid by-products (LBP). PCS synthesized via atmospheric-pressure thermal rearrangement of polydimethylsilane (PDMS) through liquid polysilane (LPS) intermediate. LPS pyrolysis at 400°C; LPS thermal rearrangement/polycondensation at 450°C for 10 h in N2 atmosphere; vacuum distillation at 300°C for 10 min to separate PCS from LBP. Target PCS molecular weight range cited as 1800-2100 g/mol with softening point ~210°C for industrial application. PCS-1 (no recycling) yield: 51.3%; PCS yield improved to 62.8% after repeated LBP recycling (up to 5 rounds). Softening point range for PCS samples: 203-267°C. LBP identified as low-molecular-weight PCS (Mn ~393 g/mol, Mw ~669 g/mol, PDI 1.70) with higher Si-H content and lower Si-CH2-Si content than standard PCS. 29Si NMR identifies SiC3H (delta ~-17.2 ppm) and SiC4 (delta ~0 ppm) structural units. Polycondensation reactions consume Si-H bonds to form Si-CH2-Si, converting low-MW to high-MW components. Molecular weight and structure of PCS not significantly altered by LBP recycling.

notes: This paper is primarily about using poly(resorcinol borate) (PRB) as a preceramic/polymeric precursor for low-temperature synthesis of B4C ceramic, not a silicon-based preceramic polymer. PRB is synthesized from resorcinol and H3BO3 (1:1 molar ratio) using FeCl3 catalyst in NMP/cyclohexane/xylene solvent system. The key innovation is the use of an aromatic precursor (high char yield, 69% at 800°C in N2) enabling B4C synthesis at 600°C in air, much lower than conventional carbothermic reduction (>1750°C). Optimal conditions: 600°C, 8h hold in air, yielding B4C with only 0.82 wt% free carbon. XPS of pyrolysis products shows C-B bond at 283.4 eV, sp2 C-C at 284.65 eV; B1s at 189.51 eV (B4C), 190.18 eV (B-O), 192.18 eV (B-O-B). Table I in paper reports elemental compositions (C, B, O wt%) of washed pyrolysis products at 600°C for varying hold times, not of the PRB polymer itself. C/B2O3 molar ratio at 600°C pyrolysis ~3.42, close to stoichiometric 3.5.

notes: This is a review paper covering multiple PSZ and PCSZ precursors used in additive manufacturing of Si3N4/SiCN ceramics. Viscosity of PSZ precursors ranges from ~30 mPa·s (PBSZ) to 12.9 Pa·s (PSZ slurry with 50 wt% Si3N4 particles); IOTA 9108 viscosity 10-30 mPa·s. Ceramic yield not quantified for most systems. Linear shrinkage <8% reported for PSZ/h-BN DIW ink after pyrolysis. mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Hardness and modulus at 600C thermal conversion: 9.7 GPa and 80.9 GPa respectively. At 600C vs TEOS comparison: PHPS hardness 9.06 GPa, modulus 78.2 GPa, density 2.12 g/cm3. Ammonia catalytic conversion at room temperature: hardness 3 GPa, modulus 60 GPa. APTES catalytic conversion (80C, 90% RH, 10 min): hardness 3.09 GPa, modulus 30.06 GPa, pencil hardness 9H. VUV + moisture cooperative conversion: hardness 4.73 GPa, modulus 50.3 GPa. PHPS film initial stress ~9.8 MPa (vs TEOS ~170 MPa). PHPS crack-free thickness >1000 nm vs TEOS ~500 nm.

notes: PHPS is a fully inorganic polysilazane with no carbon substituents (distinguishing it from organopolysilazanes). Synthesis route: ammonolysis of dichlorosilane (SiH2Cl2) with pyridine complexation in polar solvents (diethyl ether, dichloromethane), based on Seyferth 1983 method. Converts to amorphous silica rather than SiCN ceramic. Multiple conversion routes studied: (1) thermal 300-600C; (2) ammonia aqueous atmosphere room temperature catalytic, 4h, refractive index 1.41, visible light transmittance >95%; (3) APTES (5 wt%) catalytic at 80C/90% RH, 10 min, >95% Si-H and 84% Si-N conversion, volume shrinkage only 0.86% vs 20-35% for thermal, density ~1.9 g/cm3, surface roughness 0.293 nm; (4) VUV 172 nm irradiation; (5) VUV 254 nm (with 185 nm line) effective conversion thickness ~160 nm; (6) VUV + moisture cooperative strategy at 80C/90% RH 4h post-treatment, refractive index ~1.46, shrinkage ~7.0%. ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations developed for Si/N/H and Si/N/O/H systems to study conversion mechanisms. Nano-scale silicon clusters predicted by simulation and confirmed by photoluminescence and Raman spectroscopy under VUV irradiation. Application as gate dielectric in thin-film transistors: IZO TFT at 150C anneal mobility 17.3 cm2/V/s; flexible device on 100 μm bendable glass hole mobility 1.02 cm2/V/s with 94% retention at bending radius 1.937 cm.
