mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Measurements on crude 30 micrometer diameter BN fibers; tensile strength 0.18 GPa (180 MPa), elastic modulus 14 GPa

notes: This paper concerns a boron nitride preceramic polymer, not a silicon-based preceramic polymer. Polymer backbone is poly(borazinyl) (B-N based), not Si-containing. Synthesis: 2.55 g polyborazylene reacted with dipentylamine in glyme at 75°C for 192 h in vacuo; 91% yield (4.58 g). Fiber diameter: 30-40 micrometers (polymer fibers), 30 micrometers (ceramic fibers). Fiber takeup rate: 30 m/min. Melt-spinning temperature: 75-95°C. The dipentylamine modification lowers melting temperature and retards crosslinking relative to parent polyborazylene, enabling melt-spinning. No silicon, carbon, or hydrogen atomic percentages reported numerically.
source: Wideman_1996_Dipentylamine_Modified_Polyborazylene_A_New_Melt_Spinnable_P

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Vinyl group (-CH=CH2) attached to Si; Si-N-Si backbone described as primary chain

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed from 30 to 900 degrees C at 10 degrees C/min in air atmosphere on approximately 10 mg samples; activation energies calculated for selected specimens ranging from 6.72 to 20.18 kJ/mol

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical - dicumyl peroxide used as initiator at 1 wt% to aid crosslinking; thermal curing at 130, 160, or 190 degrees C

backbone_architecture.description: Primary chain consisting of Si-N-Si backbone with side groups -H, -CH3, and -CH=CH2 attached to Si and N atoms

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: YSZ/polysilazane composite coating on CFRP; XRD performed at 5-50 degrees range; elemental composition by SEM-EDX shows C, N, O, Si, P in the coated specimens

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Adhesion strength measured by pull-off test (ASTM D4541); values range from 0.525 to 0.69 MPa for SB specimens; literature standard 0.3-1.5 MPa

notes: This paper focuses on YSZ/polysilazane thermal barrier coatings (TBC) on CFRP substrates. Polysilazane (Durazane 1800) is used as a binder matrix rather than being pyrolyzed to a ceramic independently. Curing temperatures studied: 130, 160, 190 degrees C; curing times: 60, 120, 180 min. Particle sizes of YSZ: 140 mesh (105 micron), 200 mesh (74 micron), 270 mesh (53 micron). YSZ/polysilazane ratios: 70/30, 60/40, 50/50. Thermal conductivity values range from 0.16 to 0.29 W/mK. Elemental compositions reported are for the composite coating (YSZ+polysilazane), not pure polysilazane. Dicumyl peroxide at 1 wt% used as crosslinking initiator. Coating thickness of YSZ/polysilazane layer: 358.4 microns. XRD used Philips X'Pert with Cu Ka radiation at 40 kV, 30 mA. FTIR analyzed at 400-4000 cm-1.
source: Widyastuti_2024_A_study_on_thermal_behaviour_of_thermal_barrier_coating_inve

elemental_composition.other_elements: Ceramic elemental compositions (wt% atomic) reported per system: VADB: Si=27.7, B=10.7, N=35.9, C=24.6, O=0.8 -> SiBN2.6C2; TADB-VMS: Si=33.3, B=6.4, N=35.6, C=23.7, O=0.85 -> Si2BN4.3C3.3; TADB-VTS: Si=36.7, B=7.3, N=37.5, C=18.4, O=0.8 -> Si2BN4C2.3; MADB-VMS: Si=39.7, B=7.8, N=27.1, C=24.6, O=0.7 -> Si2BN2.7C2.9; MADB-VTS: Si=34.2, B=6.5, N=34.5, C=23.8, O=0.9 -> Si2BN4.1C3.3

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds present; N-CH3 bridges connecting Si and B building blocks; vinyl groups attached to silicon (Si-CH=CH2); B-N3 units; SiN4 units in ceramic network

functional_groups.other: N-methylamine terminal groups (-NH(CH3)); N(CH3) bridges between Si and B units; borazine-type B-N rings may survive pyrolysis

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Two-step decomposition observed: first step 100-300C removes residual terminal methylamine causing further crosslinking; second step 400-800C decomposes organic side groups evolving amines, methane and volatiles. Ceramic yields: VADB=52%, TADB-VMS=54%, TADB-VTS=54%, MADB-VTS=50%, MADB-VMS=36%. High-temperature TGA (heating rate 10 C/min, helium flow) performed up to 1900C. Initial 2.5% mass loss temperatures: VADB=1750C, TADB-VMS=1801C, TADB-VTS=1733C, MADB-VMS=1779C, MADB-VTS=1718C. Mass loss at 1900C: VADB=12.5%, TADB-VMS=11.5%, TADB-VTS=29.3%, MADB-VMS=9.4%, MADB-VTS=23.1%. Pyrolysis first conducted in quartz tubes to 900C, then further heat treatment at 1400C for 180 min under argon flow.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: radical - dicumyl peroxide (2 wt%) used as radical initiator; curing at 130C for 75 min or at 160C for 5-15 min; pre-crosslinking also occurs via thermal polycondensation (elimination of methylamine) up to 200C under argon

backbone_architecture.description: VADB-derived polymer: oligomeric network with N(CH3) bridges connecting Si and B building blocks, vinyl groups on Si, N(H) bridges present, terminated by -NH(CH3). VMS-derived: chain-like Si-N backbone with methyl and vinyl substituents, terminated by -NH(CH3). VTS-derived: three-fold connected at Si via methyl-nitrogen bridges giving higher crosslink degree, vinyl on Si, terminated by -NH(CH3). Copolymers formed by mixing borosilazane and vinylsilazane oligomers with heat treatment to 200C causing polycondensation crosslinking.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: All ceramics remain amorphous (SiN4 and BN3 units with free carbon embedded via nitrogen bridges). Crystallization resistance at least up to 1556C confirmed. Samples annealed at 1565C and 1660C for 180 min to determine crystallization onset. 29Si MAS-NMR signals broadened due to amorphous network distortion. Densities ~2 g/cm3 by helium pycnometry.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases identified; XRD patterns recorded on STOE Stadi-P diffractometer (Cu Ka1, Debye-Scherrer geometry); ceramics stable against crystallization up to at least 1556C

notes: Paper describes SiBNC preceramic polyborosilazane systems designed for radical curing via vinyl functionalization. Five polymer systems studied: single-source VADB and four copolymers (TADB-VMS, TADB-VTS, MADB-VMS, MADB-VTS) in 1:1 ratio. Boron is a key element in all systems (SiBNC ceramics). Ceramic densities: VADB=1.95, TADB-VMS=1.94, TADB-VTS=2.00, MADB-VMS=2.03, MADB-VTS=2.00 g/cm3. Best high-temperature stability achieved with TADB-VMS copolymer (not single-source VADB). TGA heating rate for standard pyrolysis: 5 C/min; for TGA analysis: 10 C/min. Oxygen contamination kept below 1 wt% despite use of oxygen-containing radical initiator. Ceramic system belongs to SiBNC quaternary system known for superior high-temperature properties vs SiC and Si3N4. 1H NMR used for polymer characterization (300 MHz); 29Si MAS-NMR used for ceramic characterization (79.496 MHz, 8 kHz spinning, 4 mm ZrO2 rotors). Elemental analysis: N/O by Leco TC438, C by Leco C-200, B/Si by ICP-OES after HF digestion.
source: Wilfert_2011_Curing_preceramic_SiBNC_polymers_infusible_by_radical_polyme

elemental_composition.other_elements: Polymer elemental composition not reported as atomic percent; ceramic elemental compositions reported: DMTA-derived ceramic: Si 30.74, B 11.93, N 36.64, C 18.89, O 0.81 (atomic%); One-pot ceramic: Si 31.28, B 11.55, N 35.25, C 20.84, O 1.15 (atomic%)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds present (FTIR bands at 1326 and 687 cm-1); N-CH3 bridging units; Si-N-B linkages; four-fold bonded Si and three-fold bonded B bridged by N(CH3) units

functional_groups.other: N-methyl (N-CH3) groups; methylamino groups

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Most decomposition occurs below 700C. DMTA polymer ceramic yield 60.3%, one-pot polymer ceramic yield 73.2%. Dwell at 350C and 900C (180 min each) then further heat treatment to 1400C (180 min). DMTA mass loss to 700C: 35.0%, one-pot: 23.4%; additional mass loss to 1400C: 4.7% (DMTA) and 3.4% (one-pot).

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

backbone_architecture.description: Random network of four-fold bonded Si and three-fold bonded B bridged by N(CH3) units; one-pot synthesis yields random arrangement of B and Si via condensation of tris(methylamino)borane and tetrakis(methylamino)silane

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Amorphous up to at least 1556C for 3h. At 1660C annealing, SiC reflections appear. During TGA to 1900C, SiC with stacking disorder and turbostratic BN form. DMTA ceramic: SiBN2.4C1.4; one-pot ceramic: SiBN2.4C1.6. Densities: one-pot 1.80 g/cm3, DMTA 1.82 g/cm3.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Superior creep resistance compared to commercial SiC fibers (measured by bend stress relaxation) mentioned for SiBNC ceramics generally; no specific values given for these polymers

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous up to 1556C; SiC (with stacking disorder) and turbostratic BN appear after annealing at 1660C or TGA to 1900C

notes: Two polymers compared: (1) DMTA-derived polyborosilazane from single-source precursor dichloroboryl methyl trichlorosilyl amine (DMTA), and (2) one-pot synthesized analog from SiCl4, BCl3, and methylamine. Ceramic yield range: 60.3% (DMTA) to 73.2% (one-pot); midpoint 66.75% used for ceramic_yield_pct. High temperature stability (2.5% mass loss onset): DMTA 1716C, one-pot 1785C. 29Si MAS NMR shows SiN4 tetrahedral units in both ceramics. Oxidation stability up to 1500C noted due to SiO2/BN double layer formation. FTIR bands confirm N-H, CH3, B-N, and Si-N structural features in both polymers.
source: Wilfert_2012_One_pot_synthesis_of_DMTA_analogous_SiBNC_preceramic_polymer

polymer_name: HPD (polysiloxane polyHIPE); HPD1, HPD3, HPD5, HPD10, HPD20, HPD30, HPD40 (HNT-reinforced nanocomposites)

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-CH2-Si (~1138 cm-1) formed via hydrosilylation crosslinking of Si-H and vinyl (Si-CH=CH2) groups; Si-vinyl from 1,3-divinyltetramethyldisiloxane crosslinker

functional_groups.other: Dimethylsiloxane-ethylene oxide block copolymer surfactant (DBE 224) present as emulsifier

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed from 30 to 1000 C at 10 K/min under dynamic He flow (50 cm3/min). Residual mass for HPD (no HNTs): 38.1%. HNT incorporation significantly improved ceramic yield: HPD1=57.0%, HPD3=61.5%, HPD5=62.5%, HPD10=65.9%, HPD20=63.8%, HPD30=65.6%, HPD40=64.8%. Degradation onset (T5%) increased from 256 C (HPD) to 308 C (HPD10, HPD20, HPD30). Multiple decomposition steps observed. HPD shows main mass losses at ~269 C (28.7%), ~422 C (28.5%), ~548 C (4.7%). HNT alone shows 20.2% total mass loss with residual 79.8%.

crosslink_density.value: Semi-quantitative ratio: I(Si-CH2-CH2-Si, ~1138 cm-1) / I(Si-CH3, ~1260 cm-1); crosslink density unaffected up to 10 wt% HNTs, reduced at higher loadings due to steric constraints
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic (platinum-catalyzed hydrosilylation, Karstedt's catalyst, 80 C, 24 h)

backbone_architecture.description: Macroporous polyHIPE network formed by HIPE templating with 82 vol% internal aqueous phase. Continuous oil phase (18 vol%) composed of PMHS crosslinked with 1,3-divinyltetramethyldisiloxane via hydrosilylation. Interconnected open-cell macroporous structure with voids in micrometer range. HNTs embedded in pore walls.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Porous polysiloxane network with embedded halloysite nanotubes (Al2Si2O5(OH)4, tubular morphology, 30-70 nm diameter, 1-3 um length). SEM confirmed interconnected macroporous polyHIPE morphology up to HPD20; HPD30 and HPD40 showed reduced pore interconnectivity. BET surface area 7.4-12.5 m2/g.

notes: Materials are porous polysiloxane (poly(methylhydrosiloxane)-based) polyHIPE nanocomposites reinforced with halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) at loadings of 0-40 wt%. Synthesis via one-step emulsion-templated hydrosilylation: PMHS (trimethylsilyl-terminated, viscosity 35-45 cSt) + 1,3-divinyltetramethyldisiloxane crosslinker at 1:1 molar ratio Si-H:vinyl, Karstedt's catalyst, DBE 224 surfactant, chlorobenzene porogen, 0.02 M NaCl aqueous phase. Cured at 80 C for 24 h. TG-FTIR and HT-FTIR used to study degradation pathways. HPD10 showed optimal balance of thermal improvement and network integrity. Ceramic yield values reported are residual mass at 1000 C in He. The paper is focused on thermal behavior and degradation, not on PDC ceramic conversion per se, though keywords include polymer-derived ceramics.
source: WojcikBania_2026_Porous_polysiloxane_HNT_polyHIPE_nanocomposites_influence_of

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental analysis (weight%) for poly(silapropylene): Si 43.8%, C 41.38%, H 9.04% (calculated: Si 48.28%, C 40.64%, H 9.04%); Cl present in chloro precursor polymer

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si backbone linkage (carbosilane); Si-Cl present in precursor polymer poly[(methylchlorosilylene)methylene]

functional_groups.other: Si-Cl groups present in intermediate chloro polymer; reduced to Si-H by LiAlH4

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Polymer is thermally stable up to 400 °C, then rapid decomposition between 400-500 °C. Without pre-crosslinking step: ceramic yield ~10-20% depending on MW. With pre-crosslinking at 400 °C under nitrogen for 30 min then heating to 1200 °C: 66% ceramic yield. Further heating at 1600 °C for 4 h yielded beta-SiC. Lower MW polymer (Mn=6000) gave 10% yield; higher MW (Mn=35000) gave 20% yield without crosslinking step.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - heating at 400 °C under nitrogen for 30 min; yields hard rubbery crosslinked polymer

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with polystyrene standards, toluene eluent, Waters 600 system with mu-Styragel columns

backbone_architecture.description: High molecular weight linear polycarbosilane with Si-CH2-Si backbone repeat units; atactic configuration with mixed isotactic and syndiotactic sequences; no observable branching or head-to-head sequences detected by NMR

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Black pyrolysis product heated at 1600 °C for 4 h yielded broad XRD pattern indicative of beta-SiC

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Pre-crosslinked polymer described as 'hard rubbery' after thermal treatment at 400 °C

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (broad pattern after 1600 °C, 4 h treatment)

notes: Two polymers described: (1) poly[(methylchlorosilylene)methylene] - the chloro intermediate, and (2) poly(silapropylene) [-(CH3)SiHCH2-]n - obtained by LiAlH4 reduction. Molecular weights reported for two batches of poly(silapropylene): first batch (0.016 g catalyst) Mn=6000, Mw=40000, bimodal distribution; second batch (0.008 g catalyst) Mn=35000, Mw=292750. The MW values reported above reflect the higher MW batch. Poly[(dimethylsilylene)methylene] reference polymer: Mn=260000, PDI=1.45, negligible ceramic yield. Pyrolysis atmosphere for TGA studies was nitrogen at 10 °C/min. Pre-crosslinking heat treatment: 120-400 °C over 30 min, held at 400 °C for 5 min under nitrogen. Prepared at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute via ring-opening polymerization of 1,3-dichloro-1,3-dimethyl-1,3-disilacyclobutane using chloroplatinic acid catalyst.
source: Wu_1989_Preparation_of_a_polymeric_precursor_to_silicon_carbide_via

polymer_name: ZrC-SiC ceramic precursor (PVB/dimethyl vinyl chlorosilane/n-propyl zirconate sol-gel network)

elemental_composition.other_elements: Zr present; Zr/Si molar ratio varied across samples ZS1, ZS3, ZS5, ZS7, ZS9; C, Si, Zr identified as most abundant elements by EDS

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si (1138 cm-1), Si-O-Zr (1024 cm-1), C-Si (781 cm-1), C=C (3077 cm-1), C-H (3000 cm-1), C=O (1680 cm-1), Zr-O-Zr, Zr-C, Zr-O-C bonds also identified by XPS

functional_groups.other: Hydroxyl (-OH) from PVB side chains participates in crosslinking; C=O from PVB backbone; PVB (polyvinyl butyral) serves as molecular framework

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed on ZS3 precursor in Ar at 10 C/min from RT to 1400 C. Three weight-loss stages: (1) RT to 400 C: ~4.38 wt% loss due to volatile solvents and small molecules; (2) 400 to 1200 C: ~17.80 wt% loss due to volatilization of CH4 and H2; (3) 1200 to 1400 C: ~16.14 wt% loss with evolution of CO2 and CO during carbothermic reduction. SiC and ZrC phases generated during third stage. Heating rates for pyrolysis: RT to 1000 C at 5 C/min, 1000 C to target at 3 C/min, cooling at 3 C/min. Ceramic yield reported higher than previously reported values due to PVB addition.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal and chemical (sol-gel crosslinking: Si-O-C bonds formed in first stage at 80 C reflux; Si-O-Zr and Zr-O-Zr bonds formed in second stage at 60 C for 30 h; final crosslinking in oven at 300 C)

molecular_weight.measurement_method: PVB starting material molecular weight: 170,000-250,000 g/mol (midpoint ~210,000); no GPC or MALDI reported for precursor polymer

backbone_architecture.description: Macromolecular network with PVB as main chain; silane molecules (dimethyl vinyl chlorosilane) interlinked via -OH moieties in PVB side chains forming Si-O-C bonds; Zr atoms crosslinked with Si via Si-O-Zr and Zr-O-Zr chains at corresponding Zr/Si molar ratios

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1200-1300 C: amorphous ceramics with partial ZrSiO4 crystalline phase. At 1400 C: SiC and ZrC phases appear. At 1600 C: complete conversion to ZrC and SiC; ZrC powder uniformly covers surface of SiC ceramics; high-crystallinity graphite carbon covers ZrC powder (core-shell structure). Traces of ZrOxCy and ZrO2 detected by XPS. Excess free carbon present.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: ZrC ceramics referenced as having hardness of 27 GPa (literature value, not measured in this study); carbothermic reduction process noted to cause decline in mechanical properties

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC (ICDD 01-073-1665) at 2theta = 35.6, 41.4, 60.0, 71.8, 75.4 degrees; ZrC (ICDD 03065-8834) at 2theta = 33.0, 38.3, 55.3, 65.9, 69.3 degrees; ZrSiO4 (ICDD 01-071-0991) intermediate phase at lower temperatures; free graphitic carbon by Raman (D band 1325-1350 cm-1, G band 1590-1600 cm-1)

notes: Grain sizes calculated by Scherrer equation: SiC ~50 nm, ZrC ~10 nm. Raman I(D)/I(G) ratio increases from 1.112 at 1200 C to 1.266 at 1600 C; La decreases from 3.957 to 3.476 nm indicating increasing graphitic order with temperature. Five precursor compositions prepared: ZS1, ZS3, ZS5, ZS7, ZS9 with varying Zr/Si molar ratios. Ethanol used as solvent (environmentally friendly). PVB molecular weight range 170,000-250,000 g/mol noted for starting material. Pyrolysis heating rates: RT-1000 C at 5 C/min; 1000 C to target at 3 C/min; cooling at 3 C/min; hold time 150 min. TGA heating rate 10 C/min.
source: Wu_2023_Polymer_precursor_synthesis_of_novel_ZrCSiC_ultrahigh_temper

elemental_composition.other_elements: Base PSZ elemental composition (wt%): Si 41.3, C 27.3, N 22.7, H 8.3, O 0.4; empirical formula [Si1.0C1.5N1.1H5.5]n. Boron-modified variants (PSZB_X) have variable B content targeting Si:B molar ratios of 2.5 to 30.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-N bonds formed via dehydrocoupling reactions; B-C bonds formed via hydroboration of vinyl groups; vinyl (Si-CH=CH2) groups present in base PSZ

functional_groups.other: Borane dimethylsulfide (BDMS) adduct used as boron source; B-N and B-C functional linkages introduced after hydroboration and dehydrocoupling

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Ceramic yields range from ca. 68% (SiBCN30_10, low boron) to ca. 82.5% (SiBCN2.5_10, high boron); increasing boron content significantly enhanced ceramic yield. High-temperature TGA performed up to 1800°C at 5°C/min in nitrogen to assess thermal stability of as-pyrolysed ceramics. Annealing treatments at 1400, 1600, and 1800°C (5°C/min, 2h dwell) performed in nitrogen in a graphite furnace.

crosslink_density.value: Qualitative; controlled via Si:B molar ratio (2.5 to 30); higher boron content increases crosslinking degree
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical - hydroboration of vinyl groups and dehydrocoupling of BH with NH groups using borane dimethylsulfide (BDMS)

backbone_architecture.description: Base PSZ is a poly(vinylmethyl-co-methyl)silazane with Si-N backbone bearing vinyl, methyl, and Si-H groups. Boron modification via hydroboration and dehydrocoupling introduces B-C and B-N crosslinks, converting the linear/branched polysilazane into a more crosslinked network. Viscosity and solubility tunable by boron content.

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiCN / SiBCN - amorphous at 1000°C; crystallizes to β-SiC, α/β-Si3N4, B(C)N (turbostratic BN-rich), and free carbon upon annealing
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000°C: X-ray amorphous; high Si:B ratio samples dominated by amorphous Si3N4 and disordered free carbon; low Si:B ratio samples show nucleation of β-SiC (3C) and turbostratic B(C)N phase. At 1800°C: low boron → major SiC phase via carbothermal reaction of Si3N4; high boron → stable SiC + Si3N4 + BN-rich B(C)N phase. Phase compositions (wt%) at 1000°C from Table 2: SiBCN15_10: SiC 14.5, Si3N4 68.5, C 15.2, BN 1.8; SiBCN5_10: SiC 16.0, Si3N4 55.9, C 16.2, BN 11.9; SiBCN2.5_10: SiC 27.4, Si3N4 38.3, C 15.8, BN 18.8.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: At 1000°C: X-ray amorphous with diffuse peaks; trace β-SiC (3C) nucleation in low Si:B ratio samples; B(C)N (002) peak in low Si:B samples. At 1800°C: β-SiC, β-Si3N4, B(C)N phase identified. β-SiC (220) and β-Si3N4 (200) crystallite sizes reported for 1800°C samples.

notes: Crystallite sizes (Scherrer, from XRD at 1800°C): β-SiC D_SiC: SiBCN30_18=43.9nm, SiBCN15_18=43.9nm, SiBCN5_18=29.7nm, SiBCN3.75_18=28nm, SiBCN2.5_18=15.8nm; β-Si3N4 D_Si3N4: SiBCN5_18=19.9nm, SiBCN3.75_18=22.1nm, SiBCN2.5_18=45.4nm (not detected in SiBCN30_18 and SiBCN15_18). Ceramic yield range 68–82.5%; midpoint ~75.25% used above. Boron content in ceramics at 1000°C: SiBCN15_10=0.8wt%B, SiBCN5_10=5.0wt%B, SiBCN2.5_10=9.0wt%B. Samples marked with asterisk (*) at 1800°C show very low N content indicating near-complete N loss via carbothermal reaction. NMR methods: solid-state 11B (700MHz) and 29Si (300MHz) MAS NMR used to characterize bonding. Raman D and G bands observed at ~1355 and ~1590 cm-1 indicating disordered sp2 carbon in all samples. Paper focuses primarily on ceramic behavior post-pyrolysis; polymer molecular weight data not reported in this text.
source: Wynn_2021_Tuning_of_the_high_temperature_behaviour_of_SiCN_ceramics_vi

elemental_composition.other_elements: Mo present; elemental compositions given in wt% for derived ceramics: PMoCS-8wt% ceramic: Si 44.34 wt%, C 39.36 wt%, O 0.86 wt%, Mo not quantified (NA); experimental formula SiC2.073HmO0.034Mon

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-Mo bonds present (confirmed by XPS); Si-O-Mo bonds also present as minor component; Si-CH2-Si moieties present (Kumada rearrangement product); SiC4 and SiC3H units identified by 29Si NMR

functional_groups.other: Si-CH2-Si (carbosilane bridge units); Mo-Cl eliminated during synthesis via HCl elimination with Si-H

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed up to 1200C in N2 flow at 40 mL/min with heating rate 10C/min. Ceramic yield of PMoCS prepared with 10 wt% MoCl5 is approximately 78.5% at 1200C. XRD shows ceramics pyrolyzed at 800-1000C are amorphous; beta-SiC and beta-MoSi2 crystals observed at 1200 and 1400C respectively; conversion from beta-MoSi2 to alpha-MoSi2 nearly complete at 1600C.

crosslink_density.value: PMoCS-460 is partially crosslinked (qualitative observation only)
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC (Waters-1515, THF solvent, polystyrene standard)

backbone_architecture.description: Based on polysilacarbosilane (PSCS) with basic structure -(MeHSiCH2)x(SiMe2)(1-x)-; Mo introduced via HCl elimination between Si-H and Mo-Cl; MoCl5 acts as branching/linking agent connecting up to 5 PCS chains; 29Si NMR shows SiC4 and SiC3H units; lower degree of linearity than PCS indicated by SiC3H/SiC4 ratios

microstructural.ceramic_phase: SiC + MoSi2 (beta-SiC and beta-MoSi2 at 1200-1400C; alpha-MoSi2 at 1600C)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Ceramics pyrolyzed at 800-1000C are amorphous. beta-SiC and beta-MoSi2 appear at 1200C and 1400C respectively. Conversion from beta-MoSi2 to alpha-MoSi2 nearly complete at 1600C. SiC(Mo) ceramic composition: SiC2.073HmO0.034Mon (PMoCS-8wt% derived).

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: PMoCS is melt spinnable into flexible and uniform green fibers with diameters approximately 12.2-13.4 micrometers

conformation_crystallinity.crystallinity_state: amorphous at 800-1000C; crystalline at 1200C and above
conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (at 1200C and 1400C); beta-MoSi2 (at 1200C and 1400C); alpha-MoSi2 (at 1600C)

notes: PMoCS synthesized from PSCS and MoCl5 in argon atmosphere via HCl elimination and Kumada rearrangement. Reaction is temperature-dependent; optimal synthesis at 440C for 10h. Molecular weight data in JSON reflects PMoCS-8wt% at 440C synthesis (Mn=2016, Mw=12930). Grain sizes of beta-SiC for different MoCl5 loadings: PCS (0 wt%) = 2.8 nm, PMoCS-6wt% = 2.3 nm, PMoCS-8wt% = 2.2 nm, PMoCS-10wt% = 2.2 nm. notes: This paper focuses on polyzirconoxane (PZO) as a preceramic precursor for ZrC ceramic, not a silicon-based preceramic polymer. PZO solution stable >10 days vs. only a few days for ZOC-phenolic resin solution. Organics of PZO undergo in situ carbonization during pyrolysis providing additional carbon for carbothermal reduction, enabling lower C/Zr ratio (2:1) and lower temperature (1550°C) vs. ZOC-ZrC (requires C/Zr=6 and higher temperatures). Final ZrC particle size 200-600 nm with polyhedron morphology (PZO-ZrC) or near-cubic aggregated morphology (ZOC-ZrC). Ceramic yield values (Table II) are mass ratios of pyrolyzed products to cross-linked precursors at 180°C, ranging 0.38-0.55 (PZO-ZrC) and 0.49-0.56 (ZOC-ZrC). Grain size range noted as 200-600 nm; midpoint 400 nm used.

HSR0.03 achieves highest char yield: 63.11% in N2 and 51.57% in air at 800 °C, representing 54.45% and 23.41% increases over HSR0 (40.86% N2, 41.79% air). Static pyrolysis at 1400 °C for 2 h in argon also conducted; amorphous SiOC phase up to 1200 °C, crystalline SiC and SiO2 above 1400 °C.

crosslink_density.value: Relative crosslink density reported via low-field 1H NMR T2 distribution; HSR0.01 shows highest crosslink density; crosslink density decreases with increasing Hf content beyond HSR0.01; Si-H content of curing agent: 3.05-3.10 mmol/g; vinyl content of HSR: 1.46-1.50 mmol/g
crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal hydrosilylation using Karstedt's platinum catalyst at 80 °C for 6 h

backbone_architecture.description: Crosslinked polysiloxane network formed via hydrosilylation of vinyl-functional polysiloxane (HSR) with branched/dendritic Si-H curing agent. HSR synthesized by acid-catalyzed co-condensation of DMPMS, DMVMS, and Hf precursor, end-capped with trimethylsilyl groups (TMES). Network linkages are Si-C-Si and Si-C-C-Si from hydrosilylation alpha- and beta-addition (27.2% alpha, 72.8% beta).

microstructural.ceramic_phase: amorphous SiOC (800-1200 °C); crystalline SiC and SiO2 above 1400 °C; Hf-containing SiOC (amorphous SiHfOC)
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: From 800 to 1200 °C chars are predominantly amorphous SiOC with broad XRD feature at 2theta ~21.3° plus free carbon. Hf doping broadens and shifts amorphous peak to higher angles, suppressing crystallization. Above 1400 °C: SiC peaks at 2theta = 35.6°, 60.0°, 71.8° appear via carbothermal reduction. XPS of HSR0.05 char confirms Si-C, Si-O-Si, and Hf-associated Si-O environments.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Tensile strength of cured HSRs: 0.278-0.470 MPa; elongation at break: 49.5-65.8%; density of cured specimens: 1.094-1.102 g/cm3; char layer puncture strength measured semi-quantitatively using 2 mm cylindrical probe at 2 mm/min on universal testing machine

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Amorphous SiOC (broad feature at 2theta ~21.3°) at 800-1200 °C; crystalline SiC (2theta = 35.6°, 60.0°, 71.8°) and SiO2 above 1400 °C

notes: Six sample variants prepared: HSR0 (no Hf), HSR0.01 through HSR0.05 with increasing Hf content (0.005-0.025 mol Hf). All contain DMPMS (0.4 mol), DMVMS (0.1 mol), TMES (0.005 mol). Hf precursor is di-n-propoxybis(acetylacetonato)hafnium. Crosslinker is a custom-synthesized branched/dendritic Si-H agent based on TMDPTSO, VTES, and TMDS. HSR0.03 is the optimal formulation for thermal protection: highest char yield (63.11% N2, 51.57% air at 800 °C) and minimum mass ablation rate (0.016 g/s at 2 MW/m2). HSR0.04 shows 42.36% reduction in mass ablation rate at 4 MW/m2 vs HSR0. Ablation tests: oxyacetylene at 2 or 4 MW/m2 for 30 s. Ceramic yield of 63.11% is for HSR0.03 in nitrogen at 800 °C (best performing sample). TGA also conducted in air; ceramic yield in air at 800 °C for HSR0.03 is 51.57%. Pyrolysis temperature range in table is 800 °C (TGA endpoint); static pyrolysis also done at 1400 °C for 2 h in argon. Peak area ratio of phenyl:vinyl:methyl groups = 4.1:1:5.1-5.4 from 1H NMR.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C≡C acetylene linkage in backbone (absorptions at 3282 cm-1 C-H and 2048 cm-1 C≡C); Si-CH3 groups (1403, 1258 cm-1); C=C stretch at 1635 cm-1 appears after curing

functional_groups.other: acetylene/ethynylene groups in backbone; terminal ≡C-H groups

Td5% (5% weight loss temperature) above 600°C for all thermosets; Td5% for 4a and 4b above 900°C under N2. Char yields at 900°C under N2: 4a=95.62%, 4b=95.58%, 4c=92.87%, 4d=92.37%, 4e=89.67%. Ceramic residues 5a-e show thermo-oxidative stability with weight retention at 900°C in air: 5a=98.76%, 5b=97.68%, 5c=96.29%, 5d=94.97%, 5e=91.66%. Range 89.67-95.62% at 900°C N2; midpoint ~92.62% reported.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC in THF referenced to polystyrene standards; Mw range 1072-4860 g/mol across 3a-3e; 3a Mw=1072 (nw~19 units), 3e Mw=4860 (nw~71 units)

backbone_architecture.description: Polycondensation of dilithioacetylene with dichlorosilane (H2SiCl2) and/or methyldichlorosilane (MeSiHCl2) yields linear silylene-ethynylene repeat units. Liquid at room temperature, soluble in THF, toluene, CHCl3. 3a: -(SiH2-C≡C-)n; 3e: -(SiHMe-C≡C-)n; 3b-d: copolymers with varying ratios.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD confirms β-SiC with peaks at 2θ=35.6°, 60.0°, 71.8° (111, 220, 311 planes); α-quartz peak at 2θ=26.5°. SEM-EDX and 13C MAS NMR confirm SiC and free carbon. Molar compositions from SEM-EDX: 5a: SiC 80.26%, SiO2 9.42%, excess C 10.32%; 5b: SiC 63.72%, SiO2 4.73%, excess C 31.55%; 5c: SiC 49.79%, SiO2 7.66%, excess C 42.55%; 5d: SiC 43.02%, SiO2 4.51%, excess C 52.47%; 5e: SiC 41.92%, SiO2 3.65%, excess C 54.44%.

notes: Crystallite sizes reported in Angstroms from Scherrer equation on β-SiC (111) line: 5a=16.7 Å, 5b=18.6 Å, 5c=19.7 Å, 5d=20.9 Å, 5e=22.3 Å (1.67-2.23 nm). GPC Mw values for individual polymers: 3a=1072, 3e=4860 g/mol (range 1072-4860); Mn and PDI not explicitly reported. Cure cycles differ: 3a-c heated at 2°C/min through 120/150/170/200/250°C; 3d-e at 5°C/min through 170/200/250/300°C, both under N2. DSC exotherm for 3a is 1169 J/g. Si-O bonds attributed to hydrolysis of residual Si-Cl during workup. The polymer series spans from highest Si/C ratio (3a, no methyl) to lowest (3e, all methyl), with increasing free carbon and decreasing thermo-oxidative stability in resulting ceramics. Molecular weights referenced to polystyrene standards; absolute values may differ.

elemental_composition.other_elements: EDS data reported in wt% for cured/debound/sintered alumina composite stages: Cured: C=12.79, O=37.30, Al=49.90; Degreased: C=4.1, O=44.46, Al=51.44; Sintered: C=0.79, O=53.87, Al=45.22

bonding_structure.other_bonds: C=C bonds (acrylate) consumed during photopolymerization; crosslinked network formed via radical photopolymerization of acrylate groups in CN996NS and HDDA

functional_groups.other: Acrylate functional groups (two per HDDA molecule); urethane acrylate oligomer (CN996NS, difunctional); reactive diluent 1,6-hexanediol diacrylate (HDDA)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA in air from RT to 850°C at 10°C/min. Polymer matrix begins to decompose at ~200°C and is completely decomposed below 500°C. Debinding was performed at 600°C for 3h in argon followed by 600°C for 3h in air. Sintering at 1500°C for 6h in air.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV photopolymerization at 365 nm, 10 W; photoinitiators: TPO (radical) or cationic initiator 1176

backbone_architecture.description: Crosslinked network formed by UV-initiated radical photopolymerization of difunctional polyurethane acrylate oligomer (CN996NS) and difunctional reactive diluent HDDA; filled with alumina nanoparticles (100 nm average particle diameter)

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Cured composite (optimized slurry, 75 wt% alumina): bending modulus ~125 MPa, bending strength ~5 MPa. Sintered alumina ceramic: bending modulus ~200 GPa, bending strength ~38 MPa. Tested by three-point bending (GB/T 2567-2021), specimen 80x10x2 mm, support span 30 mm, loading rate 5 mm/min.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Alumina (Al2O3); XRD used to identify crystalline phases before and after sintering

notes: This paper is primarily about alumina ceramic manufacturing via UV-assisted DIW, not a preceramic polymer paper in the classical sense. The 'preceramic' role is played by a photocurable polyurethane acrylate resin (CN996NS) filled with alumina nanoparticles; the resin acts as a binder/carrier, not a silicon-based preceramic polymer. Optimized slurry composition: 75 wt% alumina, 11.4 wt% CN996NS, 11.4 wt% HDDA, 1.4 wt% BYK-111, 0.8 wt% TPO. Density of cured sample: 2.22 g/cm3; sintered sample: 3.66 g/cm3. Linear shrinkage after sintering: ~20%. Debinding: 600°C/3h in Ar + 600°C/3h in air. Sintering: 1500°C/6h in air. UV curing: 365 nm, 10 W, 5 cm distance, threshold exposure ~36 s for maximum curing depth.

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-O-Si asymmetric stretch confirmed by FTIR at 1000-1200 cm-1; Si-H stretch at 2100-2200 cm-1 and bend at 768 cm-1; Si-C at 874 cm-1

functional_groups.other: Cyclic oligomers [CH3Si(H)O]m with m=3,4,5,6,7,8...; cyclic tetramer, pentamer, hexamer are primary products

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Pyrolysis of copolymers derived from these cyclic polysiloxanes and cyclic polysilazanes is described in Part IV of the series; no TGA data reported in this paper

backbone_architecture.description: Cyclic polysiloxanes [CH3Si(H)O]m with m=3-18 produced by hydrolysis of dichloromethylsilane; primary products are cyclic tetramer (m=4), pentamer (m=5), and hexamer (m=6) with combined yield >95 mol%

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Silicon oxynitride is the target ceramic phase obtained by pyrolysis of copolymers of these cyclic polysiloxanes with cyclic polysilazanes; details in Part IV of series

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Silicon oxynitride noted to have thermal and mechanical properties similar to silicon nitride with superior oxidation resistance; no quantitative mechanical data given in this paper

notes: This paper (Part I of a series) focuses on the hydrolysis of dichloromethylsilane (DMS) to produce cyclic polysiloxanes [CH3Si(H)O]m. The optimized hydrolysis procedure uses dichloromethane as solvent, mechanical stirring, initial HCl concentration of 0.1-3M, and total reaction time up to 5h, achieving >95 mol% combined yield of cyclic tetramer (m=4), pentamer (m=5), and hexamer (m=6). These cyclic polysiloxanes are intermediates for copolymerization with cyclic polysilazanes to form a preceramic polymer that pyrolyses to silicon oxynitride. Characterization by 1H NMR (Si-H at 4.7 ppm, Si-CH3 at 0.21 ppm, ratio 1:3), FTIR, GC, and GC/MS confirmed cyclic polysiloxane structures. No linear oligomers or end-group resonances (-HSi(CH3)OH) were detected by NMR.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: PTA-1-1600 °C: TaC 31.72 wt%, β-SiC 68.28 wt% by Rietveld refinement. Core-shell TaC@C nanoparticles formed in situ at 1400 °C with TaC core and amorphous carbon shell. Free carbon also present in matrix.

notes: The preceramic polymer AHPCS has molecular formula [SiH1.30(CH3)0.60(CH2CH=CH2)0.10CH2]n. Ceramic composition (wt%) for PTA-2 derived ceramics: 900 °C: Si 58.32, Ta 3.50, C 30.96, O 6.32, H 0.90; 1200 °C: Si 58.46, Ta 3.75, C 31.81, O 5.98; 1400 °C: Si 59.06, Ta 4.25, C 32.44, O 4.25; 1600 °C: Si 58.01, Ta 4.50, C 35.22, O 2.27 (all wt%). Grain sizes of both β-SiC and TaC remain <31 nm even at 1600 °C. TaC nanoparticle cores ~5 nm diameter at 1200 °C. Ceramic yield of 88.7 wt% reported here is for PTA-2; range across all precursors is 85.9-89.4 wt%. functional_groups.other: allyl groups (CH2CH=CH2)

Pore volume: 1.75 cm3/g (25C), 0.31 cm3/g (1000C), 0.79 cm3/g (1500C). Weight loss during pyrolysis: 64% at 1000C, 66% at 1200C, 72% at 1500C. Crosslinking characterized by ATR-FTIR and GPC. Coatings spin-coated at 700 rpm on Si(100) wafers, cured at ~23°C, 45-60% RH. Uncatalyzed dry-to-touch ~19 h; TBAC-catalyzed ~1 h. Film thickness ~5 µm. Si/C molar ratio ~2.27 (constant). Hardness and modulus values given separately per condition; midpoints used in hardness_GPa and modulus_GPa fields. No pyrolysis or ceramic conversion data reported.
source: Zhan_2022_Rapid_curing_of_polysilazane_coatings_at_room_temperature_vi

elemental_composition.other_elements: Chemical analysis of material heated to 1100°C yields average formula SiC0.9H<0.2O0.1, suggesting essentially pure SiC with residual H and trace O contamination from handling

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si linkages form during thermal rearrangement at 400°C, characteristic of polycarbosilane intermediate; linear polymer segments -MeSiH- identified by 29Si NMR at -63 ppm; terminal groups -MeSiH2 at -34 ppm

functional_groups.other: Si-CH2-Si units form as intermediate upon pyrolysis at 400°C

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Standard TGA not reproducible due to air sensitivity of polymer; bulk samples heated at 1°C/min under N2 to various temperatures and held for 0.5 h; 77% ceramic yield at 1000°C. At 400°C major rearrangement from polysilane to polycarbosilane occurs. By 600°C, hydrogenated SiC forms. By 800°C, C-H bonds absent and beta-SiC absorptions dominate. Some experiments used 5°C/min heating rate for higher temperature runs.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: catalytic; NMR indicates polymer is partially crosslinked; continued catalyst action leads to intractable gel if left to stand

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC (gel-permeation chromatography); less than 3% cyclics; Mw reported as approximately 10-12 k daltons, midpoint 11000 used

backbone_architecture.description: Primarily linear polymer segments (-MeSiH-) with minor terminal groups (-MeSiH2); partially crosslinked as indicated by proton, carbon, and silicon NMR; less than 3% cyclic content; catalyst promotes further crosslinking over time leading to gel

microstructural.ceramic_phase: beta-SiC with small amounts of alpha-SiC polytypes
microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000°C, 29Si NMR shows narrow peaks at -15.4 and -19.7 ppm consistent with beta-SiC and minor alpha-SiC polytypes. Chemical analysis at 1100°C gives SiC0.9H<0.2O0.1, essentially pure SiC. No SiO2 or Si metal detected by NMR. XRD at 1100°C shows broad features of beta-SiC; sharpens progressively at 1300°C and 1500°C.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Paper references target properties for SiC fibers: tensile strength >4 GPa and elastic modulus >400 GPa, but these are not measured values for this material

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (primary), alpha-SiC polytypes (minor); observed at 1000-1100°C and above

notes: Polymer synthesized by dehydrocoupling of methylsilane (MeSiH3) in one step with >90% yield after 8 days reaction. Crystallite sizes: 4.0 nm at 1100°C, 6.0 nm at 1300°C, 11.0 nm at 1500°C (estimated from XRD peak broadening using 2.51 Å peak, Co Kalpha radiation). Mw range given as 10-12 k daltons; midpoint 11000 used. Heating rate of 1°C/min used for bulk pyrolysis studies up to 1000°C; 5°C/min used for higher temperature runs starting from 600°C. Hold time of 0.5 h (30 min) used for most bulk pyrolysis; 1 h hold used for some higher temperature experiments. Crystalline SiC phases observed at temperatures below 1000°C, significantly lower than other SiC preceramic polymers which typically require ≥1400°C. Transformation pathway: poly(methylsilane) → poly(carbosilane) intermediate at 400°C → hydrogenated SiC at 600°C → crystalline beta-SiC at 1000°C.

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Uncured PSNB: ceramic yield 45.6% at 1000C; weight losses of 23.5% (30-300C) and 32.7% (300-800C). Cured PSNB170: ceramic yield 59.6% at 1000C; weight losses of 5.5% (30-300C) and 36.2% (300-800C). Major gaseous byproducts: H2, NH3, CH4. TGA-MS heating rate was 10 C/min under Ar from 30 to 1000C. High-temperature TGA to 1900C at 10 C/min under Ar: weight loss of 2.6% at 1900C; no obvious weight change up to 1500C. Oxidation TGA to 1350C in air at 10 C/min: weight gain of only 1.8% at 1350C.

Crystallization begins at 1600C with broad peaks at 25, 36, 42, 61, 72 deg. At 1700C peaks sharpen. At 1800C, beta-Si3N4 phase (23, 27, 50, 52, 70, 73 deg) disappears; alpha/beta-SiC peaks (36, 60, 72 deg) increase. Si-B-C-N quaternary ceramic system.

notes: Empirical formula of PSNB170 (cured at 170C): Si1.00 N1.27 B0.09 C1.49 O0.32 H4.83. Empirical formula of PSNB1000 (pyrolyzed at 1000C): Si1.00 N0.84 B0.16 C0.90 O0.15 H1.15. Elemental percentages in elemental_composition field correspond to PSNB170. Viscosity of as-synthesized PSNB below 500 mPa.s between 90-160C; with DCP below 800 mPa.s up to ~140C. Curing done at 170C, 10 C/min, 2h dwell under N2. Pyrolysis in Ar at 5 C/min, 2h hold. Ceramic shows excellent oxidation resistance attributed to passivating amorphous oxide layer from B and Si content. Oxygen in samples attributed to partial hydrolysis of moisture-sensitive precursor during synthesis/transfer.

Curing increases ceramic yield by 17% relative to uncured sample.

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with polystyrene standard calibration in THF

EDX shows Si-rich composition of Si2.76N1.03O. Amorphous SiON structure observed at 800°C by FTIR and solid 29Si NMR.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Si2N2O (2theta = 20°, 27°, 37°) and crystalline Si (2theta = 28°, 48°, 56°) at 1400°C

notes: Polymer synthesized by one-pot partial hydrolysis of H2SiCl2 followed by ammonolysis with NH3 at -30°C. Colorless viscous liquid with dynamic viscosity of 60 mPa·s at 25°C. Organic group-free precursor for carbon-free SiON ceramic. Reference polymers PHSO (perhydropolysiloxane) and PHSN (perhydropolysilazane) used for structural comparison. Ceramic yield of 87% refers to cured PSNO at 1200°C; uncured PSNO gives 70% at 1000°C. Final ceramic at 1400°C is Si-rich (Si2.76N1.03O by EDX). Oxidation stability tested by TGA in air: negligible weight change below 1000°C, only 1.2% weight gain at 1200°C. Pyrolysis heating and cooling rate both 5°C/min; hold time 2h at final temperature.

Ceramic elemental compositions given per temperature: e.g. PSN 800: Si 44.31, C 26.85, N 28.84 at%; PBSN1 800: Si 42.92, C 23.27, N 28.51, B 5.29 at%; PBSN2 800: Si 41.57, C 24.46, N 23.47, B 10.54 at%. notes: Three polymers studied: PSN (polysilazane parent, poly(vinylmethyl)-co-poly(hydro)silazane), PBSN1 (low boron, ~5.9 wt% B), PBSN2 (high boron, ~11.8 wt% B). Dual boron source approach: BH3·THF (hydroboration of Si-Vi groups) + BCl3·hexane (aminolysis with Si-NH groups). Et3N used as acid binding agent; trimethylamine hydrochloride by-product removed by filtration. Boron content in PBSN reported as >11 wt% higher than in starting PSN. Characterization by FTIR, solid-state 29Si and 11B MAS NMR, XPS, XRD, TGA-DSC-QMS, ICP-AES, and elemental analysis. Ceramic empirical formulas reported per pyrolysis temperature in text tables. microstructural.phase_composition_notes: At 1000°C in Ar: primarily tetragonal HfO2 (t-HfO2) with minor monoclinic HfO2 (m-HfO2). At 1200°C in Ar: mainly t-HfO2 with increased crystallinity. At 1400°C in Ar: HfC phase appears via carbothermal reduction. At 1600°C in Ar: mostly HfC with minor m-HfO2 remaining. In vacuum at 1200°C: HfC phase begins to form. At 1400°C vacuum: HfO2 phase disappears. At 1600°C vacuum: only HfC phase, with trace oxygen dissolved in HfC lattice.

notes: This precursor is not a silicon-based preceramic polymer but a hafnium-based ceramic precursor for HfC. Raw materials: HfCl4 (32g, 0.1 mol), acetylacetone (12g, 0.24 mol), methanol (60 mL excess), 1,4-butanediol (4.5g, 0.1 mol). Synthesis: room temperature reaction 1h, then methanol added and reacted 2h, then 1,4-butanediol added dropwise, heated to 60°C reflux 2h, then vacuum dried at 70°C to give dark brown solid PHCO. Precursor is soluble in methanol, n-butanol, and THF. Elemental composition values are in wt%, not atomic%. Grain size range for PHCO-1600 in Ar: 40-200 nm; for PHCO-1600-V in vacuum: 20-100 nm (midpoint ~60 nm used for grain_size_nm). Vacuum pyrolysis promotes more complete carbothermal reduction and produces denser ceramics with fewer pores compared to argon atmosphere.

No significant weight loss above 800 C. Ceramic yield up to 65%. Actual pyrolysis protocol: crosslink at 300 C (0.25 C/min), 300-800 C at 0.5 C/min with 2 h hold at 800 C, then 1 C/min to 1000 C with 2 h hold, cool at 5 C/min.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiBNC ceramic fibers remain completely amorphous up to 1600 C as confirmed by XRD (no sharp diffraction peaks observed). mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Average tensile strength of SiBNC ceramic fibers pyrolyzed at 1000 C: 1.05 GPa (1050 MPa). Fiber diameter ~19 µm after pyrolysis (green fiber diameter ~24 µm). Gauge length 10 mm for tensile testing.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: No crystalline phases detected; completely amorphous up to 1600 C

notes: Polymer precursor synthesized by one-step co-polymerization of SiHCl3, BCl3, and n-propylamine (C3H7NH2) in molar ratio 1:1:12 (BCl3:SiHCl3:C3H7NH2) in n-hexane at -15 to -20 C, then stirred at room temperature overnight. Oligomer condensed and heated to 230 C to form PBSZ as a yellow, highly viscous liquid. Green fibers melt-spun at 80-100 C, 60 m/min through 0.3 mm spinneret capillaries under nitrogen; green fiber diameter ~24 µm. Polymer has improved hydrolysis resistance compared to methylamine-based routes due to higher nucleophilicity of propylamine vs. water, but hydrolysis begins after ~24 h air exposure. DSC of polymer shows Tg 80-100 C, exothermal crosslinking peak ~300 C, another exothermic event ~560 C. DSC of oligomer shows Tg 50-75 C, exothermal polymerization peak ~230 C. PBSZ characterized by FT-IR, 1H, 11B, 13C, 29Si NMR, TGA, DSC, GC-MS, XRD, SEM, TEM, and elemental analysis. Target ceramic: quaternary SiBNC for high-temperature ceramic matrix composite reinforcement.

Polymer is air-sensitive and must be handled under inert atmosphere. Ceramic yield reported as both ~63 wt% (abstract) and 64.9 wt% (results section) at 900 C in N2; 64.9 wt% is the value from the detailed results. Heating rate for full pyrolysis protocol: 0.25 C/min (curing stage) and 0.5 C/min (pyrolysis stage); TGA characterization used 10 C/min. Target ceramic is SiBNC with excellent oxidation resistance. NMR characterization included 1H, 11B, 13C-MAS, and 29Si-MAS NMR. 11B NMR broad peak at 25-27 ppm confirms BN units in six-membered borazine rings.

Further heating to ~1000°C promotes evolution toward amorphous solid approaching stoichiometric Si3N4. For silica conversion, thermal treatment at 450°C in air produces dense silica coatings with density 2.1-2.2 g/cm3. mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Hardness and modulus values depend strongly on conversion conditions. Thermal 450°C air: ~5.30 GPa hardness, ~67.2 GPa modulus. Photochemical VUV 172nm RT: ≥6H pencil hardness. IPL 12.6 J/cm2 RT: 3.25 GPa hardness, 28.0 GPa modulus. Aminosilane catalytic conversion yields hardness exceeding 3 GPa. Residual stress in PHPS-derived films at early conversion stage ~9.8 MPa, rising to ~190 MPa at 600°C. Crack-free coatings exceeding 1000 nm thickness achievable.

notes: This is a review paper focused on perhydropolysilazane (PHPS) as a preceramic/precursor polymer for solution-processed silica coatings. PHPS molecular formula/repeating unit: -[H2Si-NH]n-, carbon-free inorganic backbone. Synthesis originally by ammonolysis of dichlorosilane (SiH2Cl2 + NH3). Density after full thermal conversion: 2.1-2.2 g/cm3; refractive index: 1.45-1.46; dielectric constant: ~4.2. Catalytically converted films have lower density ~1.9 g/cm3. VUV photon energy 7.2 eV (172 nm) exceeds Si-N bond dissociation energy (3.4 eV) and Si-H bond dissociation energy (3.3 eV), enabling room-temperature conversion. Dual-wavelength irradiation (254 and 185 nm) extends effective penetration depth to ~160 nm. Applications include microelectronic dielectrics, environmental barrier coatings, and functional composite systems. Dielectric constants reported: 3.8-19.2 depending on processing. WVTR values for barrier coatings range from 3.18×10^-6 to 0.72 g/m2/day depending on substrate and processing. Film shrinkage with aminosilane catalytic conversion restricted to less than 1%. Residual N content after thermal conversion: 2.70 at% (450°C air), 0.26 at% (600°C air), 0.13 at% (1000°C air/N2). Hardness and modulus values in notes field represent full range from comparison table across all conversion methods.

functional_groups.other: phenylamino groups (aniline-derived); N-methylaniline-derived blocking groups; borazine ring

thermal_pyrolysis.pyrolysis_atmosphere: ammonia (NH3); comparative experiments also done in N2
thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA conducted in argon at 10 C/min from 25-1200 C. Two-stage weight loss: stage 1 (RT-300 C) ~52 wt% loss with two endothermic peaks at ~157.9 and ~278.5 C attributed to escape of small organic molecules; stage 2 (300-1200 C) ~14.47 wt% loss with broad exothermic peak indicating curing and crystallization. Total ceramic yield 33.53%. Actual pyrolysis done under NH3 at 2 C/min; TGA is only a guideline.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal; aniline used as cross-linking agent, N-methylaniline as blocking agent during synthesis

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC with Waters 515 HPLC pump, DMF as solvent

backbone_architecture.description: TCB reacted with N-methylaniline first to consume one B-Cl bond (blocking), then the remaining two active B-Cl bonds reacted with bifunctional aniline to form a linear polymer. Polymerization degree of 319.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: XRD peaks at 26.6 and 41.9 degrees indexed to (002) and (100) planes of h-BN (JCPDS 34-0421). FTIR bands at 1383.5 and 795.5 cm-1 characteristic of h-BN. Carbon content reduced to 0.90 wt% at 1200 C under NH3. Near-stoichiometric BN achieved under NH3 atmosphere.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: BN fibers from related work (Toury et al.) reported tensile strength up to 0.69 GPa; BN ceramic fibers from PPAB had diameter ~3-4 micrometers and appeared dense and smooth without flaws by SEM, but no mechanical values reported for PPAB-derived fibers

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), JCPDS 34-0421

notes: This polymer is a BN precursor, not a silicon-based preceramic polymer. No Si is present. Polymer synthesized from B-trichloroborazine (TCB), aniline (cross-linking agent), and N-methylaniline (blocking agent) in toluene at 50 C for 13 h. Optimal molar ratio TCB:N-methylaniline:aniline = 1.0:1.5:1.0. B:N atomic ratio ~0.83:1 by XPS. Crystallite sizes at 550, 1000, and 1200 C are 1.0, 1.2, and 1.5 nm respectively. Elemental compositions of pyrolyzed ceramics at various temperatures and atmospheres given in table (wt%: N, B, C, O, H). Grain size of 1.5 nm reported for 1200 C sample. Hold time of 2 h used for pyrolysis. Polymer melt-spinnable at 70-120 C; green fibers drawn by hand and pyrolyzed to BN ceramic fibers at 1000 C under NH3.
source: Zhong_2016_A_Novel_Polymeric_Precursor_for_Boron_Nitride_Ceramics_Synth

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-CH2-Si backbone linkage confirmed by FTIR at 1040 cm-1; Si-H2 group at 940 cm-1; traces of -CH2Cl and O(CH2)4 segment from THF side reaction observed by 1H NMR

functional_groups.other: No unsaturated functional groups present in the base LHBPCS; divinyldimethylsilane additive [(CH3)2Si(CH=CH2)2] introduced separately as crosslinking monomer

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: TGA performed in nitrogen up to 1000 C at 10 C/min. Uncrosslinked LHBPCS ceramic yield: 42 wt%. UV-irradiated pure LHBPCS ceramic yields: 67.4 (15 min), 68.3 (20 min), 70.5 (25 min), 71.8 wt% (30 min). LHBPCS + 5 wt% divinyldimethylsilane ceramic yields: 66.5 (15 min), 71.2 (20 min), 76.5 (25 min), 79.0 wt% (30 min). Pyrolysis furnace atmosphere was argon; TGA measurement atmosphere was nitrogen.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: UV irradiation at 365 nm (UVITRON INTERNATIONAL IntelliRay 600, 100% intensity, 10 cm distance, room temperature); dehydrocoupling of Si-H groups and hydrosilylation between Si-H and vinyl groups of divinyldimethylsilane additive

molecular_weight.measurement_method: GPC (TOSOH HLC-8320, THF eluent, 1 mg/mL concentration); values reported for uncrosslinked LHBPCS

backbone_architecture.description: Liquid hyperbranched polycarbosilane with Si-CH2-Si backbone, synthesized via Grignard coupling of chloromethyltrichlorosilane (Cl3SiCH2Cl) followed by LiAlH4 reduction. Branched structure confirmed by 29Si NMR showing complex multiples. Approximate formula [SiH2CH2]n with Si:C ratio matching SiC stoichiometry.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Near-stoichiometric SiC ceramic obtained after pyrolysis to 1000 C. Excellent thermal stability demonstrated at 1400 C in air. XRD analysis performed (Bruker D8 Advance, Cu Ka radiation, 10-90 deg 2-theta).

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: SiC (inferred from near-stoichiometric composition; XRD performed but specific phases not enumerated in provided text)

notes: LHBPCS synthesized without unsaturated functional groups (unlike allyl- or vinyl-substituted analogues such as SMP-10). UV crosslinking via dehydrocoupling of Si-H groups; Si-H conversion reached 76.8% after 20 min UV irradiation. Addition of 5 wt% divinyldimethylsilane as external crosslinking monomer increased Mw to 5088 g/mol after 5 min UV and ceramic yield to 79.0 wt% after 30 min UV. Vinyl group reaction extent reached 79.5% after only 5 min UV irradiation. Polymer viscosity: 0.046 Pa·s at 25 C. Synthesis yield: 62.5%. Traces of O(CH2)4 segment from THF side reaction and -CH2Cl present. Two GPC tables provided: Table 1 for pure LHBPCS under UV, Table 2 for LHBPCS + 5 wt% divinyldimethylsilane under UV; molecular weight values reported here are for uncrosslinked baseline.
source: Zhong_2017_Accelerating_the_crosslinking_process_of_hyperbranched_polyc

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-C backbone as repeating unit (SiH(CH3)-CH2-)n

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PCS pyrolyzed at 1073 K (800 C) yielded ~58% mass with amorphous product and C/Si ratio near 1.6. Above 1273 K, amorphous product converted to beta-SiC plus amorphous carbon with volume ratio ~4:1. Heating profile: RT to 423 K in 30 min, held 60 min; 423 K to 1073 K in 210 min, held 90 min; cooled at ~3 K/min.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal

backbone_architecture.description: Repeating unit (SiH(CH3)-CH2-)n indicating a linear Si-C backbone chain

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Pyrolysis at 1073 K yields amorphous product with C/Si ~1.6. Above 1273 K, converts to beta-SiC and amorphous carbon in volume ratio ~4:1. In hot-pressed composites, very weak beta-SiC XRD peaks observed. Amorphous carbon content approximately 4 vol% in final composite.

mechanical_properties.other_mechanical: Fracture toughness of dense S-16 specimen: 3.4 MPa m^1/2

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: beta-SiC (crystallizes above 1273 K); product at 1073 K is amorphous

notes: PCS was used as a precursor to coat ZrB2 powder to form in-situ SiC and C upon pyrolysis for ZrB2-SiC-C UHTC fabrication. Average molecular weight reported as ~1250 (likely Mw or average, method not specified). Pyrolysis temperature in Kelvin: 1073 K = 800 C (used as pyrolysis_temp_C). Heating rate not given in C/min but detailed step profile provided. The C/Si atomic ratio after pyrolysis at 1073 K was ~1.6. Hot pressing performed at 2073 K (1800 C) for 60 min under 20 MPa in Ar.
source: Zhou_2007_Hot_pressed_ZrB2SiCC_ultra_high_temperature_ceramics_with_po

elemental_composition.other_elements: Elemental composition given in wt%: PBSZ-3: Si=19.18, C=36.84, B=8.05, N=23.76, O=3.09, H=9.08; empirical formula SiC4.48N2.47H13.26B1.09O0.28. CPSZ: Si=28.15, C=32.98, N=25.29, O=5.58, H=8.00; empirical formula SiC2.73N1.80H7.95O0.35

bonding_structure.other_bonds: B-H present (2250-2370 cm-1 and 1170 cm-1); B-N bonds formed (1350 cm-1); B-C bonds formed via hydroboration (BCH2CH2Si units); B coordinated with N (C3B←N); vinyl C=C groups in CPSZ precursor

functional_groups.other: Dimethylamine group from DMAB (B·N-H at 3220 cm-1); borane BH3 group; C-N from DMAB (1030 cm-1)

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: PBSZ ceramic yields range 77.5-80.0 wt% at 900C vs 57.8 wt% for boron-free CPSZ. Main weight loss below 300C for CPSZ (24.4 wt%) vs much lower for PBSZs (PBSZ-1: 7.2%, PBSZ-2: 6.5%, PBSZ-3: 10.0%). H2 evolved 100-250C, NH3 150-300C, C2H4/C2H2 300-700C, CH4/C2H6 500-800C. Polymer-to-ceramic transformation nearly complete by 900C. Post-900C annealing at 1200-1800C at 40C/min, hold 10 min.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: thermal - via hydroboration (B-H/C=C), dehydrocoupling (Si-H/N-H, B-H/N-H, Si-H/Si-H, Si-NH/Si-H), hydrosilylation (Si-H/C=C), and transamination reactions

backbone_architecture.description: CPSZ has approximate formula [SiH(CH3)NH]x[Si(CH=CH2)(CH3)NH]y[Si(CH3)(NH)NH]z with x/y/z=1/2.3/0.9; PBSZ formed by chemical modification of CPSZ with DMAB via hydroboration and dehydrocoupling reactions leading to a crosslinked solid polymer network. PBSZ-3 is a white solid polymer obtained in quantitative yield.

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: SiBCN ceramics remain amorphous up to high temperatures. At T>1500C, Si3N4 nanocrystals form with BN(C) phase segregating as interlayer between Si3N4 nanocrystals. SiCN (boron-free) begins crystallizing at lower temperatures. At 1800C, SiBCN-3 still retains significant N content (15.90 wt%) while SiCN is nearly depleted of N (1.20 wt%). XRD and TEM used to characterize crystallization behavior.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Si3N4 nanocrystals formed in SiBCN at T>1500C; BN(C) phase as interlayer; SiCN ceramics crystallize at lower temperatures than SiBCN

notes: Paper focuses on synthesis of polyborosilazane (PBSZ) by reaction of copolysilazane (CPSZ) with dimethylaminoborane (DMAB). Three PBSZ variants prepared at DMAB/CPSZ weight ratios of 1/4 (PBSZ-1), 1/2 (PBSZ-2), and 1/1 (PBSZ-3). CPSZ molecular weight Mn~400 g/mol, PDI=1.8, synthesized from CH3SiHCl2/CH3Si(CH=CH2)Cl2/CH3SiCl3 in feed ratio 1/2/1. Ceramic yield range 77.5-80.0% used as midpoint 78.75% in thermal_pyrolysis field. Post-pyrolysis annealing at 1200, 1400, 1600, 1800C at 40C/min with 10 min hold. SiBCN ceramics show significantly enhanced thermal stability vs boron-free SiCN. TEM confirms BN(C) interlayer formation between Si3N4 nanocrystals above 1500C. Molecular weight reported for CPSZ precursor only, not for PBSZ.
source: Zhou_2014_Dimethylaminoborane_modified_copolysilazane_as_a_novel_precu

bonding_structure.other_bonds: Si-N-Si or cyclic (-Si-N-)n linkages identified by IR at 1000-840 cm-1; absence of Si-H band at 2120 cm-1 indicates extensive crosslinking

functional_groups.other: ammonium chloride byproduct present; N-H groups from ammonolysis

thermal_pyrolysis.tga_notes: Overall weight loss of 75-83% when heated to 1200°C (midpoint ~79%). Weight loss attributed mostly to loss of NH4Cl and NH3. Above 400°C, volatiles such as low molecular weight oligomers and methane evolve. Amorphous nitride forms at 550-700°C, after which little weight loss occurs. Heating rate was 5°C/min from 20 to 500°C, then 1°C/min from 500 to 1450°C.

crosslink_density.crosslinking_method: chemical - aerosol reaction of methyldichlorosilane droplets with ammonia gas; extensive crosslinking inferred from absence of Si-H IR band and insolubility in common solvents

molecular_weight.measurement_method: Cryoscopic molecular weight determination attempted but material was insoluble in all common solvents tested; described as high molecular weight

backbone_architecture.description: Highly crosslinked silazane network formed by aerosol ammonolysis of methyldichlorosilane; insoluble in benzene, cyclohexane, methyl sulfoxide, p-dioxane, and melted camphor, indicating high crosslink density and network structure

microstructural.phase_composition_notes: Calcined product at 1450°C consists of approximately 40% alpha-Si3N4 and ~60% beta-Si3N4 with minor contamination of Si, SiC, or SiO2. Some residual amorphous phase may be present. Precursor powder before calcination is amorphous.

conformation_crystallinity.xrd_phases_identified: Precursor powder is amorphous; calcined product shows alpha-Si3N4 and beta-Si3N4 phases

notes: Silazane oligomers/polymer synthesized by aerosol ammonolysis of methyldichlorosilane (MDS) droplets with ammonia gas at -75°C in a cryogenic aerosol flow apparatus. Reaction occurs in less than 1 second. Product is a white powder mixture of silazane and ammonium chloride. NH4Cl removed by THF dissolution and filtration. Calcination at 1450°C yields spherical agglomerated particles of Si3N4 with narrow size distribution without prior crosslinking step. Precursor is described as higher molecular weight than solution-phase silazanes from same reactants. Ceramic yield reported as inverse of TGA weight loss (75-83% loss up to 1200°C); midpoint weight loss used for ceramic_yield_pct calculation (100 - 79 = ~21%, approximated as 20%). Heating rates during pyrolysis: 5°C/min from 20-500°C, then 1°C/min from 500-1450°C; held at 1450°C for 2 hours.
source: Zimmermann_1991_Synthesis_of_a_silazane_polymer_by_chemical_reaction_in_an_a
